(a) BELOW 15.7: the standing rule says stop and investigate, and the first suspects are the ones that have cost a pass each - check_dna_declarations first, then <out>/_rejects.json (a String enum handed an int is refused in SILENCE), then whether _read_metadata_overrides actually reassigned the property. Every prediction in this corpus that named a pair and a number has UNDER-read by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a flat-shaded proxy models no shadow, no AO and no antialiasing; a result under its own floor has meant a broken artifact, not a subtle one. (b) FAR ABOVE, say past 45: the courses wash is landing somewhere other than alternate courses - most likely i%2 running over the field index instead of the course index, which would recolour whole stacks and read as a much bigger change than the design makes.

primitive_pillar.label: Primitive Pillar (stacked column)

dna.default: points=5, waist_radius=0.25 - these are the constants the shipped 22-vertex table encodes, and at the default the code returns that literal table verbatim rather than regenerating it, so all 10 existing placements get byte-identical geometry with no float drift
dna.was: zero exports: a five-pointed star hard-coded as 22 literal vertices and 40 literal face indices, a magic table with no way in
dna.argues: reading the table back shows it is not a magic list at all - ten rim points at 36-degree steps alternating radius 0.25 and 0.50. Turning points and waist_radius asks where a star stops: at 12 points it is a sun or a gear, at waist 0.45 the arms sink into a polygon, at 0.10 they become needles. The artifact's own truth is 'form is data'; the axes show that the data itself has an author.

star_primitive.name: Star
star_primitive.qfep_connection: A five-pointed star given thickness — the primitive of the emblem, the shape that means before it measures. The one exhibit here whose geometry is mostly semantic: five points, a pentagram's ghost, proof that even the alphabet of pure form carries meanings it did not ask for.
star_primitive.label: Star

dna.default: cordon=cones is a no-op. _build_scene still lays the ground with the hole, then places three traffic cones (same TAU/3 spacing, same PI/6 offset, same cone_distance, same rotation.y = angle + PI, same trafficcone.tscn), then builds the four ground collision boxes, in that order; the only change is that the cone call now sits behind `match cordon:` with cones as the first case and the export default. All 10 placements (10 direct interactable tokens in 10 maps by direct count, none of which passes a config key, plus one curation_station bay that names it in an artifacts list) are unchanged. apply_grid_config is NEW and reads exactly one key: it returns before touching anything unless `cordon` is present AND names a different value than the one already built - which matters because curation_station places this artifact in an Ontological-distance bay and calls apply_grid_config with framing keys this object has never heard of.
dna.was: four exported floats - ground size, hole radius, ground colour, cone distance - no apply_grid_config at all, so every config key a map could send was silently discarded, and the warning was welded to the pit: three cones or three cones.
dna.note: The hole is the artifact; the cones are the SPEECH ACT about the hole, and they were fused to it. A hazard is not what is missing but what the surrounding matter has been made to announce, and the object could make only one announcement. cones is the shipped site: portable, provisional, stackable, a warning that expects to be taken away again. tape draws the perimeter and stops nobody - a line, not an obstacle, the rest left to your judgement. barrier is the warning become a wall: it no longer addresses your judgement, it removes the choice, and safe and permitted stop being separate things. none is the control case - the danger entirely real and saying nothing, the floor reading as floor until you are in it, which is what proves the other four were speech rather than geometry. covered is the most common answer on a real site and the most double-edged: the pit is not declared but sealed, the ground reads whole, and the absence has been made invisible rather than safe. Marking and concealing turn out to be the same gesture taken one step further.
dna.kin: `warning` (force_vortex, path_cube, path_wedge and eight more: none|stain|cage|beacon|shroud) asks this exact question and was declined, because the list cannot transfer character for character: the shipped default here is a specific piece of real-world equipment, cones, which is not in that list, and the default has to reproduce the pre-change behaviour. Taking the word with a different list would put two incompatible value sets behind one name, which is the state `presence` got into. `guard` (library_rack, exhibit_vitrine, exhibit_furniture: none|label|fixture|hood|cordon) holds cordon as one of its VALUES, a vitrine's barrier among four other things a display can do; here the cordon is the whole speech act rather than one option inside it, so it is the axis name. Nearest in spirit is you_are_here's `deixis`, promoted the same day - both artifacts are about what a sign claims - and the values deliberately do not rhyme, because one addresses a body and the other marks a pit.
dna.harness_note: The subject is a 4 m ground plane and the cordon occupies the middle metre of it, so a whole-AABB fit will dilute the difference; if the tiles read faint, crop to the middle before calling the axis inert - none and cones differ by three cones on an otherwise identical 4 m square. covered is the one value that also changes the ground reading (the pit disappears) and is therefore the strongest tile; barrier is the next. tape and barrier carry no collision by design - they are declarations, and the artifact has always been an environment piece you can walk through the props of - while covered DOES add a collision plate, because a picture of sealed ground that you fall through would be lying in one sense and telling the truth in the other.

hole_with_cones.description: Three traffic cones standing around a hole that is no longer drawn — the cordon without the site. The asphalt slab and its circular hole are still in the code behind with_ground, off by default since 2026-08-18; hole_with_cones#with_ground:true restores the full construction site.
hole_with_cones.name: Hole With Cones
hole_with_cones.qfep_connection: A ground plane with a circular hole and three warning cones — the negative primitive, a shape defined by its absence. Construction-site vernacular making the point the origin couldn't: that a void is also a form, and that the floor of this world can be told to *not* be there.
hole_with_cones.label: Hole With Cones

form_in_hand.name: A form in the hand
form_in_hand.description: An open moon court: a torus at five metres varies rings and tube segments independently, casting a real lunar shadow. Beside it, the suspended black catalyst point simplifies while held and sends its current form on trigger.
interactions: Grip: simplify the sphere
Trigger: send the current form
Release: return after two seconds
form_in_hand.qfep_connection: The form being inspected becomes a capacity in the hand; reducing divisions changes what can be sent without replacing the point.
form_in_hand.label: A form in the hand

truncatedtetrahedron.description: tetrahedron with corners cut — each vertex replaced by a triangular face, adding 4 new faces. DNA: truncation is how deep the cut goes as a fraction of the body (the parameter the Archimedean family is indexed by); origin_solid decides whether the un-cut tetrahedron stands around the result as a translucent shell, so the cut reads as a subtraction. Config: #truncation:0.9#origin_solid:ghost

dna.default: truncation=0.5, origin_solid=hidden - 0.5 reproduces the previous mesh vertex for vertex (corner vertices at ±0.1 against a body of ±0.2) and hidden is the result shown alone, so the 11 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: zero exports. The artifact claims truncation is an OPERATION and then showed exactly one frozen output of it: the cut depth lived as the bare literal 0.1 in a vertex array, a ratio of one half against the body's 0.2, named nowhere. An operation you can only ever see one result of is indistinguishable from a shape.
dna.note: origin_solid=ghost answers the question the static version could not — cut from WHAT. It closes the seed tetrahedron's four faces on the same corner vertices and stands them around the result unshaded at 16% alpha.

truncatedtetrahedron.name: truncatedtetrahedron
truncatedtetrahedron.qfep_connection: A tetrahedron with its corners cut — each vertex replaced by a triangular face, the simplest Archimedean solid. The primitive that shows how truncation makes a new regular form from an old one: slice the points off the minimal solid and thirteen semi-regular cousins become possible. Geometry reproducing by amputation, the Platonic set giving birth to the Archimedean.
truncatedtetrahedron.label: truncatedtetrahedron

cylinder_radials_rings.description: Configurable cylinder with radial segments and rings. Usage: cylinder_radials_rings:90:1:#config:12:8 for 12 radial segments and 8 rings.
cylinder_radials_rings.name: Cylinder Radials Rings
cylinder_radials_rings.qfep_connection: The map itself gets a vote on how round this is: '#config:12:8' reaches through the grid layer to set radial_segments, so 'cylinder' names a range running from square prism to smooth column. Roundness as a negotiable quantity rather than a shape.

righttriangle.capacity: READ which properties survive rotation and translation because the right angle stays invariant.

dna.default: proportion=isoceles + reading=uniform - both legs were hard-coded to triangle_size and the slab was a single uniform black surface, so the default rebuilds the original mesh vertex-for-vertex and adds no extra nodes; all 16 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: No exports at all. base_color and triangle_size were plain private vars, the two legs were both pinned to triangle_size (the isoceles case), and there was no apply_grid_config(). The artifact's stated truth - that the right angle is the invariant surviving motion - was never spoken by the form itself, which read as one mute black wedge. proportion turns the claim over: isoceles argues that the metre grid cannot name the hypotenuse, 3-4-5 argues that the rope-stretchers could build it with knots, 1-2 generates root five, kepler puts the sides in golden ratio. reading decides whether the form names its invariant out loud: corner_marked adds the draughtsman's square glyph at the origin, legs_hypotenuse colours the two given sides against the derived third.
dna.note: Existing set_base_color() and set_triangle_size() were also broken before this pass - both reached for get_child(0), which is the scene's embedded Camera3D, not the mesh. The parts list added here fixes that.

righttriangle.description: A right triangle presented as a clean spatial reference. Translation and rotation can move it anywhere, but the ninety-degree relation remains the defining invariant. inspect how a thin 2D form behaves inside 3D space

eleven_dots.name: Eleven Dots
eleven_dots.description: Max Wertheimer's array, built in a room. Eleven small matte spheres stand in the air with nothing drawn between them, and from a marked spot on the floor 3.2 m away they read unmistakably as a cross. Wertheimer's subjects reported the cross first and had to be asked twice before they counted the dots — evidence, he argued, that the whole arrives before the parts, against Mach's accumulation of discrete sense-atoms and alongside Ehrenfels on melody. The dots are NOT coplanar: each is slid along the ray from the mark through its place in the figure, so the cross is exact from the mark and sheared from anywhere else, which is what makes walking in dissolve the figure rather than merely enlarge it. The default depth (0.55 m across a 2.4 m figure) is deliberately modest — a bit under half the 0.40 m dot pitch of lateral shear at 35 degrees off-axis, so the cross survives a still while visibly not being flat. Turn it up and the figure exists only at the mark. #figure switches the demonstration: cross (proximity and continuation), square (eleven dots on a twelve-slot perimeter, the twelfth left out, and the eye closes it — that is closure, a different law), none (the control, seeded, in the cross's own bounding box). The dots have no colliders by default, because a visitor has to be able to walk into the field and because a point is position without extension. The primitives sequence opens by claiming exactly that; this is the objection standing next to it.

measurements.source: procedural, defaults: cross of 11 at spread_m 2.4 (0.40 m pitch), depth_m 0.55, dot_radius_m 0.05, mark at stand_distance_m 3.2 toward +Z

dev_themes: a point is position without extension
what you see is a fact about where you stand
eleven_dots.qfep_connection: The primitives arc opens on the point as position without extension — a definition that puts everything real in the parts and nothing in the arrangement. Eleven Dots is the counter-case standing in the same corridor: the cross is not in any dot, not between any two dots, and not anywhere in the room. It is produced by a body at a particular place, and it leaves when the body does. Reading the figure is not passive reception of what is there; it is something the visitor DOES, and the same eleven objects support a different truth from two metres to the left.
eleven_dots.note: ADDED 2026-09-09. THE ORIGIN IS THE FLOOR at the centre of the dot field — place the token on the DOT cell; the standing mark eats floor at +Z, toward the approach, which is what clearance.front is for. Config keys, every numeric one drawn from CONFIG_PARAM_NAMES because GridInteractablesComponent.gd:1705 reads an unlisted #key:<number> as the tutorial's positional shorthand: #figure:cross|square|none · #count:11 · #size:2.4 (figure height, alias #width) · #depth:0.55 (0 = coplanar) · #radius:0.05 · #outer:3.2 (metres to the mark) · #mark:false · #solid:true · #color1:e6e4dc (six hex digits, NO leading # — the token is split on # before it is parsed, so #color1:#e6e4dc loses the value entirely). Booleans must take WORD values — #solid:0 is a lone numeric on an unlisted key and is eaten as a rotation. eye_height_m is intentionally NOT reachable from a token: #height: means 'how tall is the thing' everywhere else in this corpus. No dna.axes block: the figure knob is a real family but nothing has swept or bitten it yet, and #figure:none is the honest control that a sweep would need. REVIEWED 2026-09-09: auto_ground is false because the dots are SUPPOSED to hang — with the mark painted the AABB base is 0.006 and auto-ground is a no-op inside its own 0.01 tolerance, but under #mark:false the lowest geometry is the lowest dot at 0.395 and the grid would drop the whole field by that much, eating the 0.12 m floor clearance and pulling the solved standpoint down under a standing visitor. Verified min_y 0.006 (mark) / 0.395 (dots) against the defaults; aabb_size re-measured to [1.74, 2.94, 3.82].
eleven_dots.label: Eleven Dots

dna.default: stencil=quadrant, division=frame - the shipped rug, bit-identical rather than merely equivalent. quadrant is the fall-through arm of _enforce_symmetry and runs _enforce_quadrant, which is the original four writes in the original order; its seeding branch is the original `for x in range(width/2): for y in range(height/2)` loop character for character, so the randf() stream drawn under seed(12345) is consumed in the same order and produces the same 24576 draws. That mattered: reshaping the seed loop would have changed the RNG sequence and therefore the rug, in every placement, while every stage still ran green. division=frame is _is_border's original boolean expression, now reached after one integer compare against a mode resolved once per grid build rather than per cell. MEASURED: four placements, none passing a key - `persian_rug:0:-0.49` in CA_Introduction, bare `persian_rug` in Corridor_CA_Introduction and Disposition_Test_Hub, and the name inside curation_station's `#artifacts:` list in Curation_Bay_cellularautomata_0, where the trailing #with_wall/#with_pillars/#with_barrier keys belong to the STATION and never reach this token. The `:0:-0.49` form is artifact:rotation:y_offset, not config.
dna.was: the runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS and was right, though not for the obvious reason: this file already had a dozen @exports, and apply_grid_config was a literal `pass`, so not one of them could be reached from a map token and every rug in the project was the same rug. Meanwhile the two things the artifact actually argues were not exports at all - the symmetry was welded into _enforce_symmetry as a hard-coded four-fold mirror, and the border/field boundary was welded into _is_border as a hard-coded rectangle.
dna.why_these_two: both were derived from the file's own @identity, not invented for it. `truth` says symmetry imposed on local rules turns noise into ornament - and that claim could not be tested, because the symmetry could not be removed. `critical_parameter` names the two rulesets as the tension - but the SHAPE of the boundary between them, which is the thing that makes a carpet a carpet rather than a noise field, was not a parameter. stencil turns the first, division turns the second.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: mirrored_cellular_automata - the word `stencil`, taken with its answers. `quadrant` and `none` are the same operations under the same names (four-fold mirror; no stencil, every cell drawn on its own account at the same density), and `motif` is the same idea of one small block broadcast outward. The two artifacts are the pair the @identity already names as contrasts, and on this question they measure alike.
dna.value_declined: `octant`, mirrored_cellular_automata's fourth. Its eight-fold stencil is the diagonal reflection grid[x][y], which only closes on a SQUARE grid; this rug is 256x384 and its footprint is [3,1,4] - a runner, taller than it is wide by design. Declaring octant would have named a mechanism this object lacks, which is folding_past's and bouncing_ball's fault exactly, and the sweep would have rendered it as the default. `halfturn` replaces it because 180-degree point symmetry IS native to a rectangle: the same regularity as quadrant with no mirror line anywhere in the cloth, which is the pmm/p2 distinction that ornament actually turns on.
dna.division_is_this_artifact_own_word: no sibling asks where two rulesets meet, so nothing was there to reuse. frame says ornament is BOUNDED, medallion says it RADIATES from a centre (the classic Persian centrepiece, the exact inverse of the frame), bands says it ACCUMULATES IN COURSES like a kilim, and none abolishes the inside/outside distinction altogether - the control, which asks whether the two-ruleset claim was load-bearing at all. Because _update_texture_slice also picks the ACTIVE COLOUR from _is_border, this axis moves the pink and the gold as well as the rules.
dna.still_note: the axis is legible in the very first frame and does not depend on capture timing: _initialize_grid applies the stencil to the seed before a single step runs, so a quadrant rug is symmetric at t=0 and a `none` rug never is. The automaton then re-enforces the stencil after every step, so the property holds as it evolves. The whole thing is deterministic at the default because random_seed ships false and the grid is seeded from seed(12345) - so two captures of the same value at the same settle time are the same image. apply_grid_config accepts random_seed through a _truthy() converter rather than assigning a fixture string to the typed bool.
dna.declines: the rule arrays (rule_border_born/survive/states and the inner set) stay plain exports and are NOT declared: they are the sibling family's `rule` question, and a Life-family rulestring axis on top of these two would be a third variable over the same picture. Also declined: step_interval, play_duration and pause_duration, which are rates and durations and invisible to a still - the info_board fault.

dna.default: depth=6, recession=nested - 6 is the number example_8_2_recursion_vr.tscn has always written on the root (the export is renamed from max_depth and the scene line renamed with it, so the value on disk is unchanged), and the six terms are still 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625 and 0.03125 at the same centre. depth is also the only term in the colour index and the z step, both of which read (depth - d), so iteration 0 is still red at z 0 and iteration 5 still purple at z 0.015. nested is a NO-OP by construction: _seat returns Vector3.ZERO and _drawn_size hands the size straight back, so _draw_recursive_pattern's call reduces to the shipped _create_square(center, size, d), and _frame_bounds returns the shipped initial_size square so the four frame bars land on the same coordinates with the same bar_length. All 5 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Fractals_Necklace, Hangar_Fractals_Walk and the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion and Curation_Bay_fractals_2 curation_station rosters) carry the bare token with no config keys, and GridInteractablesComponent does not even CALL apply_grid_config for a token that carries none - so no placement reaches an assignment, let alone the rebuild.
dna.was: five @export knobs and not one categorical among them: max_depth an int, size_reduction and initial_size floats, show_frame a bool, frame_thickness a size - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so the artifact advertised the hook and threw every key away. The @identity's own declared critical_parameter (size_reduction, 'the ratio between parent and child determines whether the nesting feels dense or sparse') was unreachable from any map token, and every placement got the same six squares. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.finding: THE BRANCHING FACTOR IS ONE, and it is why the ladder is cheap here and why the file's own truth line overstates its case. _draw_recursive_pattern makes exactly ONE recursive call, so this is a tail call - a loop wearing recursion's clothes - and the population at every level is a single square, not a set. Cost per rung is +1 mesh, against Menger's x20 and Sierpinski's x5. The ladder was measured rather than assumed: the walk stops on `d <= 0 or size < 0.01`, so at the shipped initial_size 1.0 and size_reduction 0.5 the terms run 1.0 ... 0.015625 and the eighth, 0.0078125, is culled. SEVEN rungs build and an eighth cannot, which is the example_8_4 fault (a rung that exists in the enum and cannot be drawn) caught before declaring rather than after.
dna.note: recession is what shape the descent takes, and it is the file's own truth line made switchable. 'A square inside a square is not decoration - it is the first evidence that a function can call itself' is a CLAIM about containment, and the artifact could only ever assert it. abreast stages the counterfactual the nesting was built to refuse: the same six terms at the same six sizes laid along X with their bottom edges aligned, succession without containment - which is what a tail call actually costs, since no frame survives inside another. strata stacks them up Y, each term sitting on the one before, oldest at the bottom: deposition rather than containment. collapsed drives the nest to its own limit, every term drawn at the innermost size inside a frame that has not moved. The run in both laid-out values is the SUM OF THE SIZES THE RULE ITSELF PRODUCED - no spacing constant is invented anywhere - and the colours, the alphas, the z step and the term count are identical at all four values, so what changes between the tiles is the arrangement and only the arrangement.
dna.kin: depth is example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr's word, one file along in the same NOC chapter and literally the same algorithm with tori instead of boxes, and through it the L-system family's (lsystem_editor, room_grammar, space_filling_curve_gallery). DELIBERATELY NOT `tick`: cantor_set, sierpinski_pyramid, menger_sponge, cube_subdivision and zeno_staircase share once|coarse|fine|dense|limit for a rule reapplied to a SET, and their top rung gestures at an idealised limit object. 8.3 refused the word because its branch is 4-fold and `limit` would be 5,461 tori; this file refuses it for the opposite reason - the branch is 1-fold, a generation here is a single term, and there is no set to rewrite - and both refusals leave the two halves of one lesson answering to the same word. THE INTEGERS ARE THIS FILE'S OWN and differ from 8.3's 1-5, because its floor is 7 and its shipped rung is 6, not 4. recession is folding_past's word with its four values in its order, and it is already in this file's @identity ('concentric squares receding in Z'). ONE THING DIFFERS AND IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE ARTIFACT: folding_past's abreast equalises the terms' SIZE, because there the rule is about time and the nesting is the only claim; here the halving IS the rule, so abreast withdraws the containment and keeps the halving. Equalising the sizes would have changed the rule instead of the claim.
dna.sweep_note: RUN THIS ONE AT --max=20. build_dna_gallery trims the SECOND axis to fit the cap, and 5 x 4 = 20 against the default 9 trims recession to a single value and drops it, leaving a sheet that measures depth alone and says nothing about the axis that carries the argument.
dna.pairs: AT depth=1 THE FOUR recession VALUES ARE ONE PICTURE, and that is the axis reporting itself honestly rather than a duplicate tile. One term has nothing to be inside, in a row with, or on top of; _seat's `along` resolves to 0.0 for the single square and _frame_bounds returns the same initial_size square, so the whole column is identical by construction. From depth 2 upward every value separates. The other pair to read with care: depth 6 -> 7 is the WEAKEST STEP ON THE LADDER by construction and should not be the pair an INERT verdict is read from. The seventh term is 0.015625 across against a frame 1.06 wide - 1.5% of the picture - so it lands as a handful of pixels at dead centre. It is declared anyway because it is the true floor and because the palette has six colours: at depth 7 the index wraps and the innermost square comes back RED, the labels running out before the recursion does. Every other pair on the ladder (1 vs 2, 2 vs 4, 4 vs 6) changes the square count and the colour census outright.
dna.still_note: the EXTENT MOVES ON recession and the camera is placed once on the union, so read the tiles with that in hand. at the shipped depth 6 and frame_thickness 0.03 the frame measures 1.06 x 1.06 for nested and collapsed, 2.03 x 1.06 for abreast and 1.06 x 2.03 for strata - the run being the sum of the terms, 2 x initial_size x (1 - 0.5^n) = 1.96875, which converges on 2.0. So the union is roughly 2.03 square and the nested tile fills about a quarter of it: well clear of the ~6% floor, but not the full-frame subject a single-value capture would have given. collapsed is the thin tile of the four - an unmoved frame with a 0.03 m multicoloured speck at its centre - and that is the value doing its job, not the bench failing. No fixture is needed: grep the file for randf, randi, noise or a clock and there is nothing, _ready ends on set_process(false), and the drawing is finished before the first frame - so a variant here is a fact and not a sample.
dna.declines: size_reduction, initial_size and frame_thickness stay plain numeric exports, now reachable through apply_grid_config but not declared: a denser nest or a bigger picture is a size change, not a different claim. A `coding` axis over the palette (the six-colour rainbow labels each generation, which is exactly what self-similarity says you cannot do) was considered and left for a later pass - it is real and it is cheap, but it argues about the LEGEND and recession argues about the recursion, and only two axes are swept.

dna.default: depth=4, packing=fused - 4 is the number the old max_depth export shipped with, so _draw_circles still starts at (0,0,0) with radius 2.0 and level 4 and lays down the same 85 tori at the same centres; fused SHORT-CIRCUITS rather than recomputing, returning before it touches radius_reduction, so the 0.6 the .tscn writes on the root survives byte for byte (PACKING_R['fused'] is 0.6 and would have written the same number, but a placement that overrode the float alone would then have been silently rescaled). No RNG anywhere in the file - grep for randf/randi/noise returns nothing - so a variant is a fact and not a sample. All 5 placements are the bare token with no config tail, and apply_grid_config, which used to be a bare `pass`, now returns on an empty dict, assigns only on a legal AND different value, and rebuilds only after _ready has built once.
dna.was: five exports and not one categorical among them: max_depth, radius_reduction, rotation_speed, rotation_per_depth and pause_duration - three of those five are RATES, invisible to a still - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so the runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS while the artifact's own declared critical_parameter sat in the source as an int nothing could reach. Every placement got depth 4 at reduction 0.6.
dna.note: hand promotion. depth is the L-system family's word (lsystem_editor, room_grammar, space_filling_curve_gallery) and this file's own - the export was max_depth, the caption already reads 'Depth: %d'. It is NOT `tick`: cantor_set, sierpinski_pyramid and zeno_staircase share tick | once, coarse, fine, dense, limit for a rewrite reapplied to a SET, and their top rung names an idealised limit object you can gesture at. Here the branch is 4-fold, the ring count is (4^d-1)/3 = 1, 5, 21, 85, 341, and `limit` would be 5,461 tori - a capture hazard, not a picture. Taking tick would have meant taking a word without its answers. packing is sierpinski_pyramid's and cantor_set's word and its four values in their order, and the geometry earns it: every child is EXACTLY internally tangent to its parent at any reduction (offset = R(1-r), child radius = rR, so the far edge lands on R), which means the outermost ring is 2.0 across at every rung and the ring count is 4^d at every rung - extent fixed, census fixed, only the claim on the neighbours moving, which is what packing means everywhere else it is used. contact = 0.50 is not a taste: it is the exact reduction at which the two in-plane children become tangent to each other (2*offset = 2*r), and it is also this file's own script default, from before the scene overrode it. ONE THING DIFFERS FROM THE KIN AND IT IS A FACT ABOUT THIS ARTIFACT: the shipped value is `fused`, the TOP rung, one past tangency - sierpinski ships at contact and has a rung above it, this one already ships overlapping, which is exactly where the moire in its own @identity comes from.
dna.pairs: depth=5 x packing=dust is the ONE cell in this sheet that is not a new picture. _draw_circles refuses any radius below 0.01, and at reduction 0.25 the fifth level is 2.0*0.25^4 = 0.0078, so it is culled and depth 5 renders identically to depth 4. Nothing is broken; the recursion has simply run out of visible scale, which is the honest bottom of a self-similar ladder. Every other rung of dust, and every rung of the other three packings, clears the cutoff.
dna.still_note: the tori tumble, so `rotation_speed: 0.0` is declared as a FIXTURE and not as an axis. The outermost ring's rate is rotation_speed*(1 + depth*rotation_per_depth), which means a depth sweep at a fixed settle time would compare five ring-counts at five different tumble PHASES and hand the critic pose difference dressed as axis difference. Frozen, both axes are standing geometry: depth changes the census inside a silhouette that by construction does not move, packing changes whether that census reads as interference, tree or dust.
dna.kin: fractal_recursion_circles is a SECOND registry name on this same scene (res://algorithms/fractals/example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr.tscn, one placement, `fractal_recursion_circles:0:-0.5`). It is deliberately NOT declared: both axes are reachable from it through the identical script, and declaring them twice would sweep one set of pictures under two names, which is the mistake lsystem_editor.preset was kept out of the registry to avoid.

parameters.tick: once | coarse | fine | dense | limit - how many splits the record carries: 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 (default dense)
parameters.walk: population | drill | spread - which cube gets split next (default population)
parameters.build_mode: capture fixture, not an axis: grow (the shipped 0.8 s clock) | instant (the finished record in one frame)
parameters.seed_value: capture fixture, not an axis: 0 keeps the shipped global randi(); any other value seeds the walk

dna.default: tick=dense, walk=population - dense SHORT-CIRCUITS: _levels() hands back the shipped max_subdivisions rather than the table's 12, which matters because cube_subdivision.tscn sets 12 while the @export default is 10, and deriving the rung from the table would silently retune the scene. population returns the shipped picker verbatim - the same global randi() % all_cubes.size() over the same array in the same order, reached through _pick_index, which short-circuits to that identical call whenever seed_value is 0. build_mode stays grow, so the artifact still creates one cube at boot and splits another every subdivision_interval seconds on the same clock. All 10 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Fractals_Necklace, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion curation_station roster and the six Trial_*_fractals plinths) carry the bare token with no config keys, so apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` before this pass - reaches no assignment and never rebuilds.
dna.was: five @export knobs and not one categorical among them: subdivision_interval is a duration, max_subdivisions and fixed_corner_index are counts, auto_start and random_corner are flags - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so not one of them was reachable from a map token. random_corner and fixed_corner_index were worse than unreachable: NOTHING read them. perform_single_subdivision picked randi() % all_cubes.size() unconditionally, so the header's 'Single path recursive ... like diving into one corner repeatedly' and the @identity's declared critical_parameter both described a behaviour the code has never had.
dna.note: tick is cantor_set's, zeno_staircase's and sierpinski_pyramid's word with its five rungs character for character; the INTEGERS behind them are this rule's own, because one tick there is a whole generation and one tick here is a single cube being split. MEASURED, not assumed - the ladder re-run in Python for all three walks: population and spread give 8 / 22 / 43 / 85 / 169 cubes, every rung distinguishable. drill SATURATES ABOVE `fine`: scale falls 0.45x per level, 0.45^7 is under 1 cm of the metre cube, and fine, dense and limit all leave 35 visible cubes and 1.777 of summed face area. The top two rungs of tick exist in code under drill and cannot be photographed - the example_8_4 fault, found here before declaring rather than after. build_mode is cantor_set's fixture word for cantor_set's problem: the shipped artifact grows on a clock, so a still at boot holds ONE cube and the whole of tick is invisible to it.

dna.default: removal=gone - the eleven deleted subcubes are not drawn, which is what this artifact has always done: _step_1_first_subdivision tagged them "remove" and simply never called _create_cube, and the new else-branch calls _spawn_removed_cell, whose first line returns when removal is "gone". Every kept cube, every deform factor (seat *0.15, legs *0.4/*0.4/*2.5, back *2.0/*0.2), the armrests and the five generation colours are untouched. All four placements (Fractal_Recursion, Proto_Fractal_Recursion, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, and the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion curation station) are bare tokens passing no keys, and apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` before this pass - now rebuilds only when a declared word both validates and DIFFERS, and only after _ready has built once.
dna.was: three exports and not one categorical among them: chair_size is a size, step_delay a duration, show_animation a bool the harness could not set (a typed bool rejects a config string before _ready). The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was true of the KIND of knob. Meanwhile the file's own truth line - 'the chair was always inside the cube, subdivision merely removed what was not chair' - was made by an object that never showed a cube.
dna.note: The word is cantor_set's, character for character, from this same registry file: gone/ghost/scar, and the two material recipes are copied value for value (ghost = unshaded alpha 0.16 at Color(0.86,0.88,0.96); scar = matte Color(0.09,0.09,0.11) at 0.22 of the cell) so the siblings LOOK alike answering it. It fits here for the exact reason sierpinski_pyramid refused it: those children's volumes interpenetrate and have no complement to draw, whereas these 27 cells partition one cube, 16 kept and 11 removed, disjoint by construction. build_mode is the FIXTURE, not an axis - the chair assembles one step every 0.5 s, so a still at the harness's 1.1 s settle catches it at step 2, seatless and legless and one frame from step 3; "instant" runs the same five steps in _ready. SIBLING NOT TOUCHED: recursive_table is a separate script and a separate scene (not a shared generator), and the same word fits it exactly - its own truth line is 'a table is a cube that kept its top layer and four corners, everything else was excess', and its 3x3x2 lattice removes 5 of 18 cells the same way. It is assigned elsewhere in this batch, so it was left alone rather than edited under two hands.

recursive_table.description: table = subdivide_3x2(cube) -> keep(top_layer, corner_legs) -> flatten(top) -> stretch(legs)

dna.default: keep=corners, assembly=full - corners returns the shipped test character for character: _is_leg_cell falls past every match case to `return (x == 0 or x == 2) and (z == 0 or z == 2)`, the four corner cells of the bottom layer and nothing else. The apron SHORT-CIRCUITS with it: leg_inset stays the shipped literal table_size * 0.35 rather than being derived, because the corner legs actually stand at table_size / 3 and deriving would move the apron of the three existing placements by 0.017 * table_size. full is the only assembly this artifact could ever build - all three gate helpers return true, so _build_instant and _execute_step run steps 0-4 in the identical order over the identical geometry. All 3 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, Proto_Fractal_Recursion, plus the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion curation_station list) are BARE tokens - the ':0:-0.5:0.2' suffix is rotation and offsets, not config keys - and both axes are read only inside `if config.has(...)`, so none of them reaches the new code.
dna.was: three @export knobs and not one categorical among them: table_size is a scale, show_animation a flag, step_delay a duration - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so not one of them was reachable from a map token, which is why the stage-2 runner refused this for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The essence line is literally `keep(top_layer, corner_legs)` and the critical_parameter is named as 'the top-layer vs bottom-layer role split', yet that split was four hard-coded corner tests buried in _step_1 - the one choice the artifact declares as its own subject was the one thing no placement could vary. The four steps then ran unconditionally, so the truth line ('everything else was excess') could only be shown as its finished result, with the excess never on view.
dna.shared_with: cube_staircase - `assembly` is that artifact's word, promoted the same week one folder over in the same subdivision family, with its terminal value `full`. The same question (how much of the built object is standing, in cumulative rungs) asked of this object's own parts. The rung NAMES are necessarily this table's, exactly as cube_staircase's treads/steps/stringers are its own; a shared vocabulary that forced a table to have treads would be the folding_past mistake. `keep` is this artifact's own word, taken from its own essence line rather than invented, and deliberately NOT `selection` - that word is already the evolution family's (drift|uniform|culled|runaway|split, four artifacts) and means natural selection.
dna.note: The fixture is load-bearing for the evidence, not decoration. show_animation defaults to true and recursive_table.tscn sets step_delay = 0.5, so the four build steps land at 0.5s, 1.0s, 1.5s and 2.0s - while capture_config_sweep's SETTLE is 1.1s. Swept as shipped, every variant would be photographed half-built at the slab stage, `legs` and `full` would be pixel-identical, and the axis would read INERT as a fact about the capture clock. Setting the flag false takes the instant path, so each frame shows the rung it names. It is a real JSON boolean, not the string "true" that a typed bool export rejects before _ready.

recursive_table.name: recursive_table

dna.fixture_note: MANDATORY for the sweep, and NOT an axis. show_construction ships true, so the staircase assembles itself one part every step_delay (0.3 s) and takes ~2.4 s at the shipped six steps. capture_config_sweep settles 1.1 s before the shot and only 0.35 s before the AABB pre-pass, so an unpinned sweep would photograph half-built stairs and place its one fixed camera on a single tread. false takes the _build_instant() branch that already existed for exactly this case. Capture bench only - no placement passes this key.
dna.default: assembly=full, step_count=6 - full is the only assembly the artifact could ever build: all three gate helpers return true for it, so _build_instant/_execute_build run the identical steps-then-sides-then-handrail sequence over the identical geometry, and 6 is the shipped export untouched. All 3 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Corridor_Fractal_Recursion, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, plus the Curation_Bay_fractals_0 / Proto_Fractal_Recursion copies) are BARE tokens with no #key:value, and apply_grid_config now returns on the first line for an empty config, so none of them reaches the new code at all.
dna.was: stair_size, step_count, show_construction and step_delay were all @export, and apply_grid_config() was `pass` - the knobs existed in the inspector and no map token could turn one. The three build phases ran unconditionally, so the @identity's claim that 'handrails and stringers arise as structural necessity from the step geometry' was a sentence no room could test, and the truth line 'a staircase is a cube that learned to subdivide itself along its own diagonal' shipped at exactly one granularity.
dna.note: assembly is cumulative, not exclusive: treads is the bare result of the diagonal cut (n slabs, nothing holding them), steps closes each slice with its riser, stringers adds the two side walls that make it an object rather than a diagram, full adds the rail, posts and balusters. It bites in the silhouette - the handrail is the tallest thing in the frame and the stringers are the widest, so removing them moves the outline, not a detail. step_count is the artifact's own critical_parameter and its argument, x4 either side of the shipped six: 1 is a single block (a stair with no stair in it), 3 coarse, 6 shipped, 12 fine, 24 where the tread is thinner than the rail and the diagonal reads as a ramp again - the discretisation never becoming the thing it approximates. The two are orthogonal: every assembly value reads at every count. dna.default: evidence=result, habit=planar - a deliberate no-op on both axes. result draws only the last generation, which is the single string the shipped rewrite loop left in _current_string; planar sets the roll to exactly 0.0 and the roll is then skipped by an `if roll_rad != 0.0` rather than applied as a zero rotation, so the turtle runs the shipped instruction sequence and no float is touched. dna.was: six exports and every one a dial: iterations, base_angle, base_length, display_size and two colours. The rule itself, F->F[+F]F[-F]F, was a hard-coded _rules dictionary; the turtle only ever rotated about dir.cross(right), so the classic plant was a flat drawing; and every generation but the last was computed and thrown away inside the rewrite loop. apply_grid_config called _generate() unconditionally, so any unrelated key on a map token re-ran the whole rewrite - and two placements do pass unrelated layout keys.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03, refused by the runner for NO TURNABLE KNOBS: the exports were there but every one was a scalar dial, nothing the artifact argues. evidence lifts the derivation the code already computes and discards - trace nests the earlier generations inside the finished plant at one origin, longhand lays generation 1..N side by side at one scale, axiom draws ONE application of the production, the rule as a picture instead of its limit. Generation 0 is never selected by any value: a single bare segment carries no picture, and after the bounds-fit it would be a hairline filling the frame. habit lifts the roll the turtle never had - 0 / 30 / 90 / 137.5 degrees applied to the branching plane at each push, planar being the shipped flat drawing and spiral the golden angle.

The axis, its allow-list, the five builders and the guarded apply_grid_config were already in commons/artifacts/jelly_cube/jelly_cube.gd (committed d3b41fbab) and the registry had never been told, so check_dna_declarations listed jelly_cube under 'promoted in code, undeclared in the registry' and the sweep could not reach any of it. What this pass added is the declaration and nothing else - not one line of the artifact was touched, because the code was already right: apply_grid_config returns unless the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already standing AND is_node_ready(), and _read_dna_meta lets a token's word be built once in _ready instead of built and torn down a frame later.

The kit is re-dimensioned by a single factor u = cube_size / 0.5 so the family's proportions, accents and captions survive at this artifact's smaller scale; `control` is the rung that argues hardest, because an empty wire cage at the size the cube had BEFORE anything happened to it turns a thing you are watching into a difference you could disagree with.
dna.still_note: THE JIGGLE IS NOT AN AXIS AND CANNOT BE, and this is why the apparatus carries the claim instead. Everything jelly_cube exposes - stiffness, damping, pressure, mass - is a STARTING CONDITION on a body that relaxes, so five cubes started five ways settle into the same shape and photograph as one object five times; cloth_straps hit exactly this and took `suspension` for the same reason. Every assay rung is standing geometry: a graduated column, a wire reference cage, a plotted board, a glass case. The chart's settling trace is CLOSED FORM (exp(-3.4f)cos(13f)) and not sampled from the running solver, because a plot that came out different every launch would be noise wearing the costume of a record.
dna.framing_note: unchecked against a capture in this pass. The subject is a 0.3 m cube on a 0.42 m plinth, and _create_vr_controls already hangs a rack panel at z = 0.36 tilted -30 degrees; `chart` adds a board behind at -0.31 and `control` a second plate 0.35 m to the right, so the union-of-variants camera is pulled well back from the jelly itself. animation.driven_by: Jolt gravity, collisions and pinned vertices

dna.argues: Four identical SoftBody3D spheres fall from drop_height onto whatever is beneath them, and what is beneath them is nothing this artifact owns. `landing` gives each cell of the 2x2 grid a surface to negotiate with, so the four resting crumples differ because the MATERIAL met a different shape, not because a clock read differently. That is the softbodies truth line at its most literal: form is not imposed, it is what is left after a falling body and a rigid obstruction finish arguing. The @identity calls the four bodies 'one event, sampled four times'; this keeps that reading and changes what the event is falling INTO, which is the only part of it a photograph can hold.
dna.still_note: floor: a squashed ball, wide contact patch - the shipped picture. pan: the sphere is pinched between two tray walls 0.70 m apart and rises, taller than wide, with two flat vertical facets; the only value where the body ends up TALLER than it started. rail: a saddle, two lobes hanging either side of a 1.6 m bar with a crease along the top. cone: a tent, the lowest point pushed up into the body's own volume, dimpling the pressure-inflated shell. Four silhouettes that differ in ASPECT RATIO, not in arrival time. Each one is where the body stops, and each stays there - which is the whole requirement in a sequence made of motion: a stiffer cloth HANGS differently and that is a still, a cloth that reaches the same drape twice as fast is invisible.
dna.default: landing=floor. _build_landing() returns before constructing anything, so the child order stays exactly SoftBody_1..4 (each the instanced softbodybody.tscn) then StopTimer_1..4, and _build_bench_floor() returns on the same kind of guard. TWELVE appearances, none of them reached. FIVE bare grid tokens - SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics, _p1, _p2, _p3 and Corridor_SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics - with no rotation, no offset and no #key, so merged_config is empty and GridInteractablesComponent never calls apply_grid_config on them at all. SIX exhibit_furniture#kind:platform#size:l#mount:softstopscene slots (Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies), and exhibit_furniture._mount_artifact() instantiates the scene and add_child()s it with NO config call whatsoever - read, not assumed. ONE curation_station roster (Curation_Bay_softbodies_2, artifacts:gridagent,softmill,softstopscene), and curation_station calls inst.apply_grid_config({"emissive": false}) on everything it curates - a key this artifact does not read, so the signature is unchanged and it returns before touching the tree. The three fixture exports are no-ops at default too: drop_height 3.0 IS the literal 3 that used to be written in the positions array and 3.0 is exactly representable; bench_floor_y -1000.0 fails the `> -999.0` guard so no plane is built; body_damping -1.0 fails the `>= 0.0` guard so damping_coefficient is never written and each body keeps softbody3d.gd's own 0.01. This token lives in physics_simulation.json ONLY - no second registry to mirror.
dna.was: Four spheres released at y=3 over whatever the room happened to put under them, and four Timers that freeze them at 7.5 / 11 / 12 / 12 seconds. The artifact's argument was entirely in the CLOCK: the landing surface was never part of the composition, so the four crumples differed only in how long each body had been falling.
dna.note: NEW word. Not `bed` and not `ground` - both taken, and both are about what a thing is displayed ON, not what deforms it. Not `assay`, which four artifacts in this sequence already hold (jelly_cube, softmill, revolving_joy_ride, softbody_gallery_part2): assay is the apparatus word, and this builds no gauge, no chart, no vitrine and no wire cage, and adds nothing the player reads a number off. Not `repose` or `settling` (taken elsewhere, and both name the PROCESS this axis refuses to be about). The four values are load-bearing collision geometry and nothing else: one shared grey material across all of them on purpose, so the critic cannot score a paint job.
dna.declined: `stop_times` ([7.5, 11.0, 12.0, 12.0]) - this artifact's own declared critical_parameter, the most seductive axis in the wave because the ladder is already written and looks like a promoted family waiting to be declared. Refused on three counts. (1) It is a set of CLOCK READINGS: capture_config_sweep fires at ~1.45 s and the earliest freeze is 7.5 s, so at the shutter not ONE of the four has fired; a sweep of it today publishes four tiles of four bodies at the same moment of the same fall. (2) Compressed into the window by a fixture it would photograph four TRANSIENTS, each frozen by a Timer whose timeout lands on whichever physics tick the frame rate happened to produce - two runs would freeze two different crumples and the bite number would be a fact about the frame clock. (3) Recorded, not fixed here: two of the four shipped values are IDENTICAL (12.0, 12.0), so the four-stop demo already collapses two of its four samples into one, which is exactly what its own @identity warns against ('set them equal and difference collapses into repetition'). Also declined: `spacing` (composition, not material) and `show_timers` (a UI toggle, and ui_labels is never populated so it currently toggles nothing).
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED ON THE BENCH THE ARTIFACT IS NOT IN FRAME AT ALL, and that is the most important thing this promotion found. capture_config_sweep._stage_default builds two DirectionalLight3Ds and a Camera3D and nothing else; the showcase profile's ground is a MeshInstance3D with no collider (_stage_showcase, ShowGround); dna.host builds a MultiMeshInstance3D with no collider (_build_host). There is NO physics floor anywhere on the bench. The four SoftBody3D spheres are released at y=3 and fall forever - the union-AABB pre-pass measures a SEPARATE probe instance at 0.35 s (about 0.6 m down) and frees it, and the photographed instance is a fresh one that lives about 1.2 s before the shutter (SETTLE 1.1 + two process frames + 0.1), roughly 7 m down, so every tile of any softbodies sweep run today is empty sky and would be reported INERT: a verdict about the harness, in the exact shape the corpus has been wrong five times out of seven. bench_floor_y 0.0 builds a StaticBody3D plane on collision_layer 1 - the layer softbody3d.gd._setup_physics sets and masks - which is the fixture supplying what a map supplies, and is what dna.fixture is for. TRAP, and it decides the number 1.35: softbody3d.gd._setup_physics contains `if global_position.y < 1.0: global_position.y = 2.0`, so ANY drop_height below 1.0 is silently overridden to 2.0 and the fixture would appear to have been ignored. 1.35 clears it with 0.35 m to spare. spacing 2.0 (from the shipped 3.0) tightens the 2x2 grid so four cells fit one frame at a distance where each body is still legible. body_damping 0.45 against softbody3d.gd's own 0.01 is what buys a SETTLED pose inside the capture window instead of a transient - see determinism.
dna.harness_note: SECOND HARNESS FACT, fixed by the same fixture and worth stating separately because it would survive a floor. Godot's SoftBody3D goes TOP-LEVEL with an identity transform on its first transform notification (it pushes the global transform to the physics server and simulates vertices in world space), so all four bodies report the same static 1 m SphereMesh AABB at the origin no matter where they actually are. _subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D - which SoftBody3D is - so the union box would be one 1 m cube at the origin and the camera would frame one cell of four. The bench floor slab is sized to spacing + 2.2 for exactly this reason: it is the only node in the subtree whose AABB tracks the 2x2 layout, so it doubles as the framing anchor and no separate layers=0 anchor is needed. The conclusion does not depend on which way the engine goes here: if Godot DOES republish a soft body's AABB in world space as it deforms, the 4.2 m slab still dominates the union and still frames all four cells - the slab makes the framing indifferent to the fall, which is also why the camera lands identically for all four variants. It is built ONLY under the fixture guard, so no map placement gains a node. Two wall-clock reads exist in softbody3d.gd (_apply_idle_behavior nudges target_color by sin/cos of Time.get_unix_time_from_system) and they are visually INERT: that colour system is self-declared 'simplified, no material dependency', nothing ever writes current_color to a material, and the bodies render through the pinktartan ShaderMaterial override. dna.default: generator=simplex, accretion=summed - both exact no-ops, and the no-op is a SHORT-CIRCUIT rather than a formula that lands near the shipped value. _noise_type_for("simplex") returns FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX, the identical enum constant setup_noise assigned unconditionally at :63; _fractal_type_for("summed") returns FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_FBM, the identical constant from :66. Nothing else in setup_noise moved - the seven property assignments run in the same order with the same arguments, and cellular_return_type is touched on the cellular rung ONLY, so at every other value that property stays at the engine default it has always had. REACH MEASURED BY READING THE MAPS, not estimated: SIX mentions in six map files by three paths, where the promotion brief carried three. Bare tokens - `voxel_noise_demo` in ISO_Introduction (interactables row 84) and Corridor_ISO_Introduction (row 76), and `marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo` in ProceduralGenerationMarchingCubesVovelNoise (row 97). Two curation_station rosters - Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_1 and Curation_Bay_proceduralgeneration_all_9, where the token is an entry in the station's `#artifacts:` list. And one transformation swap, `voxel_noise_demo->animated_noise_explorer` in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces, which is a target NAME and not a config at all. Not one of the six names an axis key. Neither registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is EMPTY at the three bare cells and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate at :1194 means _apply_artifact_config is never called - no metadata is stamped and apply_grid_config is never reached. The two rosters do not reach it either, and for a different reason worth recording: curation_station.gd:381 tests `inst.has_method("apply_grid_config")` on the ROOT of the instantiated scene, and this scene's root carries no script, so its `{"emissive": false}` call is skipped entirely. Even if it landed, that key is in no signature and the guard would return. Zero of six rebuild, and all six render the field they have always rendered.
dna.was: Seventeen @exports - the richest export surface in the sequence - and not one of them said what the field is MADE of. generate_density_field is four lines of arithmetic: sample noise.get_noise_3d at the corner (:125), map it to (noise + 1) * 0.5 (:128), store. No shape term, no gradient, no bias, no second layer. So the picture is a level set of one FastNoiseLite object and nothing else - the sequence's purest case of a surface that is only a threshold on a field - and the two lines deciding what that object IS sat three apart as bare constants, TYPE_SIMPLEX at :63 and FRACTAL_FBM at :66, reachable from no map, no token and no inspector. apply_grid_config was the single word `pass` at :407: a config channel wired to nothing, so even the sixteen knobs that WERE exported could not be set by a placement.
dna.note: generator is SHARED, and the sharing is the whole point. FIVE artifacts already carry it with the same four values in the same order and the same default - perlin_noise (promoted 2026-07-29), noise_terrain (08-03), noise_space and shader_noise_space (08-05), alongside simplex_noise in the same bench family - and every one of their notes says the same sentence: the noise sequence is built on comparing bases, so if each artifact spells the comparison its own way there is nothing to compare. cellular, not worley, for the same reason. THE APPROVED DESIGN FOR THIS PASS PROPOSED A NEW WORD, `basis`, with five rungs (value|perlin|simplex|smooth|cells), and it was refused. A census of all 996 declared axes across the registry turned up `generator` on four tokens carrying exactly this value list; a sixth spelling of one question is precisely the fault those five notes were written to prevent. So: same word, same four rungs, same order, same default, `cells` spelled `cellular`, and `smooth` declined (see declined). What this member adds to the family is the READING and not the vocabulary - the other five displace a height or tint a wall with the basis, and this one level-sets it. Five artifacts asking one question and one of them asking it of a boundary instead of a surface is a comparison worth having; a sixth private word would have been six unrelated facts. ONE DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE, stated rather than glossed. The cellular rung here also sets cellular_return_type = RETURN_CELL_VALUE, which the other five do not. FastNoiseLite's default is RETURN_DISTANCE, distance-to-nearest-feature, whose one-point distribution is strongly one-sided. This file's iso_level is fixed at 0.5 and :128 maps noise to (n + 1) * 0.5, so 0.5 cuts the field exactly at its own mean - a threshold chosen for a zero-mean basis. Against a one-sided field that threshold stops being a mean, and the rung would mostly move HOW MUCH of the box is solid rather than what its boundary is made of. RETURN_CELL_VALUE is a constant per Voronoi cell with mean zero, so the cut stays at the mean and the answer is a surface with no curvature anywhere in the frame: flat plates meeting at cell walls. This is the same move shader_noise_space recorded when it amplitude-matched its four bases with three scaling constants so its axis would measure structure and not exposure. TerrainGenerator.gd:90 in this same repo already pairs TYPE_CELLULAR with RETURN_CELL_VALUE. accretion is NEW - zero uses among those 996 - and the adjacency is named rather than left for the critic. `octaves` is taken SEVEN times (mc_cave and mc_inside_cave in this sequence, plus noise_space, noise_quarry, simplex_noise, marchingcubes_cave, marchingcubes_inside_cave) and it counts HOW MANY scales survive. accretion is the RULE by which they are combined, and the count is held at this scene's shipped noise_octaves = 4 on every rung - deliberately untouched, though it is one of the seventeen exports - so the two questions cannot overlap. summed = FRACTAL_FBM SHIPPED. single = FRACTAL_NONE, one octave, the frame that shows what the other three rungs are adding. ridged = FRACTAL_RIDGED, which rectifies each octave to 1 - |n|; against simplex's mean |n| of about 0.35 that puts the field's mean near +0.3 instead of 0, so the cut at 0.5 leaves a sparser solid and the extracted surface grows blades and fins instead of lobes. pingpong = FRACTAL_PING_PONG at the engine's default fractal_ping_pong_strength of 2.0, folding the range repeatedly into banded shells and likewise skewing the mean positive. THE ARITHMETIC OF THE PICTURE, written down so a small number can be told from a dead axis. frequency is the .tscn's noise_scale 0.05, so the base wavelength is 20 world units across a 32-unit chunk: 1.6 periods per axis, i.e. the frame is dominated by one octave's worth of blob about 10 units across. Sampling is 32 points over 32 units, spacing 1.032, so the fourth octave at wavelength 2.5 is resolved at only 2.4 samples per period - right at Nyquist, and contributing at a gain of 0.125. That is why accretion is expected to be the quieter of the two axes, and it is a second reason the octave count was left alone. AND THE CAVEAT THE WHOLE FAMILY SHARES, which none of the five siblings has written down: at a fixed seed, changing noise_type does not perturb one field, it draws a different one. simplex and perlin at seed 1337 are two unrelated realisations, not two renderings of one landscape. A large bite on `generator` is therefore close to guaranteed whatever the design, and the thing to read is not the mean but the CHARACTER - whether value shows the axis-aligned creases of a cubic lattice, whether cellular shows flat plates. That is true of all five siblings equally, which is exactly what makes them comparable; it is a property of the axis and not a defect in it.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, noise_terrain, noise_space, shader_noise_space - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order and the same default. This is the sixth member and the first to level-set the field rather than displace a height or tint a wall with it, which is the reason to keep the word rather than coin one: if a shared vocabulary is honest, the odd member out is the interesting measurement. The single documented departure is cellular_return_type on the cellular rung, argued in `note`. `octaves`, which four of those five also carry, is NOT taken here - accretion asks a different question and the octave count is pinned so the two cannot be confused.
dna.declined: `smooth` (TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH), REFUSED, and it is the refusal that cost something. The approved design asked for it as a fifth rung and predicted it would be the weakest, closest to simplex at about 4% - 'only just over the bite floor'. It is dropped because the four-value list is a comparison instrument held in common by five artifacts, three of whose notes assert 'the same four values in the same order'; a fifth rung on one member makes that member's mean incomparable with the other four, and what it buys is the rung already predicted to be faintest. If the sweep later wants the simplex-versus-simplex-smooth distinction, it belongs to the whole family at once and not to this member alone. `basis`, REFUSED as a name - see note. num_points_per_axis (32) - the sampling resolution, and `resolution` is already this sequence's family word, held by animated_noise_explorer and by queer_marching_cave. Not taking it a third time. noise_scale (0.05) - the biggest knob by visual effect and the one this promotion was most tempted by. Refused because against a fixed 32-point lattice over a 32-unit chunk it is arithmetically the SAME ratio: chunk_size x noise_scale = 1.6 periods across the box, so halving the frequency is indistinguishable from doubling the lattice spacing. Sweeping it re-argues resolution from the other side. iso_level (0.5) - `threshold`, taken by mc_torus_sculpture. Recorded in the prose instead, because :128 maps the noise to (n + 1) * 0.5 and so 0.5 cuts the field exactly at its own mean, which is why the shipped picture is a balanced sponge with roughly equal solid and void - and why the cellular rung had to be mean-matched. noise_persistence (0.5) and noise_lacunarity (2.0) - genuine spectral properties, but both are octave-weighting parameters and would argue with accretion for the same pixels. noise_octaves (4) - `octaves`, taken seven times, and held fixed here precisely so accretion is not measured against it. glass_color, outline_color, outline_width, use_shader, generate_colliders, chunk_size - material, chrome and size. voxel_scale - exported since the file was written and read by nothing in the build path; a dead knob, not an axis, and deliberately kept out of the rebuild signature for that reason.
dna.fixture_why: THE ONE ARTIFACT OF THIS WAVE THAT WAS ALREADY SEEDED CORRECTLY, so this is a pin and not a repair. noise_seed is a real @export defaulting to 1337, the .tscn sets 1337, and setup_noise assigns noise.seed = noise_seed BEFORE generate_density_field takes its first sample. The file contains no randf, no randi and no RandomNumberGenerator in 408 lines and builds exactly one FastNoiseLite. The pin exists only so the value STAYS pinned if a map or a future bench ever passes one - without it, a seeded run and an unseeded run of `generator` would be indistinguishable in the manifest, which is the queer_marching_cave audit failure in the other direction. Written as a bare JSON number, never the string "1337", because capture_config_sweep assigns fixture values straight onto the typed int export before _ready and a typed int rejects a String. NOT PINNED and deliberately: generate_colliders stays true, its shipped value. Collision is invisible in a still, but a ConcavePolygonShape3D built in C++ from an already-computed vertex array is cheap, and pinning it false would photograph a configuration no placement uses.
dna.framing_why: Explicit at the default because it was CHECKED rather than assumed: the sibling entry's own measurements block records aabb_size 32.0 x 32.0 x 32.0 with aabb_center at the origin, which is the chunk exactly. The subject is a cube-shaped, close to isotropic volume, so the fit-by-diagonal that letterboxes flat and thin subjects is honest here and no layers = 0 anchor is needed. THE ONE THING TO WATCH, because it is an inference and not a measurement: the density field is defined everywhere in the box at every rung, so every rung SHOULD reach every face - but ridged and pingpong push the field's mean positive and could in principle pull the surface in from the faces, which an AABB-fitted camera answers by zooming, turning a change of extent into a change of apparent scale. If the sweep shows two rungs framed at visibly different magnifications, that is the cause, and the fix is an anchor mesh rather than a smaller framing number.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was the single word `pass` at :407. It now reads the two axes against their allow-lists (an unrecognised value is DROPPED, not applied - the science_screen failure was a typo nothing in the chain refused) and rebuilds only when a signature of every value the build reads has actually moved. The signature is not a hand-listed tuple of the two axes: _signature() strings every export generate_world consumes, so the guard cannot drift out of step with the build. voxel_scale is deliberately absent from it - the export exists and nothing reads it, so including it would let a dead knob pay for a 29,791-cube re-march. The channel stays narrow on purpose: the two axes are the only keys READ, so a token naming noise_scale or iso_level still changes nothing, because widening the channel to honour keys nobody has ever sent would be a behaviour change hiding inside a promotion. ORDERING READ OFF THE CALL SITE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. GridInteractablesComponent stamps config_* metadata at :1656-1666 and calls add_child at :1220, so metadata always lands BEFORE _ready; _ready reads it through _read_dna_metadata and builds ONCE with the right values, records the signature, and the deferred apply_grid_config that follows finds the signature unchanged and returns. A `_built` flag guards the reverse order: config arriving before the first build assigns and returns, because _ready will read the new values on its way through. THE SCRIPTLESS ROOT IS NOT A FAULT AND WAS NOT 'FIXED'. The promotion brief called it a BLOCKING STRUCTURAL FAULT - voxel_noise_demo.tscn's root is a bare Node3D and VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd sits on a child - and it asked for the script to be moved up. The engine was read instead of the brief, and the brief is stale. GridInteractablesComponent._apply_artifact_config falls through at :1695 to _config_holder, a breadth-first search for the first descendant that handles config, which finds the child, stamps the metadata there and calls apply_grid_config on it, all before add_child; capture_config_sweep._holder_of does the same per key for the bench; and check_dna_declarations.unreachable_roots classifies this shape as CHILD-ONLY, informational, explicitly not a fault, since e0bc97b3b. Moving the script would have been a change with a real cost and no benefit - the ROOT is where GridInteractablesComponent attaches its _RotationTimer, and this script's _exit_tree used to blanket-free every ownerless child, so the move would have newly put that timer inside the blast radius. The script therefore stayed put and the free was narrowed instead: an `_owned` array holds the two nodes this script creates (the VoxelWorld mesh and the VoxelWorldCollision body) and nothing else is ever touched, which is identical in effect today and stops being identical the moment anything attaches a helper here. clear_world also now DETACHES before queue_free, because queue_free is deferred and a rebuild adds a second node named VoxelWorld in the same frame, which Godot would silently rename to VoxelWorld2.
dna.still_note: A still is a complete account, and this is one of the few artifacts in the sequence where that needs no qualification. There is no _process, no timer, no await and no call_deferred anywhere in the file; _ready runs setup_noise, setup_marching_cubes_tables and generate_world synchronously and the mesh is finished when it returns. Both axes are resolved inside setup_noise before the first of 32,768 samples is taken and neither is re-read afterwards. Determinism is real rather than asserted: one FastNoiseLite, seeded from an export before first use, and no other source of randomness in the file. Four runs of the same rung are the same mesh. BUDGET, checked because the failure mode is a watchdog kill and not a bad picture: 32^3 = 32,768 noise samples and 31^3 = 29,791 marched cubes per tile, all in GDScript, with an Array-of-Triangle-objects intermediate. The registry's own compute field calls this artifact HEAVY. On a 16-tile sweep that is the number to watch against the 16-second stall rule, not the bite.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE THE CAPTURE, and one of the two predictions deliberately DISAGREES with the approved design so the sweep can settle it - a prediction that agrees with the sweep is worth nothing. generator, closest pair: perlin x value, predicted ~30-35% of frame, i.e. nowhere near the bite floor, and the honest reading of that is that 'closest' barely means anything on this axis. Arithmetic: perlin and value sample the SAME cubic lattice at the same spacing (1 / 0.05 = 20 world units, 1.6 cells across the 32-unit chunk) and both are zero-mean, so both produce a sponge of the same characteristic blob size and roughly the same 50% solid fraction. They differ in placement, not in scale, and a pixel metric reads placement as large. cellular should be the loudest and the most obviously different - flat plates, no curvature. The part of this I am least sure of is whether `value` shows its axis-aligned creases at only 1.6 lattice cells per axis; if it does not, the value rung will read as one more unrelated sponge. accretion, closest pair: ridged x pingpong, predicted ~12% of frame. THE APPROVED DESIGN PREDICTED summed x pingpong AT ~8% AND THIS PASS DISAGREES WITH IT. Arithmetic: ridged and pingpong both rectify or fold each octave into a one-sided shape, so both fields carry a mean around +0.3 to +0.5 against summed's 0.0; after density = (n + 1) * 0.5 and the cut at 0.5, both leave a sparse thin-walled solid of roughly a quarter to a third of the volume, while summed and single both leave a balanced sponge at about a half. If the family splits that way, the design's pair is wrong and the axis is really asking 'is the octave rectified'. If summed x pingpong really is the closest, the folding is being re-sorted back into a balanced sponge by the threshold and the axis is asking 'how many scales', which would put it too close to `octaves` to keep - so this pair decides whether accretion earns its own word. Largest pair, both predictions agreeing: single x ridged. THE DEGENERACY RISK WORTH NAMING: if ridged or pingpong pushes the mean far enough that almost every corner lands on one side of 0.5, march_cube skips the cube as 'completely inside or outside' (:205) and the tile comes back near-empty - which reads exactly like an inert axis. Read the per-tile triangle count that generate_world prints at :106 BEFORE reading the bite number.
dna.kin: SIBLING DECLARATION. voxel_noise_demo (isosurfaces.json) and marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo (randomness.json) are two registry names on ONE scene, voxel_noise_demo.tscn - another of the one-scene-many-names families this corpus keeps turning up. The axes, the values, the fixture, the framing and this entire block are copied character for character between the two entries. They MUST measure alike; if they do not, the difference is in the bench and not in the artifact. Worth noting that the second entry lives in randomness.json rather than an isosurfaces file and its own map_sequences already claims both isosurfaces and proceduralgeneration_all - so the `generator` family it now joins, which is a randomness family, is the family it was already filed with.
