dna.default: workings=expression, margin=even - both are short-circuits, not recomputations that happen to land on the same numbers. expression IS the file's existing code path: show_wireframes and show_labels both shipped `true`, so the branch runs the same generate_case_mesh() and create_labels() bodies in the same order, adds no node the file did not already add, and the crossing markers exist only under `trace`. even is a bare `return case_data.densities` in _densities_for() and a bare `return SHIPPED_OUTSIDE` (0.3) in _outside_value() - the very literal arrays the fifteen dictionary entries have always carried, and the very number create_voxel_chunk_from_case has always filled the chunk with - so every case builds a byte-identical density field and the same ArrayMesh. TWELVE PLACEMENTS ACROSS ELEVEN MAPS, reaching the artifact by four different paths, every one bit-identical. (1) TWO BARE TOKENS, Corridor_ISO_LookupTable and Trial_physarum_isosurfaces: the naked string with no rotation, no y-offset and no config keys. This entry declares no default_params, so GridInteractablesComponent builds merged_config from default_params + delegate params + token params and gets an EMPTY dictionary; the `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate means _apply_artifact_config is never called at all, no metadata is stamped, and apply_grid_config is never reached. (2) ONE ROTATION-ONLY token, `fifteen_cases_demo:90` in ISO_LookupTable: the `:90` is parsed into overrides.rotation_y, never into config_data, so it takes that same empty-config path. (3) EIGHT exhibit_furniture mounts, `#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:fifteen_cases_demo`, across Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / physarum / pinch_v2 / sainsbury / soane_cabinet_vista / uffizi - the # keys belong to the FURNITURE, not to this token, and exhibit_furniture._mount_artifact loads the scene, instantiates it, positions it at _surface_y() and adds the child without ever calling apply_grid_config or stamping identity, so those build at pure export defaults. (4) ONE curation_station roster, Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_0, which DOES call apply_grid_config - with exactly {"emissive": false}, a key no build path reads - so the new guarded body stamps config_emissive into metadata, recomputes the signature, finds it unchanged and returns before any teardown. (Trial_physarum_isosurfaces carries the token twice, once bare and once mounted, which is why twelve cells sit in eleven files.)
dna.was: a 3 x 5 grid of fifteen frozen marching-cubes cells, and a bare `pass` where apply_grid_config should be - line 431, no assignment behind it, so the artifact was unreachable from a map token by any key whatsoever. The two knobs it did expose were show_wireframes and show_labels, both true, both reachable only through a keyboard shortcut in a demo whose UI Control ships visible = false; and show_wireframes did not even do what the W key printed, because the wireframe nodes were never tracked, so toggling it changed nothing at all until a regenerate. Meanwhile the 0.3 / 0.7 sample pair - the numbers that decide where every extracted vertex lands - was typed out thirty times across the fifteen dictionary literals and a thirty-first time into the chunk fill, with nothing naming it, nothing connecting the two, and no way to ask what the picture would look like if it were any other pair.
dna.note: workings is SHARED, taken from csg_difference_demo (boolean_surfaces.json), whose note says 'workings is the axis a demonstration wants and an artwork does not: how much of the operation it is willing to show.' 26 tokens carried the word before this promotion. It transplants here because this is the same kind of object asked the same question - a demonstration, not a work - and because all four of its rungs are answerable in full, which is the test implicit_surface_modeling applied when it REFUSED sierpinski_pyramid's `packing`. What the four mean for a lookup table: expression is SHIPPED - the sheets, the fifteen wireframe cages, the 120 red/blue corner beads and the fifteen billboard labels each ending 'Config: %d', which is the table entry itself; outcome is the fifteen sheets ALONE, finished geometry with no account of where it came from and no configuration number; operands is cage and beads with NO sheet - the field before the decision, which is exactly and only what marching cubes consumes, and an inverse silhouette of outcome; trace is expression plus a marker on every one of the twelve cage edges whose two ends disagree, standing at the interpolated crossing, computed with the generator's own formula so the mark is WHERE the extracted vertex is rather than near it. WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE SIBLING, said plainly: over there the operands are two solids and `trace` is the removed material put back as a ghost, so its ladder is about a volume; here the operand is eight numbers and trace is a set of POINTS, so the ladder is about a sampling. Same question, two ontologies of showing. margin is a NEW word, and it is the sequence's truth line - 'define a field, extract a surface' - turned into a knob. The demo hardcodes 0.3 for outside and 0.7 for inside against MarchingCubesGenerator's threshold of 0.5. That pair is SYMMETRIC about the threshold, so every interpolated vertex lands on the exact edge midpoint: the diagram-book picture, and an accident of two literals rather than a property of the algorithm. Slide the pair while keeping its span at 0.4 and the fifteen cases stay the same fifteen cases - same config bytes, same table entries, same topology, the same eight beads in the same eight colours in the same eight places - while every sheet slides across its cell. The table decides what the surface IS; the numbers decide where it SITS; and only one of those is in the lookup table. Values are (outside, inside) pairs and t is measured from the inside corner: even (0.30, 0.70) t=0.50 SHIPPED; starved (0.14, 0.54) t=0.10, the inside corners barely made it and the sheets hug them until the solid is slivers; swollen (0.44, 0.84) t=0.85, the sheets stand off toward the outside corners and the solid nearly fills its cell; brimming (0.48, 0.88) t=0.95, the limit case. BOTH numbers of every pair stay strictly off 0.50 on purpose: march_cube_fixed's sign test is `density < threshold`, so an outside value of exactly 0.50 flips into the inside class, the configuration collapses to 0 or 255 and the cell renders NOTHING. Two implementation details are load-bearing rather than tidy. The chunk FILL moves with the pair (create_voxel_chunk_from_case takes _outside_value(), not a literal): the chunk is 2x2x2, so seven neighbour cubes share corners with the case cube and draw their own sheets wherever a case corner is inside, and leaving the fill at 0.3 would put those seven at a different crossing from the one the rung is arguing - the cell would contradict itself. And the bead colours are computed from the SAME resolved array the chunk got, so they are identical at all four rungs by construction rather than by luck. Words considered and rejected for this axis, each because it already carries a different claim elsewhere: `bias` (pixel_cloud), `crossing` (sine_space, sine_space_explanation, fluency_seam), and `reading`. margin names the quantity actually being varied - the distance of each sample from the threshold. NOT RE-ARGUED: fusion and metaball_count are held by raymarched_metaballs/metaballs/implicit_surface_modeling (one scene, three names) and both bite hard, so 'how much the field merges' and 'how many sources' are taken; neither is asked here.
dna.declined: REFUSED BY NAME: `animate_threshold` (line 106 as shipped, the A key, and the only thing _process has ever done). It is a time-domain export twice over - it oscillates on sin(animation_time), and what it writes is material.emission_energy, a brightness ramp - so a still photographs one arbitrary phase and a sweep over it would measure the shutter rather than the artifact. Worse, its NAME promises this sequence's central question and delivers a glow: it does not move a threshold at all, it modulates emission on meshes that were already built. margin is the honest version of what that export pretends to be, and the export is left exactly as it shipped (false, untouched, still on the A key). Also refused: case_spacing and case_scale - layout magnitudes that an AABB-fitted capture camera cancels almost exactly, since scaling every cell and the gaps between them scales the subject and the frame together; and zoom_speed / min_zoom / max_zoom, which drive the scene's own Camera3D, a node _suppress_embedded_chrome hides at spawn and no capture ever looks through.
dna.fixture_why: ONE entry, and it is a BENCH SWITCH rather than a pin - the word, the two values and the gate are csg_union_demo's and csg_intersection_demo's, character for character. Nothing here needs pinning: there is no rotation, no RNG and no animation on any default path. What does need fixing is the FRAME. Both axes change the very MeshInstance3D set that capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb measures - workings=outcome deletes fifteen PRIMITIVE_LINES cages and 120 corner beads, and margin slides every interpolated vertex, so the subject's own box runs from 8.79 m wide at starved to 9.02 m at brimming - and a camera fitted per variant photographs each rung at its own magnification, which is the frame-relative verdict already recorded from the PostCrisis pass. capture_anchor=on stands an invisible layers=0 BoxMesh over the union of every value's extent, sized by construction from GRID_COLS/GRID_ROWS/case_spacing/case_scale and the margin table rather than measured from the built scene, so the box is identical at all sixteen combinations. Derived, its local corners are (-4.04, -0.04, -2.04) to (4.975, 0.975, 2.975): 9.015 x 1.015 x 5.015, diagonal 10.366. This is a CORRECTION to the approved design, which estimated the anchor at about 8.0 x 2.5 x 4.5 - the true box is wider and much flatter, because the sheets in the seven neighbour cubes of each 2x2x2 chunk reach 1 + t past the case corner while nothing reaches above 1 + t in y either. The gating is load-bearing rather than tidy: this box is also what capture_multi_angle frames and what sync_footprints reads, and 9.015 m where the registry records 8.79 would re-rate the artifact's footprint on the next measurement sweep. It defaults to 'off' and _read_metadata_overrides deliberately does not read config_capture_anchor, so no map token can switch it on; only direct property assignment - which is what dna.fixture and the sweep do - reaches it. Grounding is unaffected in either case: _auto_ground_artifact reads only min_y, and the anchor's -0.04 is the corner beads' own minimum, the number the artifact has always grounded on.
dna.framing_why: DERIVED ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT - I have not run Godot, and the first sweep should correct this. The rig places the camera at radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so the frame's world half-extent is simply radius * 1.9 * framing. The capture anchor's diagonal is 10.366, radius 5.183, giving a 19.7 m square frame at framing 1.0. The subject is a WIDE FLAT SLAB - 9.015 x 1.015 x 5.015 - and the canonical standpoint is yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, so its projected bounding box is about 10.25 m across (4.5075*cos(35.5) + 2.5075*sin(35.5), doubled) by about 3.37 m tall: roughly 8.9 percent of frame as a BOUNDING box, and the fifteen cells are a sparse grid inside that box, so measured subject share would land nearer 3-4 percent - under the ~6 percent floor at which a fit-by-diagonal shot of a flat subject stops being able to tell a real axis from a dead one. 0.8 gives a 15.8 m frame, roughly 14 percent bounding, and leaves the widest rung at 65 percent of frame width, nowhere near cropped (the crop limit is framing 0.52). The approved design specified 1.0 with 0.8 named as the contingency if a first sweep came in under 6 percent; the arithmetic above is why the contingency is taken up front instead. The labels sit 1.5 below the grid and 2.5 below the frame centre, well inside a 6.3 m half-height, so expression and trace do not lose their Config lines to the crop.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`. It now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns early on an unchanged signature (workings, margin, case_spacing, case_scale) - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. Eleven of the twelve placements never call it and the twelfth passes one key nothing reads, so not one of them is even torn down. The build is synchronous in _ready with no call_deferred anywhere on the build path. Teardown is restricted to an _owned array: the OLD KEY_R handler and the old _exit_tree both walked get_children() and freed everything, which is the CameraController this script caches, the Lighting rig, the WorldEnvironment, the UI Control - and any _RotationTimer GridInteractablesComponent attaches to the root after spawn. _rebuild() also remove_child()s before queue_free()ing, so the old nodes leave the AABB in the same frame rather than at the end of it, which is what a capture measuring straight after a config change would otherwise photograph.
dna.still_note: NOTHING IN THIS ARTIFACT MOVES on any default path - fifteen static ArrayMeshes, fifteen line cages, 120 beads and fifteen billboard labels, all resolved during _ready - which is why an axis was findable here at all in a sequence where four of six artifacts run _process. The strong rung pair is workings=outcome against operands: one removes the sheets and keeps the cage, the other the reverse, so they are inverse silhouettes of the same 8 m subject and cannot both be faint. margin is a change in sheet AREA of roughly an order of magnitude on case 1 (t=0.10 to t=0.95 on a corner triangle is t squared, 0.01 against 0.90) repeated across thirteen of the fifteen cells, with the cage and the beads deliberately held still so the still reads as an argument rather than as a resize. THE WEAK RUNG, written down here rather than discovered in the verdict, is trace against expression: they differ only by up to twelve markers per cell, and the markers sit exactly on the sheet boundary where the sheet can swallow them. CROSSING_RADIUS is therefore 0.1 - deliberately LARGER than the 0.08 corner bead - and the marker material is unshaded with emission at 1.4. If the sweep still reports trace faint, the honest remedy is to make the markers louder or to draw the residual edge segment as well, not to re-word the axis. Two cells are legitimately empty of sheet at every rung and this is truthful rather than broken: case 0 is all-outside and case 14 all-inside, so march_cube_fixed skips them and the demo stands its grey no-surface indicator there instead.

the_threshold_opinion.name: The Threshold Opinion
the_threshold_opinion.description: The isosurfaces SUPER OBJECT: a courtroom for a number. ONE field stands as a lattice of rods whose lengths are its own values; five surfaces extracted from it at five thresholds - fat, lean, pinched, thin, broken into islands - prove nothing in the field changed. A resolution row asks the same threshold of 4, 8 and 14 lattices, a brass rack holds the fifteen cases, and two wells are caught mid-merge, seamless. Every skin marched at build time. 2026-08-27.

dna.value_typing: `octaves` IS DECLARED AS JSON NUMBERS AND NOT AS THE STRINGS apply_dna_block DERIVED. The tool read them off the trailing `# 1 | 2 | 3 | 6` on the @export line (the trailing-comment branch, last in check_dna_declarations' value order) and wrote ["1", "2", "3", "6"], which would make the cave tokens the only scened entries in the corpus with string-numeric axis values, against ~35 numeric axes (noise_quarry.octaves, lsystem_dungeon.depth, star_primitive.points, mc_portal_landscape.num_portals) every one of which is spelled as numbers. THE DERIVATION CHAIN SURVIVES THE RETYPE, AND THIS WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: apply_dna_block compares `{k: [str(x) for x in v]}` against what it derives, and str(1) == "1", so both `--refresh` and a fresh `--token=... --axes=plumb,octaves` report `already matches the code` and write nothing. check_dna_declarations takes the numeric branch either way and reports ok. WHAT THE RETYPE BUYS IS THE STANDPOINT PROBE, and nothing else. build_dna_gallery reaches cabinet_sweep over a command line, so a value makes the round trip str() -> coerce() -> int and THE GALLERY IS BIT-IDENTICAL EITHER WAY. probe_anamorphic.py does not: at line 103 it reads the registry directly and keeps only `isinstance(v, str)`, writing the survivors straight into the capture spec. Spelled as strings it would hand capture_config_sweep the String "1" for a typed `int` export, and four identical frames would be published as doc/reports/anamorphic_<token>.json - which is the file the critic's standpoint gate reads, so a false 'flat from all five standpoints' becomes a manufactured conviction. Spelled as numbers the probe keeps nothing and returns an obvious null. The two failure modes are asymmetric; this takes the loud one. A SEPARATE CONSEQUENCE OF THE SAME FILTER, worth reporting on its own: probe_anamorphic cannot clear an INERT? verdict on ANY numeric axis in the corpus, because isinstance(str) empties the value list for all ~35 of them. That is a gap in the gate, not in this artifact.
dna.default:
plumb=bedded AND octaves=6, and BOTH no-ops are structural rather than arithmetic. `bedded` does not multiply by 1.0 - MarchingCubes.glsl BRANCHES on `if (params.plumbScale == 1.0)` and compiles the shipped statement `density = -(worldPos.y+100)/300 + density;` character for character. That is a stronger guarantee than the gyroid's and it was chosen deliberately, because the weaker one is not safe on this line: `a/b + d` and `a/b*c + d` are different expression shapes, and a GLSL compiler is free to contract the second into an FMA and round it once where the first rounds twice. x * 1.0 is bit-identical; `fma(x, 1.0, d)` versus `x + d` need not be. The branch removes the question entirely, and it is what the script's own docstring already claimed the shader did. `octaves` = 6 makes the loop bound `i < int(params.octaves)` evaluate to `i < 6`, an integer comparison against the same integer - there is no float anywhere on that path. Neither default is a table entry that happens to equal the shipped value.

REACH MEASURED FOR THIS TOKEN: 4 placements, and ZERO of them reach apply_grid_config, by two independent gates. Two are bare grid cells with no `#` config - ISO_LookupTable interactables[3][10] and Spine_Museum interactables[9][36] - and since this entry declares no default_params and the token carries no delegate, merged_config is EMPTY, so GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` at :1194 means _apply_artifact_config is never called at all. The other two are curation_station rosters: Corridor_ISO_LookupTable interactables[14][12] (`#artifacts:mc_cave#layout:row`) and Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_3 interactables[7][19] (`#artifacts:mc_cave,mc_inside_cave,mc_base,fountain_demo,metaball_world`). Those miss by a SECOND gate that is specific to this family: curation_station.gd:381 tests `inst.has_method("apply_grid_config")` on the INSTANCE ROOT, and marchingcubes_cave.tscn's root is a scriptless Node3D with the script on its `Terrain` child - so the {"emissive": false} call every other mounted artifact receives is never made here. Even if it were, "emissive" moves no term of the signature and the guard returns early.

THREE MENTIONS THAT ARE NOT PLACEMENTS, and none was counted: Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_3's map_info.description sentence; Spine_Museum's map_info.spine_trail[16].hero, which is metadata naming the same cell already counted once; and Trial_physarum_isosurfaces' map_info.mission_graph.swaps[2], `mc_cave->metaball_world`, which is a sentence about a substitution. Counting a sentence is the error queer_marching_cave's entry records, and it would have inflated this count to 7.
dna.was: 114 lines, ZERO @export of its own, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was the word `pass` - a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find it. Everything this artifact argues lived as a literal inside MarchingCubes.glsl: the ridged loop ran a fixed six times at :168 and the vertical bias was written bare at :180, so the audit called the artifact axis-less. It was not axis-less; its knobs were simply in a file the audit does not read. Ninety of the 114 lines are _create_simple_cave_mesh(), a hand-written 200 m sine tunnel that only the THIRD scene on this script ever renders.
dna.note:
THE SEQUENCE'S TRUTH LINE, LITERALLY. 'Define a field, extract a surface. The boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry.' This script is the one place in the wave where the SAME field is shipped twice, once to be looked at and once to be stood inside, so an axis declared here has to mean something from both sides. You are OUTSIDE this one: the scene's camera sits at (-15, 35, 50) looking in, with a DirectionalLight3D and five torches, so the field reads as a block of rock with a top surface and a sky.

plumb - WHICH WAY IS DOWN, AND WHETHER THERE IS A DOWN AT ALL. Everything this shader knows about gravity is one line, MarchingCubes.glsl:180: `density = -(worldPos.y+100)/300 + density`. It is the ONLY anisotropic term in the file; the six octaves above it are isotropic ridged noise, which on its own has no up. That one linear bias is what makes low regions solid and high regions air - from outside, the block's top surface and its sky; from inside, the floor you stand on. plumbScale multiplies it and nothing else. bedded (1.0) SHIPPED. overturned (-1.0) flips the sign: the same noise at the same threshold with inside and outside exchanged, rock overhead and nothing under your feet. weightless (0.0) DELETES the term and leaves pure ridged noise - an isotropic sponge with no floor, no ceiling and no sky, filling the sampled box to all six faces. steep (3.0) triples the gradient so the field swings 3.0 across the 300 m box instead of 1.0 and the solid retreats into the bottom third: a slab with a rough top, a crawl space. The four values are held IDENTICAL across all four declared tokens on purpose - it is one const on one script, and holding them identical is what makes the galleries comparable frame for frame.

octaves - HOW MANY SCALES OF ROCK SURVIVE THE LATTICE, AND THIS IS THE AXIS THAT MAKES THE SIBLINGS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS. :168 opens `for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++)`; each pass halves the amplitude and doubles the frequency, with the weight feedback at :174 gating each octave by the previous one. The literal 6 is the rung. What makes it worth declaring is arithmetic the two scenes do not share. THIS token: noise_scale 13.5, chunk_scale 300.0, so samplePos = worldPos x 0.04500 and octave 0 has ~22 m features; the marching lattice samples at 300.0/64 = 4.688 m, so its Nyquist limit is 9.38 m. The six octaves measure 22.2, 11.1, 5.5, 2.8, 1.4, 0.7 m, which puts 2 of them above the limit and the rest below it. On the sibling the same six octaves land differently, and that is the finding: mc_cave resolves TWO scales of rock, mc_inside_cave resolves FOUR, from the same script, the same shader, the same rungs and the same threshold. The artifact you stand inside can resolve two more octaves than the one you look at. That is the inside/outside asymmetry as a number rather than as a description, and it is why the axis is declared on both rather than on one.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE APPROVED DESIGN, both found by redoing its arithmetic. (1) The design said the inside scene resolves ONE more octave than the outside one; by the Nyquist figures above it is TWO (octaves 0-3 against octaves 0-1). (2) The design said the sub-limit octaves are 'COMPUTED AND THEN THROWN AWAY BY THE EXTRACTOR'. They are not thrown away, they ALIAS: content finer than the sampling cell still perturbs the corner values, which still moves where interpolateVerts puts the crossing. So the sub-limit rungs are predicted to be nearly degenerate, not exactly degenerate, and a small non-zero reading there is the expected result rather than a failed prediction.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE FIELD ITSELF: :170 is `snoise(samplePos) * 2 - 1` before the ridged fold, not the plain `snoise` of the usual Lague construction, so the input to `1 - abs(noise)` spans about [-3, 1] rather than [-1, 1] and the fold is off-centre. The amplitude LADDER still halves exactly (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125), which is what the octave arithmetic above rests on, but the per-octave term is not bounded by 1 and the summed density is not bounded by 1.969. Any claim about an absolute density total should be read as about the ladder, not about the sum.
dna.declined: REFUSED, `iso_level`, and the refusal is deliberate given that this wave promotes `threshold` on the torus. iso_level is the ONE export on which these two sibling scenes already disagree - 0.85 on marchingcubes_cave.tscn against 0.88 on marchingcubes_inside_cave.tscn - so an axis over it would say 'these two artifacts are one object at two thresholds', which is nearly irresistible. It is refused because on THIS shader the density carries a vertical gradient, so a constant offset to the threshold is a vertical translation of the rock/air horizon, which is the same horizon `plumb` moves: a bias of 0.15 is 45 m of horizon on a 300 m box, and plumb=steep moves it further. The two would measure each other at plumb=bedded and separate only at plumb=weightless - a conditional pair bought at the price of a confound. The torus pays gyroid_demo's bequest instead, because its field has no gradient term at all. REFUSED, the weight-gating literal 10 at :174 (`weight = max(0, min(1, noise * 10))`): it is the Lague trick that turns isotropic ridged fBm into connected tunnels and it is the closest thing in the file to an axis about whether the void is a passage or a sealed bubble - refused because at low values it also zeroes every octave after the first, so it conflates connectivity with detail and would be `octaves` wearing another name. REFUSED, `noise_offset` (a different arbitrary sample of the same field, and already fixed by the .tscn), `chunk_scale` and `center_position` (a size and a placement, both self-cancelling under an AABB-fitted camera), `continuous_update` (a rate, invisible in a still by law). REFUSED, `invert_faces`, AND THIS ONE IS A REPORTED DEFECT RATHER THAN A DECLINE. TerrainGeneratorBase:10 documents it as 'Flip triangle winding and normals (useful for objects vs caves)' and NEITHER cave scene sets it, so mc_inside_cave - the artifact whose entire premise is 'marching cubes cave seen from inside' - ships with the same winding as the landscapes, and TerrainMat.tres renders cull_back. Whichever way that winding points, the artifact named 'inside' made no different choice from the one named 'cave'. It is not an axis (two values, below the floor, and a winding order is a material-culling fact rather than a field property). It should be its own fix.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in projected-area currency, computed by hand rather than by rasterising the scene. Read it as an order-of-magnitude claim the sweep can falsify, not as the critic's own hottest-5%-of-crop number. capture_config_sweep places its OWN camera at dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, RES 760.

CLOSEST PAIR ON plumb: bedded (1.0) vs steep (3.0), AT ABOUT 11% OF FRAME. Solid requires the ridged sum to exceed isoLevel + k(y+100)/300. At k=1 that is satisfied up to roughly y = +15 for a typical sum; at k=3 the same sum is exceeded only by about y = -60. The top of the mass drops roughly 75 m in a 300 m box shown at ~53% of frame height, and the newly-empty band is 75/300 x 53% = about 13% of frame height across the ~42% of frame width the body occupies - call it 11% once the silhouette's obliquity is taken off. The LARGEST pair should be bedded vs overturned, over 35%, since the mass moves from the bottom of the frame to the top.

CLOSEST PAIR ON octaves, AND IT IS A PREDICTION THAT THE AXIS IS PARTLY DEGENERATE ON PURPOSE: 3 vs 6, UNDER 2%. The design named that pair too, but for the wrong reason and on the wrong scope. On this token only octaves 0-1 clear the 9.38 m Nyquist limit, so rungs 2, 3 and 6 differ ONLY in octaves that alias rather than resolve - the near-degeneracy is a three-way tie among {2, 3, 6}, not a single close pair, and 3-vs-6 is merely the member of it with the smallest amplitude difference (0.125 + 0.0625 + 0.03125 = 0.219 of the ladder's 1.969, gated down further by :174). The pair that MUST move is 1 vs 6: one octave is a smooth blobby cave with no wall texture at all, predicted over 25%.

IF 3-vs-6 COMES BACK NEAR ZERO ON mc_cave AND ALIVE ON mc_inside_cave, THE AXIS HAS DONE ITS JOB AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS DEAD. The degeneracy IS the finding: it is the Nyquist limit of the extraction lattice showing up as a photograph. A dead reading on the sub-limit rungs of one token and a live one on the other is the result this axis was declared to produce.

THE RUNG THAT COULD GO WRONG IS 1, and the confound is stated rather than hidden. Dropping octaves 1-5 removes up to 0.969 of the amplitude ladder (much less after the weight gating), and against the 1/300 gradient every unit of removed sum is 300 m of horizon. So `1` will look both SMOOTHER and EMPTIER, and the two effects are not separable in a still - octaves is borrowing plumb's pixels at its bottom rung. If that dominates the tile, the low rung should come up to 2 rather than the axis being called confounded.
dna.framing_why: 0.75, and the arithmetic is checked against capture_config_sweep.gd:415 rather than guessed. The union AABB over the four plumb rungs is the SAMPLED BOX, 300 x 300 x 300 - and that is the single fact that makes this axis safe to sweep. plumb=weightless deletes the gradient and fills the box to all six faces, so the union box is the full box at EVERY rung and no variant gets shrunk by another variant's growth; an axis whose extent varied would have moved the camera with the subject and measured itself down to nothing. radius = 300 x sqrt(3) / 2 = 259.8 m. dist = 259.8 / tan(17deg) * 1.9 * framing = 1614.6 * framing, and the frame is 2 tan(17deg) x dist tall. The box's half-extents project onto the camera-up axis (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) as 150 x (0.149 + 0.966 + 0.209) = 198.8, so the subject is 397.6 m tall: 40% of frame at framing 1.0, 53% at 0.75. 0.75 is chosen rather than something tighter because BOTH axes here are about the whole silhouette - where the horizon sits, and how rough the whole surface is - not about a small part of a large object, so cropping in past the box would start cutting off the very band plumb moves.
dna.fixture_why:
ALMOST NO FIXTURE, and it is worth saying which of the usual reasons do not apply. _ready() is not gated: TerrainGeneratorBase._ready() runs init_compute(), run_compute(), fetch_and_process_compute_data() and create_mesh() SYNCHRONOUSLY, so the artifact builds standalone on the bench with no map, no host and no config. There is no RNG and no seed to pin - the field is Ashima/stegu simplex noise, a pure function of position, and noise_offset is fixed by the .tscn at (200, -120, 150). There is no clock in the picture: params.time is declared and never referenced. And the settle window cannot catch a half-built mesh - the sweep waits two process frames plus 0.1 s, roughly 8 frames, while the base's re-dispatch needs 12 wait-frames for GPU sync and 90 more for the mesh thread before create_mesh could run again, so what is photographed is unambiguously the mesh _ready built.

ONE BENCH HAZARD THAT IS NOT A FIXTURE PROBLEM BUT MUST BE READ FROM THE LOG: _create_fallback_mesh() on this class builds a 200 m sine TUNNEL with none of the field in it. If the capture host cannot make a local RenderingDevice, or if process_mesh_data() trips its 500,000-triangle safety abort and sets num_triangles = 0, every tile is that decoy and both axes measure zero for entirely the wrong reason. THE RUN IS ONLY VALID IF THE LOG SHOWS 'Generation complete!' AND NOT 'Creating fallback'.

ONE REAL SIDE EFFECT AT ONE RUNG, stated because it is a behaviour change and not only a picture: plumb=weightless raises the solid fraction and with it the surface area, so the triangle count rises. dna.predicted_degeneracy:
inverse_square x wyvill, and this CORRECTS the approved design, which named inverse_square x gaussian. Solve each kernel for the distance at which ONE mean source (strength 0.85, radius 0.45, so strength*radius^2 = 0.1721) alone reaches iso 0.65, and you get the radius of an isolated ball: inverse_square 0.1721/d^2 = 0.65 -> d = 0.515 m; wyvill 0.85(1 - d^2/3.24)^3 = 0.65 -> d = 0.526 m; cone 0.85(1 - d/1.8) = 0.65 -> d = 0.424 m; gaussian 0.85exp(-d^2/0.405) = 0.65 -> d = 0.330 m. inverse_square and wyvill are 2.2% apart and every other pair is 20-36% apart, so gaussian is the FARTHEST rung from the default, not the nearest. The design read long-tailed as similar, and the tail is not what sets the ball.

What separates the close pair is therefore not the ball but the BACKGROUND. At emplacement=column ten sources span about 6 m; under inverse_square a point 1.5 m from the nearest still collects 0.0765 from it and roughly 0.15 more from the other eight, so the local iso is effectively 0.65 - 0.20 = 0.45 and the column's radius solves to 0.618 m. Under wyvill everything past R = 4 x radius = 1.8 m is exactly zero, so the same column stands at 0.526 m. A 17% radius change on a tall thin body: PREDICTED 5% of frame, 9% focus. If it lands under 3% the honest reading is that a 17% waist on a subject occupying a narrow vertical strip is simply not enough pixels, and the crop (framing 0.85) is the first thing to check - not the axis.

SECOND PREDICTION, crossed, and the one worth the pass because it can fail loudly. At emplacement=shell the ten sources sit on a Fibonacci sphere of radius min(bounds)*0.7 = 1.575 m. The field AT THE CENTRE is 10 x 0.1721/2.4806 = 0.694 under inverse_square against iso 0.65 - a 6.8% margin, so the bag is SOLID - and 10 x 0.85(1 - 2.4806/3.24)^3 = 0.110 under wyvill, so it is HOLLOW. That is a real difference in the field and the camera CANNOT SEE IT, because the bag is closed either way and from outside both are a ~3.6 m sphere. It is written here so that a small number on shell x kernel is read as the closed surface it is and not as a dead axis. The rung where kernel is loudest is scatter, not shell: uniform in a 4.5 x 9.6 x 4.5 m box the mean nearest-neighbour spacing is about 1.49 m, and at the midpoint gaussian gives 2 x 0.85exp(-0.555/0.405) = 0.43 (BELOW iso, ten separate beads) where inverse_square gives 0.62 plus tails = 0.77 and wyvill 0.97 (both connected).
dna.default:
emplacement=column AND kernel=inverse_square, and both are SHORT-CIRCUITS rather than table entries that happen to land on the shipped number. _emplace() at column evaluates the same three expressions the loop always evaluated, in the same order, drawing from the same stream: _jitter(null, bounds.x * 0.3) is randf_range(-half, half) where -half is an exact IEEE sign flip of the identical product, then bounds.y * y_frac * 0.7 with no draw, then the z jitter. Strength and radius follow, then Metaball._init's six animation draws with rng == null - the shipped global calls, unchanged. And inverse_square is not a kernel branch inside the hot loop but its OWN triple loop: the same load and the same divide, mb_sr2[m] / dist_sq, because a general kernel evaluated at the parameters that reproduce an inverse square is not the same instruction stream as an inverse square.

REACH MEASURED, and the count is 11, not the 1 the design carried. Every one of them is untouched, by three different mechanisms:
  - ONE bare grid cell, ISO_Metaballs interactables[1][1], the token metaball_world with no #. The entry declares no default_params, so merged_config is empty and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` (:1194) means _apply_artifact_config is never called at all.

Pure defaults.
  - TWO curation_station rosters, Corridor_ISO_Metaballs interactables[31][12] and Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_3 interactables[7][19]. These are the only placements that reach a config: curation_station.gd:381-382 calls inst.apply_grid_config({"emissive": false}) on the instance ROOT. Before this pass that landed on a bare `pass`; now it is forwarded to the child, where it moves no term of the signature and returns before the rebuild. That forward is the single behavioural delta of this promotion in a live room, and it terminates in a return.

TWO MENTIONS THAT ARE NOT PLACEMENTS, and neither was counted: Trial_physarum_isosurfaces map_info.mission_graph carries a cast: metaball_world with a rect - a roster reservation, no interactables cell, no config - and ISO_Showcase_12's map_info.description reads "Test: metaball_world + queer_marching_cave" while its interactables layer holds rhizome_cave_demo, marching_cubes and marchingcave and NOT this token. That stale sentence is already on the record in queer_marching_cave's own entry, where counting it would have inflated a 3 to a 4.
dna.was: Nine exports, an apply_grid_config whose entire body was the word `pass` on the generator, and a SECOND bare `pass` on the scene root above it - so the artifact was unreachable twice over. The field's ten sources were laid out by one hardcoded expression, a vertical stack with a small horizontal jitter, which against this scene's own 4.5 x 9.6 x 4.5 m volume is the entire reason a marching-cubes metaball rig reads as a lava lamp. And the whole thing was unseeded twice over: four randf_range draws per source in generate_metaballs and six more inside Metaball._init, so "the same field twice" was not something this artifact could do and any variant sweep would have been photographing ten different objects.
dna.note:
emplacement is WHERE THE FIELD'S SOURCES STAND, which is the half of the metaball question metaballs.tscn does not ask. That artifact owns metaball_count (how many sources) and fusion (how hard they blend), and both bite at 53% and 74%. This one holds the count at the scene's own 10 on every single rung - same summands, same kernel, same iso - and moves only the geometry of provenance, so the sweep demonstrates that where is independent of how many. column = SHIPPED, a stack from -3.36 m to +2.69 m with +/-0.675 m of jitter. ring = a circle of radius bounds.x * 0.6 = 1.35 m in XZ at y = 0; neighbours land ~0.85 m apart, inside every kernel here, so the extraction closes into a torus rather than into ten beads. pair = two clusters at +/- bounds.y * 0.6, 5.76 m centre to centre, the count split evenly, with a 0.72 m vertical spread inside each cluster so the five members merge into one body and the two bodies do not - the arrangement in which a FIXED threshold decides whether this artifact is one thing or two. shell = a Fibonacci sphere at min(bounds) * 0.7 = 1.575 m, sources on a hollow. scatter = uniform through the whole volume, against column's 0.3 of it.

kernel is WHAT ONE SOURCE CONTRIBUTES, and the relation to the taken word is said out loud rather than left for the critic. fusion on metaballs.tscn is smin(a, b, k), a smooth-minimum BLEND between two signed distance functions in a raymarcher that never sums anything. kernel is the falloff of the summands in a potential field that IS summed, on a 30 x 64 x 30 scalar grid that IS marched. One is an operator between distance functions; the other is the function being added. They will still produce related silhouettes at their extremes - gaussian on a wide scatter looks like fusion=distinct - and the reason is not that the axes are the same question but that a tight kernel and a disengaged smin both refuse to join two bodies. falloff was the natural word and is taken by wave_propagation_3d.

inverse_square = SHIPPED: strength * radius^2 / d^2, INFINITE SUPPORT, which the code then truncates at 5% of iso to afford it. That truncation is the artifact admitting what its field is made of, and it is why this axis exists at all. wyvill = s(1 - d^2/R^2)^3 for d < R with R = 4 x radius, exactly zero beyond - the only rung on which the cull is not an approximation but the kernel's own edge, so _update_influence_radii returns R itself there rather than a solved tail. gaussian = s exp(-d^2/2r^2), smooth, long-tailed, and by the arithmetic in predicted_degeneracy the TIGHTEST ball of the four. cone = s max(0, 1 - d/R), only C0, so the summed field creases where two sources meet and the extracted surface carries the crease.

ONE THING THIS PASS DID NOT DO THE OBVIOUS WAY. The validator for both axes reads the property's own @export_enum hint_string at runtime (_accepts) instead of comparing against a const allow-list kept beside the enum. Two lists in one file is the science_screen fault at file scale - a sweep sets a value the allow-list rejects, the artifact falls back to its default, and identical frames get published under a green gate. There is one list here and the enum is it.
dna.declined: iso_level (0.65 in the .tscn) - that is threshold, taken by mc_torus_sculpture, and holding it fixed is what makes emplacement=pair a question at all. metaball_count (10) - taken by metaballs.tscn, and held CONSTANT across every rung of emplacement precisely so the two questions stay separate. grid_size (30,64,30) and cell_size (0.15) - the sampling lattice, i.e. resolution, already a family word used twice (queer_marching_cave, animated_noise_explorer); a seventh claim on it was not worth making here. animation_speed, step_duration, max_steps, regen_interval and TIME_BUDGET_MS - rates and durations, invisible in a still by law 2, and this artifact runs _process. The culling constant CULL_FRACTION = 0.05 - refused as an axis and folded into kernel's subtext instead: at the shipped kernel it is an approximation error rather than a field property, and at any conservative value it is invisible by construction. surface_shader (PinkTeleport) - declined as an axis, but NOT chrome, and this is the loudest thing found in the pass. The shader was read rather than assumed: PinkTeleport.gdshader takes `float time = TIME` at :36 and drives ALBEDO, EMISSION and ALPHA from it - an animated spiral (sin(radius*wave_frequency - time*portal_speed + angle*3)), pulsing rings (sin(radius*15 - time*pulse_speed)), a highlight at sin(time*2), a UV swirl at sin(time*1.5)/cos(time*1.2), a noise sample scrolled by time*0.1, and a centre glow at sin(time*3). capture_config_sweep freezes nothing - no Engine.time_scale, no TIME override - and its SETTLE is 1.1 s per tile, so consecutive tiles are captured at least 1.1 s apart and the centre-glow term alone advances 3.3 radians, over half a cycle, between them. EVERY TILE THEREFORE DIFFERS IN FULL-FRAME SURFACE COLOUR AND ALPHA FOR REASONS THAT BELONG TO NEITHER AXIS. This is the inverse of the corpus's usual failure: it manufactures a FALSE BITE rather than a false INERT, and it will do so on both axes at once and on every crossed pair. Read any number from this artifact's sweep as an upper bound until the clock is pinned. The mitigation is not inside this artifact - the export can only be set to null, and setup_scene()'s fallback then load()s the same shader by path - so it belongs to the harness (freeze time before the shot) or to a second run whose tiles are captured at equal TIME. No such change was made here; PinkTeleport is shared and is not this token's to edit. And a genuine DEAD EXPORT pair reported and left alone: collision_shape and static_body are declared at :108-109 and never assigned by any line in the file, so this entry's description claim of "with collision" is false. Wiring them would change what eleven live placements do and is not this pass's business.
dna.fixture_why: max_steps = 0 is the neat part, and it invents nothing: _ready() calls generate_metaballs() and generate_mesh() unconditionally and then starts the animation only if max_steps > 0, so zero leaves the mesh in exactly the state t = 0 produced and _process returns on `not stepping` forever after. A static, deterministic pose reached through an export that already shipped. metaball_seed = 7 is the determinism fix: 0 keeps the shipped global RNG call for call, non-zero routes every draw through TWO local streams - one for position, one for body. The split is load-bearing rather than tidy. ring and shell draw NO positional randomness while column, pair and scatter draw two or three floats per source; on a single stream that difference would shift every strength and radius downstream, so ring would differ from column in ten ball sizes as well as in one arrangement, and the axis would be measuring two things at once. Metaball._init's six animation draws take the body stream too, because they happen in the CONSTRUCTOR and are consumed even at max_steps = 0 where update() is never called - a stream that skipped them would move every later source. This is a fresh fixture dict; there was no existing one to merge into, which is the hazard that bit twice yesterday.
dna.rebuild_guard:
apply_grid_config on the generator takes a value only when the export's OWN enum hint accepts it, then compares a signature over every term the build reads - emplacement, kernel, metaball_seed, metaball_count, iso_level, grid_size, cell_size - and returns before touching the mesh when none of them moved. It also returns when _built is false, since before _ready there is nothing to redraw. A rebuild frees and creates NO nodes: generate_mesh clears and refills the one ArrayMesh setup_scene already made, and _exit_tree now frees only the _owned array (mesh_instance, the single node this script creates) instead of walking every child and freeing whatever has no owner.

THE FAULT THAT MADE THIS NECESSARY, because it would have shipped silently: metaballworld.tscn's root MetaballWorld carries metaballscene.gd, whose apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`, and the generator that owns every export is a CHILD. GridInteractablesComponent stamps config_* and calls apply_grid_config on the ROOT, and because the root does answer has_method() the component's own rescue branch for child-held config (:1695) is skipped by construction. Two declared axes, green on the bench, and every key a player's map ever wrote dropped on the floor. The root now forwards.

STALE PATHS, and this one was NOT harmless. Both ext_resources in metaballworld.tscn named res://algorithms/proceduralgeneration/metaballgenerator/..., a folder that holds only an orphaned copy of the scene; the real scripts are under hybrid_complex/. Godot resolves by uid and both uids match (b6m62uve4s5ol, c3l817nt0dv02), so the game was fine - but check_dna_declarations and apply_dna_block resolve by PATH, found neither file, and reported the source unreadable, which would have failed this token at the gate for a reason that has nothing to do with its axes. Both paths corrected to where the uids already pointed; the orphan at algorithms/proceduralgeneration/metaballgenerator/metaballworld.tscn is untouched.

DERIVATION NOTE, since it deviates from the tool: apply_dna_block.py refuses this token. Its derive() reads source_for(), which returns the scene ROOT's script, and the axes live on the generator child - the same shape as six other already-promoted tokens (tessellation_lattice_demo, draw_dot_time_domain, evolutionary_algorithms and three more). The axes above were therefore derived by calling check_dna_declarations.code_values() against the script that actually exports each axis - the same per-axis resolution the gate itself uses at :414-418 - and written with apply_dna_block's own splice(). No value list was typed by hand, and check_dna_declarations.py reports both axes ok.

csg_union_demo.name: CSG Union Demo
csg_union_demo.description: Two CSG primitives combined with the union operator. Visualizes A union B as a single composite solid.
csg_union_demo.qfep_connection: A∪B: two solids declared one. The chapter's opening insistence that composition is not a pile: the moment two forms join, their boundary is renegotiated, and the inside of the whole is more than the sum of the insides.

csg_intersection_demo.name: CSG Intersection Demo
csg_intersection_demo.description: Two CSG primitives with intersection operator. Only the overlap survives.
csg_intersection_demo.qfep_connection: A∩B: only the overlap survives. The strictest operator — intersection keeps solely the space both solids agreed to occupy and discards everything else, so two large forms can yield a tiny sliver or nothing at all. The primitive of the joint: where two things meet is not where they touch but where they *coincide*, and this operator is the chapter's tool for finding that shared interior.

csg_difference_demo.description: A box with a sphere subtracted. The operator that makes cavities and openings.
