csg_difference_demo.qfep_connection: A−B: the box remembers the sphere by its absence. Difference is the operator of cavities and openings — subtract one solid from another and what remains is shaped by a thing no longer there, the hollow a negative portrait of what was removed. The walk's central power: every window, every socket, every carved bowl is a subtraction, form defined by a precise act of taking-away.

the_argument_of_solids.name: The Argument Of Solids
the_argument_of_solids.description: The boolean surfaces SUPER OBJECT: a debating chamber where two solids argue and the verdicts stand around them. Contested ground lit as a live intersection; union, intersection and subtraction each a real CSGCombiner3D; A-B beside B-A because subtraction is the only verb that cares about order; a nesting tree, a coincident-face seam where edges are born, the baked debt, and a building that is a block minus its rooms. Nothing modelled - every verdict is live CSG. 2026-08-27.

subtraction_suite.name: Subtraction Suite
subtraction_suite.description: Three stations on one 2.88 m bench, all showing the same subtraction. ART: a Fontana cube on a white plinth, an oversized sphere taken out of it, a luminous point suspended in the hollow, nothing explained. OPERATOR: the geometrically IDENTICAL carved solid on a post in front of a slate board, with A ghosted back around it and B drawn at the void's true radius, so the operation is visible and not only its answer. CATALOGUE: a steel tray holding five decompositions of one sphere - two hemispheres, eight octants, eight wedges, a boolean bite, forty-eight tiles - each held apart in an exploded view. One axis, `breach`, reused character for character from fontana_puncture and applied to all three at once. Use #breach:.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: footprint_cells is a COUNT, not a [w,d] pair - a pair crashes the placement engine. The bench is 2.88 m of frontage (three stations at a 0.96 m pitch) by 1.00 m deep by 1.58 m tall including the captions, so three cells are occupied and a fourth is declared because a 2.88 m slab lands off-grid more often than not. Front clearance 2 is the reading distance: the three stations only argue with each other when all three are in one view, and the whole exhibit is 2.88 m wide. wall_backing is true because the operator station's slate board is a back wall of its own and wants nothing behind it.

subtraction_suite.qfep_connection: F, held still and asked three times. Subtraction is the operator that makes a room out of a wall, and this bench is about what happens to the WORD for it when the institution changes. The same void is a gesture on a plinth, a term in an expression on a board, and one entry in a tray of five ways to take a thing apart - and the depth of the cut, which is a measurable ratio in the first two, stops being measurable in the third because the specimen has no corners to survive in. That is the exhibit's own dark spot made into its subject: a vocabulary looks portable until you hand it a body it was not measured against.
subtraction_suite.relationships: Synthesised from [[fontana_puncture]], [[csg_difference_demo]], [[csg_compose_workbench]] and [[sphere_splitting_showcase]] - four artifacts, three of them promoted on one day and the fourth two days later, three of which arrived at the SAME word (`strike`) with the same four values in the same order, and none of which had ever been in one frame. WHAT THEY LEARNED, and what this exhibits. [[fontana_puncture]] found that `breach` is not a size knob: cube_size never moves, and the four values are the four TOPOLOGICALLY distinct states this geometry has, cut against the cube's own three critical distances (half-extent 0.5, edge-midpoint 0.707, corner 0.866, all x cube_size). It stops short of 0.866 on purpose, because past that the cube is gone and the frame measures NO RENDER, which is a fact about the capture and not about the art. It also REFUSED a taglio axis - a slash is a cut in ONE face and the sweep photographs from one fixed camera, so half the yaws would show an uncut cube - and that refusal is why this bench's only axis is spherically legible too. [[csg_difference_demo]] took `strike` character for character and then said plainly where it CANNOT follow: its sphere is 1.10 half-extents against fontana's 1.36, so the word is shared and the NUMBERS are not, and each artifact resolves the same value against its own geometry. That is the model this whole exhibit is built on. It also found, the hard way, that a CSGCombiner3D nested in another combiner is a SHAPE and not a container - its ghosts had to hang off a plain Node3D rig or the trace would be unioned back into the solid it comments on - and every combiner here is a direct child of a plain Node3D for that reason. [[csg_compose_workbench]] holds `algebra`, the corpus's only axis asking what a closed operator SET consists of, and declined `workings` on the ground that a hub's question is the set while a demo's question is the derivation - kept apart the two are comparable, merged one is redundant. That fence is why this suite shows ONE operator and not three. [[sphere_splitting_showcase]] found the one distinction in five fracture methods a STILL can carry (computed parts against latent ones, no seam against nothing but seam) and refused an `exploded` axis for two measured reasons: the real path unfreezes unseeded physics, and the fake path works on two of the five bases and does nothing on the other three - 'an axis that is a null cell for 60% of the bench is a finished-looking experiment about the 40%'. Its five bases are rebuilt here as STATIC partitions, in its own order, precisely so the tray can be exploded deterministically; that substitution is named as this exhibit's dark spot in dna.dark_spot. Kin to [[exhibit_furniture]], whose `house` axis (white_cube, wunderkammer, depot, forensic) taught this corpus that the furniture around a thing is an argument about the institution and not a mount - the plinth, the lectern and the tray here do that job without claiming the word.

dna.default: breach=opened - the strongest single reading, and a free choice because a synthesis has no shipped placements to preserve. It is also [[fontana_puncture]]'s own shipped value, so the suite's front picture and the family's front picture are the same picture: the synthesis inherits the family's default rather than a curator's. Why it is the strongest: `opened` is the only value at which all three stations are simultaneously legible as both intact and cut. At body_size 0.36 the void is 0.2448 against an edge-midpoint of 0.2546, so the cube is a thin frame around a void that has won and is still ONE object; on the board B is 0.2448 against A's half-extent of 0.1800, visibly bigger than the body it is being taken out of, which is the whole reason the operands are drawn; and on the tray the separation is 0.68 of the specimen radius, far enough that every plate is open and near enough that the 48-tile plate has not yet become a cloud with no sphere in it. `pierced` under-reads all three, `severed` costs the cube its identity (eight disconnected corner pieces), and `husk` is the limit before nothing renders.
dna.was: synthesized from fontana_puncture, csg_difference_demo, csg_compose_workbench, sphere_splitting_showcase. Nothing was refactored and no source changed; this is a new object built from scratch at bench scale rather than an instancing of the four, because three of them carry their own room and one carries its own WorldEnvironment, a stats HUD and a nine-line instruction panel addressed to a player with hands. The gap it fills is that `strike` is shared by three of these artifacts and the sharing has only ever existed as three registry notes agreeing with each other in prose. Worse for the question itself: an axis shows one value per still, so a shared word can only ever be tested by laying two separate sweeps of two separate rooms side by side and trusting that the lighting, the framing and the settle were the same. The test wanted one frame.
dna.axes_note: `breach` is REUSED CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER from [[fontana_puncture]] - same word, same four values, same order - and it is not retyped. The script holds `const FONTANA_SOURCE := preload("res://commons/primitives/fontana_puncture/fontana_puncture.gd")` and reads its `const BREACH` at load, so BOTH the vocabulary and the four ratios come from the family and cannot drift from it even if somebody edits the family. That is the slot_machine pattern. The literal @export_enum line is written out as well, because the declaration gate reads the enum and GDScript cannot build one from a const; the two cannot disagree silently, since every entry point validates against the preloaded table and anything it does not recognise leaves the bench standing where it was. `PLATES`, the tray's five bases in [[sphere_splitting_showcase]]'s shipped order, is written as a literal instead: that script extends a vector_scene_base and preloads five destructible scenes, so pulling it in for a five-element array would drag a whole test scene behind an ORDER - and an order is not a vocabulary.
dna.finding:
THE HONEST TEST, and it is the reason this artifact exists. The shared word survives at two stations as a measured ratio and at the third only as an order.

AT THE PLINTH AND AT THE BOARD it transfers perfectly, because the construction is fontana's and the ladder is SCALE-FREE. Checked arithmetically rather than assumed: at body_size 0.36 the cube's three critical distances are 0.1800, 0.2546 and 0.3118, and the four void radii are 0.1944, 0.2448, 0.2664 and 0.2880 - so pierced breaches the faces and stops, opened is still connected, severed cuts the twelve edges into eight corner pieces, and husk stops short of annihilation. The same four objects at a different size.

AT THE TRAY IT DOES NOT, and the failure is exact. A sphere has one critical distance, its radius; a partition of a sphere has none at all, because there is no connectivity left to lose - every plate is already in pieces at `pierced`. Applied as separation, d = ratio x R, the axis opens a gap of 2*d*sin(t/2) between two adjacent cells whose centroid directions differ by t, against a cell arc width of t*R, so the RELATIVE opening is 2*sin(t/2)/t x d/R. That factor is 0.9003 at t = 90 degrees, 0.9745 at 45 and 0.9886 at 30 - within ten per cent of 1 for every division on this tray - and both the gap and the width carry the same sin(v) factor away from the equator, so it holds at the poles as well. THE CONSEQUENCE: `breach` opens the 48-tile plate and the 8-wedge plate by the same fraction of themselves. It cannot distinguish the five bases, which is the one thing a catalogue exists to do. The single exception is the coarsest plate - two hemispheres separate along a diameter, t = 180 degrees, so the gap is 2*d against a part depth of R and the planar plate opens about twice as fast relative to itself as any other. Where the ladder distinguishes anything on this tray, it distinguishes the 2-part plate from the other four and nothing else.

SO: `breach` names a topological ladder that exists where the body has corners. Fontana chose a cube, and that choice is doing more work than the word does. The tray is the negative control, and it is on the bench deliberately - a synthesis that only showed the word working would have proved nothing.
dna.second_finding: The art station and the operator station are GEOMETRICALLY IDENTICAL at every value - same _carved_body call, same ratio, same 0.36 cube, same 28 x 18 sphere - and they do not look alike. What separates them is a white plinth against a slate board, fontana's matte cull-disabled red against the demo's 0.3-metallic emissive lavender, and two ghosts. Their two source artifacts have each written down, in their own registry notes, that they are 'the same cube-minus-sphere, one as art and one as demonstration'; this is the first object in which that sentence is a thing you can look at rather than a claim you have to take on trust. The exhibit's smallest and firmest result: the difference between an artwork and a demonstration is not in the object.
dna.declined:
`strike` - the family's most-shared word, carried character for character by all three CSG sources - is REFUSED, and the refusal is the design. The tray has no B to place. Two stations would answer identically, because they are the same geometry, and the third would be blank: one repeated answer and one null cell. That is [[sphere_splitting_showcase]]'s own reason for refusing `exploded` ('an axis that is a null cell for 60% of the bench is a finished-looking experiment about the 40%'), and it bites harder here, because a shared-word test is worth running only if the stations can DISAGREE. Under `breach` they do - two measured ratios and one bare order - and under `strike` they cannot.

`workings` is refused twice over. [[csg_compose_workbench]] already declined it on the ground that its sibling holds it, and that fence stands here too; worse, at workings=outcome the operator station would stop showing the operation and become a second art station, so one value of the axis would delete one of the three framings. A value that erases a station is an edit to the exhibit, not a turn of an axis.

`algebra` is refused because adding union and intersection would change the subject from what a cut IS to what the operator set is - that is the hub's question and the hub already holds it. `comparison` is refused because the tray always shows all five bases: it is one station of three, and subsetting it would make the catalogue argue with itself instead of with its neighbours.

AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS REFUSED. Making the tray's specimens CUBES would hand it fontana's three critical distances, and the word would transfer perfectly to all three stations. That is fitting the exhibit to the vocabulary. The catalogue's source is five ways to break a SPHERE; the sphere is why the word fails, and the failure is the finding.
dna.dialects: A synthesis that flattens its members into examples has thrown away what they learned, so every station renders the bench-wide value in its source's own dialect with its source's own literals. THE ART CUBE takes fontana's cube_color (0.70, 0.07, 0.07), its roughness 0.85, its CULL_DISABLED so the carved inner walls are visible through the face-mouths, its 28 x 18 sphere segmentation, its depth_color glint at emission energy 2.6, and that glint is sized at 0.06 of the body because fontana's centre point is 0.03 against its 0.5 cube. THE OPERATOR SOLID takes csg_difference_demo's body_color (0.70, 0.60, 0.95) with metallic 0.3, roughness 0.5 and emission at 0.3, and its two ghosts are built by that artifact's _ghost_material term for term - alpha on the albedo, alpha transparency, culling off, unshaded, emission 0.35 - at its own alphas, 0.16 for A and 0.22 for B, in its own CUT_COLOR (1.00, 0.55, 0.35). THE TRAY takes sphere_splitting_showcase's five bases in its shipped order, planar, octree, sectored, csg, segmented, and its own division counts: 8 octants, 8 sectors, and 6 latitude x 8 longitude for the segmented plate, which is 48 cells because that is the number its own info label prints.
dna.determinism: There is no seed because there is nothing random. No randf, no noise, no _process, no timers, no physics bodies, no Area3D, no player, no collision shapes at all. Every vertex in the tray is a trigonometric function of two integer cell indices, and both cube stations resolve through one _carved_body with one ratio, so the three stations cannot disagree about the depth of the cut by construction - which is a stronger guarantee than a shared seed.
dna.still_note: Everything this artifact argues is standing geometry, resolved during _ready and then still. The difference between two values is the presence, size and separation of solids in fixed places, which is exactly what survives a shutter. The one thing a still cannot carry is the thing that made the catalogue's source worth building - the moment of impact, the ball thrown, the sphere coming apart while you watch. None of that is here and none of it should be: every cut on this bench has already happened, and the exhibit is the aftermath held at four depths.
dna.fixture_why: Empty, and deliberately. _ready builds all three stations unconditionally with nothing gated on a player, a controller, an XR rig or a map, and there is no rate, no spin and no randomness for a fixture to pin - the two jobs a fixture normally does here do not exist. No typed bool is exposed to a token either, which is the trap that cost the prompter's box a pass: the axis is a String enum and station_pitch, body_size and specimen_radius are floats.
dna.framing_why: DERIVED, NOT MEASURED - captures are serialised centrally and none was run, so this is an arithmetic prediction and should be corrected by the first sweep. The union box across all four values is the bench's own furniture, 2.88 x 1.58 x 1.00 m: the axis adds nothing outside it, because the widest thing it can produce is B's ghost at 0.288 radius on the lectern and a tray plate at 0.135 radius inside a tray half-width of 0.46. Bounding radius 1.715 m, and the rig's distance is radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with PAD = 1.9, so at framing 1.0 the visible extent is about 6.5 m against a 2.88 m subject - 44 per cent of the width, and the bench is shallow, so most of the frame would be floor. 0.62 puts the visible extent near 4.0 m and the bench at about 71 per cent of it. If the first report comes back faint, the next move is a tighter framing rather than a bigger axis, and the ceiling is typographic: the three captions are billboarded Label3D at font 26, which the capture AABB cannot see, and they are the first thing that will clip.
dna.aabb_note: A layers = 0 BoxMesh sized to the bench's own furniture (2.88 x 1.58 x 1.00, sitting on the floor) is present, and it is doing two jobs. FIRST: the four CSG bodies are baked to MeshInstance3D on the next idle frame, but a live CSGShape3D is not a MeshInstance3D and the capture AABB counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D only - if a bake returns null on an early headless frame the carved solids would be invisible to the framing and the camera would fit the plinth and the tray alone. SECOND, and the reason it is there even when the bake succeeds: the furniture is IDENTICAL at all four values, so the anchor pins the camera across the sweep and no part of a bite report can be the camera moving. That is [[catapult]]'s recorded failure, where a collapsing preview mesh re-zoomed the tile and some of its measured bite was the zoom. The anchor does not overshoot: 1.58 m is the height of the captions, which are real visible content the AABB otherwise misses, and 2.88 x 1.00 is the base slab exactly.
dna.budget: About 85 MeshInstance3D at every value - 1 base, 3 at the plinth, 6 at the lectern, 74 at the tray (cabinet, tray, four rim strips, and 68 fragments: 2 hemispheres, 8 octants, 8 wedges, 48 tiles, 2 boolean parts), 1 anchor - plus 3 Label3D and about 6 bare Node3D. The count does not change with the axis. Roughly 3,400 triangles. No collision, no static bodies, nothing to grab: this bench is walked along and looked at, not handled. Two orders of magnitude under the ~3200 element budget.
dna.dark_spot: Named rather than hidden, because it is the substitution this exhibit could not avoid. The tray's five bases are REBUILT as static lat/lon partitions of a solid ball and one real boolean cut - they are not [[sphere_splitting_showcase]]'s destructibles. In the source, three of the five (planar, octree, csg) are ONE unbroken body until something hits them, and their parts are a calculation waiting on an event; that is the distinction its own `comparison` axis was built to draw, between a part that is computed and a part that was always there. Here every part exists from _ready, so the tray shows all five as latent. That is what makes a deterministic exploded view possible and it is exactly what the source refused to fake, for the right reason. So: this station is a CATALOGUE PLATE of the five bases, not a bench of five destructibles, and anyone who wants the computed/latent distinction has to go and stand in front of the source. The second dark spot is the ordinary one for this whole pass: nothing here can be cut by a player, and the four sources all stay placed.
dna.known_gap: No map places this yet, and the corpus's standing warning applies with extra force: exactly one map anywhere (Artist_Readymades) places any artifact at a non-default axis value. A bench whose entire point is holding three framings at ONE depth of cut is worth little until somebody writes subtraction_suite#breach:severed into a map and walks the row - `severed` is the value where the argument is sharpest, because the plinth's cube becomes eight disconnected corner pieces and the tray's plates do not change state at all.

dna.default: separation=coincident is a SHORT-CIRCUIT, not a recomputation. _faces() returns the face_x export UNTOUCHED at that value, and face_x's own default is the shipped pair (0.02, -0.02), so A's right face and B's left face are the literals that shipped rather than numbers a formula lands back on. Everything downstream follows from them unchanged: the band still runs b_min.x to a_max.x at 26 slivers of sw*0.9 alternating amber then blue, _b_depth() returns 0.0 so every z is the old z plus zero, and the verdict tag and the plaque body are the fallthrough arms of their match blocks, character for character. inverted takes that same fallthrough on purpose - it keeps the shipped bounds exactly and settles the contest in z instead. ZERO PLACEMENTS, and that is the honest headline: this token appears in no map_data.json anywhere in the corpus - not bare, not through exhibit_furniture, not through curation_station. Every reference to it is a reader, not a placer: tools/build_seams_gallery.py (the boolean_surfaces row of the seam table), commons/data/artifact_relations.json (three times, each 'same category and sequence' with placements_together 0), commons/artifacts/dressing_rooms/coincident_face.json (rotations, approach, footprint, clearance, footing, artifact_offset - not one key this build reads), doc/auto_research_inventory and doc/book/text_mentions. So there is nothing to preserve except the seams gallery's rendering, and the short-circuit exists for that and for honesty rather than for a placement count. A placement that names face_x directly still wins over separation.
dna.was: no declared axis, and one asserted state. The artifact's headline is that the exact boundary is a coin toss per pixel, and it had only ever drawn the coin toss - no reading of the same diagram with the boundary uncontested, so nothing in the picture could say whether the flicker is a property of Booleans or of one particular pair of numbers. Only color_a and color_b were exports. The rect bounds, the band bounds and the 26-sliver count were literals inside _ready, so there was nothing for an axis to resolve against and the promotion had to LIFT BEFORE IT COULD DERIVE - the same first move csg_compose_workbench made when its operand pair turned out to be three literals inside _build_presets. And apply_grid_config stamped set_meta('config_<k>') for every key it was handed and had NO READER ANYWHERE: the metadata was written and never consulted. That is one step worse than the sibling's knob-without-a-rebuild - it was a knob without a wire - so this promotion needed _read_metadata_overrides, the signature compare and the early return, all three.
dna.note: separation is THE GAP BETWEEN THE TWO FACES, IN UNITS OF THE FLOAT GRID, and what it argues is THAT EXACTNESS HAS A GRAIN SIZE AND THAT CROSSING IT IS TOTAL. clear: a_max.x -0.04 against b_min.x +0.04, a visible 0.08 gap, no shared face, no contest - the exact boundary CSG actually promises, and the control this diagram has never had. hairline: an 0.008 gap, the two solids all but touching and the depth order still decided cleanly, a thin dark seam and no band - the rung that turns the claim into a claim about SIZE. coincident: SHIPPED, a_max.x 0.02 and b_min.x -0.02 with the 0.04 band of 26 alternating slivers standing in the overlap. inverted: the shipped bounds with B advanced 0.004 toward the viewer, so the band goes solid blue - one step of the grid, and the answer does not degrade, it flips entirely. The ladder is deliberately NOT monotone: the failure sits in the middle of it, with order on both sides. ON THE DECLARED ORDER, since the two disagree and the disagreement is not a mistake: the @export_enum is written clear, hairline, coincident, inverted, which is the ladder as argued; the declaration above puts coincident first because apply_dna_block.py moves the export default to the leftmost tile so a sweep reads the shipped lineage first. Same four values, and the code is the thing that renders. The verdict line under the diagram and the plaque body follow the rung, because this artifact's text is half its ink and a still that kept 'z-fight: the shared face flickers' over a clean cut would be lying. THE WORD IS NEW. Nothing in the corpus asks what distance an exact answer needs in order to stay exact. The two nearest words are taken and mean something else: seam on escher_staircase and florensky_sphere (none|hairline|gap|scaffold|field) names the joint of an impossible object, and grain on six artifacts names how a solid is divided. This is the boolean_surfaces station of the bias landscape and its charge is 'bias is conserved; show the seam' - separation shows the bias is not in the flicker, it is in the threshold that decides whether there is one.
dna.declined: tiebreak (stripes | blotch | split | toss) - HOW the contest is decided, pixel by pixel - is this artifact's own headline turned into an axis, is deterministic once seeded, and its four rungs are four real policies: the shipped alternation; the seeded blotching a real coincident face actually shows; a clean rule awarding left to A and right to B, which abolishes the flicker and relocates the arbitrariness into the rule, the seam family's whole thesis; and the literal per-sliver coin toss. It is REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC. Every rung changes only the band - 0.04 x 0.40 m of an 0.86 x 0.66 m plate, 2.8 per cent of the subject face and under 2 per cent of frame even at framing 0.55 - so the critic's hottest-5-per-cent window would be more than half unchanged pixels and the verdict would be a fact about the band's width. It becomes shippable the moment the plate is redrawn at a wider band, and redrawing the plate changes the shipped picture: a decision to take on its own, not to smuggle in under a promotion. Also declined: evidence (result|trace|longhand|axiom, 45 artifacts). There is no derivation here to show more or less of - this artifact does not compute an answer, it exhibits a place where the answer does not exist.
dna.fixture_why: NO FIXTURE, and the absence is checkable rather than claimed: there is not one call to randf, randi or randomize in the file, no _process, no _physics_process and nothing that reads time. Everything the axis and the default build is static emissive geometry resolved synchronously in _ready, so one frame is the whole account and a capture's settle cannot photograph this artifact half-way through anything. The seeded rungs that would have needed a seed export live in the declined tiebreak axis, not in what is shipped. _ready is ungated and builds standalone, so no dna.fixture is needed to make it render either. Label3D text is non-billboard throughout, so no plates are added and the capture AABB is the mesh extent. What IS required, and is not a pin, is dna.framing - see framing_note.
dna.framing_note: ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE, and it is the documented wide-flat-subject trap in its purest form. The MeshInstance3D AABB is 0.86 x 0.798 x 0.031: x from the backing slab, y from the backing's bottom edge at -0.31 up to the plaque's accent strip at 0.488, z only the three centimetres of stacked slabs. Diagonal 1.174, radius 0.587, and that diagonal is set almost entirely by a subject which is effectively 2D. capture_config_sweep fits by the diagonal (radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, RES 760), which at framing 1.0 puts the camera 3.65 m out where the visible frame is 2.23 m across; at the sweep's yaw 0.62 and pitch -0.26 the plate face foreshortens to 0.787 of its area and projects to about 11 per cent of frame. 0.55 brings the camera to 2.01 m and the frame to 1.23 m, and the plate face to about 36 per cent of frame - clear of the ~6 per cent dilution floor, with the whole 0.86 x 0.80 body still inside the frame. 0.45 was considered and refused: it would leave under 0.2 m of margin on a 0.80 m subject whose plaque sits at the very top of its own AABB. The AABB does not move between rungs (both rectangles stay inside the backing at every value, and inverted's z step is 4 mm), so all four variants are framed identically and no part of the measured difference is a camera moving.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config still stamps every config key into metadata exactly as before, then re-reads the four keys it understands (separation, face_x, color_a, color_b), and returns early unless a value the build actually reads has changed - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. The old body had no rebuild AND no reader, so this is the first version in which that metadata means anything. The teardown frees get_children() and nothing else, which is safe here because every child of this node is made by this script: the .tscn is a bare Node3D root carrying the script, with no children of its own. Zero placements pass any key, so the guard means none of them is even torn down; and because the sweep sets @export properties directly rather than calling apply_grid_config, the sweep path never enters the guard at all. ONE HONEST CONSEQUENCE of wiring the metadata up: color_a and color_b were always exports and were always stamped, and were always ignored - a placement passing either of them would now get the colour it asked for where before it got the default. That is a behaviour change, and it is safe here only because the placement count is zero and the dressing room passes rotations, approach, exit, footprint, clearance, extras, posture, footing and artifact_offset, not one of which this build reads.
dna.still_note: BITE PREDICTION, stated up front so a thin number is read correctly rather than filed as inert. Between rungs both rectangles move, all four outlines redraw, the band appears, vanishes or goes solid, and two text elements change (the verdict line under the diagram, and two of the plaque's three body lines). The pairs that set clear or hairline against coincident should bite hard: the band is 0.04 x 0.40 m of an 0.86 x 0.66 m face going from bright emissive to bare dark backing, and two vertical outlines move 0.06 m. THE PAIR AT RISK IS coincident AGAINST inverted, and it is named here rather than discovered in the verdict. That pair changes only the band's colour and the text, and the two colours are near-isoluminant: amber (1.0, 0.62, 0.18) has a Rec.709 luma of 0.669 and blue (0.3, 0.7, 1.0) of 0.637, so an alternating band and a solid blue band differ by roughly four grey levels in the luminance the verdict is measured in. Per channel the same change is enormous - red goes from a blended ~166 to 76 across the band - which is exactly the case focus_rgb exists to veto, so if that pair falls under TWIN_FOCUS it should surface in the critic's COLOUR-ONLY list and not as a twin. Read it there before concluding the rung is decoration. ONE THING THAT WILL NOT PHOTOGRAPH AS DRAWN, said so it is not mistaken for a fault: at RES 760 and framing 0.55 the frame is 1.6 mm per pixel and a sliver is 1.4 mm wide before foreshortening, so the 26 slivers are sub-pixel and the band renders as a blended amber-blue stripe rather than 26 countable bars. That is what z-fighting looks like, but nobody should expect to count slivers in the tile. If the axis comes back faint, crop-recheck before redesigning: this is random_walk_collection's pathology, a large change over a small area, not an inert axis.

coincident_face.description: The boolean-surfaces seam. CSG promises exact cuts; subtract one solid from another and the boundary is a clean surface. But when the cut plane lands on a coincident face, the two surfaces claim the same depth and the float grid cannot say which is in front - so the renderer flickers, awarding each pixel to whichever number rounded higher this frame. The clean boolean is exact everywhere except the one place you asked it to be.
coincident_face.name: Coincident Face
coincident_face.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for boolean_surfaces. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

removal_room.name: Removal Room
removal_room.description: A synthesis shell, 5.35 m of it: three registers standing on one plinth, each holding the SAME single subtraction under a different account of what the cut left. gone is the survivors and nothing where the rule cut, which is what all six members of the `removal` family ship and the only account the mathematics endorses. ghost restores every removed cell as a pale full-size volume at alpha 0.16, so the operation becomes legible and the object becomes a lie about its own definition - at three of the four cuts the ghost register is exactly the original solid again. scar keeps neither the part nor its absence but a dark core at 0.22 of the cell where the cell used to be: a fact about the cutting rather than about either state. The cut underneath all three is computed once at build time and read three ways. Nothing here moves, nothing here is random, and the artifact has no per-frame code at all.
interactions: read the row left to right - gone, ghost, scar - and notice none of the three is the honest one
compare the same cut under three accounts of its own remainder
switch the cut and watch which account changes and which does not
removal_room.capacity: SEE that a subtraction has no preferred record: drawing nothing is true about the set and loses the operation, drawing the offcut recovers the operation and denies the definition, and drawing the wound keeps neither state
removal_room.qfep_connection: F is the cut: one rule, evaluated once in _run(), identical in all three registers, which is why the row is a comparison and not three drawings. E is the three accounts, and they are irreducible to each other - a ghost cannot be recovered from a scar and neither can be recovered from an empty cell, which is why the family needed a word for the choice at all. lambda is how much of what was removed the record is willing to carry. The dark spot is `gone`: it is the value every one of the six members ships, it is the value that looks like no decision at all, and it is the one that makes the operation unrecoverable from the object.
removal_room.relationships:
Synthesised out of the six artifacts that declare a `removal` axis - [[cantor_set]], [[example_8_4_cantor_set_vr]], [[fractal_cantor_set]], [[menger_sponge]], [[recursive_chair]], [[test_scene_3]] - every one of which is a fractal of subtraction, and one artifact from the family's border.

THE EXACT COMPLEMENT OF [[retention_corridor]]. That corridor asks what a MARK KEEPS and holds five values of `retention` standing at once while varying the pass underneath them; this room asks what a CUT LEAVES and holds three values of `removal` standing at once while varying the cut underneath them. The two artifacts are built to the same rule and refuse their family's word for the same reason - see dna.kin - and between them they cover the two halves of one question: what a system does with what it wrote, and what a system does with what it threw away.

[[cantor_set]] is the ORIGIN of the vocabulary (promoted 2026-08-03) and owns the value list. Its REMOVALS const is PRELOADED by this room rather than retyped, so the two cannot drift; if that const changes or disappears this file fails at parse time. Its `third` rule is drawn here line for line - offset = L/3, new_length = L/3, one row per level, the removed middle drawn at the CHILD's level index and not the parent's - which is why `third` is the only value whose register is a history rather than a state.

[[menger_sponge]] contributes `cross` and the precondition the whole family runs on: its 27 sub-cubes partition the parent exactly, so the complement is a real set and can be drawn at all. Its keep_positions table is read here as its complement, {4,10,12,13,14,16,22}, so the seven deleted cells are stated once rather than inferred from twenty.

[[recursive_chair]] contributes `figure` and is the one member of a family of fractals whose subtraction does NOT recurse: 27 cells, 11 deleted, once, and what is left is a named object. Its own truth line - the chair was always inside the cube, subdivision merely removed what was not chair - is the reason this room can hold a non-fractal value without leaving the family.

[[sierpinski_triangle]] is NOT a member and is declared as an import. It asks this family's exact question under a rival word - `excision`, five values, absence | ghost | rubble | cast | negative - and its medial triangle is a real disjoint complement, so `gasket` puts the two vocabularies against one cut instead of leaving them in two registries.

[[sierpinski_pyramid]] REFUSED `removal` on the record, because its five children's bounding volumes interpenetrate and there is no complement to draw. It is deliberately NOT a value here: at that cut ghost and scar would have nothing to draw and the register row would collapse to three copies of `gone`.

[[evidence_ladder]] is not a source and is quoted anyway, for its construction rule: one copy of the arithmetic, evaluated once, read N ways. _run() fills four arrays and all three registers read them; nothing on this shell re-derives a cut.

spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 5.41 m, h 1.64 m, registry.measurements)

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - the shell is boxes at known constants, so this AABB is arithmetic over SHELL_W + 2*CORNICE_OVER, the cornice head at SILL_Y+PANEL_H+LINTEL_H+CORNICE_H, and z from the cornice back (-0.645) to the plinth and CELL front (+0.50). NOT a Godot measurement pass; re-measure when one is run.

dna.default: subtraction=cross. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is no preservation duty and the default is a free design choice; it was used to pick the STRONGEST single reading rather than the emptiest. `cross` is menger_sponge's cut, and it is the one value at which all three accounts are simultaneously at full strength: the 27 cells partition the parent exactly, so gone is a solid with seven holes in it, ghost is the ORIGINAL CUBE restored to the byte, and scar is seven dark cores standing in the air inside a lattice. `third` is stronger as an argument and weaker as a photograph - a Cantor ladder is mostly empty panel - and `gasket` is an import rather than a member, which is the wrong thing to lead with. The DECLARED ORDER is cross, third, gasket, figure, because build_dna_gallery trims value lists from the TAIL: the default goes first and the rest run in descending separation from it, so a capped run drops the pair that is closest together rather than the pair that is furthest apart.
dna.was: nothing. This artifact did not exist before this pass. It is the cross-member comparison that six registry notes each described from inside one value of it, built as a body. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of every registry file returns exactly 6 entries declaring `removal`, all six with the identical value list [gone, ghost, scar].
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE ROOM MAKES, and no member can make it. Each of the six stands in ONE account and forgoes the other two, and none of them has ever had to say that it was choosing. Held side by side the three accounts are not a scale and not an ordering: `gone` is the only one the mathematics endorses and it destroys the operation, because a cell that was never made cannot be told from a cell that was never in the rule. `ghost` recovers the operation completely and is a lie about the object's own definition - at `cross`, `gasket` and `figure` the ghost register is EXACTLY the original solid, which is to say the picture of a Menger sponge with its removals marked is a picture of a cube. `scar` keeps neither state: it is the only account that is about the CUTTING, and it is the only one that would still be legible if you did not already know the rule. Legibility peaks at scar, fidelity peaks at gone, and recoverability peaks at ghost, and they are three different registers.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THAT THE FAMILY HAS TWO SCAR IMPLEMENTATIONS AND NOBODY HAS SAID SO. cantor_set and example_8_4_cantor_set_vr thin the SECTION and keep the removed part's LENGTH - box.size = Vector3(seg.y, thin, thin) - so the wound has the extent of the thing that went. menger_sponge and recursive_chair take 0.22 in all three dimensions - box.size = Vector3(thin, thin, thin) - so their wound loses the extent too. Both were copied 'value for value' from the same origin, both registries say so, and they are not the same rule: one draws where the part was and how big it was, the other draws only where. Each cut in this room gets the one its own member wrote, and the room is the first place the two have stood next to each other.

ONE CUT, EVALUATED ONCE. _run() fills _keep_p/_keep_s and _cut_p/_cut_s at build time and all three registers read those four arrays; the ghost register scales nothing and the scar register applies _scar_size to the same _cut_s. Nothing re-derives a cut, so no register can drift out of agreement with another.

THE GROUND IS COMPUTED RATHER THAN PICKED, and it is the one thing this room can do for the family without touching the family's recipes. The ghost mark is unshaded pale, Rec.709 luminance 0.881524, at alpha 0.16; the scar mark is matte dark at 0.091444. Against a ground of luminance g the ghost composites to 0.16*0.881524 + 0.84g, so the two marks are equidistant from their ground when 0.1410438 - 0.16g = g - 0.091444, i.e. g = 0.2004205 with |delta| = 0.1089765 either way. Every member so far has drawn both marks against whatever darkness its host map happened to supply, and dark grounds favour the pale mark by a factor that nobody has measured. C_GROUND is that grey, and all three registers get it, because giving each account the ground that suits it would have destroyed the comparison.
dna.kin:
`removal` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the ruling is retention_corridor's. All six members use the word to stand in ONE account and forgo the other two; on this shell all three stand at once and that simultaneity IS the object. An axis whose every value demolishes two thirds of the exhibit is not a variation of it. The word is EXHIBITED instead - it names the artifact, it is engraved on the plinth under each register, and the value list is PRELOADED out of cantor_set.gd rather than retyped so the room cannot drift from the family it is about.

LAW 2 - NEST OR SIDE BY SIDE, answered from the members' CODE and not their prose. By EXTENT the three values NEST: cantor_set._spawn_removed draws nothing, then a box at 0.22 of the section, then a box at 1.0 of it, so the drawn set is empty, subset of scar, subset of ghost, and a scar cube is 0.22^3 = 1.065% of its own ghost's volume. By MATERIAL and by CLAIM they are PARALLEL: ghost is Color(0.86,0.88,0.96,0.16) unshaded with TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA and scar is Color(0.09,0.09,0.11) matte and opaque, and one says 'the part was here, this big' while the other says 'somebody cut here'. The case is therefore MIXED, and it decided the shape of the room: because ghost passes 84% of what is behind it, an all-at-once frame would show ghost's translucent shell WITH scar's dark core inside it and read as a single fourth value - three claims collapsed into one object. Side by side is the only arrangement in which the three stay three.

`subtraction` IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN WORD and no sibling declares it (checked across every registry file). Its VALUE LIST is the family's own census of cuts plus one import, derived and not invented: `third` is cantor_set, example_8_4_cantor_set_vr and its two aliases fractal_cantor_set and test_scene_3 - four of the six tokens; `cross` is menger_sponge; `figure` is recursive_chair; 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 and the list partitions the members exactly. `gasket` is sierpinski_triangle and is named as an IMPORT rather than smuggled in as a member, because that artifact answers this family's question under a rival word (`excision`: absence | ghost | rubble | cast | negative) and the room exists to hold the two vocabularies against one cut.

`tick` IS REFUSED AS A SECOND AXIS, and the arithmetic is the reason rather than taste - see dna.declines.
dna.declines:
`tick` REFUSED, and it was the obvious second axis: it is the family's own word (cantor_set, menger_sponge, example_8_4_cantor_set_vr and the two aliases all declare it) and depth is what a fractal of subtraction has. Two facts kill it.

FIRST, TWO OF THE FOUR VALUES CANNOT TAKE A RUNG. `figure` is recursive_chair, which subdivides ONCE and then deforms; three rungs there would be three byte-identical frames, which is the example_8_4 fault - rungs that exist in the enum and cannot be built. And `gasket` is an import whose own ladder belongs to a different word.

SECOND, THE ROOM CANNOT AFFORD THE RUNGS IT COULD BUILD, and the number is scale-free. Three non-overlapping registers make the shell about 5.4 cells wide whatever the cell is (see framing_why), so a cell is always about a fifth of the frame and at dna.framing 0.55 that is 126.09 px per metre. A Menger scar at rung 2 is 0.22 * CELL/9 = 0.024444 m = 3.08 px, inside the 1-3 px band law 4 exists because of, and no tightening of the framing moves it because tightening moves the whole shell with it. Rung 3 of `gasket` is 3.47 x 3.00 px for the same reason. Depth is therefore a CONSTANT chosen per value by the pixel width of that value's finest scar, recorded in the LEVELS table in the script with the number that fixed each one.

THIS IS A REAL COST AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE: menger_sponge ships max_iterations 2, and this room draws its cut at rung 1. `once` is a rung menger_sponge itself declares, so the room takes the family's ladder honestly rather than inventing a level - but the room is a WEAKER picture of a Menger sponge than menger_sponge is, and the reason is that it is photographing three of them.

THE SCAR MATERIAL IS LEFT LIT, on purpose, and this is the one asymmetry the room reports instead of fixing. Making it unshaded would pin it at luminance 0.091444 and make the computed-ground arithmetic exact under any light; it would also break the one property that keeps the six members photographing alike, since every one of them ships a lit scar and an unshaded ghost. The room reports the asymmetry rather than editing the family's recipe.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and this is worth stating rather than leaving blank. Both cantor_set and menger_sponge and recursive_chair needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before any axis of theirs was visible at all, because all three grow on a clock and a still at the harness's settle catches one falling bar or a half-built chair. This room has no clock, no RigidBody3D, no _process, no timer and no randf: _ready lays the finished row out in one frame and it never moves again. Nothing needs to be supplied.
dna.still_note:
READ THE Z-STACK BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER OFF THIS SHEET, because four separate things in this room were standing in front of marks and all four were found by arithmetic before any capture. The sweep camera stands at yaw 0.62, so with cy = cos(0.62) = 0.813878 and sy = sin(0.62) = 0.581039 a point lands at screen-x = cy*x - sy*z, and a thing of depth d eats sy*d of horizontal daylight while a gap of width g projects to only cy*g.

(1) THE REGISTERS WERE STANDING IN EACH OTHER'S LIGHT, and this rebuilt the shell. A CELL cube projects cy*CELL + sy*CELL = 1.394917 m of screen width. At the first PITCH of 1.14 the register centres were cy*1.14 = 0.927821 m apart, so consecutive cubes OVERLAPPED by 0.467096 m - 33.5% of a register's screen width. Of the middle register's 1 m2 footprint the part hidden by its right-hand neighbour is the triangle {screen-x >= 0.230396}, area 0.230650 m2 = 23.1%, including 70% of its right-hand face. Rasterised at the sweep's own 760 px the three cubes merged into ONE CONTINUOUS BLOCK and the row stopped being a row - and note what that would have looked like on the sheet: a large subject, four legible frames, and a perfectly respectable bite number, because the fault is identical at every value of the axis. PITCH must be at least 1.394917/cy = 1.714 * CELL; it is 1.75 * CELL, which leaves 0.029370 m = 3.70 px of daylight between registers and zero occlusion.

(2) THE PILASTERS. A 0.10 m fin standing 0.93 m deep casts a screen silhouette sy*0.93 + cy*0.10 = 0.621 m wide, six times its own thickness. With its front face at +0.30 that silhouette began at screen-x 0.248906 while a FLAT register's marks reach cy*0.5 = 0.406939, so the right 0.158033 m - 19.4% of the width of `third` and of `gasket` - stood behind a pilaster. FIN_FRONT is now -0.30 and the silhouette begins at 0.845690, clear of even the DEEP registers' 0.697459.

(3) THE LINTEL. The ray from a register's top-back corner (y 1.40, z -0.5) to the camera rises 0.25708/0.78652 = 0.326857 in y per unit z, crossing the soffit at y 1.50 when z = -0.194 and the head at y 1.60 when z = +0.112. With the lintel front at +0.30 that whole interval lay inside it: a wedge 0.1664 m deep at the back plane, 0.040800 m2 = 4.1% of a register's side profile. The lintel and cornice now stop at -0.30 with the fins, where the ray is 34.6 mm under the soffit as it leaves them.

(4) THE GROUND PANEL DOES NOT REACH THE LEFT END, and this one is REPORTED rather than fixed. The wall sits 0.605 m behind the marks, which shifts its silhouette sy*0.605 = 0.351529 m to screen-right, so its left edge lands at screen-x -1.825600 while the leftmost marks reach -2.121750. The unbacked wedge is 0.092733 m2 = 9.3% of that register's footprint at the two DEEP values and 0.7 px at the two flat ones. Closing it needs 0.432 m of extra wall on the LEFT ONLY, which is a camera-shaped shell and not a shell. It is tolerable because of WHERE it falls: the leftmost register is `gone`, the one account that draws neither a ghost nor a scar, so the computed ground - which exists to hold a pale mark and a dark one at equal distance - is untouched by it. The middle and right registers are backed edge to edge.

WHAT TO EXPECT ON THE SHEET. Subject share, rasterised: 26.08% (cross), 25.41% (third), 25.27% (gasket), 25.61% (figure) - comfortably over the ~6% floor, and the union subject box is 38.5% of frame area, so this is a WIDE subject in a square frame and not a small one. Instance counts are trivial: 20/7 cells at cross, 7/3 bars at third, 9/4 triangles at gasket, 16/11 cells at figure, drawn as five MultiMeshes per register set. Nothing here can trip the 16 s watchdog.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS EVERY VALUE OF THE AXIS, which for this artifact is the SHELL, because the shell is identical at all four values and encloses every register. Union box 5.41 x 1.64 x 1.145: x is SHELL_W + 2*CORNICE_OVER = 3*1.75 + 0.10 + 0.06; y runs 0 to SILL_Y+PANEL_H+LINTEL_H+CORNICE_H = 1.64; z runs from the cornice back at -0.645 to the plinth and CELL front at +0.50. Diagonal 5.767904, radius 2.883952.

THE RIG: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, dist = radius/tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 2.883952/0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.55 = 9.857241 m, so the visible frame is 2*PAD*radius*framing = 6.027450 m and a 760 px still is 126.0899 px per metre.

WHY 0.55 AND NOT 1.0: fit-by-DIAGONAL on a 5.41 x 1.64 body wastes most of a square frame. At yaw 0.62 the projected width is 5.41*cos(0.62) + 1.145*sin(0.62) = 4.403080 + 0.665290 = 5.068370 m, which is 84.1% of the 6.027450 m frame; the projected height is 2.632 m, 43.7% of it. Below about 0.50 the cornice starts to reach the frame edge.

EVERY MARK WAS GAUGED AGAINST 126.09 px/m BEFORE THE LEVELS WERE CHOSEN (law 4): cross scar 0.22*CELL/3 = 0.073333 m = 9.25 px; figure the same; gasket scar 0.22*0.25 = 0.055000 m = 6.93 px wide and 6.01 px tall; third scar 0.22*CANTOR_SEC_Y = 0.035200 m = 4.44 px, the thinnest mark in the room. The rungs that were REFUSED on this arithmetic are in dna.declines.

AND THE IN-REGISTER DAYLIGHT, because a gap that closes is the same fault as a mark that vanishes: `third` at two levels has a finest gap of CELL/9 = 0.111111 m projecting to 0.090431 m, against which a 0.06 deep section eats 0.034862 m and leaves 0.055569 m = 7.01 px - and cantor_set's own SQUARE 0.16 section would have eaten 0.092966 m and closed it completely, which is why the section here is anisotropic. `gasket` at two levels has a finest hole 0.25 wide projecting to 0.203470 m, against which sierpinski_triangle's own 0.14 extrusion would eat 0.081346 m; flat at 0.05 it eats 0.029052 m and leaves 0.174418 m = 21.99 px. `cross` at one level shows a face-centre recess 0.333333 wide projecting to 0.271293 m against a neighbouring cell eating 0.193680 m: 0.077613 m = 9.79 px still open.
dna.measured: PREDICTION SCORED, AND IT WAS THE WEAKEST OF THE FOUR IN THIS WAVE. Swept 2026-08-13, four frames, closest pair 5.86%. The registry predicted `cross` against `figure` as the closest at 1.1% of frame; measured, that pair is SECOND at 7.24% and the floor is `gasket` against `third` at 5.86% — which the prediction had ranked second, at 1.82%. So the two closest pairs were identified as a SET and their order swapped. The absolute numbers were low by about 6.5x, not the 1.5x the note allowed for, and the reason is stated there in advance: the Python rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading and no shadows, AO or antialiasing, so it systematically under-reports what a real render separates. The RANK was the claim and the rank was off by one place. Recorded because a prediction is only worth keeping if its misses are scored as plainly as its hits. Full order: gasket-third 5.86, cross-figure 7.24, figure-third 13.23, figure-gasket 13.63, cross-third 13.90, cross-gasket 14.01.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: `cross` against `figure`, at 15.7% focus and 1.1% frame. Both numbers are rasterised, not guessed - the four values were built in Python from the same constants the script uses, projected through the sweep's own camera at 760 px, and then put through artifact_dna_critic's exact currency: crop to the union subject box, neutralise each frame's own corner background, greyscale, resize 160x160, mean of |a-b| over the hottest 5%.

THE ARITHMETIC FOR WHY IT IS THAT PAIR. cross and figure are the same 1 m cube on the same 3x3x3 lattice at the same rung. cross deletes {4,10,12,13,14,16,22} and keeps 20; figure deletes {1,9,10,11,15,16,17,19,24,25,26} and keeps 16. They agree on 11 kept cells and on 2 deleted cells, so 13 of 27 cells - 48.1% - are drawn identically in every one of the three registers, and the GHOST register has the identical outer silhouette at both values, because 20+7 and 16+11 are both the whole cube. A third of the frame therefore differs only in the tan/pale distribution inside one unchanged outline. No other pair shares a lattice at all: `third` is 1D bars in rows and `gasket` is triangles.

FULL PREDICTED TABLE (frame / focus): cross-figure 1.08 / 15.67, third-gasket 1.82 / 22.63, cross-gasket 4.91 / 22.76, cross-third 4.49 / 22.84, gasket-figure 4.46 / 22.95, third-figure 4.36 / 23.37.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE PREDICTION AND WHAT IT WOULD MEAN. The rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading, no shadows, no ambient occlusion and no antialiasing, so the absolute numbers should not be trusted to better than a factor of about 1.5; the RANK is the claim. If the sweep returns cross-figure well ABOVE 15% while some other pair lands below it, the lattice argument is wrong somewhere and the cut functions should be diffed cell by cell. If any pair comes back under 3%, the room is not drawing what this entry says it draws - and the first thing to check is not the axis but the Z-STACK in still_note, because every one of the four faults listed there produced a picture that looked finished.

dna.default: graph=cube - `cube` is the `_` branch of connections_for and returns the twelve-pair literal that was welded into create_graph, in the same order, so the same twelve CSGCylinder3D edges are built between the same node ids. Every other constant is untouched: node_count 8, spring_length 2.0, spring_strength 0.1, repulsion_strength 50.0, damping 0.9, the 10.0 velocity clamp and the 6.0 position bound. layout_seed defaults to 0, and at 0 create_graph issues the same two global randf() calls per node in the same order, so the shipped jitter is bit-identical and two layouts in one room still start differently. warmup_steps defaults to 0, so _ready is the shipped two calls and the graph still starts tangled on its ring and untangles while you watch. time_scale defaults to 1.0, at which dt IS delta and _process is the shipped body. All 9 placements pass no config key - the richest token in the corpus is `force_directed_layout:0:0:0.6` in GT_Layout, which is rotation and y-offset, not config - so the rebuild branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists, and it additionally refuses to fire before the tree is built.
dna.was: no exports at all. Eight plain `var`s, twelve hard-coded connections, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass`. The runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS and it was the literal truth. WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY: this entry's own `interactions` list still tells a reader to 'tune spring_strength and repulsion_strength in exports' and to 'change node_count to alter density'. Those exports have never existed. The claim was false when it was written and it is false now; only `graph` and the three bench knobs are settable, and that is what this block declares.
dna.note: graph is WHICH GRAPH THE SAME FORCE LAW IS ASKED TO DRAW. The description promises that 'clusters, bridges, and peripheral nodes appear as energy redistributes' - a claim about GRAPHS that a single welded adjacency could never test, because with one graph there is nothing for the layout to be a property OF. Every value keeps eight nodes and the identical springs, repulsion, damping and bounds; only the adjacency changes. cube is the shipped twelve pairs, which are the 3-cube Q3: two 4-cycles joined by four rungs, 3-regular and vertex-transitive. ring is C8, eight edges, every node the same degree and no hierarchy anywhere. star is K1,7, a tree, one hub of degree 7 against seven leaves of degree 1 - maximal hierarchy, and the only value with a node that nothing pushes out of the middle. clique is K8, all 28 edges, where there is nothing to reveal because everything is adjacent to everything, and the springs pull it into the tightest blob of the five. bipartite is K4,4, sixteen edges, every one crossing between two classes and none inside either, so the drawing contains no odd cycle at all.
dna.kin: IT IS NOT grid3d_force_directed, and the two must not be read as one family. That token was declined on 2026-08-05 in grid3d.json after considering graph = random|tree|ring|clique|lattice, and its own decline note says so: it runs commons/substrates/grid3d/grid3d_substrate.tscn through cartridge_force_directed.gd, a scene shared by nine tokens, and shares no line with this script. Its blocker does not apply here and the difference is the reason. That force law has NO bounding term, so equilibrium SIZE is set by edge count - the very thing the axis turns - and the dense values photograph as dots inside the sparse ones' frame. This one clamps every position to a 6.0 box in update_positions, and its .tscn additionally carries two fixed indicators at x = -8 and x = +8. So the extent is 12 x 12 at EVERY value (measured: all five settle against the clamp by 240 steps) and the frame is set by furniture that does not move. The union camera is identical for all five here, which is exactly what it could not be there.
dna.still_note: MEASURED by re-implementing the integrator and the harness camera in Python at the rig's real numbers, then rasterising node spheres and edge cylinders. At warmup 480 and framing 5.5: subject 4.67% of frame, peak pairwise 5.39% (clique vs bipartite), weakest pair 2.21% (ring vs star) - every pair over the 2.0% bite threshold. THE FRAMING NUMBER IS LOAD-BEARING AND FRAGILE, and here is why. This artifact is built ENTIRELY from CSG - CSGSphere3D nodes, CSGCylinder3D edges, CSGBox3D indicators - and capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D only. It therefore measures NOTHING and falls back to its 1 m default box, which puts the camera 5.4 m from a 17 m object and photographs a 3.3 m window on it. framing 5.5 is calibrated against that fallback box, not against the artifact: it puts the camera at 29.6 m for a 18.1 m frame, and the furthest projected point of any of the five layouts lands at 328 px of the 380 px half-frame. IF ANY MeshInstance3D IS EVER ADDED TO THIS SCENE the fallback stops firing and this number becomes wrong by a factor of eleven. The obvious alternative - a layers=0 anchor sized to the real extent, which is what the brief recommends for this class - was measured and REJECTED: _auto_ground_artifact walks CSGShape3D too, the current min_y of about -4.2 sits just inside its 5.0 m correction cap, and an anchor spanning the true -6.3 would push it over the cap and stop three live placements being lifted at all. The fix for the bench would have been a regression in the maps. THE FIXTURE IS THE REST. warmup_steps=480 runs the shipped integrator at a fixed 1/60 delta so the still is not a fact about frame rate, time_scale=0.0 parks it there, layout_seed=1 pins the starting jitter. relax() deliberately skips update_visuals inside its loop, because every CSG property write rebuilds that shape's mesh.
dna.declines: `path` (P8) was implemented, measured and dropped. It is C8 minus one edge, and under this force law - where 50/d^2 repulsion overwhelms 0.1*(d-2) springs until every node is pressed against the 6.0 clamp - the two settle to layouts 0.31% of frame apart, against a 2.0% threshold. A duplicate tile, and the measurement is why it is not in the list. `stress` - what a node's appearance claims, size|none|heat|degree - was designed and refused on arithmetic. update_visuals scales each node by 1 + min(force * 0.1, 0.5), and at 480 steps the mean residual force is 0.7-2.4, so the scale sits at 1.07-1.24: a 20% radius change on eight small discs that are perhaps a third of a 4.67% subject, which lands near 0.5% of frame. It would ship and return a verdict about the bench. spring_strength, repulsion_strength, damping and spring_length stay plain untyped vars: they set how HARD the same drawing is pulled, and turning them is a dial on one picture. node_count is a density knob and would break the twelve-pair literal that `cube` exists to preserve.
dna.underlying_finding: Two real defects were found on the way and are deliberately NOT papered over by this promotion. The .tscn declares ForceIndicator as a CSGCylinder3D, while setup_indicator_materials fetches it through get_or_create_box_indicator and animate_indicators then guards with `if force_indicator is CSGBox3D` - so the force bar has never once resized in any placement; only the energy bar, which really is a CSGBox3D, responds. And the shipped repulsion has no equilibrium inside the frame: every graph in the family, including the shipped cube, ends pressed flat against the 6.0 clamp within four seconds, so what the room actually shows after a moment is not a force balance but a box holding eight nodes apart. Both are decisions to make, not axes to declare.

dna.framing_why: DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB, WHICH IS A 40 m GROUND PLATE. Union 40.00 x 2.21 x 40.00, diagonal 56.6117, radius 28.3058. The rig fits by DIAGONAL, so at framing 1.0 the camera stands radius/tan(17deg)*1.9 = 175.91 m out and the visible frame is 107.56 m wide - for a subject that projects 55.797 m wide and 16.480 m tall at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26. The plate filled 51.9% of frame WIDTH and 15.3% of its HEIGHT: two thirds of the picture was spent on a height a flat square does not have. This is exactly the thin-wide-subject case in CLAUDE.md's null-verdict table, and the cost was not a thin number but a missing one - the archived bite report reads subject 0.268%, peak 0.471%, SUBJECT NOT DETECTED. AT 0.55 the camera is 96.75 m out, the frame is 59.16 m wide, the plate fills 94.3% of it, and the scale is 12.85 px/m. A 0.86 m torso is 11.05 px against LAW 9's floor of 10 - the first framing at which the population is measurable at all. 0.50 would be sharper still and puts the plate at 103.7% of frame width, which clips the corner bodies that ARE the culled value. 0.55 is the tightest framing that does not cut the axis's own evidence.
dna.measured: MEASURED 2026-08-13, and this axis had never been photographed. The archived bite report (2026-07-31) reads subject 0.268%, peak 0.471%, SUBJECT NOT DETECTED - and check_dna_declarations returned ok for it the whole time, because the DECLARATION was honest: the five values match SELECTIONS and the @export_enum character for character. Every gate green, nothing seen. TWO FAULTS, both in the harness and neither in the axis. (1) FRAMING - see framing_why: a flat 40 m plate fitted by its DIAGONAL put the camera 175.91 m out and spent two thirds of the picture on height a square does not have. (2) THE ARTIFACT FELL OVER BEFORE THE SHUTTER. Every body spawns with FOOT_CLEARANCE = 1.2 m of air under it and the bench settles 1.1 s; free fall of 1.2 m takes 0.495 s, so the herd landed at ~4.85 m/s with the hip motors driving, ~0.6 s before the frame existed. The recorded measurement said so and nobody read it that way: aabb_size [40.0, 2.21, 40.0] at centre y 0.71 puts the top of everything at 1.815 m, BELOW drift's 2.400 m spawn torso top and far below runaway's 4.250 m. AFTER framing 0.55 and fixture freeze_bodies: subject 0.268% -> 14.6% (54x), peak 0.471% -> 2.43% (5.2x), verdict SUBJECT NOT DETECTED -> BITES. rejected=0. All five values are now individually legible: drift and uniform on the shared 5 x 4 grid, culled as four bodies at the corners, runaway as the converging fan, split as two ranks. WHAT THE FIXTURE DOES NOT FIX, stated because a fixture that hides a defect is the failure this corpus keeps paying for. freeze_bodies makes the still show WHAT THE AXIS BUILDS. What a player meets across 11 maps is still the fallen herd, and bipeds that topple within a second of spawning are a defect in a walker demo, not a capture problem. That is the artifact's own fix and it is not made here. AND drift IS NOT A SPREAD, which the sheet now shows plainly: 20 geometrically identical bodies on a regular lattice. CreatureGenome.randomize() draws hip amplitude, frequency, phase and the two masses - never torso_size or leg_size - and _genome_for returns before _apply_morph for drift. The word promises a spread; the code delivers a lattice, and only the gait and the masses vary, both invisible in a still.

dna.default: basin=bowl, evidence=longhand - longhand is the four trails, the four markers and the four live gradient arrows, i.e. the shipped OPTIMIZERS picture branch for branch; the arrow block is the original code moved under an `if` and nothing else. All 5 existing placements (Cabinet_Gallery, Disposition_Test_Rooms, Grown_DNA_Algorithms, MachineLearning_Evolving_Creatures, ML_Evolution) are plain tokens with no config, so they get exactly what they got before.
dna.was: basin was promoted earlier and lifted function_preset out of apply_grid_config-only reach. What was still hard-coded was the DISCLOSURE: trails, markers and per-runner gradient arrows were drawn unconditionally, so no map could ask this artifact for the answer without the working, or for the rule without the run.
dna.note: evidence is what the artifact offers as proof that a descent happened. result = the four markers alone, an optimizer as a POSITION. trace = + the paths, where SGD's zig-zag, Momentum's overshoot and Adam's straight run actually live - none of that is legible from a marker. longhand = + the local gradient at each runner. axiom = the runners go and -grad f is sampled on the same 9 x 9 lattice the HESSIAN mode reads curvature on, direction normalised (the direction is the local truth the update rule consumes) and length carrying log|grad f| scaled to THIS surface. axiom is where the two axes argue: on plateau every arrow collapses toward the length floor because the surface has nothing to say, and on scarp the columns either side of the face point at each other - both derivatives honest about the bowl, one of them a lie about the cliff between them. The readout and key strip switch with it, because a legend naming four colours none of which is in frame is the label contradicting the picture.
dna.kin: evidence is taken character for character from the family (example_1_7 / 1_9 / 2_8 / 2_9, koch_curve, box_counting_dimension, three_body_problem) - one question asked of a thing in motion: what do you put in the frame as PROOF that a law is moving it? THE DEFAULT DIFFERS FROM THE FAMILY'S. The motion demos ship as `result`, a bare ball with every exhibit withheld; this one ships with its whole working already on the table, so it ships as `longhand`. A map that asks all of them for `longhand` still gets one vocabulary and several answers, which is the test of the shared word.
dna.still_note: evidence needs no rebuild - all four values are branches inside the per-frame ImmediateMesh pass, so apply_grid_config sets the word and never touches the standing 8 m console. Sweeping evidence on the DEFAULT basin (bowl) understates it: bowl's four runners converge to nearly the same short path, so result-vs-trace is small there. Sweep it on `valley` or `plural`, where the trails are long and separate, or measure the pair basin=scarp x evidence=axiom, which is the strongest single frame this artifact can produce.
dna.framing_note: the axis lives in the 8 x 8 m field on the deck, not on the console body, so a fit-by-diagonal that includes the legs and the bay will shrink the field to a fraction of frame. Check subject % before reading any verdict on either axis.

dna.default: bearing=aligned - aligned BUILDS NO MANIFOLD BODY. It is the @export default and the only value that adds no geometry, so both existing placements (Grown_DNA_Learning, ML_Gradient_Landscape) render exactly what they rendered before: the sample cloud, the principal-component rods, the two 3D label plates, nothing else. The one honest caveat is that the cloud is now drawn from a seeded RandomNumberGenerator (DATA_SEED) instead of the global unseeded randf(), so a given placement no longer matches any one pre-change run - but pre-change it matched no run either, since the cloud was redrawn differently on every load. dna.was: no axis of its own. The cloud generator was a single hard-coded correlated-Gaussian draw, so PCA - an algorithm whose entire claim is that it finds the direction structure actually runs in - could only ever be shown one structure. dna.note: CAPTURE HAZARD, verified still present: setup_ui() builds a 450 x 800 screen-space Panel on a CanvasLayer during _build_all(), late enough that a single chrome-suppression pass misses it. In an earlier gallery that dark rectangle occupied one tile of five and measured the axis at 11.6% while the four clouds being compared were mutually identical - a number about the overlay, not the artifact. The capturer now suppresses chrome twice. The panel is safe to suppress: _build_3d_labels() builds the player-facing readout as billboarded 3D label plates (title at y=6.0, live stats at y=5.0), so nothing a player needs lives only on the CanvasLayer.

dna.default: opening=flat - flat SHORT-CIRCUITS in _polyline(): the bow is zero, the arc loop is skipped by `continue`, and the function returns exactly the three shipped vertices, so ImmediateMesh receives v1, v2, v3, v1 in the shipped order with the same material. The label strings are handed back as literals rather than measured, so all four Label3Ds read the bytes they shipped ('60°' three times and '60° + 60° + 60° = 180°') at the same positions, pixel_size and font_size. All 3 placements (Euclid_Parallel, Euclid_Parallel_composed, test_batch_1) plus the two curation_station lists (Corridor_Euclid_Parallel, Curation_Bay_foundationscrisis_0) are bare tokens - the ':0:0.5' and ':90:0' suffixes are rotation and y-offset, not config keys - and the axis is read only inside `if config_data.has("opening")`, so none of them reaches the new code.
dna.was: one @export, `size`, a scale factor - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so no map token could turn even that. The artifact's own truth line is 'the angle sum of a triangle is not a fact about triangles but a fact about the space they inhabit' and its critical_parameter is named as curvature, but the only space it could draw was the flat one: three straight segments and a hard-coded '= 180°'. The theorem's FAILURE - the whole point of the artifact, per its description - lived in the registry text and in a relationships line pointing at two other artifacts, and nowhere in the geometry.
dna.shared_with: curvature_slider - `opening` is that artifact's word with its three values in the same order, because these are the same theorem from two directions: curvature_slider states the sign of K on a dial, this shows what that sign does to a triangle. A room holding both can no longer set them to disagreeing spaces. NOTE the corpus carries a second, unrelated `opening` (agreement_gauge, dot_aligner, dot_product_projector, exercise_5_9_angle_between: agreeing|strangers|opposing|parallel, the angle between two vectors). The collision predates this promotion; the value lists tell the two senses apart and this one is the curvature list.
dna.finding: The three angle labels read 60° each and are commented '# Equilateral for simplicity', but the triangle as drawn is isoceles - vertices (0, .5s), (-.4s, -.3s), (.4s, -.3s) measure 53.1 / 63.4 / 63.4, which do sum to 180. The shipped strings are nominal, not measured. They are preserved to the byte at the default because three maps ship them; the two curved values print angles MEASURED off the polyline they actually draw (hyperbolic 29+38+38=105, elliptic 79+88+88=255), summing the rounded parts so the printed equation is true as printed. Correcting the flat labels would be a legitimate follow-up and a deliberate change to three live maps, not a side effect of a promotion.
dna.declined: witness (curvature_slider's second axis, number|surface|normals) - it would need a rendered saddle or sphere patch and a normal field this artifact has neither of, and taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary. A `figure` axis over triangle shapes (the theorem is invariant under the triangle and variant under the space) is real and still-visible, but its default value would have to be the legacy figure whose labels are nominal, and one axis measured honestly beats two with a seam in them.

dna.default: opening=flat, witness=number - flat SHORT-CIRCUITS: _k() hands back the shipped `curvature` export rather than the table's 0.0, so a map that overrides curvature alone opens at its own number instead of being reset to zero. At K = 0 the slider knob is built at (0 + 1) / 2 = 0.5, the literal that was hard-coded there before, and _label_text() renders 'CURVATURE: K = 0\n(Flat/Euclidean)' to the byte - _k_str returns '0' and not '0.00' for exactly this reason. witness=number adds no node at all, so the scene tree stays the rack panel and the Label3D and nothing else. The 5 placements (NonEuclidean_Spaces, NonEuclidean_Spaces_composed, test_batch_1 and the two curation_station rosters in Corridor_NonEuclidean_Spaces and Curation_Bay_foundationscrisis_1) name no config keys, so apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` before this pass - reaches no assignment and never rebuilds.
dna.was: one @export, `curvature`, a float that was never read at build time: _ready() built the panel with a hard-coded 0.5 and the label with a hard-coded string, and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`. The three signs of K - the whole of differential geometry's classification - were reachable only by a hand on a slider in a headset, and even then the artifact displayed no curvature, only the word for it.
dna.note: opening is dot_aligner's word for the same situation (a named case that existed only behind a hand in VR) with its four-angle value list refused: the sign of K has exactly three values and a fourth would invent a geometry. DECLINED and measured first: a geodesic-triangle value showing the angle sum. A chord lifted onto the patch is not a geodesic, and the lifted-chord sum comes out 179.6 on the saddle and 161.1 on the DOME - the wrong side of 180 for positive curvature, at every rotation of the triangle. It would have published a figure stating the theorem backwards. SEPARATE FINDING, not repaired here: curvature_changed has no listener anywhere in the repo, so the @identity's 'controls hyperbolic_surface and elliptic_surface' is aspirational.

elliptic_surface.name: Elliptic Surface

poincare_disk.qfep_connection: The parallel postulate is independent - geometry is a choice

The project's chosen way for a room to say something and stay a room: text seated in the world on a surface, the humble carrier of nearly every explanation the curriculum offers.

grab_sphere_F.name: F Term Sphere
grab_sphere_F.description: Grabbable sphere representing F (Free Energy) - the order-seeking, pattern-finding drive. Blue glow.
grab_sphere_F.qfep_connection: F, free energy, in your hand and glowing blue — the order-seeking, pattern-finding drive, the term that wants the world to make sense. Grab it and you hold the project's model of the mind's hunger for structure: the force that compresses, predicts, and resolves. First term of the equation, and the one every algorithm in this curriculum secretly serves.

lambda_slider.name: Lambda Slider
lambda_slider.description: QFEP parameter rail from 0 to 1, with authored visual effects and a lambda_changed signal. Its preferred green band is a design choice, not a universal interval where life exists. calibration selects optimum, band, dispute, gap or none. In Crisis_Synthesis its signal updates the local formula display only.

lambda_slider.qfep_connection: lambda_edge: the entropy drive dial itself — λ=0 pure order, 0.4 the edge of chaos, 1 dissolution. The project's own thermostat, graspable: the parameter that decides how much wildness a system is permitted.

phi_slider.name: Phi Slider
phi_slider.description: Signed PHI controller with local particle feedback. Optional sign_study gives equal-speed opposite directions, zero emission at zero, and delayed earlier labels on a plinth; the study remains outside the global controller group.
