parameters.sign_study: on/off, default off: local sign encounter with optional earlier interpretation

phi_slider.qfep_connection: lambda_edge: the sensitivity dial — φ below zero resists change, above zero embraces it. The second hand on the QFEP clock: not how much entropy, but how the system FEELS about its rate.

qfep_balance_workbench.name: QFEP Balance Workbench
qfep_balance_workbench.description: Four normalised controls evaluate F - lambda*E + phi*0.30. A four-axis diagram keeps the contributions visible; the colour/name comes from the nearest of seven authored project references. Opt-in comparison adds KEEP for one retained outline and total. No entropy measurement or physical phase detection.
qfep_balance_workbench.interaction: grab_slide; press KEEP in comparison mode

parameters.comparison: Optional on/off; default off. KEEP retains one four-value arrangement and its total. Enabled in QFEP_Introduction.
parameters.settling: Initial example: edge, order, entropy, integration or synthesis. These are authored tuples, not detected physical phases.

orange_and_apples.name: Orange and Apples
orange_and_apples.description: Heisenberg's own 1927 analogy, built so a visitor has to perform it. A low bench holds a tray of eighteen identical dark knobs under a cantilevered hood; three of them are apples and the rest are decoys, made from the SAME mesh with the SAME material instance, so which is which cannot be read off the surface. Beside the bench stands a rack of oranges, and an orange is a grabbable throwable in both lanes - RMB and LMB on the desktop crosshair, grip and trigger in the headset. A struck apple registers WHERE it was, as a lit pin standing on the tray floor, and in the same instant takes a kick in a direction nobody chose. Position is bought with momentum. THE TRADE IS THE OBJECT AND NOT A CAPTION ON IT: on the panel above, a single outlined rectangle has WIDTH = the spread on position and HEIGHT = the spread on momentum, and its AREA NEVER CHANGES - squeeze it narrow and it has to grow tall. Above that rectangle sits the same rectangle drawn four times at four widths, dim, as a printed scale, so a still photograph shows the law without anyone touching anything. Impact speed sets all of it from one number, which is the actual content of the 1927 argument rather than decoration on it: a fast orange is a short wavelength, so it resolves the apple to a hairline pin and a narrow rectangle AND shoves it harder; a gentle one barely tells you anything and barely moves it. There is no throw that buys the first without paying the second. The concealment is geometry, never shadow - an unlit box photographs as a black rectangle and hall lighting is not a constant across this museum - so the apples hide in a CROWD, under a roof that cuts the sight line to the back rows. Note the sizes: the orange is 10.4 cm and the apple is 9.0 cm, and the probe being bigger than the thing probed is the reason the disturbance cannot be made small.
dev_themes: a look is done WITH something, and the something arrives
the record of a measurement outlives the state it recorded
a rectangle of constant area is the whole relation, and it survives a still
orange_and_apples.qfep_connection: The laboratory's other observer-effect piece, two_point_ruler, makes the OPPOSITE claim and the pair are worth standing near each other: there the subject is honest throughout - it never changes, so nothing about the reading is wrong - and the displacement lands on a bystander you can only catch by looking away from your own instrument. Here the displacement lands on the thing measured, which is Heisenberg's case rather than Schroedinger's, and there is no innocent subject anywhere in the room. Together they say the two things QFEP wants said about measurement at once: that an instrument alters what it is not pointed at, and that it alters what it is.
interactions: Look into the hood before throwing anything. Eighteen identical knobs, and the question the artifact asks is already fully posed: which three of these are apples? Nothing about the surface answers it.
Throw gently. The pin comes up fat, the rectangle stays broad and flat, and the apple barely shifts. You have learned roughly where something was and cost it almost nothing.
Throw hard. The pin is a hairline, the rectangle stands up narrow and tall, and the apple leaves fast in a direction you did not choose. Same gauge, opposite proportions, same area.

Come back to the pins after four or five throws. There is one per apple, standing where that apple was when you last measured it and describing nothing presently in the tray - each was made by the act that emptied its own spot. It is not a growing bed: a second reading on the same apple moves its pin, because a record that accumulated would fill the tray and you could no longer see into it.
Place it once with #mode:open. The roof is gone, the apples are visible, no throw is needed and the instrument has nothing to say. That is the control condition and it is worth walking.

config.mode: hood | open | deep - how hidden the apples are. `open` removes the roof and cheeks entirely and is the artifact's own control condition. `deep` reaches 16 cm further forward and drops 6 cm, hiding more WITHOUT narrowing the aperture; lowering the roof instead was tried first and left a 9 cm slot, which a 10.4 cm orange cannot enter.
config.cols: 2-9, default 6 - columns in the bed of knobs.
config.rows: 1-4, default 3 - rows in the bed. cols x rows is the size of the crowd the three apples hide in, which is what 'hard to find' actually means here.
config.count: 1-8, default 4 - oranges on the rack. The rack is SIZED from this, so a bigger magazine is a longer shelf and never two oranges spawned inside each other.

orange_and_apples.config_note: Every key is either word-valued (mode) or already in GridInteractablesComponent.CONFIG_PARAM_NAMES (rows, cols, count), so none can be eaten by the tutorial's #key:number shorthand. The number of APPLES is deliberately not a config key: it is three because the source says three, and a numeric #apples:3 is not in that list, so it would be read as tutorial_id:rotation, leave the artifact at its default and make the map token look correct while doing nothing.

spatial_needs.clearance_note: The front clearance is 3 and it is not padding. A visitor has to stand back far enough to throw an orange on an arc into a 28 cm slot; at 1 cell they are leaning over the tray and can only drop. This is the one artifact in the room whose clearance is a fact about a trajectory rather than about a sightline.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry at the shipped defaults, no Godot was run for this figure. Width: the assembly is centred on the origin by construction (_bench_x derives the offset rather than typing it), running from bench_x - SLAB.x/2 to rack_x + shelf/2, and at count 4 the shelf is 4 x 0.128 + 0.06 = 0.572, so bench_x = -0.336 and the span is -1.036 to 1.036. Height: SLAB_TOP 0.78 + PANEL.y 1.12 = 1.90, and the readout plate tops out at 1.82 inside it. Depth: the back panel's rear face at -0.29 to the caption screen's glass at +0.245, with the hood roof reaching +0.24 and the tray's front rim +0.255. `deep` mode pushes the roof to +0.40 and takes the depth to 0.69; `open` removes it and leaves 0.545 unchanged. A larger #count lengthens the shelf and widens the whole box by the same amount at BOTH ends, because the centring is derived - at count 8 the width is 2.584 and the origin is still the middle.

orange_and_apples.note: Built 2026-09-09. Physics contract, because it is the part a later editor will break by tidying: apples are RigidBody3D on collision_layer 1 with mask 1|4 - layer 1 so the orange's shipped pickable mask (196615) reaches them, and deliberately NOT layer 3, since an apple on the grab layer could be lifted out and read with the hand, which is the one thing this bench must not allow. Decoys are StaticBody3D on layer 1. Oranges are instances of addons/godot-xr-tools/objects/pickable.tscn with their collision layer and mask left exactly as shipped (layer 3, which is what DesktopInteractionPointer.GRAB_MASK 393220 and the VR hand both look for); a bare RigidBody3D was the cheaper build and was rejected because function_pickup.gd:294 rejects anything without a pick_up() method before it reaches the grab list, so a plain body can be carried on desktop and never lifted in the headset. Contact monitoring lives on the ORANGE, not on the eighteen knobs, and the impact speed used for the reading is the one recorded at the top of the physics frame - by the time body_entered is emitted the step has already resolved the bounce and linear_velocity is what the fruit is doing on its way back out. The throw is action_pressed to charge and action_released to release, connected at build time because DesktopInteractionPointer._fires refuses to call action() at all unless the signal already has a listener; a charge held past CHARGE_S + 0.45 s launches anyway, so a lost release event cannot strand the fruit in a visitor's hand. NO dna.axes block: this artifact has never been swept and the declaration gate has never been run against it, and a hand-typed axis that does not match the code is the fault this project most often catches in itself.

qfep_formula_3d.name: QFEP Formula 3D
qfep_formula_3d.description: Spatial display of Ada’s QFEP research proposal. Opt-in reading_study binds this hall’s lambda and phi sliders to term colours and a numeric reading panel; three reachable buttons select questions. It does not calculate entropy, free energy or QFE.
qfep_formula_3d.interaction: observe; term buttons in reading_study mode

dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS because the five existing exports (animate, pulse_speed, glow_intensity, font_size, depth) had no apply_grid_config to reach them, and none of them changes what the formula argues. The axis is named posture, not layout, because curation_station already owns the key `layout` with an overlapping vocabulary (row/corner/ring)

parameters.reading_study: Opt-in local slider connections, reading panel and term buttons; on in Crisis_Synthesis. Default off.

qfep_formula_3d.qfep_connection: synthesis: the whole formula in the air — QFE = F − λE(S) + φΔE(S,t), each term glowing its signature color, answering the sliders live. The project's thesis as a walkable object: free energy, entropy drive, and the felt rate of change, summed.

grab_sphere_E.name: E Term Sphere
grab_sphere_E.description: Grabbable sphere representing E(S) (Entropy) - the freedom and possibility space. Red glow.
grab_sphere_E.qfep_connection: E(S), entropy, glowing red — the freedom and the possibility space, everything F would tidy away. Grab it and you hold disorder not as decay but as *room*: the vast unmapped territory from which anything new must come. The equation subtracts it (−λE) because order costs freedom, and the whole drama of QFEP is how much freedom to spend.

grab_sphere_lambda.name: Lambda Term Sphere
grab_sphere_lambda.description: Grabbable sphere representing λ (lambda) - the entropy drive parameter. Green glow.
grab_sphere_lambda.qfep_connection: λ, the entropy drive, glowing green — the dial that weighs how much freedom the system spends against order. Grab it and you hold the single most important number in the project: λ near zero is crystal, λ near one is dissolution, and λ≈0.3–0.5 is where life is. Everything alive is a setting of this sphere.

shannon_workbench.name: Shannon Workbench
shannon_workbench.description: Binary source entropy H(p) and a finite fixed-seed sample. Moving p re-thresholds stored draws. The readout reports source uncertainty, not an exact encoding length for this grid. Optional prediction_study adds EXPECT 0/1, expected error and counted misses with amber cell underlines.
shannon_workbench.interaction: grab_slide; EXPECT 0/1 buttons in prediction study
shannon_workbench.capacity: Compare source uncertainty with predictor fit

film_shannon_threshold.description: Lift fixed source-generated random draws into height, sweep the threshold, and distinguish sample count from binary source entropy.
interactions: Look at the screen to play.
Pause, replay, step or turn the view.
film_shannon_threshold.qfep_connection: Private 64-draw sample; H(p) is source entropy, not thermodynamic entropy or proof of QFEP.

snap_tetrahedron_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle where connecting 4 snap points forms a tetrahedron that spawns a cube.
snap_tetrahedron_puzzle.name: Snap Tetrahedron Puzzle
snap_tetrahedron_puzzle.qfep_connection: Four snap points, and a tetrahedron forms — which then spawns a cube. The minimal solid conjuring the familiar one: the puzzle stages the chapter's whole ascent, from the simplest possible volume to the one everything in this grid is made of.

crystal_cluster.name: Crystal Cluster
crystal_cluster.description: Ordered crystalline formation representing λ=0 (pure order). Alias for crystalcluster primitive.

dna.default: growth=scatter, facet=taper - scatter makes the same six rng draws in the same order as the shipped code and taper keeps the 0.7 top ratio, so all 27 existing placements are vertex-for-vertex unchanged

dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS because the script exposed no exports at all; growth is the macro order (how the five relate) and facet the micro order (the habit of one crystal)

crystal_cluster.qfep_connection: λ=0 made solid: a crystalline formation, pure order, frozen pattern. The cold end of the spectrum where F has won completely and E(S) is starved to nothing — perfect structure, perfect death. Beautiful and uninhabitable, the pole the edge-of-chaos rooms define themselves against.

bias_visualizer.description: Interactive visualization of statistical and algorithmic bias — demonstrates how initial conditions, training data, or parameter choices create systematic skew in outputs. A critical theory artifact making invisible biases tangible.
interactions: observe
bias_visualizer.name: Bias Visualizer
bias_visualizer.qfep_connection: Bias is frozen E(S) â€” entropy collapsed into stereotypes. The model minimizes prediction error (F) by encoding societal patterns. Critical Ï†: questioning whose data, whose categories.

dna.default: disclosure=origin, analogy_type=0 - both existing placements are untouched. Every rung of this ladder is already on the face of the case (axis inlay, connection lines, analogy screen, interpretive caption), so `origin` IS the shipped state and the only value that changes nothing; analogy_type=0 is the export default the .tscn already sets.
dna.was: The case showed all five rungs unconditionally and apply_grid_config was `pass`, so every token a map put on a placement was parsed, logged and silently discarded. analogy_type existed as a working export but was never declared, which is why the runner reported NO TURNABLE KNOBS.
dna.note: `disclosure` is prng_crank_machine's ladder, read by preload from the file that owns it (the same link slot_machine makes) rather than copied — oracle < tally < ledger < works < origin, monotone. Read here: oracle = twenty words coloured by the gender the embedding gave them, with no axis drawn, no lines, a dark screen and a blank label — the deployed condition, where the skew arrives inside the output and the machine does not mention it. Then + the aggregate (the MASC/FEM axis machined into the deck), + the per-item record (each profession wired to the pole that pulled it), + the mechanism (man - woman + nurse = ?), + the origin (Who was in the training data?). NOTE the default departs from the family's legacy `works` because this artifact's legacy face carries the caption; an unreadable token therefore falls back to `origin`, not `works`, so a typo cannot strip the provenance question off a wall two rooms already read. analogy_type is declared as its int samples because cabinet_sweep coerces numerics and the gate range-checks them; the words behind them are Gender-Profession, Gender-Trait, Algorithmic Redlining.

situated_readout.description: Authored subject readout: an explicit station key or position hash selects a verdict and supplied confidence. Address variants hide, print or stage its source. Optional FOOTNOTE / COVER / WITNESS controls change the presentation while keeping the claim fixed.
situated_readout.name: Situated Readout

identity.essence: A verdict that changes with where it speaks from
identity.desire: To be read alongside three siblings showing incompatible answers to the same input
identity.truth: There is no view from nowhere — the classification belongs to the location, not the subject

situated_readout.qfep_connection: A visible address makes an assertion traceable without making it true. Comparing the unchanged claim under covered and embodied presentation asks how authority is staged; the symbolic eye performs no measurement.

dna.default: perspective_blend=0.0 - the pre-promotion state, so its three existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: perspective_blend is this artifact's declared critical_parameter and was a PRIVATE var pinned at 0.0, with apply_grid_config() an empty pass. Every placement showed the god's-eye view; the compressed perspective the artifact exists to deliver was reachable only by grabbing a VR slider, and appeared in no capture, gallery or still.
dna.note: Hero artifact of postfoundationscrisis, the spine-terminal sequence, where it recurs across three maps.

bias_from_inside.description: A word-position study with 24 terms in two authored, seeded arrangements. COMPRESSION interpolates their coordinates with materials held fixed; READ reveals the project interpretation. The visitor can move around the study. No camera movement or empirical embedding measurement is implied.
bias_from_inside.name: Bias From Inside
bias_from_inside.qfep_connection: The same array can retain every word while making distinctions harder to see. The grouping, endpoint coordinates and available control are authored decisions; the encounter asks which of those decisions should be revisable.

filled_pocket.name: Filled Pocket
filled_pocket.description: A tabletop grid from the source figure, kept faithful: bad cells grey, the route from x to y in blue through the good cells, and every free cell the flood cannot reach drawn FILLED in amber - open floor absorbed into the walls, because reachability, not occupancy, is what a map answers to. The pocket is discovered, never authored: a flood fill runs from x, the route is its parent chain to y, and the layouts are hand-written character maps with no RNG. wall sets what the bad cells form (open / u_bend / ring / split) and door removes one or two named wall cells. Measured: the open field routes in 12 steps with nothing sealed; the U costs 14 and seals nothing, because a trap with an open mouth is reachable; the ring seals exactly 9 cells of perfectly good floor and one door drains all 9; the split kills the route outright, stranding 45 cells, and a mid-wall door restores it at 10 steps. Where the door names a cell that was never wall, the plate says so - an artifact whose answer to an undefined question is to look unchanged cannot be told apart from a broken one. Readable in code via route_steps(), pocket_cells(), reachable_cells().

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. Both doors reconnect the halves, so the route threads the wall either way and the plate prints the same verdict shape; the differences are one extra opened cell in a nine-row wall and possibly a shorter thread for double. One cell of eleven-by-nine is 1 percent of the board; the route shift adds a little. FRAME = 1.8 percent.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS. Below about 1.8 percent the likely causes in order are (a) the sweep setting door before wall so the setter rebuild order masks one value - both setters rebuild, so this should not happen, but check _rejects.json first; (b) the route choosing the same thread through either door so only the second opened cell differs - that is a genuine 1 percent and the floor of this prediction; (c) a door value DOORS does not carry, failing silently to sealed.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, sixth artifact running. door at wall=open and wall=u_bend names cells that are ALREADY FLOOR: nothing changes but one plate line - the artifact says '(the door names open floor)' precisely so these near-twins are declared rather than discovered, bridge_cut's lesson applied in advance. Expect door to be CONDITIONAL on wall, alive only at ring and split; read the per-pair rows grouped by wall, never the axis mean.

excluded_class_visualizer.name: Excluded Class Visualizer
excluded_class_visualizer.description: Two clusters separated by a classifier boundary, plus a third red cluster ON the boundary. Bias as visible structural incompleteness.
excluded_class_visualizer.qfep_connection: Two clean clusters, one confident boundary, and a third cluster pulsing red beside the line: the points the model never had words for. Bias is not staged as an error but as a shape — every classifier drawn this sharply has an outside, and here you can walk around it.

godel_statement_plaque.description: Self-referential plaque cycling through increasingly paradoxical statements, culminating in Gödel's incompleteness
godel_statement_plaque.qfep_connection: Proves pure F-minimization is impossible - every formal system has an outside
interactions: click to advance statement
grab to cycle

room_shape_demonstrator.name: Room Shape Demonstrator
room_shape_demonstrator.description: Miniature seating plans: long table, circle, pair, a ring with a raised centre, or vacant rooms. Optional visitor controls select plans and a neutral or authored palette. Chair count and scale vary between plans; switching only palette preserves the geometry.
room_shape_demonstrator.qfep_connection: An arrangement proposes participation before anyone speaks. Compare the authored choices, including colour, without mistaking equal angular spacing for equal opportunity. The models contain no speaking or listening process.

florensky_sphere.description: Florensky-inspired visual antinomy. In hold_both mode, the double-sided sphere holds the label A AND not-A while its colours change; observation and cycling cannot collapse it. It illustrates two readings, not a formal logic.
florensky_sphere.gamwell_reference: Chapter 3: Florensky's 'Pillar and Ground of the Truth' - supralogic
florensky_sphere.qfep_connection: Ask how an unresolved account can remain open to investigation. Rendering two faces does not establish a true contradiction or a QFEP theorem.
interactions: Florensky hall: circle the sphere and wait; both readings remain. Legacy desktop observation/cycling remains available when hold_both is off.

parameters.hold_both: Opt-in sustained BOTH reading; on in Florensky_Paraconsistent. Disables observation and state cycling without altering seam geometry.

florensky_sphere.name: Florensky Sphere

merge_conflict_visualizer.name: Merge Conflict Visualizer
merge_conflict_visualizer.description: Four authored arrangements of branches A and B: separate uprights, intersecting boxes, A at full height with B as a stump, and diverging branches. Optional MERGE controls expose the comparison; MARKER hides the glow without changing branches.
merge_conflict_visualizer.qfep_connection: Keeping incompatible accounts available permits investigation of their sources and of the decision to suppress one. The branches are a spatial analogy; this artifact neither derives logical consequences nor proves formal paraconsistency.

superposition_display.name: Superposition Display
superposition_display.description: Visual toy with two basis-state forms whose opacities cycle and a slider that changes their pace. Opacity is not a quantum amplitude. The display has no measurement or collapse operation.
superposition_display.qfep_connection: The shared visual language invites a comparison, not an identification, of quantum superposition and logical contradiction.
interactions: Move the slider to change the pace of the opacity animation; no measurement control is present.

schrodinger_box.description: A labelled visual toy: desktop click chooses a random ALIVE/DEAD outcome, opens the lid, then resets after a timer. It is not a quantum simulation; tracked-hand opening remains unimplemented.
schrodinger_box.qfep_connection: Compare a scripted revelation with the sphere that holds two readings. Quantum superposition and logical contradiction are different questions.
interactions: Desktop click selects a random outcome and opens the lid; timer resets. No tracked-hand opening is implemented.

cap_theorem_walk.name: CAP Theorem Walk
cap_theorem_walk.description: Three pillars in a triangle. A slow rotation lights two at a time. The CAP trade-off cycle made visible.
cap_theorem_walk.qfep_connection: Three pillars, and the light can only ever hold two: consistency, availability, partition tolerance traded in a slow rotation where the dim pillar names today's sacrifice. The walk refuses an optimum — living with a proven limit is shown as a rhythm, not a settlement.

rhizome_vault.name: Rhizome Vault
rhizome_vault.description: Pods and crossing tunnels with no main entrance, no center, no front — glowing root-runners propagating between heterogeneous chambers. Enter anywhere; a map, not a tracing.

forbidden_bands.name: Forbidden Bands
forbidden_bands.description: A tilted dish whose rim carries raised red walls, and a soft ball that rolls downhill and settles wherever the bands leave open - the resting azimuth is the artifact's answer, measured off the settled body. With no bands the ball rests straight downhill at azimuth zero: the control that makes every later deflection attributable. A pair of bands straddling downhill sends it to minus thirty degrees, sixteen past the band's edge - refusal measured as an angle. A belt leaves no clear arc and the ball rests ON the forbidden: when everything is foreclosed, refusal has nowhere to send you. On a level dish the rim is never consulted and the bands are honestly scenery. Gated at 60 and 90 Hz. Three findings are built into the geometry and documented in the script: the minimum of a tilted bowl is interior (early leans parked the ball 45 mm out and the bands were never met), a curved bumper exerts zero tangential force at azimuth zero so nothing ever deflected off it (the bands are FLAT chord walls now, like the source figure's straight cuts, and the slide to the edge falls out of the plane projection), and droplet_cusp's wedge-grip acted as static friction here, so the dish runs slick at 0.12. The ball is the family's owned verlet pressure shell; resting ON a band means the body's centroid stands in its sector while the shell leans on its wall - a point grazing a band's end corner on the way past is a clear rest. The Q at the blanket's edge made physical: where you come to rest is the shape of what refused you. Readable via rest_azimuth_deg(), on_band(), at_rim(), nearest_band_edge_deg().

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. At level the ball sits centered and identical in both frames, so the only difference is scenery: two extra red walls of roughly 110 x 50 mm on a dish that fills perhaps 35 percent of frame. Two walls are about 10 percent of the dish's projected area at an oblique view. FRAME = 0.35 * 0.10 = 3.5 percent.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS. Below about 3.5 percent the likely causes in order are (a) the capture standpoint putting the two extra quartet walls at 90 and 284 degrees behind the dish's near rim, which is occlusion, not inertness - probe_anamorphic before any verdict; (b) the ball not yet settled when the frame was shot, adding noise that masks the walls (is_settled is readable); (c) a bands value BANDS_SET does not carry, failing silently to pair.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, seventh artifact running. Expect lean to be CONDITIONAL on bands only weakly (the ball's rest moves at every lean), but expect bands to be CONDITIONAL on lean STRONGLY: at level all four band values hold the ball at dead centre and differ only as furniture, and at faint the interior minimum keeps the rim out of reach, so the axis argues only at firm and steep. Read per-pair rows grouped by lean. The verdict plate changes text in nearly every cell, which is honest here because the azimuth it prints is measured off the settled body, not captioned.

the_fourth_limit.name: The Fourth Limit
the_fourth_limit.description: Four gates in one rank, built to one standard so the eye compares them without being asked. I is solid brass with the Konigsberg graph in relief - four banks, seven bridges - and it will not open because it CANNOT. II has a peephole that is dark: you may look, and looking tells you nothing. III stands ajar at 45 degrees with three fading ghosts of itself at 67.5, 78.75 and 84.4, each push taking half of what remains. IV is GLASS, locked, with a small screw beside the plate and a warm lamp burning behind it. Three limits you accept, live or approach; the fourth you can SEE THROUGH. A default has no image of its own - the only way to picture one is to stand it in the rank beside real limits. No plaques. Roman numerals cut into the sill and nothing else. 2026-08-27.

peer_production_tool.name: PeerProductionTool
peer_production_tool.description: Generated peer nodes send source-identified packets into an authored helix. Interactive placements expose held flow, order/source colour, piece selection, dispute, revision and version changes. Counts distinguish arrivals, per-version sources, lifetime sources and source-version participations. This is a geometric model, not a networked editor.
peer_production_tool.qfep_connection: A shared form can retain its sources while its assembly remains centrally authored. Marking and revising a piece changes the record without proving the change justified; participation counts do not establish knowledge.

the_commons_table.name: The Commons Table
the_commons_table.description: The post-crisis SUPER OBJECT and the spine's closing body: a round table with NO HEAD. Partial instruments sit around it, each honest about its outside - a classifier whose OTHER drawer outnumbers its labelled bins (counts computed), a sorter with its comparator printed, two contradictory readings held in one bracket without collapse, a camera admitting it is somewhere, a rootless rhizome of cords, and the engine's defaults shelved as somebody's opinion. Where a chairman would sit: a lit ring around nothing. 2026-08-27.

dna.family: ONE SCENE, TWO REGISTRY NAMES. `rhizome_cave_demo` and `rhizome_cave_system` both resolve to res://algorithms/spacetopology/marchingcubes/scenes/rhizome_cave_demo.tscn, so both entries declare the same two axes and a sweep of either measures the same object. Path verified rather than assumed: that .tscn's ext_resource names the real RhizomeCaveDemoController.gd and the ROOT node carries it, so both axes are reachable from a map token. DO NOT read algorithms/marchingcubes/scenes/rhizome_cave_demo.tscn — a second file of that name exists there and is an empty three-line stub ([gd_scene format=3] plus a bare Root node), and neither registry entry points at it.
dna.default: anastomosis=netted returns the float 6.0 — the same literal the controller's hardcoded rhizome_params dict has always handed to set_growth_rules — and bore=tunnel returns 1.0, where `radius * 1.0` is the identical bit pattern for every finite float, so carve_sphere receives the argument it always did. Both are SHORT-CIRCUITS out of a constant dictionary, not values re-derived from a formula that happens to land nearby. REACH MEASURED, and it is 3 direct grid placements plus 16 indirect hosts: `rhizome_cave_demo` bare in SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network and bare in ISO_Showcase_12; `rhizome_cave_system:0:-0.5` in Gallery_ProceduralGeneration, which is rotation and y-offset and carries no config; two curation_station rosters (Corridor_SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network and Curation_Bay_postfoundationscrisis_2); and fourteen `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:s#mount:rhizome_cave_demo` mounts across eight Trial_* museum maps. The `#` parameters on those host tokens belong to the HOST and are never forwarded to the mounted artifact. Neither registry entry declares default_params, so merged_config is empty at every one of the nineteen and GridInteractablesComponent does not reach _apply_artifact_config at all — the guarded rebuild below is unreachable from every map that exists.
dna.was: merge_distance = 6.0, typed into the rhizome_params dict at RhizomeCaveDemoController:62. The carve radius had no multiplier at all: carve_sphere used node.radius directly, from the initial node radius 3.0 (RhizomeCaveGenerator:332) and the chamber multiplier 2.0 (:366).
dna.note: WHERE THIS ARTIFACT'S FIELD COMES FROM, which is what wave 3 of the isosurfaces sequence is asking. Nowhere else in the sequence is the answer 'from a history'. Every other member samples a function at each lattice point — a gyroid, a noise, a sum of metaball kernels. This one evaluates nothing: generate_cave_async fills the whole chunk with density 1.0 (:346-349) and then SUBTRACTS, carve_sphere writing min(current, dist/voxel_radius) (:265) along a graph that grew iteration by iteration out of an RNG. The field is a record of what happened. Both axes are lifted out of that record, one from the growth and one from the carve, and they are orthogonal by construction: anastomosis decides the graph and never touches a radius; bore scales the radius and cannot reach the graph, because the graph is finished before the first voxel is written. ANASTOMOSIS asks whether a branch that meets an existing one rejoins it or stops. RhizomeGrowthPattern.find_merge_candidate (:171-176) returns the first existing node within merge_distance of a proposed branch tip; on a hit create_connection adds an EDGE and `continue` suppresses the new node, which is the only way a circuit can enter this graph. tree=0.0: nothing is ever within 0 m, so nothing ever merges — a pure arborescence with dead ends and no circuit, the figure Deleuze and Guattari oppose and the thing this artifact's own truth statement claims to refute, rendered here for the first time. netted=6.0 SHIPPED. matted=12.0. knotted=20.0. THE CONFOUND, stated rather than hidden: raising merge_distance both adds edges and SUPPRESSES nodes, because the merging branch does not create the node it was going to create. The network gets loopier and smaller at the same time and no still can separate the two. BORE asks how wide the same graph is carved. The multiplier lives inside carve_sphere, the single gate every carve passes through (carve_tunnel reaches the field only by calling it), so the graph is bit-for-bit identical across all four rungs — same seed, same nodes, same positions, same rng draws. At thread the carve radius is 1.2 m against a 1.0 m voxel and the solid boundary sits at 0.6 of a voxel, so the tube is thinner than the sampling lattice and a continuous field extracts as a broken string of beads; at hollow the tubes swallow each other and the surface merges what the graph deliberately kept apart. Same field-making history, different surface: the boundary is not a property of the field alone.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: NEW WORDS, both. `anastomosis` is already the project's own — the mycelium substrate work names it as its open gap — and the nearest taken word is `fusion` (the metaballs family), which is how much two FIELDS merge; this is whether two PATHS rejoin, decided in the graph before any field exists. `bore` is not `bulge` (queer_marching_cave), which swells a wall locally as a function of position, and it is deliberately not `resolution`: voxel_scale is held at 1.0 on every rung and only the carve radius moves, which is exactly what makes the lattice interaction legible at thread instead of confounded with it.
dna.crossed_wire: The two axes are orthogonal in the arithmetic and NOT in the picture. A large bore visually fuses tubes the graph never joined, so inside the `hollow` column anastomosis reads weak and inside the `tree` row bore reads weak — both frames are the same swallowed box. GROUP THE CRITIC'S NUMBERS BY VALUE PAIR ACROSS CONTEXTS, not by per-axis mean, or anastomosis will be convicted of the bore's doing. Measured on the replica at the fixture's seed: the weakest single CELL is bore hall x hollow inside the tree row at 0.6%, and the weakest grouped PAIR is anastomosis netted x matted at ~26%. Those two numbers are forty times apart and they are about the same sixteen tiles.
dna.declined: threshold (0.5, RhizomeCaveGenerator:10) — taken by mc_torus_sculpture, and worse: on a field carved as the linear ramp dist/voxel_radius a constant threshold is EXACTLY a uniform change of carve radius, so it would argue with bore for the same pixels. vertical_bias (0.3, applied as direction.y *= vertical_bias at RhizomeGrowthPattern:157) — real and visible, the difference between a flat sheet of tunnels and a ball of them, but it is the same question as `plumb` (mc_cave, mc_inside_cave): which way the field prefers to go. Declined for the rhyme and recorded here rather than dropped. chamber_probability (0.25) — too close to `bulge`, and stochastic: at 0.25 over ~30 iterations the variance between seeds would exceed the difference between rungs. branch_probability (0.6) and max_depth (4) — population counts, the same shape of question as `metaball_count`. voxel_scale and chunk_size — the sampling lattice, i.e. `resolution`, already taken twice. REPORTED, NOT SWEPT: setup_parameters (:285-292) read only chunk_size, voxel_scale and threshold, so the `seed` key every caller has always passed — `"seed": randi()` in this controller, `"seed": 12345, # Reproducible generation` in examples/simple_cave.gd — has never reached the RNG. That key is now read, defaulting to -1, which is the sentinel RhizomeGrowthPattern._init already understood. It is not a bug that shows, which is why it survived.
dna.fixture_why: FOUR NUMBERS AND A FLAG, EACH ANSWERING A MEASURED FAULT. cave_seed=7: RhizomeCaveGenerator:321 built RhizomeGrowthPattern.new(randi()), so five variants of this artifact were five different caves and any bite number would have been noise dressed as evidence (law 4). chunk_extent=24: RhizomeVoxelChunk._init never takes a world_position, so it defaults to Vector3.ZERO and the sampled volume is world 0..N. min/max branch length 3.0..26.0: NOT cosmetic — see `finding`. build_synchronously=true: _ready deferred generate_cave_async and the build then spent five awaited process_frames plus a mesh loop that yields whenever it passes 8 ms, so law 6 was not met as shipped and the capture's 1.1 s settle was a race. The flag is read at the four `await get_tree().process_frame` sites inside the generator and nowhere else, so there is one build path and one thing that can be wrong; every player-facing placement leaves it false, because a 13k-voxel march must not gate map load.
dna.finding: TWO THINGS THE READING FOUND, both invisible to every gate in the loop, both measured on a numpy replica of RhizomeGrowthPattern's growth loop and RhizomeCaveGenerator's carve rather than argued. (1) THE PROPOSED CAPTURE FIXTURE WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A DEAD AXIS THAT LOOKED LIKE A DESIGN FAILURE. find_merge_candidate compares a proposed branch tip against every existing node, and the tip sits at most branch_length from its own parent, which is already a node. So a merge_distance above max_branch_length merges EVERY attempt with its parent, create_connection rejects the self-edge (node1 != node2), and the network never grows past its seed node. At the approved 2.0..6.0 the four rungs replicate as merge rates 0 / 100 / 100 / 100 percent and node counts 175 / 1 / 1 / 1 — netted, matted and knotted would all have photographed as ONE carved sphere, the closest pair would have been 0.00% twice, and the verdict would have been a fact about a fixture. The shipped 5.0..20.0 collapses knotted alone, since 20.0 is exactly max_branch_length. The fixture uses 3.0..26.0, which measures 0 / 34 / 59 / 89 percent merged and 175 / 65 / 18 / 3 nodes: four different graphs, monotone, none degenerate. (2) bore=hollow AT THE APPROVED 3.5 CANNOT BE PHOTOGRAPHED. The multiplier lands on node.radius and create_chambers has already multiplied that by rng 2.0..4.0, so at 3.5 a single chamber reaches 42 m and swallows any chunk this artifact can afford to march. Replicated, the hollow column at 3.5 is 100 / 100 / 93 / 9 percent of the box carved: tree and netted are the same empty box and that anastomosis pair measures 0.0%. hall and hollow are therefore implemented at 1.6 and 2.4, which leaves surface in fifteen of the sixteen cells; thread=0.4 and tunnel=1.0 are exactly as approved, because they are the default and the lattice argument and that is where this axis makes its point.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE THE CAPTURE, from the replica run at the fixture's own seed, extent and branch lengths. Grouped BY VALUE PAIR across all four bore columns — which is how `crossed_wire` demands they be read — the weakest anastomosis pair is netted x matted at ~26% of the projected silhouette: the two middle rungs differ 3.6x in node count (65 against 18) but both silhouettes are dominated by the same root chamber and its first-generation tunnels. tree x netted is ~34% and matted x knotted ~33%. The weakest bore pair is hall x hollow at ~16%. The silhouette is a projection and therefore an UPPER bound on a rendered frame, so expect roughly a third of these on frame: netted x matted around 8%, hall x hollow around 5%. THE APPROVED DESIGN PREDICTED matted x knotted as the closest anastomosis pair at ~7%, and the replica disagrees — it is the strongest of the three, because knotted collapses to three nodes while matted still carries eighteen. A prediction that agrees with the sweep is worth nothing; this one already disagrees with the design it came from, and the disagreement is what found the fixture fault above.
dna.budget: chunk_extent 24 is 13,824 voxels against the shipped 1,728 — 8x — and the mesh march is one 8-corner lookup per voxel per tile. The carve is the real cost and it is bore-dependent: replicated over all sixteen tiles at the fixture's seed it totals 13.0M voxel writes, about 0.8M per tile. That is only affordable because carve_tunnel's sample spacing is now floored at a quarter of the carved radius on the rungs above 1.0; at the shipped half-voxel spacing bore=hollow alone sweeps the entire chunk about fifty times per tunnel. Four samples per radius cannot leave a seam between consecutive spheres, and the gate is `carve_radius_scale > 1.0`, so bore=tunnel and bore=thread evaluate the shipped expression unchanged. Do not reach for 40^3: that is 37x and will meet the 16-second rule.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` — a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find it. It now stamps config_<key> metadata, re-reads the overrides and compares a signature built from the same accessors the build calls (_merge_distance(), _bore_scale(), cave_seed, chunk_extent, both branch lengths, build_synchronously), so the signature cannot drift out of step with what reaches the generator. Equal signature returns before touching anything. A real change calls _rebuild(), which frees ONLY RhizomeCaveGenerator._owned — the CaveMesh and CaveCollision this script created — and re-runs the same build; a blanket free of get_children() is what cost three scripts a pass in an earlier wave. _ready reads the metadata BEFORE building, and on the grid's own ordering (config stamped at GridInteractablesComponent:1195, add_child at :1220, apply_grid_config deferred afterwards) the first build already has the right values and the deferred call finds nothing to do: exactly one build per spawn.
dna.still_note: Nothing in this scene runs _process. More usefully, the picture is unusually literal about the axis: the chunk starts solid and RhizomeVoxelChunk.get_density (:38) returns 1.0 out of bounds, so the outer faces of the box carry no surface of their own and the only geometry is the inner wall of the carved network, drawn cull_mode CULL_DISABLED (:384). The frame IS the graph as a set of tubes, and a tree and a knotted net are different objects on sight. The one thing a still cannot separate is the confound named in `note`: loopier and smaller arrive together.
dna.kin: isosurfaces wave 3, the field-provenance wave. metaballs owns `fusion` and `metaball_count`, gyroid_demo `intrusion` and `period`, mc_torus_sculpture `threshold`, queer_marching_cave `bulge`, mc_cave and mc_inside_cave `plumb` — all of them properties of a function being sampled. This is the only member whose field is carved rather than evaluated, which is why its two words are about a history (whether paths rejoined) and a tool (how wide the cut was).

rhizome_cave_demo.description: Rhizomatic cave — Deleuze-inspired branching cave generation using growth patterns + marching cubes.
rhizome_cave_demo.compute: HEAVY — CPU growth simulation + marching cubes
rhizome_cave_demo.name: rhizome_cave_demo
rhizome_cave_demo.qfep_connection: A cave grown as rhizome — Deleuze's centerless, multiply-connected figure carved into stone by branching growth and marching cubes. The post-crisis answer in geology: after the foundations fell, you build spaces with no single entrance and no privileged path, structures that are all middle. A world you enter anywhere and cross more than one way — formalization's limits turned into an architecture of the between.
rhizome_cave_demo.map_note: The Rhizome Network hall opts into passage_study:true: authored walkable circuits and an upper return in a 31 by 37 metre hall. Default placements retain the stochastic cave. The companion grower is a different model.

flex_connector.name: Flex Connector
flex_connector.description: Two rigid poles anchored in grey side walls run into a bounded region and stop on its boundary. A red flexible cord joins their ends, and the piece asks whether the join can be made without leaving the region. approach sets where the poles arrive from, different sides or the same side; slack sets how much cord there is, from taut to a little over twice the straight-line distance. The cord is solved by bisection to the requested length, sampled, and every sample tested against the region; the part that leaves is drawn in amber and the plate reports FITS INSIDE or ESCAPES with the count. The two approaches are not two decorations of one situation: at the same relative slack, a cord fits easily when the poles arrive from opposite sides and escapes immediately when they arrive from the same side, because the chord is short and a small proportional bulge is a large absolute one. Readable in code via fits_inside(), samples_outside() and cord_ratio().

predicted_degeneracy.basis: GROUNDED IN THE PROBE, not forecast blind, and said before any pixel was measured. probe_flex_connector reports samples-outside of taut=0 easy=47 loose=47 coiled=47 at approach=same. Those last three have IDENTICAL containment verdicts and identical plate wording except the ratio figure, so they differ only in how far the amber bulge reaches: the cord is 1.55x against 2.1x the chord, a bulge roughly 35% longer. The cord is a thin tube, maybe 4% of the subject's projected area, and the differing portion is perhaps a third of it. FRAME = 0.04 * 0.35 = 1.4%. It is a LOWER BOUND like every prediction in this corpus, which have under-predicted by 1.5x to 6.7x.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS. Below ~1.4% the likely causes in order are (a) the bisection converging to the same control point for both values, which would be a real bug and is checkable by printing cord_ratio() -- the probe already reports it; (b) the escaped cord being drawn outside the capture crop, since the bulge leaves the region by design and the AABB anchor is sized to the walls, not the bulge; (c) a slack value the SLACKS dictionary does not carry, which fails in silence and leaves the default. Read <out>/_rejects.json and open the PNGs.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, and this is the third time of asking -- the two artifacts before this one both had a structural degeneracy I failed to name, so the habit is now to look for one first. Expect slack to be CONDITIONAL on approach, in the opposite direction to the obvious: at approach=different the axis has room to work across all four values because the chord is long, while at approach=same it saturates after the first step and three of its four values are near-twins. A mean over the cross product will therefore understate it. Read the per-pair rows grouped by approach, never the axis mean.

MolecularDesigner.name: Molecular Designer
MolecularDesigner.description: Automatic catalogue assembly exhibit: reusable parts move towards authored body, furniture and molecular-style arrangements. Bonds are declared connections; chemical valence is not simulated.

markov_blanket_room.name: Markov Blanket Room
markov_blanket_room.description: A cubic lattice classified into internal cells, blanket cells and external cells, built at room scale so a body stands inside the interior. It does not draw a membrane and call it a boundary: a breadth-first search runs from the centre, blocked by blanket cells only, and asks whether any path reaches the rim. The verdict plate reports SEPARATED or REACHED, and when a path exists it is drawn in full. leak removes blanket cells (sealed, pinhole, breach, dissolved) and shell decides how the boundary was built at all (shell, patchy, double, none). patchy is the instructive value: a boundary with a third of its cells missing usually still separates, because separation is about paths and not about coverage. The search result is readable from code via is_separated() and escape_path_length(), so the claim can be checked without reading pixels.

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction measured in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. A pinhole removes the blanket cells within radius 1.9 of one picked cell: about 25 of roughly 1100 blanket cells, 2.3% of the shell. Those cells are orange cubes at 0.78 of cell size; the shell occupies perhaps 38% of the subject's projected area, so the removed cells are 0.023 x 0.38 = 0.9% of subject. The verdict plate also changes colour and wording, but it is small in frame and the arithmetic deliberately ignores it.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS. Below ~0.9% the likely causes in order are (a) the pinhole falling on the far side of the shell and being occluded by the near side, which is a FIXTURE problem and not an axis problem -- change the standpoint, not the design; (b) the Label3D not rendering headless, so the verdict change is invisible; (c) the sweep setting leak to a value the enum does not carry, which fails in silence. Read <out>/_rejects.json before writing anything down.
predicted_degeneracy.note: sealed <-> pinhole is the smallest pair BY DESIGN and it is the pair that carries the argument: both still report SEPARATED, so the picture barely changes while the question does not change at all. The honest risk is that this reads as INERT when it is merely SMALL. Do not record a dead verdict without running probe_anamorphic.py -- five of seven dead verdicts in this corpus were false, and a shell is exactly the kind of subject whose far side is invisible from one standpoint. By contrast leak sealed <-> dissolved should be enormous: most of the shell gone plus a drawn yellow path plus a recoloured plate.
predicted_degeneracy.measured_2026_10_13: SWEPT. shell BITES at 5.38% frame / 58.88% focus. leak is CONDITIONAL, and the prediction above named the WRONG DEGENERACY -- which is the only reason the pass was worth running. I predicted the closest pair would be sealed<->pinhole at 0.9%; it measured 23.49%, twenty-six times higher, consistent with every prediction in this corpus being a lower bound. The real degeneracy is STRUCTURAL and I did not foresee it: at shell=none there is no blanket, so removing blanket cells changes nothing and every leak pair measures exactly 0.00%. Wherever a blanket exists, leak measures 23-52% (dissolved vs sealed 52.58% at shell=patchy). That is correct behaviour, not a dead axis -- leak is only defined where there is something to leak from -- so read the per-pair rows grouped by shell, never the axis mean. No rejects file was written, so no value was refused on assignment.

boolean_neck.name: Boolean Neck
boolean_neck.description: A bar with a row of spheres subtracted from it, biting in from above and below so the material narrows to a neck at each bite. It is genuinely CSG: a CSGCombiner3D holding a CSGBox3D with CSGSphere3D cutters in subtraction mode, with the cutters drawn again as faint ghosts so the operation stays legible and not only its result. gap sets how deep the bites go and row how they are arranged. The claim is that a difference operation is also a connectivity operation: nobody cuts the bar in two, they only make a hole slightly too big. Measured along the bar, the remaining half-thickness gives the thinnest neck and the number of pieces, so the threshold can be read rather than guessed: open 40.5 mm, narrow 14.4, pinched 1.35, then severed into five. Godot will not report the component count of a CSG result, so that number is derived analytically from the same cutter array that positions the spheres. One source, two readings, which is noted in the script as the known drift risk it is.

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. Both values place eight cutters in two opposed rows; only the spacing along the bar differs, four evenly spread against two tight couples. At gap=open the bites are shallow (measured thinnest neck 40.5 mm of a 90 mm bar) so the silhouette barely moves and the change is in where the scallops sit, not how deep. Scallop edges are maybe 12 percent of the bar's projected area and about a sixth of that area shifts. FRAME = 0.12 * 0.17 = 2.0 percent.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS. Below about 2 percent the likely causes in order are (a) CSG failing to rebuild between variants, which would make every frame the default -- check that the bar is not identical across ALL values, not just this pair; (b) the ghost spheres at alpha 0.12 washing out the scallops they are meant to explain; (c) a row value ROWS does not contain, which fails in silence. Read the rejects file and open the PNGs.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, because the two artifacts before this one both had one I failed to name. Expect row to be CONDITIONAL on gap, and in a way that cuts against intuition: at gap=severed the bar changes COLOUR, turning amber the moment it is in pieces, so every row value shares that flip and the axis mean will be inflated by a difference that is not row's doing. Conversely at gap=severed the piece COUNT differs sharply by row -- measured 5 for even against 2 for single -- so the plate text differs while the silhouette may not. Read the per-pair rows grouped by gap, never the axis mean.

bridge_cut.name: Bridge Cut
bridge_cut.description: A small graph at arm's length. A bridge is an edge whose removal disconnects the graph, and the word does real work: most edges are not bridges. So the cut axis carries its own control. bridge removes the edge that matters and the nodes recolour into the two components they fall into; chord removes an edge that looks exactly as important and nothing happens at all. You cannot tell which is which by looking, which is the point. graph=theta goes further, two hubs joined by three disjoint paths, where every edge lies on a cycle and there is no bridge to cut; asked for one the artifact cuts nothing and says so. Components are computed by union-find over the surviving edges on every change, and the bridge is found by definition rather than hard-coded, by removing each edge in turn and asking whether the component count rose. The cut edge stays as a short red stub, because an edge that vanishes cannot be seen to have been the one that mattered. Readable in code via component_count() and has_bridge().

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction measured in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. Both values leave the graph in one piece, so no node changes colour and the plate reads STILL CONNECTED either way -- the ONLY difference is that one of seven edges is drawn as a 45%-length red stub instead of a full grey rod. Rods are roughly 9% of the subject's projected area; one of seven of them, shortened by half and recoloured grey(0.65) to red(0.85,0.20,0.22), is 0.09 * (1/7) * 1.0 for the vacated half plus a strong hue change on the rest. FRAME = about 1.2%.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN. Below ~1.2% the likely causes in order are (a) the chord chosen by _find_special being hidden behind a node from the canonical standpoint, which is a FIXTURE problem -- move the camera, not the design; (b) the sweep setting cut to a value CUTS does not contain, which fails in silence and leaves the default; (c) the artifact being under ~6% of frame at hand scale, so a real change is diluted past the measure. Read <out>/_rejects.json and open the PNGs before writing anything down.
predicted_degeneracy.measured_2026_10_13: SWEPT TWICE. Final: cut BITES at 20.32% frame / 49.71% focus, graph BITES at 19.14% / 76.96%, no twins, no inert, cut correctly CONDITIONAL on graph. THE FIRST SWEEP FOUND A REAL DEFECT and the prediction below is why it was recognised rather than explained away: cut=chord rendered BYTE-IDENTICAL to cut=none at graph=chain and graph=tree, flagged as a twin pair. The cause was not the axis. A chain and a tree have no chord -- every edge is a bridge -- so there was nothing to remove, and the artifact stayed SILENT about it while already announcing the mirror case (NO BRIDGE TO CUT in a theta graph). An artifact whose answer to an undefined question is to look unchanged cannot be told apart from a broken one. Adding NO CHORD TO CUT and NOTHING TO CUT removed both twins and took cut from 10.24% to 20.32%: making the conditional case speak doubled the axis. I predicted the WRONG structural pair again -- I named none<->bridge at theta, the measured one was chord<->none at chain and tree -- but predicting that there WOULD be a structural pair, and that it would be conditional rather than inert, is what made the twin report readable in a minute instead of being filed as a dead axis.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, because last time I predicted the wrong kind of pair and the sweep had to teach me: markov_blanket_room's real degeneracy was structural (leak does nothing at shell=none) and I had only predicted a small one. The structural pair here is cut none <-> bridge at graph=theta. A theta graph has no bridge, so there is nothing to remove and the two frames differ ONLY in the plate text, NO BRIDGE TO CUT against STILL CONNECTED. Expect that pair near the floor of the measure, well under 1%, and expect it to be CONDITIONAL rather than inert: cut is only defined where a bridge exists, exactly as leak was only defined where a blanket exists. Read the per-pair rows grouped by graph, never the axis mean.

edge_ground_synthesis.name: EdgeGroundSynthesis
edge_ground_synthesis.description: The trilogy synthesis: incompleteness, bias, contradiction, rhizome each turn from problem into design material feeding one constructive core.

accountability_ledger.name: AccountabilityLedger
accountability_ledger.description: An illustrative ledger cycles through paired, prewritten design choices and exclusions. Six visible examples form a bounded buffer while the entry count continues. It does not record visitor decisions or persist a visit.

assembly_return.name: The Body That Returned
assembly_return.description: Two standing bodies reconstruct the original Assembly body and the latest locally kept body, including coordinates and connections. A changed connection is turquoise. With no record, the second bay stays empty. The hand trajectory and intention are not retained.
assembly_return.qfep_connection: An actual alteration survives the room that produced it. The same points and connection count can conceal different connected groups. Both graphs are retained; the gesture and reasons remain absent.

film_body_aperture.name: A passage follows a body
film_body_aperture.description: The wall opens near an approaching body and moves its gap as the body walks along it.
interactions: Look at the screen to play.
Pause, replay, step or turn the view.
film_body_aperture.qfep_connection: Actual per-slat targets, clearance rule and hinge transforms on a private copy. Shows target poses rather than live easing and visitor detection.

approach_wall.description: A wall of slats that is closed and opens exactly where you approach it, then closes again behind you. Not a door - a door has one hinge and one place it opens; this one makes way where your body is, so the aperture is a portrait of your approach. Opens by swinging, sinking or parting.
approach_wall.name: Approach Wall
approach_wall.qfep_connection: A boundary that is a function of who is standing at it is not the same object as a boundary. The wall keeps its identity - every slat is where it always was - and stops being an obstacle, which is the chapter's question about invariants asked from the far side.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: At the canonical standpoint the wall is photographed with no visitor, so every value renders the SAME closed wall and all three should measure near zero. Photographed open, swing turns each slat about its inner edge (95 deg, so its face leaves the plane entirely) while slide_x moves it along the plane by up to a slat's width - both clear roughly two thirds of the aperture but only swing changes the silhouette's shading. slide_y sinks the slats and is the odd one out. This axis is expected to need a fixture holding a visitor at the wall; without one it is INERT for a reason that is about the capture, not the design.

measurements.measured_from: derived from width_m x height_m x thickness_m; the swing mode sweeps up to about 0.5 m out of the plane, which is why the footprint claims 2 cells of depth

carve_grid.description: A solid lattice of small cubes standing in the way, which loses every cube your body touches, so walking through cuts a tunnel that stays cut. Translation performed with your legs: the corridor is the only record of where you went. Nothing in it moves on its own.
carve_grid.name: Carve Grid
carve_grid.qfep_connection: The trace is the only evidence, and it is shaped like the body that made it rather than like the rule that permitted it. Space here is not found and not given: it is subtracted, and by you.

measurements.measured_from: derived from the built extent: (cells - 1) * cell_m + (cell_m - gap_m), defaults 11 x 4 x 11 at 0.34 with a 0.05 gap

approach_scale.description: A field of blocks set too close together to walk between. The ones near you scale down about their own centres until the gap is wide enough to pass, and grow back once you are through, so the size of the room is a function of how close you are standing.
approach_scale.name: Approach Scale
approach_scale.qfep_connection: Scale as the reciprocal of the grower block: there the world grows into you and the transformation is a threat, here it withdraws and the same arithmetic is hospitality. Nothing about the operation changes - only which way the factor runs, and who it is measured from.

measurements.measured_from: derived from (cols - 1) * spacing_m + block_m, defaults 3 x 3 at 1.5 spacing with 1.15 blocks

film_foundation_state.name: A response can remember
film_foundation_state.description: A teaching clock moves a cube while two physical gate models compare present proximity with a retained visit. FRAME, APPROACH / AWAY and RESET let the visitor separate the events.

Your choices remain when you look away. DEMO returns to the demonstration.

pusher_block.description: A red cube that translates back and forth along one axis, physically pushing the player into pits. Uses AnimatableBody3D for proper physics collision. The translation transformation made dangerous.
pusher_block.name: Pusher Block
pusher_block.qfep_connection: Translation as force — the simplest transformation becomes the most direct threat. The block does to the player what the player does to objects.

free_ball_launcher.description: A mouth at the side of a room that throws a heavy ball across it on its own clock, for ever, whether anybody is standing there or not. The ball is real physics - it arcs, lands, rolls, bounces and drops into whatever pit is under it - and it shoves a visitor it reaches rather than wounding them, because in Trans_Pit the pit does the killing and the hazards only move you. It never aims, never leads and never corrects.
free_ball_launcher.name: Free Ball Launcher
free_ball_launcher.qfep_connection: A hazard that aims at you has already agreed that you are the point. This one has not, and that is the whole of it: the room becomes dangerous without becoming about you, which is a harder thing for a room to be and the only honest way to be thrown by a transformation you were not the subject of.

measurements.measured_from: the barrel and collar only, standing at mount_m; the balls in flight are pooled and are not part of the mount. Front clearance of 6 cells is the throw, not the body: a level throw at 7 m/s falls about a metre in the first 3.2 m and then rolls, so a launcher facing a wall a metre away fires perfectly and does nothing.

grower_block.description: A cube that pulses between tiny and huge, physically pushing the player as it grows. When small you can pass, when large it fills the corridor and squeezes you into the pit. Color shifts from green (safe) to red (danger).
grower_block.name: Grower Block
grower_block.qfep_connection: Scale as pressure — the uncanny transformation that changes everything while appearing to change nothing. You don't move; the world moves into you.

transformation_airlock.qfep_connection: The same operations can occupy a route or make room. Transformation changes relations between the panels, the frame and a body; the fixed frame makes those changes observable.
interactions: Approach from either side to open
Wait beside the opening and compare the three movements
Walk through; leave the clearance area to see the sequence reverse

Configurable motion can hold it still, translate, rotate, scale or combine these operations. Bobbing and scale pulses can use sine or linear interpolation. A visitor can watch before approaching; hold:demo disables collection and keeps the specimen available for repeated observation.

catalyst_pedestal.name: Catalyst Pedestal

dna.was: zero exports: a fixed ROYGBIV double arc, Newton's seven bands hard-coded as if the spectrum had seams
dna.note: total arc width is held constant across banding, so the knob argues about how many names the spectrum gets, not how big it is; substance turns an optical event with no location into an arch that could hold a shadow, which contradicts the artifact's own truth line on purpose

SpectrumVisualizer.capacity: SEE that the color wheel is a perceptual invention — magenta is the seam where the brain closes what physics leaves open
SpectrumVisualizer.description: The visible spectrum bends from a line into a circle. Wavelength-to-color animation phases between linear layout (physics) and circular layout (perception). Magenta dots fill the gap that physics leaves empty — magenta is not a spectral color, it is the brain's invention to close the loop. The color wheel is a lie the brain tells to make the spectrum feel complete.
SpectrumVisualizer.gamwell_reference: Color spaces (RGB, HSV, Lab), perceptual color science
interactions: watch auto-animation (linear to circular phase)
observe magenta dots appearing in the gap
SpectrumVisualizer.name: SpectrumVisualizer
SpectrumVisualizer.qfep_connection: Lambda between physics and perception — the linear spectrum is pure F (physics, ordered by wavelength). The circular wheel is F + E (perception, with magenta invented to fill the gap). The animation IS the lambda sweep from one to the other.

dna.default: structure=named returns the .tres palette list unchanged - _structured_colors is the identity function at this value, so all 10 existing placements render the same twelve cultural sets, in the same order, with the same labels.
dna.was: Twelve palettes read straight out of color_palettes.tres and laid out as grabbable sticker grids. The .tres already held twenty named cultural sets (frida_kahlo, harlem_renaissance, bauhaus_palette, stonewall_freedom, rothko_chapel ...) and the registry declared none of it - the data was a parameter space nobody had turned.
dna.note: The axis is WHERE A SET COMES FROM: a history somebody is answerable for (named), or a construction the colour wheel hands you from one hue (the other four). Non-named values keep each palette's dominant hue (max s*v) and every sticker's own saturation and value, so the twelve sets stay twelve distinguishable sets - the light survives, the history does not. TWO AXES DECLINED. (1) Layout: the sibling three files over, grabcolorcollection, already carries `arrangement` (grid|ramp|ring|stack) and its ramp/ring already sort by luminance and hue; a second word for the sibling's axis would split one vocabulary in two. (2) What the sticker SAYS (hex|name|both|none) is the axis this artifact's truth statement deserves - and the rig is 6 m wide, so a Label3D on a 0.195 m sticker is a few pixels in any still. An axis only a reader standing in the room can see cannot be argued for with one PNG.
