ball_painting_demo.description: Shared painting canvas with optional automation. tools:spray replaces pigment balls with grabbable, trigger-operated spray cans and soft grainy deposits; distance, angle and time shape the mark. Other placements retain balls.
ball_painting_demo.name: ball_painting_demo

dna.default: priming=white - PRIMING_COLOR['white'] is Color(1, 1, 1, 1), the exact literal reset_canvas() used to pass, so the same splat runs at the same size with the same argument and the shipped path is unchanged down to the call. _settle_priming() walks up for config_priming metadata and every placement of both tokens carries none, so the loop runs to the top of the tree, finds nothing, and leaves the export where it was. No node is added, no .tscn is touched, no process is started, and nothing outside reset_canvas() reads the axis. The four references - Color_Paint (ball_painting_demo:180:0.5), Color_Sphere, Corridor_Color_Paint, Kernel_Demo2, plus the Curation_Bay_color_0 station collection - pass no priming key.
dna.was: no export on the axis at all, and a scriptless .tscn ROOT on both scenes that run this script, which is why the runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. reset_canvas() splatted a hard-coded Color(1, 1, 1, 1) across the whole 4 x 2.5 m surface - a white ground handed over as though white were the absence of a decision rather than a recent and specific one.
dna.note: ONE SCRIPT, TWO TOKENS - this corpus's most common hidden family, found again. paper_draw_surface.gd is the entire visible body of both ball_painting_demo (a framed canvas with thirty grabbable pigment balls on a shelf) and drawing_paper (the same surface as a sheet with a pen), so both are declared with the same word and the same values, and they should MEASURE ALIKE. That is the check on the shared vocabulary, not a coincidence to explain away afterwards. Reached with NO new root script: GridInteractablesComponent stamps config_<key> on the artifact root at line 1195, before the add_child at line 1220, therefore before any _ready in the subtree - so an ancestor walk reads the token one call EARLIER than apply_grid_config could and the ground is laid once instead of being laid white and then relaid. The consequence, stated: priming is a spawn-time choice only. There is no runtime re-priming, because the scriptless root has no apply_grid_config to call, and adding a script to a shipped scriptless root was judged the riskier change for four placements when the metadata path already works.
dna.declined_word: 'ground' is the obvious art term and is already taken, one day earlier and in this same colour sequence, by flashlight_demo (white | swatch | relief | mirror | none) where it means the surface a beam is demonstrated AGAINST. That is a different question - what light falls on, not what the first mark falls on - and only 'white' would have carried over. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary, so this took a word of its own.
dna.harness: the axis is on the SURFACE and not on the balls, and that was a measurement decision rather than a taste one. The thirty pigment balls are 3 to 9 cm across (grab_sphere's SphereMesh radius 0.025, scaled 0.65 to 1.8) for about 0.085 m2 of projected area, while the sweep fits a 4.15 x 2.8 x 2.1 m box from roughly 17 m - so the balls land near 0.08% of frame and any axis on their colour would have come back INERT by dilution, which is the random_walk_collection failure (a huge change across a share of frame too small to measure). The surface is about 7-8% of frame at that fit and every value covers all of it, so no framing hint is needed. One pre-existing dependency to know about: the canvas IS a nested SubViewport texture (render_target_update_mode = ALWAYS, clear NEVER, transparent_bg), so if it fails to render headless the canvas is blank in every frame - that condition predates this axis and would make the artifact unphotographable, not the axis inert.

ball_painting_demo.qfep_connection: The brush is a grabbable ball whose tip is a raycast, its hits quantized to a snap grid on the paper: the canvas records not intention but wherever the held sphere's ray happened to land, mark-making pushed one joint away from the hand.

configuration_notes.automated: Shared painting canvas with optional automation. tools:spray replaces pigment balls with grabbable, trigger-operated spray cans and soft grainy deposits; distance, angle and time shape the mark. Other placements retain balls.

dna.default: harmony=spectral - SHORT-CIRCUITS. _gradient_colors() returns the literal seven-stop array and never reaches a hue calculation, so the gradient texture is built from the same PackedColorArray at the same seven offsets, and _light_color() returns the shipped `Color.from_hsv(fmod(t + gradient_offset, 1.0), 0.8, 1.0)` line verbatim, so the three omni lights keep their own hue sweep rather than being pulled onto the wall colours. The CSG geometry is not touched by this axis at all: same 8 combiners, same radii, same wall_thickness, same collision. All 4 placements (Color_Walls, Corridor_Color_Walls, TestMap_Unused_16 and the Curation_Bay_color_4 curation_station roster) carry the bare token with no config keys, GridInteractablesComponent does not call apply_grid_config for a token that carries none, and capture_anchor defaults to "off" so no placement gains a node either.
dna.was: ten exports and not one argument among them. animation_speed is a shader clock (TIME * animation_speed in the fragment stage) and glow_intensity/emission_strength are strengths; cone_mode, start_radius, end_radius, num_segments, segment_length and wall_thickness are the tunnel's dimensions. A map could make the hallway longer, wider, brighter or faster and could not make it say anything else - the colour you walk through, which is the whole subject, was seven Color literals welded into setup_hallway(). apply_grid_config accepted five of the sizes and then called setup_hallway() UNCONDITIONALLY at the bottom, on any call including one naming nothing it owns: the force_pad fault, now guarded.
dna.harness_note: THIS ARTIFACT OWNS NO MeshInstance3D. Every visible thing in it is a CSGCombiner3D holding two CSGCylinder3D. GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb handles CSGShape3D (via get_meshes()[1]) and so grounds it correctly in maps - but capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D ONLY and falls back to AABB(-0.5, 0, -0.5, 1, 1, 1). Left alone the sweep would place its camera about five metres from the origin, which is inside the mouth of a sixteen-metre tunnel of radius 4.3, and photograph a fragment of tube wall - the rhizomatic_maze_space failure, found by reading the harness before declaring rather than by looking at the tiles afterwards. dna.fixture.capture_anchor adds ONE BoxMesh at the tunnel's true extent (2r x 2r x num_segments*segment_length, centred at -span/2) with layers = 0, so it renders to nothing and exists only to be measured. It is a fixture and not an axis, and it is OFF by default, precisely because an always-on anchor would also enter _compute_local_aabb and could move the grounding of four standing placements. The general fact for whoever meets the next CSG artifact: the sweep's AABB helper is behind the grid's, and a CSG-only artifact reports a 1 m box rather than nothing, so it never trips the `size.length() < 0.001` rescue either.
dna.still_note: animation_speed is declared as a FIXTURE at 0.0 for example_8_3's reason. The fragment stage reads `fract(coord + gradient_offset + TIME * animation_speed * 0.1)`, so at the shipped speed of 1.0 four variants photographed after a fixed settle would be four different PHASES of the gradient as well as four different palettes, and the critic would be handed phase difference dressed as axis difference. At 0.0 the TIME term drops out and gradient_offset alone places the ramp, identically for every value. The shader material is applied as material_override on each combiner, so the OUTER wall carries the same z-driven gradient as the inner one and the axis is legible from outside the tube - which is the only place a fit-to-AABB camera can stand. If the subject still reads small in the tiles, dna.framing is the lever and not the axis: the extent is 8.6 x 8.6 x 16 m and fit-by-diagonal on a long box under-fills the frame.
dna.note: harmony is which rule chooses the colours the walk passes through, and it is this file's own truth line made switchable: 'a hallway of color is not a hallway with color on it - it is a space where color becomes the architecture itself' is a claim the artifact could only ever assert, in one spectrum, once. The three new rules are DERIVED from the shipped gradient's own first stop (Color(1.0, 0.2, 0.2), hue 0.0) rather than chosen beside it, and all four keep seven stops at the same seven offsets. complementary alternates a hue with its opposite, so every stop cancels its neighbour and the passage is between two colours with nothing in the middle but grey. analogous holds the whole tunnel inside a twelfth of the circle - colour that changes without ever becoming another colour. monochrome withdraws hue entirely and leaves value, which is the counterfactual to the artifact's own title: the same architecture, walked the same way, arguing nothing about colour at all.
dna.kin: `banding` was CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, and rainbow is this file's declared predecessor in its own @identity ('follows rainbow (static arc vs immersive tunnel)'), so the refusal is worth the words. rainbow's roygbiv|six|continuous|two counts how many names the spectrum gets, and it can, because rainbow draws SEPARATE ARC MESHES and a band there has an edge. Here the colours live in a GradientTexture1D sampled per fragment, which interpolates linearly between stops: seven, six and continuous all render as one smooth wash and the axis would report itself inert. Making it bite would mean giving the Gradient a CONSTANT interpolation mode - inventing seams this hallway has never had - which is taking a word without its answers. `palette` (platonicsolids: pride|trans|mono) was declined too: it asks WHOSE colours these are, a question about politics, and this asks BY WHAT RULE, a question about colour theory. Same subject, different argument, so a different word.
dna.declines: the taper (start_radius 4.0 -> end_radius 1.5, which the @identity names as the critical parameter - 'whether the tunnel feels like entering or being swallowed') is a real second axis and is deliberately NOT declared in this pass. It MOVES THE EXTENT, and the extent is exactly what this artifact cannot currently be trusted to report to the bench; a geometry axis should wait until capture_anchor has been proven by a sweep. cone_mode is a dead export - nothing in the file reads it, and _generate_cone_segments lerps between the radii unconditionally - which is worth repairing before it is ever declared.

dna.still_note: AWAITING A RE-SWEEP ON A FIXED BENCH. Two separate faults were found on 2026-08-05, and the previous still_note was wrong about both. (1) THE AXIS WAS HOLLOW. The note claimed the three readings were implemented; they were not. commit 1fe54b36a says in its own message that it implemented them, and its diff never touches _add_glass_wall - the export, the MIXTURES allow-list and a thirty-line header existed and no function read the variable, so the byte-identical frames were honest. Now implemented as the header specifies: bench falls through the shipped material untouched, light sets alpha 1.0 and BLEND_MODE_ADD so the three 60-degree panes sum to a white core, retina goes opaque and unlit and builds no OmniLight3D at all. (2) THE GREEN WAS THE BENCH, AND IT IS NOT THIS ARTIFACT'S PROBLEM - it is on every sheet the rig has ever published, riemann_pump included. NatureRenderer is an autoload; its _find_world_environment walks the tree matching on CLASS, found capture_config_sweep's own staging WorldEnvironment, took its Environment resource and tweened fog_light_color to Color(0.6,0.6,0.6).lerp(Color(0.55,0.7,0.5), density), which at density 1.0 is exactly the measured RGB(130,165,118) by ratio (0.786/0.714 against 0.788/0.715). density comes from EcosystemManager restoring user://ecosystem_progression.json - the developer's own save, all 25 sequences complete - so the bench's background colour was a function of how much of the game the operator had played. Fixed in capture_config_sweep.gd: the Environment now lives on Camera3D.environment with no WorldEnvironment node for the bridge to find, the SubViewport owns its World3D, and the ecosystem autoloads are stood down. Not re-swept here - captures are serialised centrally. Expect a strong bite; if it still measures low, suspect the axis, not the fog.

declines.pigment: Legacy mixture axis only (not layout=planes, added 2026-10-01 with pale backing and layered alpha tint). A fourth reading, refused. Subtractive mixing needs a white ground to subtract FROM, and a room of freestanding partitions has none - the light behind a cyan pane is whatever the next pane happens to be, so a pane that removed red would go black against half the room and read as an unlit slab rather than as ink. visual_color_mixing, the standing bench of the same sequence, solved this with a white TABLE. The architectural member of the family cannot borrow that answer, so it does not borrow the word.

dna.default: start=empty. The instruction waiting for its draftsman, which is the artifact's claim: the choice in each square belongs to whoever stands here. This artifact is new and has zero placements, so the default is a design choice with no preservation duty.
dna.note: DERIVED from the @export_enum line by tools/apply_dna_block.py (values empty|drawn), then re-indented by hand to the file's tabs; the values were not retyped. The axis is what the wall ARGUES before anyone touches it: an instruction with no execution, or one execution already on the wall. `drawn` is AUTHORED by hand in the script's DRAWN_SHEET (each row mirrors left to right with the diagonals swapped, except one pair in row 4), not generated: there is no RNG in the file, so the two tiles are two fixed pictures. columns and rows are exported and reachable from a token but are NOT axes: they change the size of the wall, not its argument. Nothing interactive shows in a still; the press is the probe's to prove (commons/testing/probe_wall_drawing_291.gd), not the sweep's.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: REGISTERED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE. A two-value axis has one pair, so it is also the closest. The drawn sheet has 20 straight lines (11 V, 9 H) at 0.296 x 0.016 m = 0.00474 m2 each, 0.0947 m2, and 20 diagonals at 0.4026 x 0.016 m = 0.00644 m2 each, 0.1288 m2: 0.2235 m2 of light chalk on the black face. The face is 3.85 x 2.20 = 8.47 m2, so the lines are 2.64% of it. The plate's last line also changes ('0 of 40 squares drawn' to 'all 40 squares drawn'), about 0.68 x 0.037 m with maybe half the glyph pixels different, under 0.02 m2, adding about 0.1%. The canonical camera fits by the DIAGONAL, and a 3.85 x 2.20 m flat wall seen at yaw 0.62 fills about 40% of frame, so about 2.75% x 0.40 = 1.1% of frame pixels differ. The difference is light on near-black, the largest contrast the scene has, so a focus metric on the hottest pixels should read far higher than the area share. A LOWER BOUND like every prediction in this corpus. If the sweep comes back BELOW 1.1%, suspect the harness before the axis: a 1.6 cm line across a frame about 5 m wide is 2-3 px at 512 px and can alias away, and a fit-by-diagonal on this wide flat body may leave the grid too small, which dna.framing below 1.0 would fix.

wall_drawing_291.name: Wall Drawing 291
wall_drawing_291.description: A black wall ruled into 30 cm squares, 8 across and 5 up, the lowest row half a metre above the floor. After Sol LeWitt, Wall Drawing 291 (1976), whose instruction the chapter 'Regularity' in 10 PRINT CHR$(205.5+RND(1)); : GOTO 10 sets beside the one-line program (p. 81): a 30 cm grid on a black wall, one line bisecting each square (vertical, horizontal, diagonal right or diagonal left), every square filled, and the direction in each square left to the draftsman. The program flips between two diagonals; the instruction offers four directions and leaves the choosing to a person. Here that person is the visitor. Every square is its own press target. The first press draws a vertical line in light chalk; each further press turns it, vertical to horizontal to diagonal right to diagonal left and back to vertical. A drawn square is never blank again. The plate reads the rule in paraphrase and keeps a count that describes rather than grades: 'N of 40 squares drawn', then 'all 40 squares drawn'. START AGAIN clears the wall. There is no randomness anywhere in the code; whatever irregularity the wall ends up with came from a hand.
interactions: press a blank square: it gets a vertical line
press a drawn square again: the line turns, vertical to horizontal to diagonal right to diagonal left, and never goes back to blank
fill all forty and watch the plate change from a count to 'all 40 squares drawn'
press START AGAIN and draft a different wall under the same rule
walk up to it already drafted: #start:drawn hangs one execution authored by hand
wall_drawing_291.token_note: `columns` and `rows` are BOTH listed in GridInteractablesComponent.CONFIG_PARAM_NAMES (the list at :16: `rows` in its first lines, `columns` under the art history gallery params, `cols` too), so `#columns:10#rows:6` arrives as values and not as the tutorial rotation shorthand. `cols` is accepted as an alias. If a count ever arrives as the boolean true (the shorthand misparse of an unlisted key), _count_value refuses it and keeps the current value instead of reading it as 1. columns clamps to 1..16 and rows to 1..10. `start` is word-valued (`empty` | `drawn`) and safe under any key. The default 8 x 5 needs no config. A config that changes columns or rows rebuilds the wall; a config that changes only start re-drafts the same wall in place, with no rebuild. Both clear what the visitor drew. A config that changes none of the three does nothing.
wall_drawing_291.map_note: A WALL WORK, 3.85 m wide at the default 8 x 5 (0.20 m black margin, 2.40 m grid, 0.25 m gutter, 0.80 m plate column, 0.20 m margin) and 2.20 m tall, presenting +Z with its base at y = 0 and all 6 cm of its thickness behind z = 0. NO BODY COLLIDER by contract; the press areas (40 push_button.tscn instances with their round meshes hidden, their cap bodies switched off at layer 0 / mask 0, and their area widened to a 27 x 27 cm box that runs from 5 cm in front of the face to 25 cm behind it, so a hand pushing through the collider-less wall stays one press) and START AGAIN's panel sit under nodes marked em_local_instrument, so the museum's seal walk does not read them as footprint. The press boxes reach 19 cm past the work's own back face, so a hand reaching through whatever backs it from the far side could press a square. The top row's centre is at 1.85 m and the bottom row's at 0.65 m: a standing hand reaches every square, and the desktop pointer (5 m ray) presses any of them from about a metre in front. Wants a front approach and room to step sideways along it. Placed 2026-09-16 in Pattern_Foundry (tiling, hall 1) at (21,36), rotation 180, against the row-37 wall, with sculpture_clear_rects [19,33,24,37] keeping dressing off its standing area. It uses no randomness, so it may stand before the randomness sequence: the exception comes from the visitor's hand.
wall_drawing_291.qfep_connection: LeWitt's sentence hands the direction of every line to the draftsman and then says nothing about how to choose. Most executions of 291 hide that choice inside a crew and a date; this wall puts it in the visitor's hand one square at a time, so the rule and the person carrying it out stand in the same room. The book reads the instruction beside 10 PRINT, where a coin flip decides each diagonal. Here nothing is flipped. Any pattern or any mess on the wall is a record of a body deciding, and START AGAIN keeps the decision open instead of sealing it into a finished object.

pattern_tile_puzzle.name: Pattern Tile Puzzle
pattern_tile_puzzle.description: Create patterns on a small tile grid. Watch them repeat across a carpet. Handmade meets computational - from textile traditions to pixel art.
pattern_tile_puzzle.qfep_connection: Pattern-making as play: paint a small tile, watch it repeat across a carpet, adjust, repeat. Handmade meets computational — the room where the abstract truth (a pattern is a tiled array) becomes a thing your hands discover by doing, the carpet answering every edit instantly.

dna.default: motif=blank, dyelot=natural - _motif_value() returns 0 for every cell, which is literally the old `row.append(0)`, and DYELOTS has no `natural` key so _apply_dyelot() returns before touching the palette literal. The 33 existing placements render byte for byte as before. Their tokens carry config (#p4m, #cursor, :270) so apply_grid_config DOES run for them, but neither key is present, so the has()+differs guard never fires a rebuild.
dna.was: an empty grid over an empty carpet in one fixed set of eight yarns - the artifact argued that a small decision is amplified by a symmetry rule, and then shipped with no decision made and one dye range to make it in, so every photograph of it showed the amplifier with nothing in it
dna.note: Both axes live on the SHARED script behind six registry tokens (pattern_tile_puzzle, _4x4, _mirror, _8x8, _brick, _herringbone), which differ only by config {tile_size, repeat_mode}. dna.default: taxonomy=table, chapter=all - both defaults are short-circuits, not recomputations. `table` returns the cell the legacy layout loop already computed, coordinate for coordinate, and every specimen keeps its Label3D at the same offset it always had; `all` admits the array unfiltered in source order, so the loop below sees exactly the array it always saw. All 7 grid placements (Array_Patterns, Corridor_Array_Patterns, Facade_Classical_Orders, Facade_Columns_Rhythm, Facade_Custom_Composition, Facade_Wall_Basics, Facade_Windows_Doors) plus the two curation_station#artifacts collections (Curation_Bay_array_tutorial_1, Curation_Bay_facades_0) pass neither key, and curation_station forwards nothing anyway. The ONE structural change: the twenty specimens and their labels now hang off a `Gallery` Node3D at the origin with an identity transform instead of being parented straight to the root, so a token arriving after _ready can drop them in one call - world positions are unchanged.
dna.was: two exports, `spacing` and `object_height`, both pure dimension, which is why the auto-runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Twenty procedural specimens with their recipes welded into one 240-line function, laid out in a 4x5 lattice with a name label each, and no way for a map to ask the gallery for less than all of it or for a different claim about how the twenty are related.
dna.note: taxonomy is what ORDER the display claims the family has; the members never change. table = the lattice, position IS the recipe's place and every member captioned. ladder = one ascending file, a grammar as a sequence going somewhere. stack = one column on one footprint, twenty descriptions of one object. heap = coordinates abandoned AND the captions withheld, the claim that the classification was ours and the forms never carried it. The captions are the pivot exactly as on the combine benches, and the axis bites hardest here because 'Coral Fingers' and 'Barnacle Sphere' are blue-grey lumps without their labels - the recipe that separates them was never in the picture to begin with. chapter is DERIVED, not written: the source's own row headers already group the twenty four at a time and each header names a class of operation, so _chapter_of reads the grouping off the index rather than restating it in a second list that could fall out of step. topology = the four that only move faces plus the bare seed they are measured against; organic = the four that make a sphere behave like a body; compound = the four where rules act on the OUTPUT of rules, the only place a grammar stops being a filter; decoration = the four that add material the surface did not have; bridge = the L-system and the cellular automaton wired in as operations.
dna.kin: taxonomy and its four values are taken CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER from combine_capsule / combine_sphere / combine_portals, and the ladder/stack/heap placement arithmetic and the _index_hash scatter are theirs unchanged, with object_height added back so the specimens stand on the floor this scene draws and those do not. Same apparatus - a generator's output laid out as a gallery - so it gets the same vocabulary rather than a private one. chapter is deliberately NOT `exhibit` (pattern_mill / pattern_machine_c: bolt|unit|operation|catalogue). That axis asks how much of a CLOSED set of seventeen wallpaper groups the goods put up; this one asks which of five open classes of operation is on the table, and `bolt` means nothing here. Borrowing the word while dropping half its list would claim a comparability that does not exist.
dna.fixture_note: no fixture needed for taxonomy - `heap` scatters from a hash of the index and never randf(), so every boot piles the same pile and the critic measures the axis rather than the noise. NOTE that the SPECIMENS are not all deterministic: several recipes select faces with random:0.12 / up_random and one seeds a cellular automaton at seed_value 42, so the finer forms differ between boots. That noise is common to every value of both axes and pre-dates this promotion; it is paintwork on a large layout change, not a confound, but it is the reason no verdict here should rest on small-percentage differences.
dna.still_note: the scene draws its OWN 14 x 16 floor plane, two DirectionalLight3Ds and a Camera3D, and the floor fills most of any frame. Expect a low subject percentage in every mode and read the bite against the specimens, not the frame. taxonomy separates on gross layout (a 4x5 lattice / a 14 m diagonal file / a 7.8 m column / a 1.3 m pile with no text) and should be unmissable; chapter removes sixteen of twenty objects for any value but `all` and re-centres the remaining four in the same lattice, which is a large change measured against a mostly-empty floor. Both are visible in a single still.
dna.registry_mismatch: FLAGGED, NOT FIXED. The scene it points at, res://commons/mesh_grammar/mesh_grammar_demo.tscn, contains none of that: it is a mesh-grammar gallery of twenty organic specimens (coral fingers, petal flowers, barnacle spheres, an L-system tree). Those Italian presets are real and live in commons/facade_parts/presets/ (26 JSON files, including villa_san_michele.json) behind facade_composer_demo.tscn, which no registry token points at. Two maps repeat the false description in their own text (Array_Patterns 'Classical facade presets and elements', Facade_Wall_Basics 'Italian presets showing zoning'). The axes here are DERIVED FROM THE CODE THAT ACTUALLY RUNS, not from the description, which is the only way a declaration can be honest; re-pointing the token or renaming it is a separate decision with 7 placements behind it.

dna.default: census=chorus - PRESERVES all seven placements exactly. _census_limit() returns GROUP_NAMES.size() at chorus, so `group_index % _census_limit()` is character for character the `group_index % GROUP_NAMES.size()` that shipped, at both call sites (the wall pass and the ceiling/floor pass). Critically, census clamps the GROUP ONLY: palette_id stays `group_index % PALETTES.size()` and the domain-texture seed stays `group_index * 7 + 1`, both on the RAW group_index. Clamping those too would have been tidier and would have changed Track_Symmetry, which is 164 rows deep and runs group_index past 50 - far beyond the seventeen - so every placement with more than 17 clusters would have been repainted. apply_grid_config is still assignment-only with no rebuild behind it, and an unrecognised census word is ignored rather than assigned, so a typo falls back to the shipped chorus instead of silently rendering group 0. The one placement that passes config (Cove_Display_Gallery, #cluster_size:3#tile_scale:4.0#emission_strength:1.0#grout_width:0.02) names no census key.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Four exports existed and every one of them is a size or a palette: cluster_size (a distance, the declared critical_parameter), tile_scale, emission_strength, grout_width. The artifact's actual claim was a modulus. `group_index % GROUP_NAMES.size()` dealt the seventeen wallpaper groups in IUC table order, one per cluster, forever, in every placement - and the seventeen are a CLOSED set (Fedorov: exactly seventeen ways a pattern can repeat in the plane, no eighteenth), so how many of them a room uses is a mathematical statement wearing the costume of a loop counter.
dna.note: one puts a single group on every surface of the whole walk while the palette and the domain motif keep changing cluster to cluster, because those are deliberately NOT clamped. That is the artifact's own truth line put under load: 'symmetry is not decoration' is an assertion until you hold the symmetry still and let the decoration run, and then it is a picture. pair is the minimum at which a comparison exists; triad is three; chorus is the shipped seventeen. Declined: a surface or coverage axis - walls only against the shipped walls + ceiling + floor enclosure - which is a real question this artifact could argue and would photograph badly, because from one fixed camera removing surfaces mostly changes how much of the FRAME is lit and the critic would read a fact about the camera as a verdict on the design. cluster_size stays a plain named float: 'how much space one symmetry occupies' is a continuum, not a set of names.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: paradox_stalker, on census (one | pair | triad | chorus), same word and same four values, taken because the question is the same one - how many distinct members are standing in the room - and resolved here against seventeen wallpaper groups instead of five humanoid bodies. Said plainly so nobody is surprised by the numbers: its chorus is five and this one's is seventeen, so the two will not measure alike in MAGNITUDE even though they measure alike in kind. The nearer-looking words were checked and rejected: `order` (ascend | descend | together, on animatedcubebuilder) is about the order of a construction in time, not the size of a repertoire, and `arrangement` (grid | ramp | ring | stack) is about layout in space. Its sibling pattern_atlas_gallery is NOT sharing this word - that artifact stands named traditions on plates and its question is curation and credit; this one deals a closed mathematical set onto architecture. Same room, different claim.
dna.stand_in: THIS ARTIFACT OWNS NO GEOMETRY. It is an operation on a host map's grid - it hunts the grid_system group, reads structure_component.cube_positions, and paints overlays onto cubes it did not build - so photographed alone it returned early and rendered a black frame. dna.host cannot fix it: the generic host builds a MultiMeshInstance3D, and this artifact needs a node in the grid_system group exposing cube_positions / cube_size / gutter. So the fallback lives in the artifact: with no host in the tree it now raises its own corridor (two walls, two cubes high, fifteen rows deep = five clusters at the default cluster_size, the shortest walk in which triad and chorus are still different rooms) and paints that. The branch cannot fire in any of the seven placements - every one is a token in a map, and a map always has a grid_system.
dna.measurement_risk: the stand-in corridor is 15 long against 5 wide and 4 tall, and the sweep fits by the union AABB's DIAGONAL, so the frame will be dominated by the length and the subject share is the number to check before believing any verdict here. No dna.framing is declared, because guessing one blind would be the same error in the other direction - set it from the first sweep's reported subject percentage, not from this note. On the axis itself: one against chorus repaints four of the five clusters and is the strong step; triad against chorus repaints two of five and is the weak one. Do not read a faint triad/chorus pair as a dead axis without checking one against chorus first.

kaleidoscope.name: Kaleidoscope
kaleidoscope.description: A small kaleidoscope on a low stand — a horizontal cylindrical brass-and-steel tube whose axis runs along +X, a smaller dark eyepiece at +X, and a flat disc at -X divided into pattern_segments emissive pie-wedge shards that alternate between three accent colors so the eye reads mirror_count-fold dihedral symmetry (D3 at default = 3 mirrors). A Portal-orange emissive accent torus rings the tube at its midpoint. In the lab's grammar the kaleidoscope is the DIHEDRAL SYMMETRY GROUP / REFLECTION ALGORITHM in object form: the wedge is the fundamental domain, the mirror_count is the group order, and the disc is the orbit. Change mirror_count and you change the group the prop embodies.

parameters.eyepiece_visible: Bool — render the eyepiece at +X (default true)
parameters.mirror_count: Order of the dihedral symmetry group 2-8 — 3 = D3 standard kaleidoscope (default 3)
parameters.pattern_radius: Pattern disc radius at -X end in meters (default 0.05)
parameters.pattern_segments: Number of pattern wedges in the disc 2-24 (default 6)
parameters.accent_color: Tube accent ring color (default Portal orange)

thread_loom.name: Follow the Thread — hand loom
thread_loom.description: Take the shuttle from the lit side, carry it through the opening, then press its trigger or BEAT. PLAIN/TWILL and the lift buttons affect future passes. PASS supplies a guided desktop alternative. UNDO removes one pass; RESET clears the sample. Geometry represents interlacement; yarn tension and friction are not simulated.

dna.default: group=unset - _ready() still returns before building anything when neither a config_path nor a group is named, which is what every existing placement is: 10 bare `pattern_artifact` tokens across 6 maps (Symmetry_Group, Track_Symmetry x2, Trial_gate10_21, Trial_gate8_sym_size x2, Trial_gate8_sym_type x2, Trial_gate8_sym_typeM x2), not one of them passing a config. They render nothing today and render nothing after this change - byte for byte the same empty floor slot. apply_grid_config now returns without rebuilding unless a key it recognises arrived, ignores a group name that is not in the list rather than assigning it, and never rebuilds before _ready has built once (it used to _clear() and _build() unconditionally, which would have double-built any placement that ever did pass a config).
dna.was: no axis, and the seventeen groups one function call away. Every parameter came from a JSON file named by config_path, and config_path defaults to empty - so a map token could name this artifact but could never name a group, and PatternSim.GROUPS, the closed set of seventeen this artifact exists to display, was unreachable from map data entirely. The ten placed tokens are the proof: all bare, so all silent. An invisible artifact holding a 2x2 floor slot in six maps.
dna.note: group is DERIVED, not transcribed: the eighteen values are PatternSim.GROUPS in PatternSim's own IUC order with `unset` prepended, and PatternSim.group_enum() is the code that resolves each name. The seventeen are a CLOSED set - Fedorov: exactly seventeen ways a pattern can repeat in the plane, no eighteenth - so naming one is not a style choice, it is the whole claim a tile makes about which symmetries it obeys. `unset` is the eighteenth value and it is not a group: it is the shipped silence, declared because the export default has to be inside the declared list (the gate fails a default that is not) and because it is the state every map is actually in. When a group is named without a config the artifact builds from DEFAULT_DNA - PatternSim's own defaults (tile 32, seed 7, bauhaus, canvas 512) with one departure the staged corpus already made, a dot motif at radius 0.38 rather than a random one, because a random motif at density 0.5 buries the symmetry in noise and the symmetry is the only thing this axis is about.
dna.measurement_risk: READ THIS BEFORE BELIEVING A VERDICT. Without the fixture, the default frame renders NOTHING - the axis's own default is the blank state - and a blank against seventeen patterns would score an enormous bite that is a fact about an empty room. So dna.fixture supplies a tracked staged config (pt03_p4m_alhambra: dot motif, seed 3, alhambra palette, tile 32) and the sweep becomes a controlled experiment in which only the group varies. Two consequences to expect and not misread: (a) the `unset` and `p4m` frames are IDENTICAL by construction, because pt03's own group is p4m and unset means 'let the config decide'; (b) the neighbouring groups are genuinely close pictures - p3 against p31m, p4 against p4g - so a faint pair there is the mathematics, not a dead axis. Check p1 against p6m first, which is bare translation against six-fold rotation with mirrors.
dna.declined: palette (8 named palettes in PatternSim.PALETTES). It would be the strongest-biting and emptiest axis available: it repaints every pixel and says nothing about symmetry, which is a colour swatch, not an argument. Also declined: motif (random | dot), which is real - whether the group's symmetry is legible depends on the repeating unit having a form - but it is two-valued and it is a fact about the thing the group ACTS ON, so in one frame the two would fight and the critic would measure the collision. tile_size, canvas_size and quad_size are sizes.

dna.default: credit=named - the tradition tag at y=0.42 and the makers tag at y=0.30 beneath every plate, built with make_tag's own default ink and ground, which is board for board what the gallery has always built; the 7 existing placements are untouched and the room keeps its 'the makers, named' headline

dna.refused: colophon (pattern_loom) and exhibit (pattern_mill, pattern_machine_c) both ask how much of the RULE the goods admit to; three of their four values need each pattern's repeat period or plane symmetry group, which this gallery does not know for nineteen heterogeneous traditions and in several cases (kente strips, batik crackle, hitomezashi) does not have. Adopting either word would have meant inventing the measurements.

pattern_atlas_gallery.name: Pattern Atlas Gallery (the makers, named)
pattern_atlas_gallery.description: Twelve world pattern traditions reproduced AS SHADERS (the rule, not an image), each on an upright plate with its makers named beneath: Kente strip-weavers of Ghana, ikat resist-dyers, bingata stencil-dyers of Ryukyu, kanga printers of the Swahili coast, indigo shibori dyers, Tibetan tiger-rug carpet-knotters, Iznik fritware potters, al-Andalus zellige tile-cutters, the Pompeii mosaic workshops, Anni Albers, Sonia Delaunay, Vasarely, Bridget Riley. The commons ledger's return performed in-game, plus Investigation II: Wang tiles (Hao Wang/Berger — tiling is undecidable), Javanese batik makers (the kawung and the crackle), Kuba/Shoowa weavers of DR Congo, sashiko/hitomezashi stitchers of northern Japan, Sami band weavers of Sapmi, adinkra carvers of Ghana.

pattern_temple.name: Pattern temple
pattern_temple.description: A Moorish court built from primitives - quads, boxes, cylinders, a hemisphere and a ring - in which every surface is a pattern receiver: floor, far wall, east and west walls, the entrance wall with its corbelled arch, eight columns, the dome they carry and the frieze. One desk targets a surface and dresses it through wallpaper_tile.gdshader: SOURCE (zellige, stars, lattice, khatam, brick, three rasters from the tiling halls, every package the Pattern Studio has saved under commons/patterns), GROUP (the 17 wallpaper groups), PALETTE (Alhambra, terracotta, azul, midnight), SEED, AGE (dirt, wear, dust, cracks, chips, sun fade together), ALL and CLEAN. Map-token keys: age 0-4, source, group, palette, target.
pattern_temple.qfep_connection: The same rule dresses a floor, a wall, a column and a dome differently because the receiver is a body with an orientation, a curvature and a distance from the eye; the pattern does not decide what it is on.
interactions: TARGET moves the glowing marker to the next surface: floor, far wall, east, west, entrance, columns, dome, frieze.
SOURCE, GROUP, PALETTE and SEED change what the targeted surface wears; AGE weathers it in four steps.
ALL copies the targeted surface's dressing to every surface; CLEAN removes the weathering everywhere.
The studio's Save to Godot adds a package to the SOURCE cycle on the next visit.

dna.default: notation=label - the white billboarded [x, z] built inside the cube loop, the same node in the same place with the same font size, outline, no_depth_test and colour as before. MEASURED, not assumed: 14 real mentions across 13 map files - bare tokens in Corridor_Tutorial_2D_Build, Kernel_Demo2, Trial_antrooms_array_tutorial, Tutorial_2D, Tutorial_2D_Build and Tutorial_Single; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:grid_2d_4x4` in seven museum trials, where the # keys belong to the furniture; and `curation_station#artifacts:column_3_z,grid_2d_4x4,grid_3d_4x4x4` in Curation_Bay_array_tutorial_4, where they belong to the station. None passes a notation key. The layout values (cols, rows, spacing, label_size, label_color) were locals inside apply_grid_config with exactly the defaults _ready hard-coded, so promoting them to members lets one builder serve both paths and changes nothing at the default.
dna.was: a 4x4 of pickup cubes each wearing [x, z] in the air, which asserted that an address is a tag the object carries and hid that this is one answer among several - pick the cube up and the address leaves with it, while grid_data[x][z] quietly becomes 0 and the slot it named stays behind unmarked. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS; the exports it did have were a debug flag and a table toggle.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: column_3_z - the same word and the same five values in the same order with the same default, character for character. This artifact's own @identity names column_3_z as the thing it extends to two dimensions, and the two are the same object at n=1 and n=2: pickup cubes on a floor with an index each. Every value has a real 2D answer rather than a fudged one - tape becomes two rules along the two origin-side margins (an address is two distances read off two scales, which is also the matrix margin), tally becomes x strokes on the face looking back down X and z strokes on the face looking back down Z (two counts, each on the face pointing at the origin it counts from), and plate is the strongest fit of the five here, because the floor plaque that stays when the cube is taken is exactly what grid_data[x][z] = 0 has always meant in data and never showed in space.
dna.nearly_declined: recorded so the next agent does not reopen it. The obvious reading is that this is scaffolding whose only knob is how many cubes there are, and grid dimensions are the decoration case - prebaked_loader and path_game_controller were both declined that way. What separates it is that the artifact makes a claim (an address is a tag on the object) that it never admitted was a choice, and its 1D sibling had already named the question.
dna.still_note: notation is resolved during _ready and the dressing is static geometry - boxes, and one non-billboarded Label3D per slot under `plate`. Nothing here animates, so a single frame is a complete account of the axis.
dna.framing_note: the BinaryTableDisplay sits at (-2.0, 1.8, 1.5), about 0.9 m square, and does NOT change with notation, so it dilutes the bite by roughly its share of the frame. Expect a smaller number than column_3_z measures for the same five values; that is dilution, not a weaker axis. All notation geometry stays inside the cubes' own X/Z envelope (-0.25 to 3.25 at default spacing), so the sweep frames the same box whichever value it shoots.
dna.repair: apply_grid_config tore down every child and rebuilt on ANY non-empty config, including one naming nothing it owns - the force_pad fault. It is now guarded: a value has to actually move, and nothing rebuilds before _ready has built once. _create_binary_table also read a hard-coded 4 x 4 while feeding it cols x rows of data; it now reads the members, which is identical at the default and merely coherent above it.

dna.default: frame=orthonormal, readout=none - orthonormal returns Basis.IDENTITY, which _apply_frame writes into the CoordinateAxes node's transform as Transform3D(IDENTITY, ZERO), i.e. the transform that node already had, and moves the three billboard letters to (1.2,0,0)/(0,1.2,0)/(0,0,1.2), which is where create_axes literally put them; readout=none is the `_:` branch of _build_readout and adds no node at all. All 7 placements (Tutorial_Single, Tutorial_Row, Tutorial_2D_Build, Tutorial_2D_Color, Tutorial_App, Spine_Museum, Lab) are bare tokens with no config, and apply_grid_config only assigns when the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the value already held, so nothing is torn down for them.
dna.was: four exports and every one a dial on HANDLING - initial_scale, rotation_speed and two camera sensitivities - and not one about the coordinate system the gadget exists to argue about. The three rods were three literal CSGCylinder3D blocks with hard-coded rotations, and there was no apply_grid_config at all, so no map token could reach anything.
dna.note: frame is the argument. This artifact's own truth statement is that a coordinate system is a convention about shared directions and not a property of space, and until now it could draw exactly ONE convention - right angles, equal lengths, right-handed, aligned with the room - which is that claim's contradiction standing in seven rooms. Each value drops one property the identity silently bundles: tilted drops nothing but agreement with the walls (the rung the artifact's own `emerges` note is about, where 'X goes right' stops being true); skewed drops orthogonality; stretched drops unit length, so the same point in the world carries quite different numbers; mirrored drops right-handedness and Z points backward. The map is applied to the CoordinateAxes node, so the rods, the readout collars, the lattice and the invisible FrameAnchor all move as one system - the letters are moved by hand instead of re-parented, because moving them in the tree would change what GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb sees among the root's direct children and every live placement would ground differently.
dna.kin: frame is taken character for character from basis_vectors_rig (promoted the same day), which asks the same question of the same geometry: three coloured legs from one origin, and a name - `basis`, `coordinates` - claiming more than the drawing can support. The shared word is honest here because the geometry IS the geometry; the rig adds the linear-combination staircase, this one adds the graduations. Both ship orthonormal, so the family measures alike at its default. readout is taken character for character from xyz_slider_plate and line, which carry the same four rungs; those two are the plate and the segment, this is the frame they are read against.
dna.pairs: skewed x lattice is the strongest single frame this gadget can produce - a graduated oblique lattice is the one picture in which 'the grid' and 'the right angle' visibly come apart. Sweeping frame at readout=none understates it, because a bare rod carries no marks to shear.
dna.still_note: every rung of both axes is standing geometry under a standing linear map; nothing animates, so a still holds it. frame needs no rebuild at all (one transform write plus three label positions); readout rebuilds only its own Readout node.
dna.framing_note: the gadget is CSGCylinder3D and Label3D only, and both AABB walks in this repo type `is MeshInstance3D`, so an invisible layers=0 FrameAnchor already exists inside CoordinateAxes to give the capture something to measure. It is sized for the ORTHONORMAL frame; under stretched and mirrored it is carried by the same basis and grows with the rods, but check subject % before reading a verdict.

xyz_coordinates.description: Cartesian coordinate system, x y z godot
xyz_coordinates.name: XYZ coordinates
xyz_coordinates.qfep_connection: The addressing scheme laid bare — x, y, z, the three numbers that turn empty space into an array of positions. Before any value can be stored somewhere, somewhere has to be nameable; this is the chapter's quiet foundation, the Cartesian grid that makes 'the cell at (3,1,4)' a sentence with a referent.

grid3d.name: Grid3D Substrate
grid3d.description: Universal 3D graph visualization. MultiMesh spheres + cylinder edges. Defaults to BFS. Use #algorithm:<name> to select cartridge.
grid3d.qfep_connection: The array grown a third dimension: a lattice of spheres and edges, traversed by BFS. Where the bar row was 1D and the tiles 2D, this is the array as volume — a graph in space, indices become coordinates, and the data structure becomes a place you could walk. The bridge from list to world.

bar_array.name: BarArray Substrate
bar_array.description: Universal 1D array visualization. MultiMesh bars with emission and smooth transitions. Defaults to Bubble Sort. Use #algorithm:<name> to select cartridge.
bar_array.qfep_connection: The array itself, standing up: a row of bars whose heights ARE the values, index by index. The chapter's first primitive and its whole thesis in one object — that a list of numbers is a shape, and that to store data in order is already to draw it. Every sort, search, and histogram downstream is this row, rearranged.

dna.fixture_note: MANDATORY for the sweep, and neither key is an axis. order_seed 0 is the shipped behaviour - the cartridge's Fisher-Yates uses the GLOBAL unseeded randi(), so without a pin the shuffled tile is a different array every run and any bite number partly measures the RNG (the generative-artifact trap in CLAUDE.md). auto_play false stops the clock: with it true the sort advances ~13 steps during the 1.1 s SETTLE, which is still close to the initial state but is 13 steps of drift that differ per value and would be read as part of the axis. auto_play is a typed bool and this fixture value is a real JSON false, not the string "false" - a string would be rejected by the typed export before _ready.
dna.default: initial_order=shuffled with order_seed=0 - _arrange short-circuits and hands the cartridge's own array straight back, so the shipped super.initialize() Fisher-Yates is the only code that ran and nothing is recomputed. The 4 existing placements (Test_Substrates, Test_Substrates_Placed, Tutorial_3D, Zone_TemporalStorage) are byte-identical.
dna.was: array_size, step_interval, auto_play, label_text and an Algorithm enum. Every one of those is a count, a rate, a caption or the FAMILY IDENTITY - algorithm is what tells the nine bar_array_* tokens apart via _resolve_algorithm_from_lookup_name, so sweeping it would photograph the siblings, not this artifact's variation. The one thing bubble sort argues, that the same code is O(n) on one input and O(n^2) on another, was unreachable because the starting array was always the same unseeded shuffle.
dna.notes: SORTING IS TIME-DOMAIN AND A STILL CATCHES ONE ARBITRARY PASS, so "how far through" was never a candidate. What a still can hold is the array BEFORE the first comparison, and that is the artifact's own subject: reversed is the worst case at n(n-1)/2 inversions, sorted is the best case at one pass and no swap - the early-exit branch in cartridge_bubble_sort.step() that no placement has ever shown - and nearly_sorted is the case where bubble sort is genuinely competitive. The bars carry it twice over, because get_bar_color is a function of VALUE: sorted draws a smooth colour ramp, shuffled draws colour noise, so the axis moves hue as well as height. DECLINED THE FAMILY WORD: entropy_jar and entropy_morphogenesis declare found_state = sorted|stirred|mixed for a question of the same shape, and three of these four values map onto it cleanly, but reversed does not and cannot be added without breaking it - on an entropy ladder reversed sits at the same rung as sorted, being perfectly ordered, while being the single most expensive input bubble sort can be handed. Taking the word would have meant corrupting a sibling's ladder or dropping the one value that carries the lesson (the cost model is inversion count, not disorder), so it takes a different word instead. ONE SCENE, MANY NAMES: the export lands on bar_array_substrate.gd, which all nine bar_array_* tokens share, so insertion, selection, merge, quicksort, heap, histogram, fibonacci and prime_sieve all gain the knob and none of them declares it yet - _arrange therefore ASKS THE CARTRIDGE (get_category() != "sorting" returns the array untouched) rather than hard-coding a list of names, so histogram, fibonacci and prime_sieve cannot have their bin count, series or sieve overwritten by a ramp, and a tenth cartridge answers for itself. The five other sorts are honest candidates for this same word and are deliberately NOT declared here - each needs its own default-preservation check and its own placement count, and quicksort in particular inverts the argument (already-sorted input is its WORST case, not its best). Expect them in the gate's promoted-in-code-undeclared list until someone does that work; that is a known consequence of one scene carrying nine names, not an oversight. framing 0.55 because PAD is 1.9 and the subject is 1.37 m wide by 0.31 m tall: fit-by-diagonal frames a letterbox in a square.

bar_array_bubble_sort.name: BarArray — Bubble Sort
bar_array_bubble_sort.description: Bubble sort on a MultiMesh bar array. Adjacent comparisons, largest bubbles to the end. O(n²). The canonical first sort.
bar_array_bubble_sort.qfep_connection: The array in motion: bubble sort walking the bars, comparing neighbors, swapping, the largest rising to the end pass after pass. O(n²) and honest about it — the slowest useful sort, chosen here because you can SEE it think. The algorithm made a dance the eye can follow, index against index.

sorting_algorithm_race.name: Sorting Algorithm Race
sorting_algorithm_race.description: Four rows of 16 colored bars sort simultaneously using Bubble, Insertion, Selection, and Merge sort. Animated step-by-step so you can watch algorithms race and feel the difference in strategy.

shelf.name: shelf
shelf.qfep_connection: Display furniture that holds other artifacts at hand height — the gallery's quiet servant, staging the exhibits without joining them.

shelf_with_stickers.name: shelf_with_stickers
shelf_with_stickers.qfep_connection: A CSG-carved wooden pigeonhole shelf whose compartments hold the project's own grant-application doubts as grabbable papers — 'risk of aestheticizing harm,' 'what if the queer potential gets commodified.' Institutional self-audit turned into furniture you can rummage.

SimultaneousContrast.name: SimultaneousContrast
SimultaneousContrast.qfep_connection: The same 0.5 gray twice, on dark and on light ground, and your visual system refuses to agree with the code. The hidden connector bar is the instrument's cruelty: proof that the difference you see was manufactured by context, never present in the value.

MetamerismLab.name: MetamerismLab
MetamerismLab.qfep_connection: One pure 580nm wave on the left, a red–green duet on the right, and both resolve to spheres of the exact same yellow. Two different physical events collapse into one percept the eye cannot appeal — color as the retina's lossy compression, metamerism as where the loss shows.

hue_carousel.name: Hue Carousel
hue_carousel.description: A fairground carousel whose canopy is the hue wheel - twelve from_hsv seats at full saturation on the rim, grey-ish seats near the pole, the pole itself the value dimmer. Color taxonomy rung 3, 2026-08-27.

grabcolorcollection.name: grabcolorcollection
grabcolorcollection.qfep_connection: A palette becomes graspable paper: pull a sheet off the stack and the system names its color by nearest neighbor in the web-color table. Every hue you hold is snapped to the vocabulary a 1990s standards body left behind — continuous color, colonized by a finite lexicon.

color_mixing.description: Interactive color mixing — combine colors and see the result in different color spaces. Additive (light) vs subtractive (pigment) mixing made visible.
color_mixing.name: Color Mixing
color_mixing.qfep_connection: The two triads don't simulate mixing; they hand the question to the renderer, so CMY darkens through alpha blending while RGB whitens through additive blend mode. Subtraction and addition turn out to be GPU policies, not paint facts.

dna.default: bands=seven, evidence=result - the two defaults together reproduce the shipped sculpture vertex for vertex. seven returns the SPECTRUM array itself, in order, so the fan loop still divides by size()-1 = 6 and every line ends where it always did; the incident beam stays overbright white because the monochromatic tint is reached only at bands=one. result is the early-return in _apply_evidence: no law node is ever constructed, the tree gains not one child, and the beams are painted by the same code path with the same three colour constants. apply_grid_config is guarded three ways - the key must be present, the value must be one the code can build, and it must differ from the current one - and it returns before repainting until _built is true, so the 2 placements (Corridor_Color_Nails, and the Curation_Bay_color_2 curation_station shelf) render exactly what they rendered before.
dna.was: No exports at all. The seven colours, the fan geometry and the absence of any normal or angle were locals inside _create_trace_beams, so every placement was the same picture and a map could say nothing about it. Refused by the runner for NO TURNABLE KNOBS.
dna.note: bands is the artifact's own dark spot: the fan has seven lines because Newton named seven, and he named seven to match the diatonic scale - a cultural fact wearing the costume of a physical one. one is the experimentum crucis (take one colour out of the fan, send it in again, and nothing further happens - the ray that will not split, drawn monochromatic on entry as well as exit so the frame does not claim white in and green out); three is the display's primaries taken from the same seven, so it reads as a SUBSET of Newton's and not a different palette; continuum is sixty-four samples through the same anchors, the seven revealed as a naming convention over a smooth ramp. evidence asks whether the law is in the frame at all: the shipped sculpture has no normal, no angle and no formula, so it shows the result and withholds the reason. trace draws the two surface normals dashed and the pair of arcs at the entry point - theta_1 between the incoming ray and the normal, theta_2 between the internal ray and the same normal, which is exactly the pair Snell relates. longhand measures every band: its own arc against the exit normal at its own radius, plus a rule at the end of the fan carrying a tick where each wavelength lands, so wavelength-dependence stops being a spray the viewer takes on trust. axiom withholds the rainbow and keeps the normals, the arcs and n1 sin(theta_1) = n2 sin(theta_2) in symbols - the album cover refused, the law kept.
dna.kin: evidence is the family word (26 artifacts: fibonacci_sequences, koch_curve, pythagorean_triangle_angles, gradient_descent_visualization, bouncing_ball and the rest) and the ladder is taken character for character in the family's own sense - how much of the working is admitted alongside the result, with axiom the symbolic assertion rather than the withheld one, exactly as pythagorean_triangle_angles uses it. bands is NOT shared with any sibling. The nearest words were rainbow.substance (light|glass|solid), which is what the arc is MADE of and not how finely it is divided, and vector_field_grid.coding (magnitude|direction|banded|uniform), whose banded/uniform pair is about a colour ramp's quantisation rather than about how many wavelengths a beam is claimed to contain. Neither is the same question, so neither word was borrowed.
dna.still_note: bands should bite hard: one draws two coloured lines where seven drew nine, continuum fills the same wedge solid. evidence is strongest at axiom (the fan, which is most of the ink, disappears and a formula appears) and at longhand (a rule and seven arcs added outside the existing silhouette); trace adds only four dashed normals and two arcs against a bloom-heavy black frame, so it is the value most likely to come in thin - if it does, check the framing before calling it inert, because the artifact adds its own WorldEnvironment with glow_bloom 0.5 and the added grey lines are deliberately unbloomed while the beams are overbright.
dna.gotcha: This scene adds its own Camera3D and WorldEnvironment in _ready. Both are embedded-chrome that GridInteractablesComponent._suppress_embedded_chrome handles; nothing here changes that, but a capture harness that does not suppress them will photograph through the artifact's own camera at (0, 0, 4) and no axis verdict from such a frame means anything.

two_roads.name: Two Roads
two_roads.description: Two walkable roads between the same teal and orange: the RGB road greys out mid-way (its exact mud held up on a plinth), the HSV road stays saturated round the wheel. A gradient is a choice of path. Color taxonomy rung 8, 2026-08-27.

grab_stick.name: grab_stick
grab_stick.qfep_connection: Grab it, point it, and it reads the texture's stored pixel at the hit UV — the asset, not the light. Color here was never a property of surfaces but an image wrapped around geometry, and the stick turns that archival fact into something you hold.

fabric_shader_studio.name: From Source to Skirt — Shader and Fabric Studio
fabric_shader_studio.description: An editable four-by-four source feeds a wall and skirt preview. Inspect UVs, repetition, cut-outs, matte/metal finish and bounded vertex displacement; save/load a recipe, deliberately dress the player or runway performers, and undo application.

Inspect shader stages with mounted controls
Save and load the recipe
Wear the saved recipe on the skirt
Apply to runway skirts
