garment_cutting_table.name: Cutting table and robot tailor
garment_cutting_table.description: Choose SUIT, A-LINE, GOWN or PLEATED and preview the shape. Load committed cloth saved at the Jacquard loom, inspect ten labelled panels, CUT their outlines, ASSEMBLE them one at a time with the robot arm, then WEAR on the real avatar. Shape and cloth persist together; TAKE OFF restores the prior look. Includes tartan, houndstooth and optical samples. Geometric tailoring, not cloth physics or a production sewing draft.
garment_cutting_table.qfep_connection: A retained weave meets a selected cut and an inferred avatar body; exact source data does not make the fit universal.

pulsar_visualizer.name: Pulsar B1919+21 Visualizer
pulsar_visualizer.description: The first pulsar discovered (1967). Binary table + 3D glass tubes. Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures made interactive.

coloredlines.description: Interactive colored line visualization and manipulation algorithms
coloredlines.name: Colored Lines

RotatingLaser.name: RotatingLaser
RotatingLaser.qfep_connection: Wave, focus, spread, scan, chaos — a concert rig's whole emotional vocabulary is one MultiMesh and a phase offset per beam, colors rotating on a ten-second timer. Spectacle revealed as cheap: crowd-shaped feelings driven by a pattern enum.

minimalglitch.description: Minimal glitch aesthetics — subtle data corruption effects that reveal the digital substrate beneath visual representation.
minimalglitch.name: Minimal Glitch
minimalglitch.qfep_connection: Corruption at survivable dosage: fifteen cubes cycling well-behaved functions that impersonate damage, in a demo that ships its own camera and lighting. That total safety is the aesthetic claim — glitch consumed as style only once it is separated from loss.

glitchcolor.description: Color glitch effects — channel shifting, bit corruption, and chromatic aberration. What happens when color data breaks in beautiful ways.
glitchcolor.name: Glitch Color
glitchcolor.qfep_connection: Bit rotation, XOR, quantization — integer operations performed on color, each cube a different violence to the byte. The resulting palette was never chosen by anyone; it is what the number system looks like when you watch it work.

advancedglitch.description: Interactive colored line visualization and manipulation algorithms
advancedglitch.name: advancedglitch
advancedglitch.qfep_connection: Datamosh, buffer overflow, memory leak — fifteen failure modes each given a pedestal, a name, and an animation schedule. Nothing here is actually broken, which is exactly how corruption becomes a repertoire: glitch as aesthetic requires the removal of loss.

colortrails.name: colortrails
colortrails.qfep_connection: Each hand writes a spline ribbon that begins dying the moment it exists — trail_lifetime caps the drawing at the last 1.75 seconds of you. Gesture is archived at exactly the rate it is erased, so the only way to keep the trace alive is to keep moving.

neon_garden.name: Neon Garden
neon_garden.description: Flowers with albedo black and petals of pure emission, breathing on seeded phases under a dark pergola. Emission owes the room nothing. Color taxonomy rung 5, 2026-08-27.

strobe_lasers.name: strobe_lasers
strobe_lasers.qfep_connection: Sixteen beams and one visibility bit flipped at 12Hz — the nightclub's oldest trick is a square wave applied to the whole scene at once. The strobe outsources half the animation to the viewer's retina, which insists on continuity the code never renders.

disco_lights.description: Interactive colored line visualization and manipulation algorithms
disco_lights.name: disco_lights
disco_lights.qfep_connection: The geometry is a default sphere; the party is three sine waves at incommensurate frequencies inside the light() pass, red, green, and blue never returning to the same phase together. Disco as a Lissajous figure — spectacle located entirely in the lighting equation.

one_bulb_room.name: One Bulb Room
one_bulb_room.description: A dark chamber, six pure-albedo bodies, ONE swinging bulb on a cord (real damped pendulum + OmniLight3D). No light, no color - albedo is a promise light has to keep. Color taxonomy rung 1, 2026-08-27.

laser_turret.description: Standalone laser turret that auto-targets and destroys balls. Place separately from ball_dropper to customize layout. Demonstrates vector subtraction (direction), magnitude (range), normalization (aim), dot product (lock).
interactions: Automatic targeting - no direct interaction needed
laser_turret.name: Laser Turret
laser_turret.qfep_connection: The turret as computational subject - continuously computing direction vectors to track moving targets.

euler_drift.description: The forces seam. Continuous dynamics integrated in jumps: the true parabola (amber) vs the Euler path (blue) drifting off it, gaining energy it was never given; and at a big step a fast body tunnels clean through the wall. The force is real; the stepping is the machine's.
euler_drift.name: Euler Drift
euler_drift.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for forces. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

launch_arc.name: Launch Arc (projectile motion)
launch_arc.description: Projectile motion made playable - the launch / F=ma toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc (the pad that throws you). A launch pad fires at angle theta with speed v; gravity bends the straight launch vector into a parabola. The launch velocity decomposes into a horizontal vx (carries you) and a vertical vy (fights gravity); the trade between them sets the range = v^2 sin(2theta)/g - which peaks at 45 degrees. Shows the tilted glowing pad, the stroboscopic projectile arc, the launch vector + its vx/vy components, and apex / range markers. DNA: angle 0..1 sets the launch angle (flat to steep), power 0..1 the launch speed; color_a pad + components, color_b the arc + launch vector, accent pad glow + apex/range.

parameters.angle: 0..1 launch angle, flat to steep - range peaks at 45 deg (default 0.5)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)
parameters.comparison: single | fan | pairs | envelope - what the one throw is shown against, every companion fired at the same v0 (default single)

dna.default: workings=trace, comparison=single - both are the fall-through arm of their own match and run no code whatever, and both matches sit AFTER _settle(rig). Nothing above that line was touched by this pass: the tilted pad, the base plate, the ground bar, the stroboscopic parabola, the launch vector, the dashed vx/vy legs and the apex/range/drop markers are the same calls with the same literals in the same order, so the fit, the scale and the placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. All 4 existing placements (MindMap_VectorForces, VFM_05_Launch, VFM_Forces_Playground, Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion) carry the bare token launch_arc or launch_arc:0:0 with no config overrides, so apply_grid_config never sees either key
dna.was: workings was written into the script in the 2026-08-02 rescue batch and never declared, so the sweep had no axis to turn and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS - seed, angle, power, complexity and three colours are @exports that move or recolour one fixed arc and argue nothing. comparison did not exist in any form: the bench drew ONE throw while its own description claimed range = v0^2 sin 2theta / g peaks at 45 degrees, which is a statement about a FAMILY of throws that a single arc cannot make. The angle slider sweeps the family one member at a time and the exhibit forgets each as it goes
dna.shared_with: workings is transform_composition_workbench's word with its four values in the same order, seconded by its bench-mates dot_aligner, vector_add, vector_sub and projection_shadow; DERIVED from the @export_enum in launch_arc.gd, not transcribed. comparison is seed_replay_demo's and space_filling_curve_gallery's question - what is this one instance shown against - and keeps their 'single' anchor value character for character. The other three answers are this artifact's own, because a projectile's companions are angles and not grammars or replicas
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. comparison is the axis because the thing this exhibit teaches is a RELATION between throws and it could only ever draw one. fan fires five angles from the same launcher at the same v0: 45 lands furthest, and the five flights leave only THREE pips, because 20 and 70 land together and 35 and 55 land together, so the peak and the symmetry about it are both in the picture instead of in the caption. pairs is that symmetry alone, 25/65 and 40/50, each pair sharing a colour and ONE landing pip - a flat fast throw and a high slow one arriving together. envelope drops the individual flights for the boundary of everything reachable at this v0, y = v0^2/2g - g x^2/2v0^2, which the live arc kisses from inside at exactly one point because it IS the envelope of the family. Every companion is integrated with the same GRAVITY and the same v0 as the live launch, so the only difference between any two of them is the angle. The axes are independent: comparison adds ghost flights, workings decides how the live one is annotated, and the fan is still five arcs at workings=expression
dna.declined: foresight (catapult's word, seconded by force_pad) was considered and refused, though the brief handed it over as the obvious third use. It names how much of the flight you are given BEFORE you fire, and on both of those machines that is a real stance because both fire: the catapult has a FIRE button and a ball that follows the arc, the pad throws the player who steps on it, and in each case the drawn parabola is a prediction of an event that has not happened. Nothing on this bench ever fires. Its parabola is not a preview, it is the exhibit - a strobe photograph of a flight already complete. Worse, the word would be a second name for a knob that exists: workings=outcome already strips the strobe and keeps the apex and range markers, which is exactly foresight=landing, and workings=trace is foresight=parabola. Declaring both would give the sweep two words for one drawing and no rule for which wins when a map sets them against each other. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary; taking a word whose answers are already spoken by another axis is the same fault twice
dna.declined_gravity: an axis over GRAVITY (const 3.0, the one hard-coded constant left in the file, and the one thing here that is not the launcher's choice) was designed, checked and thrown away, and the reason is worth keeping. At fixed v0 and theta, changing g is a SIMILARITY TRANSFORM on the trajectory: range = v0^2 sin 2theta / g and apex = v0^2 sin^2 theta / 2g both scale as 1/g, so the arc's shape is invariant and only its size changes. This artifact is a ToyConsole and _settle() rescales the demo to a fixed 0.78 m span, which undoes precisely that. A weak-gravity and a strong-gravity variant would therefore photograph as the SAME PICTURE, and the only pixels that moved would be the fixed-size furniture - the 0.42 m pad, the 0.05 m strobe spheres - shrinking against a renormalised arc. A bite report would have measured the scaler and called it physics. Only g = 0 genuinely changes the shape (a straight ray, no apex, no range), which is one real value against two decorative ones
dna.harness_note: the axes are declared comparison-FIRST on purpose. build_dna_gallery takes the first two axes and trims values off the END of each list until the cross product fits --max, which defaults to 9: 4 x 4 is 16, so whichever axis comes second loses half its values. workings is already measured on five bench-mates and comparison is the claim that needs evidence, so comparison keeps all four and workings is cut to outcome|trace. Run --max=16 for the full cross. Then: read the bite report with this in hand. The comparison geometry is added after _settle, so the demo rig keeps the shipped scale and the ghost arcs reach past it: the envelope's ceiling stands at v0^2/2g = 1.35 in rig units against the live arc's apex of 0.70, and the 65-degree fan member at 1.10. The capture AABB counts MeshInstance3D, so the camera does pull back for those three values and part of any measured change is that pull-back. It was kept because the pull-back here is small where catapult's was total: this is a console, and the 1.5 m housing, the monitor, the slider and the label plates are identical in all four frames and dominate the box, so the demo cannot collapse the AABB the way a bare 8 m trajectory preview did. If the report comes back faint anyway, the fixture to reach for is demo_only=true, an @export on the shared ToyConsole base that drops the housing and photographs the demo alone at 1.9 m. It is deliberately NOT declared as a fixture, because demo_only is a TYPED bool and this pass could not run a capture to prove that whatever sets it passes a real bool rather than the string "true"

dna.default: workings=trace - trace is the fall-through arm of the match and runs no code at all, and the whole match sits AFTER _settle(rig, 1.9), so the legacy fit and placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. Two edits above that line: three nodes bound to locals that were previously passed straight into add_child, and the four dashed cone edges wrapped in an identity Node3D named SpreadCone so the axis can reach the whole envelope in one call. pickable_prop._subtree_aabb recurses into Node3D children and does NOT apply their transform, and this holder is never moved, so the settled box is bit-identical. The gun, the reservoir, the trigger, the seeded bubble pool and _process are untouched. All 3 placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, MindMap_VectorForces, Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion) carry the bare token `bubble_blaster` or `bubble_blaster:0:0` with no config key at all, so the new branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists.
dna.was: no axis at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. seed, output and four colours are @exports that lengthen, widen or recolour ONE fixed claim: a single mean arrow down the muzzle axis and four dashed edges sketching where the spray stops. The artifact's own truth line says every emitter is a little vector field made of thousands of tiny departures, and the object had exactly one way of drawing that - as one arrow, the average of a thing it was arguing is not one.
dna.shared_with: transform_composition_workbench's word with its four values in the same order, seconded by its own bench-mates dot_aligner, vector_add, vector_sub, projection_shadow, launch_arc, torque_crank and bounce_well. A launch velocity is a scalar times a direction, which is the same product those benches take apart. DERIVED from the @export_enum in bubble_blaster.gd, not transcribed.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. WHAT IT SHOWS STANDING STILL, checked first because firing needs a hand the bench does not have: _build calls _place_bubbles(), which distributes the whole pool across phases 0..1 along the cone, so the still already shows a full spreading cone of bubbles at _fire_level 0 - dim rather than glowing, and drifting at a tenth speed. Nothing about this axis depends on the trigger. OPERANDS is the value that carries the argument: the averaged arrow and the dashed envelope go dark and thirteen departure vectors are drawn from the nozzle instead, all of the same LENGTH (the speed is the scalar) along a golden-angle spiral through the cone disc (the spread is the direction), with the half-angle swept as an arc against a thin axis ray. The spiral is arithmetic, not randomness - no RNG is touched, so the bundle is the same bundle in every frame. OUTCOME is the picture of this machine NOT doing the one thing it exists to do: arrow, envelope and readout unlayered, leaving a gun and some soap, which is what every other bubble machine looks like. EXPRESSION promotes v_i = v_out . d_hat_i onto a plate with the live numbers substituted.
dna.declined: `foresight` (catapult's word, seconded by force_pad and human_catapult) was handed over as the promising reading and is refused on two grounds. The value list is parabola|apex|landing|none, and this thing has no parabola: the bubbles leave in straight lines inside a cone, under no gravity, and recycle at the far end. There is no apex and there is no landing, so three of the four answers name a mechanism this object lacks - folding_past's refusal, exactly. And the premise fails too: foresight is how much of the flight you are given BEFORE you fire, which requires a before. This gun wears its launch vector on the muzzle whether or not anyone is holding it, so there is no state in which the vector is a prediction rather than a label. launch_arc refused the same word for the mirror-image reason - its arc is a completed flight rather than a preview - and the two refusals together are the shape of the word: it belongs to machines that fire ONE thing and can show you where it will land. ALSO REFUSED, and this one was measured rather than reasoned: `field`, the shape of the launch distribution (solid cone, hollow shell, parallel beam, flat fan). It is a genuine argument, it is this artifact's own, and `output` cannot reach it - spread is clamped to 7..28 degrees and never zero. It is not shipped because it is INVISIBLE TO A STILL AT THIS SCALE. The 11 to 26 bubbles have radii 0.020-0.055 m and _settle scales the rig by about 0.888; at framing 0.60 the frame is roughly 2.9 m across at 760 px, so the entire bubble pool covers on the order of 0.4 percent of frame. Moving all of it would sit an order of magnitude under the bite threshold, which is the 'axis real in world space, invisible in frame' row of the brief's table bought in advance. output and seed stay plain exports; a longer arrow is a bigger photograph of the same claim.
dna.still_note: framing 0.60, derived rather than guessed, and honest about being the tight end. The union box with expression's board is roughly (1.90, 1.44, 0.75) after _settle, radius about 1.25, and the no-crop floor is 1/PAD = 0.526, so 0.60 leaves about 14 percent margin on the furthest corner. It is needed because the ink this axis moves is THIN: the launch arrow is about 1.37 m long and 0.05 m wide and the four dashed edges are 0.012 m wide, which is on the order of 1 percent of frame at framing 1.0. They are also the BRIGHTEST pixels in the frame - glow energy 1.8 on the arrow against a matte pink body - so the focus number (hottest 5 percent) should move far more than the frame number, and operands should be the strongest value because it replaces one arrow with thirteen. ONE RESIDUAL RISK, named rather than hidden: _process advances _stream_t by delta * 0.10 while idle, so the bubble pool drifts a little during the 1.1 s settle and the exact bubble positions depend on frame timing rather than on the axis. The bubbles are small and identical across values, so this is noise and not bias, but it is the reason a sub-1 percent verdict on this artifact should be read as a capture fact before it is read as a design fact. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass.

bubble_blaster.name: Bubble Blaster (output velocity vector)
bubble_blaster.description: A soap-bubble gun that fires a spreading cone of bubbles and wears its launch vector on the muzzle - an embodied force-display prop. Pull the trigger and bubbles pour out; the muzzle shows an arrow for the output velocity and a faint cone for the spread. Crank the output and the arrow stretches, the cone widens, the bubbles fly faster and further. Every emitter is a little vector field - each particle leaves with a velocity, and the spray's force is just that launch vector made of many departures. DNA: output 0..1 dials the launch (vector length, spread angle, bubble speed/count); seed jitters the bubbles.

parameters.output: 0..1 launch output - vector length, spread, bubble count (default 0.6)

catapult.name: Catapult
catapult.description: Procedural wooden catapult: A-frame base, torsion pivot, a long throwing arm with a basket at the tip and a counterweight at the short end. A console with ANGLE + FORCE sliders and a FIRE push-button sits in front. Changing a control retilts the arm and redraws a live predicted-trajectory parabola; FIRE swings the arm and launches a ball that follows the arc. Always-on velocity (green) and gravity (red) vector arrows with labels make the parabola = initial velocity + constant gravity legible. DNA: throw sets the initial condition the machine is built for - mortar and flat turn the aim at unchanged force, heavy and weak turn the force at unchanged aim; foresight sets how much of the arc is previewed and vectors how the release is annotated. Use #throw:, #foresight:, #vectors:.
catapult.qfep_connection: F_force: a throw is an initial condition. You write direction and magnitude at release; gravity, constant and given, bends the rest. The parabola is the sum of what you give and what is given.

dna.default: foresight=parabola, vectors=sum, throw=balanced - the full dotted arc plus one velocity arrow and the gravity arrow is exactly what the 4 existing placements draw today; the component arrows are not even instantiated at that value, and throw=balanced is the else-branch of _apply_throw, which is character for character the two clamps _ready always ran (default_angle_deg 50, default_force 9.0) and never touches the counterweight. Scene tree and capture AABB unchanged
dna.was: the predicted parabola was always the whole flight path, and the throw was always drawn as a single arrow beside a single gravity arrow - both hard-coded in _update_trajectory and _update_vector_arrows with no way to say otherwise
dna.deepened: 2026-08-03 - added `throw`. foresight and vectors both draw the arc; nothing turned the arc itself. default_angle_deg = 50.0 and default_force = 9.0 were plain vars with no export, so although apply_grid_config would have accepted an #angle:/#force: token, no map has ever sent one: all 4 placements (ForcesArena, VFM_05_Launch, Zone_WarehouseLab, Zone_WarehouseLab_Packed) stand at 50 deg / 9.0 m/s and draw the identical parabola. A foresight axis over one arc is a preview of a foregone conclusion. The four values are a 2x2 around the shipped throw: mortar (75 deg) and flat (20 deg) turn the DIRECTION at unchanged force and bracket the 45 deg optimum from both sides - flat lands shorter than balanced, which is the half of that lesson a single arc can never tell; heavy (13 m/s) and weak (5 m/s) turn the MAGNITUDE at the unchanged 50 deg aim, where range goes as v^2. Direction and magnitude, one pair each, which is the artifact's own truth line.
dna.counterweight: the counterweight block was a fixed 0.26 m cube for every throw. It now scales with the cube root of force / 9.0 (mass goes as volume), so it is exactly 1.0 at the shipped force and moves only for heavy (1.13) and weak (0.82) - mortar and flat keep the shipped block, since they change the aim and not the force. The scaling is guarded on THROWS, so `balanced` never touches the geometry even if a map overrides the force through config. It deliberately does NOT track the FORCE slider: the counterweight is what the machine was built to deliver, the sliders are the aim taken with it.
dna.independence: throw is orthogonal to both older axes. foresight decides how much of the arc is drawn, vectors decides how the release is annotated, throw decides which arc exists at all. The arm tilt alone separates mortar/flat/balanced whether or not any preview is drawn, so throw still bites at foresight=none.
dna.harness_note: read the next bite report with this in hand. The sweep frames each variant from its own subtree AABB, and the trajectory ImmediateMesh is a MeshInstance3D whose vertices ARE the predicted arc - roughly 8 m against a 1.5 m machine at the default. That is why the wave-1 report shows subject_pct 3.41 (the machine is small because its own preview inflates the box) and why foresight=parabola vs none scored 3.48% while parabola vs apex scored 0.93%: turning the preview off collapses the AABB and re-zooms the whole tile. The same applies to throw - flat/mortar shorten the arc, heavy roughly doubles it - so part of any measured change is the camera moving, not the picture. It was kept anyway: a stronger throw honestly IS a bigger object, and the values were chosen to keep the range inside about 2.5 to 17 m rather than the 26 m a 45-degree full-force throw would have needed. A layers=0 framing anchor would pin the camera, but it would also inflate the measured footprint that sync_footprints.py writes, so it is left undone deliberately rather than by omission.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 30.0% of frame width and 25.1% of its height, with a subject share of 0.30%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.32. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

force_play_torque.name: Where you push matters
force_play_torque.description: A gate, seesaw and crank retain actual hinges while rose hand grips transmit forces.

dna.default: foresight=parabola, vectors=velocity - together these are the shipped machine exactly: the full predicted parabola drawn from the basket, plus ONE accent-coloured launch-velocity arrow, with gravity left undrawn. `parabola` is the fall-through arm of _foresight_mesh and runs _arc_mesh, which is the shipped p(t)=p0+v0*t+0.5*g*t^2 loop character for character - same 0.08 s sampling, same `while t < 4.0`, same break at p.y<0, same SurfaceTool LINE_STRIP. `velocity` is the fall-through arm of _build_indicators and runs the same two lines that always built the single arrow, in the same order, so _accent_mats gets the same one entry. MEASURED, not assumed: all three placements carry the bare token form - `human_catapult` in ForcesArena, `human_catapult:90:0` in Force_Preview and VFM_05_Launch. That form is artifact:rotation:y_offset, not config, so not one of them passes a foresight or vectors key, and the new apply_grid_config returns without rebuilding unless a key is present AND differs from the value the node already holds.
dna.was: a machine whose only knobs were MAGNITUDES - launch_force, launch_angle, gravity_magnitude. Turning them flings the same body further; none of them is an argument. And the flight is an EVENT, which one still cannot hold. Worse, apply_grid_config was actively harmful: it queue_free()d every child and call_deferred("_ready") on ANY call, including one whose dictionary named nothing this machine owns - and because queue_free only detaches at end of frame, the deferred rebuild could run while the old frame was still parented. That is the force_pad trap, and it is fixed here in the same way.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: catapult and force_pad, both words and both value lists character for character. The three are one machine at three scales - each hands a body a velocity and lets gravity have it back - and only the DEFAULT differs, honestly, because they shipped at different rungs of the same ladder: catapult was born drawing the whole parabola AND the gravity arrow (parabola/sum), force_pad was born drawing none of the arc and one arrow (none/velocity), and this one was born in between, whole arc and one arrow. Three siblings measuring alike on the same question is what makes the shared word honest rather than decorative.
dna.why_the_word_fits_here: launch_arc refused foresight last pass on the correct ground that its parabola is a strobe of a flight already completed, so nothing is being foreseen. This machine has a FIRE button, a basket you stand in, and an arc drawn from that basket BEFORE the button is pressed - the word's literal condition. And because the payload is the PLAYER, the axis stops being a display option and becomes a question about consent: at `none` you climb into a cup and find out where you land; at `landing` the floor already says; at `parabola` the whole flight is written before you move.
dna.still_note: both axes are static geometry resolved at build time - no rate, no decay, no animation. _process only calls _refresh() while _firing, and the armed emission pulse needs a player body in the Area3D, so with no player present the frame is deterministic and one still is a complete account. Note for the sweep: at the shipped angle/force the arc runs about 15 m from a 3.2 m frame, so the union camera is set by the arc; three of the four foresight values reach 7-15 m and only `none` is small in that frame. The pairwise difference is a 15 m emissive line present or absent, so the risk here is a large bite, not a null.
dna.declines: launch_force, launch_angle and gravity_magnitude stay plain numeric exports reachable through apply_grid_config but undeclared as axes - a longer arrow and a further arc are size changes, not different claims. Also declined: an axis on the arm swing or the rest pitch, which is animation and invisible to a still.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 31.4% of frame width and 18.4% of its height, with a subject share of 0.43%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.24. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.
dna.current_interaction_note: 2026-10-07: automatic boarding countdown, cancellation on exit, desktop/XR detection, local -Z launch, thick red preview in correct coordinate frame; earlier still-only notes describe the prior build.

dna.default: workings=trace - trace is the fall-through arm of the match and runs no code at all, and the whole match sits AFTER _settle(rig, 2.8), so the legacy fit, scale and placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. The only edit above that line binds five nodes to locals that were previously passed straight into add_child, plus an identity Node3D named ThetaArc holding the eleven arc spheres so the axis can reach the whole arc in one call; pickable_prop._subtree_aabb recurses into Node3D children and does NOT apply their transform, and this holder is never moved, so the settled box is bit-identical to the one that ships. All 3 placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, MindMap_VectorForces, Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces) carry the bare token `force_mower` or `force_mower:0:0` with no config key at all, so the new branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists - and when it IS reached, an unrecognised word is ignored rather than assigned, so a typo falls back to the shipped picture instead of blanking the diagram.
dna.was: no axis. Seven exports - a seed, a 0..1 push_angle and five colours - could move or recolour ONE fixed diagram, and the runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. What the machine draws OF the work was welded into _build and drawn always, in the same order: F down the handle, the horizontal F cos theta, the dashed green waste, the theta arc, the long purple displacement and a billboard readout. A map could set how STEEP the push was and what COLOUR it was, never what the object claimed the product W = F d cos theta is made of.
dna.shared_with: transform_composition_workbench's word with its four values in the same order, seconded on this bench by dot_aligner, vector_add, vector_sub, projection_shadow, launch_arc, torque_crank, bounce_well and length_lantern. W = F.d is the dot product doing manual labour - the same product those benches take apart - so it takes their word rather than inventing a second vocabulary for one question. DERIVED from the @export_enum in force_mower.gd, not transcribed.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. Each value names something this object genuinely has, which is the test for borrowing a word. OUTCOME is where this member departs from its family and earns the word rather than renting it: every sibling answers `outcome` with a length left lying on a rail, and this one answers with a change in the world. All five vectors and the readout leave the render layers and what remains is a machine standing on grass with a strip cut out of it - the work done, stated as mown ground. OPERANDS fixes something the shipped picture never said out loud: F is drawn at the grip and d is drawn down at ankle height, so the two factors of the product never meet and the diagram never claims they are two vectors at an angle. Here d is redrawn leaving the grip beside F, theta is swept between them at double the shipped radius, and a right-angle gnomon is planted where F drops onto the line of d; the DERIVED quantities go dark, because F cos theta and the wasted F sin theta are answers and not ingredients. EXPRESSION stands a plate above the machine writing W = F . d . cos theta with the DRAWN numbers substituted - F_MAG and D_MAG, the lengths actually on the object - rather than the live _dist the readout accumulates, so the board is about the picture and not about how far someone has pushed it. Removal is `layers = 0` on the VisualInstance3D leaves throughout, never visible = false.
dna.declined: `opening` (agreement_gauge's word, seconded by dot_aligner, dot_product_projector and exercise_5_9_angle_between) was the obvious handed-down third use and is refused on TWO independent grounds, either of which is sufficient. First, projection_shadow's test: the pose the word names - the angle between the two vectors whose product this is - is ALREADY the live exported slider. push_angle is 0..1, config-reachable through apply_grid_config, declared in the registry parameters block, and it sweeps exactly theta. A second word for a knob that exists is a fake genome. Second, and worse, the answers do not fit: agreeing/strangers/opposing/parallel are 35, 90, 140 and 0 degrees, and a mower handle at 90 degrees is a pole and at 180 degrees is a mower being pulled backwards by a rope. push_angle spans 16 to 64 degrees because that is the range in which the object is still a lawnmower, so three of the four values would name a machine this one is not. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary. ALSO REFUSED: a purchase-style trade of F against d at constant product, which is torque_crank's bargain applied to W = F d. It is real arithmetic and it is unmeasurable here, because _settle normalises the rig to a fixed 2.8 m span - lengthen d and the whole diagram is scaled down to compensate, so two values differ as the same picture at two magnifications. capture_config_sweep's own header calls that the single worst measurement bug this rig has had; there is no reason to buy it deliberately. push_angle and the five colours stay plain exports: a steeper push and a recolour are not arguments.
dna.still_note: framing 0.65, and the reason is a SIBLING NODE. _ensure_lawn deferred-spawns a 6.9 x 5.3 m lawn - a soil slab plus 440 seeded blades - onto get_parent(), which in the sweep is the SubViewport, so it is not measured by _subtree_aabb (a sibling, not a descendant) but it is very much in frame. At framing 1.0 the union box is about (2.81, 1.99, 0.68) with expression's board included, radius 1.76, and PAD 1.9 opens the frame to roughly 6.7 m across - the lawn then fills it wall to wall and every value shares a large constant background, which is dilution. 0.65 narrows the frame to about 4.3 m, putting the machine at roughly 65 percent of frame width. It cannot crop: the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and the no-crop floor is 1/PAD = 0.526, so 0.65 keeps about 24 percent margin on the furthest corner. The lawn is seeded from hash(seed) ^ 0x5A17 and seed is 0 in every variant, so it is identical in all four frames and adds no noise - only dilution, which is what the framing hint is for. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass and this arithmetic is the evidence offered in its place. If the critic reports faint, check subject share before touching the design: the candidate fault is the lawn, not the axis.

force_mower.name: Force Mower (W = F d cos θ)
force_mower.description: Work made physical. In VFM_03_Motion, lesson:flower_garden gives the mower a 20 × 28 m lawn: grip the pink handle, push forward, steer by moving the hand left/right, and feel simulated rolling drag. The 14 kg body cuts grass into stubble and leaves flowers. A handle readout integrates model push dotted with actual displacement; it does not measure human muscle force. Other placements retain the original angled-force diagram and workings choices.

parameters.lesson: flower_garden selects the hand-driven, ground-plane mower; absent keeps the original diagram
parameters.lawn_width: Garden width in metres; current museum 20
parameters.lawn_length: Garden length in metres; current museum 28
parameters.push_angle: 0..1 handle/push angle θ (flat to steep) - cos θ shrinks the work (default 0.45)

force_play_vortex.name: The field takes a turn
force_play_vortex.description: Eighteen prefabs move through a visible swirl; the visitor meets the same acceleration field.

VectorFieldFlow.description: F(p) = swirl(p) - radial(p). A vector field assigns a direction to every point. The particle reads the field and follows.
VectorFieldFlow.name: VectorFieldFlow

dna.default: field=spiral, lattice=square - spiral restores the exact pre-promotion formula (swirl gain 1.0, radial gain 0.1, so _field_value returns Vector3(-z, breath, x) - position * 0.1 unchanged) and square rebuilds the same 9x9 = 81 arrow grid, so all 7 existing placements are pixel-identical; the lattice rebuild is guarded on a real value change plus an already-built scene
dna.was: one field hard-coded in _field_value as swirl minus 0.1 * radial, sampled on one 9x9 Cartesian arrow grid - the @identity itself named the swirl-to-radial ratio as the critical parameter and asked for a way to blend the two
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-07-29 - the runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. field changes what the instruction written in space SAYS: spiral (circles and falls, never repeats), orbit (closed circles, kept at the radius you arrived with), sink (origin is destiny), source (the field is an exile). lattice changes how the invisible is made visible: the Cartesian grid, the field's own polar rings, or nothing at all - inferred from the tracer's path instead of read off a diagram.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 45.4% of frame width and 28.4% of its height, with a subject share of 2.09%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.36. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

wind_room.name: Wind Room (walk-in field)
wind_room.description: The room-scale, walk-in end of Wind: a field of tall windsocks you stand among, all leaning the same way, so the invisible field becomes a place. A wind field is one direction and one speed filling the space. Wind is a force that has decided to be everywhere at once - and you are in it.

force_vortex.name: Force Vortex
force_vortex.description: Rotating whirlpool force field. An Area3D (cylinder, player_body layer) captures the player; each physics frame the field overwrites their velocity with inward pull + tangential spin + gentle lift, spiralling them toward the core; crossing eject_radius throws them outward + up, then a cooldown. Rotating spiral arms + glowing core + boundary ring. DNA: field_radius (3.5), pull/spin/lift, eject_force/up.
force_vortex.qfep_connection: F_force: a field is a velocity per point — pulled in, spun, thrown out; the body rides the vector current.

dna.default: depiction=spiral, warning=none - together these ARE the shipped vortex. spiral is the `_:` branch of the match and computes the same arithmetic line for line (3 arms, 14 beads, t*TAU*1.1, radius lerpf(0.25, field_radius*0.98, t), height 0.15+t*1.2, size lerpf(0.12,0.04,t), colour field_color->core_color, energy lerpf(3.2,1.4,t)); only the four lines that instance the bead moved into _bead(). warning=none returns on the first line of _build_warning and builds no node at all. Neither key is passed by any existing placement - force_vortex is named in 11 map files (Force_Preview, VFM_Field, VFM_04_Fields, Zone_WarehouseLab, Zone_WarehouseLab_Packed and six museum trials) and every one of them renders byte-identically. apply_grid_config is now guarded: it used to free every child and re-enter _ready() on ANY call, and now rebuilds only when a value actually differs AND the first build has happened.
dna.was: eight @export knobs and every one a magnitude - field_radius, pull_strength, spin_strength, lift, eject_radius, eject_force, eject_up, cooldown_time. Turning them made the same whirlpool pull harder or throw further; not one of them was a claim, and the throw itself is an event no still can hold. The drawing - three arms, fourteen beads, 1.1 turns, a 1.2 m rise - was hard-coded in the body of _build_field with nothing able to reach it. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the kind of knob.
dna.note: depiction is WHAT A FORCE FIELD IS DRAWN AS, with the law held fixed: every value applies the identical v_in = -r-hat*pull + (y-hat x r)*spin + y-hat*lift and the identical throw, and lays the identical bead - same taper, same gradient, same emission falloff - in a different arrangement. spiral is a current you can see before you are in it; spokes is the textbook arrow picture, the inward pull drawn honestly and the swirl not drawn at all; rings is level sets, where you are and never which way you are going; funnel is the rubber-sheet well, gravity's metaphor imported into a vortex with no mass in it; column puts every bead on the boundary, a field as a room you are inside. NOT named `field` although vector_field_grid declares an axis by that word - those five values are five different laws the plane obeys, these five are one law drawn five ways, and the distinction is the whole point. warning is reused character for character from path_block (which took it from catalyst_vent): how much the object tells you BEFORE it costs you anything. It fits here because eject_radius is 0.9 m and the shipped drawing marks it NOWHERE - the core column is 0.22 m of cylinder and the floor ring is the outer boundary, so the circle where the field stops pulling and starts throwing you is invisible. That is a true statement about the artifact, so it is the default. Both axes are appearance-only: the Area3D, the capture cylinder and the throw are identical at every value, because a field you cannot see is not a weaker field.
dna.declines: pull_strength / spin_strength / lift / eject_force / eject_up / cooldown_time stay plain numeric exports - a faster spiral is a rate, and the evidence here is one still per value.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 35.5% of frame width and 20.8% of its height, with a subject share of 0.86%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.27. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis. CORRECTED after verification: the solve assumed the subject box grows exactly as 1/framing, and under a 34-degree perspective camera it grows faster. At 0.27 the box measured 100% of frame width - clipping - so the framing was backed off to 0.36. The 1/f model orders framings correctly and overshoots the last 25%.

gravity_oval.name: Gravity oval
gravity_oval.description: A walk-in artificial field carries 24 familiar prefab bodies up the left column, over the top and down the right in a repeating vertical oval. Step into the stream to travel with them; walk sideways to leave. Real contacts, hand pickup, finite bodies and local reset. The field supplies energy; the tracked head stays upright.

force_play_liquids.name: Walk into resistance
force_play_liquids.description: Three large transparent drag regions slow falling points and the visitor. Approximate drag and buoyancy, not fluid simulation.

force_play_friction.name: The slope does not choose the ending
force_play_friction.description: Four slopes compare cube/ball and smooth/rough contact; trajectories leave trails.

viscosity_layers.description: Three transparent columns side by side — air, water, and honey. Drop identical balls into all three simultaneously and watch them descend at wildly different rates. Quadratic drag makes the honey ball crawl while the air ball plummets. Real-time speed readouts let you compare terminal velocities directly.
viscosity_layers.name: Viscosity Layers
viscosity_layers.qfep_connection: Resistance as information — the medium tells you what it's made of. Drag is the environment's signature, entropy in the friction between motion and medium.

centrifuge_ring.name: Centrifuge Ring (walk-in centripetal)
centrifuge_ring.description: A body-scale prescribed circular path. The moving pod displays tangential velocity and the inward acceleration v²/r required by that path. The configured comparison changes speed between 2, 4 and 6 m/s while its radius stays at 3.4 metres; radius is separately configurable in source or map data. It does not integrate a force to obtain the orbit or automatically carry the visitor. The distinction between a drawn acceleration and a dynamic cause is part of the encounter.

parameters.speed: 0..1 parameter mapped to prescribed linear speed 2..9 m/s

force_play_springs.name: Pull one, disturb the row
force_play_springs.description: Seven hanging familiar points share restoring springs; pull one and disturb its neighbours.

pendulum_noise.name: The Same Release / A Recorded Push
pendulum_noise.description: Pull either familiar point to set both releases. Compare a recorded four-second horizontal force off/on, then the same input with different damping. Local controls,20s clock,angles,peaks and terminal settling tolerance. Angular model; not a contact or Jolt hinge simulation.
interactions: Pull either point; release both
Force strength
Comparison damping
Run/pause
Replay
Switch comparison
Next seed
