pendulum_noise.qfep_connection: Separate a retained disturbance from its receiver. A changed response need not imply a changed rule or adaptive controller.

force_play_swings.name: How long should a disturbance last
force_play_swings.description: Three connected swing pairs compare weak, medium and strong damping.

force_play_constraints.name: Attachment changes the possible
force_play_constraints.description: Basket, three-link chain, suspended plank and articulated arm use physical joints.

SpringSuspension.description: A car-like suspension system using a Generic6DOF joint configured as a vertical spring. A wheel hangs below a chassis, free to bounce vertically but locked in all other axes. The spring stiffness and damping create the characteristic suspension feel — press space to drop the wheel and watch it oscillate to rest. This demonstrates how a single 6DOF joint with carefully chosen axis locks and spring parameters can simulate complex mechanical behavior.
SpringSuspension.name: SpringSuspension
SpringSuspension.qfep_connection: Classical F with lambda-tuning — the 6DOF joint's spring stiffness and damping are the lambda parameters that tune between rigid constraint (high stiffness) and free motion (low stiffness). The sweet spot produces naturalistic suspension.
SpringSuspension.gamwell_reference: Spring-damper systems, suspension mechanics, Generic6DOF joints, Hooke's law in constrained systems, shock absorber dynamics
interactions: press space to bounce the wheel and watch it oscillate
observe the spring-damped settling behavior
notice how vertical motion is free but lateral motion is locked
SpringSuspension.capacity: EXPLAIN how a 6DOF joint with spring parameters on one axis and locks on all others creates suspension behavior.

dna.measured: SWEPT 2026-08-27: 2.55% / 44.5%, BITES, vs floor 3.0 - 0.85x, an under-floor that was NOT broken: the bob's frame share was overestimated. Direction recorded.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: CLOSEST PAIR: bob weight vs crate, floor 3.0% whole-frame (the axis has one pair). Arithmetic: the bob is 1.0 x 0.8 m at eq_y in a 2.9 x 5.8 body; at subject ~35% of frame the bob is ~4%, and box-to-crate changes about three quarters of it - the glow dies, the slats arrive - so 3.0%. Registered 2026-08-27, before the first capture.

spring_tower.name: Spring Tower (walk-in Hooke)
spring_tower.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of spring_bob: a heavy mass bobs on a giant coil at its real period T = 2π√(m/k); the coil stretches and compresses while the spring force (−kx) and the weight trade places at body scale. F = −kx, the signature of everything that keeps time. Stand beside the tower and watch it tick.

phase_rod_array.name: Twenty clocks
phase_rod_array.description: Twenty light rods with eyes on their tips that keep looking at the player: shift one phase, form a phase wave, or drift two rows by changing their frequency. Eye direction follows the visitor independently of rod phase.
phase_rod_array.qfep_connection: The relation between local rules and collective outcomes is inspectable. Difference can make a pattern or produce congestion; this exhibit does not measure entropy or establish a QFEP threshold.
interactions: ONE +
WAVE
DRIFT
RESET
RULE

force_trial_conveyor.name: The belt keeps going
force_trial_conveyor.description: Feed 32 grabbable museum prefabs onto a contact-driven belt. Pull a spring-closing hinged gate; hold its trigger for faster deliveries. The second half arrives oversized. Cargo rocks a hinged receiver and spills; ordinary spills persist until local reset. Reuses crate, chair-kit, extinguisher and PointBody geometry.
learning_objectives: Contact motion, input/output rate, accumulated backlog.
force_trial_conveyor.qfep_connection: An available operation changes a situation; the body and environment retain its consequence. This trial makes no numerical entropy claim.

force_play_mutual.name: You become another source
force_play_mutual.description: Five larger orbiting points; the visitor becomes the sixth source. Softened attraction with contact disabled.

force_play_magnet.name: The catch must end
force_play_magnet.description: A large timed magnet attracts twelve prefabs for three seconds. A held point also becomes a trigger-driven gravity gun.

force_play_tower.name: One brick holds the question
force_play_tower.description: Pull the bottom rose brick; forty-two upper bricks lose their support. A small companion table carries nine loose shapes: pick up, turn and reorder the stack by hand; its reset is independent.

force_play_gravity.name: The room lets go
force_play_gravity.description: An entry threshold releases a hinged trapdoor, suspended cargo and a leaning pole.

orbit_walk.name: Orbit Walk (walk-in two-body)
orbit_walk.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of orbit_pair: stand at the barycenter while a heavy star and a lighter planet wheel around you on opposite sides, the equal-and-opposite gravity vectors (F = G m1 m2 / r squared) riding each body. Make one heavier and the barycenter slides toward it, the orbits resizing to keep the balance. An orbit is two things falling toward each other and missing, around a centre that belongs to neither.

parameters.mass_ratio: 0..1 — heavier star slides the barycenter toward it

force_play_support.name: Move a leg, inherit the load
force_play_support.description: Move an actual table leg beneath a tall uneven load; contacts decide the collapse.

one_leg.description: Single IK leg demo — the fundamental unit of procedural locomotion. One joint chain finding ground contact. The building block from which all multi-legged creatures emerge.
one_leg.name: One Leg
one_leg.qfep_connection: The progression's axiom: one skeleton chain, one spring-found contact point, and a body that must bounce because balance on a single foot can only ever be serial. Everything the later critters elaborate — plant, stretch, step — is reduced here to whether the leg can reach the floor at all.

four_leg_critter.description: Four-legged procedural walker. A prescribed body drift stretches the planted feet; the gait code selects the most stretched eligible leg and moves one leg at a time. In VFM_09_Legs this visible walking is compared with physical support, which this walker does not solve.
four_leg_critter.name: Four Leg Critter
four_leg_critter.qfep_connection: The comparison exposes a choice hidden by a convincing gait: a branch selects one foot, and a commanded body does not negotiate support forces. The form is an opportunity to inspect that rule, not evidence that a diagonal trot or stable gait emerged from physics.

six_leg_critter.description: Six-legged procedural walker. Insect-like alternating tripod gait — three legs always grounded. The most common arthropod configuration.
six_leg_critter.name: Six Leg Critter
six_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Six thresholds firing independently keep drifting toward the insect answer — three feet down, three swinging — because with legs at 60° that is simply what does not fall over. Four hundred million years of hexapod convergence restaged as the accident of a step rule.

sentry_turret.description: Half-Life style sentry turret. Targets balls and/or player. Simple reliable targeting with bullet physics. Emits signals for hits.
interactions: Automatic - targets balls and player
sentry_turret.name: Sentry Turret
sentry_turret.qfep_connection: The turret as autonomous agent - continuously computing vectors to track and engage targets.

ball_dropper.description: Drops colorful physics balls one at a time. Pair with laser_turret for targeting demo. Balls cycle through colors and have configurable physics properties.
interactions: Automatic dropping - configure via parameters
ball_dropper.name: Ball Dropper
ball_dropper.qfep_connection: Entropy source - introducing moving targets into the system for the turret to track.

force_play_bowling.name: Ten pins, one commitment
force_play_bowling.description: Ten compound rigid pins, a black sphere, long lane, bumpers and banked sides.

dna.default: face=bullseye, flag=progress - together these ARE the shipped object. bullseye is the `_:` branch of the match and runs the loop that used to be inline in _generate_rings, line for line: radius_step = max_radius / n, palette[0] outermost, a 1 mm z-offset per ring, cylinders rotated 90 degrees on X. progress returns the same eight Progress Pride colours in the same order the literal array carried. All 3 placements (ForcesArena and Forces_Drone_Game at rotations 90 and -90, VFM_08_Arena bare) pass no config key at all, and apply_grid_config returns before touching anything unless a word actually moved. Neither axis reaches the CollisionShape3D, the audio, the particles, the flash tween or the score: every arrangement is hit in exactly the same way.
dna.was: five magnitude exports (points_per_hit, breathing_speed, breathing_amount, target_radius and target_thickness - the last of which the build never read) and no apply_grid_config at all. Both of the lists that decide what this object IS were hard-coded, and the palette carried the comment `(removed outer yellow/orange/red)`: an editorial decision about which stripes it wears, left in a parenthesis.
dna.note: The identity block already claimed that 'the same geometry is two cultural objects depending on intent - flag when still, target when sighted' about a build that only ever produced one of the two. face makes the claim checkable rather than asserted: bands is the flag standing where the target stood, with no centre for the colours to converge on; spokes puts every colour the same distance from the middle so no ring is the bull and none the outer; column lays the face down into a ziggurat that faces nobody, which the truth line says a target cannot do. flag is the second hard-coded list: rainbow is the 1979 six-stripe the shipped palette is a revision of, trans is the only symmetric palette here (it has no outer), full restores what the source comment removed, and archery is the regulation FITA face - the object with the flag taken off it, which is the counterfactual the artifact needs. Ring count follows palette size, so flag changes the geometry and not only the colour. A new export, breathing_phase, defaults to -1.0 = the shipped random start phase per instance; dna.fixture pins it at 2.0 for the sweep, because otherwise the 2 percent breathing scale walks between frames and arrives in the critic numbers dressed as the axis.

queer_cylinder_target.description: A target face built from Progress Pride stripes: eight concentric emissive disks, outermost first, each a millimetre in front of the last, breathing gently on a sine. Hits anywhere flash every ring white, fire a burst of coloured cubes and score - the same surface reads as a flag when still and as a target when sighted.
queer_cylinder_target.name: queer_cylinder_target
queer_cylinder_target.qfep_connection: a target that takes the hit and keeps its difference — the cylinder the throwing room aims at; consequence's address.

force_punching_bag.name: A push comes back
force_punching_bag.description: A seven-kilogram padded bag swings on a real pin joint. Nearby tracked hands wear local collision mitts; held clubs and loose balls also strike it. Pull the rose force grip without detaching the bag. Local reset.
force_punching_bag.qfep_connection: Contact redistributes motion; the joint permits a return while preventing free translation. The encounter does not measure muscular force or entropy.

force_play_recoil.name: The launcher also moves
force_play_recoil.description: Compare equal opposite impulses on free and braced carts.

momentum_cradle.name: Momentum Cradle (p = mv conserved)
momentum_cradle.description: Momentum conservation made playable - Newton's cradle, rebuilt as a console. Lift an end ball and the blow travels through the still middle balls untouched and kicks the far ball out to the same height: one in, one out, p = mv conserved. lift 0..1 sets the swing amplitude.

parameters.carried: one | two | all - how many balls go in, and therefore how many come out (default one)
parameters.demo_only: capture mode: drop the console, demo only

dna.measured: SWEPT 2026-08-27, both axes read separately as the prediction demanded: bobs 4.59% / 59.6% (predicted 4-5), carried 2.49% / 41.7% (floor 2.0). Neither axis hides the other.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: CLOSEST PAIR: carried one vs two, at bobs=uniform, floor 2.0% whole-frame. Arithmetic: the pair moves exactly two end bobs (r 0.12) through ~31 deg on 0.62 m strings inside a 1.54 x 1.4 rig; at subject ~35% of frame each bob is ~0.8%, plus the string sweep, so 2.0%. The bobs axis (uniform vs museum) reskins all five bodies and should read 4-5%. NAMED RISK: this is now a TWO-AXIS sweep, so the headline peak will be the bobs axis - read the per-pair rows or a dead carried pair hides behind a live bobs one (the tier_terrarium failure). Registered 2026-08-27, before the first capture.
dna.default: carried=one - _carried_in() returns 1 from the fall-through arm of its match, which makes n_in = 1 and n_out = 1, and the loop's two tests then reduce to exactly the code they replace: `i < 1` is the old `i == 0` and `i >= BALLS - 1` is the old `i == BALLS - 1`. The arrow guard is the same reduction - `lift > 0.04 and not is_zero_approx(ang)` is true on precisely the two end balls when the old `(i == 0 or i == BALLS - 1) and lift > 0.04` was - and the readout's new %d in / %d out substitutes 1 and 1, reproducing the shipped string character for character. BALLS is still 5, the frame, the strings, the spacing and the settle are untouched, so all 4 existing placements (MindMap_VectorForces, VFM_08_Arena, VFM_Forces_Lab, Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation), every one of which carries the bare token, render byte-identically
dna.was: seven @exports, six of them a rate, a size or a colour, and the seventh - lift - a swing amplitude. Not one of them changes what the cradle argues, and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The demonstration itself was welded into the ball loop as `if i == 0` and `elif i == BALLS - 1`: the console could draw exactly one sentence, one in and one out, and that sentence is only the first line of the lesson
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. THE AXIS IS THE COUNT, because the count IS the demonstration - lift two and two leave, which is the fact that separates a momentum cradle from any other row of hanging balls. At one, three balls stand still as couriers; at two, the courier line is down to a single ball; at all, every ball is lifted together, nobody is left to carry anything, nothing is transmitted and the readout says 5 in, 0 out - a five-ball pendulum wearing a cradle's frame. Appearance only in the strict sense: no collision rule, no mass, no timing and no physics of any kind is touched, because this console DRAWS its pose rather than integrating it. That is also why the axis exists here at all
dna.shared_with: nothing, deliberately. standstill (newton_cradle, none|catch|chalk|scale|tally) was considered first, as the direct sibling's word, and refused: it names what an apparatus says with its balls hanging DEAD, and this console's balls are never dead - at the shipped lift of 0.6 the two ends stand at 31 degrees with momentum arrows over them, and the one pose that would satisfy the word is already reachable by pulling the exported lift slider to zero. Its five answers are release catches, chalked arcs, graduated quadrants and bead tallies - hardware invented to stand in for a motion that could not be photographed. Here the motion IS photographed
dna.harness_note: one axis of three values, so nothing is trimmed at the default --max=9 and the shipped pose is always one of the three frames. The hot pixels are the accent momentum arrows and the glowing balls, which is exactly what the axis moves - two arrows at one, four at two, five at all - so a fixture should not be needed. If it is, demo_only=true is an @export on the shared ToyConsole base that drops the 1.5 m housing and photographs the demo alone at 1.9 m; it is left undeclared here because demo_only is a TYPED bool and this pass could not run a capture to prove that whatever sets it passes a real bool and not the string "true"
dna.note_declined: the two artifacts are the same claim under opposite conditions, and it is worth writing down which way round. newton_cradle REFUSED this very axis on 2026-08-03, under the name lift, because its swing is integrated in _physics_process: _release_left() sets an angle and the balls are moving on the next frame, and with a 0.6 m string the quarter period is 0.39 s, so a settled capture photographs a cradle mid-swing at an arbitrary phase. It took standstill instead, and could only take standstill. momentum_cradle has no _physics_process at all - _build_demo computes each ball's angle and places it - so the pose that is unphotographable there is the only thing that exists here. Neither artifact could have taken the other's axis

newton_cradle.capacity: SEE that momentum transfers through a chain — the middle balls are messengers, not movers

dna.default: standstill=none - the one word _build_standstill() returns on before adding a single node, so the scene tree is the bare frame, five balls, five strings, the info label and the button panel, exactly as shipped. All 9 existing placements are untouched.
dna.was: eight exports - ball_count, ball_radius, string_length, ball_mass, gravity, damping and three colours. Sizes, rates and palette: not one of them changes what the cradle argues, and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS.
dna.note: DERIVED from the @export_enum in NewtonCradle.gd, not transcribed - the code shipped the axis in last night's rescue batch and the registry never carried it, so the sweep could not reach it. Values are the code's STANDSTILLS array character for character. THE AXIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE SWING: five balls at rest are five identical balls in a row, and a still cannot photograph a rate, so the claim is made in the hardware that survives the stopping - a release catch, chalked arcs, a graduated quadrant, a bead tally. Appearance only: nothing here touches _angles, _angular_velocities or the collision rule, so the conservation law is taught by the same code in all five. A SECOND AXIS WAS DECLINED - see note_declined.
dna.note_declined: lift (one|two|three balls raised) was considered and refused. It is the demonstration - lift two and two leave - but it is not photographable: _release_left() sets the angle and _physics_process starts the swing on the next frame, and with string_length 0.6 the quarter period is 0.39 s, so by the time a capture settles the lifted ball is already at the bottom. A sweep of it would publish three finished-looking frames of a cradle mid-swing at three unrelated phases and call the scatter a finding. It would also be inert at the default: standstill=none draws no arcs and no pips, so the count would have nothing to write itself on.

newton_cradle.description: The iconic desktop physics demo: 5 pendulum balls suspended from a frame. Pull one back and release — momentum transfers through elastic collisions, ball-by-ball. Shows conservation of momentum and energy, elastic collision mechanics, and the satisfying click-clack of F=ma made tangible.
newton_cradle.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, numerical methods
interactions: pull and release end balls
observe momentum transfer
count oscillation cycles
newton_cradle.name: Newton's Cradle
newton_cradle.qfep_connection: F-conservation — momentum and energy transfer through a chain of collisions. What enters on one side exits on the other. The middle balls appear still but carry the signal.

free_vector.name: Free Vector (direction + length)
free_vector.description: The intimate companion to VectorBasics for Vector basics: one arrow and its ghost copies, carried to different origins to show a vector has no home. A vector is two facts only - a direction and a length; slide it anywhere and it is the same vector. A vector is a journey with no starting address.

force_field.description: Dual-nature force zone: every hazard is also medicine. Fire warms or burns. Poison kills or reveals. Q-FEP: same potential, different restraint, different manifestation. Bring a mediator object into the field to transmute hazard into benefit.
force_field.name: Force Field
force_field.qfep_connection: Central demonstration of Q-FEP: identical potential under different relational constraint produces opposite outcomes. The player experiences this directly.

dna.default: decomposition=both - `both` is the `_` branch of the match and rebuilds the shipped body of _redraw line for line: the three dashed 0.006 guides walking ZERO -> (fx,0,0) -> (fx,fy,0) -> tip at the same dim 0.6/0.62/0.68 glow, then the three 0.016 component arrows leaving the origin behind the same absf(f) > 0.05 gates, then the 0.03 resultant and the same billboarded readout, added to demo_root in the same order. Nothing else moved: _resting_force, _build_body, _process and the _last_f short-circuit are untouched. All 3 placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace, Void_Crossing) place the bare token `force_cube` with no config key at all, so the new branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists - and when it IS reached, _last_f is only invalidated if the word is in DECOMPOSITIONS and differs from the current value, so a call naming nothing this artifact owns still rebuilds nothing.
dna.was: seven exports - five colours, a seed and a push - and one hard-coded way of taking a force apart. The three coloured legs left the origin and a dashed staircase walked the same three components tip to tail, both always, welded into the body of _redraw. A map could set how LONG the vector was and what COLOUR it was, never what the object claimed a vector is made of. The runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and on the question that matters that was true.
dna.note: decomposition is HOW THE COMPONENTS ARE PUT ON THE GEOMETRY, and the word plus the meanings of chain, box and none are taken character for character from basis_vectors_rig (commons_artifacts), vector_magnitude_demo and example_1_5_vector_magnitude_vr, which ask the same question of the same three RGB legs. This is the one member of that family you can PICK UP, which is why the word belongs here: on the other three benches the decomposition is of a vector drawn for you, here it is of a vector you are holding, and the legs re-resolve in the cube's own frame as you turn it. chain walks the legs tip to tail as solid arrows so the last one lands exactly on the resultant's point; box draws the twelve edges of the solid the components span, closed on the tip so the resultant IS its diagonal; none leaves the claim to the arrow and the readout.
dna.kin: The value list is NOT the family's list, and the missing rung is `star` - all three legs leaving the origin, the terms rather than the path. It is absent for a MEASUREMENT reason, not a taxonomic one, exactly as `source` is absent from vector_field_grid's `field`. This artifact already draws the star: `both` IS star plus the walked guide, so `star` would differ from the default by the presence of three dashed cylinders of 6 mm radius and nothing else. Rasterising the four values at the harness's own numbers (RES 760, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, union AABB, four plausible seeded resting directions) puts that pair at 0.12-0.29% of frame against a 2.0% bite threshold: a duplicate tile bought in advance, which is the refusal ftc_bridge made of `axiom` on the same grounds.
dna.still_note: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the number is honest about being marginal. This subject is thin ink - a 0.40 m glass cube plus one 0.03 m resultant, three 0.016 m legs and up to sixty 0.006 m dashes on a 1.24 m vector - so the axis is real in world space and close to the floor of what this bench can see. Rasterising the four values over four plausible resting directions at framing 0.55 gives a peak pairwise change of 2.01-2.58% and a weakest pair (both vs chain) of 0.46-1.46%; at framing 1.0 the same axis peaks at 0.51%. framing 0.55 is the tightest value that still cannot crop, because the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and 0.55 is above 1/PAD = 0.53; the raster agrees, putting the furthest projected point at 325-355 px of the 380 px half-frame. THE ONE THING THAT COULD STILL GO WRONG: _resting_force draws its direction from _rng seeded with hash(seed), and a draw close to a single axis (say 0.95, 0.25, 0.05) leaves almost nothing to decompose - that direction measured 2.01% where a well-spread one measured 2.58%. If the sweep returns faint, change `seed` before believing anything about the design. No fixture is needed otherwise: the cube is frozen with zero velocity, so _process takes the resting-vector branch and the still is already reproducible.
dna.declines: `rest` - what the cube claims when no hand is on it - was designed, measured and refused. _resting_force invents a seeded arbitrary vector for an object nobody is touching, and sample|weight|normal|zero is a genuine argument about that. It is not shipped for two reasons, both hard. A vertical weight or normal has ONE nonzero component, so at two of its four values the decomposition axis has nothing to draw and the cross sweep would publish identical tiles under different words - the same fault refused above, bought twice. And `rest` is the axis a player destroys by picking the cube up, which is the one thing this artifact is for; decomposition is the axis that survives the hand. push and seed stay plain exports: a longer arrow is a bigger photograph of the same claim. The five colours stay plain exports; a recolour is not an argument.

force_cube.name: Force Cube (a vector you hold)
force_cube.description: A grabbable cube that draws the force you apply as an arrow out of its centre, split into x / y / z components - an embodied force-display prop. The cube IS the tail of the vector: wherever you push it the arrow points, and the three coloured component arrows (red Fx, green Fy, blue Fz) plus a dashed decomposition box show how one push is really three. A faint motion trail follows. DNA: push 0..1 is the force magnitude; seed sets its direction (live, both come from the grabbing hand's motion).

vector_machine.name: Vector Machine (the dial of gravity)
vector_machine.description: A console composes a world-coordinate acceleration vector from pitch, yaw and magnitude and posts it to force_field receivers. The configured Force-as-Place lesson labels magnitude ACCEL, exposes an idle yaw at a vertical pole and begins at downward 9.8 m/s². Cube and visitor receivers retain and update motion differently; a drawn arrow alone does not guarantee passage.

parameters.force_max: max magnitude the FORCE slider reaches (default 15)

force_field_zone.name: Force Field Zone (a force made into a place)
force_field_zone.description: A local acceleration volume with a wireframe boundary and field arrows. Unfrozen rigid bodies inside have ordinary gravity disabled and receive velocity += field_vector * delta, without division by mass; their contacts and damping remain. The museum visitor uses a separate velocity-carrying locomotion receiver, retaining incoming motion while inside and returning control on exit. The configured five-metre crossing keeps a solid plank for comparison. Legacy force naming identifies the artifact; the applied quantity is acceleration.

parameters.law: gravity | lift | crossing | weightless - which constant vector rules the volume (default gravity)
parameters.boundary: flow | cage | corners | open - how the zone declares its own edge (default flow)
parameters.flow_time: capture fixture, not an axis: 0.0 freezes the streaming chevrons (default 1.0)

dna.default: law=gravity, boundary=flow - gravity SHORT-CIRCUITS: _apply_law() returns before touching anything, so field_vector stays the shipped @export Vector3(0, -9.8, 0), and a map that overrides field_vector alone keeps its own vector instead of being reset to the table's. boundary=flow builds the twelve edge cylinders, then the eight corner spheres, then the six-face BoxMesh carrying force_flow.gdshader - the same three blocks in the same order as before this pass, with nothing added and nothing skipped. All 9 placements (MindMap_VectorForces, Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace, Void_Crossing and the six Trial_*_forces rooms, which mount it through exhibit_furniture) carry the bare token with no config keys, so apply_grid_config reaches no assignment, sets no dirty flag and never rebuilds.
dna.was: four @export knobs and not one categorical among them: size is a length, field_vector three numbers, edge_color and arrow_color two colours. The zone had exactly one look - a wireframe cage with flowing faces - and exactly one law unless a vector_machine stood next to it and a hand moved its sliders. apply_grid_config tore down every child and rebuilt on ANY call, the force_pad trap.
dna.note: law is force_field_visualizer's word and shares its gravity value; its other three (point_charge, dipole, vortex) are REFUSED, because those are position-dependent fields and this zone adds ONE constant f to every body inside it - that uniformity is the whole of what it argues. boundary is vr_tile_editor's word with its value list refused: a volume of space has no cells and no lattice. flow_time is the fixture, not an axis - the chevrons stream on TIME and two variants shot a fraction of a second apart would differ by phase alone.

invisible_hill.name: Invisible Hill
invisible_hill.description: The Force-field hero, elevating force_field_zone: a dead-flat green where glowing pucks swerve around a hill that exists only as force (mu/r2, integrated live) - their trails pile up into the invisible summit's portrait. Category-heroes pass, 2026-08-27.

endless_racer.name: Endless Drive
endless_racer.description: Board an arcade car inside the museum. Grip the steering wheel, right trigger accelerates, left trigger brakes. A bounded road pool supplies endless bends, collectible cubes and barriers. Reachable restart and museum return.
endless_racer.qfep_connection: Steering selects a path while speed, inertia and resistance constrain corrections. Arcade rules are explicit; this is not a physical tyre model or an entropy measurement.

force_capability_lab.name: Forces — a capability court
force_capability_lab.description: Two carried points apply thrust; a cake mortar launches hollow physical rings; a launch pad meets a moving platform; a hinged pole falls; spring points collide; loose cubes cross a drag lane. Ordinary aftermath persists until an explicit reset.
force_capability_lab.qfep_connection: A known object gains a capacity. Release lets the environment participate; the next attempt inherits the aftermath. Pulling, resistance and drag can be read together without equating their meanings.

force_play_flight.name: A mat, two points, a way through
force_play_flight.description: Two inherited trigger-thrust points carry the visitor and a visual flying mat through four elevated gates.

film_catenoid_sections.name: A waist and sixteen intervals
film_catenoid_sections.description: Boundary rings, the narrow waist and sampled sections reveal how the actual catenoid surface is assembled.
interactions: Look at the screen to play.
Pause, replay, step or turn the view.
film_catenoid_sections.qfep_connection: Analytic catenoid with c=0.82, height range -1 to 1, 16 by 48 intervals. No settling, stability test or universal area-minimum claim.

cable_builder.description: Move four grabbable control beads to redraw a cable. Per-span Bezier handles add a chosen downward sag; the curve is drafted from those controls rather than found by a physical chain solver.
cable_builder.name: Cable Builder

catenoid.name: Catenoid
catenoid.description: A sampled parametric catenoid generated from cosh and circular sections. A grabbable model of a minimal surface, not a live soap-film simulation or a guarantee of globally least area for arbitrary ring separation.
catenoid.qfep_connection: Compare a boundary-conditioned analytic construction with a drafted cable. An elegant form can make a model convincing; its formula and rendering do not establish that material has performed an optimization in this room.

helicoid.name: Helicoid
helicoid.description: A sampled parametric helicoid with straight ruling lines and screw symmetry, presented as a grabbable model. Its mathematical relation to a catenoid can be discussed, but this artifact performs no continuous deformation between the two.
helicoid.qfep_connection: A different parameterization opens a different surface while keeping the construction inspectable. The small model is a comparison of forms, not a staircase for the visitor or a measured least-area experiment.

laundry_line_cathedral.name: Laundry Line Cathedral
laundry_line_cathedral.description: Three sampled cosh washing lines with shirts and towels, supported by end crossbars, and mirrored ghost arches above. The analytic curves and inversion make a structural analogy visible; the artifact does not solve loaded ropes or masonry equilibrium.

mass_spring_bench.name: Mass-Spring Bench (a shape nobody specified)
mass_spring_bench.description: A connected lattice relaxed for a fixed number of initialization steps, then displayed with prescribed rocking. The frozen geometry preserves a finite computational history; the display does not keep solving spring dynamics.

dna.default: relaxation=worked, and the word returns the literal 4 that line 85 already declares (`@export var constraint_passes: int = 4`) and that `_make_sim` has always handed to the solver. It is a SHORT-CIRCUIT, not a formula that lands near it: RELAXATION_PASSES is a const dict with the integer 4 written out, so `sim.constraint_passes` is assigned the same value from the same table on every build. The pre-existing numeric contract survives intact — a config carrying `constraint_passes` sets `_passes_pinned` and `_effective_passes()` returns the number instead, so the word can never override a map written before this promotion. Both fixture exports are exact no-ops at their defaults: `still = false` selects the original gust branch character for character (`gust = sin(_t * 0.8) * 0.6`, `gravity = Vector3(gust, -3.0, 0.3 * sin(_t * 0.5))`, dial `sin(_t * 0.3) * 0.6`, sway `sin(_t * 0.25) * 0.06`), and `settle_steps = 60` is the literal count the shipped `for _i in 60` ran. ONE PLACEMENT in 2420 maps: FormFinding_Relaxation, token `verlet_workbench:90` — a rotation suffix and nothing else, so merged_config is empty, GridInteractablesComponent never calls apply_grid_config, and that placement never reaches a line this promotion added. No exhibit_furniture mount and no curation roster names it. The one behavioural change at the default is the deletion of `_rng.randomize()`; `_rng` is inherited from embodied_prop.gd and read nowhere in this file (grep: zero hits), so nothing observes it, and leaving it would have been a loaded gun for the next person who adds a randf to _build.
dna.was: a dial, a readout and a claim — none of them reachable by name. `constraint_passes` was already a clamped config key and `_readout_text` already printed `passes: %d`, so the bench could always be told to relax harder; but no map ever told it to, and there was no word a sweep could use. More seriously, it had no resting state at all: `_process` drove `_sim.gravity` from `sin(_t * 0.8)` off the wall clock and re-ran the integrator once per RENDERED frame, so the pose was a function of both elapsed time and frame count. Measured on a python replica of soft_body_sim.step(): with the gust running, `worked` moves 25.6 mm of max vertex displacement between render frame 66 and frame 90 — three times the entire worked-to-held separation of 8.5 mm. Any bite number taken from the shipped artifact would have been a fact about the shutter.
dna.note: `relaxation` is SHARED with cloth_simulation in this same wave, deliberately and character for character — apply_dna_block derived the same four values in the same order from two independent solvers: soft_body_sim's `for _p in constraint_passes` with a stiffness gain of 0.75, and ClothSimulation.gd's own iteration loop with a hard-coded gain. It is the same question, how insistently is a distance constraint enforced, so their bite numbers should ORDER the same way and sit within about a factor of two of each other; if they do not, that disagreement is evidence about the harness rather than about either design. The word exists at all because apply_dna_block refuses a numeric axis by design — sample points on a continuum are a design choice, not a fact about the code — so the four points are named here and derived there: nudged = 1, worked = 4 (the shipped literal), pressed = 8, held = 12. This artifact already WAS this axis; @identity states the claim outright (crank the passes up and the cloth stiffens; drop them and it sags — yet no linear system is ever solved). What was missing was the word.
dna.declined: `damping` (0.99), the purest rate axis in the sequence: four values reach the SAME drape, some sooner, and a still cannot tell them apart at rest — declined by name because this wave exists to refuse exactly that. The gust amplitudes (0.6 lateral, 0.3 in Z) move the cloth about seven times as far as the whole axis does and are still wrong, because they are a DRIVE: `sin(_t * 0.8)` never stops, so photographing them is photographing the clock, and the fixture's entire job is to switch them off. Cloth resolution (cloth_cols 10 / cloth_rows 8 / cell 0.085) is a real and interesting claim — the discretization IS the material — but `grain` is already the corpus's word for how a body is subdivided, across six artifacts with a different value set, and inventing a seventh synonym to serve ONE placement is worse than shipping one axis that is exactly right. The pin mode (`top_corners`, with six values already sitting in soft_body_shapes._cloth_is_pin) is flagdancer's `heading` in this same wave; if verlet_workbench ever wants it, the honest move is to take flagdancer's word and values, not a synonym.
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED THIS ARTIFACT IS NEVER AT REST, so without this fixture every number the sweep produces is about the frame clock rather than about the material. `still` zeroes the four things the bench drives off the wall clock — the lateral gust, the Z gust, the bench sway and the dial spin — in one guarded branch, so `_sim.gravity` holds the constant (0, -3, 0) the pre-settle already used and both rotating nodes hold rotation 0. `settle_steps` raises the existing SYNCHRONOUS pre-settle from 60 to 420 so every value reaches ITS OWN fixed point before frame 1. All of this is measured on a python replica of soft_body_sim.step() rather than argued: at 420 steps the pose is 0.050 mm from the 2400-step pose for nudged and bit-identical for worked, pressed and held; 66 further rendered frames then move nudged by 0.066 mm and the other three by 0.0000 mm. At the shipped 60 the same comparison moves nudged by 21.0 mm — ten times the closest pair's separation — because at step 60 nudged is still in transient overshoot, moving 0.88 mm in step 61 against 0.0010 mm in step 421. The step SIZE cannot drift with frame rate: soft_body_sim.step takes `dt: float = 0.0166667` and no caller passes another. The simulator holds no RNG and `_rng.randomize()` is deleted, so with the pose fixed in _ready two runs of one value are the same picture.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config assigns every key it accepts, then compares `_build_signature()` — relaxation, the effective pass count, cloth_cols, cloth_rows, cell, emissive, stiffness, all four colours, still and settle_steps — and RETURNS before touching a live simulation when nothing the build reads has changed. Teardown walks an `_owned: Array[Node]` rather than `get_children()`, which is what the shipped version did: that loop freed every child on every config call, taking any plinth, highlight, collider or pickup plumbing the grid had attached down with the artifact, and it rebuilt unconditionally because there was no signature to compare. _ready() builds synchronously and there is no call_deferred anywhere in the build path.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: pressed vs held, and the arithmetic is the solver's own fixed-point law. Residual stretch scales as 1/(passes x gain) at gain 0.75, so the four values sit at 1.33 / 0.33 / 0.167 / 0.111 residual units and the last two are 0.056 apart against nudged-to-worked's 1.0 — 18:1 predicted. MEASURED on the replica at settle 420, as max vertex displacement: pressed-vs-held 2.154 mm and nudged-vs-worked 34.458 mm, a ratio of 16.0:1. The law holds and the prediction was 12% high. NOW THE PART THAT CAN BE WRONG, and it is about pixels rather than millimetres. The camera does not move between tiles: the merged MeshInstance3D AABB is 1.32 x 1.34 x 0.70 for all four values, because the cloth hangs between y 0.659 and 1.30 and never touches a face of it. At dna.framing 0.65 the frame is 2.479 m over 760 px, i.e. 3.261 mm/px — which puts pressed-vs-held at 0.66 px, SUB-PIXEL, and nudged-vs-worked at 10.6 px across a cloth holding 7.6% of frame. And the cloth is flat-shaded: _rebuild_cloth_mesh writes Vector3.UP into every normal, so its interior is a near-uniform emissive field and almost all of the change is SILHOUETTE, not shading. Counting the moving edge (a 235 px bottom travelling ~10.6 px, plus two 186 px sides averaging half of that) gives roughly 4,500 changed pixels out of 577,600. PREDICT nudged-vs-worked frame ~0.8%, focus ~9%; pressed-vs-held frame ~0.05%, focus ~1%. THE RISK IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: the frame number will look weak and only focus can carry this axis over the bar. If the whole axis reads under 2% on focus, suspect the harness before the ladder — check that `settle_steps` arrived as the integer 420 and not the string, and that `still` arrived as a bool — because the ladder is four genuinely different equilibria and is not in doubt. If it is real but faint, the remedy is dna.framing 0.45, which doubles the cloth to 15.8% of frame at the cost of cropping the readout panel.
dna.framing_why: The merged MeshInstance3D AABB is 1.32 x 1.34 x 0.70, radius 1.0035, and it is the SAME box for every value of the axis — the cloth sits comfortably inside it on all three axes, so the camera is genuinely fixed across the tiles rather than approximately so. At framing 1.0 the visible half-extent is radius x PAD = 1.0035 x 1.9 = 1.907 m and the 0.765 x 0.607 m cloth is only 3.2% of frame, under the ~6% floor. 0.65 brings the half-extent to 1.239 m and the cloth to 7.6%. It is chosen over the tighter 0.45 because 1.239 m still exceeds the AABB's circumscribed radius of 1.0035 m, so NOTHING is cropped: the constraint-pass dial and the `passes: N` readout stay in frame, and they are half of this artifact's argument — the readout says in digits what the cloth says in its silhouette.

verlet_workbench.name: Verlet Workbench (constraints that hold themselves)
verlet_workbench.description: A cloth uses current and previous positions plus iterated distance constraints. In the Form Finding comparison, PASSES selects 1/4/8/12 corrections per fixed step; RESET repeats the initial condition and WIND switches the continuous lateral drive. Mean and worst relative spring errors expose different readings of the result. Legacy placements retain their ambient dial.

frozen_glass_vessel.name: Frozen Glass Vessel
frozen_glass_vessel.description: A transparent closed skin formed by top pins, initial radial inflation, gravity and a fixed number of Verlet steps. The frozen mesh is lifted to its floor datum and carries matching two-sided surface collision. Reconstructing replaces the old skin. The sphere topology has no cut mouth or traversable interior.

film_form_relaxation.name: A network settles into a body
film_form_relaxation.description: A 4-by-3-by-4 lattice gains springs and settles through the bench solver, retaining a ghost of the starting shape.
interactions: Look at the screen to play.
Pause, replay, step or turn the view.
film_form_relaxation.qfep_connection: Fixed-seed replay of source initialization; the museum bench normally displays only its settled snapshot.

dna.default: lever=solved, evidence=longhand - solved never enters the new branch at all: dl = arm*wr/total and dr = arm*wl/total are the shipped two lines and lp/rp the shipped two expressions, and no branch adds or removes an _rng draw, so the four placements (FormFinding_Equilibrium, Sky_Climb, Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation, Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text) and the sibling scene calder_object_mobile build the identical tree from the identical draw order. longhand keeps every gram tag and the plaque, and the plaque's second line still reads 'balanced: tau = w*d at every arm' because lever is solved. apply_grid_config no longer rebuilds on every call - only when a value both validates and CHANGED, and only after _ready has built once. Skipping that rebuild is byte-identical rather than merely equivalent, because _rng.seed = hash(seed) makes _build deterministic: the torn-down mobile always came back the same mobile.
dna.was: six exports - seed, use_objects, depth, span, leaf_prob, top_y - and every one a dial on the same sculpture: a different tree, a deeper tree, a longer rod. The one thing nothing could turn was the claim in the @identity, that every arm obeys tau = w*d. The artifact could not be photographed being wrong, and a claim that cannot fail is not visibly true either.
dna.note: lever is WHETHER THE LAW BINDS, not which law. solved is Calder's arithmetic, pivot placed so w_l*d_l = w_r*d_r and every rod dead level. halved cuts each rod in the middle - symmetry mistaken for balance, the mistake anyone makes who has not done the sum. inverted applies the law with the ratio reversed, the heavier child on the LONGER arm. The residual moment is not styled: the rod is hung by it, at asin(residual / (arm*W)), and the ladder falls out of the algebra rather than being chosen - halved leaves arm*(wr-wl)/2 and inverted leaves arm*(wr-wl), so the sign error leaves exactly twice the residual of the naive cut, in the same direction; sin(theta) doubles exactly and the angle a little more than doubles, since asin is convex. ONE HONEST PROXY, stated plainly so nobody mistakes it for physics: a rod whose loads hang on free wires carries cos(theta) in every moment term, so its only equilibrium is vertical with the heavy end straight down, and the true free-swing answer would fold the sculpture into a tangle at every non-default value. What is drawn is the residual normalised by the largest moment the arm could carry - zero exactly when the law is obeyed, which is why solved is untouched.
dna.kin: evidence is the family word taken character for character from the 34 siblings, THREE VALUES not four. There is no axiom tier because the plaque already IS the symbolic assertion - tau = w*d is printed on it at longhand - so a fourth value would be the third one minus its numbers, which is trace read backwards. The default is longhand rather than the motion demos' result, for weather_vector_field's stated reason: this artifact was born with its whole working on the table, a gram tag under every disc and a total on the plaque. NOT named `law`, although force_field_visualizer declares an axis by that word: over there the four values are four different force laws falling off differently, here there is one law and the question is whether it is solved, ignored or inverted. NOT `balance` either - that names the state, and lever names the mechanism that produces it.
dna.still_note: lever is the silhouette axis and should bite hard: every rod above the leaves rotates, so each disc moves in x AND y and the whole tree goes lopsided; inverted should measure at AT LEAST twice halved's displacement, in the same direction, so the two are ORDERED and not merely different - a pair that comes back unordered is a bug in the tilt, not a soft axis. evidence is the thin one: it removes a handful of Label3D gram tags and a four-line plaque from a 3.6 m sculpture, so expect dilution and crop-recheck before believing INERT. One coupling to know about: the plaque's own text changes with lever (balanced -> NOT balanced), so a diff along evidence at a non-default lever is not measuring evidence alone. Judge evidence at lever=solved.
dna.declines: use_objects stays a plain export and is deliberately NOT an axis: the corpus already ships that value as a separate token, calder_object_mobile.tscn, which sets use_objects=true, seed=13, depth=3 and has its own registry entry and its own placement in Sky_Climb. Declaring it here would sweep a family whose second member already has a name. seed, depth, span, leaf_prob and top_y stay dials - a different random tree is a different object, not a different argument.

calder_mobile.name: Calder Mobile (balanced, real weights)
calder_mobile.description: A static tree of painted discs and rods. Nominal disc masses use area, thickness and aluminium density; massless arms place each pivot so left mass times distance equals right mass times distance. Nameplates expose the arithmetic. No dynamic rigid-body balance, rod mass, wire mass or wind response is simulated.
calder_mobile.qfep_connection: The balance is encoded in a chosen mass model and geometry. Inspect what the recursive calculation includes and what it leaves out before treating the hanging image as a physical test.

fractal_truss_tower.name: Fractal Truss Tower (recursive storeys)
fractal_truss_tower.description: A tower recursively divided into shorter braced storeys, with smaller corner members overlapping earlier ones and prescribed sway. This constructs a visual hierarchy; it performs no material, strength or buckling analysis.

tensegrity_triangle.description: Three rendered struts and joints with a prescribed sinusoidal scale pulse. It depicts a triangle but has no member-force, hinge or load solver and no tension cables; the legacy identifier does not make it a tensegrity demonstration.
tensegrity_triangle.name: Tensegrity Triangle
tensegrity_triangle.qfep_connection: A convincing pulse invites the question of what was actually tested. Compare the authored animation with the constraint needed to establish rigidity; the current sculpture poses that experiment rather than performing it.

energy_landscape_bench.name: Energy Landscape Bench (height is energy)
energy_landscape_bench.description: A soft body settling on a wavy energy-landscape surface where height is energy, descending into the nearest basin.

simulated_annealing.description: A Rastrigin search with random neighbouring proposals and temperature-dependent acceptance of uphill changes. Recent acceptance adapts the cooling schedule. Stagnation or HOP invokes a separate unconditional relocation and reheating rule. START T sets a future reset temperature and participates in proposal scaling; it does not directly set the running temperature.
simulated_annealing.name: Simulated Annealing
simulated_annealing.qfep_connection: Changing which moves are admitted can make another basin accessible. The separate hop and cooling policies expose authored escape mechanisms; no run guarantees a global optimum or measures a biological Q quantity.

dna.default: basin=plural, evidence=longhand - plural short-circuits to the shipped problem_type 'rastrigin' WITHOUT WRITING IT: _sync_basin_from_exports only assigns problem_type when basin is something other than its default, so the objective string, the height range, the mesh and the colours are the same objects built by the same code as before. evidence=longhand is the shipped picture branch for branch - trail, both markers, hop marks, the P(accept) histogram and both working label lines - and _apply_evidence deliberately draws nothing itself, so the default does not even move the histogram's first frame. All five placements (Cabinet_Gallery, FormFinding_Annealing, Gallery_Misc, Gallery_Misc_Placed, Placement_Simulated_Annealing) are BARE tokens with no #key:value, and GridInteractablesComponent only calls apply_grid_config when merged_config is non-empty, so none of them reaches the new code at all. The two fixture exports default to 0 and 0, which are 'leave the global RNG alone' and 'run nothing early'.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Twenty-eight exports existed and every one was a temperature, a rate, a count or a dimension; the one categorical knob, problem_type, was a bare String with its four legal values in a trailing COMMENT, reachable only by typing the exact word. apply_grid_config read fourteen keys and then, unconditionally on ANY call, tore the console and the control panel down, re-cut them, threw the search away and started a new one - the force_pad trap, dormant only because no token has ever carried a key.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. basin is gradient_descent_visualization's word and its five values, character for character, and taking it is the point rather than a convenience: annealing and descent are the same picture - a runner on a relief - differing in exactly one thing, that this one is allowed to move UPHILL. That licence is meaningless on a bowl and is the only way out of an egg-crate, so the argument does not exist until the surface is named. A map that asks both tables for the same basin gets one landscape and two policies on it, which is the comparison neither can make alone. TWO OF THE FIVE FORMULAS ARE THE SIBLING'S UNTOUCHED (bowl = x^2+y^2, valley = the same Rosenbrock) and scarp is ported from it below; plural and plateau are served by THIS artifact's own shipped Rastrigin and Ackley instead of the sibling's Himmelblau and tanh disc, because both are textbook members of the class the word names and because swapping them in would have discarded the default this artifact ships with. Where the functions differ the word still means the same thing. evidence is the same four rungs the motion family uses, asked here of a search that is permitted to be wrong on purpose.
dna.scarp_note: THE RISE IS THE FAMILY'S PROPORTION, NOT ITS NUMBER. gradient_descent fixes a 3.0 step against a bowl spanning 2*4^2 = 32 over its domain and renders it with a per-function y_scale; this artifact normalises every relief over its own measured min/max, so a literal 3.0 against a domain-5 bowl spanning 50 would flatten to two thirds of the sibling's contrast and read as `bowl` with a smudge on it. SCARP_RATIO = 3/32 reproduces the ratio at whatever search_space_size is set to. Since the surface is coloured by normalised height, the whole x>0 half of the plate shifts band - this should be the loudest value on the axis, and if it is not, suspect the capture and not the function.
dna.still_note: EVERY RUNG OF BOTH AXES IS STANDING GEOMETRY, but the walk that draws three of evidence's four is not standing yet when the shutter opens. The bench settles 1.1 s, step_interval is 0.06, and _process performs at most ONE step per frame whatever step_interval says - so an unpinned capture photographs about eighteen steps of a thousand: a stub of trail, an almost-empty histogram, no basin hops (stagnation_threshold is 80) and nothing rejected. result / trace / longhand would then differ by a few centimetres of line and the axis would read INERT as a fact about the shutter. prerun_steps runs the search forward synchronously in _ready; anneal_seed pins the whole thing, without which four basin frames differ by the surface AND by four unrelated random walks drawn over it. The temperature schedule itself is NOT an axis and cannot be: cooling is the one thing this artifact does that a still cannot hold.
dna.framing_note: unchecked against a capture in this pass. The axis lives in a 1.4 m plate that is 0.15 m deep in relief, the sweep camera sits at pitch -0.26 rad, and _create_console now stands the whole thing on a 0.90 m deck with a rail ring and a control pad - so a fit-by-diagonal sees a near-edge-on plate inside a much taller box. Deliberately NOT given a dna.framing number here: the identical geometry on gradient_descent_visualization carries the same warning and no number, and inventing one without a frame to check it against would be guessing at two artifacts at once. Check subject % before reading any verdict on either axis.

max_q_basin_room.name: Max-Q Basin Room (the liveliest minimum)
max_q_basin_room.description: A constructed comparison of a static cube in a deep well and a driven soft lattice in a shallow basin. The two bodies receive different rules; depth is not a measured common objective. Form Finding starts with DEEP/SHALLOW labels and reveals the Q proposition on INTERPRET. The installation asks which responsiveness the author values; it does not measure a universal life/death boundary.

impossible_end_table.name: Impossible End Table
impossible_end_table.description: An authored mesh arrangement of separated table parts, drawn cables and an unbothered teacup. No contact, cable-tension or rigid-body balance solver tests the pose. Its visual stillness is a question to investigate, not evidence that the displayed force system balances.

self_shaping_forge.name: Self-Shaping Forge (the thesis made flesh)
self_shaping_forge.description: A staged transformation interpolates raw vertices toward authored target shapes, with a prescribed progress/Q display. Retained as a sculpture about becoming; it does not optimize a measured Q objective or discover its targets through physics.

balance_puzzle.capacity: JUDGE which translations and rotations preserve stability in a stacked structure.
balance_puzzle.description: Stack pieces until the system stops moving. Each drop translates and reorients a block, but the goal is not motion for its own sake: it is finding a configuration whose center of mass and support relations hold long enough to trigger the creature reward. The puzzle turns balance into a lived lesson about which transformations preserve stability and which topple it. It frames transformation as a negotiation with gravity.
interactions: grab and drop pieces into a taller stack
raise the structure past the height threshold
hold the arrangement stable until the timer completes
watch the reward creature emerge from a successful configuration
balance_puzzle.name: Balance Puzzle
balance_puzzle.qfep_connection: Transformation changes S while stability acts as the invariant. The stack only counts as coherent when many local moves preserve a global equilibrium.

gradient_descent_optimizer.name: Gradient Descent Optimizer (the bridge to learning)
gradient_descent_optimizer.description: A point follows a finite-difference downhill update on an authored scalar surface, with a retained trail, energy readout and repeated starts. It distinguishes SMALL SLOPE from a BOUNDARY that prevents a significant feasible step. No neural network, training data or soft-body mechanics are present.

PendulumWave.description: One integrated pendulum leaves a timestamped position record: sample age becomes depth. FINE, COARSE and measured-period STROBE expose physics-tick sampling, a 300-mark budget and a ten-second age limit; RESET restarts this experiment.
PendulumWave.name: PendulumWave

foucault_pendulum.description: A brass pendulum swings from high above, drawing rosette patterns on a cream canvas below. The swing plane slowly precesses—Foucault's elegant proof that Earth rotates beneath us. Dark ink traces accumulate into intricate spirograph-like figures over time.
foucault_pendulum.name: Foucault Pendulum
foucault_pendulum.qfep_connection: The pendulum maintains its F (swing plane) while the frame rotates beneath it. Inertia as F-preservation — the system resists external perturbation, holding its internal model constant against a changing reference frame.

seismograph.description: Seismograph-style traveling-pen chart — draws the driving signal over time onto a scrolling paper strip, reading oscillation as a physical trace.
seismograph.name: seismograph

dna.default: retention=none - NOTHING IN THIS ARTIFACT'S CODE CHANGED. The axis was already exported, already implemented and already reachable; the promotion is the declaration and a fix to the checker that could not see it. _ready calls super._ready(), which reaches _ret_read_config() and _ret_build() at the end of the parent's body, and "none" is the first case of that match and builds no record at all. MEASURED, not assumed: 8 mentions across 7 map files, not the 4 the promotion brief carried, by two reach-paths - bare tokens in WaveFunctions_Pendulum and its three parts, and three curation_station collections (Corridor_Point_One, Corridor_WaveFunctions_Pendulum, Curation_Bay_wavefunctions_3) whose #layout and #with_wall / #with_pillars / #with_barrier flags belong to the station and not to this artifact. None carries a retention key, and the inherited apply_grid_config returns on its first line unless a config actually carries one.
dna.was: refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and that refusal was a fact about a line-oriented parser rather than about the artifact. This file is 92 lines beginning `extends "res://commons/primitives/point/draw_dot.gd"`, and its whole standing genome - the retention export, the RETENTIONS allow-list, the five _ret_* builders, the gated apply_grid_config - is the parent's. GDScript forbids redeclaring an inherited member, so the child cannot restate it and should not: the honest fix was to teach tools/check_dna_declarations.py to follow `extends "res://..."`, which it now does, and which closes the same gap for any artifact whose axis lives one class up.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: draw_dot (the parent script), draw_triangle_faces, grab_sphere_point_snap, interactive_point_origin_force, player_trace, mystic_writing_pad, oscillation_controlled_cube - `retention` with the same five values in the same order and the same default. Here it is inherited rather than copied, so the sibling cannot drift: it is literally the same code.
dna.declined: time_axis_speed, sample_interval and lock_origin_on_ready - this file's own three exports, and all three declined. The first two are a rate and an interval, which one still cannot tell apart; that is the info_board result exactly. The third is invisible by construction. And the live trace itself is declined as a subject: with no player and no grab, the draw sphere never moves, so every sample lands on the same point and the +Z push draws them into a straight 0.2 m line - a degenerate figure that is the same figure at every value. The standing, photographable record in the reference frame is the parent's retention record, which is why that is the axis and the time axis is not.
dna.still_note: the record is built once in _ready inside the 0.5 m reference frame and never moves, so a still is a complete account of it. The child's _process advances the live trail along +Z but touches no part of the record.

draw_dot_time_domain.description: Draw dot with time-domain trace along +Z.
draw_dot_time_domain.name: draw_dot_time_domain
draw_dot_time_domain.qfep_connection: oscillation: a dot that draws its own history — motion smeared into a time-domain trace; the simplest possible oscilloscope.

dna.default: stance=bench + finish=wood - bench rebuilds the same four corner legs and the same four ankle-height beams, and wood keeps base_color at Color(0.6,0.3,0.1) with the original shader parameters verbatim, so all 13 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: No exports at all. The understructure was four corner legs plus a four-beam skirt at ankle height, hard-coded in two literal arrays, and base_color was a private var pinned to dark wood - the artifact's own declared critical_parameter, unreachable from a map. stance lifts what holds the zero plane up, which is what decides the claim the surface makes: bench is furniture that expects weight and hands, pedestal drops the legs for one central column on a foot so the top reads as a plinth and whatever stands on it becomes the subject, trestle swaps them for two end panels and one stretcher - the board that admits it comes apart. finish carries the material argument: wood is the nineteenth-century bench where the experiment is craft, steel the clean room, stone the slab that outlasts the work, glass the surface that refuses to hide what is under it.
dna.note: finish only overrides base_color when it is not the wood default, so set_base_color() stays authoritative on the default path.

lab_table.description: Procedural wooden lab table with legs and support frame. Surface for placing instruments and apparatus. The workbench where oscillation becomes experiment.
lab_table.name: Lab Table
lab_table.qfep_connection: a laboratory table — the bench the experiments stand on; marks the inhabited workspace without asserting content.

GlassRack.description: Modular laboratory glassware system. Configurable spiral condensers, wobbly tubes, flasks, junctions. Use #config:spiral_tube, #config:spiral_condenser, #config:distillation_rack, or #config:simple_tube. Turtle path commands: f,l,r,u,d,spiral,wobbly,flask,junction.
interactions: observe

GlassRack.qfep_connection: oscillation: the glass rack chassis — the eurorack made walkable; modules at body height, patching as architecture.

VRAudioMonitor.name: VR Audio Monitor
VRAudioMonitor.qfep_connection: the monitor — level meters for the inhabited mix; it marks what is sounding without asserting content.

WavePaintings.description: Three pendulum-painting stations—grab the bob to swing it, watch oscillation become visible trace. Each pendulum paints on a wet canvas below, translating harmonic motion into color trails. The physics of swinging becomes the brush; chaos becomes art.
WavePaintings.name: Wave Paintings
WavePaintings.qfep_connection: Oscillation as the fundamental pattern of non-rest — perpetual movement between poles. The simplest E(S) that isn't random: structured, predictable, yet never still. Painting makes the wave's F-structure visible as trace.

BigPipeSystem.description: Industrial drain pipe network built from modular segments — straights, corners, T-junctions, crosses, vertical bends. Pipes as frozen flow: the physical infrastructure that channels movement. WFC-adjacent: each segment constrains its neighbors.
BigPipeSystem.name: Big Pipe System
BigPipeSystem.qfep_connection: oscillation: the organ's logic at room scale — pipes whose lengths ARE their pitches; geometry as tuning, the building as instrument.

sine_flow_tray.name: What Will Leave? — Sine Contact Tray

Change peak-to-trough relief or sphere radius between releases; compare outlet crossings, still-in bodies and other exits at a twelve-second deadline. A side console keeps the surface visible. RELIEF changes only height range
SIZE changes sphere radius at fixed mass
RESET restores declared settings
RULE reveals the sampled sine and collision construction
