dna.default: cut=skin - every quad of the 48-column sample grid gets a surface, one row per column, so _update_wall_mesh emits y=0.0 and y=wall_height in the same order with the same vertex colours as the pre-promotion loop. Byte-identical, not merely equivalent: strata and lattice are the only values that subdivide vertically. The six existing placements (Corridor_WaveFunctions_Sine_Space, Curation_Bay_wavefunctions_3, WaveFunctions_Sine_Space and its p1/p2/p3 variants) carry no #cut token and none of them changes.
dna.was: a 1 m display case whose mini-wall was always a closed ribbon - the wave presented as a finished object, with the 48-sample grid that produced it invisible.
dna.shared_with: sine_wall_corridor - same word, same four values, character for character. The corridor answers the question at 24 m with the player inside it; this case answers it at 90 cm with the formula written above. Both decide which cells of a sample grid get a surface and neither touches the displacement function, so they measure alike by construction.

sine_wall_explanation.description: 1m display case showing how sine function shapes corridor walls. Animated mini-corridor demonstrates x = A·sin(f·z)—the wave displacement that creates the sine_wall_corridor effect. Shows amplitude, frequency parameters with live wave propagation.
sine_wall_explanation.name: Sine Wall Explanation

sine_wall_corridor.description: Layered sine displacements shape two walls. The shipped seven-metre scene has animated, noncolliding walls over a supporting floor; AMP, PHASE, FREEZE and RESET compare running and frozen folds and display the local-X gap. Script defaults differ from this configured scene.
sine_wall_corridor.name: Sine Wall Corridor

sine_space.name: Sine Space
sine_space.description: 3D space defined by sine waves — walls, floors, and ceilings undulate according to wave parameters. An environment where the sine function becomes architecture.

dna.default: manifold=cycle, crossing=product - a deliberate no-op on both. cycle is the shipped 5-second carousel through all five topologies and leaves current_topology at FLAT_SINE where its initialiser already put it; product is the sin(f*a+phase)*sin(f*b+phase*k) that every topology function computed inline before _wave() existed. All 5 existing placements undulate exactly as they did.
dna.was: one carousel. The five coordinate systems were a timer, not a choice, so no placement was ever a cylinder — every placement was all five for five seconds each. The product of two sines was the only way the two directions were allowed to meet.
dna.note: Two things a capture has to get right here. The surface is a MultiMeshInstance3D and the four controls are CSG nodes, so nothing in this artifact was a MeshInstance3D and it measured 16.9 x 3.58 x 1.0 — the pillars, with the 10 m field reading as 1 m of depth. _create_capture_anchor() adds an 11 m box at layers = 0 so the measurement is of the space rather than its dials; no camera in the game draws it. And the instances all sit at the origin until the first _process tick positions them, so a shot taken before the settle photographs a dot. Sweep at the default manifold=cycle: the topology timer has not fired at 5 s, so the frame is the plane, which is where `crossing` is legible.

unit_circle_advanced.description: A point progresses around a circle with horizontal and vertical projection rods while a finite sampled graph builds beside it. The default graph reads the sine coordinate; configured alternatives expose other correspondences. Collision boxes do not by themselves establish a verified walking route.
unit_circle_advanced.name: Advanced Unit Circle
unit_circle_advanced.qfep_connection: One angle supplies two coordinate projections. Their graph depends on which coordinate is retained and how angular progression is placed on a new axis; this construction does not imply that every oscillation is physically driven by rotation.

dna.default: correspondence=both - the `_` branch of _wave_value() returns sin(step_angle), which is the literal expression _create_bridge_step() used before, and _apply_correspondence() at "both" sets every rod visible, which is the state they were already created in. No tangent rod is constructed at all unless the value asks for one, so all 5 existing placements build the identical node tree.
dna.was: one reading, unnamed. The scene drew both projection rods and unrolled sin(theta) into a walkable bridge, and no placement could ask the circle for its other shadow, for the tangent that runs off to infinity at a quarter turn, or for the helix the two shadows are shadows OF.
dna.note: The fixture is the whole reason this is measurable. The bridge lays one plank per frame and takes ~16 s to finish, so a still shot at t=1s catches 6% of the figure and the verdict becomes a fact about the shutter; `buildup: complete` builds all 400 planks in _ready. start_angle_deg=50 is there because the shipped angle 0 is degenerate — sin and tan are both zero there, so three of the four values would photograph identically. wave_length is shortened for the bench only: the shipped 28 m bridge against a 2.4 m circle is a wide flat subject and fit-by-diagonal reduces it to a line. Sibling token `unit_circle` runs this same scene and is deliberately NOT promoted here: it is include_in_map_data false and reaches no map.

SimpleOscillatingBridge.description: A walkable surface that breathes—rising and falling in sine wave motion. Cross it to feel oscillation in your body, the ground itself becoming unstable in a predictable rhythm.
SimpleOscillatingBridge.name: Simple Oscillating Bridge

film_circle_projection.name: A turn leaves its coordinates
film_circle_projection.description: Original rotating-point and bridge functions show sine projection, then retain cosine in depth with the source helix option.
interactions: Look at the screen to play.
Pause, replay, step or turn the view.
film_circle_projection.qfep_connection: One 81-sample cycle. Small non-colliding bridge specimens; interpolating between sine and helix is explanatory staging.

film_wave_neighbours.name: A movement reaches its neighbours
film_wave_neighbours.description: A centre pulse reaches neighbouring oscillators; a second lattice with zero coupling receives the same pulse.
interactions: Look at the screen to play.
Pause, replay, step or turn the view.
film_wave_neighbours.qfep_connection: Existing fixed-step oscillator solver; private start-state copies, slowed for inspection.

coupled_oscillator_lattice.description: A 12 by 12 grid of damped oscillators exchanging forces with up to eight neighbours. Optional comparison controls restart the same lattice with coupling on or off, using the existing continuing sine drive or one pulse. Default 2 Hz sine excitation produces a subtle neighbour response; the pulse makes propagation more visible. Fabric variants change representation without changing these forces.
coupled_oscillator_lattice.name: CoupledOscillatorLattice
coupled_oscillator_lattice.qfep_connection: Coupled oscillators demonstrate how local F-interactions propagate into global wave patterns. Each oscillator only knows its neighbors, yet collective modes emerge — local order generating distributed E(S) dynamics.

kusama_sine.description: Yayoi Kusama inspired sine wave patterns
kusama_sine.name: Kusama Sine

wave_propagation_3d.name: 3D Wave Propagation
wave_propagation_3d.qfep_connection: Waves propagating through 3D space — energy spreading from a source, dissipating as it expands. The inverse-square law as entropy increase: concentrated E(S) becoming diffuse, order radiating into the surrounding volume.

dna.default: falloff=exponential, source=center - a no-op on both, and provably so rather than approximately. _attenuation() falls through its match to `exp(-distance * wave_damping)`, the expression that was on that line before, and at a single source at the origin the new summation loop runs exactly one term, so displacement evaluates to `amplitude * sin(phase) * attenuation` and the colour intensity to `sin(phase)` - the two expressions it replaced, not near-copies of them. No node is added at the default, WaveSource is repositioned to (0, y, 0) which is where the .tscn already put it, and WaveRings keeps visible = true. All 7 maps that place this artifact are unchanged and no map carries a #falloff: or #source: token today
dna.was: nine exports, every one of them a rate or a size, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass`. The sweep refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and it was right for a reason worse than the count: three of those nine (frequency, amplitude, wave_speed) are OVERWRITTEN every frame by animate_controls() from the clock, so the .tscn's frequency = 0.9 and amplitude = 1.8 survive for one frame and then the artifact goes back to driving itself. There was nothing on this artifact a photograph could be a photograph of.
dna.note: the caution that shaped this promotion: propagation is time-domain and a still catches one arbitrary phase of a self-driving field. Sweeping frequency or speed would have produced four beautiful frames answering nothing - and worse than nothing here, because animate_controls would have erased the swept value before the shutter opened. So both axes are properties the FROZEN field has. `falloff` is the law energy obeys on the way out, and it is also this entry's oldest unpaid debt: the qfep_connection above has claimed the inverse-square law since the day it was written and the code has always run exp(-d * damping), which is not that law but absorption by a lossy medium. The axis is the difference between those two claims, made walkable. `source` is where the disturbance is born, and it settles the artifact's own truth line - `every point in a wave field is the sum of all waves that have reached it` - which was aspirational, because the arithmetic summed exactly one wave. At `pair` the sum has two terms and the superposition is real; at `line` the source is straight and the rings become plane fronts, the same law in the geometry that makes a swell instead of a ripple.
dna.kin: DELIBERATELY NOT `evidence`, although wave_interference_tank and wave_interference_3d are the obvious neighbours and wave_interference_3d calls the tank's evidence_name() so the twins cannot drift. Their rungs are result | trace | sources | longhand, where `sources` and `longhand` name the two addends being summed - and at this artifact's default there are no two addends, one pulse and one field and nothing added, so two of the four rungs would be unreachable. That is the same refusal wave_equation_solver's neighbour made, and taking a family word with a shortened value list is the exact failure check_dna_declarations exists to catch. NOT `law` either, which is force_field_visualizer's word: its four values are four different FIELDS (gravity, point_charge, dipole, vortex) and these four are four thinning laws of one field, so the answer sheets do not transfer even though both questions start `which law`. `boundary` (wave_equation_solver: fixed | free | absorbing | periodic) is the nearest true relative and asks what happens at the EDGE of the medium; `falloff` asks what happens on the way there. They compose rather than compete.
dna.interaction: the two axes are not independent in the photograph, and that is the interesting part rather than a flaw. At `line` the distance to the source is a coordinate, not a radius, so falloff stripes the floor front-to-back instead of ringing it; at `corner` inverse_square puts every surviving peak in one corner and leaves five sixths of the floor flat. The weakest pair is exponential x lossless at `center`: the shipped damping only takes the far rim down to 0.61, so those two frames differ by about a third of the displacement at the edge and not at all in the middle. The colour is the honest dilution to declare in advance - intensity is driven by sin(phase) alone and NOT by attenuation, so the yellow-and-blue rings are identical at all four falloff values and only the relief moves. Making colour attenuation-aware would have bitten far harder and would have changed the default frame, which is not a trade this pass is allowed to make.
dna.capture_note: this artifact draws its field with a MultiMeshInstance3D and everything else with CSG nodes, so per CLAUDE.md the capture AABB - which counts MeshInstance3D only - can measure a 11.6 m floor as a small box. If a sweep of this token comes back with the subject under a few percent of frame, that is the harness, not the axis. The fix is dna.framing (this subject is wide and flat, so fit-by-diagonal will undershoot), NOT a layers = 0 anchor: artifacts auto-ground base-to-floor from their AABB, so an anchor mesh would move the artifact vertically in all 7 shipped maps.
dna.declined: frequency, amplitude, wave_speed, wave_damping, grid_size, tile_size - dials, and the first three are erased by animate_controls before any shutter. floor_tilt_degrees is declared and never read by anything; it is dead, and lifting a dead export into an axis would have produced four identical frames with a green pipeline behind them.

RackSineBasic.description: Basic sine wave synthesizer rack with frequency, amplitude, and duration controls. Includes waveform display. The purest sound—a single frequency oscillating smoothly. Grab sliders in VR to shape the wave, hear mathematics become music.
RackSineBasic.name: Sine Wave Rack
RackSineBasic.qfep_connection: oscillation: the pure tone rack — one sine, the chapter's atom. Every sound the domain will ever make is this module admitting friends.

harmonic_distance_table.description: Tabletop artifact with 12 chromatic pitch nodes in circle-of-fifths layout. Grab nodes to hear intervals; spatial distance corresponds to harmonic consonance. Activate a node as tonal center to see all others recolor by harmonic function (tonic=green, dominant=blue, subdominant=yellow). Glowing overtone connection lines show shared harmonics between pitches. Cognitive compression: harmonic distance becomes a felt spatial relationship.

dna.fixture_why: NOT an axis: line_scale defaults to 1.0 in code and `x * 1.0` is bit-identical, so no room changes. It exists because of a number. The thickness ramp is remap(shared, 2, 16, 0.001, 0.006), but 16 is the UNISON and no two distinct notes are a unison apart; the largest non-unison entry in SHARED_OVERTONES is the perfect fifth at 5. So every overtone line this table has ever drawn is between 1.00 and 1.36 mm - the bottom fifth of its own range. At arm's length in VR that is four or five pixels and perfectly legible. At the sweep camera's 3.9 m it is a THIRD OF A PIXEL, which is the whole reason circle_of_fifths and chromatic - two values whose only difference IS the web - measured 0.53% apart. The fixture restores the player's-eye legibility to the instrument, the way turing_pattern_generator's warmup restores the chemistry it never let run. The shipped quirk itself is deliberately NOT fixed: rescaling the ramp would change every one of the seven placements, and the promotion rule outranks the measurement.
dna.framing_why: MEASURED, and it was the smaller half of the problem. The subject is a 0.86 m disc lying flat and photographed from 14.9 degrees above the horizon, fitted by its DIAGONAL: the plate alone is about 2.6% of the frame and the twelve nodes and the whole web together are under 1%, which is the entire 2.84% the sweep found. 0.5 is set against the clipping limit rather than by eye. The union box is fitted by its DIAGONAL, radius about 0.64 m once LabelFramer's twelve 0.18 x 0.09 note plates and the helix lift are counted, while the widest thing that has to stay in frame - the plate rim, and a horizontal disc projects to its own radius in screen-x whatever the yaw - is 0.43 m. dist = radius / tan(17 deg) * PAD 1.9 * framing, so the floor is 0.43 / (0.64 * 1.9) = 0.35 and 0.5 keeps about 40% headroom while multiplying every measured area by 4. Ratios like this are scale-invariant, which is why the estimate is usable without a boot: if the true box is bigger than the arithmetic says, dist and the screen extents grow together.
dna.default: pitch_space=circle_of_fifths, consonance_theory=western, line_scale=1.0 - a no-op on all three. _pos_circle_of_fifths is the shipped expression character for character (angle = -PI/2 + i/12*TAU, Vector3(cos*circle_radius, 0.02, sin*circle_radius)) and _shared_for short-circuits to this file's own SHARED_OVERTONES before it ever touches a theory table, so the twelve nodes land on the same twelve coordinates and the same 36 lines are drawn at the same thickness. dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04. The file's own QFEP audit says the circle of fifths 'is specific to Western tonal theory' and that 12-TET 'approximates but doesn't match' the ideal ratios - two admissions written as comments while the ordering and the table stayed law. pitch_space turns the first into a knob: the same twelve notes and the same twelve relations, re-mapped. Under chromatic the notes occupy the identical ring and only the LINES move, which is the cleanest statement of the axis - proximity is a claim, not a fact about the notes. tonnetz is the honest two-dimensional rival (4 columns of fifths x 3 rows of major thirds covers all twelve pitch classes exactly once, verified); keyboard is the layout the hand actually knows; helix is Shepard's, where B is eleven semitones above C rather than one below it. consonance_theory is chord_tension_spring's word, its four values and its four tables, PRELOADED from that file rather than copied - this artifact's @identity already names it as the contrast piece, and a shared vocabulary with two private copies of the numbers is two vocabularies waiting to happen. Because a line here joins two pitch CLASSES, each interval is scored by whichever of (interval, 12-interval) the theory rates higher, which is what keeps the blues claim about the dominant seventh alive in a graph that cannot tell a minor seventh from a major second. Under flat every pair scores alike and the web becomes the complete graph on twelve nodes at one uniform weight: no interval privileged, which is exactly what that theory says.
dna.deepened: 2026-08-05, and the diagnosis is arithmetic rather than taste. The sweep's weakest pair was circle_of_fifths vs chromatic at 0.53%, and it SHOULD be weak: those two layouts are the same twelve points, because multiplication by 7 is a bijection mod 12, so the node picture is byte-identical and the entire difference is the line web. The web then turns out to render at a third of a pixel (see fixture_why), and the plate - which never moves - is 2.6% of the 2.84% subject. Three moves, none of which touches a shipped look. (1) dna.framing 0.5, set against a computed clipping limit of 0.35, which multiplies every measured area by 4. (2) dna.fixture line_scale 3.0, so the instrument sees the web the player already sees. (3) A SIXTH pitch_space, `consonance`: angle by chroma, radius by harmonic distance, read through the same _shared_for the lines use so the layout cannot contradict the web. That third one is the deepening proper, because it is the only value where consonance_theory MOVES THE NODES instead of thinning sub-pixel lines - under `ratio` the fifth sits at 0.125 of the radius and the semitone at 0.81; under `blues` the flat seventh and the blue third come inside 0.19 while the semitone stays at 0.875; under `flat` all twelve including C land on one ring, which is that theory's claim drawn. Under the default `western` the shells are shallow (0.8125 / 0.875 / 0.9375 plus C at the centre) and that is worth reading rather than fixing: SHARED_OVERTONES counts harmonics 1..16 and its largest non-unison entry is the fifth at 5, so a table calibrated on unisons cannot spread the intervals that actually occur. NOT MEASURED YET: consonance_theory has never been swept at all. build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 keeps the first axis that fits and drops the rest, so five pitch spaces exhausted the budget and the second axis was silently skipped - it needs --max=24 for the 6 x 4 grid. rack_room.description: ONE EQUIPMENT RACK AT WALK-UP SCALE, and five conditions of what it admits exists behind its own controls. 1.12 m wide, 1.60 m tall, on a 1.30 x 0.74 m floor tile: sixteen bay positions on a real rack grid (two columns of 19-inch panel width, eight rows of 4U), five of which carry bare controls - a master knob pair, a screen with two knobs, an 18-way patch field, a four-fader bank with a meter, a six-knob row. The controls are identical at every value of the axis. none leaves nothing behind them. plate puts one dark panel across both columns with a lip and a lit foot strip. vacancy adds a blanking cover over every position no control occupies, merged along each row, screwed down in lighter metal - and leaves ONE BAY OPEN: a 0.44 x 0.15 m hole with 0.47 m of cavity behind it, punched rails, a connector, and four empty screw holes in the jamb where its cover went. frame strips the panel to four uprights, eight cross members and four punched rack strips with the room visible through the middle. works strips it to boards on standoffs, component blocks, a wiring spine, a transformer and a heatsink. THERE IS NO AUDIO IN THIS ARTIFACT AT ANY VALUE - no player, no generator, no bus, no sound_type, no synthesis - and no interaction: it is BoxMesh and StandardMaterial3D throughout. It is a room about the RACK.

at vacancy, look into the open bay and find the four empty screw holes beside it
compare frame and works: one shows you how much space the machine occupies, the other shows you what is in it and loses the boundary

Synthesised from the nine registry tokens that declare a `machinery` axis, all of which were read - code, registry entry and doc block.

dna.default:
machinery=vacancy. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so nothing is being preserved and the default is a free design choice; doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md's rule that outranks everything is about promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest, and `none` - which all nine family members ship as their default, because for them it is the legacy lineage that must not move - is exactly the emptiest.

WHY VACANCY. It is the only value on this axis that can state an ABSENCE. Ordered by how much of the machine you are shown, the five run none - plate - vacancy - frame - works, and vacancy is a middling third. Ordered by what the rack can tell you about what is NOT in it, only vacancy says anything: `works` shows you the most machine and has no vocabulary at all for a part that was never fitted, because a circuit does not have positions; `frame` shows you empty SPACE, which is not the same as an empty PLACE; `plate` and `none` show you nothing about capacity in either direction. Ten covered positions and one open one are eleven statements about a module that is not there, and they are the only such statements the axis can make. A visitor who meets only the default therefore meets the axis's whole argument; a visitor who meets `none` meets a handful of knobs floating over a floor tile and no question.

THE OBJECTION, ANSWERED. At `vacancy` the rack is mostly shut, so a default tile shows less machine than three of the other four values. That is the point rather than a cost: the thing being shown is the FORMAT, and a format is most visible when it is empty.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched; not one line of the nine members' code or registry entries was edited by this pass. This is the cross-member argument those nine leave implicit, built as a body.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE ROOM MAKES, and no member can make it, because it needs a bay you can see into.

Every one of the nine is a bench rack about 0.95 x 0.63 m whose machinery is drawn on a 0.08 m cell grid. On that grid a blanking cover is a 74 mm plate and an unoccupied cell is 80 mm across with nothing behind it, so `vacancy` can only ever mean CLOSED: the family's own builder covers every free cell, and that is the correct choice at that size, because there is nothing to look into. Put the same five words on a 19-inch panel with 0.47 m of depth behind it and the third value acquires a second half it never had: an uncovered position is a cavity with rails down it, a connector at the back and four empty screw holes in the jamb. That is what this room is for, and it is the ONE departure from the family's builder - the covers are all still there, ten of them over eleven free positions, and the eleventh is open.

SO THE ROW TURNS. Ordered by how much of the machine is visible: none - plate - vacancy - frame - works. Ordered by what the rack can say about what is missing: everything ties at nothing except vacancy. Those two orders disagree at the top, and that disagreement is the whole reason `vacancy` is worth building rather than being read as a decorated `plate`.

WHAT EACH VALUE LETS YOU KNOW ABOUT THE MACHINE'S EXTENT, which is the reading the bench cannot stage: `none` - there is no extent, the machine is the parameters. `plate` - you learn its FRONT and nothing else; the depth behind it is unknown and that is the value's entire content. `vacancy` - you learn its CAPACITY, and it is the only value that says a NUMBER: sixteen positions, five used. `frame` - you learn its VOLUME, because the uprights bound a box and the room shows through it, so you can see how much of the machine is empty space. `works` - you learn its CONTENTS and lose the boundary: with no panel there is no edge, and where the machine stops becomes a question about where the wires go.

THOSE NUMBERS ARE EXECUTABLE. `vacancy` is defended above as the only value that says a NUMBER, and the whole argument rests on sixteen positions, five used, ten covered and one open - so _census_check() counts them at _ready from the same tables that draw the geometry (MODULES, _cover_runs(), OPEN_COL/OPEN_ROW) and push_errors if they do not sum to COLS x ROWS, or if the open bay is also a module position. A count typed into a note cannot fail; this can. sorting_hall counted cells whose value changed as a proxy for work and thereby stated that merge sort is free on sorted input.

AND ONE THING THE PICTURE SAYS THAT THE DESIGN DID NOT INTEND. At `vacancy` the covered positions are the most finished-looking thing in the rack: clean sheet metal, screwed down, straight edges. The occupied positions are bare controls on a dark panel, because the modules deliberately have no faceplates. What this rack has done best is the part of it that does nothing.
dna.kin:
THE WORD AND ITS FIVE VALUES ARE READ OUT OF THE FAMILY, NOT RETYPED. rack_room.gd opens with `const MACHINERY_SOURCE := preload("res://addons/element_editor/element_layout_node.gd")` and validates against MACHINERY_SOURCE.MACHINERIES at _ready. That file is the owner on every count: it AUTHORED the axis (a 40-line doc block at line 51 is where the five words are defined), it serves SEVEN of the nine tokens from one script, and it preloads nothing, so pulling it in costs no dependency chain - its five load() calls are all runtime. It is git-tracked; checked with `git ls-files`, because a promotion has previously landed inside a gitignored addon. The element_editor plugin is not in project.godot's enabled list, which is irrelevant: class_name registration comes from the project-wide script scan and the seven rack scenes reference the script by path.

GDScript will not build an @export_enum hint from a constant, so the literal list is duplicated exactly once as HINT_VALUES and _assert_vocabulary() push_errors if it ever differs from MACHINERY_SOURCE.MACHINERIES, and again if the standing value is not in that list. _read_metadata_overrides() keeps the standing value on an unrecognised word and push_errors LOUDLY if nothing legal was standing - the science_screen path, where the sweep sets a property the code cannot reach and the whole loop turns into an experiment about a typo.

THE MACHINERY COLOURS ARE THE FAMILY'S BUT ARE A TRANSCRIPTION, said out loud with the lines they came from (element_layout_node.gd 1446-1447, 1454, 1464-1465, 1496-1497, 1519-1522). Unlike warning_yard, which preloads path_block's named WARN_* constants, this family writes its palette as inline Color() literals inside the four builders, so there is nothing to read. Three of its numeric constants ARE reused unchanged and survive the jump from a 0.08 m grid to a 0.483 m panel without scaling, because all three are real rack dimensions rather than bench-relative ones: MACH_PLATE 0.016 m of panel, an 8 mm lip 4 mm behind it, MACH_COVER 0.010 m of proud blanking cover.

ONE GEOMETRY CHANGE FROM THE FAMILY, FOR THE operations_gallery REASON. The family's lip is a full-size box behind the panel that shows only as a rim. At this scale it also stands behind the open bay, and the cavity then photographs as the back of the lip - measured in the Python model, where 4,897 px of the frame came back as lip rather than cavity, before it was fixed. It is now four rails: same colour, same 8 mm, same 4 mm gap, nothing opaque behind the opening. A frame is four rails, not a slab.
declines: THE HERO MOVE - stand all five conditions at once in one frame and vary something else. Refused twice over. First, the family's case is MIXED and this is derived from its code, not its prose: element_layout_node.gd's `match machinery` at line 1428 calls _machinery_plate THEN _machinery_vacancy for "vacancy", and calls neither for "frame" or "works". So plate NESTS inside vacancy while plate, frame and works sit SIDE BY SIDE - one nested pair inside a set of parallel readings, which is operations_gallery's third case. There is no top value for an all-at-once frame to collapse to, and standing plate and vacancy together would just be vacancy. Second, a synthesis whose axis nobody else declares is a new artifact with a borrowed name; the whole point of reusing a family vocabulary is that the nine can be measured against it.

ANY AUDIO AT ALL - a player, a generator, a bus, a sound_type, a spectrum. Refused on the one-still rule, which is the family's own position and not an imposition: eight of the nine members ARE working synthesisers and their axis is deliberately not about sound, and timbre_sculptor's registry entry says in as many words that the sound is invisible to a still and no axis there pretends otherwise. This room is about the RACK. Adding a voice would add a thing the evidence cannot see, and would make a diorama claim to be an instrument.

MODULE FACEPLATES. Every installed module in a real rack has one, and every one of them was left off. A faceplate is a plate; five of them would put `plate` inside `none` and the first step of the axis would then be measuring a panel that was already there. The cost is that the occupied positions read as bare controls on a dark panel - which is exactly what the family's `none` looks like, and is where the note's last paragraph comes from.

COVERING EVERY FREE POSITION, which is literally what _machinery_vacancy does. Declined for one bay left open, on the record: at 0.08 m per cell a cover is the entire statement because there is nothing to see into, and at 0.4426 x 0.1538 m with 0.47 m behind it, keeping every position shut would have photographed `vacancy` as `plate` with lines ruled on it. The ten covers stay, so the family's reading is fully present and comparable; the hole is the part the bench could not hold.

REPAINTING THE LIP TO MAKE IT VISIBLE. Measured, not assumed: the family's lip colour Color(0.075, 0.078, 0.092) renders at luminance 16.7 on the sweep's default rig, and that rig's background renders at 16.8. The rim the `plate` value describes is invisible on this bench. It was kept anyway - it is the family's colour, it reads under a map's lighting, and a measured fact about the family's palette is worth more than the pixels a repaint would buy. Its SHAPE was changed, for occlusion, which is a different question.

AN OmniLight3D, A SECOND EMISSIVE STRIP, OR ANY OTHER CHEAP CONTRAST. A broad even brightening is exactly the change the critic's own subject_fraction note flags as suspect (frame and focus coming out equal is the tell that a difference is uniform), and a value whose evidence is that it lit the room is measuring the light. There is one emissive surface on the machinery, the family's own lit foot strip, and it is on `plate` and `vacancy` only because it is on the family's `plate` only.

WIDENING THE FOUR SUB-GAUGE DETAILS. The cover's 10 mm proud step is 3.04 px, the punched holes in the rack strips 4.26, the works standoffs 4.26 and the heatsink fins 2.19, all under the 5 px floor. Each is a real dimension, each is texture on a mark that is itself 35-52 px, and no part of the axis is measured on any of them - so they are named here and in _gauge_check's docstring rather than fattened. field_room's ruling: if a thing is thin because the thing it describes is thin, say so with numbers and leave it.

ANY MOTION - a fan, a blinking meter, a sliding fader, a rebuild on a timer. There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween and no physics in the file, so a capture's settle cannot photograph this artifact half way through anything.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, AND NOT BY HAND. The whole box list below was rebuilt in Python, projected through the sweep's own camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, exact per-pixel ray-plane depth so nothing is occluded by a painter's algorithm), shaded with capture_config_sweep.gd's frozen default rig (background 0.055/0.055/0.070, AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR 0.62/0.65/0.72 at 0.55, key 1.25 at (-42,-35,0), fill 0.45 at (-20,130,0), Godot's FILMIC curve, sRGB out, PIL luminance), and then run through artifact_dna_critic.py's exact metric - crop to the union subject box, resize to 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5% of |dL|.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS plate <-> vacancy, AT 11.77% FOCUS (2.89% frame).

WHY IT IS KNOWN IN ADVANCE: the family's code says so. `vacancy` calls _machinery_plate and then adds covers, so plate and vacancy differ by exactly the covers, their screws and the one opening, while every other pair differs by a whole body. A nested pair is the minimum by construction, not by luck.

THE ARITHMETIC. dna.framing 0.58 on the union box (radius 1.09605) puts the camera 3.9507 m out, where the visible frame is 2.41569 m across at 314.61 px/m - a square frame of 5.8356 m2. Six cover runs over ten positions present 0.85247 m2 of panel face; at this standpoint a front face keeps cos(0.62) x cos(0.26) = 0.78652, so 0.67049 m2 of screen = 11.49% of the frame, changing from shell luminance 33.7 to cover luminance 57.1, a step of 23.4 grey levels. Add 28 screws at 0.29% of frame and a step of 57.8, the open bay's cavity at 0.71% and a step of about 28, and the two inner rails at 0.06%. Total 80,475 changed pixels of the 577,600 in the tile = 13.93%, mean |dL| over them 24.3. Because the changed area is far above the hottest-5% cut, focus is set by the top of that distribution - the screws, the cavity edges and the cover-to-panel steps - and lands at 11.77%.

THE FALSIFIABLE PART IS THE GAP, NOT THE NUMBER. Runner-up is none <-> plate at 15.87%, only 1.35x larger, and that is far tighter than warning_yard's 2.0x. If the sweep returns none <-> plate as the smallest pair instead, the cause is named in advance and it is SHADOWS: this model has none, and a blanking cover standing 10 mm proud of the panel casts a hard line under all six of its runs in the real render, which adds contrast to plate <-> vacancy and to nothing else. So the model is biased LOW on exactly the pair it is calling closest, and the honest reading of a flip is 'the prediction was right about the mechanism and wrong about which of two effects wins'.

EVERY PAIR, PREDICTED (focus): plate-vacancy 11.77, none-plate 15.87, none-frame 20.21, frame-works 22.02, none-vacancy 23.03, plate-frame 24.08, vacancy-frame 24.38, none-works 24.69, plate-works 27.87, vacancy-works 28.09. MEAN 22.20% -> PREDICTED VERDICT: BITES. No pair is anywhere near the 6% twin bar, and none is predicted identical: the five bodies are geometrically disjoint apart from the one nesting.

KNOWN BIASES OF THE MODEL, so a disagreement can be attributed. It has no shadows, no specular, no ambient occlusion and flat per-face Lambert, and it draws the round controls as boxes - the last of which cannot affect any pair, because the controls are constant and cancel in every diff. All three of the missing terms ADD local contrast, so the real focus numbers should run HIGHER than these across the board; the ORDER is the claim.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL FIVE VALUES, and the union is set by CONSTANT geometry in two of its three axes, which is the point. Union 1.30 x 1.6024 x 0.74: X and Z are the floor tile, which is present at every value, and Y is the rack head, which is present at plate, vacancy, frame and works and exceeded by nothing. The three inequalities that make it true - EXT_W 1.1212 < TILE_W 1.30, frontmost control face 0.330 < TILE_D/2 = 0.37, rearmost body -0.280 > -0.37 - are written into _solve()'s comment. So no value of the axis can move the camera even in principle, which is the trap dna_specimen fell into from the other side.

THE ARITHMETIC. Diagonal sqrt(1.69 + 2.5677 + 0.5476) = 2.19210, radius 1.09605. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 6.8115 m and show a 4.16 m frame - PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding radius, and a 1.6 m object in a 4.16 m frame is 38% of it.

AT 0.58 the camera comes to 3.9507 m and the frame to 2.41569 m, i.e. 314.61 px per metre on a 760 px tile. Projecting the eight corners of the union box through the actual perspective camera, the object spans 65.0% of frame width and 79.6% of frame height, with its worst corner at 0.89 of the half-frame - an 11% margin, which is the reason 0.58 was chosen over 0.55 (94% of the half-frame, a 6% margin, and one bad assumption from a crop). Predicted subject share runs 8.2% at `none` to 23.9% at `plate`; the max across values is what artifact_dna_critic.py uses, so the blank-render check sees 23.9% against its 0.2% bar. `none` is SUPPOSED to be the sparse one - it is the value that says there is no machine.

GAUGE AT 314.61 px/m, AND IT IS EXECUTABLE. _gauge_check() runs at _ready off _g["px_per_m"] - the same single copy of the arithmetic every builder reads, computed from TILE_W, rack_y1, TILE_D, PAD and DNA_FRAMING rather than quoted - and push_warnings any mark under 5.0 px. Seventeen marks are checked, classified by which way the read dimension runs: "s" standing x cos(14.90) = 0.9664, "w" across x sin(0.62) = 0.5810 (the worse of the two horizontal runs, never credited with the yaw's diagonal widening), "d" into the view x sin(14.90) = 0.2571. They run 5.49 to 80.9 px: works side post 5.49, cover screw 6.08, works spine 6.58, rack strip 7.68, works component and works loom 7.90, lit foot strip 9.12, corner upright and lip side rail 9.51, cross member 15.81, lip head rail 22.81, heatsink block 35.10, open bay height 46.76, works board 51.02, transformer 51.69, cover run 52.23, open bay width 80.91. The works side post was 0.020 m and 3.66 px until this check was written and run, and 0.030 m is still an honest rack post.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body, no audio node and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is ungated and builds the floor, all five control clusters and the machinery body standalone, so nothing has to be supplied for a still and the sweep's rescue path (apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire. The fader levels and the component-block positions are fixed tables, not draws. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THE SWEEP SETS THE @export DIRECTLY BEFORE add_child, the grid sets config_machinery metadata, and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary; all three land on the same _read_metadata_overrides. apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY the machinery host and ONLY when the word actually changed and _ready has already built once - the force_pad trap, and a live one here, because curation_station calls apply_grid_config({"emissive": false}) on everything it mounts and that is how all seven promoted racks are placed today.

MEASURE UNSTAGED. This is a 1.6 m floor-standing object with its own floor tile; a --staged run would put a plinth under a thing that already has ground contact and grow the pair AABB, and the union in X and Z would stop being constant.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE, by construction: the floor tile and 76 meshes of controls - the master knob pair with its two buttons, the screen with two knobs, eighteen jacks, four faders with an eight-segment meter, six knobs. That is 8.2% of the frame that cannot move, and it is what makes the five tiles a comparison rather than five pictures. Anything that changes between tiles is machinery.

STRONGEST PAIRS, predicted: anything against `works`, because works is the only value that puts the frame's brightest large surfaces (standoffs and spine at luminance 84, wiring at 108) in the middle of the picture while removing the panel behind them. vacancy-works at 28.09% is the maximum.

WEAKEST PAIR: plate against vacancy, at a predicted 11.77%, and it is weak for a reason that is a finding rather than a fault. The family's own palette puts a blanking cover (albedo 0.215) on a shell (albedo 0.125): 11.5% of the frame changes, but by only 23 grey levels, because a rack is a dark object with slightly less dark panels bolted to it. THE MOST IMPORTANT VALUE ON THIS AXIS IS ALSO ITS QUIETEST STEP. If that comes back under the critic's 12% WEAK bar it is not evidence that `vacancy` is decoration - the axis is judged on the mean of ten pairs, predicted 22.20% - it is evidence about how little contrast the family gave itself between a panel and the thing you bolt over a hole in it.

AND THE HONEST WARNING ABOUT THE OPEN BAY: it is 0.71% of the frame. The single most important object in this artifact - the empty bay that the whole room was built to photograph - is under one percent of the tile, because a bay is one sixteenth of a rack and a rack seen at 3.95 m is not large. Its two dimensions are 46.76 and 80.91 px, so it is legible; it is just small. Do not read a modest plate-vacancy number as the hole failing to render. Look at the PNG: at `vacancy` there is a black rectangle in the left column, fourth row, with a lit rail down its far side and four dark dots in the jamb beside it.

ElphabaDress.description: Cloth simulation as wave—fabric responds to movement with ripples propagating outward. The dress becomes a visible record of motion, trailing oscillations behind every gesture.
ElphabaDress.name: Elphaba Dress

bernini_columns.description: CPU-generated spiral columns combine a helical centre offset, sinusoidal radius variation and angular phase through height. Their shafts rotate through time while the repeated plan creates intervals and sight lines. Procedural accompaniment is generated separately; this is not a noise-displaced vertex shader or a touch instrument.
bernini_columns.name: Bernini Columns
bernini_columns.qfep_connection: oscillation: the Solomonic columns — Bernini's baroque twist as frozen oscillation; a sine wave carved in marble three centuries before Fourier named it.

vowel_sound_board.description: vowel(formant1, formant2) -> pulse_train filtered through formant resonances
vowel_sound_board.name: vowel_sound_board

dna.fixture_note: The board starts a phrase at t = 1.0 s and the shutter opens at 1.1 s, so without this the mapper's point and the word label are caught 0.1 s into 'Right Here Right Now' - different frames of an animation on top of the axis being measured. Ambient off leaves the board at rest so the tiles differ only by what `chart` draws. Bench only; the shipped default is true and every placement keeps speaking.
dna.default: chart=anchors - `none` is the only value that skips the shipped label loop; every other value runs it unchanged and then adds to it, so `anchors` reaches the end of _spawn_visual_anchors() and stops, node for node the build the 4 placements have always had. No mesh, no material and no extra child is created at the default. apply_grid_config is gated three ways - the key must be present, the word must be in CHARTS, and the value must have CHANGED - and only rebuilds after _ready has drawn once, so a config call naming nothing this board owns cannot tear the chart off a live placement.
dna.was: three exports, all of them audible or temporal: phrase_selection (12 words), is_ambient_enabled, repeat_interval. apply_grid_config existed but only accepted `say` and `repeat`, i.e. more speech. The board's whole visual argument - that a vowel is a POSITION in an F1/F2 plane, which is what its @identity truth says - was one hard-coded loop hanging seven billboarded phoneme labels at their coordinates. The plane itself was never drawn.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The formant plane IS a real diagram and the board did draw its landmarks - the seven ANCHORS labels - but not the space: no figures, no bounding figure, no continuum. The four alternatives are four positions in phonetics, not four decorations: a vowel as a named landmark (anchors), as an unlocated sound (none), as a measurement in Hz (ticks), as a vertex of the canonical published quadrilateral (quadrilateral), or as one conventional stop on a continuum that has none (field). REFUSED, and this is the tempting one: an axis over ANCHORS or the F1/DELTA bounds - a child's vowel space, a soprano's, another language's - which is a live argument about whose mouth is the reference, but retunes the instrument instead of changing it, and would render as the same seven labels a few pixels apart. ALSO REFUSED: everything audible. phrase_selection's twelve words, repeat_interval, pulse_hz, the plosive/fricative/nasal chain. The evidence is one still PNG and this board's real work is a time series of formant transitions; twelve phrases photograph as twelve identical boards.

dual_display_test.description: Visualizes frequency spectrum as a sine wave where amplitude is modulated by spectral content over time
dual_display_test.name: dual_display_test
dual_display_test.qfep_connection: a dual display rig — two panes for before/after comparison; container furniture.

dna.default: chance=none, ensemble=ring - none returns the passed colour and the 0.45 m radius unchanged, and ring is the shipped figure kept verbatim (drone at x=-1.5, ambience at x=+1.5, five effect players on a 2.2 m circle at hue 0.55 + i/n), so all 5 existing placements are bit-for-bit what they were
dna.was: no exports at all. The permanent body — seven glowing orbs, one per audio source — had its hue fixed by a deterministic spectral fan and its radius fixed at 0.45, and its layout hard-coded in setup_visualizers(). apply_grid_config() was 'pass'.
dna.note: the finding is the default. A piece named after the composer who handed his scores to the I Ching surrenders NOTHING visible to chance: the only randomness in the scene is the 20-particle loading halo, which deletes itself the moment generation completes. chance=none is therefore both the shipped value and the diagnosis, and turning the axis is the question 'what would it mean for this machine to actually roll the dice on what you see'. ensemble is orthogonal to it and asks where the sources stand in relation to the body among them: inside an environment (ring), along a score read left to right (line), up a stack of layers (column), collapsed into one object that happens to make every sound (cluster), or overhead and underfoot with no floor (shell).
dna.fixture_note: WITHOUT THIS FIXTURE THE SWEEP MEASURES THE WRONG OBJECT. The loading bar sits at (0, 2, -5) and scatters 20 particles on a radius of 5-8 m, so the merged AABB is ~16 m and the 4.4 m constellation the axes actually move is a speck in frame — and the bar is transient anyway (it fades and queue_frees on completion), so it is in every still and in almost none of the lived minutes. progress_display=none photographs the permanent body. audio_mode=silent skips the generation thread only (players and orbs are still built) because this artifact is in the known headless-hang class — a threaded synthesiser that never yields. chance_seed pins the dice so each value renders ONE constellation rather than a new object per boot.
dna.sibling_note: tech_noir_audio is a second registry token pointing at this same scene (res://algorithms/wavefunctions/technoirgameaudio/john_cage_tech_noir.tscn) with no map_sequences. It inherits the code but not this declaration.

john_cage_tech_noir.description: A prepared vocabulary of synthesized effect clips is scheduled by chance above drone and city-ambience layers. Non-spatial AudioStreamPlayers mix the sounds; luminous forms report activity. It references John Cage without performing a particular score. Chance changes event order inside a finite vocabulary, and repeats remain possible.
john_cage_tech_noir.name: john_cage_tech_noir

dna.default: weave=grid, nesting=single - grid emits the two index pairs in the shipped order from the shipped loop (the loop was moved into _add_indices() and its body copied verbatim into the fallthrough case), and single creates no node at all, so no host, no inner mesh, no change to the scene tree. The 6 map_data.json files that place this token (WaveFunctions_John_Cage and its _p1/_p2/_p3, Corridor_WaveFunctions_John_Cage, Curation_Bay_wavefunctions_5) render exactly as before. The agenda's count of 4 is the sequence's official map list; the working tree carries six.
dna.was: One surface of revolution with a full inspector of exports and apply_grid_config() = pass, so no map token could reach a single knob. Everything that WAS exported is a size or a rate: u_resolution and v_resolution are mesh density, height and max_radius are scale, rotation_speed and the six audio fields are time-domain and invisible to a still. The claim in the artifact's own description - nested surfaces that oscillate between inside and outside - was written down and never built: the code draws exactly one skin, and always the same lattice over it.
dna.notes: weave is WHICH SEGMENTS EXIST between the same vertices, not how many there are; u_resolution and v_resolution stay deliberately un-promoted, because a resolution knob is a density knob and argues nothing. rings drops the meridians (the form reads as stacked contours), meridians drops the loops (a birdcage), diagonal crosses each quad corner to corner, which is the nearest a vertex grid comes to the crocheted loop the wire physically is. Openness rises grid -> diagonal -> rings, which is the half of the claim that matters, because an inner form is only visible through a skin loose enough to see through. radius_curve is untouched at every value: the lobed silhouette is the artifact's declared critical_parameter and the scene ships its own eight-point curve, so the profile is identical across the whole sweep and the axes cannot be confused with a change of shape. A lobe-count axis was considered and dropped for exactly that reason - it would have moved the silhouette, which is the one thing already settled. Inner forms are strictly inside the outer, so the merged AABB and therefore the sweep camera are identical at every value. framing 0.8 because the form is 4 x 10 x 4: fit-by-diagonal (11.5) frames an extent that is never wider than 4. At --max 9 the sweep takes 4 x 3 = 12 and will trim nesting to within_within; --max 12 shows the cross product, which is where the argument lives (nested plus opaque grid hides the inner form; nested plus rings reveals it).

ruth_asawa_sculpture.description: Wire forms inspired by Ruth Asawa's crocheted metal sculptures—nested surfaces that oscillate between inside and outside, solid and void. Topology as frozen wave, material as line drawing in space.
ruth_asawa_sculpture.name: Ruth Asawa Sculpture

resonating_metallophone.description: Strike-triggered synthesized tones: chosen note frequencies set each bar’s visible length. Each bar plays one decaying sine voice; striking it again restarts that voice. The table stand displays their sampled source-audio sum before spatial attenuation.
resonating_metallophone.name: Resonating Metallophone

dna.default: tuning=pentatonic - TUNINGS["pentatonic"] IS the shipped PENTATONIC_SCALE constant, referenced and not retyped, so every bar rings at exactly the frequency it always did and the sound of all 7 placements is unchanged. The APPEARANCE is not preserved, and could not be: see dna.was.
dna.was: eight identical boxes in a row, none of which was ever drawn. resonating_bar.tscn carries a bare MeshInstance3D with no `mesh` property, and ResonatingBar._setup_visual only built a BoxMesh when that node was MISSING - so the branch never fired, mesh stayed null, and the artifact rendered as a Label3D reading HIT THE BARS WITH THE STICK floating over eight invisible colliders. The registry's own measurement agrees: aabb_size [1.74, 0.1, 0.12] centred at (-0.32, 0.5, -0.29) is the grab stick and nothing else. The registry description meanwhile claimed 'each bar's length determines its pitch, shorter bars vibrate faster', which was false twice over - the bars had no length because they had no body, and pitch was a number handed to an audio generator.
dna.note: The mesh is now built whenever it is missing, and each bar gets its OWN BoxShape3D because the .tscn's is a shared sub-resource that would otherwise resize the whole row. Bar length comes from the physics of a free-free bar (f = k*h/L^2, so L goes as 1/sqrt(f)) with the lowest note keeping the shipped 0.30 m. AUDIBLE decay and ring are deliberately NOT an axis - a still cannot show them.
dna.fixture_note: The combined-wave display hangs 2.5 m above the bars and the grab stick is a 1.74 m rod offset to x=-0.5, so the fitted AABB is mostly empty air and the row of bars - the entire subject of this axis - lands at about a sixth of the frame. Dropping the visualizer to bar height lets the framing come in without cropping the row off the bottom. If the sweep still reports faint, suspect the framing before the design: the bars are 0.04 m thin and the sweep camera looks 34 degrees off their long axis.
dna.open: CombinedWaveVisualizer._find_resonating_bars scans get_parent().get_children() for ResonatingBar, but the bars live inside the 'Bars' container it is a sibling of - so it finds zero bars and the combined wave has never summed anything. Invisible to a still, left alone here, recorded so it is not lost. SECOND, from the deepening pass: about half of the frame is the grab stick and the black X/Y/Z debug readout that comes with grab_long_stick.tscn, and neither of them is ever tuned. Every bite number this token reports is diluted by that constant, and a bench-only prop switch would recover roughly a factor of two - not done here because the stick belongs to a shared primitive used well beyond this artifact.
dna.deepened_why: THE COUNT, which the first cut left out. The 2026-08-05 sweep measured pentatonic against just at 0.233% on a subject filling 11.3% of frame - so not a framing fault, a design one. Cause, arithmetic not impression: both are just-ish ratios, so L = 0.30*sqrt(261.63/f) put those two rows within 0.4 mm on bars 1-2 and under 2.3 cm on the rest, eight bars at eight identical x positions differing by under a tenth of their own length. The axis re-cut the bars and never changed the instrument. A tuning is a rule for dividing a range and the first thing that rule fixes is HOW MANY notes there are; five to the octave and twelve to the octave is the entire difference, and it was the one thing every value agreed on. So each value now states its scale over the range the shipped row already spans (C4 to E5) at its own cardinality: pentatonic 8 bars, just 10, equal 17, harmonic 12. No two rows share a bar count, and because x = (i - n/2) * 0.12 the row centres differ too - pentatonic starts at -0.48, just at -0.60, harmonic at -0.72, equal at -1.02 - so no two rows line up bar for bar and the closest pair now differs across its whole width instead of at its tips. EVERY LIST IS A PURE APPEND: not one frequency that was already declared has moved, and pentatonic is not touched at all. Cost: the equal row is 2.00 m wide against the shipped 0.92, so the union AABB grows from about 1.74 m to 2.13 m and every variant is photographed roughly 30% smaller. That is paid for several times over by the change becoming wholesale rather than marginal. framing stays 0.45: at the new union the projected subject is about 86% of the frame width, which is tight but not clipped.
dna.expected: A PREDICTION, so the next sweep can falsify it rather than just re-describe it. Measured off the existing pentatonic frame rather than estimated: the row is 337 px wide for 0.761 projected m, so 442.7 px per projected metre, frame width 1.717 m, fitted union diagonal 2.008 m. The 17-bar equal row takes the union x from 1.74 m to 2.13 m, the diagonal to 2.354 m and the frame to 2.013 m, at which the projected subject is 88% of the frame width - tight, uncropped, and 0.85x linear / 0.72x area on everything. The pentatonic row currently inks 14667 px (2.54% of frame); after the shrink it is about 1.8%, harmonic's twelve shorter bars about 1.65%, and because a 0.12 m centre shift is larger than the 0.08 m bar width NO bar lands on its neighbour's old footprint in any pair. Expect every pair between roughly 2.5% and 5%, closest pair pentatonic-vs-harmonic. IF IT COMES BACK UNDER 1% AGAIN, do not re-cut the scales: check first that the row grew at all, because a bar count that did not change means TUNINGS was not the table the code read.
dna.deepened_declined: A SECOND AXIS, `cut` (length | thickness | shared) - WHICH DIMENSION carries the pitch, since f = k*h/L^2 has a two-dimensional solution set and a gamelan bar is tuned by thinning its underside where a xylophone bar is tuned by shortening it. Real, independent of tuning, visible in a still, and default-preserving. Not taken in this pass: it is a second claim laid on top of one that had just been measured wrong, and the discipline that produced the count fix was fixing the measured thing first. Worth taking next. NOT worth taking, and recorded so nobody tries: a `width` value, because the flexural frequency of a free-free bar is independent of its width - a row tuned by width would be a picture of a law that does not exist.

This case shipped dark walnut and was never white; defaulting it to white_cube would repaint nine placements to prove a point about vocabulary. wunderkammer also carries no band and no plate here, because the shipped case has neither and a default may not grow one. `seal` is a NEW word, not `guard` and not `disclosure`: guard is one ordered ladder of apparatus between visitor and thing (none|label|fixture|frame|hood|cordon) and only two of its six rungs are buildable on a free-standing cube, while cube_lines - literally this case's Frame node - owns `disclosure` for how much of a SOLID is shown. samplevialrack.description: Six sample vials demonstrating phase relationships. Each vial glows with a sine wave offset by TAU/6 from its neighbor, creating a visible wave propagation effect. samplevialrack.name: Sample Vial Rack
samplevialrack.qfep_connection: Six vials, each glowing with a sine offset from the last — phase made visible as light. The purest exhibit of the chapter's subtlest idea: that two identical waves can differ only in *when*, and that this difference — phase — is what lets waves cancel, reinforce, and interfere. Time's signature on a wave, racked and lit.

All 5 existing placements pass neither key, so they render byte-identically.
dna.was: an export block written 2026-08-02 in the rescue batch and never implemented. `becoming` was declared with four documented rungs, four constants (BC_GRAIN_COUNT, BC_GRAIN_R, BC_GOLDEN) and four cache variables - and _ready called only _setup_materials and _setup_helix, so the axis existed as prose. Declaring it as found would have shipped four identical frames and an INERT verdict about a missing function. This pass writes the four rungs the comment describes and adds the axis the helix itself argues.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: queer_morphology_specimen - `becoming` is the same word with the same four values in the same order. Both are jarred bodies asking how far out of the classifying container they have come, so the pair can be compared rather than merely contrasted.
dna.handedness_note: Not a style flip. B-DNA is right-handed, Z-DNA is left-handed, and the same sequence adopts both under different salt and strain - so a specimen jar that can only hold one is making a claim about which DNA counts as DNA. Implemented one node down in doublehelix.gd as a sign on the angle step (additive, default right, every other user of that scene untouched) and pushed through by the specimen's own export.
dna.still_note: every rung is meshes and transforms resolved during _ready - a moved lid, a shorter fluid cylinder, a doubled container, 220 grains on a golden-angle spiral with no randf in them. Nothing depends on the rotation or the emission pulse, so one frame is a complete account.

oscilloscope.name: Oscilloscope
oscilloscope.description: Bench oscilloscope — rectangular dark-steel chassis with a recessed phosphor screen face, a dim emissive 8x6 graticule, an emissive dot trace sampled along the chosen waveform (sine, square, sawtooth, triangle, or composite-Fourier), a row of small control knobs along the screen's lower band, and a single status LED at the top-right corner. In the lab's grammar the oscilloscope is the FOURIER DECOMPOSITION TABLE — the place where a signal becomes its shape. The composite shape draws the truncated square-wave Fourier series (sin(f) + sin(3f)/3 + sin(5f)/5) so the trace IS the decomposition.
