dna.default: turned=series. The chapter (p. 80) presents the four grids together as a graded series with no privileged value, so the default shows all four and privileges none of them. The four single-grid values exist for collations: several placements on one wall, each one work.
dna.framing_why: capture_config_sweep fits by the AABB diagonal: dist = radius / tan(17 deg) * 1.9 * framing. The singles measure 1.34 x 1.752 x 0.42 m (radius 1.123), so framing 1.0 puts the camera 6.98 m out with a 4.27 m frame, which is 178 px per metre and draws a 7 mm stroke at about 1.2 px. The axis lives in 0.35 m grids on a 1.75 m board. At 0.6 the camera comes to 4.19 m, the frame to 2.56 m (297 px per metre, a stroke at about 2 px, a cell at about 10 px), and the board projects to roughly 52% of the frame's width and 70% of its height, so nothing is cropped. The series (1.894 m wide, radius 1.307) gets a 2.98 m frame at the same setting.
dna.note: THE AXIS IS THE COUNT, and it is the only thing that differs between the grids. `series` shows all four; `one`, `five`, `thirty` and `fifty` show a single grid with that many turned cells. All the values share one deal per (seed, draw): the permutation of the hundred indices is drawn once, and grid k turns its first k entries. So the series is ONE deal read at four depths (the cell turned in `one` is among the five turned in `five`, and so on up to `fifty`), and `five` on its own is the series' five-count grid cell for cell. That nesting is what makes the plate's sentence literally true: between neighbouring grids only the count changes. What it forecloses: the four grids are not four independent samples, so a visitor cannot compare four unrelated patterns at four doses. What lives in the dark spot: at fifty the turned and the unturned cells are equal in number, so which diagonal is the 'base' and which the 'intrusion' is undecidable from the picture alone. Only the order of the series says which is which. What the nesting costs the EVIDENCE: the DNA critic should list one/five, and probably thirty/fifty, as TWINS, because those pairs differ by exactly 4 and exactly 20 marks. That is the argument drawn to scale, not a dead value; predicted_degeneracy gives the numbers in both the sweep's units and the critic's.

predicted_degeneracy.metric: changed_pct as cabinet_sweep writes it and score_wave ranks it: pixels whose summed RGB difference exceeds 26, as a share of the whole 760 x 760 frame. NOT the critic's focus; see the arithmetic for both.
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Registered before any capture, as a floor. The four single-grid values share one camera: their AABB is identical (1.34 x 1.752 x 0.42 m) because only the stroke directions and one digit differ, so every single-to-single pair differs only in (a) cells whose diagonal flips and (b) the count's digits in the caption and on the plate. Nested deals make (a) exact: one vs five flips 4 cells, thirty vs fifty 20, five vs thirty 25, one vs thirty 29, five vs fifty 45, one vs fifty 49. One flipped cell is the XOR of a rising and a falling stroke: 2 x (0.0495 m x 0.007 m - 0.007^2 at the crossing) = 0.000595 m^2 of board face. Projection at yaw 0.62 and pitch 0.26: cos 0.62 x cos 0.26 = 0.787. Frame at framing 0.6: 2.559 m square = 6.551 m^2 (760 x 760 px). The text term is small when the digit count is unchanged: '1' and '5' are the same width in the project face, so about 0.0005 m^2 face for the caption digit plus the plate digit. When the digit count changes ('5' against '30') both lines re-centre and about 0.008 m^2 face flips. So one vs five = (4 x 0.000595 + 0.0005) x 0.787 = 0.00227 m^2 = 0.035% of frame, about 200 px. Next: thirty vs fifty = (20 x 0.000595 + 0.0005) x 0.787 = 0.0098 m^2 = 0.15% (about 860 px); five vs thirty 0.28%; one vs thirty 0.30%; five vs fifty 0.42%; one vs fifty 0.45%. Every pair with series moves the camera (1.894 m against 1.34 m wide) and the board itself changes shape, so those are expected in the tens of percent. THE BRIEF EXPECTED THIRTY AGAINST FIFTY, and to a visitor it probably is the closest pair, because both have gone past the count at which the rising lines still read as a field of parallels. That is a gestalt, which is the question this artifact asks and not something a pixel difference can measure: the critic counts flipped cells, and 20 flipped cells is five times 4. So the prediction names one against five (both single grids) and registers thirty against fifty second. IN THE CRITIC'S UNITS, WHICH ARE NOT THESE. Every figure above is changed_pct, a share of the frame. artifact_dna_critic judges FOCUS instead: the mean grey-level change over the hottest 5% of a 160 x 160 resample of the pair's union subject box, set against INERT_FOCUS 3%, TWIN_FOCUS 6% and WEAK_FOCUS 12%. The two must not be read against each other. For a single board that box is about 395 x 535 px, so one resampled pixel covers about 2.5 x 3.3 frame px. A flipped cell (about 41 frame px of changed ink at 297 px/m and 0.787 projection) comes to about 5 resampled-pixel equivalents, and the hottest 5% is 1,280 pixels, 326,400 grey-level-pixels at full contrast. The contrast itself cannot be known before a render, because the critic folds each frame around its own corner colour before it converts to grey, so ink and board pixels that sit at similar distances from the backdrop read alike. Bracketed at 30 to 175 grey levels, a flipped cell carries 150 to 875. One vs five: 4 cells plus a digit, about 0.2 to 1.3% focus. Thirty vs fifty: 20 cells plus a digit, about 1.0 to 5.6%. Five vs thirty: 25 cells plus a re-centred line, 1.8 to 10%. One vs fifty: 49 cells plus a re-centred line, 2.9 to 17%. Every pair against series changes the board's shape and the camera, so expect tens of percent. EXPECTED CRITIC OUTPUT: the axis mean is carried by the four pairs against series and should BITE, while one/five is certain, and thirty/fifty probable, to be listed as TWINS (under 6% focus in grey and per channel). Neither is a false declaration. One/five differs by exactly 4 marks and thirty/fifty by exactly 20, and that difference is the whole argument. THE NESTING COSTS EVIDENCE HERE, knowingly. Because one deal serves all four counts, thirty against fifty flips exactly 20 cells. Four independent deals would flip 30 + 50 - 2 x 15 = 50 cells on average (0.36% changed_pct, 2.9 to 17% focus), which would probably clear the twin bar. Nesting was chosen so that the plate's sentence, only the count changes, is literally true between neighbouring grids. The price is paid in DNA evidence for exactly the pair the brief expected to be closest. Investigate if one vs five comes back BELOW about 0.02% changed_pct or 0.1% focus (strokes aliasing away at 2 px, or the grid dealt identically), or if any single-to-single pair measures 0.00%, which would mean the axis never reached the deal.

composition_stochastique.name: Composition Stochastique
composition_stochastique.description: A free-standing board with four ten-by-ten grids of diagonal strokes on a light ground, after François and Vera Molnar's Composition Stochastique (1959), which the chapter describes as left and right diagonals at 1, 5, 30 and 50 percent, to show chaos intruding on order. On a hundred cells those percentages are exactly 1, 5, 30 and 50 cells, and that is what is drawn: in each grid every cell carries the same rising diagonal except EXACTLY k cells, which carry the falling one. The counts are exact because the cells are dealt, not rolled. A seeded shuffle of the hundred cell indices picks the first k. A chance per cell would only hit those numbers on average: a 30 percent chance per cell turns exactly thirty cells about one time in eleven (8.7%), and a 1 percent chance turns exactly one cell only 37% of the time. So the only thing chance decides here is WHERE. One shuffle serves all four grids, so the turned cells of each grid include those of the grid before it, and between neighbours only the count changes. A caption under each grid gives its count ('30 of 100'), and a plate asks where the grid stops reading as a grid. RESEED deals again: every position moves, every count holds. At the defaults (seed 1959, no presses) the four pictures are the same on every boot.
interactions: walk the row from one to fifty and find the count at which the rising lines stop reading as a field of parallels
press RESEED (poke it in VR, click it on desktop): every turned cell moves, and every count stays exactly 1, 5, 30 and 50
find the one turned cell of the first grid inside the second, the third and the fourth: it is one deal read at four depths
at fifty, try to say which diagonal is the grid and which is the intrusion
composition_stochastique.token_note: `seed` and `cell_size` are in GridInteractablesComponent.CONFIG_PARAM_NAMES, so `#seed:7` and `#cell_size:0.05` arrive as values. `turned` and `solid` are NOT listed: write them as WORDS (`#turned:thirty`, `#solid:off`). `#turned:30` would be read as the tutorial rotation shorthand, the artifact would receive the boolean true (which it refuses, keeping the series with a warning), and the map would gain a silent 30 degree rotation. `#solid:0` has the same trap and turns the collider ON. A seed given as text with a decimal ('1959.0') is read as 1959: the parser does not use String.to_int, which drops the point and would read 19590.
composition_stochastique.map_note: Stands on its own feet and presents to +Z, origin at the base. The grids' centres sit at about 1.49 m, a little under eye height, and the RESEED button at about 1.0 m, right of the plate. Wants a front approach with about two metres of standing room: the grids are made to be read from walking distance, and a visitor has to be able to step up to the button. The series board is 1.89 m wide; a single grid (`#turned:five`) stands on a 1.34 m board, the same height, so a row of singles on one wall reads at one scale.
composition_stochastique.qfep_connection: A chance and a count are different instruments, and the corpus is easy to fool about which one it has. A percentage per cell describes a tendency that never promises any single grid; a dealt count promises every grid and hands chance only the positions. This board keeps the count fixed and asks the visitor to find the threshold at which order stops reading as order, a threshold that is in the person looking and not in the code, which only ever knows 1, 5, 30 and 50. At fifty the picture cannot say which diagonal is the rule and which the exception: 'deviation' is a fact about the order you walked, not about the marks.

measurements.source: computed from the shipped defaults for turned=series: board 1.87 m wide plus a 12 mm edge reveal on each side; feet from y 0 to 0.03, z -0.26 to 0.16; plate 0.60 to 1.095; captions to 1.29; grids 1.32 to 1.67; board top 1.74 plus the reveal. A single grid (turned=one/five/thirty/fifty) measures 1.34 x 1.752 x 0.42.
measurements.measured_at: unmeasured in engine; run tools/sync_footprints.py after the first capture

textile_comparison.name: 10 PRINT / cloth and dressing room
textile_comparison.description: Three draped mesh fabrics read the same 252 stored 16-bit draws as diagonal ribbons, horizontal/vertical stitches or large/small pixels. Choose the marks, palette and repeat count; keep/replay the complete print; fit an A-line, gown or pleated dress and wear it on the active desktop or VR avatar. A walk-in changing alcove contains a live planar mirror. Later design edits leave the worn snapshot alone; TAKE OFF restores the previous outfit. Printed motifs with yarn-scale shading, not a physical weave or cloth simulation.
textile_comparison.qfep_connection: The random record stays fixed while its vocabulary and receiving surface change. A rule worn on a body acquires seams, scale and a different point of view.
interactions: RIBBON / STITCH / PIXEL select the printed marks
SEED + changes the retained draws; PALETTE and REPEAT keep them
KEEP / REPLAY preserve and restore the print
SHAPE previews A-LINE, GOWN or PLEATED; WEAR applies it; TAKE OFF restores the previous outfit

nature_system_demo.description: Visual test scene for the Q-FEP Nature System. Spawns critters from all 4 kingdoms (tree, creature, flower, fungus) in a grid. Keyboard controls: 1-4 spawn by kingdom, R randomize DNA, E evolve, L cycle LOD, H toggle hybrids, SPACE reset grid.
nature_system_demo.name: Nature System Demo
nature_system_demo.qfep_connection: Transmutation as free energy minimization — every critter is an algorithm exploring possibility space under constraints. Bonding with a critter changes the relationship, not the critter. The poison was always medicine. Donna Haraway meets Q-FEP.

dice_throw.description: A physical simulated die on a felt table, with face frequencies and a running mean read from settled orientation. Equal face probabilities and mean 3.5 are comparison hypotheses, not guarantees about a user’s throwing procedure. Rewards default to 16 balls per pip: 96 for a six and 16 for a one.
dice_throw.name: Dice Throw
dice_throw.qfep_connection: Equiprobability — each face equally likely. Fairness as geometric symmetry.

coin_toss.description: The simplest random experiment. Grab coins from a tray and toss them. A counter tracks the heads/tails ratio converging to 0.5 over many flips. Gold side = heads, silver side = tails.
coin_toss.name: Coin Toss
coin_toss.qfep_connection: Bernoulli trial — the atom of probability. p = 0.5 as perfect symmetry.

dna.default: disclosure=works - the shipped code path, so existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: a coin that returned a verdict and showed none of its working — the sequence of outcomes, the running count and the generator behind them all existed and none of them were ever on the table
dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 — the axis was already in the script and the registry had never been told, so the sweep could not reach it

paired_dice_column.name: Two throws, one height
interactions: Throw each die into its own tray
Compare the coloured sum column with the two faces
Inspect the twelve most recent paired results
Return loose dice or clear the record
paired_dice_column.description: Two physical dice, reused from dice_throw, make one coloured unit column after both releases settle. Retains twelve recent pairs and a total count; no generated throws or model histogram. Loose dice recover without contributing a result.
paired_dice_column.qfep_connection: Different ordered pairs can share a total. The column keeps each contribution in colour while its overall height merges them. Equal independent face probabilities remain a hypothesis about the throws.

continuing_die.name: The six that does not finish
continuing_die.description: A grabbable physical die adds each settled face to a labelled column. Six permits another throw; a non-six closes the chain. Five throws is a visible display limit, with unfinished chains marked. Separate worked example: 6+6+3.
continuing_die.qfep_connection: A result is both an amount and permission to continue. Distinguish the rule that permits further growth from the resource limit that interrupts it; retain the difference rather than naming both completion.
interactions: Throw the die into its felt tray
Throw again after a six
Return a fallen die without changing the chain
NEW CHAIN clears the live column

random_object_spawner.description: A spawning algorithm that randomly generates and places objects in the environment
random_object_spawner.name: Random Object Spawner

dna.fixture_note: UNPHOTOGRAPHABLE WITHOUT THIS, by construction. The first cube arrives at next_spawn_time = 1.0 s and the shutter opens at SETTLE = 1.1 s, so every variant of every axis renders the same single cube; and the duplicated grab_cube_wood is a live RigidBody3D, so on a bench with no floor it has fallen six metres by the time it is photographed, out of a frame that was measured at 0.35 s. initial_population = -1 fills to capacity during _ready, freeze_arrivals holds every body (including the hidden template) where the law put it, spawn_seed pins the draws so one value is one arrangement rather than a fresh object per boot. WHAT THE FIXTURE HIDES, stated rather than buried: frozen, `spigot` photographs as ONE cube, because that is literally what the placement law does. In a lived map the coincident arrivals are shoved apart by collision into a heap, so the tile shows the rule and not the pile it settles into. All three flags ship OFF and no placement sees them.
dna.default: dispersal=spigot, capacity=20 - spigot returns spawn_position and takes NO draw at all, so the global RNG stream is consumed exactly as before (the only other draw, next_spawn_time, moved from randf() to _rf(0.0, 1.0), which with spawn_seed=0 is randf_range(0.0, 1.0) = one identical draw off the same stream); capacity=20 is `const MAX_CUBES: int = 20`, kept in the file and used as the export's default so the default is provably the constant it replaced. play_wood_sound is now passed the cube's own position, which under spigot IS spawn_position. apply_grid_config was `pass` and now returns having touched nothing unless a key is present; it never tears down, and a dispersal change is deliberately not retroactive. The 4 placements spawn the same column they always spawned.
dna.was: three exports (cube_size, gutter, spawn_position - two of them dead: total_size is computed and never used), a `const MAX_CUBES` the file's own @identity block named as the critical parameter, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass`, so nothing was reachable from a map token. The registry described it as an algorithm that 'randomly generates and places objects in the environment' and the placement was the one thing never left to chance: every cube in the artifact's life entered at exactly spawn_position. The randomness was all in the clock and the kill.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. dispersal's values are ecology's three textbook dispersion patterns (random / clumped / even) plus `spigot`, which names the shipped degenerate case - a point process with zero variance - honestly. Ecology is this file's own vocabulary already: carrying capacity, metabolism, 'each spawn requires a death'. THE WORD WAS NOT BORROWED FROM random_cubes: its `macrostate` (uniform|corner|layered|spilled) asks which REGION a fixed pile occupies so the ways-it-could-have-been can be counted, and none of its four values can name a single point. Same substrate, different question, so taking the word would have meant taking it without its answers. DECLINED here: the mortality rule (uniform vs oldest-first vs newest-first is a real argument about memorylessness, but a wooden cube carries no visible age, so four rules photograph as one heap), the 0.3-1.3 s interval, and the wood-knock synthesis - a rate and a sound, both invisible to a still.

random_edge_profile.description: A planar surface that generates random edge profiles and patterns
random_edge_profile.name: Random Edge Profile
random_edge_profile.qfep_connection: Chance under clamped boundary conditions: the heights are pure RNG draws, but the profile is forced to start and end at 0.5. Randomness admitted only in the interior; the frame stays negotiated.

Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.description: Applies random rotation on all three axes (X, Y, Z), creating fully randomized orientations for chaotic arrangements.
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.name: Random Rotate XYZ
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.qfep_connection: The room's namesake engine: grid cubes spun by three independent draws, one per axis. Orientation surrendered to chance while position holds — the grid keeping order in one register and losing it in another, which is the whole trick of controlled entropy.

random_decay_multimesh.description: Two MultiMesh stacks accumulate bounded drift, rotation, sinking and darkening at different configured rates. Both use fixed one-metre specimen units by default. Optional stack_fit fits both complete displays to a given width with a common geometry scale, a 0.6m gap and floor-aligned initial faces; controls retain full size. TOGGLE preserves the ramp clock; RESET restarts it.
random_decay_multimesh.name: Random Decay MultiMesh

RotateGridCubes.description: Gradient slope test with animated rotation for walkability check.
RotateGridCubes.name: Slope Gradient Cubes

random_walk_collection.description: Interactive paper that demonstrates random walk algorithms with grab and manipulation capabilities
random_walk_collection.name: Random Walk Grab Paper
random_walk_collection.qfep_connection: Many walks released together: each path senseless alone, the ensemble growing the square-root halo the mathematics promised. The collection is the lesson — randomness has laws, but only in the plural.

random_walk_terrarium.description: Five random walkers in a reflecting glass tank: fixed-length 2D/3D proposals or bounded inverse-square-root LONG STEP proposals. The legacy LEVY_FLIGHT enum remains compatible. A 200-position tail and optional logbook expose the named seed, two clocks and ONE/ALL emphasis.
interactions: observe
random_walk_terrarium.name: Random Walk Terrarium
random_walk_terrarium.qfep_connection: The next step does not consult the stored trail, although position, generator and timing state persist. Reflection, finite history and a catch-up cap change what can be seen and repeated. An entropy interpretation requires a defined measure; the cabinet displays mean squared displacement.

random_walk_leash.description: A glowing orb on a leash that tugs in random directions. Grab it in VR and feel the random walk through your hand. The orb pulses with each impulse. A trail traces the walk path. Stats track drift vs sqrt(N) theoretical scaling.
random_walk_leash.name: Random Walk Leash
random_walk_leash.qfep_connection: Embodied randomness — the walk isn't watched, it's felt. Your arm becomes the accumulator of stochastic impulses.

random_draw_dot.name: Hand + chance
random_draw_dot.description: The original drawing grip with a visible tip accumulating bounded random steps around the moving hand.

random_position_rails.name: Somewhere to start
random_position_rails.description: Paired rail carriages compare fresh positions with accumulated steps. Shared sampled input, advance targets, matched motor timing and a grabbable prediction marker.

dna.default: bias=rise, evidence=result - the shipped build exactly: +Y weighted by upward_bias (3.0) and every other direction 1.0, one randf() per step in the same order, the path cubes and nothing beside them. walk_seed defaults to -1, which draws from the global stream as before, so the 8 existing placements keep rolling a fresh sculpture per launch; the fixture above is for the sweep only.
dna.was: grid_size, num_cubes, cube_spacing and upward_bias were @exports that apply_grid_config ignored (its body was `pass`), so no map token could reach the pull the @identity block names as the critical parameter; the refusals that shape a self-avoiding walk were discarded at build time and only the surviving path was ever shown.

pixel_cloud.description: Builds an upward-biased self-avoiding random walk and places cubes along the path to form a pixel cloud sculpture.
pixel_cloud.name: pixel_cloud

random_walk_128.description: Fine-grained random walk on 128x128 grid using tiny cubes
random_walk_128.name: Random Walk 128x128
random_walk_128.qfep_connection: A walk at 128x128 grain: one wanderer, tiny steps, no memory. The fine grid turns the walk's statistics visible — dense scribble near the origin, thinning frontier — chance accumulating into a shape no single step intended.

dna.default: law=gaussian, evidence=none - gaussian IS the export default of `distribution`, and at that word _ready assigns nothing at all, so anything the scene or a map already set survives; evidence=none constructs no generator and lays down no draws, leaving the histogram empty exactly as it has always been found. All 10 placements are bare or rotation/offset tokens, so none of them can reach either axis.
dna.was: a sampler whose four distributions were reachable only by pressing a VR button or a number key in-session, and whose histogram was always empty at the moment anyone looked - the axis existed in the code and nothing outside the room could turn it
dna.note: the fixture is the whole reason this is measurable: the histogram builds at 50 samples/second, so a still 0.35s after _ready catches an empty chart. evidence=census pre-seeds 1000 deterministic draws (its own generator, seeded by evidence_seed - the live sample_seed and the global stream are untouched) and auto_sample=false stops live unseeded draws polluting the frame. When `evidence` is itself swept the per-variant value overrides the fixture, which is why its list is declared richest-first: a 4x4 cross exceeds the sweep's default --max=9 and the sweeper trims from the END of each list, so an ascending list would have crossed all four laws against an empty chart. Same set, same code, informative under truncation - run --max=16 for the full cross. Deliberately not promoted: samples_per_second and auto_sample as axes (a rate is invisible to a still), and the per-law shape knobs, which tune ONE law rather than choosing between laws.

distribution_sampler.description: Sample uniform, guarded Gaussian, Poisson and exponential laws. The optional cabinet exposes a named seed, pause/batch/rebin controls, issued and landed counts, clipping and binned estimates; pale model counts and a separately scaled orange shape support comparison.
interactions: observe
distribution_sampler.name: Distribution Sampler
distribution_sampler.qfep_connection: A sampling law, an edge clamp and a bin partition retain different aspects of the values. Rebinning can change a displayed centre without changing its population. Frequency and expected shape do not define what a body ought to be; an entropy claim requires its own measure.

GaussianPaintSplatter.description: Generates paint splatter patterns using Gaussian distribution, creating natural clustering around a center point with density falling off like a bell curve.
GaussianPaintSplatter.name: Gaussian Paint Splatter

galton_board.description: Balls drop through a triangular peg array. Each peg deflects left or right with equal probability. After many rows, the bin counts form a binomial distribution converging to a Gaussian bell curve. VR buttons: DROP, AUTO, RESET, SPEED.
galton_board.name: Galton Board
galton_board.qfep_connection: CLT as convergence — many independent binary choices accumulate into Gaussian structure. Order from repetition.

dna.default: comparison=rules, evidence=sample - rules rebuilds the shipped uniform/gaussian/exponential lineup in the same order with the same three colours (the palette is now keyed by law, and at rules that is the old positional blue/green/orange exactly), and evidence=sample is 1000 draws, the number _sample_count was born with. Every one of the 34 map placements is a bare token or a rotation/offset token - no config token in any map_data.json can reach these axes - so all of them render unchanged.
dna.was: three hard-coded columns and a hard-coded 1000 draws, with apply_grid_config() implemented as `pass`. The sign says ONE SOURCE - THREE RULES and the machine could never show the control for that claim: one rule three times, which is what replicas is.
dna.note: fixture pins the draw (evidence_seed defaults to -1 = randomize, the legacy stream); without it two frames of the same variant are two different histograms and the sweep measures the dice. The evidence list is declared richest-first ON PURPOSE: a 4x4 cross exceeds the sweep's default --max=9 and the sweeper trims from the END of each value list, so an ascending list would have crossed all four lineups against an empty chart and a one-draw chart. Same set, same code, informative under truncation - run --max=16 for the full cross. Deliberately not promoted: RESAMPLE and the exponential rate - a button press is time-domain and lambda only slides one column's mass along its own axis.

distribution_comparator.name: Distribution Comparator
distribution_comparator.description: Side-by-side comparison of 3 probability distributions — Uniform (blue), Gaussian (green), Exponential (orange). Three columns of 16 histogram bars generated from the same sample count. Slider scales samples from 100 to 10000; resample button regenerates all three.
distribution_comparator.qfep_connection: Three distributions from one random source — the channeling rule (F) determines shape. Uniform is maximum entropy; Gaussian is the attractor of summation; Exponential is memoryless decay. Same randomness, different constraints, different forms.

dna.default: assay=none is the export default and the `_:` branch of _build_assay, which does not even create the Assay wrapper node, so the bare dish stands on nothing exactly as it did in all 3 rooms. Every rung builds under one Node3D appended AFTER create_petri_dish, so no legacy child index moves and the grid's auto-grounding walk - which types only the root's DIRECT children - cannot see any of it. All 3 placements are bare rotation/offset tokens (Corridor_Random_Mushrooms `bubbles_random`, Random_Mushrooms `bubbles_random:0:-0.5:1.0`, TestMap_Unused_4 `bubbles_random:0:2`) and not one passes a config key. bubble_seed defaults to -1, at which _rf and _rf_range return the global randf and randf_range this artifact has always called - not a private generator that merely behaves like them - so the shipped cloud is drawn from the same stream in the same order and the same count.
dna.was: twenty-eight exported knobs and not one of them a claim: spawn_area_size, four min/max bounds, max_bubble_count, spawn_rate, three lifetime and fade durations, six light numbers, four dish dimensions, eight sound numbers. Every one is a magnitude, a rate or a colour. apply_grid_config existed and its entire body was `pass`, so every key a map could send was silently discarded, and the runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS - which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not their number.
dna.note: assay is the softbody bench family's word and its five values character for character - seventeen artifacts already ask what apparatus a specimen is surrounded by, and petri_dish_worms, the corpus's other petri dish, joined the same word on 2026-08-05. This artifact's own truth line - `Randomness with a ceiling and a floor is still randomness. The dish is the constraint that lets the dispersion be read' - is that question stated from the inside, so a private synonym would have split one question across two vocabularies for no gain. `control` is the rung that argues hardest and argues harder here than for the worms: an empty second dish is the only thing that can turn a cloud of luck from a thing you are watching into an experiment you could disagree with. THE BUBBLES ARE NOT ROUTED THROUGH THE AXIS: every rung spawns the same cloud from the same draws in the same order, because a variant that changed the specimen would be changing the answer rather than the showing. Every apparatus dimension is petri_dish_worms' absolute number divided by its AS_DISH_R of 0.16 and multiplied by this dish's own radius, so the two dishes carry the same apparatus at their own sizes instead of one carrying a scale model of the other - which is what `the siblings measure alike' has to mean when the objects are 22x apart. The one place the rungs diverge is the chart's plotted line: the sibling draws a logistic because a worm population grows, and a bubble dish has no growth curve, so this plate carries a flat-topped histogram between a marked floor and a marked ceiling - the artifact's own thesis as a picture. Fixed, never sampled: a rung that rolled dice would make every capture a different frame.
dna.fixture_note: bubble_seed is a fixture and NOT an axis. This dish costs TEN unseeded draws per bubble (three position, one size, one rise speed, two wobble, two horizontal drift, one light ballot) plus one more consumed by the dead sound gate, and it spawns ten bubbles a second, so at the 1.1 s settle five sweep frames would be five different clouds and the critic would read that noise as a confident BITE on whatever axis happened to be varying. The two drift draws used to be made inside Bubble._init, which an inner class cannot route through the outer node's generator; they moved out to spawn_bubble at exactly the point in the sequence they were made from before - after wobble_speed, before the light ballot - so the -1 stream is unchanged.
dna.declined: constraint = none|gravity|jet|vortex|drag, particle_chaos's word, was considered and REFUSED. Its `none` means a cloud under no law at all, and this cloud already obeys one: buoyant ascent at 0.5-2.0 m/s with a sine wobble and a lateral drift. Adopting the list would mean either calling that shipped behaviour `none', which is not what the word means where it already lives, or forking the list with a sixth value - the folding_past fault, taking a word without its answers. The two artifacts would not have measured alike either: particle_chaos's `none` photographs as an isotropic burst, this one's would be a rising column. Also refused: spawn_rate, bubble_lifetime, bubble_fade_time and bubble_scale_down_rate (a rate and a duration are invisible to a still - the info_board fault), and the distribution behind the draws, which has nothing in frame to be read off. Not refused but not taken: the dish is 6 m of spawn box inside a 7 m round vessel with no collision between them, so bubbles already rise through their own glass at the corners. That is a defect to decide about, not an axis to declare.

bubbles_random.description: A particle system that generates random bubble effects with dynamic spawning
bubbles_random.name: Random Bubbles

mushrooms.description: A procedural arrangement of template copies, noise-filtered candidates, explicit fairy rings and clusters. The optional specimen table exposes SHOW, KIND, SIZE, REGROW and NEW SEED; one seed controls the build and a related seed its ground. Optional edible mushrooms add pickup and a timed perception effect at the bed edges.
mushrooms.name: Mushrooms
mushrooms.qfep_connection: A bounded repertoire permits some differences and requires new construction rules for others. Unit scale preserves template differences; placement permissions differ between routines. This is a material comparison for QFEP inquiry, not a computed entropy or ecological model.
mushrooms.gamwell_reference: Spatial Poisson processes, noise-driven procedural generation, fairy ring mycology, bioluminescent fungi, ecological niche theory
interactions: Under stand:specimen, SHOW follows copies of one template
KIND separates scattered, ring and cluster members from rejected candidates
SIZE removes per-instance scale variation while preserving the seeded draws
REGROW repeats construction; NEW SEED changes the current seed
Under edible:some or many, pick up the edible mushrooms at the bed margins
mushrooms.capacity: Explain which decisions create a population: template choice, transform variation, candidate filtering, explicit rings/clusters and separate interaction capabilities.

silhouette_arrivals.name: Who arrives?
silhouette_arrivals.description: Seeded sampling without replacement fills six authored places. DRESS resamples the wardrobe; FORMS switches branching instructions while retaining its dress seed. Both leave arrival order unchanged; REPLAY restores that order. Flat billboard figures gain different outlines, not locomotion.

seeded_room.name: A plan becomes a room
seeded_room.description: An 8 by 8 seeded plan rises into a walkable room. Replay, change seed, flatten, raise, or compare independent and Perlin samples. The blue passage is an explicit fixed rule.
interactions: Replay or advance the seed at the entrance
Flatten or raise the same plan
Walk the blue passage
Compare independent draws and a coherent field
seeded_room.qfep_connection: The seed changes the available heights while a declared passage mask decides where a body may pass. Chance and access are different decisions.

perlin_noise_bridge.description: Compare seeded uniform heights with FastNoiseLite Perlin samples in two 16×16 grids. Frequency changes the scale of spatial correlation. Both fields use comparable column displays, while their sampling procedures and distributions differ.
perlin_noise_bridge.name: Perlin Noise Bridge

env_one.description: A procedural environment generation algorithm using randomness for kitbashing
env_one.name: Environment One
env_one.qfep_connection: A whole environment kitbashed by draw: parts picked, placed, and joined by chance. The room-scale claim of the chapter — not an object randomized, but a *place* that entropy furnished.

curl_noise_particles.description: Divergence-free curl noise driving 300 particles in smooth swirling ribbons. Cross product of two noise gradients guarantees incompressible flow. Particles color-shift from deep blue (slow) through cyan to white (fast), with trailing flow lines for visualization.
curl_noise_particles.name: Curl Noise Particles

random_transformations_geometric.name: Random Transformations - Geometric
random_transformations_geometric.qfep_connection: Geometry under dice: translate, rotate, scale, each parameter drawn. The form survives as a family resemblance across its own variations — identity loosened, not lost. Entropy applied to shape is variation; applied without bound, dissolution.

sculpt_one.description: An artistic sculpting algorithm that randomly modifies and shapes geometric forms
sculpt_one.name: Sculpt One
sculpt_one.qfep_connection: Sculpting by random modification: a form shaped by accepting the dice's suggestions. The sculptor keeps only the veto — chance proposes every stroke. Authorship as curation of accidents.

dna.default: hand=composition, substance=mixed - the three existing placements are untouched: `composition` runs the same five sculpting moves in the same order create_composition() always ran them, and `substance` returns from _apply_substance() before touching a single material, leaving the curated palette exactly as create_materials() built it.
dna.was: One still-life with no knobs. Five sculpting moves ran unconditionally and the piece was their sum; the palette was eight hand-typed materials. The @identity had asked for a palette dial, a reseed and a gloss-to-fabric slider as [missing] since the file was written.
dna.note: `hand` is maze_generation's word — which procedure makes the form — with this artifact's own moves as its rungs. `substance` is rainbow's word — what the thing is made of — with a rung list this piece can actually be: a still-life of cloth and liquid has no 'light'. Colour is held constant across substance, so the axis is a claim about surface and nothing else. sculpt_seed defaults to 0 = unseeded, which is the shipped behaviour (a fresh composition every launch); the fixture pins it so a sweep photographs ONE object under two axes instead of nine different objects. AXIS ORDER IS DELIBERATE: build_dna_gallery trims the SECOND axis to fit the 9-frame cap, so substance leads with all four rungs and hand contributes composition|pour — 4x2=8 frames covering both — rather than hand taking all five and leaving substance unmeasured.

dna.default: support=floor - the shipped staging to the two numbers: rotation_degrees (-90, 180, 0) at y = floor_height (0.02), the same escape hatch when place_on_floor is false, and the frame and backing panels built off that same transform. The 3 existing placements pass no support key, so apply_grid_config returns on its first line and nothing restages.
dna.was: the canvas was hard-coded flat on the ground. Pollock's break was not a mark but a POSTURE - the canvas came off the easel and went on the studio floor, and the body walked around a thing it could no longer face - and this artifact shipped that decision as an un-turnable boolean. The axis restores the ladder the drip argued against: the floor stood over, the table leaned across, the easel it was supposed to sit at, the wall the finished picture ends up on. The word `support` is the art-historical term for the thing a painting is made on; the value list is NOT the one code_display and catalyst_target use for the same word, because theirs asks what furniture holds an instrument up and this asks which posture the body has to take.

pollock_painting_in_3d.description: Automatic Pollock-inspired painting on a 2D canvas in 3D: sampled marks, a moving stroke cursor, and floor/table/easel/wall supports.
pollock_painting_in_3d.name: Pollock Painting in 3D

monte_carlo_dartboard.description: Uniform generated points estimate an inscribed circle’s area fraction; four times inside/total estimates pi. THROW, AUTO and RESET expose finite sampling, whose estimate need not improve with every point.
monte_carlo_dartboard.name: Monte Carlo Dart Board
monte_carlo_dartboard.qfep_connection: Computation through accumulation — random sampling converges to mathematical truth.

pipe_dream.description: A bounded 3D pipe grows through six axis directions, preferring some straight runs and rejecting immediate reversal. The default path retains up to 180 segments; earlier paths can be crossed.
pipe_dream.name: Pipe Dream
pipe_dream.qfep_connection: The Windows Pipes screensaver reborn: a pipe growing by random turns, filling the volume with plumbing nobody designed. Idle-machine art — the desktop's oldest proof that a few dice and a growth rule can furnish a world.

dna.fixture_why: BOTH ENTRIES ARE MANDATORY and neither is an axis. walk_seed: the run is nothing but accumulated draws from an rng that _ready calls randomize() on, so five unseeded frames are five different pipes and any bite number would be measuring the generator rather than the rung — the generative-artifact trap in CLAUDE.md. -1 is the default and keeps randomize(), so no placement sees the pin. growth: the shipped walk lays one length every 0.08 s, i.e. 14.4 s for the full 180. The sweep settles 1.1 s (about thirteen lengths) and its fixed-camera AABB pre-pass settles 0.35 s (about four), which is why this artifact's measured aabb_size in this very file is [0.24, 0.24, 0.95] — the size of ONE segment. Without the pin the sheet would compare five pictures of a stub and the camera would be framed for a stub. `instant` lays the whole run inside _ready; `live` is the default and is the shipped screensaver. It is a String enum and not a bool because the sweep sets exports from JSON before _ready and a typed bool silently rejects a fixture string.
dna.default: residue=path - the shipped drawing, in the shipped order. At `path` the rung is 2, _create_next_segment calls exactly the two functions it always called (_add_segment then _add_joint), and none of _mark_head, _trim_tail, _refresh_rails or _build_ghosts is reached; the only work this promotion adds on that path is one append to a PackedVector3Array and one dictionary lookup per length. The turn rule was refactored to take its generator and position as arguments so the ensemble's counterfactuals can call the same function, and the draw order is unchanged: one randf() for the straight-ahead check, then one randi_range per shuffle swap, exactly as before. _add_segment now derives its basis from the span end-start rather than from the `direction` member, which is the identical vector at that point by construction. MEASURED, not assumed: 6 mentions across 5 map files - bare tokens in Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness, Room_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness and Random_Rotate_Random_Y, `pipe_dream:0:5` and `pipe_dream:0:8` in Corridor_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness (rotation and y-offset, which the grid consumes, not this artifact), and membership in two curation_station collections in Curation_Bay_randomness_7 and Corridor_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness whose #layout and #with_* keys belong to the station. Not one of them carries a residue key, and apply_grid_config returns on its second line unless a token names this axis.
dna.was: eleven exports and not one of them turnable: pipe_radius, segment_length, max_segments, bounds_extent, turn_interval, continue_straight_chance, growth_tween_time and five colour and energy fields - how BIG and how FAST, never what the cube is left holding. apply_grid_config was a literal `pass`, so none of the eleven was reachable from a map token even as a number. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS on exactly that ground.
dna.note: The word is the group's, taken with its answers rather than borrowed as a label: head < tail < path < envelope < ensemble, the same five in the same order and the same meaning as random_walk_128, random_walk_leash and random_walk_collection. The one place this member differs is worth stating plainly - THE WINDOW AT `tail` IS CUT IN TIME here, not in space. The three siblings draw on pages and keep pixels, so `recently` had to be approximated by a disc around the walker; this record is a list of turns in the order they were taken, so the window is the real thing. The rungs stay strictly nested either way, so no rung invents pipe the run did not lay. `envelope` is the rung this artifact answers best and is why the word fits at all: the desire line says the pipe explores a sealed cube until the cube is full, bounds_extent is the cube it was ALLOWED, and the rails are the cube it USED - never the same box, and the tangle alone cannot say which.
dna.declined: joint - the turn rule (ball / bare / collar), and the strongest other candidate in the file. The sphere at each corner is what makes 180 loose cylinders read as continuous plumbing, and removing it reveals the pipe as sticks that merely overlap, which is a genuine argument about the object. It is declined for a CAMERA reason and not a design one: a corner is 0.34 m on an object whose fitted box is about 13 m across, so at the sweep's fit-by-diagonal framing four values would differ by a handful of pixels - the line_interface fault. It wants its own pass at dna.framing near 0.3 and cannot share a sheet with an axis whose whole subject is the extent of the tangle. Also declined: continue_straight_chance, the file's former declared critical_parameter, because inertia changes how much tangle there is and not what the tangle claims (the reason rhizomatic_maze_space declined its six growth floats); and turn_interval and growth_tween_time, which are rates and invisible to a still.
dna.finding: THE @identity WAS WRONG ABOUT THE ALGORITHM and the header is corrected in this pass rather than papered over. It called this `a self-avoiding 3D random walk ... never crossing itself`. It is not, and never was: _choose_next_direction refuses only the reverse direction and any step that would leave bounds_extent, there is no occupancy set anywhere in the file, and the run crosses itself freely. Making it genuinely self-avoiding would be a different artifact and a change to all five existing placements, so it is not done here.
dna.still_note: residue is resolved before each length is laid and the rungs differ in how much geometry exists, so one frame is a complete account. Expect head-vs-path to be the loudest pair by a distance - one 0.5 m sphere against a 13 m tangle is a silhouette, not a texture. envelope-vs-path is the pair to check second and the one most likely to read small: twelve rails at 0.034 m radius on a 13 m box is thin ink, so if it comes back under 1% compare the silhouettes before believing it. ensemble triples the ink inside the same cube and should be unmistakable.

extreme_randomness.description: Five cycling particle studies: persistent random pushes, smooth trigonometric flow, spiral patterns, flocking-style interactions and target-ranked following. The selection chapter moves a fixed set of particles; it does not breed a population.
extreme_randomness.name: Extreme Randomness

dna.default: chapter=all - 'all' is the value that pins nothing. _chapter_demo_index() finds no match for it in CHAPTER_DEMOS, falls through to the legacy forced_demo (-1 everywhere this token is placed), returns -1, and _ready's gate never fires: display_time stays at its shipped 10.0 and the whole of the staging is the start_demo(0) that was always there. The four direct placements (Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness, Room_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness, Corridor_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness, TestMap_Unused_6) and the Curation_Bay_randomness_7 station collection pass no chapter key, and apply_grid_config returns on its first line for a config that does not name one. The one deliberate asymmetry: at a pinned chapter 0 the code FREEZES rather than restaging, where the old forced_demo path called start_demo(0) twice - so 'all' and 'chaos' are the same picture rather than two draws from different stretches of an unseeded stream, and the axis is not handed a bite it did not earn.
dna.was: an int called forced_demo with no names attached, a registry that declared nothing, and an apply_grid_config that was literally 'pass'. Five chapters existed in full in the file - each with its own opening arrangement in start_demo, its own update rule, its own colour law, its own title and its own paragraph of prose - and there was no way to stop on one, so every map that places this shows whichever page the ten-second clock happened to be on. The five differ in SILHOUETTE before they differ in anything else (a 10 m cube, a flat 20 x 5 panel, a disc, a 2 m ball, a 2 m line), which is what makes the axis legible in one still rather than a claim about motion.
dna.note: THE AXIS ALREADY SHIPPED AS FOUR SEPARATE REGISTRY NAMES. extrem_randomness.gd is one script behind five tokens: particle_randomness_pure, _perlin, _patterns and _emergent are four .tscn wrappers that set forced_demo = 0/1/2/3 with display_time = 1e6, which is chapter = chaos / noise / pattern / emergence spelled as four artifacts. 'evolution' has no wrapper and has therefore never been placed anywhere in the corpus. Those four are deliberately NOT declared here: each token's NAME is its pinned value, and an axis on them would let a map make particle_randomness_perlin show emergence. check_dna_declarations reports them under 'promoted in code, undeclared in the registry' because they share this source file - that is a fact about one script serving five names, not an unfinished promotion. The word 'chapter' and the leading 'all' are facade_grammar_demo's, where 'all' likewise admits the whole book unfiltered; the chapter names belong to this book.
dna.harness: READ THIS BEFORE BELIEVING AN INERT VERDICT. The body is 100 CSGSphere3D plus two Label3D, and capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D ONLY - so the particle cloud is invisible to the sweep's own framing and would fall back to a 1 m box. What the camera will actually fit is the MeshInstance3D plates LabelFramer builds behind the two labels before the AABB is taken, roughly x +/-2.5 by y -4.5..3.7, which lands it near 30 m with an 18 m window over a cloud spanning +/-5 to +/-7. That is close enough to leave framing at 1.0 and no anchor was added, because a +/-5 anchor would be fitted BY DIAGONAL and push the camera out to ~54 m, which is worse. If the sheet comes back cropped or tiny, the AABB is the first thing to check and not the design. The game's own grounder, GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb, DOES walk CSGShape3D, so the two measurers disagree about this artifact by construction.

extreme_randomness.qfep_connection: Randomness at full amplitude: particles driven by draws with no damping, no distribution's comfort. The room's outer limit — past structure, past statistics-as-shape — where entropy stops being a resource and becomes weather.

dna.default: rule=trail - trail is the fall-through arm of the match in _choose_next_position and reproduces the shipped law line for line: the same eight compass directions in the order they were always built, the same seed value best_pheromone = -1.0, a STRICT > so ties fall to the first entry (which on blank ground means Right, and that quirk is preserved deliberately), the same bounds test, the same single randf() before it and the same randi() modulo n on the random arm. The random STREAM is unchanged too: _create_walkers still takes exactly two draws per walker in the same order, and the heading added to the walker dictionary is assigned from COMPASS by INDEX rather than drawn. walk_seed defaults to -1, which routes every draw back to the global unseeded generator exactly as today, and warmup_steps defaults to 0, which returns before touching anything. apply_grid_config was literally `pass` and is now an ASSIGNMENT-ONLY body that rebuilds nothing - it arrives through call_deferred, so it lands after _ready has built the grids, and a rebuild would wipe a terrain the room has been growing since the player walked in. All 3 placements (Random_Pheromone, Room_Random_Pheromone, Corridor_Random_Pheromone) carry the bare token with no config keys at all, so not one branch of it is reachable from any map that exists.
dna.was: no axis, and no way in at all: apply_grid_config was a one-line `pass`, so the fourteen @exports were unreachable from a map token and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. That was literally true here in a way it was not for most of the batch. The walker's decision law - eight directions, argmax pheromone at sensor_distance, otherwise random - was welded into _choose_next_position with the direction list rebuilt inline on every call, and the only thing the scene could argue with was how MUCH the walkers follow (pheromone_attraction, and only by editing the .tscn), never WHAT following means.
dna.shared_with: `rule` is mold_network's word for exactly this slot - the transition law - seconded by structure_growth, complexity_pattern and lifeform_walker, and it is taken deliberately rather than invented. THE VALUE LIST IS NOT SHARED AND CANNOT BE, for the same reason mold_network gives for not sharing with the Life family: those are survive/born bands over a cell's neighbours and this is one walker choosing one of eight compass steps, a different alphabet in which '4-6/5-7' means nothing. These should NOT be compared as a family measurement. The word carries; the numbers must not.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. THE RULE IS VISIBLE IN A STILL AND THE RATE IS NOT, which is the whole reason this is the axis. deposit-per-step, decay-per-second and steps-per-second are the knobs a reader reaches for first and every one of them is a fact about time that a single frame cannot hold; what a frame CAN hold is the shape the ground ended up in. Each value changes one clause of the same decision and nothing else - which neighbours are candidates, or the sign of the comparison. trail is self-reinforcing and converges: the walkers commit to paths they made and the plot grows a few thick ridges. sniff gives the walker a heading and only the three steps in front of it, so it cannot double back into its own trail and the same attraction lays long smooth arcs instead of knots - the Physarum reading, in which the body remembers as well as the environment. avoid flips the sign and flees the strongest scent, so no ridge ever forms and the plot churns evenly - the anti-stigmergy case the artifact's own @identity names when it says it contrasts with pixel_cloud. grid narrows the candidates to the four cardinal neighbours, and the lattice stops being a substrate and becomes the result: right-angled ridges, a street plan rather than a delta. TWO THINGS THE SHIPPED CODE DID NOT SURVIVE UNPATCHED, both found by reading rather than by running: the border branch of _walk_step `continue`s WITHOUT choosing a direction, so a heading-locked walker would push at the same wall for ever - the heading is reversed there, which costs no random draw and is inert under the other three values; and _forward_cone returns STRAIGHT ON first, because the shipped law breaks ties on the first entry and on unwalked ground every candidate senses 0.0, so a turn at index 0 would fill the plot with same-handed spirals and publish a fact about list order as a fact about stigmergy.
dna.fixture_note: two knobs, both new, both defaulting to shipped behaviour so neither is an axis, and both necessary before any frame of this artifact means anything. walk_seed pins the walk: it defaults to -1, which routes every draw to the global unseeded generator exactly as the shipped code did, and without it four rule variants are four different landscapes and the sweep measures the RNG - the brief's 'confident bite on a generative artifact' row. warmup_steps makes the frame a KNOWN AGE. This is the harder of the two: _process only rebuilds the mesh on a step, walk_speed is 5 so a step is 0.2 s, and the capture settles for 1.1 s - so the shipped artifact photographs as a FLAT PLANE with five or six vertices nudged, under every value, and the axis would have read INERT as a fact about the bench. 400 steps decayed at the real 0.2 s interval is the shipped dynamics played fast rather than a different process; at raise_amount 0.2 that is 1600 vertex raises on a 60 x 60 interior, enough for ridges of a metre or more on a 20 m plate. It costs about 2.6 M grid touches inside _ready, which is a fraction of a second and well inside the watchdog's grace, but it is the number to lower first if a boot stalls.
dna.still_note: framing 0.65, derived: the plate is 20 x 20 m so the box radius is about 14.1 m, the no-crop floor is 1/PAD = 0.526, and 0.65 opens the frame to roughly 34.8 m across - the plate at about 57 percent of frame width with 23 percent margin on the corners, against 37 percent at framing 1.0. THE COLOUR SURVIVES, which was checked rather than assumed: the scene's material is the SimpleGrid wireframe shader, not a StandardMaterial3D, so the vertex_color_use_as_albedo line in _ready never fires - but the shader reads COLOR into instanceColor and, because modelColor is grey rather than white, takes the instance colour whenever it is not white. _update_mesh writes Color.WHITE.lerp(pheromone_color, intensity), so unwalked ground stays grey and fresh trail reads magenta. So the frame carries the argument twice over: the HEIGHT is the permanent record and the MAGENTA is the short-term one (a cell decays from 0.6 to 0 in fifteen steps), and the two say different things about the same rule. The camera sits 15 degrees above the horizon, which foreshortens a flat plate but shows relief against the horizon, so ridge SHAPE reads better than ridge position. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass and this arithmetic is the evidence offered in its place.
dna.declined: pheromone_attraction is NOT an axis, although the artifact's own @identity nominates it as the critical_parameter. It is a continuous dial between the shipped law and a pure random walk, it is now config-reachable through apply_grid_config like every other numeric export, and naming a value `wander` for attraction = 0 would be a second word for a knob that exists - projection_shadow's test. That is also why the value list has no null anchor: the null of this axis is a number, and it is already spelled. Nothing in the deposit / decay / speed group was considered for longer than it took to remember that a still cannot see a rate.

pheromone_terrain.description: Walkers deposit decaying pheromone and accumulate visual height. Existing trail, sniff, avoid and grid rules change which local signal is followed. An optional paused comparison exposes attraction and avoidance from the same seed and starting walkers, with single-step, 20-step and replay controls.
pheromone_terrain.name: Pheromone Terrain

noise_mixer.description: A visual mixer of finite sine-based spatial layers with seeded offsets. OCT, LAC and PER regenerate the sum live; each texture is normalized to its own range before an earth-toned palette is applied.
noise_mixer.name: Noise Mixer

worley_noise.description: Voronoi/cellular noise texture on a floor quad. Scatters random seed points and computes F2-F1 (second-nearest minus nearest distance) for the classic cell boundary look. Complement to Perlin/Simplex noise.
worley_noise.name: Worley Noise

random_space.description: A crystal that contains mathematical chaos algorithms
random_space.name: random_space
random_space.qfep_connection: The floor re-rolls its own heights every tick while collision updates on a slower interval, so what you see and what holds you are briefly two different terrains — chaos rationed to protect the frame rate and the ankles.

dna.framing_note: MEASURED, not guessed, and the number comes out of this file: aabb_size above is [11.0, 0.24, 20.0]. Fit-by-diagonal puts the sweep camera about 71 m out, where 0.24 m of relief is roughly four pixels of a 760 px frame - the documented fit-by-diagonal-on-a-thin-subject fault, and it would have reported a real axis as inert. This axis does not live in the silhouette at all: it lives in the SHADING, because the field is sampled every 0.22 m in x and 0.40 m in z with a peak-to-peak of 0.24 m, so adjacent vertices differ by up to 50 degrees of slope and the surface reads as texture. 0.32 puts the camera about 23 m out, where a cell is 12-22 px and the speckle statistics of the four laws are legible. The slab will overfill the frame and that is intended: the subject is the field, not its outline.
dna.default: law=uniform - and a SHORT-CIRCUIT rather than a recomputation. At `uniform` _draw returns `rng.randf_range(-chaos_level, chaos_level)`, which is the shipped expression itself, same call, same argument order, one draw from the same seeded stream; it does not re-derive the same number through randf(), which would be equal today and hostage tomorrow to how the engine implements randf_range. The .tscn's own values are untouched (seed_value 1, chaos_level 1.0, height_scale 0.12, resolution 50, space_size 11x20, enable_animation false), so the three rooms get the field they have always had. MEASURED, not assumed: 3 mentions across 3 map files - bare `random_space` in Random_Space and Room_Random_Space, and `random_space:0:-0.3:1.4` in Corridor_Random_Space, where the trailing numbers are rotation and y-offset consumed by the grid and not by this artifact. Not one of them carries a law key, and apply_grid_config returns without regenerating unless a key is present AND its value differs from the one the node already holds.
dna.was: eighteen exports and no way to reach any of them. TopologySpace declares no apply_grid_config and RandomSpace had none either, so chaos_level, seed_value, animation_type and the rest were editor-only: every placement got the identical field and map_data could not say otherwise. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Underneath that, the artifact named for randomness knew exactly ONE meaning of the word - a single hard-coded uniform draw per vertex - while sitting in the sequence that exists to teach that random is not one thing.
dna.note: THE FOUR LAWS ARE MONOTONE TRANSFORMS OF THE SAME DRAW, which is what makes them comparable rather than merely different. Each law consumes exactly one number per vertex from the same seeded stream and each is non-decreasing in it, so vertex i gets the same u under all four and a peak stays a peak: the four surfaces share their layout exactly and differ only in how amplitude is distributed over it. Four fields drawn from four streams would also have differed, and the difference would have been the streams. That alignment rests on randf_range being one linear randf, which it is in Godot 4; the DEFAULT rests on nothing of the kind, because at uniform the transform branch never runs at all. gaussian uses the A&S 26.2.23 normal quantile (error < 4.5e-4, four orders finer than a vertex of this mesh can show); poisson is the pmf accumulated directly at lambda 1.5 and capped at 4, giving five populated terraces; exponential is the inverse CDF at rate 3, where the median vertex sits at 0.23 of the range and about one in twenty saturates - the only asymmetric law of the four, and the one that gives the ground a base level that is not the middle of the range.
dna.declined: animation_type (WAVE/RIPPLE/RANDOM_WALK/CHAOTIC) is the obvious enum and declines twice over: it is time-domain, so a still catches one arbitrary phase, and it is dead in every placement anyway because the .tscn sets enable_animation false - promoting it would mean switching the animation on and changing what all three rooms do. chaos_level and height_scale change how MUCH relief there is and not what the relief claims. surface_color and emission_tint are which-colour, which is never an argument. `generator` is deliberately NOT borrowed from noise_space: that word names which CORRELATED basis fills a field, and this artifact's whole position in the sequence is that its vertices are independent, so taking the word would claim the two floors are the same kind of object.
dna.finding: THE FIELD IS DRAWN TWICE ON BOOT AND ONE OF THE TWO IS NEVER SEEN. super._ready() runs generate_space(), which builds the mesh from the first draw; _ready() then calls _generate_base_heights() again, leaving base_heights holding a second, different field that is never displayed while enable_animation is false - which it is in the .tscn, hence in all three rooms. Not repaired here, because repairing it would change which field those rooms show. apply_grid_config works around it instead: it reseeds before regenerating, so a rebuilt surface is the FIRST draw again and a config call that changes only the law changes only the law.
dna.still_note: law is resolved once per vertex before the mesh exists and never moves again, so one frame is a complete account of it. Expect poisson to be the loudest value - five discrete terraces against a continuum is a categorical change in the shading, not a shift in it - and exponential second, because it is the only law that moves the base level off centre. uniform-vs-gaussian is the subtle pair and the honest test of the framing: they share every peak and differ only in how much of the surface sits near the middle. If ALL SIX pairs come back under 1%, suspect the camera before the axis and check that dna.framing arrived.

dna.default: posture=cycle, warning=beacon - both no-ops. `cycle` takes the identical _ready path (_set_state(IDLE) then a deferred loop start) and is guarded out of _apply_posture entirely; `beacon` leaves the indicator rule as `is_visible and true` and builds no extra nodes. The 6 existing placements (Random_Game, _HumanoidWalker, _Hybrid, _Placed, _SimulatedAnnealing, TemplateMap_Descent13, all writing the token `r_c:0:0:1#4`) render byte-identically, and the numeric-shorthand span path still ends in _restart_cycle_loop() exactly as before.
dna.was: A cube that sank out and rose back in on randomised timing. Every export was a DURATION - waits, sink, rise, collider lead and lag - and a still cannot photograph a duration, so the runner correctly refused it as having no turnable knobs. posture lifts the CycleState enum, which already drives height, colour, indicator and collider together but could never be selected from outside the loop. warning names the answer the cube already shipped (a lit mote on its crown) and puts it in the hazard family's vocabulary.
dna.notes: The fixture pins posture=leaving because that is the one pose where all four warning values are photographically distinct: beacon lights the mote, stain marks the floor, cage stands the bars, none shows a bare cube. At a resting pose beacon and none are identical by construction - which is the axis's own point, not a harness fault. cycle_seed pins _rng, whose randomize() would otherwise make five variants five different moments. Map syntax: r_c:0:0:1#posture=sunken#warning=cage.
dna.declined: Every timing export (wait_min_seconds, wait_span_seconds, sink_duration, rise_duration, disable_collider_delay, enable_collider_delay) is time-domain and invisible to a still. sink_distance was considered and left out: on a 1 m cube it is a distance, and posture already photographs the two ends of the travel.

r_c.name: Random Cycle Cube
r_c.description: A cube with fixed state order, random standing/hidden waits and separately switched collision. Optional chasm staging supplies three seeded stones, a recoverable pit, state tablet, REPLAY, NEW SEED and CUE.
r_c.qfep_connection: A floor tile with its own randomized schedule: it sinks, drops its collider after a 0.2-second grace, waits hidden, rises again. Ground stops being a promise and becomes a rhythm you must read off the state colors.
interactions: With stand:chasm, REPLAY restores standing stones and seeded waits
NEW SEED chooses a different current crossing seed
CUE toggles advance rings; movement beacons and state tablet remain

random_doors.name: One passage, two fire jets
random_doors.description: One passage, two fire jets; an owned simulation with reachable replay controls.

door_timing_trials.name: When did the door decide?
door_timing_trials.description: Three matched walk-through trials: draw-reveal-choose, choose-draw-reveal, and draw-choose-reveal. Floor plates select a lane; its result opens a direct shortcut or leaves a longer path around a wall. Seeded algorithmic assignment, not physical entropy. Independent replay controls reject resets while a player occupies the route.
interactions: Step on A or B to choose
Walk the direct passage or the longer route
Read the retained event order
Replay from outside or start a new seeded round
door_timing_trials.qfep_connection: A decision and access to that decision are separate events. Changing disclosure changes what a visitor can act upon even with the same possible routes.

dna.default: warning=none is the export default and the `_:` branch of _build_warning, which adds no node at all. All 9 placements are unchanged: Corridor_Random_Game, MindMap_Primitives, Room_Random_Game and Random_Game_* x5 plus TemplateMap_Descent13, of which six carry the long #mode:field#field_size:8x8#... chain and none of the nine passes a `warning` key. _build_warning runs LAST in _ready, after _setup_spawner, _find_player and activate_spawner, so MeshInstance3D, SpawnTimer, SpawnPoint, WarningParticles, SpawnSound, WarningSound and Label3D all keep their child indices. configure() reads the key only when it is PRESENT and names a legal value DIFFERENT from the one already standing, which matters because six of the nine send a dozen field_* keys on every load and must not tear the dressing down. An unrecognised word keeps the current value: a typo must not silently uncage a live hazard.
dna.was: BROKEN, and not by omission of a genome. The axis, its allow-list, its five-rung doc block, the field_seed pin and the idle_still fixture flag were already in CubeSpawner.gd from an earlier pass, and _ready and configure both CALLED _build_warning() — a function that existed nowhere in the script. In GDScript 4 that is a resolution error at parse time, so the script did not load and cube_projectile_spawner rendered nothing in any of its nine rooms. The declaration gate cannot catch this class: the export is real and its values are real, and it is the builder that is absent (dna_specimen's fault one step further along). The whole of this pass is the five builders, the bounds reader, the cover-height reader and this declaration. Found by scanning every .gd in b0428de74 'rescue(dna): 35 promotions that were written and never committed' for self-calls with no definition; the other eight hits were inherited helpers or a comment, so this is the rescue's only casualty.
dna.note: warning is kaleidocycle_enemy's word and its five values character for character — miura_crawler, scissor_stalker, kresling_spire, origami_droideka, path_cube, path_pyramid, path_wedge and force_vortex already ask it, and a room cannot coherently cage its crawlers and leave the thing that shoots at them unannounced. The colours, the `hazard_warning` group and the four builders are that artifact's, resized from this one's own AABB rather than copied at its scale, so the family photographs as one apparatus at eight sizes. The sharpest case in the family for its own reason: the spawner is not the danger, it is the SOURCE of the danger, and between two firings it is a box on the floor doing nothing at all — so what the room says about a currently idle box is not a property of the box. stain is legible only from inside the field of fire; beacon is the only rung that reaches you at the doorway; shroud reaches up past the placard at y 1.5 so the machine and its own hazard sign go under the canvas together, because a wrap that left the sign legible would not be a wrap. APPEARANCE ONLY: spawn_interval, projectile_speed, max_projectiles, target_prediction, spawn_mode and every field_* number are byte-identical across all five, and no value adds or removes a collider. A hazard that hides itself is not a gentler hazard.
dna.fixture_note: idle_still is a fixture and NOT an axis. auto_start is true, so activate_spawner runs in _ready and starts both a looping 0.5 s pulse tween on the housing and the 50-particle warning plume; a still 1.1 s in catches the box at an arbitrary scale between 1.0 and 1.2 and the plume at an arbitrary density, which is per-variant noise on top of the axis. idle_still skips both and is declared as the STRING "true" on purpose — the export is untyped for exactly this reason, since a typed bool rejects a fixture string before _ready and does it silently. field_seed is not in the fixture because it is not reachable in a still: spawn_mode defaults to FORWARD, which never draws from _rng, and the first projectile is due at t=6.0 s against a 1.1 s settle, so no capture of the default has a projectile in it at all.
dna.declined: spawn_interval, projectile_speed, fall_min/fall_max and jitter_interval were all considered and refused: a rate and a duration are invisible to a single frame, which is the info_board fault. spawn_mode = forward|falling_field is real, argues something (a shot aimed at you versus weather that does not know you are there) and is ALREADY reachable from a map token via configure()'s `mode` key — but the difference lives entirely in cubes that do not exist until t=6.0 s, so a still of the two modes is the same red box twice.

cube_projectile_spawner.description: A timed emitter with forward and falling-field modes. Field mode samples initial x/z positions and velocities; each projectile has independent later jitter. Optional stand:field supplies local RUN / STOP and CLEAR controls and a marked initial-position region.
cube_projectile_spawner.name: cube_projectile_spawner
cube_projectile_spawner.qfep_connection: It does not shoot at you, it shoots at where its model says you will be: target_prediction leads the player's velocity before every launch. Being hunted here means being forecast, with the warning glow as the only courtesy.
