dna.fixture_why: Every visible parameter of this room is driven off a clock in _process — time, time_scale, cloud_density and both colours all move — so a still is taken at whatever instant the shutter happened to fall. `frozen` leaves the .tscn's own authored uniforms in place and never advances them, which makes four basis frames comparable instead of four different moments. It is a String enum, not a bool, because the sweep sets exports from strings before _ready and a typed bool silently rejects "true" — the trap that has eaten fixture flags twice. `live` is the default and is the shipped behaviour, so no placement sees the pin.
dna.default: generator=perlin - the perlin branch of the shader's dispatch is the shipped noise2d body, character for character (diffed against HEAD, not eyeballed), and _apply_generator writes 1 into a uniform whose own declared default is already 1. Note the default is perlin and NOT simplex, the opposite of the bench artifacts, because that is what this file has always computed: hash2 returns a gradient per lattice corner and the interpolation dots it with the offset, which is Perlin's construction with a sine hash instead of a permutation table. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 13 mentions across 11 map files, not the 5 the promotion brief carried, by three reach-paths - bare tokens in Noise_6_Wall, Corridor_Noise_6_Wall, Noise_Functions, TestMap_Unused_23 and Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:shader_noise_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value and the # keys are the furniture's; and `perlin_noise->shader_noise_space` in Trial_erosion_noise, which is a transformation target and not a config. None carries a generator key, and apply_grid_config returns unless a token names a word this file knows AND that word differs from the one it holds.
dna.was: seven exports, every one of them a rate or a toggle on the animation loop, and the runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The decision that carries the argument was not an export at all: it was the body of a single function called noise2d, hard-coded to one basis in a room whose walls, ceiling and floor are made of nothing else.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, noise_terrain - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order. The noise sequence is built on comparing bases; spelling the comparison a second way would leave nothing to compare. cellular, not worley, for the same reason. What differs here is the scale of the question: on the bench a basis is a tabletop of displaced cubes you look down at, and here it is the room you are standing inside.
dna.amplitude_note: The four bases are AMPLITUDE-MATCHED rather than merely swapped in. Measured over 30,000 samples each returns mean |value| = 0.137, which is what the shipped perlin returns; the three scaling constants in the shader (0.770, 38.0, 0.827) exist only for that. Without them the sweep would mostly have been reading which basis is BRIGHTER once the six-octave sum is pushed through smoothstep(0.2, 0.8), and the axis would have been about exposure instead of about structure. Their own characters survive the matching: measured local step per unit distance is 4.7% of mean for value, 8.4% perlin, 11.0% cellular, 13.9% simplex.
dna.declined: animation_speed (this file's own declared critical_parameter until now), time_scale_variation, color_cycle_speed and density_variation - four rates, all real, all audible in the room, and all invisible to one still. Promoting any of them would have produced the info_board result: a finished-looking experiment answering nothing. `octaves` was also declined despite simplex_noise carrying it as a numeric axis: the fbm here runs six octaves over a wall two metres from the eye, so the lower rungs would read as a blurrier wall rather than as a claim about self-similarity, and one honest axis is worth more than a second one that argues about resolution.
dna.still_note: the basis is a fragment-shader uniform, so it is resolved every frame and never settles into geometry — but it is also constant in time under the fixture, so one frame is a complete account. The subject is a closed 16 x 12 x 27 m box of CSGBox3D walls with cull_disabled, so the sweep's camera sits outside and photographs two or three wall faces filling the frame. That is the field at full size, which is the best case for measuring a basis; if the bite comes back small, suspect the clock, not the axis.
dna.finding: QueerNoiseShader.gdshader and WallNoiseShader.gdshader were BYTE-IDENTICAL, header comment included — the room-sphere shader carried the wall shader's filename at the top of the file. The @identity's claim that 'the two materials run independent shader noise loops' out of phase is one shader run twice with different uniform values and a 0.7x offset on time. Both files now carry the same dispatch so the room and its walls change basis together.

shader_noise_space.qfep_connection: Noise evaluated per-pixel at framerate: the GPU as noise organ, procedural texture with no texture stored. The room turns as you move because nothing in it is a picture — everything is a function, sampled where you look.

voronoi_strands.name: Voronoi Strands
voronoi_strands.description: An open three-dimensional Voronoi edge skeleton drawn in thin charcoal tubes, with shared junctions and cords anchored directly to surrounding floors, walls and ceilings. Seeded sites define the cell geometry. No opaque cell faces or line collision. An enlarged eight-legged spider lays the lines progressively, tracing the mathematical graph as an artwork rather than simulating natural web growth. All strands belong to one connected graph with shared 3D junctions and explicit attachments to room surfaces. The completed net relaxes under gravity with tension-only cables, fixed room anchors and unbreakable shared knots.
voronoi_strands.qfep_connection: A partition remains legible as lines while its faces no longer bar passage. The attachment cords depend on the host architecture. Releasing the net distinguishes its distance construction from its shape under load: shared knots transmit a pull while fixed room anchors carry it.

parameters.weave: Build progressively with a spider; false immediately releases the complete net
parameters.weave_speed: Spider travel speed in metres per second, 0.1 to 20
parameters.tension: Release the completed net under gravity; false preserves the Voronoi construction
parameters.compliance: Cable stretch per newton, 0.000001 to 0.001 m/N
parameters.knot_mass: Mass per free shared knot, 0.001 to 0.1 kg

Inspect the polygon edges from different viewpoints
Watch the spider lay strands and retrace completed branches

dna.default: generator=simplex, octaves=4 - octaves=4 is the shipped @export byte for byte. generator=simplex does NOT assign a noise type: the shipped file set frequency and fractal_octaves and never touched noise_type at all, so this ground has always been whatever basis FastNoiseLite itself defaults to, and _build_noise leaves it alone at the default value instead of assigning TYPE_SIMPLEX - assigning it would be a silent correction that reshapes the terrain under every existing placement. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 11 mentions across 10 map files, by three reach-paths - bare tokens in Corridor_Noise_Space_10, Noise_Space_10 and Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:noise_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value and the # keys are the furniture's; and `simplex_noise->noise_space` plus `noise_space->noisetorus` in Trial_erosion_noise, which are transformation targets and not config. None carries a generator or octaves key, and apply_grid_config returns without regenerating unless a key is present AND its value differs from the one the node already holds.
dna.was: an artifact named for its noise that never said which noise, and three @exports nobody could reach. TopologySpace has no apply_grid_config and NoiseSpace had none either, so noise_scale, octaves and persistence were editor-only: every placement got the same 10 x 10 m landform and map_data could not say otherwise. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS on exactly that ground - the knobs existed, nothing was connected to them.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, shader_noise_space, noise_terrain - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order and the same default. cellular, not worley, for the same reason: the noise sequence is built on comparing bases, and spelling the comparison four ways would leave nothing to compare. `octaves` is simplex_noise's word for the same quantity, but the ladder is 1-2-3-4 rather than its 1-2-4-6, and the difference was computed rather than chosen: this mesh samples every 0.1 m across a 10 m space (resolution 100) while the base wavelength is about 2 m (frequency 0.1 against coordinates pre-multiplied by noise_scale 5.0), so octave k has wavelength 2 / 2^(k-1) and octaves 5 and 6 land at 0.125 and 0.0625 m, below the mesh's 0.2 m Nyquist wavelength. Declaring 6 would ship a rung that differs from 4 only by aliasing at a sixteenth of the amplitude.
dna.vocabulary_declined: readout (relief|plate|column), carried by perlin_noise, simplex_noise, perlin_noise_terrain, random_edge_profile and mandelbrot_set. Declined for exactly the reason noise_terrain recorded when it declined the same word: readout asks a geometric question about a tabletop field, and this is a walkable substrate with a trimesh collider under it, so plate and column would change what the player STANDS ON rather than what the field claims to be, and the word would stop meaning one thing across the sequence. noise_terrain's own second axis `legend` (contours|relief|mood) is declined too, for the opposite reason: there both encodings already existed in the file and only a 2D button chose between them, while here there is exactly one material - a flat organic-green StandardMaterial3D with no height encoding at all - so the shipped look is neither contours nor relief nor mood, and taking the word would mean inventing a fourth value to hold the thing that actually ships. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary.
dna.still_note: both axes resolve during _ready and never move again - the noise object is fully configured before the 10,201-vertex mesh is built, and nothing on this artifact animates - so a single frame is a complete account of both. Deterministic besides: FastNoiseLite is left on its default seed and nothing in the file calls randf(), so four generator frames are four bases over one footprint rather than four landscapes, and no seed pin is needed.
dna.framing_note: the subject is a 10 x 10 m slab carrying about 4 m of relief, and a fit-by-diagonal camera is roughly right for it (the plan diagonal and the box diagonal are within 4% of each other), so no numeric framing is set. If the bite reads modest, compare silhouettes before believing it: expect cellular to be the loudest value by far and octaves=1 to be the smoothest.
dna.repair: persistence has been an @export since the file was written and was never spent on anything. It is the fBm gain and is now wired to fractal_gain - but only when it differs from its own shipped 0.5, so a placement that never names it leaves the noise object untouched no matter what FastNoiseLite's own default gain is. It is a repair, not a declared axis.

noise_space.description: A noise heightfield with matching mesh and collision. The optional stand:walk study in Noise_Space_10 keeps one OpenSimplex2S field fixed while HEIGHT changes its contribution to an eight-metre terrain. A level margin, two proposed routes and a supported profile instrument let the visitor compare a section with an actual crossing. Unconfigured placements retain their original ten-metre terrain.
noise_space.name: Noise Space Explorer
noise_space.qfep_connection: The chapter's thesis as a place: a whole environment driven by configurable noise, walked from inside. Not an exhibit about noise — an exhibit *made of* it, where changing a parameter re-decides the room around you.

dna.default: readout=relief, octaves=4 - relief is the legacy cube.position.y = value line and 4 was the hard-coded fractal_octaves, so all 8 existing placements render exactly as before
dna.was: no exports on the root at all: the whole parameter space lived in a 2D Control panel that the grid strips out of map placements, so every placement was the same 20x20 field of half-metre cubes displaced in y and tinted pink-to-teal, and map_data could not say otherwise.

simplex_noise.description: Interactive Simplex noise generation and visualization for high-quality procedural content
simplex_noise.name: Simplex Noise
simplex_noise.qfep_connection: Perlin's own second draft: the simplex grid replaces squares, fewer artifacts, better behavior in high dimensions. Standing beside its ancestor it teaches versioning as a mathematical practice — even noise gets revised.

dna.default: generator=simplex, readout=relief - both are exactly what the shipped code did (NoiseVisualizer hard-coded FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX and lifted a uniform cube to its sample), so the 7 existing placements render identically
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: simplex_noise - readout is the same axis with the same three values and the same default on both, so the pair can be compared instead of merely contrasted
dna.was: no exports on the root at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The two decisions that carry the argument sat one node down as constants: which basis fills the field, and whether a sample is read as elevation or as measurement. Note that the artifact called Perlin Noise has been drawing SIMPLEX noise since it was written; the promotion makes that a declared choice (generator=perlin is now available) rather than silently correcting it and rewriting seven maps.

perlin_noise.description: Interactive Perlin noise generation and visualization
perlin_noise.name: Perlin Noise
perlin_noise.qfep_connection: Perlin's gift to graphics: gradients on a lattice, interpolated smoothly — randomness that flows instead of stutters. Every organic-looking surface in games descends from this trick. The demo hands you the dials: octaves stacking detail, persistence deciding how loudly the small scales speak.

perlin_noise_terrain.description: Interactive 3D terrain generation using Perlin noise algorithms
perlin_noise_terrain.name: Perlin Noise Terrain
perlin_noise_terrain.qfep_connection: The Perlin pipeline run to its natural end: octaves become mountain ranges, persistence becomes ruggedness. Parameter names turn geological — the chapter's clearest case of mathematics wearing the world's clothes.

configurable_portal.qfep_connection: The door as parameter: size, rotation, destination all data. Passage itself made configurable — the humblest artifact in the room and the most honest about what this world is (everything, including exits, is a setting).

dna.fixture_why: MANDATORY for the sweep, and it is a fact about the bench rather than about the artifact. The bridge grows one row per generation_speed seconds out of `length` rows - at the scene's own 0.05 s x 120 rows that is six full seconds of wall clock. A still photographed at the bench's settle time catches a stump, and worse, a different stump per value, because a rule that spawns more cubes renders slower: four frames that differ by how far each one got. build_rows 0 is the shipped grow-over-time behaviour and is what all four placements get; a positive number builds that many rows synchronously inside _ready and then stops, so the capture photographs a finished deck. Capture bench only - no map sets it.
dna.default: rule=30 - the shipped @export default, which the .tscn does not override (it sets width 31, length 120 and generation_speed 0.05 and nothing else). MEASURED, not assumed: seven string occurrences across five map files - `ca_bridge:0:-5` in CA_GameOfLife, bare `ca_bridge` in Disposition_Test_Maze, bare `ca_bridge` and `ca_bridge:180:0.0` in Zone_ForbiddenWetLab, and `curation_station#artifacts:ca_bridge...` in Corridor_CA_GameOfLife and Curation_Bay_cellularautomata_0 where the # keys belong to the station rather than to this token. The `:0:-5` form is artifact:rotation:y_offset, not config. None passes a rule key, and the new apply_grid_config returns without regenerating unless a key is present AND differs from the value the node holds - so all four keep walking rule 30 at the same speed as before.
dna.was: everything this artifact argues is one 8-bit number, and the number was unreachable. `rule` was already an @export, but apply_grid_config was a literal `pass`, so no map token could name it and every placement walked rule 30. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS: the knob existed and nothing was connected to it.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: complexity_pattern, lifeform_walker, mold_network, structure_growth - the WORD `rule` only. All four use it for the same question, which local update law is in force, and the registry already carries it over two disjoint value lists (Life-family rulestrings, and agent behaviours), so a third is consistent rather than a drift.
dna.vocabulary_declined: life|highlife|seeds|replicator|maze|coral, the value list complexity_pattern and lifeform_walker share. Those are 2D Moore-neighbourhood birth/survival rulestrings and this is a 1D three-cell automaton: there is no `life` here to name, and taking those answers would name a mechanism this object does not have. For an elementary CA the rules ARE their numbers, and the artifact's own @identity already says so - `critical_parameter: rule (0-255)`. Same shape as bouncing_ball taking `regime` and refusing under/critical/over. Also declined: a second `seeding` axis (one cell vs a random row), for the reason complexity_pattern recorded when it declined density - the initial row is drawn with an unseeded randf(), so four random-start frames would be four different bridges and any bite number would measure the RNG rather than the rule.
dna.ladder_note: the four values were MEASURED, not taken from a textbook. The exact update in _apply_rule was re-implemented in Python at this scene's own geometry (width 31, periodic wrap, single centre seed, 120 rows) and every rule 0-254 scored for fill and pairwise difference. 184 and 22 were dropped for filling about 3% of the deck - a thread, not a bridge, and far too small a subject to photograph. What ships spans Wolfram's classes and no two values share more than 58% of their cells: 30 is 48.0% full (class 3, chaotic - a broken deck), 90 is 23.5% (class 2, the Sierpinski gasket - nested self-similar gaps), 110 is 49.7% (class 4, the universal one), 250 is 87.5% (class 1/2, near-solid - the control, a ramp that computes nothing).

mold_network.qfep_connection: relation: the slime mold's answer — a network grown by local reinforcement, efficiency without an engineer. The biological cousin of every rule in the room.

dna.default: rule=reinforce, wake=hold - reinforce is survive 4-6 / born 5-7 and hold is 10 states, which composes to "4-6/5-7/10/M", the exact string MoldNetwork.tscn already carries. And the composition does not even run at defaults: _ready writes rule_string ONLY when an axis is off its default, so at the shipped values not one byte is assigned and the scene's own field stands. apply_grid_config regrows only when a value both validates and differs, and none of the 27 placements passes a rule or wake key, so all 27 rooms are unchanged.
dna.was: no axis at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The script has fifteen exports, but they are grid dimensions, cell size, tick rate, two colours and a gradient, and the one field that carries the whole argument, rule_string, is a single opaque slash-separated string set as a constant in the .tscn. apply_grid_config was literally `pass`, so a map token could not reach anything at all.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. A slime mould is a law about how much company a filament needs. survive/born decides whether the colony commits to thick reinforced tube or pushes thin exploratory strand; the state count decides how much of everywhere-it-has-been is still standing, because a cell that fails survival does not vanish - it walks up the dying states, rendering the whole time and refusing rebirth until it reaches zero. So `wake` is simultaneously the visible mass of spent tissue and the refractory period behind the front, which is exactly the kept-versus-pruned question and is spatial, not temporal: at any fixed generation hold shows the accreted body and none shows only the live froth. NOT cell_size or grid_size, which are the artifact's size and not its argument. THE FRONT ADVANCES ONE CELL PER GENERATION UNDER EVERY VALUE (birth needs a live neighbour), so the silhouette stays the same size between values and only the texture and density of the shell change - which is what makes these four frames comparable pixel to pixel instead of the same picture at four magnifications.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: complexity_pattern and lifeform_walker - `rule` is their word for exactly this slot, the transition law, and it is taken deliberately rather than invented. The VALUE LIST is NOT shared and cannot be: those two are 2D Life-family rules over 8 neighbours, this is a 3D Generations rule over 26, a different alphabet in which B3/S23 is instantly extinct. So the word carries across and the numbers must not - these three should NOT be compared as a family measurement.
dna.rule_derivation: the bands were derived, not guessed, because the failure mode of an invented CA rule is a blank frame that reads as an inert axis. The seed is a 7^3 block at density 0.5, so a dead cell one step outside a face sees Binomial(9, 0.5) live neighbours: P(born) is 0.73 for explore (3-6/4-7), 0.48 for reinforce (4-6/5-7, shipped), 0.25 for compact (5-7/6-8) and 0.41 for strand (2-4/5-6). All four keep the front moving, which is the check that none photographs as an empty grid. strand is the one that is not merely a density step: surviving only on 2-4 neighbours means cells die wherever they are crowded, so what persists is wiry and isolated rather than a shell. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass, and this arithmetic is the evidence offered in its place.
dna.shared_script_warning: CellularAutomata3D_Flexible.gd is shared. StructureGrowth.tscn authors "6-8/6-8/3/M" and biome_paint_dispatcher._spawn_fungus hands per-cell `rule=` overrides in before add_child. Composing rule_string unconditionally in _ready would have silently overwritten both - the biome's whole fungus kingdom included. That is why the compose is gated on an axis being off its default, and why any future edit here must keep that gate. SIDE EFFECT: check_dna_declarations now lists `structure_growth: rule, wake` as promoted-in-code-undeclared, because that scene runs the same script. Do NOT close that line by copying this block into structure_growth - its authored rule is the Builder rule "6-8/6-8/3/M" and these four bands were derived from the mould's seed density, so they would be a fake genome for it. If it deserves an axis it needs its own bands.
dna.fixture_note: three knobs, all already in the file, all defaulting to shipped behaviour so none of them is an axis. growth_seed pins the soup: it defaults to -1, which randomizes, and without it four rule variants are four different organisms and the sweep measures the RNG. The other two make the frame a KNOWN GENERATION rather than whatever the 1.1 s settle happens to land on - at the shipped 0.1 s interval the shot falls around generation 11 and moves with frame timing; at 0.01 s the automaton reaches generation 14, pauses, and then sits frozen for the rest of the settle, so every variant is photographed at the same age. 14 keeps the front around 10 cells from the centre of a 30-cell grid, well clear of the boundary layer _step refuses to touch.
dna.measurement_risk: capture_anchor is deliberately NOT in the fixture. It stands an invisible box around the whole 30^3 volume - a 6 m cube - while the growth at generation 14 spans maybe 2 m, so it would shrink the subject rather than frame it. The sweep's _subtree_aabb already measures MultiMeshInstance3D, so this artifact has a real box without it. The residual risk is that MultiMesh AABB covers the whole allocated buffer, and unset instances sit at the node origin, which is a CORNER of the volume - so the measured box may be inflated toward the corner and the mould framed off-centre. If the critic reports faint, check subject % and consider a framing hint before re-cutting either axis.

dna.default: tick=limit, removal=gone - limit is TICK_LEVELS['limit'] = 5, the max_iterations this file has always shipped, so the number of rows, the y of every row (vertical_spacing * (max_iterations - level)) and the hue of every bar (level / max_iterations) are unchanged; gone draws nothing where the middle third was, which is exactly what the artifact has always done, since the middle was simply never created. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` before this pass and is now guarded twice - a word is taken only when it validates AND differs, and _rebuild() fires only after _built - so the 5 existing placements pass no key, reach no rebuild, and grow and fall on their 2-second clock exactly as before.
dna.was: six @export knobs and not one categorical among them: iteration_interval, initial_bar_length, bar_thickness and vertical_spacing are a duration and three sizes, and max_iterations - the @identity's own declared critical_parameter - was unreachable from any map because apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`. Every placement got five removals, on a two-second clock, with the deleted middles absent and unmarked. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the kind of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.note: tick is the halving argument as one ladder, exactly the question zeno_staircase asks. removal is the question Zeno cannot ask: a staircase SUBDIVIDES and keeps everything, Cantor DELETES, and until now the deletion had no representation at all. gone is the shipped silence; ghost restores each removed middle as a pale full-thickness volume, so a row reads as the complete interval with its holes marked and the eye can see measure leaving; scar leaves a thin dark rod at 22 percent of bar depth where the bar used to be, so the row reads as a comb rather than as scattered dust. The thirds arithmetic is shared line for line between the grown and the instant build - offset = L/3, new_length = L/3 - so the axis can never be a fact about which builder ran.
dna.kin: tick is taken from zeno_staircase character for character (once | coarse | fine | dense | limit), the same ladder of subdivision named the same way. TWO THINGS DIFFER AND BOTH ARE FACTS ABOUT THE ARTIFACT, not drift in the word. The rungs are 1,2,3,4,5 rather than Zeno's 1,3,9,27,81; and the shipped value sits at the TOP of the ladder rather than in the middle, so this axis runs one way only - what the record LOSES as you coarsen it. A sixth row would be segments of 12 mm against the bar's own 300 mm depth, a picture of the mesh's minimum feature rather than of Cantor. removal is NOT a family word and deliberately not `evidence`: evidence values withhold parts of an artifact's own working (a caption, a secant, a source marker), while these values ADD back the thing the rule threw away. Withholding an explanation and drawing an absence are opposite moves.
dna.still_note: tick is the strong axis in pixels: once is two bars on a two-row ladder, limit is 32 segments on six rows, and the silhouette changes wholesale. removal is the thinner measurement - ghost adds 31 pale volumes spanning as much width as the survivors and should bite; scar adds 31 thin dark rods against a dark background, so crop-recheck that value before believing an INERT verdict on it. BOTH AXES ARE INVISIBLE WITHOUT THE FIXTURE, and this is the whole reason the token had no usable capture: the shipped artifact grows one row every 2 s and drops every bar with an unfrozen RigidBody3D, so at the sweep's settle there is a single bar in freefall, well below frame. dna.fixture sets build_mode=instant, which lays the completed ladder out frozen inside _ready by the identical thirds rule. This is the library_rack case - config the artifact needs SUPPLIED before any axis can be seen at all - and build_mode is deliberately NOT declared as an axis, because its `grow` value renders as one falling bar and would ship half the sheet as near-blank frames.

dna.default: tick=fine, removal=gone - fine is the SHIPPED RUNG and it short-circuits: it hands back the literal 0.01 width floor rather than deriving one, leaves max_depth at 6 (which is also the denominator of the per-row fade, so no surviving row is repainted) and leaves the status label byte-identical. Verified by re-running both stop conditions in Python over the whole recursion - the shipped `depth > 6 or width < 0.01` and the new `depth > 6 or depth > 3 or width < 0.01` produce the SAME 15 bars at the same 15 positions and widths, because 0.8/3^4 = 0.00988 was already under the floor. gone draws nothing where the middle third was, which is what this file has always done: the middle was simply never created. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` and is now guarded twice - a value is taken only when it validates AND differs, and _rebuild fires only after _built - and all 6 existing placements (Fractal_CantorSet, Fractals_Necklace, Hangar_Fractals, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, Corridor_Fractal_CantorSet, Curation_Bay_fractals_1) carry the bare token with no config keys, so none of them can reach a rebuild.
dna.was: three @export knobs, every one of them a count or a size, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass` - so max_depth, initial_width and vertical_spacing were unreachable from any map token and no placement could differ from any other. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.finding: MAX_DEPTH 6 HAS NEVER BEEN REACHED. The recursion stops on `depth > max_depth OR width < 0.01`, and 0.8/3^4 = 0.00988 trips the floor first, so every placement since this file was written has drawn four rows and fifteen bars rather than seven rows and 127. The shipped number was aspirational, and that is why the default rung is `fine` (3 removals) and not `limit`. Nothing above fine is reachable without relaxing that floor, which _min_width() now does by exactly the amount the requested rung needs and no more - measured: dense 0.00494, limit 0.00165, while once and coarse keep the shipped 0.01 because the level cap stops them long before the floor matters.
dna.kin: tick and removal are cantor_set's two words with cantor_set's own value lists, and TICK_LEVELS is its table copied rung for rung (once 1, coarse 2, fine 3, dense 4, limit 5) - the same ladder of subdivision zeno_staircase names. The ghost colour, the 0.16 alpha, the unshaded flag and the 0.22 scar ratio are lifted unchanged as well, so the two Cantors in this corpus photograph alike and a room can set the physical one and the NOC translation to one rung and expect them to agree. THE DEFAULT DIFFERS AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THE ARTIFACT: cantor_set ships at the TOP of the ladder (limit) and this one ships in the MIDDLE (fine), because its mesh floor cut the recursion off two rungs early. So unlike the sibling's, this axis runs BOTH ways - what the record gains as well as what it loses.
dna.note: removal is the question this file's own @identity already claimed to be about - 'the eye learns to see what is missing, not what remains' - while drawing nothing at all where the middle used to be. gone is that shipped silence. ghost restores each removed third as a pale full-thickness volume, so a row reads as the complete interval with its holes marked and the eye can watch measure leaving; scar leaves a thin dark rod at 22 percent of the bar's section, so the row reads as a comb rather than as scattered dust. Removed middles are drawn only when the row they belong to is itself drawn, so the record's extent - and therefore the capture's union AABB - is identical at all three values and the bite measures the drawing and never the camera.
dna.one_scene_many_names: this .tscn is ALSO the body of `fractal_cantor_set` and of `test_scene_3` in this same registry file - the corpus's most common hidden family, found again here. The axes live on the script, so both siblings inherit them the moment they are placed; only this token carries the declaration, and the other two should be checked before either is promoted separately.
dna.still_note: MEASURED, not assumed: the recursion was re-run in Python at every rung. tick is the strong axis - 3 / 7 / 15 / 31 / 63 bars over 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 rows, so the silhouette changes wholesale and no two rungs come out identical (checked explicitly, because a naive ladder would have made dense and limit the same picture). removal is the thinner measurement: at the default rung it adds 7 volumes totalling 0.563 of drawn length against the 15 survivors' 1.926, so ghost is about 29 percent more drawn material - but at alpha 0.16 and unshaded, so crop-recheck before believing an INERT verdict on it. scar is thinner still, 7 dark rods of 3.3 mm section against a dark background, and is the hardest value in this pair to photograph. At `limit` the narrowest segment is 3.3 mm against a bar section of 15 x 20 mm, which is Cantor dust and deliberately the last rung: the next one would be a picture of the mesh's minimum feature, the same reason cantor_set stopped at five.

dna.default: habit=planar, settlement=live - both no-ops. planar resolves to a roll of exactly 0.0 and the rotation is SKIPPED rather than applied as a zero turn, so _grow_tree hands _rotate_vector the literal Vector3.FORWARD and Vector3.RIGHT it always passed, at every level, and the same randf_range calls run in the same order; live is _ready's original tail line for line (reset the deepest level's velocities, is_separating = true, set_process(true)). rng_seed stays 0, which keeps the shipped randomize(). Nothing in the 3 existing placements changes.
dna.was: the fork always turned about the WORLD axis Vector3.FORWARD and the third branch always leaned out on the WORLD axis Vector3.RIGHT, hard-coded at every level of _grow_tree, so the tree was a flat drawing with one branch out of plane and no way to say otherwise; and the separation phase always ran live, once, over separation_duration seconds per level - 15 s at the shipped values - so the artifact's own truth statement (a canopy is negotiated, not designed) could only be seen by someone standing there for the whole of it.
dna.family: habit is branching_vine's word, its four values and its mechanism - a roll of the branching plane applied at each descent, 0 / 30 / 90 / 137.5 degrees. The table is PRELOADED out of branching_vine.gd rather than retyped, so the two artifacts sharing the word cannot drift into two vocabularies. Deliberately NOT growth_form: branching_coral's five values are coral names (staghorn, fan, table, whip, brain) and taking that word would mean answering it with a list this artifact does not have.
dna.fixture_why: 'stochastic' is the artifact's first name: every fork angle and every child length is a randf_range and _ready calls randomize(). Unseeded, five swept variants are five different trees and the critic would measure the RNG. rng_seed defaults to 0, which is the shipped randomize(), so pinning it is a bench act only.
dna.note: settlement=live is NOT REPRODUCIBLE and that is a fact about the artifact, not the bench: _apply_separation accumulates velocity per FRAME (`branch_a.velocity += force`) and multiplies only the offset by delta, so how far the canopy has opened at capture time depends on the frame rate. settled and grown are both static states and are byte-stable under a fixed seed. The pre-existing frame-rate coupling was left alone - fixing it would change what the 3 placements do.

recursion_observatory.name: Recursion Observatory
recursion_observatory.description: Four recursions held at one rung on four plinths, ordered by D = log(N)/log(s): Cantor 0.63, Koch 1.26, Sierpinski 2.32, Menger 2.73. Each plaque etches the branching factor, the dimension, how many rungs that artifact's own ladder declares, and which of two walls ends it.
recursion_observatory.qfep_connection: F-compression at its limit. Each of these four rules is a complete description of an endless object in one line, which is the highest compression ratio anything in this corpus reaches. What the row exhibits is the part the compression cannot carry: a rule is scale-free and a drawing is not, so every one of them stops, and the rung it stops on is set by the width of the pen or by the instance budget rather than by the mathematics. The residue that will not compress is the apparatus.
recursion_observatory.relationships: Synthesis of [[cantor_set]], [[koch_curve_3d]], [[sierpinski_pyramid]] and [[menger_sponge]] — the four artifacts that share the `tick` word. WHAT THEY LEARNED SEPARATELY: [[cantor_set]] reaches 5 rungs and 32 bars, and stops because a sixth row is 12 mm of segment against its own bar's 300 mm depth. [[koch_curve_3d]] declares 3 rungs and SKIPS n=3, because the bump added at generation n has amplitude 0.076 m against a drawing tube of radius 0.2 m, and iterations 3, 4, 5 and 6 measured as one photograph. [[sierpinski_pyramid]] declares 5 rungs and stops on instance count at the 3125 its @identity names — and it also refused [[cantor_set]]'s `removal` word, because its children's volumes interpenetrate and there is no complement to draw. [[menger_sponge]] declares 3, because each tick multiplies the cube count by 20 and a fourth rung would be 160,000. WHAT ONLY THE ROW CAN SAY: held side by side the ladders run 5, 3, 5, 3 against branching factors 2, 4, 5, 20, and they are NOT ordered by the branching factor. Sierpinski branches faster than Koch and reaches two more rungs. What ends a ladder is whichever wall arrives first — COUNT, where N^n exceeds what can be instanced, or THICKNESS, where extent/s^n falls under the pen that draws it — and which wall that is depends on how the artifact is drawn, not on the rule. None of the four is replaced or moved: each keeps its own drawing here (Cantor its hue-per-level law, Koch its emissive line and its arch head), and all four stay placed in their own maps.

spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 5.90 m, h 1.96 m, registry.measurements)

dna.default: tick=fine — UNCHANGED by the 2026-08-11 deepening, and still the value at which the whole claim is on show at once, now with `dense` one rung above it rather than nothing: at n=3 Cantor and Sierpinski are on rung 3 of a 5-rung ladder and still climbing, Koch is on the last rung its own file will draw, and the Menger plinth is HELD at n=2 with its plaque saying so, because its third rung is 8000 leaves. `once` and `coarse` are the same row earlier. Nothing is preserved by this choice and nothing can be regressed by it — this artifact has no shipped placements, so the default is a free design choice, and this is the strongest single reading.
dna.was: synthesized from cantor_set, koch_curve_3d, sierpinski_pyramid and menger_sponge — four separate promotions, each of which declared `tick`, stopped its ladder at a different rung, and wrote the reason into its own registry note where no one can stand in front of it.
dna.kin: `tick` is the word all four sources share, and the only word all four share, so it is the only word this row takes. FOUR RUNGS since 2026-08-11: once | coarse | fine | dense, all four names taken character for character from cantor_set's and sierpinski_pyramid's five-rung table. IT SHIPPED WITH THREE, on the argument that three is the INTERSECTION — the deepest rung every member can honestly be shown at — and that `dense` would be menger_sponge's example_8_4 fault one level up, a rung two members cannot reach. THAT ARGUMENT WAS HALF RIGHT AND IT WAS ALREADY BEING BROKEN BY THE OBJECT ITSELF. At `fine` the Menger plinth is held at n=2 and its plaque reads HELD, because 20^3 is 8000 leaves; the `room` cap and the HELD line exist for exactly that case. example_8_4's fault is a value that falls back SILENTLY. A plinth that stands at its cap and prints the count it would have needed is the opposite of a silent fallback — it is the exhibit, and three rungs only let it happen once. At four it happens twice, on two different plinths, for the two DIFFERENT walls: Menger on COUNT at fine, Koch on THICKNESS at dense (a fourth-rung segment is 1.602/3^4 = 0.020 m long against this row's 0.024 m pen), while Cantor and Sierpinski, whose own ladders are five rungs, climb past both. That is the row's whole claim — the ladder lengths are not ordered by the branching factor — turned from a sentence on a plaque into a sequence you can step through. `limit` (n=5) IS STILL DECLINED and the reason is now a different one: at five rungs only Cantor still moves (Koch held at 3, Sierpinski held at 4 because 5^5 is 3125 leaves on top of Menger's 400 and past this row's own budget, Menger held at 2), so three quarters of the object would stop answering the axis. An exhibit that makes its point by ceasing to be an exhibit has made a different point. ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE SOURCES' USE OF THE WORD, deliberate and on the record: here `tick` names the RULE-APPLICATION COUNT n and nothing else, matched across the four, because n is the only quantity comparable between a thirds rule and a 3x3x3 lattice. koch_curve_3d's own `fine` is n=4, its table skipping 3 because 3 and 4 measured as one photograph at its shipped 0.2 m line width; this row's third rung is n=3 for everybody, and it can show n=3 on Koch because it draws with a 0.012 m segment against a 1.02 m span rather than 0.2 m against 4.71 m. The wall is a property of the drawing, which is the row's whole thesis, so moving it is allowed as long as it is said out loud.
dna.note: Four plinths on one base, ordered left to right by D — 0.63, 1.26, 2.32, 2.73 — with a dimension rail along the front running 0 to 3 and a marker under each member's true D. The plinths are evenly spaced and the markers are not: Sierpinski and Menger are close neighbours in dimension while Cantor sits below one, and the mismatch between even spacing and true dimension is the row's second reading. Each plaque carries four lines: the name; N, s and D; how many rungs that artifact's own ladder declares and which wall ends it; and the rung this row holds it at, with the leaf count. THE LADDER LENGTHS ARE READ, NOT TYPED — `LADDER n RUNGS` is TICK_LEVELS.size() off each source's own script through a preload, which is slot_machine's pattern, so the four cannot drift from what this row claims about them. THE FOUR RULES ARE DRAWN HERE, NOT INSTANCED: cantor_set grows a row every 2 s and drops its bars with unfrozen RigidBody3D, menger_sponge subdivides on a 1 s clock and every leaf it makes is a cube_scene carrying a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D, and both needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before a still could see them at all. A row of four cannot afford four fixtures and four hundred colliders, so each rule is re-implemented as plain MeshInstance3D boxes out of the source's own arithmetic: Cantor's thirds and its Color.from_hsv(level/max_iterations, 0.8, 0.9) hue law, Koch's four-point iteration and its `head = arch` mapping line for line, Menger's 3x3x3 lattice. Menger's keep set is DERIVED rather than copied — drop every sub-cube with two or more centre coordinates — and that rule was checked against the source's keep_positions table and reproduces it exactly, removing 4, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16 and 22. The lattice index is built from three nested loops because the source computed it as i % 3, (i / 3) % 3 and i / 9.0, and that last float divide is the one character that meant the shipped object was not a Menger sponge.
dna.finding: SIERPINSKI_PYRAMID BRANCHES BY SIX, NOT FIVE, AND ITS OWN MEASUREMENT PROVES IT. SierpinskiPyramid.gd's _recursive_build makes SIX recursive calls: a `# Top` at pos + (0, half_size, 0) on line 109, a second `# Top` at pos + (0, offset, 0) on line 174 where offset = half_size / 2, and then the four bottoms. Its @identity says 'pyramid(depth) = 5 * pyramid(depth-1)', its DNA note says 'each increment multiplies complexity by 5, from 5 cubes to 3125', and its registry entry says 'all 625 leaves land on the same coordinates' and 'limit builds 3125 static bodies where the shipped depth builds 625'. Re-implemented in Python from the file and run at every depth, the six-call recursion gives 6, 36, 216, 1296, 7776 leaves and an AABB at depth 4 of 8.50 x 12.25 x 8.50 with centre y 1.88 — which is that entry's own measured aabb_size and aabb_center, to the centimetre. The five-child rule gives 8.50 x 8.50 x 8.50 with centre y 0.00, and does not. So the shipped depth builds 1296 cube_scene instances rather than 625, and the declared `limit` rung builds 7776 static bodies rather than 3125 — 2.5x the frame that entry's still_note already flagged as the one that could trip the 16-second watchdog, and its COUNT wall arrives correspondingly sooner than it says. NOT REPAIRED HERE: the fix changes what six live placements draw, which is that artifact's own pass and not a synthesis's business. This row draws the rule the artifact ARGUES — five copies at half scale, apex plus four base corners — and etches that. A SECOND, SMALLER MISMATCH in the same entry: its `packing` note reads 'the Sierpinski tetrahedron has Hausdorff dimension exactly 2', which is the FOUR-child tetrix. A five-child square-based pyramid at half scale has D = log 5 / log 2 = 2.3219, and 2.32 is the number on the plinth.
dna.declines:
`removal` REFUSED. cantor_set and menger_sponge share it (gone | ghost | scar) and it is the obvious second axis to reach for — and it fits only two of the four members. sierpinski_pyramid already refused it and was right to, its children's bounding volumes interpenetrating so that there is no complement to draw; and koch_curve_3d has no complement at all, because the Koch rule takes the middle third and hands back two sides of a triangle, so the drawn figure is continuous and nothing anywhere is missing from it. Declaring `removal` across this row would be folding_past's fault exactly — taking a word without its answers on half the objects it is applied to.

`packing` REFUSED for the opposite reason: it is applicable everywhere and means a different thing in each place. On sierpinski_pyramid the leaf is an atom sitting on a lattice cell of known spacing, and shrinking it withdraws a claim about MEASURE the drawing was making by accident. On Cantor the surviving segment IS the set — shrinking it does not reveal a point cloud, it draws a different fractal. Same word, two questions.

A TEXT AXIS REFUSED ON A MEASUREMENT rather than on taste. `evidence`, the corpus's most-shared word, would suit an observatory well — how much of its own arithmetic the apparatus shows — and it cannot be photographed here. The five plaques and the rail caption together cover roughly 0.30 m2 of a 6.36 m fit-by-diagonal frame, about 0.7% of it, and only a fraction of that is glyph. The strongest possible swap of every word on the object lands under the 2% bite floor, so declaring it would ship a finished-looking experiment that answers nothing, which is info_board's fault.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and this is worth saying rather than leaving blank: there is no clock, no RigidBody3D, no @tool path and no randf() in the file, so _ready lays the finished row out in one frame and it never moves again. Both cantor_set and menger_sponge needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before any axis of theirs was visible at all; this one needs nothing supplied.
dna.still_note:
`tick` changes three plinths of four and DELIBERATELY LEAVES THE FOURTH ALONE between coarse and fine. That identity is the exhibit and not a fault: Menger's third rung is 8000 leaves, so the row holds it at n=2 and its plaque reads HELD - n=3 IS 8000. An INERT reading of that quadrant is the finding arriving on schedule.

THE FRAME NUMBER WILL LOOK THIN AND THE FOCUS NUMBER WILL NOT, and the gap is geometric. Estimated by mirroring this file's constants in Python and rasterising a front elevation at 1400 px across the fit-by-diagonal frame with every box filled and outlined — a boolean silhouette XOR is the WRONG metric for this family and reports 0.73% for a frame that changes wholesale, because self-similarity is exactly the claim that the outline does not change:

    n=1 -> n=2    frame 1.34%    focus (hottest 5%) 26.7%
    n=2 -> n=3    frame 0.59%    focus (hottest 5%) 11.9%
    n=1 -> n=3    frame 1.83%    focus (hottest 5%) 36.7%

So the axis clears the 3% focus floor by 4x at its weakest step and clears 2% of frame at no step at all. THAT IS DILUTION, the known trap: the changing part is four small densely textured volumes inside a 5.90 m row, and the subject covers 10-12% of frame at every rung. Crop-recheck per plinth before believing anything measured frame-wide. These are estimates from an orthographic elevation and not the bench, which is perspective from a raised angle; its numbers will differ.

The union AABB is 5.90 x 1.96 x 1.34 m and is IDENTICAL at all three rungs, because every fractal's extent is held constant while its texture changes — so the fixed camera fits all three variants equally and no value is photographed from further away. Element count is about 55, 471 and 627 meshes at once, coarse and fine, every one a plain MeshInstance3D with no collision and no MultiMesh, well inside the 3200 budget; the 400 Menger leaves are the bulk of it at both coarse and fine. dna.framing IS NOW DECLARED AT 0.52, and the sentence that used to stand here — that the diagonal is only 8% over the width, so fit-by-diagonal is nearly fit-by-width and anything below 1.0 would crop the end plinths — WAS WRONG, in a way worth naming because other entries reason the same way. It omitted PAD. The rig computes dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with PAD = 1.9, so at framing 1.0 the visible HALF-extent is 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius and the row was only ever going to fill about half the frame width, before any sparseness. Measured, the subject came in at 5.48%. The arithmetic, done properly: AABB 5.90 x 2.02 x 1.34 (identical at all four rungs, since every envelope is held constant), diagonal 6.38, radius 3.19, so the visible half-extent is 6.06 * framing; at the sweep standpoint the row projects to a half-width of 2.79 m, which at framing 0.52 fills 89% of the half-frame with no clipping and puts the subject near 20% of frame instead of 5.5%. That alone should multiply every pairwise number by about 3.7 without touching a single piece of geometry.

WHERE TO MEASURE `dense`. fine -> dense moves TWO plinths of four (Cantor 4 rows -> 5, and because the stack height is held the existing rows all shift as well; Sierpinski 125 leaves -> 625 at half the leaf pitch) and leaves Koch and Menger identical by construction, both HELD and both saying so. It is expected to be the closest pair, around 1.2-1.4% after the framing fix against 0.45% for coarse -> fine before it. An INERT reading of the Koch or Menger quadrant at that step is the finding arriving on schedule and must not be filed as a dead axis — crop to the Cantor and Sierpinski plinths and measure there. ALL THE NUMBERS IN THIS PARAGRAPH ARE ESTIMATES: captures are serialised centrally and none was run for this pass. Re-run tools/verify_batch.py --tokens=recursion_observatory to replace them.
dna.deepened: 2026-08-11. MEASURED FIRST: closest pair 0.446% (coarse vs fine) at a subject share of 5.48%, under the 6% floor, so framing was the first suspect and it was the right one — see still_note for the PAD arithmetic the original framing reasoning omitted. Two changes. (1) dna.framing 0.52, derived, no geometry touched. (2) A FOURTH RUNG, `dense`, which is the deepening the object actually needed: the row argues that four ladders end at different rungs for two different reasons, and with three rungs exactly one of them was ever seen to end. The `room` cap and the HELD plaque line already existed for that case and were used once; `dense` uses them twice, for both walls, on two plinths, while the two five-rung members climb past. Supporting change: the Cantor stack height is now held at 0.90 m with the row pitch as 0.90/rung, which is exactly the 0.30 m this file shipped with at rung 3, so the default's GEOMETRY is unchanged mesh for mesh and the union AABB stays identical at every rung. DEFAULT PRESERVATION, said plainly: tick=fine is still the default, every body it builds is in the same place at the same size as before this pass, and the single difference anywhere in that frame is two words of plaque text - the Menger tail now reads HELD ON COUNT rather than HELD. `once` and `coarse` DO change, because the Cantor stack no longer shrinks with the rung; there are zero placements so nothing regressed, but that is a change and it is not being called a preservation; and the HELD line now computes the count at the row's rung rather than multiplying the shown count once, which was only correct when the gap was a single rung. At tick=dense the Menger plaque reads HELD ON COUNT - n=4 IS 160000. The per-member caps also stopped being hand-typed guesses: Cantor 5 (never binds), Koch 3 on THICKNESS (its fourth-rung segment is 0.020 m against a 0.024 m pen, computed), Sierpinski 4 on COUNT (5^5 = 3125 on top of Menger's 400 is past this row's budget), Menger 2 on COUNT. Element count at dense is about 63 + 64 + 625 + 400 bodies plus furniture, roughly 1170, well inside the 3200 budget — which is why `limit` was declined rather than being the obvious next rung.
dna.framing_why: DERIVED, and it corrects a reasoning error rather than a taste. The union AABB is 5.90 x 2.02 x 1.34 m and is identical at all four rungs, diagonal 6.38, radius 3.19. The rig computes dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing at FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, and PAD is the part the original note left out: at framing 1.0 the visible HALF-extent is 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, so the row was only ever going to fill about half the frame width even before its own sparseness. It measured 5.48 percent of frame. The visible half-extent is 6.06 * framing; at the sweep standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) the row projects to a half-width of 2.79 m and a half-height of 1.15 m, so 0.52 puts the width at 89 percent of the half-frame and the height at 37 percent, with no clipping and no plaque outside the frame (the widest Label3D sits at x 2.37 against a mesh edge at 2.95). Expected subject share about 20 percent.

dna.default: tick=fine, head=arch - fine SHORT-CIRCUITS: _levels() hands back the shipped `iterations` rather than the table's 4, which matters because the @export default is 4 and a scene is free to override it, and deriving the rung from the table would silently retune it. arch returns the original map_to_arch body line for line - the same PI * (1 - t) angle, the same portal_width/2 radius, the same point.z * 0.5 radial offset - and never touches the new head-curve code at all. rotation_speed stays 0.0, line_width stays the .tscn's 0.2, depth_layers stays 6. All 3 placements (Fractal_KochSierpinski at 'koch_curve_3d:0:-0.5', Corridor_Fractal_KochSierpinski, RecursiveEmergence_Iterated_Function_Systems_IFS) carry the bare token with no config keys, so apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` before this pass - reaches no assignment and never rebuilds. THE AXIS DEFAULTS PRESERVE THE GEOMETRY EXACTLY; the SCENE SHAPE changed and is a repair, see `finding`.
dna.was: eight @export knobs and not one categorical among them - a count, five lengths, a spacing and a rotation rate - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`. Worse than unreachable: the script was not on the scene root at all, so no map token could address it by any route. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the kind of knob and about the scene shape, not about the artifact.
dna.finding: TWO DEFECTS, both older than this promotion. (1) THE SCRIPT WAS NOT ON THE ROOT. KochCurve3D.tscn was [Main] (unscripted Node3D) with the script on a KochCurve3D child alongside the camera and the light. GridInteractablesComponent sets config_* metadata and calls apply_grid_config on the ROOT (line 1672), so `iterations` - which this artifact's own @identity names as its critical_parameter - has never been reachable from a map, and the README's documented usage `portal.iterations = 5` on the instantiated scene has never done anything. The script now sits on the root, carrying the four overrides the child held (line_width 0.2, portal_width 3.0, depth_layers 6, layer_spacing 0.2) at the child's identity transform, so the drawn geometry is unchanged to the millimetre. (2) THE FRACTAL SATURATES TWO GENERATIONS BELOW WHAT IT SHIPS. Every segment is a cylinder of radius line_width = 0.2 m; the bump added at generation n has amplitude (4.71 / 3^n) * sqrt(3)/2 * 0.5, which is 0.076 m at n=3 and 0.025 m at n=4. Measured by re-implementing the geometry in Python and rasterising the tube union at the sweep's framing: against the shipped iterations=4, iteration 3 differs by 0.27% of frame and iteration 5 by 0.03%. Iterations 3, 4, 5 and 6 are one photograph. The three maps are paying for 2304 cylinders to draw a picture 144 of them already made. Nothing was changed about it - a smaller line_width would be a regression on three live rooms - but the ladder is declared honestly around it.
dna.kin: tick is cantor_set's, zeno_staircase's, sierpinski_pyramid's, cube_subdivision's and menger_sponge's word, and once | coarse | fine are the first three of the family's five names character for character. THE LADDER STOPS AT THREE FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT MENGER'S, and the difference is the point. Menger stops because each tick multiplies its cube count by 20. Koch's multiplies by only 4, so 4^5 = 1024 arch segments is affordable - what stops this ladder is THE LINE THICKNESS, a fact about how the artifact is drawn rather than about the rule it draws. The integers behind the names are this artifact's own (1, 2, 4), and 3 is SKIPPED rather than named, because measurement put it 0.27% from the shipped rung: declaring `dense` and `limit` here would be the example_8_4 fault, rungs that exist in the enum and cannot be told apart. head is a NEW word and deliberately not koch_curve's `evidence`: the 2D sibling asks what a finished figure shows of its own iteration, which is a question about teaching. This one is a DOORWAY, and its question is which architecture the curve is bent into - arcuated, trabeated, pitched or funicular. Taking `evidence` would have meant answering a question this object does not ask.
dna.note: head is the artifact's own claim made variable. Its @identity has always said the Koch bumps 'become architectural ornament', and until now the architecture was one hard-coded semicircle. Every value maps the IDENTICAL Koch point list and throws the IDENTICAL point.z * 0.5 displacement; only the curve the points lie on, and the outward normal they are displaced along, change. All four share the springing points at (+/- portal_width/2, leg_height) so the legs meet the head exactly, and all but lintel share the crown at leg_height + portal_width/2, so this is a curvature axis and not a size axis. lintel is the one that drops the crown by 1.5 m, and it is the honest degenerate case: the fractal admitted to be ornament on a straight beam.
dna.still_note: head is the strong axis and is legible by construction - a static silhouette, complete at frame zero. Measured on a rasterised tube union at the union framing: lintel 15.2%, gable 8.8%, catenary 4.1% of frame against arch, and no pair of the four closer than 4.1%. tick is the thinner measurement and the numbers are stated so no one has to guess: once is 7.4% from the shipped rung and coarse is 1.9%, so COARSE SITS JUST UNDER THE 2% BITE FLOOR and should be crop-rechecked before anyone believes an INERT verdict on it - it is thin for the reason in `finding`, not because the rule does nothing. dna.framing is 0.5 because the union AABB is roughly 4.8 x 4.1 x 1.2 m of very thin tubing: at framing 1.0 the sweep would photograph a 12 m frame for a 4.8 m subject and the lit pixels would be about 3% of it.
dna.declines: line_width, portal_width, leg_height, depth_layers and layer_spacing stay plain exports: they are sizes, and a size axis is the thing this loop exists not to ship. rotation_speed is time-domain and invisible to a still. portal_height is DEAD - nothing reads it, the crown has always been derived from portal_width - and it was deliberately not repurposed, because giving a dead export meaning changes what a scene that sets it draws.

dna.default: tick=coarse, removal=gone - coarse SHORT-CIRCUITS: _levels() hands back the shipped max_iterations rather than the table's 2, so a scene that overrides the count in the inspector is not silently retuned by this promotion. gone draws nothing where the seven cross-cubes were, which is what this file has always done, because the removed positions were simply never built. build_mode stays grow, so the sponge still subdivides once per subdivision_interval second on the same clock. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` and is now guarded twice - a word is taken only when it validates AND differs, and _rebuild() fires only after _built - so the nine placements pass no key, reach no assignment and never rebuild. THE AXIS DEFAULTS PRESERVE AND THE ARTIFACT DOES NOT: two defects were repaired in this pass and they DO change what those nine maps draw. See `finding`. Both are repairs toward the object this entry, the README, the @identity and the file's own comments have always described, and neither is reachable as an axis value.
dna.finding: TWO DEFECTS, both older than this promotion, both repaired here. (1) THIS WAS NOT A MENGER SPONGE. `var z = i / 9.0` is a FLOAT divide, so the z layer index of the 3x3x3 lattice came back as 0, 1/9, 2/9 ... 26/9 instead of 0, 1, 2. The twenty kept sub-cubes were smeared along z at ninth-of-a-cell offsets and ran from z=-3 to z=+5.67 against a parent spanning -4.5 to +4.5 - which is why this entry's own footprint reads 10 deep on a 9 m cube. x and y were computed correctly and the keep_positions table is correct (it removes exactly {4,10,12,13,14,16,22}, the six face centres and the body centre), so the entire fault was one character, and the three orthogonal corridors the @identity promises never existed. The fix makes the object SMALLER in z and never larger, so no placement can gain a collision from it. (2) IT ATE ITS NEIGHBOURS. find_all_cube_scenes() walked get_tree().current_scene - the whole map - and matched any node named CubeScene* or InitialCube or instanced from cube_scene.tscn. GridSystem.gd holds exactly such a node at $CubeScene (line 69), hides it, duplicates it to build the floor and re-acquires it BY NAME on reload; a dozen other artifacts are built from the same primitive, cube_subdivision and sierpinski_pyramid among them. Every one of those was subdivided into twenty pieces and the original freed, once per second, in any map holding this token. The walk now starts at `self`.
dna.was: three @export knobs and not one categorical among them: subdivision_interval is a duration, max_iterations a count, auto_start a flag - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so max_iterations, which the @identity names as this artifact's critical_parameter, was unreachable from any map token. Every placement got two iterations on a one-second clock. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.kin: tick is cantor_set's and sierpinski_pyramid's word, and once | coarse | fine are the first three of their five value names character for character. THE LADDER STOPS AT THREE AND THE SHORTNESS IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN ARGUMENT, not drift in the word: every Menger tick multiplies the cube count by TWENTY, so the rungs are 20, 400 and 8000 cube_scene instances and a fourth would be 160,000, each carrying a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D. Cantor reaches five rungs at 32 bars because its rule multiplies by 2, and Sierpinski at 3125 because its multiplies by 5. D = log(20)/log(3) = 2.727 is exactly why this ladder is short, so declaring dense and limit would be the example_8_4 fault - rungs that exist in the enum and cannot be built. The shipped value sits in the MIDDLE of what remains, so this ladder runs both ways. removal is cantor_set's word with its three values, its ghost colour, its 0.16 alpha, its unshaded flag and its 0.22 scar ratio lifted unchanged, so the 1D and 3D removal fractals photograph alike. sierpinski_pyramid REFUSED this same word and was right to: its five children's bounding volumes interpenetrate and there was no complement to draw. Menger's 27 sub-cubes partition the parent exactly - no overlap, no gap - so here the complement is a real set and ghost can put it back.
dna.note: removal is this artifact's own truth made drawable. 'A solid made entirely of holes' has until now been argued by an object with nothing at all where the holes are. gone is that silence. ghost restores each deleted cross-cube as a pale full-size volume, so the sponge reads as the whole cube with its subtractions marked and the eye can watch volume leave at every scale at once; scar leaves a small dark core at 22 percent of the cell, so the holes read as a lattice of markers rather than as empty air. build_mode is deliberately NOT an axis and is the fixture instead, for cantor_set's reason: the shipped artifact subdivides once per second, so a still taken at boot holds ONE 9 m cube and the whole of tick is invisible to it. `instant` runs the identical subdivide call inside _ready, carrying the frontier list forward explicitly rather than re-scanning, because queue_free does not take effect until the end of the frame and a second scan within one _ready would find the already-subdivided originals again.
dna.still_note: tick is the strong axis: 20 / 400 / 8000 cubes at 3 m, 1 m and 0.333 m inside an unchanged 9 m envelope, so under fit-to-AABB framing the silhouette holds while the texture inside it changes wholesale - which is the point, since self-similarity is exactly the claim that the outline does not change. COST WARNING for whoever runs the sweep: `fine` builds 8000 cube_scene instances, each with a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D, which is 2.5x the frame sierpinski_pyramid already flagged as the one that could trip the 16-second watchdog. It is built inside _ready, so it falls under the 45 s boot grace rather than the 16 s stall timer; if it still trips, the fix is the grace and not a shorter ladder. With removal=ghost that same frame adds 2947 translucent boxes on top of it. removal is the thinner measurement and should be judged at once or coarse before an INERT verdict is believed at fine, where the outer ghosts overlay the inner survivors.
dna.declines: subdivision_interval stays a plain export: a rate is invisible to a still, and it is the thing the fixture exists to step around rather than a thing to declare. auto_start stays a flag - its false value renders as one bare cube, which is half a sheet of near-blank frames for no argument.

dna.default: grammar=warren, depth=3 - warren is the pair of productions this file used to hold in two plain vars (axiom F, F -> F+RF-FF-FR+F, R -> RFRFRF) and _resolve_grammar writes them back verbatim, while depth 3 is the number the old `iterations` export shipped with. The turtle has no randomness at all, so identical inputs give an identical picture; apply_grid_config rebuilds only when a value actually changed and only after _ready has built once, and none of the placements (LSystems_Architecture, the two curation_station bays, the two Mission maps) sends any config. Nothing in the corpus moves.
dna.was: one grammar, hard-coded. `_axiom` and `_rules` were ordinary vars holding a single pair of productions with no export and no config key, so the only thing about this artifact that was ever variable was how many times its one grammar got rewritten - and the registry description ('corridors and rooms emerge from string rewriting') was describing a rewrite nobody could rewrite. `depth` is the old `iterations` export under the word the rest of the L-system family already uses.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03, the lsystem_editor case a second time: the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS while a whole parameter space sat in the source as two string literals. NOT SEEDED, and it does not need to be - grep the file for randf/randi/noise and there is nothing; the turtle is deterministic, so a variant is a fact and not a sample. The three new grammars were written against the turtle this file already interprets (F forward, R room at the current point, +/- 90 degrees, [ ] push/pop) and each argues a different PLAN TOPOLOGY, which is what a top-down floor plan is for: warren a dense net, spiral a coil of growing runs, branch the only one that touches the stack and comes out a corridor TREE, meander the quadratic-Koch single crenellated hall. depth is declared 1-4 and not 1-5 although the code range is 1-5: warren multiplies F sixfold per rewrite, so depth 5 is roughly 7,800 corridor slabs and 15,600 wall slabs as separate MeshInstance3D nodes, which is a capture-time hazard rather than a picture.
dna.kin: lsystem_editor.grammar and lsystem_editor.depth ask exactly these two questions in the same sequence and the words are taken from there unchanged. The VALUE lists are not shared and should not be: lsystem_editor's seven are botanical and fractal curves (koch, plant, fern), and naming a dungeon plan 'fern' would make two artifacts look like siblings that measure alike when they do not. space_filling_curve_gallery.depth names its samples (sketch|sparse|standard|fine) because it draws one fixed curve at four settings; here, as in lsystem_editor, the honest unit is the rewrite itself.
