branching_coral.description: Marine L-system coral colony — multiple shoots with wide branching angles produce organic fan and staghorn forms. Color gradient from deep purple-brown base to bright pink coral tips on a rock base.
branching_coral.name: Branching Coral

dna.default: growth_form=staghorn, condition=living - staghorn IS the shipped build, value for value: its rules are the old CORAL_RULES strings unchanged, angle_scale and decay_scale are 1.0 so current_angle stays base_angle and decay stays length_decay, and spread 0.6 / out 0.3 / lift 1.0 are the literals that were baked into _grow_shoot's shoot_angle and base_dir. living returns [base_color, Color(0.8, 0.35, 0.3), tip_color], the third of which was a local named mid_color inside _draw_coral. So both existing placements (LSystems_Competition at (6,4), LSystems_Living at (2,6), plus the three curation_station rosters that list the token) draw the identical colony.
dna.was: no enum export at all. One grammar: CORAL_RULES was a const read directly by _grow_shoot, the fork angle was base_angle alone, the shoot fan was the literals 0.6 and 0.3, and the depth ramp was base_color -> a local mid_color -> tip_color. Every knob that existed (iterations, num_shoots, base_angle, length_decay, display_size) turned the SIZE of one fixed coral; nothing turned the coral into a different coral. apply_grid_config also called _generate() unconditionally, so any config pass redrew the mesh.
dna.note: growth_form is the grammar, not the scale - a different production read by the same turtle, off a differently tilted holdfast. fan drops the roll symbols so branching stays in the shoot's own plane and the shoots barely spread (one surface held into the current); table tilts the holdfast almost flat and throws the shoots right around, growing sideways for light instead of upward for height; whip runs long between rare forks; brain pushes the fork angle past 60 degrees, which folds each branch back over itself so the colony closes into a mound instead of opening into a thicket. condition turns what the colour gradient REPORTS. In this artifact the purple-brown-to-pink ramp is a readout of recursion depth - a segment's colour says how deep in the grammar it sits. bleached does not reshape one branch; it deletes that readout, so the colony is still there and no longer says where it is. fluorescent and encrusted re-key the same three stops without touching the geometry, which makes the pair separable: growth_form moves the lines, condition moves only their colour.
dna.kin: growth_form, not form. branching_growth_algorithm, recursive_tree and space_colonization_algorithm already spend the bare word `form` as a VALUE of their staging axis `aftermath`, and reusing it as an axis NAME here would have made the family's vocabulary ambiguous in the one place it is meant to be shared. No sibling in the corpus declares growth_form or condition, so both words are new rather than borrowed-and-bent.
dna.fixture_note: no fixture is needed. The colony was already fully determined - _ready seeds the rng at 77 and every shoot reseeds to 77 + shoot_idx * 13 before it draws - so two values of an axis differ by the axis and nothing else. The literal 77 is now the var _base_seed, which also makes the pre-existing but dead `seed` config key actually reach the geometry (it used to set _rng.seed only to have _grow_shoot overwrite it on the next line); no placed token passes seed, so nothing shipped moves.
dna.reads: the .tscn root is the scripted node (branching_coral.gd, class_name BranchingCoral) so both axes are reachable from a map token and from the sweep. apply_grid_config accepts growth_form (or form) and condition, IGNORES an unknown value instead of assigning it - a silent fallback to the default is how a sweep publishes N identical frames and calls the axis inert - and rebuilds only when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once.

dna.default: pressure=none - a pure no-op. _evolve() returns on its first line when pressure is "none", so _dna is still CritterDNA.random_kingdom(0, dna_seed) with dna_seed at its shipped -1, which is byte-for-byte the old CritterDNA.random_kingdom(0) call (the parameter's own default is -1, so the same unseeded randomize runs). _build_ui builds the same eight-slider rack at the same position and rotation, the same pedestal, and _rebuild_tree calls TreeMorphology.build(_dna, _tree_root, _mapper, 2) unchanged. All five placements (LSystems_Living, Corridor_LSystems_Living, Curation_Bay_lsystems_2, AutoGenTest, AutoGenTest2) are bare tokens passing none of these keys, and apply_grid_config now regrows only when a value actually DIFFERS and only after _ready has built once - the shipped version regrew the whole tree on the mere presence of dna_seed.
dna.was: no axis and no exports at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The entry claims 'genetic algorithm selection' and there was no selection in the script: _ready drew one unseeded random genome and built it, so the picture in every room was always generation 0 - the thing evolution starts from, standing in for the thing evolution produces. The eight sliders are a designer's hand, and a still cannot photograph a hand moving.
dna.note: pressure states in the geometry WHAT the genome was selected for, which is the argument the name has been making without evidence: selection is never for better, it is always for something, and one ancestor under four tastes grows four incompatible trees. reach = deep recursion, narrow forks, no droop. spread = wide forks, many branches, tropism. thicket = deep, many-forked, heavily leaved. spare = shallow, two-forked, bare, fast taper. Each is a seeded greedy hill-climb over the SAME eight genes the sliders expose - mutate, score, keep if better, `generations` times - so an evolved tree is always a tree a player could also have dialled by hand, and the search is deterministic given dna_seed. GENERATIONS IS DELIBERATELY NOT AN AXIS: convergence is asymptotic, a gen-20 and a gen-40 climb under one taste land on the same tree, and the upper rungs of a generation ladder would be identical frames dressed as an experiment. Its bottom rung is pressure=none already. REBUILD_COOLDOWN is not an axis either - a 0.3 s debounce is time-domain and invisible to a still.
dna.kin: `selection` (drift|uniform|culled|runaway|split, four declarations: evolved_creatures, evolving_flowers, evolvingflowers, non_teleological_evolution) was handed to this artifact and DECLINED. It asks the right question - what a pressure did, and whether any was applied - and its first rung, the unselected shipped default, maps onto this one exactly. But three of its five values are POPULATION pictures: culled is three survivors on a sixteen-plot grid with thirteen plots bare, split is two incompatible tastes filling opposite halves of a 20 m plane, uniform is sixteen copies of one optimum. This artifact is a workbench with ONE tree on a 0.6 m pedestal - its identity is 'design a tree's genome, watch it grow live' - and turning it into a bed of sixteen would make it a second evolving_flowers rather than a sculptor. Taking the word with a different value list is the exact failure check_dna_declarations exists to catch, so the word was left alone. pressure is a new word: same question asked of one genome instead of a population, and the two should NOT be expected to measure alike. lsystem_editor.grammar and lsystem_tree.evidence/habit were also considered and are about which rule is run and how much of it is shown, which this artifact does not vary at all.
dna.fixture_note: TWO things the sweep must be given or the axis is unmeasurable. bench=bare omits the eight-slider control rack; the rack sits at (0, 0.85, 1.2) rotated -25 degrees and the registry's own measurement of this token is aabb 4.91 x 22.68 x 0.08, i.e. a flat panel, so an AABB-fitted camera frames the furniture and photographs the tree at a few pixels. dna_seed=7 pins the ancestor: CritterDNA.random_kingdom(0) is unseeded by default, and five variants of an unseeded generative artifact are five different trees rather than five pictures of one search. bench is a String enum and not a bool on purpose - a typed bool export rejects a fixture string before _ready. generations=24 is the script default restated so the fixture reads as a complete statement of the bench.
dna.measurement_risk: TreeMorphology seeds its own rng from root.get_instance_id(), which differs per instantiation, and that seed gates leaf PRESENCE (rng.randf() < leaf_chance) and per-branch material variation. The branch skeleton is fully determined by the DNA and is clean; the foliage carries per-variant noise that no seed reachable from this artifact can pin. thicket and spare therefore push depth and fork count as hard as they push leaf_density, so both differ structurally and not only in leaves. Leaves are also batched into a MultiMeshInstance3D, which the capture AABB does not count - the frame is set by the branch tubes. Do not read a faint thicket/spare pair as a dead axis without looking at the silhouettes.
dna.still_note: every value is standing geometry decided before the first frame. The only motion in the artifact is the 0.3 s slider debounce in _process and the 0.3 s PLANT tween, neither of which runs with no player in the scene.

dna.default: odds=0.5, alphabet=diagonals - 0.5 is the literal `_rng.randf() < 0.5` fair coin and diagonals returns the same box at the same rotation.z = +/-PI*0.25, so all 7 placements weave exactly the cloth they wove before; apply_grid_config is now guarded and rebuilds only on a real change (it previously tore the loom down on every call, and on a pre-_ready call it built the bolt twice)
dna.was: a hard-coded fair coin between two hard-coded +/-45 degree bars. The only exports were cols and rows - the size of the bolt, not what it says.
dna.fixture_note: weave_seed pins the flip so five odds tiles differ by their bias and not by five different draws; weaving false freezes the scroll so a still is one cloth rather than one mid-scroll frame. Both default to the shipped behaviour (seed 0 = randomize, weaving on).
dna.vocabulary_note: alphabet is taken from GeneticProgramming.alphabet - the symbol set a generator draws from - which is precisely the question here. odds is a new word: bias was already spent on pixel_cloud for a spatial lean (rise/none/spire/sprawl) and chance on random_cubes for WHICH property is randomised, neither of which is the weighting of a coin. panel_bridge_loom's threading_draw / treadling_order were considered and declined: those name a deterministic weaving draft, and this loom's whole content is that there is no draft, only a flip.
dna.declined: scroll rate and row cadence (_step 0.18 s) are time-domain and invisible to a still; cols and rows are size.

ten_print_textile.name: Ten Print Textile (fabric loom)
ten_print_textile.description: A tool: 10 PRINT as a textile loom, weaving an endless bolt of slash/backslash fabric - the pattern doing a design job.

grid_substrate_runner.description: Integrated substrate component — single-cell artifact that mounts visibility (and optionally colour) mutators on the MAP'S existing GridMultiMesh. Same integration shape as gridcolorizer: doesn't build its own multimesh, finds the floor that's already there. Cycles Wolfram CA, fractal, and BFS-frontier expressions on the actual cubes the player walks. Floor-plan SPAWN_LARGEST keeps reachability honest.
grid_substrate_runner.name: Grid Substrate Runner
grid_substrate_runner.qfep_connection: the substrate mount — a single cell that plays rule-patterns through the map's own floor grid; infrastructure that lets the room itself be the automaton, never dominant as an object.

dragon_bench.name: Dragon Bench (order as chaos)
dragon_bench.description: The dragon curve folding into being on a bench - order so deep it reads as chaos.

mamma_monster_gallery.name: Mamma Monster (the origin gallery)
mamma_monster_gallery.description: Kristina Torsson's pattern vocabulary as living shaders — varma backen, Fjader, Bonan, the Mah-Jong stripe (1966, with Helena Henschen and Veronika Nygren), Rutan Oscillerar (the Vamlingbo room's oscillating check), and Moders Drom (Mothers Dream 2023, the img2img oscillation breathing on TIME). Ada Research begins in a landscape of my mother's patterns; this room says so, with her name on it.

incompleteness_scale.name: Incompleteness Scale
incompleteness_scale.description: A balance that cannot weigh itself, tilting forever — Gödel as furniture, the limit built into the shape of the thing.
incompleteness_scale.qfep_connection: A balance that cannot weigh itself, tilting forever — Gödel as furniture. In the grammar chapter it stands as the fine print on the whole enterprise: every rewriting system rich enough to describe growth is too rich to certify its own limits. The forest the sentence becomes contains questions the sentence cannot answer.

pg_workshop_console.name: Procedural Generation Workshop Desk
pg_workshop_console.description: Compact physical controls for the existing artifacts in five PG halls.

branching_growth_algorithm.description: Interactive visualization of branching growth patterns and algorithmic plant generation
branching_growth_algorithm.name: Branching Growth Algorithm
branching_growth_algorithm.qfep_connection: Growth as a rule iterated — a tip that splits, angles, and splits again, each branch a smaller copy of the decision that made it. The engine behind the organic_space beside it: structure accumulating from a repeated local choice, the procedural chapter's handshake with the fractal one next door.

dna.default: formation=chance, cast=all - reproduces the shipped build exactly. formation=chance calls the same coin flip at the same two thresholds the hard-coded expressions used (0.5 on the shell's deformation spheres, 0.3 on the tunnel details), and cast=all runs membranes, crystals and growths together as before, so all 13 existing placements are untouched.
dna.was: One hard-coded expression, twice: `OPERATION_UNION if randf() > 0.5 else OPERATION_SUBTRACTION` on the shell and the same at 0.3 on the tunnel details. The artifact's own truth line says organic form 'is what remains after noise has eaten away at geometry from within' — but the code was flipping a coin between eating away and piling on, and never said so. formation states the position; erode is the truth line taken literally, accrete is its opposite, alternate is neither chance nor doctrine but rhythm. cast was three generators that always all ran; the word and the all-plus-one-each shape are borrowed verbatim from particle_systems.cast, which asks the same question of its emitters.
dna.fixture_note: MANDATORY for the sweep. Every draw in this artifact was an unseeded global randf/randi, so without a pinned seed the N variants are N different caves and any bite number measures the RNG, not the axis (the trap CLAUDE.md names for generative artifacts). form_seed now routes all randomness through one RandomNumberGenerator; 0 keeps the shipped fresh-every-run behaviour, so this pin is capture-bench only and no placement sees it.
dna.framing_note: The subject is 25 m across (space_size 25,18,25 in the .tscn) and mostly hollow shell. If the sweep reports a small subject share, that is the shell's thin wall against a big frame, not an inert axis.

organic_space.description: An algorithmic exploration of organic geometries and natural forms, creating flowing, non-Euclidean spaces that challenge traditional geometric assumptions
organic_space.name: Organic Space
organic_space.qfep_connection: A space that looks grown rather than built — chambers and passages with the irregular rightness of something that developed instead of being placed. The proof that 'organic' is not a texture but a *process*: authorless form has a feel, and the walker can tell.

percolationnetwork_ca.description: P(occupied) = threshold -> CA flow propagation from top to bottom — does the random lattice percolate?
percolationnetwork_ca.name: percolationnetwork_ca

dna.default: occupation=conductive (p = 0.40), inlet=face - the shipped constant and the shipped top-face seeding exactly, same materials and same collision rule, so all 5 existing placements are unchanged; no map carries an #occupation: or #inlet: token today
dna.was: zero exports on the one artifact in the corpus whose whole subject is a number. Its own @identity block names PERCOLATION_THRESHOLD as the critical parameter and then lists a threshold control under `needs` as MISSING - the value was a const, so every player who ever met this lattice met p = 0.40, comfortably above the 3D site-percolation point p_c ~= 0.3116. The claim 'below the threshold nothing connects, above it everything does, and at the threshold the system decides' was only ever demonstrated on its winning side.
dna.note: occupation is p, how much lattice there is: sparse 0.20 (well under p_c - isolated pockets, the flow dies near the inlet face), critical 0.31 (at p_c - the incipient cluster, fractal, the outcome genuinely open), conductive 0.40 (the shipped value), dense 0.60 (everything connects and the paths stop being paths), solid 0.80 (a wall; percolation is trivial and the network is no longer one). inlet is the boundary condition - where the flow is injected: face = every open site on the +z face, the shipped rain front; point = the open site nearest that face's centre, so one dendrite grows and the question becomes about ONE cluster instead of all of them; seam = one row, a line source spreading as a sheet; shell = all six faces, flow arriving from outside inward, which asks not whether the lattice spans but whether anything in it stays dry. An inlet only ever marks sites the lattice already opened, so p and the boundary stay independent.
dna.warning: WHITE (occupied) CUBES CARRY COLLISION and the player walks inside this lattice. dense and solid are honest arguments and bad rooms - they are bench values. Nothing above conductive should be placed in a walked map without re-running the pathfinder on it.
dna.fixture_note: the lattice and the flow jitter have always come from the global unseeded randf(), so five variants of an unseeded lattice are five different objects rather than five values of one axis. lattice_seed = -1 preserves the shipped behaviour exactly and is the default; the fixture pins 7 so a sweep measures the axis and not the dice.
dna.reads: this scene's root carries the script, so apply_grid_config arrives directly; it is guarded on change (a rebuild recasts 5,832 cells and their collision bodies, which must not happen because a placement passed an unrelated key). _read_grid_config_meta also reads the config_<key> metadata the grid writes before the scene enters the tree, so a token builds the right lattice once instead of building the default and tearing it down.

percolationnetwork_ca.qfep_connection: Percolation: raise the density of open cells and, at one sharp threshold, disconnected pockets suddenly span the whole space — a path appears from edge to edge where an instant before there was none. The turn's physics: connectivity is not gradual, it is a phase change, and the procedural world snaps from rubble to network at a single critical value. Where forests burn, fluids seep, and rumors spread.

caverandomwalk.description: N walkers carve air from solid voxel grid — biased random walk inward, then upward level by level
caverandomwalk.name: caverandomwalk
caverandomwalk.qfep_connection: A cave dug by a random walk — a wanderer eating rock as it drifts, and the tunnel it leaves behind is the cave. The chapter's most direct marriage of the randomness thread and the space one: chance given a chisel, and the negative of its stagger becomes a place you can stand.

maze_generation.description: VR-scale walkable maze with recursive backtracking generation
maze_generation.name: Maze Generation
maze_generation.qfep_connection: A walkable maze carved by recursive backtracking — the algorithm drills forward at random, and when it hits a dead end it reverses just far enough to try a new direction, until every cell has been visited exactly once. The result is a perfect maze, one path between any two points, and no designer ever saw the whole of it. Getting lost in a corridor no mind laid out.

cube_mound_scene.description: Procedural mound built from stacked cubes — layered cellular logic deposits cubes where conditions permit, producing terrain that is both built and eroded.
cube_mound_scene.name: cube_mound_scene
cube_mound_scene.qfep_connection: A mound built by stacked cubes under cellular logic — deposit a cube where the local conditions say yes, and a landform accretes with no landscaper. The chapter's plainest proof: give a rule a place to look and a thing to drop, and terrain grows itself, one conditional at a time.

dome.description: Half-sphere primitive produced by boolean subtraction — used as reference geometry for enclosures and shelters.
dome.name: dome
dome.qfep_connection: A half-sphere cut from a solid by boolean subtraction — reference geometry for enclosure, the simplest roof. In the procedural rooms it stands as the authored control against which the grown forms are measured: this is what shape looks like when someone *drew* it, so you can feel how different the grown ones are.

layered_membrane.description: Procedural membrane generation with layered structures
layered_membrane.name: Layered Membrane
layered_membrane.qfep_connection: Surfaces accreted in layers, each draping over the last — sediment, skin, stratum. Form as history made visible: the membrane is a record of the order in which its rule fired, procedural generation wearing its own timeline.

mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d.description: Interactive 3D cellular automata with mirroring and texture generation capabilities
mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d.name: Mirror Cellular Texture for 3D
mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d.qfep_connection: Cellular automata run and then mirrored — local disorder folded across an axis into pattern with a spine. The room's demonstration that symmetry is cheap: take any grown texture, reflect it, and the eye reads intention where there was only a rule and a fold.

dna.fixture_why: MANDATORY for the sweep, and not an axis. The layout is drawn entirely from the UNSEEDED global randf/randi — generation_seed only ever fed the two FastNoiseLite fields, never the growth — so four topology frames would be four different mazes and any bite number would be measuring the RNG rather than the rule. This is the generative-artifact trap in CLAUDE.md. layout_draw defaults to `fresh`, which is the shipped every-launch-is-a-new-maze behaviour and is the artifact's point, so no placement ever sees the pin.
dna.default: topology=rhizome - the shipped network line for line. generate_primary_connections keeps the same three-nearest loop with the same randf() draw against the same branch_prob, generate_secondary_branches builds the same 250 nodes from the same three randf_range calls and hands over the same flat 0.7 width_multiplier, sever_network returns on its first line, and the seed ring keeps the identical layer_y expression. The tree, plateau and rupture code is reachable only from a non-default word, so the RNG consumes exactly the draws it always consumed in exactly the order it consumed them. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 14 mentions across 12 map files, not the 5 the promotion brief carried, and four reach-paths rather than one - bare tokens in PG_Mirrored_Patterns and its three parts and in ProceduralGeneration_Eight; a curation_station collection in Corridor_PG_Mirrored_Patterns whose #layout and #with_* flags belong to the station and not to this artifact; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:s#mount:rhizomatic_maze_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value; and `rhizomatic_maze_space->layered_membrane` in Trial_rooms_proceduralgeneration, which is a transformation target and not a config. Not one of the fourteen carries a topology key, and apply_grid_config returns unless a token names a word this file knows AND that word differs from the one it holds AND _ready has already grown the maze once.
dna.was: thirteen float and int exports, none of which said what the artifact is FOR. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS because nothing enumerated: branch_probability could be turned from 0.7 to 0.8 but there was no way for a map to ask for the thing the name promises. An artifact called rhizomatic shipped exactly one topology, and — measured rather than assumed — it was mostly a TREE: the only rhizomatic operation in the file is the three-nearest-neighbour pass over about 20 seeds, while the 250 secondary branches each attach by exactly one edge and close no loop at all.
dna.note: The axis is Deleuze and Guattari's own opposition, not a dial. `tree` is a minimum spanning tree from the lowest seed with growth oriented away from the root and tunnel width tapering by depth, so hierarchy is visible as thickness — there is no critically-rhizomatic middle value, the way bouncing_ball found there is no critically-bouncing. `severed` is asignifying rupture performed ON a finished rhizome rather than a different way of growing one, and it recounts node degrees afterwards so the chamber pass cannot drop a nine-metre CSG sphere into the fissure it just opened. `plateau` keeps every seed the four levels would have made and puts them all on one, so the comparison is about arrangement and not about how much was grown.
dna.declined: branch_probability, growth_iterations, merge_threshold, chamber_probability, organic_distortion and tunnel_segments — six knobs that are already exports and all of them decline for the same reason: they change how MUCH tangle there is, not what the tangle claims. connection_probability and deadend_pruning are declined for a different reason worth recording: they are exported, they are set in the .tscn, and no line of code reads either of them.
dna.still_note: topology is resolved before a single tunnel mesh is built and never moves again, so one frame is a complete account of it. Expect plateau to be the loudest value by far — a 25 m tower collapsing to a flat mat is a silhouette change, not a texture one. tree and rhizome differ in loop structure and in tunnel thickness rather than in extent, so compare where routes close and how width falls off toward the periphery.
dna.deepened_why: THE BENCH HAD NEVER PHOTOGRAPHED THIS ARTIFACT, and that is the finding — the axis was not on trial, it was never called. The sweep reported peak 0.062% across ALL SIX pairs on a subject of 8.217%, and the tell is that the peak was rhizome-vs-plateau, the pair the still_note above had predicted would be the loudest in the batch by a distance: a 25 m tower against a flat mat cannot differ by six hundredths of a percent. A number that impossible is a fact about the instrument. Three causes, all measured in the sheet at doc/reports/sweep_rhizomatic_maze_space.png rather than guessed: (1) the .tscn carries a DebugInfo Control — a 390x110 panel with a RichTextLabel reading 'Generating organic tunnel network...' — and the sweep's chrome suppressor stands down CanvasLayer and Camera3D only, so a Control under a Node3D drew straight into the viewport and IS the 8.2% subject, identical in every frame. The statistic that was supposed to report on the axis was mostly a photograph of a debug readout. (2) NavigationHelpers hangs four 0.6 m marker spheres at x,z = +/-25; they are MeshInstance3D, so they pin the fitted AABB to a 50 m box no matter what the maze does, which put the camera about 220 m out. (3) At 220 m the artifact's own WorldEnvironment — volumetric fog at density 0.03 over a 50 m length, authored for a player standing INSIDE the tunnels — fills the frame with haze: the background samples (130,165,118) and the 90th percentile of per-pixel difference from it is SEVEN grey levels. The maze is a ghost, and it visibly MOVES between the four tiles, which is the proof the values were arriving all along. Repair: a bench-only `bench_stage` export, the same shape as the existing layout_draw, defaulting to `scene`; `bare` frees the Control and the marker spheres and turns off exactly two properties on the environment (fog_enabled, volumetric_fog_enabled) rather than freeing it — with the sweep rig adding a WorldEnvironment of its own, two in a tree is undefined enough that freeing would make the picture depend on node order, and this scene's own 0.02/0.02/0.08 background is the best backdrop available for tunnels of albedo 0.7/0.8/0.9. It touches no generator code and no placement sets it. THE SECOND REPAIR IS THE DESIGN ONE and it stands on its own: severed cut the graph in half and left both halves where they were, measuring 0.012% against the intact rhizome. The tempting reading is the Deleuzian one — that cutting a rhizome changes nothing because any point still reaches any other — and it is wrong about this code: a plane cut removes EVERY crossing edge, so the graph really does fall into two components. The failure was that CONNECTION IS NOT A VISIBLE PROPERTY. The fissure is now 0.14 of maze_size.x instead of 0.08 and the two fragments stand 0.06 apart on each side, so the wound is about 20 m of a 50 m object and reads in the silhouette; tendrils are suppressed over the gap so nothing sews it shut. Extent grows about 12%, which the freed camera repays many times.
dna.expected: NO NUMBER IS PREDICTED HERE, and that is honest rather than evasive: nothing about this artifact has ever been photographed, so there is no scale to extrapolate from. What IS predicted is the SHAPE of the result, and it is falsifiable. (1) The frame should stop being a flat field: the background sampled at (3,3) should come back near (5,5,18) instead of (130,165,118), and the 90th percentile of per-pixel difference from it should rise from 7 grey levels into the dozens. (2) The loudest pair should become rhizome-vs-plateau, because a 25 m tower against a flat mat is a silhouette. (3) The subject share will probably FALL from 8.2%, and that is the fix working, not failing - the 8.2% was a debug panel that has now been freed, so the number will finally be about the maze. IF EVERY PAIR IS STILL UNDER 0.1%, the fixture did not arrive: check that bench_stage reached the root before concluding anything at all about topology.
dna.deepened_declined: A FIFTH VALUE, `radicle` — Deleuze and Guattari's own middle figure, the fascicular root whose principal root has aborted and onto which an indefinite multiplicity of secondary roots grafts. It is the strongest thing missing from this axis, because it is the figure that LOOKS tangled and still is not a rhizome, which is the distinction the whole Introduction turns on, and the axis currently ships the two easy poles and two operations. It is not taken in this pass on a sequencing judgement: not one of the four existing values has ever been photographed, so designing a fifth against an imagined frame is the finished-looking-experiment failure the promotion brief warns about — 'an artifact that does not build is a finding, not an axis' applies just as well to an artifact that has never been seen. Take it after a clean sweep exists. Implementation sketch so the next agent does not start cold: connect_as_radicle() builds a short thick taproot from the lowest seed to a graft node above it, joins every other seed to that ONE graft at equal width (the star, against tree's spanning chain), and generate_secondary_branches concentrates the flourish near the graft with NO taper, because in a radicle the unity is the pivot and not the branching. The 20 primary connections are only about 16% of the 270 the file builds, so the secondary rule has to carry the value too or it will read as a variation on tree.
dna.open: THE SAME THREE CHILDREN SHIP INTO EVERY MAP, and this is NOT repaired here. All fourteen placements get the DebugInfo Control — a panel reading 'Generating organic tunnel network...' with the parameter list under it — because neither the sweep's chrome suppressor nor GridInteractablesComponent._suppress_embedded_chrome stands down a raw Control, and a Control under a Node3D draws to the viewport regardless. They also get a WorldEnvironment that overrides the map's own environment with volumetric fog, and four navigation marker spheres at +/-25 m that inflate the AABB the grid auto-grounds against. Every one of those is a change to what fourteen rooms look like, so fixing it belongs in its own pass with its own walk, not smuggled in under a DNA deepening. Worth checking how many other artifacts carry a Control child before repairing this one alone — the suppressor is the shared meeting point and this is likely a class, not a case.

rhizomatic_maze_space.description: A labyrinthine exploration of rhizomatic growth patterns, creating interconnected maze-like spaces that grow organically like fungal networks or plant root systems
rhizomatic_maze_space.name: Rhizomatic Maze Space
rhizomatic_maze_space.qfep_connection: A labyrinth grown as rhizome — interconnected, centerless, any point reachable from any other by more than one route. The counter-maze: where recursive backtracking makes a tree with a single path, this makes a mesh with many, Deleuze's figure walked as architecture. A world with no author and, deliberately, no throughline either.

flex_cloth_pad.name: Flex Cloth Pad
flex_cloth_pad.description: Hanging cloth simulated as spring-mass vertices. The integration phase affordance: the bracelet's flex/drape mode nudges the cloth and watches it settle.

grab_long_stick.name: grab_long_stick
grab_long_stick.qfep_connection: F_force: the probe — a graspable stick trailing a long cloth ribbon. It is how the hand asks a soft world questions: poke, drag, sweep, and the ribbon writes the answer in folds. The instrument of contact in the softbodies rooms; force made holdable.

revolving_joy_ride.name: Revolving Joy Ride
revolving_joy_ride.description: A rotating ride with hanging soft bodies colliding with obstacles.

dna.default: flesh=soft, occurrence=scattered - soft returns the shipped linear_stiffness 0.2 / damping 0.05 / pressure 0.5 value for value, and scattered draws the SAME two randf_range calls in the same order off the same global generator (rng_seed defaults to 0, which leaves the seeded generator null). The 10 map placements grow the garden they always grew.
dna.was: three unnamed SoftBody3D numbers and a for-loop over randf_range. The @identity truth says 'a mushroom cap does not decide its shape - the pin constraint, gravity and whatever bumps into it negotiate the form', and the tissue doing the negotiating was hard-coded at one setting. The scatter was not a decision at all: it is what a loop does when nobody asks, yet it is a claim about fungal ecology - that fruiting bodies come up independently - and it is not the only one fungi make.
dna.note: flesh is a MATERIAL property, not a time-domain one, but the sweep photographs at 1.1 s and a SoftBody3D at stiffness 0.05 with damping 0.05 is still moving then. The four values will differ in the frame - turgid holds a ball while slack has already collapsed - but the picture is a snapshot of a negotiation in progress, not four rest states. Deterministic under the fixture's seed, so the comparison is fair; it is simply earlier than rest. occurrence is a positional axis and is at rest immediately.
dna.fixture_note: rng_seed and spawn_span are bench knobs added for this, both defaulting to 0 = 'as shipped'. Without a seed, fifteen unseeded randf_range draws per variant make five variants five different gardens and the sweep measures noise - the documented failure for any generative artifact. Without spawn_span the field is the measured 19.45 x 20.07 m, which puts a 2 m cap at roughly 26 px in a 760 px frame: the caps become specks and an axis about cap SHAPE cannot be read at all.
dna.open: spatial_needs.footprint_cells is 9 while measured_footprint_cells is 420 - the registry books this 20 m field as a 3x3 prop. Not touched here; recorded so it is not lost.

softbody_gallery_part2.name: SoftBody Gallery Part 2
softbody_gallery_part2.description: Part 2 of the soft body test gallery.
softbody_gallery_part2.qfep_connection: A drop-test census: the same softness settings pressed onto sphere, box, capsule, and torus, each cell labelled and tracked as it falls and settles. Softness revealed as a negotiation between material parameters and the shape they inhabit.

breathing_room.name: Breathing Room
breathing_room.description: A corridor with soft body walls that rhythmically expand and contract.

dna.default: substance=solid, aperture=ajar - both are strict no-ops. `solid` returns from _apply_substance() before a StandardMaterial3D is constructed, so material_override stays unassigned and the slabs keep Godot's default grey; `ajar` returns from _apply_aperture() before either transform is read, so the authored x = -2.3185759 and x = +3.5541987 are untouched. All twelve appearances render exactly as before: the 5 grid tokens (SoftBodies_Obsticals, _p1, _p2, _p3, Corridor_SoftBodies_Obsticals), the 6 exhibit_furniture#mount:breathing_room slots in Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies, and the Curation_Bay_softbodies_0 roster. None carries a #substance: or #aperture: token, and a bare token leaves merged_config empty so apply_grid_config is never called at all.
dna.was: the .tscn root carried NO SCRIPT - two hand-authored SoftBody3D slabs with baked pinned points, no material override, and no breathing. The sinusoidal pressure loop the description promises lives in the sibling breathing_room.gd, which nothing in the repository loads.
dna.declined: breath_speed and breath_amplitude, the orphan script's named critical_parameter. They modulate pressure_coefficient over time, the evidence here is one still per value, and soft bodies are still settling at the 1.1 s capture settle - sweeping them would photograph the settle, not the axis.
dna.note: aperture is applied in _enter_tree, before the SoftBody3D children enter the tree and pin their empty-path attachments to world space. A value arriving later through apply_grid_config can still change substance but cannot move a live soft body.

dna.default: crimp=swell, heading=none. `swell` returns the literal 0.25 that the shipped `var wave_offset := i * 0.25` already multiplied i by, so the line is now `float(i) * gradient` computing the same IEEE product. `none` sets `shaped = false` and the envelope multiply is never reached, so `xform.origin.z = base_wave + wind_noise` stands character for character as it shipped. The two determinism exports are no-ops at their defaults too: `frozen_phase` -1.0 fails its `>= 0.0` test so t is `float(Time.get_ticks_msec()) * 0.001 + time_offset` as before, and `wave_seed` -1 returns from setup_joyful_animation() on the shipped `time_offset = randf() * TAU` - the same single draw off the same global generator, in the same order, so even the RNG stream is untouched. THIRTEEN appearances, each read out of its map JSON for this pass, and NOT ONE of them carries a `#key:value` tail: five grid tokens (SoftBodies_Obsticals as `flagdancer:90`, and SoftBodies_Obsticals_p1 / _p2 / _p3 / Corridor_SoftBodies_Obsticals as the bare word - a rotation suffix is not a config, so merged_config is empty and apply_grid_config is never called), seven `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:flagdancer` mounts (Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / lattice_pm_17 / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies), and the Curation_Bay_softbodies_0 curation_station roster. Were a host to forward its own keys anyway, apply_grid_config reads only the four it declares, so the signature is unchanged and it returns before assigning anything.
dna.was: one hard-coded wave, and no held edge at all. `i * 0.25` fixed the spatial period at two thirds of a wave across six metres for every flag in the project, and every bone got the SAME amplitude (0.4 and 0.15) because `progress` entered the noise's PHASE and never its ENVELOPE - so the shipped object is a sheet floating free in space, undulating exactly as much at one end as the other. The maps have been describing something else for months: SoftBodies_Obsticals/critical.md says the flag is 'pinned at one edge - attached, constrained, unable to leave its pole', and technical.md says 'A cloth surface pinned along one edge'. No line of code ever pinned an edge. `heading=hoist` is the value that makes this artifact do what its own documentation has been claiming it does.
dna.note: `crimp` is NEW and free corpus-wide - the textile word for the wave standing in a fabric. Not `fold` (polyhedron_nets_cube: whether a net is folded, a discrete state); not `swell` (marching_cubes: terrain amplitude class); not `weave` (ruth_asawa_sculpture: which wire topology gets emitted, a construction, where crimp is a deformation of one fixed construction). `heading` is NEW - the vexillological and curtain-making name for the reinforced edge a cloth is attached by. Deliberately NOT `suspension` (cloth_straps, spring_system): that axis names the FURNITURE a hanging body hangs from and builds a rank of steel around an untouched cloth. This one builds nothing and moves no prop; it changes which part of the cloth is allowed to move. Not `anchorage` (ant_colony_v2, nest-site arrangement), not `hang` (gallery_winner_showcase, the arrangement of hung objects), not `attach` (point: float/stake/plate). Both axes were chosen for the only property of a wave that survives being frozen - its SHAPE ALONG THE CLOTH - because everything in this sequence moves and the evidence is one still.
dna.declined: `wind_strength` (1.0), the @identity's own declared critical_parameter and the most tempting knob in the file. Refused because at a frozen phase it is nothing but a uniform amplitude multiplier on a sine: four values are four SCALINGS of one shape, which the union-AABB camera then partly divides back out again, and in motion it reads as speed-of-flapping rather than as form. `celebration_intensity` is worse - it is consulted only while `celebration_mode` is true, and celebration_mode can only be turned on by a live ui_accept press that no capture will ever make, so all four values would render byte-identically. Also declined: the sine frequencies 2.0, 3.7 and 0.8, which are pure rates - one photograph each of an arbitrary instant.
dna.placements: 13 appearances, 0 configured: 5 grid tokens + 7 exhibit_furniture mounts + 1 curation_station roster. None carries a config tail, so none reaches the new code.
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED THERE IS NO DETERMINISM HERE, TWICE OVER, and 'has it settled by 1.45 s' is not even the right question: there is no simulation to settle. The pose is a closed-form function of `t = Time.get_ticks_msec() * 0.001 + time_offset`, so the flag is never at rest and the shutter photographs the wall clock; and `time_offset = randf() * TAU` is drawn off the global generator with no seed, which is five different objects across five variants. (The file LOOKS like it seeds something - `var noise_seed := int(time_offset * 1000) % 1000` - and that local is never read again. Decoration, not a seed. The second random draw the brief warns about, `randf_range(0.8, 1.2)`, is inside create_flag_parade(), which nothing in the repository calls.) frozen_phase 2.35 makes t a constant, so time_offset is never read, the flag is MOTIONLESS, and the picture is a pure function of the exports on every machine. 2.35 rather than a round number because it gives a well-spread wave at the default - bone 0 at sin(4.70) = -1.000, bone 8 at sin(6.70) = +0.405, bone 16 at sin(8.70) = +0.666, all times 0.4 - where a near-flat instant would flatter every value equally. wave_seed 20260812 is for the WORLD, not the bench: in a live map the phase must keep running, and an explicit integer (never `rng.seed = randi()`, which is the opposite of seeding) makes it the same flag on every launch. Both are written as NUMBERS, not strings, because they are assigned straight onto typed float and int exports before _ready.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config checks each word against CRIMPS / HEADINGS, builds a signature of all four values, and RETURNS before assigning anything when it equals `_config_sig` - which _ready() primes with the shipped values, so a call carrying keys this artifact does not declare is a strict no-op. Nothing rebuilds geometry in any case: all four values are read fresh by _process every frame, so a live placement changes shape without a single node being freed. setup_joyful_animation() re-runs only when the seed itself moved, so a config repeating the shipped -1 never spends a second randf() and never re-rolls a running flag. _ready() builds synchronously and there is no call_deferred in the build path. Teardown now frees an `_owned` array (skeleton, mesh, particles) instead of the shipped `for child in get_children(): if not child.owner: child.queue_free()`, which took down every node any other system had parented to this artifact at runtime.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, and it disagrees with the design on BOTH axes, which is the only kind of prediction worth writing. Method: the sheet carries no material (see `finding`), so its interior is uniform and only the SILHOUETTE can differ; project each of the 17 bone columns with the canonical rig (world +Z maps to (-0.581, -0.209) screen metres at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26), rasterise the union of the 16 quads between columns, and take the symmetric difference. crimp: the design named ripple vs corrugation. WRONG - that pair is FOURTH of six. The closest is flat vs corrugation at 0.69% of the full frame (6.8% of the subject crop, ~2.3% critic frame), because at 1.2 rad per bone corrugation's wave averages out over the silhouette and its end column lands near where flat's does; ripple vs corrugation is 1.41% (~4.6% critic frame), a factor of 2.0 wider. Structural note the design missed: bone 0 has wave_offset = 0 * gradient = 0 for EVERY value, so all four crimp tiles share their left edge exactly and the difference grows linearly toward bone 16. heading: the design named hoist vs fly as the closest and the likeliest to miss the bar. It is the WIDEST of the six - 0.90% of frame at the swept default crimp=swell (2.9% critic frame). The closest is hoist vs both at 0.42% (4.1% of crop, ~1.4% critic frame), because the `both` bunting envelope and the `hoist` ramp agree at the dead hoist end and differ only over the fly half. On FOCUS both axes should saturate near 33% rather than separate, since every differing pixel is a full-contrast sheet-versus-background flip and the differing area exceeds the hottest-5% window: on a silhouette-only subject FOCUS IS THE WRONG DISCRIMINATOR and `frame` is the informative number. ALL OF THIS IS CONDITIONAL - see `finding`. The design also assumed the flag fills ~60% of frame; it is 9.5% at framing 1.0, a factor of 6.3, which is why every predicted percentage here is smaller than the design's.
dna.finding: DO NOT SWEEP THIS TOKEN YET - IT PHOTOGRAPHS AS A WHITE QUAD, AND THE AXES ARE NOT THE REASON. The only capture that exists (user://multi_shots/flagdancer, 2026-04-20, four angles) shows a single small white quadrilateral and no flag from any angle, and no commit has touched this folder since, so it is current. That quad is the .tscn's own vestigial 1x1 QuadMesh; the procedural 6x4 m flag is in the AABB and not in the picture - the camera had pulled back to about 15 m of framed extent, which is the 7.2 m mesh diagonal times the capturer's pad, so the mesh resource exists and draws nothing. Cause, read out of the code: create_pride_flag_with_bones() assigns `skinned_mesh.skeleton = skeleton.get_path()` immediately after add_child, when the Skeleton3D still has ZERO bones and before the mesh is committed. Godot resolves that path at assignment and, with no explicit Skin, caches an auto-skin built from the rest transforms of nothing; the 17 bones added afterwards never regenerate it, so the surface is skinned against an empty bind array. Two working procedural skinned meshes in this repository do the opposite in both respects - commons/artifacts/ik_arm_demo (explicit Skin, bind poses set from `skeleton.get_bone_rest(i).affine_inverse()`, `skeleton` assigned LAST) and commons/hazards/octapod_crawler/one_leg (explicit Skin, MeshInstance3D parented UNDER the Skeleton3D). SECOND defect on the same mesh: st.commit() is assigned with no material and SurfaceTool sets none, so the default StandardMaterial3D renders it white with `vertex_color_use_as_albedo` off - every stripe colour in flag_colors is written into the mesh as vertex colour and then never shown. A pride flag that renders white. NEITHER IS FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately: both change what all 13 shipped placements look like, both are unverifiable without a Godot run, and this pass was forbidden one. The axes, the defaults and the fixture are complete and correct behind them.
dna.measurement_risk: Even once it renders, the subject is only 9.5% of frame at framing 1.0 - the AABB is 6 x 4 x ~0, a wide flat sheet, and PAD 1.9 on the DIAGONAL wastes most of the frame. A `dna.framing` near 0.62 would put it at ~25% and roughly triple every frame number above; it is deliberately NOT set here, because tuning a framing value against a subject that has never been photographed would be a guess wearing the clothes of a measurement. Set it in the same pass that repairs the render, and measure. Second risk: the sheet's normals are all +Z and the bone bases carry no rotation, so shading cannot vary across the surface - with or without a material the axes live in the silhouette and in the stripe boundaries, never in shading.

turing_pattern_generator.description: Generate reaction-diffusion Turing patterns in real-time — spots, stripes, and labyrinthine structures emerge from the interplay of activator and inhibitor chemicals diffusing at different rates. Alan Turing's morphogenesis made visible.

dna.framing_why: MEASURED, and it is the whole story rather than a polish pass. The update rule was ported to numpy and the six regimes compared ON THE TEXTURE at the fixture (resolution 40, 1600 steps): spots vs coral changes 15-21% of the pattern cells and stripes vs coral changes 93%. The sweep reported 0.497% and 2.089%. The ratio is the frame - the pattern is a 1 x 1 m quad lying FLAT and photographed from 14.9 degrees above the horizon, so it presents 0.257 of its own area, and the union box is stretched to a 1.68 m diagonal by the VR control panel at z=0.65 and the framed info plate at z=-0.58. 2.7% of frame times 20% of the pattern is 0.54%, which reproduces the measurement to within a tenth of a percent: the axis was never weak, the camera was 5.2 m away. 0.6 is set against a computed clipping limit - the widest screen extent is the far corner of the base plate at 0.765 m, so the camera cannot come closer than 0.48, and 0.6 keeps a quarter of the frame as margin while multiplying every measured area by 2.78. Uniform scale is not an alternative: display_size scales the AABB with the artifact, so the camera pulls back by the same factor and nothing is gained.
dna.fixture_why: MANDATORY, three separate reasons, and all three default to shipped behaviour in code so none of them is an axis. pattern_seed pins the five seeded blobs - _seed_random draws them with the global randi_range, so six regime frames would be six different inoculations and the bite number would measure the RNG, not the feed/kill pair (the generative-artifact trap). warmup runs the chemistry before the first frame: at the shipped 4 steps per frame a 0.35 s settle reaches step 84 and all six values photograph the same five undifferentiated blobs. resolution 40 rather than the shipped 64 is a TIME budget, not a look - this is an interpreted CPU Gray-Scott loop and 1600 steps at 64x64 is 6.5 M cell updates inside _ready, which blocks the boot past the capture watchdog; the code caps it at 4 M regardless of what a fixture asks for.
dna.fixture_ladder: Measured, not assumed. The update rule was re-implemented exactly (same 0.2/0.05 laplacian weights, same clamp, same 5-disc seeding) and run per preset at 32/40/48/64 cells and 300-6000 steps. The six regimes are indistinguishable below ~800 steps and fully settled by ~2000; at resolution 40 / 1600 steps the V-coverage reads spots 0.06, stripes 0.21, maze 0.16, mitosis 0.07, coral 0.03, waves 0.13, and every pair differs by at least 0.04 mean |dV| per cell (most by over 0.11). Two facts worth knowing before reading the sheet: at the shipped seeding (U=0.5, V=0.25 in five discs) the Coral preset very nearly dies out - it settles at 3% coverage - and the Spots preset stabilises as a handful of isolated dots rather than filling the field. Those are facts about the presets, not about the capture.
dna.deepened: 2026-08-05, two moves, and the first one is a correction of the verdict rather than of the artifact. (1) dna.framing 0.6. The regime axis is not close to weak: ported to numpy at the fixture settings, the six presets differ by 15% (spots vs coral, the reported worst pair) to 93% (stripes vs coral) OF THE PATTERN CELLS. The sweep saw 0.497% and 2.089% because the pattern surface is only about 2.7% of the frame, and 2.7% x 20% = 0.54% reproduces the reported number almost exactly. A flat 1 m plate seen from 14.9 degrees shows a quarter of its area, and a control panel 0.65 m away in +z and a framed info plate 0.58 m away in -z stretch the fitted diagonal to 1.68 m. Nothing about the chemistry needed changing. (2) A SECOND AXIS, `seeding`, which is the argument this file's own truth line makes and no knob could reach: 'pattern emerges from the ratio of two diffusion rates - not from a template, not from a gene'. regime moves feed and kill; the truth sentence is about neither, and every placement in the corpus has started from the same five random discs since the artifact was written. The four values were chosen by measurement, not taste - all four run at all six regimes, and the value list is what survived: `noise` was tried at five densities from 0.08 to 0.8 and no density ignites more than two regimes, so it was dropped rather than shipped as four blank tiles; `band` was dropped because under mitosis it and `ring` both die to an empty field, which is two values showing one picture, the twin fault the critic exists to catch. THE RESULT IS TWO-SIDED, which is why it is worth having: under `maze` the four seedings settle at coverage 0.434 / 0.410 / 0.443 / 0.440 while 39-73% of the CELLS differ - the law fixes how much, the seed fixes where, and the truth line holds. Under `waves` the lattice never ignites and under `mitosis` the ring dies out, so the seed also decides IF there is a pattern at all. Minimum pairwise texture difference across all six regimes is 9.7% and the median is around 45%, comparable to regime's own spread. NOT MEASURED YET: 6 x 4 is 24 variants and build_dna_gallery's default cap is 9, which keeps the first axis that fits and silently drops the second - this needs --max=24. Worth knowing regardless: the last sweep of `regime` only rendered FIVE values. Cap trimming drops from the END of the list, so `waves` - the preset furthest from the others in the phase space, at f=0.014 / k=0.047 - is the one value that has never been photographed.
dna.default: regime=spots, seeding=discs - both no-ops. _seed_discs is the shipped inoculation moved into a named function and not otherwise touched: the same five discs, the same random centres and radii, drawn in the same order and the same count from the same generator, so an existing placement is inoculated byte for byte as before. apply_grid_config pulls `seeding` out of the blanket write-through loop for the same reason it pulls `regime` - writing the word alone would change what the RESET button draws next while leaving the field on screen inoculated the old way, so the artifact would be labelled one thing and showing another - and it re-seeds only when the word validates against SEEDINGS, DIFFERS from the one held, and _ready has already built the grids. None of the 14 rooms sends either key. AND, unchanged from the promotion: regime=spots - spots is PRESETS[0], which is f=0.055 / k=0.062, which is the pattern_type the .tscn has always written on the root. _resolve_regime assigns pattern_type ONLY when the resolved index differs, so at the default not one byte is written and the setter never fires; _ready is otherwise the same six calls in the same order. pattern_seed and warmup both default to 0, which is the shipped fresh-every-launch inoculation and no pre-run at all, so a player still meets the blank field and watches it organise. apply_grid_config keeps its legacy write-through loop untouched and handles regime separately, guarded on the word being one PRESETS builds and on it differing; neither of the two curation bays nor the five museum trials that mount this artifact sends it, so all 14 rooms are unchanged.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and the axis was already sitting in the source. The six-point phase space was an @export_enum INT called pattern_type with a working setter and a VR slider wired to it, and the registry had never been told. Worse, the integer was unreachable from a map token even by hand: map_data.json config values arrive as STRINGS and apply_grid_config's whole body was a blanket `if key in self: set(key, ...)`, so 'turing_pattern_generator#pattern_type:2' tried to write "2" into a typed int, was rejected, and silently rendered Spots. Fourteen placements, one regime.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04, the lsystem_editor case again. regime is the corpus's word for 'which named case of this system's parameter space is in force' (harmonic_motion_demo, mass_spring_damper, bouncing_ball, bifurcation_diagram) and the values are DERIVED from PRESETS - _regime_index reads the third column of the table, so the declared list cannot drift from the code the way science_screen's did. The axis is deliberately the named regime and NOT feed or kill as continuous floats: this loop's evidence is one still per value, a slider position is not a claim, and the whole teaching point of the @identity ('each preset is a point in that space') is that the interesting structure is a handful of named islands. CAUTION ON RECORD: reaction_diffusion, the GPU sibling this file's @identity names, was measured GENUINELY INERT - 62% of frame and 15 grey levels. That verdict was about a continuous parameter on an unwarmed field; the regimes here differ by a factor of seven in coverage once the chemistry has actually run.

particle_swarm_walk.name: A place remembered
particle_swarm_walk.description: Walk among 24 grabbable PointBodies on a12m score field. See personal and shared best positions. Change the objective while preserving current bodies and motion.
particle_swarm_walk.qfep_connection: A remembered score is accountable to the rule that produced it. Shared success can gather bodies without rewarding diversity.

tick_flock.description: The swarm-intelligence seam. A flock looks alive - emergence, a whole beyond its parts. Underneath: N agents, each reading neighbours and doing arithmetic, advanced one discrete tick at a time. Between ticks nothing moves; the glide is frozen frames the eye splices. Blue: each boid's positions, one per tick, visibly separated - it teleports, it does not fly. Amber: the arc we imagine. Slow the clock and the flock is a for-loop.
tick_flock.name: Tick Flock
tick_flock.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for swarmintelligence. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

fitness_landscape_politics.name: Fitness Landscape Politics
fitness_landscape_politics.description: PSO particles compare convergence, distance from centre and distance from an evolving archive. RESET repeats the starting scatter; novelty rescoring keeps remembered positions comparable under the current archive. A ridge mandate is also available by configuration.
fitness_landscape_politics.qfep_connection: The fitness function IS the power structure. Switching landscapes does not change the agents' F-model — it changes what counts as low energy. Who defines the loss function defines the world.

dna.default: cue=trace - trace resolves through _mode_for_cue() to STIGMERGY, which is the mode _mode was hard-pinned to before the promotion, so all 10 existing placements open on the deposit heatmap they already opened on. Draws come off one seeded _rng (BUILD_SEED) rather than the global stream, and seed()/randomize() is never called, so the artifact neither consumes nor reseeds the process-wide RNG other artifacts in the same map are drawing from.
dna.was: no axis of its own. _mode was pinned to STIGMERGY and the other two modes were reachable only by pressing MODE in the headset - an artifact built to argue that order has three possible sources shipped exactly one of them to every map and every capture. The MODE button now walks `cue` rather than going behind it, so the headset and the map token cannot disagree about what is on screen.
dna.note: NOT the reaction_diffusion inert class. The three values are not three parameter settings of one field - they change which readout is built and where. `neighbour` clears the centre plate and adds a 2.0 x 4.8 m phase graph at x -5.5..-3.5, two metres of geometry no other value builds and on the opposite side of the body; `trace` and `slope` build the right-hand order bar that `neighbour` removes. The differences are gross layout, not fine texture, so they survive a still. A fourth no-medium value (all coupling off, empty field) was considered and cut: a blank plate is how a render scores INERT, and it is not an argument.

self_organizing_patterns.description: Stigmergy, phase transitions, and attractor basin visualization — 3 modes: stigmergy field with deposit/evaporation heatmap, Ising-like phase transition with order parameter sweep, Voronoi-colored attractor basins with flow field arrows
self_organizing_patterns.name: Self-Organizing Patterns
self_organizing_patterns.qfep_connection: Three windows on order-from-below: a stigmergy field where deposits recruit deposits, phase transitions where a parameter nudge flips the regime, attractor basins where histories converge. The theory shelf of the chapter — why local rules don't just make patterns, but make *stable* ones.

population_account_walk.name: Who keeps the count?
population_account_walk.description: A12m ecosystem of grabbable PointBodies. Births, losses and supplied bodies are counted separately; gold rings identify supplied organisms. Filter the account without removing actual support.
population_account_walk.qfep_connection: An apparent recovery has conditions. The account names supplied bodies without treating care as a failure of autonomy.

enhanced_kmeans.description: Interactive K-means clustering visualization with adjustable k, colored cluster assignments, and centroid movement animation.
enhanced_kmeans.name: Enhanced K-Means Clustering
enhanced_kmeans.qfep_connection: K-means IS iterative F-minimization — centroids move to minimize within-cluster variance. Each step reduces the system's free energy until convergence. K itself is a λ-like parameter: too few clusters = underfitting, too many = overfitting.

svm_visualization.description: SVM hyperplane separator with support vectors highlighted. Shows maximum margin classification and kernel trick for non-linear boundaries.
svm_visualization.name: Support Vector Machine Visualization
svm_visualization.qfep_connection: SVM finds the maximum-margin boundary — the F-minimal separation between classes. Support vectors are the critical data points where the decision boundary is defined. The kernel trick lifts data to higher dimensions for linear separability: same F-minimization strategy as homogeneous coordinates.

random_forest_visualization.description: Visual representation of random forest ensemble — multiple decision trees voting on classification, showing how diversity improves accuracy.
random_forest_visualization.name: Random Forest Visualization

neural_network_visualization.description: Layered neural network with visible activations, weights as line thickness, forward pass animation. See how information transforms through layers.
neural_network_visualization.name: Neural Network Visualization
neural_network_visualization.qfep_connection: Neural networks learn F-models through gradient descent — each weight update reduces prediction error. Overfitting = F too low (memorization); regularization = intentional λ (noise tolerance). Generalization lives at the edge of chaos between memorization and randomness.

neural_networks_vr.description: Walkable neural network with visible weights and backpropagation
neural_networks_vr.name: NeuralNetworks_VR
neural_networks_vr.qfep_connection: The network turned inside out and made walkable — weights hanging in the air as visible thicknesses, activations lighting up as you pass, and backpropagation running the error backward through the whole structure like a confession travelling upstream. The primitive of deep learning shown honestly: not a brain, but a landscape of numbers that adjusts itself by measuring how wrong it just was.

fine_tuning_vr.description: Transfer learning tower with frozen and trainable layers
fine_tuning_vr.name: FineTuning_VR
fine_tuning_vr.qfep_connection: A network as a tower with padlocks: frozen storeys keep their inherited weights while gradients flow only through the unlocked top. Transfer learning staged as property law — most of the model is estate, and 'learning' happens in the floors you are permitted to renovate.

computer_vision_vr.description: Interactive image processing with spatial convolution filters
computer_vision_vr.name: ComputerVision_VR
computer_vision_vr.qfep_connection: Convolution made spatial — a filter sliding across an image, and you inside the sliding. The room where a machine first *sees*: not by understanding, but by sweeping the same small question (is there an edge here? a corner?) across every position until a picture becomes a field of answers.

convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr.description: Walkable CNN architecture with interactive kernels
convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr.name: ConvolutionalNeuralNetworksCNNs_VR
convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr.qfep_connection: The walkable CNN — kernels you can grab, feature maps stacking from edges to textures to parts to faces. The architecture that taught machines to see by insisting the same detector works everywhere: translation invariance as a built-in belief, the eye's humility written into the weights.

vogue_timeline.name: Vogue — a phrase of your own
vogue_timeline.interaction: dance / record / replay / teach poses / teach height / teach phrases A and B / train / test / check intention
vogue_timeline.description: Two airborne hand paths follow a 32-beat dance reference. Beside it, the same sphere learns pose categories, continuous hand-height control, one four-second two-hand phrase or two labelled phrases A and B. Unfamiliar and ambiguous performances can be withheld. CHECK compares declared intention with predictions and preserves earlier model results. Fresh tests and local saves remain separate from training. These measured relations do not judge dance quality.
vogue_timeline.qfep_connection: A dancer can replace the supplied reference with their own phrase. The measured relation remains smaller than the dance.

lstms_vr.description: Interactive LSTM cell with walkable memory flow
lstms_vr.name: LSTMs_VR
lstms_vr.qfep_connection: A memory cell you can walk through — gates deciding what to keep, what to forget, what to let out. The LSTM is the chapter's answer to time: a network that carries a thread of context forward, forgetting on purpose so the important thing survives. Memory as a valve, not a vault.

transformers_vr.description: Interactive transformer with attention beam visualization
transformers_vr.name: Transformers_VR
transformers_vr.qfep_connection: Attention drawn as beams — every token reaching to every other, weighting what matters, and the whole sequence understood at once instead of in order. The architecture underneath the machine writing these very words: not memory marched step by step, but relevance computed all at once. The room where the curriculum quietly meets the intelligence walking it.

generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr.description: Spatial GAN arena with generator and discriminator zones
generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr.name: GenerativeAdversarialNetworksGANs_VR
generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr.qfep_connection: Two networks locked in a duel — a generator forging samples, a discriminator calling the fakes — each making the other better until the forgeries pass. Creation as adversarial pressure, art from an arms race. The world room's unsettling proof that convincing can be reached without ever understanding.

anomaly_detection.description: Outlier detection algorithms — isolation forests, statistical boundaries, autoencoder reconstruction error. Finding what doesn't belong.
anomaly_detection.name: Anomaly Detection
anomaly_detection.qfep_connection: Anomalies are high-F surprises — data points that the F-model cannot predict. Detection algorithms learn the boundary between expected E(S) and genuine novelty. The queer reading: who counts as anomalous depends on whose F-model defines normal.

joint_learn_walk.description: RL agent learning to walk — reward shaping, policy gradient, emergent locomotion. Joints discover coordinated movement through trial and error.
joint_learn_walk.name: Joint Learn Walk (Reinforcement Learning)
joint_learn_walk.qfep_connection: Reinforcement learning as embodied F-minimization — the agent builds an internal model through interaction, reducing surprise about its own body. Emergent locomotion is the system discovering its own edge of chaos: coordinated movement from noisy exploration.

explainable_ai_xai_vr.description: Interactive SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM explanations
explainable_ai_xai_vr.name: ExplainableAIXAI_VR
explainable_ai_xai_vr.qfep_connection: SHAP, LIME, Grad-CAM — the instruments that ask a black box *why*, and get partial, honest, contestable answers. The accountability room: after seven chambers of learning that works without understanding, this one insists the machine show its reasons. Not because the reasons are the truth, but because a decision no one can question is a decision no one can refuse.

russell_paradox_workbench.name: Russell's Paradox Workbench
russell_paradox_workbench.description: Six set descriptions, from subsets to unrestricted Russell comprehension and finite separation. Opt-in physical IN / OUT buttons let visitors test both self-membership assumptions. At cell 5 both answers contradict the rule. Cell 6 filters the existing set of finite ordinals U={0,1,2,3}; the result equals U but is not a member of U, so OUT agrees. Dots and orbit illustrate the argument; the workbench does not decide arbitrary set formulas.
russell_paradox_workbench.capacity: Test the membership rule, then change its domain

self_membership_set.name: SelfMembershipSet
self_membership_set.description: The set that contains itself, all the way down - R = {x : x not-in x}, is R in R?

barber_paradox.name: BarberParadox
barber_paradox.description: Russell's Paradox: the barber who shaves all who don't shave themselves - does he shave himself? The rule eats itself.

russell_set_box.description: Nested boxes visualizing Russell's Paradox - the set of all sets that don't contain themselves
russell_set_box.qfep_connection: Self-reference creates edges in formal systems
interactions: click to open layers
reveals infinite regress

russell_set_box.name: Russell's Set Box

liar_loop.name: LiarLoop
liar_loop.description: The liar paradox: THIS STATEMENT IS FALSE - a truth value that oscillates forever, never settling.

hilbert_hotel.description: Animated Hilbert's Hotel paradox - infinite rooms all occupied, yet a new guest always fits by shifting n to n+1
hilbert_hotel.gamwell_reference: Chapter 6: Cantor's transfinite numbers and Hilbert's Grand Hotel
hilbert_hotel.qfep_connection: Infinity is not a limit but a structure - countable infinity accommodates more without expanding

dna.measured: PREDICTION FALSIFIED. Predicted 3.5-4.0%; actual 1.16-1.20%, unchanged from 1.17% at framing 1.0. Same diagnosis as its two siblings: the case, dial, arcs and SELF-TEST header are invariant, and what the axis moves is a thin black needle, a 3 cm lamp, a lever and a small card. RUN-TO-RUN NOISE MEASURED AT +/-15%: two identical sweeps of unchanged code and registry gave rice_verifier_booth 1.32% then 1.11%, and critic_regress_stack 5.07% then 4.35%. The sweep is not deterministic, so any single-run verdict within about 15% of the 3% threshold is a coin toss reported as a fact. Numbers below are the range across both runs, not a point.
dna.remedy: Ink. The needle is the thinnest element and it carries the injected-vs-green distinction almost alone. THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS DELICATE: two of the five values are MEANT to be nearly identical -- `unproven` and `certified` differ only by a sealed wire, a caption and the mounted red card, because the difference between them is history rather than reading. A repair that separated those two would be a repair AGAINST the artifact's argument. The correct move is to enlarge the red record card, not to make the two greens differ.
dna.colour_finding: The critic rescued two pairs here from a false twin verdict: absent vs unproven (focus 4.69%, colour 10.59%) and absent vs silent (focus 5.07%, colour 12.93%). Luminance cannot see the lamp's hue change; the eye can.
dna.still_note: TWO OF THE FIVE VALUES READ GREEN AND ARE MEANT TO BE NEARLY IDENTICAL. `unproven` and `certified` differ by a sealed lever wire, a caption, and the mounted red record card -- and that near-identity IS the argument, because the difference between them is history rather than reading. A twin verdict on that specific pair would be the artifact working, not failing. The values that must separate are injected (needle hard over into the red arc, a wholesale change) and absent (no lever at all). First sweep: frame 1.17%, focus 14.84%, LOCAL.
dna.expected: At framing 0.55 the frame edge is 1.25 m against 2.28 m, 3.3x in area, so expect frame near 3.5-4.0%. If the critic reports a TWIN on unproven-vs-certified, read it as confirmation and not as a defect -- the correct repair would be to make the red record card larger, not to make the two greens differ.

negative_control_fixture.name: Negative Control Fixture
negative_control_fixture.description: A gauge that earns its green light only by first being made to go red on a planted fault
negative_control_fixture.qfep_connection: The one honest move after Rice: an instrument cannot be proven correct, but it can be proven capable of failing

dna.measured: THE ONE THAT BITES, and the only one whose axis is silhouette-scale rather than detail-scale: frame 4.35-5.07%, focus 29-31%. Confirmed by per-variant pixel measurement rather than by the verdict alone -- subject HEIGHT varies 19% (single) / 22% (circular) / 39-40% (stacked, outside, sealed) of the frame, while every sibling holds constant height across all five of its values. Camera distance is fixed per token, not per variant, so that height variation is the artifact and not the rig. This is why leaving it at framing 1.0 was correct: its argument is in the outline. RUN-TO-RUN NOISE MEASURED AT +/-15%: two identical sweeps of unchanged code and registry gave rice_verifier_booth 1.32% then 1.11%, and critic_regress_stack 5.07% then 4.35%. The sweep is not deterministic, so any single-run verdict within about 15% of the 3% threshold is a coin toss reported as a fact. Numbers below are the range across both runs, not a point.
dna.framing_why: LEFT AT 1.0 DELIBERATELY, while its three siblings come in to 0.55. This axis is not a detail: the dark mark travels the full height of the body -- footing to crown is about 1.3 m on a 1.32 m subject -- and `sealed` adds a shell over the whole stack. That is a silhouette-scale change, which is what full-frame fitting is for, and it is why this was the one token of four to bite on the first sweep at frame 2.95% / focus 25.50%. Tightening it would raise the number without making the argument any more visible, which is chasing the metric rather than reading the picture.
dna.still_note: The mark is the same object under every value -- same radius, same unlit black -- and only its POSITION argues. An axis that shrank it as critics were added would contradict the file's own truth line. `outside` is the one exception and it is principled: the mark shrinks there because a differently-constructed check genuinely does catch more, and it reappears under the outsider rather than vanishing.

critic_regress_stack.name: Critic Regress Stack
critic_regress_stack.description: Add a critic to check the system, then a critic to check the critic; the blind spot never closes, it moves
critic_regress_stack.qfep_connection: Conservation of the irreducible one level up: inductive bias can be relocated, never removed
