It carries a set_lambda() that shifts blue to green to red with distance from 0.4, and nothing in the repository calls it (qfep_reactor connects a slider to its own set_lambda, not to this one), so in every room the core stands green and alive for every value of lambda there is. You cannot see that the edge is NARROW if the two things it is narrow between are never present. The two tints are copied out of that dead function, not invented: order is the blue it lerps toward below 0.4, chaos the red above it. order crystallises the same anatomy - a 7-segment faceted shell you can count the sides of, twelve fixed nodes at exact intervals instead of an orbit, and _process returning immediately, so no pulse, no rotation, no shimmer. chaos removes the shell (the boundary goes first) and leaves a dim speck inside ninety seeded scattered points with nothing holding them.
dna.declined: THE PULSE, which is the tempting knob and the one the identity block names as critical. A rate is invisible to a still - info_board was swept across five duration exports and produced six identical tiles - so pulse_speed and pulse_amount stay exports and stay undeclared. Every value above is form: facet count, node count, a shell that is there or is not.
dna.kin: lambda_slider and phi_slider share `calibration` (optimum, band, dispute, gap, none) for how a RAIL marks the right answer. Not reused: this is not a rail and has no scale to mark. fluid_form (phi>0) and rigid_sculpture (phi<0) are bodies at positions the way this one is, and `station` would fit all three - but not one value list, because their line is phi (resist vs embrace change) and this one's is lambda (order vs chaos). Same question, different term of the formula; a shared word over two vocabularies would claim a kinship the geometry does not have.
dna.still_note: the scatter is seeded (SCATTER_SEED), so chaos is one arrangement rather than a new object per boot, and order is frozen, so its frame is deterministic. Only the default's pulse is still time-dependent at capture, and it is compared against two values that differ in structure and hue rather than in phase.
dna.framing_note: framing 0.45: the chaos cloud reaches about 1.15x core_radius, so the fixed camera unions to roughly a 1 m box and the 0.8 m shell would otherwise sit at about 5% of frame.

edge_core.name: Edge Core
edge_core.description: Central orb for edge of chaos. Pulsing, alive, responsive to λ.
edge_core.qfep_connection: The central orb of the edge of chaos — pulsing, alive, responsive to λ. Turn the dial toward 0.4 and it quickens; this is the equation's beating heart, the place where F and E(S) balance closely enough that neither wins and *complexity* becomes possible. The single most important object in the laboratory.

droplet_cusp.name: Droplet Cusp
droplet_cusp.description: A boolean funnel and a soft ball, and the question of whether they can fit. Rebuilt 2026-10-13 at Palle's instruction from a posed surface of revolution into a physics experiment: the block, flare, bore and waist washer are genuine CSG subtractions, sectioned so the interior argues in public behind a glass pane, and a soft sphere is dropped on the mouth. The settled pose is the verdict, printed on the plate: PASSED (through to the tray), HANGS IN THE WAIST (the droplet forms, bulged below and necked above - nobody drew that teardrop, the waist makes it), or RESTS PROUD. waist sets the washer hole as a fraction of the ball's rest radius; flesh sets what the ball negotiates with - firm bites where it touches, jelly lubricates, balloon insists on volume. Measured at both 60 and 90 Hz: snug/firm passes, scant/firm never passes, and at the tight waist firm hangs at -91 mm while jelly drips clean through to the tray - softness measurably buys passage. The ball is the artifact's OWN verlet pressure shell (42 points, 80 faces, per-flesh grip) colliding analytically against the same flare/bore/washer numbers the CSG draws, because four engine substrates failed measurably first: CSG trimesh let jelly tunnel 4.3 km, sphere and capsule colliders generate no soft contacts at all in this engine (probe_softbody_shapes), a box ring fed the solver contradictory push-outs, and a post-and-collar deck ejected the ball off its edges. GodotPhysics SoftBody3D cannot do squeeze-through-aperture; owning the sim gives one source of truth and determinism without a seed. Readable in code via verdict_word(), ball_top_m(), ball_bottom_m(), is_settled().

predicted_degeneracy.basis: LOWER BOUND, as every prediction in this corpus has been, by 1.5x to 6.7x. At snug the hole is wider than the ball, so every flesh value PASSES and settles in the same tray; firm and pliant differ only in how much the resting shell slumps (12 vs 6 constraint iterations), a few millimetres across a ball that is maybe 15 percent of frame behind the section cut. FRAME = 0.15 * 0.07 = 1.0 percent.
predicted_degeneracy.what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: STOP AND TEST THE HARNESS. Below about 1 percent the likely causes in order are (a) the capture shooting before the ball settles - the pose IS the verdict and a mid-fall frame is a verdict about nothing; is_settled() is readable and the plate says SETTLING; (b) the passed ball sitting so low in the tray that the section lip hides it from the canonical standpoint, which is a fixture problem; (c) a flesh value the recipe match does not carry, which silently returns the firm default. Open the PNGs.
predicted_degeneracy.structural_degeneracy_predicted: SAID BEFORE THE SWEEP, fourth artifact running, because every one so far had a structural pair I either missed or half-named: expect flesh to be CONDITIONAL on waist at BOTH ENDS - at snug all four fleshes pass (the hole outruns the material), at scant none pass (geometry outruns it again), and the axis only argues in the middle two values. Equally expect waist to look alive everywhere, since the drawn washer hole changes even when the outcome does not. Read the per-pair rows grouped by waist, never the axis mean, and read the 60-versus-90 Hz question as settled: the probe gates both.

edge_of_chaos_unlocked.name: Edge of Chaos Unlocked
edge_of_chaos_unlocked.description: Gray-Scott field on an authored lambda parameter route. Every tenure uses a normalized neighbour stencil and bounded timestep. Optional comparison_study shows equal-time fields with dt and dt/2; restart repeats the seed, new seed changes it.

parameters.comparison_study: on/off: paired timestep display, compact controls and B-field RMS difference

edge_of_chaos_unlocked.qfep_connection: Who chooses the model, numerical resolution and observable used to recognise a pattern? Parameter bands do not establish criticality or life.

dna.default: station=edge, readout=numeral - the shipped orb line for line. station=edge holds current_lambda at 0.4, which is this file's own initialiser, so _update_visuals paints exactly the colour, light energy, particle velocity and spread it always painted; the core is the same smooth 32x16 sphere at radius 0.3, the cloud the same 0.35 m emission sphere, and the particle count is int(50 * 2.0 * 1.0), the same 100 the old line computed. readout=numeral builds the same Label3D - same text, font_size 32, position (0, 0.6, 0), billboard, modulate white at 0.8 - and rungs 2 and 3 are skipped, so no rule and no plane geometry is created at all. The five reach-paths are Corridor_QFEP_Sandbox (bare token), QFEP_Sandbox (qfep_reactor:0:1.5, which is rotation and y-offset shorthand, not config), MissionHall_Qfeplaboratory and Trial_wfc_qfeplaboratory (qfep_reactor->edge_of_chaos_unlocked, a transformation target), and Curation_Bay_qfeplaboratory_6 (inside a curation_station collection, whose #with_wall / #with_pillars / #with_barrier flags are the station's). None carries either key, and apply_grid_config returns without touching anything unless a token names a word the reactor does not already hold, so nothing rebuilds for any of them.
dna.was: no declared axis and nothing to declare - the runner's NO TURNABLE KNOBS was literally true. The file had ZERO @export and no apply_grid_config. Everything the description leads with (pulses, glows, blue to green to red) was computed every frame from current_lambda, a plain var, driven by a set_lambda() that nothing calls.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04. THE DRIVER IS DEAD. _connect_to_sliders() waits one frame and collects the group 'qfep_slider'; no file in the repository ever calls add_to_group('qfep_slider') - lambda_slider.gd and phi_slider.gd declare the signals and neither joins the group - so set_lambda and set_phi have never fired in any room and current_lambda has stood at 0.4 everywhere, forever. An orb whose entire claim is that the state MOVES has only ever drawn the middle state. That is the same disease edge_core was promoted for earlier the same day, found independently in a second file, and `station` is the same cure: where this reactor stands when nothing is driving it, which today is everywhere. Nothing about it is invented - COLOR_ORDER, COLOR_EDGE and COLOR_CHAOS are already constants in this file (they are the very ones edge_core's promotion copied out), and the three lambdas are read off this file's own branches: 0.05 is CRYSTALLINE by get_state_name() and below the 0.3 colour split, 0.4 is the shipped value, 0.95 is DISSOLUTION and above both the 0.7 pulse split and the 0.6 jitter split. Each station is also a FORM, not only a tint: order facets the orb to 7 segments and 4 rings (edge_core's numbers, so the pair crystallises alike), chaos shrinks the body to a 0.12x speck and takes the boundary off the cloud (emission radius 0.35 -> 0.85, three times the population). `readout` is the second question, about the placard rather than the body: numeral is the shipped label; gradation lays the lambda line under the orb with the edge band painted across 0.3..0.5, the interval is_at_edge() has always tested for and the artifact has never drawn; lattice raises that line into the lambda x phi plane this reactor is standing in, with the band as a REGION and a marker at its point. set_lambda() itself is untouched, so if a driver is ever wired up it overrides the colour exactly as before.
dna.kin: `station` (edge, order, chaos) is edge_core's word, its three values and its fallback rule, character for character, and reused on purpose: these are two bodies on ONE line - lambda, order against chaos - and they should measure alike, which is itself the check. edge_core's own note says station would fit fluid_form (phi>0) and rigid_sculpture (phi<0) as positions but not with this value list, because their line is phi; that reasoning is what licenses the reuse here and forbids it there. `readout` (none, numeral, gradation, lattice) is taken from commons/primitives/line/line.gd, its twin xyz_slider_plate.gd and qfep_calibrator, including the rank-ladder shape (each rung strictly additive over the one below) and the rule that an unrecognised word reads as numeral rather than none, so a typo cannot strip the placard off a live room. NOT REUSED: `calibration` (optimum, band, dispute, gap, none) belongs to lambda_slider and phi_slider and asks how a RAIL marks the right answer - the rule this artifact grows at rung 2 does mark a band, but the axis it belongs to is about which rung the placard is at, not about the marking; `formation` and `flux` are the neighbours' words for arrangement and for where a displacement is spent, and neither is a position on a line. NOTE also that qfep_reactor_bench is a DIFFERENT token with its own `complement` axis - nine of the eleven map hits for the string 'qfep_reactor' are that bench, not this orb.
dna.declined: THE PULSE AND THE GLOW, which are what the registry description leads with ('pulses and glows based on lambda and phi'). The evidence is one still PNG per value and a rate is invisible to it - info_board was swept across five duration exports and produced six identical tiles. pulse_speed, the breathing scale and the emission wobble are left exactly as written and none is declared. Every value above is form or place: facet count, cloud radius, a scale drawn or not drawn.
dna.fixture_note: freeze_time pins pulse_phase and the chaos jitter so that three stations are three photographs of one instant instead of of three phases - the breath is about +/-10% of core scale and the pulse SPEED itself differs per station (1.0, 3.0, 5-7), so an unpinned sweep partly measures which frame the camera caught. It ships at -1.0, which is live time and the shipped behaviour, and is left UNTYPED on purpose because a typed float rejects the string a fixture passes before _ready. The jitter and the chaotic pulse term now draw from a seeded RandomNumberGenerator (JITTER_SEED) instead of the global randf, so chaos is one arrangement rather than a new object every boot; neither branch is reachable at the default lambda of 0.4.
dna.measurement_risk: On `station`, chaos shrinks the only MeshInstance3D in the scene from 0.3 to 0.036 m radius - the particle cloud is a GPUParticles3D and the capture AABB counts neither it nor the light - so a fit-by-diagonal camera will zoom hard on the speck and that frame is NOT comparable with edge's until subject % is checked. Read subject % before reading the verdict, and add a framing hint or a layers = 0 anchor if chaos measures as an implausible landslide. On `readout`, the rule and the plane are deliberately built inside the core's own vertical extent (|y| <= 0.28 against radius 0.3) and in front of it at z = 0.52, so the AABB grows sideways only and the artifact's seating on the floor is identical at every rung; but they are fine geometry beside a bright emissive orb and may need a framing hint the way line_interface did.
dna.wiring_study_note: 2026-09-20: the historical driver account above describes the default mode. QFEP_Sandbox now opts into a separate, explicit same-hall connection with visible received values. Other placements retain their original mode.

qfep_reactor.name: QFEP Reactor
qfep_reactor.description: An animated orb with authored lambda colour/speed and signed phi lightness mappings. Optional wiring_study connects exactly one pair of same-hall handles, displays received values, and can cut or repeat the response. Its toy score does not measure entropy.

parameters.wiring_study: on/off: local CONNECT / CUT and REPEAT experiment; actual receiver values and particle maximum speed

qfep_reactor.qfep_connection: A local experiment in who receives a control value. CONNECT delivers two handle values, CUT retains the last accepted inputs, and REPEAT restarts the animation. The response law remains authored: a colour or pulse is not a measurement of freedom, life or entropy.

reactive_particles.name: Reactive Particles
reactive_particles.description: Alias for reactive_particle_field. Particles that respond to λ and φ parameters.
reactive_particles.qfep_connection: A particle field that answers λ and φ directly — move the dials and the swarm reorganizes, order to chaos to edge, live feedback between the equation and its consequences. The laboratory's responsiveness made ambient: proof that the terms are not decoration but *controls*, and the world obeys them.

queer_morphology_specimen.description: A contained soft-body specimen with local Lambda stiffness/pressure and signed Phi damping/drag controls. Live mechanical readout, three sample pairs and PULSE / STEADY reveal authored conditions of response. Jarred, cracked, escaped and clouded forms remain distinct.
interactions: observe
queer_morphology_specimen.name: Queer Morphology Specimen
queer_morphology_specimen.qfep_connection: Ask who can revise the conditions under which a body holds together: the visitor can change coefficients and imposed breathing, while the response law and container remain authored. This is not an assay of life, entropy or queerness.

entropy_ceiling.description: The QFEP-laboratory seam, the thesis at its most self-aware. The lab measures order and disorder, but its meters are quantized - a finite ladder of ticks, a needle that steps. True maximum entropy is a limit the instrument can never reach; push toward it and the needle pins at the last tick, reading MAX - a finite number standing in for an infinity it cannot hold. The lab that studies the limit is built out of the limit.
entropy_ceiling.name: Entropy Ceiling
entropy_ceiling.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for qfeplaboratory. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

entropy_meter.name: Entropy Meter
entropy_meter.description: Visual gauge showing current E(S) entropy level. A filling tube that responds to lambda. Low=blue, medium=green, high=red. Classic lab instrument aesthetic.
entropy_meter.qfep_connection: The tube reads E(S), but the value poured into it is λ itself, renamed at the signal boundary and lerped at smoothing 5 so the liquid never startles. Lab-instrument calm is the actual product: a scalar in glass, made slow enough to trust.

grasp_cabinet.name: Grasp Cabinet
grasp_cabinet.description: Six compartments, three over three. Five hold the SAME 56 mm object under the `grasp` family's five theories of its handle — atom, socket, chorus, hollow, swarm — read live out of qfep_term_grasp.gd's own const and never retyped. The sixth holds the ledger. A hand at true human scale (18 mm fingertip pads, a 15 mm finger, a 158 mm opening span) closes on all five at once, and `contact` changes what that hand is: a palm cupping from below on eight golden-angle pads, a two-point pinch across the equator, three fingers hooking up from underneath, or a twelve-point icosahedral net closing from every side. `closure` changes how much of the closing is drawn: the hand open and nothing claimed; plus a mark where each contact actually stopped; plus the track it swept getting there; plus the ledger, five rows of bars above and below a rule at the thing's own nominal surface. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one closure computed per theory at build time from one part list, and that same part list is what gets drawn.
interactions: find the two compartments a hand cannot tell apart, and work out why
set contact=pinch and notice that the socket and the wireframe hold your fingers out at almost exactly the same place, 0.28 mm apart, for completely different reasons
set contact=net and read the socket's twelve bars: four at the rim, four on the dome, four down among the ribs — one object, three answers
set closure=depth and see that the only theory whose bars go ABOVE the rule is the one with nothing to pick up
walk the top row against the bottom row and ask which of the five is a claim about the object and which is a claim about its neighbours
grasp_cabinet.qfep_connection: Five theories of where a handle lives — in the object, in its bounded absence, in the set it belongs to, in its outline, in a distribution — standing at once so that none of them can pass as the natural one. The cabinet cannot exempt itself: six compartments holding five claims IS a housing, and a housing is what `socket` says the grip belongs to, so the most innocent-looking piece of furniture in the room is already taking one of the five sides. What the hand then shows is that the affordance was never a property of the object at all. Change nothing about the thing and change only what closes on it, and four of the five readings rearrange; change to a grip that never leaves the body's own surface and two of the five theories become indistinguishable, not because they agree but because one of them was never talking about the body.
grasp_cabinet.relationships: synthesis over the `grasp` family; adopts its five words by exhibiting them rather than sweeping them. Closest relative is taxonomy_hall, which does the same thing to `taxonomy` — five bays instead of four, and a hand instead of a rank rail.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: 0.576 x 0.446 x 0.189 m — a bench cabinet, well inside a single 1.0 m grid cell, and it wants a table under it: at floor level the ledger row is 3 cm off the ground and unreadable. Every compartment opens toward +Z and there is no glass, no door and no front lip, so the artifact wants approaching from +Z; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. The back is a solid panel, so it takes a wall happily. There is no collider anywhere in the file — the pathfinder will route straight through it, which is correct, because there is nothing to walk into that a table would not already have declared.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node here is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh, SphereMesh, TorusMesh or CylinderMesh. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particle system and no Label3D, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present. X = 3 compartments of 0.18160 plus 4 panels of 0.00784 = 0.57616. Y = 2 compartments of 0.21120 plus 3 shelves of 0.00784 = 0.44592, running from 0 (the carcass underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 0.44592. Z from -0.09864 (behind the back panel) to +0.09080 (the compartment mouths). THE BOX IS IDENTICAL AT ALL SIXTEEN VARIANTS: the carcass encloses every mark either axis can draw, because the compartment was sized to the hand's opening envelope (OPEN + PAD_R = 0.088) plus 0.0028 of clearance, and no closure rung puts anything outside it. The camera therefore does not move between tiles for any reason whatever.

dna.axis_shape: `contact` sits SIDE BY SIDE — four different KINDS of closure (two opposed points, a cupping cone, three parallel insertions, a converging polyhedron), none of which contains another, so they are a set and any two of them are a comparison. `closure` NESTS — none is contained in closed is contained in travel is contained in depth, each rung keeping every mark the last one drew, so it is a sequence and must be swept in order. Both are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a parallel axis loses a case, dropping the tail of a nested one only lowers the ceiling. `contact` is declared FIRST for exactly that reason — build_dna_gallery sweeps the first two axes and trims the LATER one from the tail.
dna.default:
contact=palm, closure=closed. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `palm` AND NOT `net`. `net` is the fullest grip and the wrong default: twelve pads plus twelve marks per compartment surround the body so completely that the five theories are largely hidden behind the hand, and a cabinet whose exhibit is obscured by its own instrument is showing the instrument. `palm` comes from BELOW, so the top of every body is clear in every compartment and the five theories are all legible at a glance, while the eight contacts are still enough to show a profile rather than a point. It is also the grip a 56 mm sphere actually invites. `pinch` is the thinnest — two contacts, and they land at the equator where all five theories put their outermost material, so it is the grip that separates them LEAST (four of its ten theory pairs are under 3 mm). `hook` is an insertion rather than a closure and is a special case, not a baseline.

WHY `closed` AND NOT `depth`. `depth` is the most striking single frame and the most misleading one: it ranks the five theories by how far in the hand got, and on that ranking `swarm` wins outright — the one theory of the five where there is nothing whatever to carry off. A scoreboard that calls the emptiest claim the best grip is a fact about scoreboards, which is why it is one token away rather than the frame a visitor meets first. `closed` shows the open pad and the shut pad together, so the whole closure is legible without a single added mark and nothing is asserted that is not shown. `none` is the emptiest rung by definition: a hand held open around five objects and no answer.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the five `grasp` declarations leave unbuilt — and in this family it is not merely unbuilt but unbuildable, because all five names are one scene: a single sphere can only be one of atom, socket, chorus, hollow or swarm at a time, so no member can ever put two of the five side by side.
dna.kin:
THE ONE-SCENE-MANY-NAMES CASE, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. All five tokens that declare `grasp` resolve to res://commons/primitives/point/grab_sphere_point_with_color.tscn — one distinct scene across five names. The tell the corpus keeps rediscovering is identical export counts across siblings, and here it is exact by construction: the scene's four scripts (grab_sphere.gd 10, point_mesh.gd 1, point_color.gd 2, qfep_term_grasp.gd 1) give every one of the five tokens the same 14 exports, and all five carry the same `parameters` block (footprint, size_group). Four of them additionally carry a `default_params.color` that distinguishes them — FF6060, 4080FF, 40FF80, FF80FF — and the fifth, the plain primitive grab_sphere_point_with_color, carries none. That is the entire difference between the five names.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS CABINET. When a shared vocabulary is honest the siblings measure ALIKE; here they cannot measure otherwise, because they ARE the same object. So the family's `grasp` axis has, strictly, one subject and five labels for it, and the interesting question is not whether the siblings agree but whether the five VALUES do anything distinguishable — which is what this cabinet answers, and the answer is that two of them do not, under any grip.

THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED. grasp_cabinet.gd opens with
const GRASP_SRC := preload("res://commons/primitives/point/qfep_term_grasp.gd")
and the bays, their number and their order come from GRASP_SRC's own GRASPS at build time, read as a direct const access rather than through Object.get() — a const is not a property, so get() would return null and the cabinet would fall back silently to its own copy, which is the exact drift the preload prevents. get_script_constant_map() was considered and rejected: it is non-static and cannot be called on the class. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a value the family declares that this cabinet has no bay for, and a bay this cabinet builds that the family has dropped.

ONE DECLARATION ORDER, NO DIVERGENCE. Unlike `taxonomy`, which had two orders across seven members, all five `grasp` declarations list atom | socket | chorus | hollow | swarm character for character — which follows trivially from their being one scene. There is no trimming hazard on the family word.

SOLIDITY IS BORROWED FROM THE FAMILY TOO, and this is the borrowing that does the most work. qfep_term_grasp.gd's _mat(c, energy, alpha) enters its transparency branch iff alpha < 1.0. That one line is taken as the family's own definition of a surface that is there, and this cabinet's probe reads it: the socket's lower shell is alpha 0.55 and a hand passes through it; the swarm's outer two shells are 0.92 and 0.72 and a hand passes through those too, so only the innermost twelve grains stop anything; everything else is 1.0 and stops a hand. Nothing about what is SOLID here was chosen by this artifact.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A CABINET RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

The family's five words are five claims about where the handle of a thing lives. `atom` says in the object: one closed pellet, uncuttable, self-identical. `socket` says in a bounded absence: half a body and half a measured void behind a bright rim. `chorus` says in the set: the thing is one of four on a rail and you lift the row when you lift it. `hollow` says in the outline: the substance is gone and the contour survives, and your hand closes on a contour. `swarm` says in a distribution: no body at all, a graded population you could be inside rather than an object you could carry off. Five registry names declare this word and every one of them STANDS IN one claim and forgoes the other four — and because all five names are ONE SCENE, that is not a habit but a hard limit. No member can ever hold two of these at once.

So the cabinet builds the thing ONCE — a 56 mm sphere, one colour, one radius — and stands it five times in the family's own order, read live from qfep_term_grasp.gd. What varies instead is the SECOND decision every one of these claims makes and none of them states: what closes on it. A handle is only a handle relative to a grasper, and the family draws no grasper at all.

WHAT IT FOUND, all of it computed in Python before anything was built.

(1) A HAND CANNOT TELL `atom` FROM `chorus`. Under all four grips the two bays return penetration profiles identical to the bit — 0.00 mm, not 0.00-to-two-decimals — because chorus does not touch the body. Read the family's own code: `atom` returns before the match and leaves the shipped SphereMesh alone; `chorus` also leaves `mesh` alone, sets material_override and adds a rail BESIDE it. Every other value replaces the mesh or effaces it. So of the five theories, exactly one makes no claim about the object at all, and it is unfalsifiable by touch — which is not the same as being wrong. THIS IS THE FINDING, NOT A DEAD BAY. The two compartments still look nothing alike.

(2) THE WIREFRAME HOLDS YOUR HAND OUT FURTHER THAN THE SOLID BALL DOES, which is the opposite of the obvious reading. `hollow` measures -11.52 mm against `atom`'s -9.00 under pinch and net. The family builds its rings as tori of ring radius R and tube 0.090 R, so the cage stands 1.09 R proud of the surface it describes, and a fingertip meets wire 2.52 mm before it would have met ball. An outline is not an opening.

(3) `socket` IS THE ONLY ONE WHOSE ANSWER DEPENDS ON WHICH SIDE YOU COME FROM. Palm from below: -2.69 to -1.04, mean -2.100. Pinch at the equator: -11.80, the furthest OUT of any theory under any grip, because the rim's outer surface is at 1.10 R. Net from all sides: a three-tier reading of -11.80 (four pads on the rim), -9.00 (four on the dome) and -3.42 to -3.26 (four down among the ribs). A swing of 14.4 mm on one object. The other four theories are isotropic; this one is a fragment and reports as one.

(4) `socket` AND `hollow` MEASURE ALIKE UNDER `pinch`, 0.28 mm APART, AND IT IS A COINCIDENCE WORTH KEEPING. The socket's rim reaches 1.10 R and the hollow's great circles reach 1.09 R, so a two-point grip at the equator is held out at nearly the same place by a bright flange and by a wire. Two completely different theories, one number. Nothing was tuned to produce this and nothing will be tuned to remove it.

(5) THE ONLY THEORY A HAND GETS INSIDE IS THE ONE WITH NOTHING TO HOLD. `swarm` returns positive penetration under every grip, +2.70 to +6.91 mm, because its outer two shells are drawn transparent and a hand passes through them to the twelve opaque grains at 0.42 R. It is the deepest reading in the cabinet and it is a reading of a cloud. That is precisely why `depth` is not the default.

AND TWO FAULTS IN THE INSTRUMENT, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE REPLICA AND BOTH THE SAME FAULT.

(a) The `net`'s twelve directions were first taken from the family's own _fib_points(12) — which is exactly how the swarm's inner shell of twelve grains is built. All twelve probes ran straight down the twelve grain axes and returned one number to the millimetre. Replaced with the twelve icosahedron vertices.

(b) The `palm`'s eight pads were first spaced evenly at 45 degrees — which is exactly the spacing of the socket's eight ribs. Every pad landed on a rib and the bay reported -2.69 mm with a standard deviation of 0.000. Offsetting by half a step is not a fix: all eight then slip between the ribs and report +0.02 mm, sd 0.000 — a swing of 2.71 mm and a change of SIGN, still an artefact. At golden-angle azimuths the same eight pads read -2.69 to -1.04, mean -2.100, sd 0.564. The hollow bay tells the same story more quietly: sd 0.000 at even azimuths, 0.345 at golden. A measuring instrument built out of the thing it measures will report perfect uniformity and be believed, twice in one file.
dna.declines:
`grasp` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design.

The five values sit SIDE BY SIDE, read out of the member's CODE and not its prose. qfep_term_grasp.gd spends the word in a single `match grasp:` whose branches are mutually exclusive treatments of ONE mesh: atom returns before the match and keeps it; socket REPLACES `mesh` with a hemisphere; chorus keeps it and adds a rail beside it; hollow and swarm both call _efface_body() and add rings or grains. Three different fates for one mesh — kept, replaced, effaced — so no value contains another and there is no all-at-once reading that is secretly the top rung. Parallel values means the simultaneity is the object: hold all five standing and vary something else. An axis on the word would demolish four fifths of the exhibit at every turn, and the big number it produced would be a measurement of the cabinet being dismantled.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE HANDED-DOWN READING OF THE WORD. The brief this artifact was built from glossed the five values, and on three of them the code says something else. The code wins and the correction is recorded here.
  `socket` was glossed as "a receptacle — the grip belongs to the housing, not to the object". There is no housing anywhere in the family's socket. What the code builds is a solid upper hemisphere, a bright rim torus at the equator, a lower hemisphere of radius 0.985 R drawn at alpha 0.55, and eight ribs from rim to south pole. It is HALF A BODY AND A BOUNDED VOID: the receptacle is part of the object, and the object is admitting it is a fragment and showing exactly how much of it is not there.
  `chorus` was glossed as "many identical handles where any will do". The family's siblings are the OTHER THREE TERMS of QFE = F - lambda*E(S) + phi*deltaE(S,t), in their own registry colours, in the formula's written order — the whole point being that they are NOT interchangeable and that lifting one lifts a structured set. See below for what this cabinet had to give up to transpose that.
  `hollow` was glossed as "a grip defined by what is absent, the space your hand goes into". Half right. The code keeps the OUTLINE and destroys the substance, so a hand closes on a contour rather than into a recess — and this cabinet measures that the contour is 2.52 mm PROUD of the surface it describes, so the hollow thing is harder to reach into than the full one. The prose predicts a recess; the geometry delivers a cage.

WHAT THE CHORUS BAY GAVE UP, stated rather than buried. Three deviations from the family's numbers, all forced by there being one thing here and no formula.
  The siblings are the same colour as the body, dimmed, where the family gives them three different hexes. There is no formula, so there are no other terms; four copies of one thing is the honest transposition and what it loses is exactly the claim the family's chorus makes best.
  CHOR_SPAN is 1.25 R against the family's 2.7 R and CHOR_OVER 0.35 R against 0.9 R. At the family's pitch the rail is 9.9 R wide, which would set the width of all six compartments and leave five of them four fifths air.
  CHOR_RAIL_Y is -3.6 R against the family's -2.4 R, and this one is not cosmetic. The hand's opening envelope is a sphere of radius 3.143 R about the body; the nearest sibling sits 1.25 R aside with radius 0.60 R, so the rail must drop until sqrt(1.25^2 + y^2) - 0.60 > 3.143 + 0.321, i.e. |y| > 3.527 R. At the family's -2.4 R the hand's own opening position is INSIDE the rail and the cabinet would be drawing a hand embedded in furniture. THE COST IS FINDING (1): with the rail out of reach, nothing the hand does can distinguish chorus from atom. That cost is reported, not hidden, and it was measured rather than assumed.

THE RECURSION WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, and it is the interesting decline. Six compartments holding five theories IS a housing, and a housing is what one of the five theories says the grip belongs to — so the cabinet is standing inside the question it asks, exactly as taxonomy_hall's row of bays is itself the table claim. It could have gone further and applied the family word to its own compartments. It does not, for the mechanical reason taxonomy_hall gives: the registry would then carry a sixth `grasp` declaration with the same five values as the other five, and every tool that groups a family by axis name would compare its bite against theirs as though it measured the same thing. It does not: theirs restage a BODY, this one would restage a CABINET. So the recursion is stated in prose and not swept.

PER-BAY CAPTIONS ARE DECLINED. There is no text anywhere in this artifact. At 1021.84 px per metre a legible glyph would be about 1.2 cm tall, a fifth of the object's diameter, and there is no surface in a compartment to hang it on that is not in front of a mark. Identity is carried by the geometry: no two bays share a silhouette.

A `scale` AXIS WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED — the same hand at four sizes, which is a real question about affordance and would have been a second axis about the hand. Refused because two axes both about the grasper would leave the exhibit itself never varying in any respect, and because the honest version of it is a single fact better stated once: at the family's own 24 mm a human fingertip pad is 75% of the object's diameter and there are not four distinguishable grips to be had. That is why this cabinet's thing is 56 mm.
dna.measured: PREDICTION HIT, EXACTLY. Swept 2026-08-13 at --max=16, all sixteen frames. Closest pair 0.16% of frame at subject 46.8% — and the registry had named that pair before any capture: `closure` closed against travel AT `contact` = pinch, predicted 0.11% frame. Right pair, 1.5x on the number. The arithmetic holds up: at pinch there are two contacts per compartment, so `travel` adds ten stems of roughly 364 px each against a 625x582 crop — about one percent of it. At `hook` the same pair has fifteen stems and is wider. NOT THE FURNITURE-IN-FRONT CASE despite looking exactly like it: 46.8% subject with a 0.16% pair is the signature that table row warns about, and here the carcass is honest load-bearing furniture — six bays are what lets five theories of the grip stand at once — and nothing occludes a mark. Checked against the PNG, not inferred. Left alone.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5% (1,280 samples). Every number below comes from rasterising this exact geometry at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.52) in Python with a painter's depth sort and pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `closure` closed <-> travel, AT `pinch`, PREDICTED 2.13% FOCUS / 0.11% FRAME. The arithmetic: the `travel` rung adds one stem per contact, and at pinch there are two contacts per compartment, so the whole cabinet gains TEN stems. Each is 8.28 px wide and about 44 px long in screen, i.e. roughly 364 px, so 3,640 px on a subject crop of 625 x 582 = 363,750 px — one percent of the crop, at a contrast of about 120 grey levels against the compartment interior. The second closest is the same pair at `hook` (three contacts, fifteen stems), predicted 2.74%.

THAT PAIR IS ALSO THIS PASS'S OWN CRITICISM OF ITSELF. Grouped by VALUE PAIR across all four contacts rather than by context — which is how a conditional axis must be read — `closed|travel` is the weakest rung transition at 5.12% mean, against `none|depth` at 18.85%. The reason is not a drawing failure: the open pad and the shut pad are BOTH visible from the `closed` rung on, so the travel is already legible as the gap between them, and the stem only names it. If the sweep confirms it, the finding is that `travel` is a nearly redundant rung and it should be recorded as such rather than trimmed out of the declaration in advance to flatter the axis mean.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED, over the 24 same-axis pairs each: `contact` 2.17% frame / 28.69% focus -> BITES comfortably. `closure` 0.63% frame / 11.40% focus -> lands on the WEAK/BITES line at 12%, and I expect the real capture to come in ABOVE the prediction rather than below it, because the replica renders flat Lambert shading with NO emission at all while every closed pad and every ledger bar in the artifact is emissive cyan at 1.4x. If `closure` comes back under 12%, that is not a harness fault and should be reported as measured.

`closure` IS CONDITIONAL ON THE PROBE COUNT, by a factor of four, and must be grouped by value pair rather than by context mean. Its pairs run 10.66-32.54% at `net` (twelve contacts per compartment) and 2.13-9.38% at `pinch` (two). That is structural, not accidental: every mark this axis adds is one per contact, so the axis is exactly as loud as the grip is many-fingered.

WIDEST PAIR ON THE SHEET, predicted: `contact` hook <-> net at closure=depth, 36.21%. THINNEST `contact` pair: pinch <-> hook at closure=none, 9.89% — two pads at the equator against three at the underside, with no marks drawn yet.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. `atom` and `chorus` return penetration profiles identical to the bit under every grip, so the obvious expectation is that those two compartments photograph alike. They do not, and the difference is not subtle: the chorus bay carries three 34.33 px siblings, a 5.72 px rail 143 px long and a 5.72 px riser 62 px tall, none of which exists in the atom bay. The theories are indistinguishable to a hand and not remotely indistinguishable to a camera, which is the whole of finding (1). If a future reader crops to those two bays and reports them as twins, they will have measured the argument and called it a bug.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB, which here is also every individual variant's AABB: the carcass encloses everything either axis can draw, so the box is 0.57616 x 0.44592 x 0.18944 in all sixteen frames. Diagonal sqrt(0.331960 + 0.198845 + 0.035888) = 0.752790, radius 0.376395. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera at 0.376395 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 2.33915 m and shows a 1.43030 m frame around a 0.576 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.52 the camera comes to 1.21636 m and the frame to 0.743756 m, which is 1021.84 px per metre. From this standpoint a horizontal along X projects at cos(0.62) = 0.81388, a vertical at cos(0.26) = 0.96639, and depth contributes -0.58104 to screen x and -0.20923 to screen up. The subject's screen box is therefore 0.81388 x 0.57616 + 0.58104 x 0.18944 = 0.57907 m wide by 0.96639 x 0.44592 + 0.20923 x 0.18944 = 0.55065 m tall, i.e. 77.9% of frame width and 74.0% of height, leaving 84 px of clear margin on each side. Rasterised, the union subject box measures 82.2% of frame width by 76.6% of height (the drawn content overhangs the analytic box slightly because the hand's pads are spheres tangent to the compartment walls) and the subject covers 16.85% of the frame at the default tile — well above the ~6% dilution floor and above the blank-render check. 0.50 was measured too (81.0% of width) and rejected: 72 px of margin is thinner than the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model.

GAUGE CHECK AT 1021.84 px/m, because foresight_range shipped a bench's 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. THE AXES' OWN MARKS FIRST, since those are the ones a verdict is about: fingertip pad 0.018 m -> 18.39 px; finger 0.015 -> 15.33 px; the pad's swept track 0.0081 -> 8.28 px; ledger bar 0.00804 wide -> 8.22 px and 0.01463 tall at the largest reading -> 14.95 px, on a 43.16 px row pitch, against a ceiling gauge 35.48 px tall. Nothing either axis draws is under 8 px.

THE EXHIBIT'S OWN MARKS, which are constant across both axes and are the family's ratios rather than this artifact's choices: the thing 0.056 m -> 57.22 px; socket rim outer 0.0616 -> 62.95 px with a 4.58 px tube; socket rib 0.0042 -> 4.29 px; hollow ring tube 0.00504 -> 5.15 px and latitude tube 0.00403 -> 4.12 px; swarm grain 0.00924 -> 9.44 px; chorus sibling 0.0336 -> 34.33 px on a 5.72 px rail; carcass panel 0.00784 -> 8.01 px. The four-pixel marks are the socket's ribs and the hollow's latitudes, and they are kept at the family's own 0.075 R and 0.072 R rather than thickened: the family sized those explicitly to survive a capture, they are part of the exhibited body and not a gauge of this artifact's, and they are constant in all sixteen tiles. Recorded rather than fixed.

THE CABINET IS 3 x 2 AND NOT A ROW OF SIX, and that was a framing decision with a number. Six compartments in a line gives a union 6.3x wider than tall, a screen box of 30.5 R by 6.2 R, and at 78% frame fill only 259 px/m — every mark 2.5x smaller, with the socket's ribs at 1.7 px. Occlusion, which is what pushed taxonomy_hall into a row, does not bite here: the compartments are 0.211 m tall and the shelves 0.0078 m thick, so at a 15-degree downward pitch a shelf hides 5.7 mm of the compartment below it, which is the empty air under a body that sits 0.0148 m above the compartment centre.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, checks the family list against the preload, measures, and builds the whole cabinet standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

EVERY POSITION IS ARITHMETIC. The swarm's sixty-eight grains come from the family's own _fib_points, character for character, keyed on the index; the net's twelve directions are the icosahedron's vertices; the palm's eight azimuths are k times the golden angle; the socket's eight ribs are k times a quarter turn. Nothing is rolled and nothing is hashed. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THE CLOSURE IS DETERMINISTIC TO THE BIT, which is the one place this artifact could have leaked a difference between runs. The probe is sphere-traced against exact distance fields and then BISECTED twenty-four times, so the stop does not depend on the march path. Without the bisection it did: `atom` and `chorus` are the same body to a hand, and they came out 0.02 mm apart purely because chorus's riser is nearer at the start and shortened one early step. A residue of the instrument, reported as a difference between two theories.

THE SORT IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION. Godot's Array.sort_custom is not stable, so _sorted_pen does not use it: it runs a hand-rolled selection sort over at most twelve elements whose comparison is (value, index) and therefore TOTAL, so there is nothing for stability to decide.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_contact / config_closure metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against _is_contact / _is_closure, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

`atom` AND `chorus` ARE THE SAME BODY TO A HAND, BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. Their penetration profiles are identical to the bit under all four grips. They are NOT the same picture: the chorus bay carries a rail, three siblings and a riser that the atom bay has no equivalent of. If a future reader crops to the readings and reports the pair as degenerate, they will have measured finding (1) and called it a bug. See dna.note.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `closure`: the carcass, all five bodies, and the open pads. Everything that changes between the four closure tiles is the record of the encounter, which is that axis's whole subject. Constant at every value of `contact`: the carcass and all five bodies. Nothing about the exhibit ever moves; only the hand does.

THE SIXTH COMPARTMENT IS EMPTY OF BARS AT THREE OF THE FOUR CLOSURE VALUES, and that is deliberate. It still carries its five rules and its ceiling gauge, so it reads as a ruled page rather than as an unfinished cabinet, and it is the honest picture of a count that has not been asked for.

FOUR OF THE FIVE BAYS HAVE AN EMPTY LOWER THIRD, and it is a cost rather than a fault. The compartment must be tall enough for the chorus bay's rail at -3.6 R, so the body sits 0.0148 m above the compartment centre in every bay and only chorus uses the space beneath. This is why the subject covers 16.85% of frame rather than more; the union box fills 82.2% of frame width, so the framing is not at fault. A sparse subject is not a small one.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. There is not one Label3D, not one glyph, in any tile — see dna.declines for why. LabelFramer therefore has nothing to hang panels behind, and nothing enters or leaves the capture AABB on that account.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh, SphereMesh, TorusMesh or CylinderMesh; there is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG and no particle system, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check four things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery's default cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `closure` is measured on [closed, none] alone — a mean of 8.84% published as a verdict about four rungs. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=16.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 0.58 m cabinet is far under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink. In a MAP this artifact does want a table under it — spatial_needs.platform says so — but the sweep should photograph the cabinet alone.
(3) Is the verdict about `closure` rather than about the probe count? That axis is CONDITIONAL by a factor of four, 10.66-32.54% at `net` against 2.13-9.38% at `pinch`, because every mark it draws is one per contact. Group by value pair across contexts, not by context mean.
(4) Is the standpoint doing the work? The five bays rank in screen X and Y and the canonical camera sees the front elevation at 35.5 degrees off its normal, which is the angle at which the compartments' side walls and the chorus rail's depth both read. A probe from straight in front would flatten the rail into the body and one from above would put every hand between the camera and its object. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.

dna.default: algebra=triad, strike=corner - PRESERVES all seven placements exactly, and both defaults are short-circuits rather than recomputations. _recipe() at triad returns the same three dictionaries _build_presets used to hold inline, in the same order, with the same colours and the same labels; the bench width formula preset_spacing * (count + 0.2) evaluates at count=3 to preset_spacing * 3.2, the literal that shipped, and the layout formula (i - (count-1)/2) * preset_spacing evaluates to (i - 1) * preset_spacing, likewise the literal. strike=corner returns preset_offset (0.2, 0.1, 0.1) untouched instead of resolving a fraction of box_size. All seven placements are bare tokens passing no config keys at all, plus two reach-paths through curation_station whose #with_wall / #with_pillars / #with_barrier flags belong to the station and are never forwarded here. A placement that names preset_offset directly still wins over strike.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Three exports existed and none of them was an argument: bench_color is palette, rotation_speed is a rate and invisible to a still, preset_spacing is the declared critical_parameter and a distance. The operator SET - the thing the artifact exists to hold - was a three-element literal array inside _build_presets, and the operand pair (box 0.45, sphere r 0.3 at (0.2, 0.1, 0.1)) was three more literals in the loop below it. apply_grid_config assigned preset_spacing with no rebuild behind it, so the one knob it exposed could not take effect after _ready.
dna.note: algebra is a NEW word. Nothing in the corpus asks what a closed operator set consists of; the nearest neighbours ask about one operation's depth (fontana_puncture's breach) or its exposition (workings). triad is Godot's three CSG primitives and the three the bracelet offers. ordered adds B - A beside A - B, and that pair is the entire proof that difference is the only non-commutative operator here - which is exactly the demonstration csg_difference_demo declined to swallow into its own workings and deferred to 'a second object beside this one'. This is that object. complete adds the symmetric difference, built as a nested (A union B) combiner minus a nested (A intersect B) combiner, and labelled longhand rather than as a symbol because the label IS the claim: XOR is derivable and is not a primitive of the tool. atoms drops the operators entirely for the three disjoint regions A-B, A intersect B, B-A that every one of them is a union of - three benches again, and the identical count is the point, since the room looks like the shipped one while arguing the opposite thing. strike is reused CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER from fontana_puncture and csg_difference_demo: same word, same four values, same question. The numbers are not theirs and cannot be - fontana's sphere is 1.36 half-extents, the demo's 1.10, this bench's 1.33 (r 0.3 against a 0.225 half-extent) - so the same fraction of box_size cuts a different topology in each, which is what makes the three comparable rather than merely identical. On this artifact it does something neither sibling can: one offset drives every operator on the bench at once, so the axis puts the bench's own claim (that these are one family) under load. At centred the union is a ball with eight box corners through it, the intersection is that ball flattened on six faces, and the difference breaches all six faces so the box survives as its twelve edges - three unmistakably different solids from a single placement of B.
dna.declined: workings (outcome | trace | operands | expression), the twelve-artifact family word, genuinely FITS this artifact and is still not shipped. The sibling already holds it: csg_difference_demo's promotion is precisely how much of ONE operation is drawn, and repeating it here across up to five presets would fill the frame with translucent ghosts and say the family's existing thing five times over. The hub's question is the set, the demo's question is the derivation; kept apart the two artifacts are comparable, merged one of them is redundant. Also declined: an axis over preset_spacing, the declared critical_parameter. It is a distance, and a distance is legible as a number - it does not need a vocabulary laid over it.
dna.fixture_why: Every preset root spins at 0.25 rad/s from the first frame, so without this the sweep photographs each variant at whatever yaw its settle happened to land on and the diff measures rotation instead of the axis. rotation_speed is a plain float export read only by _process, so pinning it to zero holds the presets at the yaw they have at spawn - the shipped look at t=0, not a new one. Numeric and not the string '0.0': the sweep assigns fixture values straight onto the property before _ready, where a String would be rejected by the typed float.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns early unless a value the build actually reads has changed - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. The old body assigned preset_spacing and had no rebuild at all, which worked only because config always arrives before _ready. All seven placements pass no keys, so the guard means none of them is even torn down.
dna.still_note: everything both axes build is standing CSG geometry resolved during _ready. There is no animation on this bench except the yaw the fixture pins, so a single frame is a complete account of both values.

csg_compose_workbench.name: CSG Compose Workbench
csg_compose_workbench.description: Workbench holding all three CSG operators side by side. The introduction artifact for the csg-compose catalyst affordance.
csg_compose_workbench.qfep_connection: All three operators on one bench — union, intersection, difference, side by side, the chapter's grammar laid out as a palette. The workbench where you learn that solids have an algebra: any complex form is a sentence in these three verbs, and constructive solid geometry is the claim that you can say any shape by combining primitives lawfully enough.

sphere_splitting_showcase.description: sphere → fragments(method). Five fracture algorithms: planar cut, octree division, orange-peel sectors, CSG boolean, pre-segmented mesh. One sphere, five deaths.

dna.default: comparison=all - `all` is the fall-through arm of _bench()'s match and returns the shipped BENCH_ALL in the shipped order, and _slot_x then reduces to the five literals it replaces: for a bench of five, (i - 1.5) * spacing IS -spacing*1.5, -spacing*0.5, +spacing*0.5, +spacing*1.5, +spacing*2.5, term for term. Every scene is instantiated in the same order, every signal is bound to the same handler with the same name, every stats entry and every info label carries the same text, and the instruction wall and the throw balls are not touched by the axis at all. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` before this pass and now returns on its first line unless a config names `comparison` AND names a different value AND _ready has already built the bench. All 5 placements across 4 maps (Corridor_ForcesArena, Curation_Bay_forces_6 x2, ForcesArena, Forces_Destruct) are bare tokens with no config overrides, so none of them can reach it.
dna.was: three @exports, all of them about the AMMUNITION - how many throw balls, how high they hang, how far apart. Not one of them touches a fracture algorithm, and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The five decompositions were five hard-coded instantiations at five hard-coded x, so the bench that exists to compare fracture bases could not be asked to compare any particular two of them.
dna.shared_with: comparison is riemann_pump's and launch_arc's word for the same question - what stands beside what - and keeps their `single` anchor value character for character. The other three answers are this artifact's own, because a decomposition's companions are other decompositions and not other partitions or other throws. DERIVED from the @export_enum in sphere_splitting_showcase.gd.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. The value list is the one distinction in this material a STILL can carry, and it took reading all five destructibles to find it. planar, octree and CSG each build ONE frozen body at level 0 and compute their parts at impact - intact, they are three smooth unbroken surfaces. sectored ships as 8 wedges and segmented as 48 tiles with a 0.01 gap between them - intact, they are nothing but seams. So `computed` is a bench with no seam in the frame and `latent` is a bench that is all seam, and the axis draws the line between a part that is CALCULATED and a part that was always there. That line is the artifact's own truth statement (each method is a decomposition basis) made visible instead of asserted.
dna.declined: an `exploded` axis (whole | exploded) was designed and refused, and the reason is worth keeping because the obvious reading of this artifact demands it: fracture is an event, so the aftermath is what a still wants. It cannot be had honestly. Firing the real path means calling each destructible's _shatter_all_* , which unfreezes every piece (freeze = false, gravity_scale = 1.0) and applies impulses - by the rig's 1.1 s settle the bench is a pile on the floor, and the impulses are not seeded, so five variants would be five different piles and any bite report would be measuring the physics engine. Faking it - offsetting each frozen piece radially by its own mesh-AABB centre, which is deterministic and needs no impulse - works beautifully on sectored and segmented and does NOTHING on the other three, because they have exactly one piece until they are hit. An axis that is a null cell for 60% of the bench is a finished-looking experiment about the 40%. A `grain` axis over the five bases' fineness (max_split_levels 3, max_subdivision_levels 2, initial_sectors 8, latitude x longitude 6 x 8) was refused for the mirror reason: it is visible in a still on sectored and segmented and invisible on the three that only subdivide after impact.
dna.harness_note: framing 0.7 is declared because this subject is WIDE and SPARSE and the axis lives in the sparse part. The bench spans 6.6 m of x with five 0.6 m spheres in it, the throw balls hang 3 m in front at z = 0.5, and the instruction wall is a nine-line Label3D at y = 2.3 that is the single largest bright object in the frame and is IDENTICAL in every variant - deliberately so, because rewriting the caption per value would have measured the caption. Fit-by-diagonal on that box puts each sphere at well under 1% of frame, so removing two of them is a change the critic would read as decoration even though it is 40% of the bench. The caption stays fixed and the camera comes in instead. If the report is still faint, the next move is a tighter framing and not a bigger axis. SEPARATE FINDING, not repaired here: this token is a full test SCENE - it carries its own DirectionalLight3D, WorldEnvironment, a stats HUD and a nine-line instruction panel addressed to a player with hands, and it is placed as an artifact in four maps.

dna.default: openwork=sampler, interior=none - PRESERVES all eleven placements exactly, and both defaults are short-circuits rather than recomputations. _build_openings matches on openwork and sampler falls to the `_:` branch's `front` arm, which is the shipped body verbatim: _sub_door, _sub_porthole(porthole_offset), _sub_arch(arch_offset_x), in that order, from those literals, with no scaling, no counting and no layout arithmetic anywhere in the path. The wall box short-circuits too - at run_len == wall_size.x it assigns wall_size itself rather than rebuilding a Vector3 that happens to equal it. interior=none returns from _build_interior_runs before a second run exists and never touches _build_ground, so the slab stays 5.4 x 0.04 x 4.4 at y -0.02 and the child order is WallRoot, Label3D, Ground exactly as it shipped. THE ELEVEN, counted: 2 bare tokens (Boolean_Architecture_Cavity and Color_Context_Placed, both the naked string with no rotation, no y-offset and no config keys); 7 exhibit_furniture#kind:plinth#size:m#mount:csg_architecture_cavity mounts across Trial_castelvecchio, Trial_grande, Trial_halls, Trial_kanazawa, Trial_sainsbury, Trial_thoronet_circumambulation_void and Trial_uffizi - pure export defaults, because _mount_artifact instantiates and seats the scene and never calls apply_grid_config at all; and 2 curation_station reach-paths (Corridor_Boolean_Architecture_Cavity, Curation_Bay_boolean_surfaces_0) which forward exactly {"emissive": false}, a key no build path reads. The entry declares no default_params, so ArtifactIdentity.stamp adds only artifact_lookup_name. A placement that names door_size, door_offset_x, porthole_radius, porthole_offset, arch_size, arch_top_radius or arch_offset_x still WINS: openwork chooses WHICH subtractions exist, never how big they are, so there is no fraction-of-the-export path for it to lose to and no explicit-override flag is needed.
dna.was: one wall run, one ratio, one label. The declared critical_parameter is 'wall_size against the opening sizes - the ratio of solid to void', and it had shipped exactly one value of that ratio across eleven placements; the three subtractions were literals inline in _build_wall_with_openings and the only way to move any of them was to name a raw Vector3. The @identity then said in so many words what was missing - 'a second wall to make an enclosed room the player can stand inside' - and that sentence had been sitting there unbuilt. apply_grid_config assigned wall_color and had no rebuild behind it, and since the grid delivers config through call_deferred (after _ready), the one knob it exposed could never take effect at all.
dna.note: openwork asks WHAT A WALL'S HOLES ARE, and at what density mass stops being mass. A ladder in count and kind against a 3.4 x 2.6 m face of 8.84 sq m, read as solid fraction of the front run: door = the rectangular doorway alone, 1.44 sq m void, 84 percent solid - the minimum claim, one difference and it is already architecture. sampler SHIPPED = doorway + porthole + arched window, about 75 percent solid, three unlike opening types arguing that all three are one operator. arcade = the same arch repeated on even piers and nothing else, 5 bays, 3.37 sq m, 62 percent - repetition of a single difference, and the wall becomes rhythm. screen = a 7 x 5 lattice of 0.36 m square subtractions on a 0.486 x 0.52 pitch leaving 0.126 and 0.16 m mullions, 4.54 sq m, 49 percent - past the tipping point, where the wall reads as a filter rather than as mass with holes. It stops there deliberately: thinner mullions read as NO WALL and the verdict would become a fact about the capture. The Label3D follows the rung ('wall - door = room', 'wall - 5 arches = room', 'wall - 35 cuts = room') because on this artifact the label is part of the claim. interior asks WHETHER THE SUBTRACTION HAS PRODUCED AN INSIDE - the thing one wall can demonstrate and never deliver. none SHIPPED, the single 3.4 m run. corner = two runs meeting at a right angle, shelter and a claim on space, still no inside. court = three runs open at the back, enclosure felt before it is closed. room = four runs, the first rung on which the player is INSIDE and the void is bounded, which is the sequence's payoff standing up rather than being asserted. The two axes COMPOSE - every added run carries the active openwork, so interior=room at openwork=screen is a lantern - and one rule governs the composition, the rule that makes 'room' honest: only the FRONT run is entered, so the ground-level doorway appears there and nowhere else. Windows repeat around the room; doors do not. Bay and column counts scale with run length rather than staying fixed, so what wraps the enclosure is the PITCH, and the fabric reads as one fabric. Both words are NEW and both were checked against the corpus before use. openwork is the craft term for exactly this - work defined by its openings - and the plainer names are taken: `opening` is held by agreement_gauge and five siblings for the pose two vectors are found in, `aperture` by breathing_room for how far a door stands open, and one letter between opening and openings across artifacts that share the Trial_* museum maps is the collision exhibit_vitrine's regard->guard rename exists to prevent. `interior` likewise: `plan` is room_shape_demonstrator's (pair|head|circle|panopticon|vacant) and `enclosure` is exhibit_vitrine's (box|bell|cradle|niche|open) for the case around an exhibit - and exhibit_vitrine stands in the same Trial_* maps as this wall, which is precisely where one word cannot mean two things. Nothing in the corpus asks what a wall's holes ARE, or whether an operation has produced an inside; the nearest neighbour, fontana_puncture's breach, asks how deep ONE hole has eaten.
dna.declined: strike, the family word shared character for character by fontana_puncture, csg_difference_demo and csg_compose_workbench, is NOT promoted here, and the reason is specific to this artifact rather than borrowed from its siblings. The word is technically reachable - this wall does have a sphere subtraction with an offset - and it would have to pick a favourite. Those three each have ONE B to place. This wall's B is three things at once, a box, a sphere and a box-union-cylinder, and moving any one of them across four named positions changes about 2 percent of the face while announcing itself as the artifact's structural axis. That is subtraction_suite's refusal in another key ('the tray has no B to place'); here there are three Bs and no single one of them is the strike. Also declined: an axis directly over the solid-to-void RATIO, which is this artifact's own declared critical_parameter. It is a fraction, a fraction is already legible as a number, and csg_compose_workbench declined an axis over preset_spacing for exactly that reason - openwork moves the same ratio as a CONSEQUENCE of changing what the holes ARE, which is the thing a vocabulary is actually needed for.
dna.fixture_why: NOTHING IS PINNED, and this is the only artifact of the four that needs nothing pinned: no _process, no rotation, no RNG, no deferred build. Every value of both axes is standing CSG resolved synchronously in _ready, so one frame is a complete account. What IS required is framing, and it is derived rather than measured. capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D only (MultiMesh as a fallback) and every part of this wall is CSG, so the measured box is the GROUND SLAB ALONE: 5.4 x 0.04 x 4.4, diagonal 6.97, against the wall's own 3.4 x 2.6 x 0.4, diagonal 4.30. 4.30 / 6.97 = 0.617, hence 0.62. Note that this lands on the same number by different arithmetic than a CSG-counting merge would give (5.4 x 2.64 x 4.4, diagonal 7.45, ratio 0.577) - the coincidence is worth recording so the next reader does not 'correct' it back. Do NOT reach for a layers=0 anchor here: the ground is walkable and part of the shipped look. THE KNOWN RISK, to correct from the first sweep: because the AABB is the flat slab, the camera aims at y -0.02 and the wall rises 2.6 m above the aim point, so at 0.62 the wall sits high in frame at roughly an eighth of its area - legible and uncropped by about six degrees of margin, but not centred. If the first sheet shows it small, the fix is a smaller framing (0.50-0.55 still clears the label at y 2.95), not a change to the geometry.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns early unless a value the build actually reads has changed - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. The signature covers all eleven: openwork, interior, wall_color, wall_size, door_size, door_offset_x, porthole_radius, porthole_offset, arch_size, arch_top_radius, arch_offset_x. Nine placements pass no keys and two pass {"emissive": false}, which is stamped as metadata nobody reads and leaves the signature identical, so not one of the eleven is torn down. A rebuild frees only the nodes this script added, tracked in _owned, rather than every child - the grid and the curation station both attach things of their own to an artifact root after _ready. The four wall runs are SEPARATE top-level CSGCombiner3D nodes under the Node3D root, never nested: a CSGCombiner3D inside another combiner is a shape, not a container, and nesting them would union the returning runs into the front wall instead of standing them beside it.
dna.still_note: Everything both axes build is standing CSG resolved during _ready, and this artifact has no _process at all, so a single frame is a complete account of every one of the sixteen combinations. The returning runs are sized FROM the shipped ground slab - depth is (wall_size.z + 4.0) / 2 minus half the wall thickness minus a 0.1 m margin - so all four interior rungs stand wholly on it, the measured AABB is identical at every value, and one framing number serves the whole sweep. spatial_needs is deliberately left alone: corner, court and room want roughly four clear floor cells and the default does not, and the default is what every existing map places.

boolean_burrow.name: Boolean Burrow
boolean_burrow.description: A seeded walk places eleven overlapping cutters in a rock block. The rock is a CSG difference with collision. The sphere profile makes scalloped hollows; the level profile uses upright cylinders with the same centres and radius. A section cut exposes the interior, and roof variants change overhead enclosure. The cast displays the cutter union without the stock or its collision. Reported components and cycles describe the overlap graph, not traversable routes or topological holes.

predicted_degeneracy.basis: frame-share, and it is a LOWER BOUND — every prediction measured in this corpus under-predicted by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a flat-shaded estimate has one light, no shadow, no AO and no antialiasing.
