iso_shapes_console.description: Controls the existing gallery repertoire and level, with two independent held meshes.

dna.default: repertoire=household and likeness=exact, both a deliberate no-op. household SHORT-CIRCUITS: _roster() returns the shipped list [0,1,2,3,4,5], which is term for term, in the same order, what `for i in range(6): generator.shape_type = i` produced on the old line 11, at the same grid positions from the same col/row formula. The captions are now DERIVED from TerrainGeneratorShapes.ShapeType rather than read out of a second hardcoded array, and that reproduces the old list rather than replacing it: Human, Chair, House, Bottle, Cup, Computer are exactly String(key).capitalize() of the first six enum members. exact returns the literal 0.0 the old line 25 assigned to generator.iso_level, not a dictionary lookup that happens to land on it. Nothing else in the build moved - noise_scale 1.0, chunk_scale 120.0 (hoisted to a const, same number), center_position zero, invert_faces true, the per-slot hsv material, the spacing/shape_scale exports. The hue still indexes the SLOT and not the shape id, so a new roster cannot recolour the grid. use_fallback is forwarded as false, which is what TerrainGeneratorBase already defaulted to, and capture_anchor defaults to "off" so the anchor node does not exist in a map. REACH MEASURED across the whole map corpus: 4 files - a bare grid cell in Corridor_ISO_ShapesGallery, `mc_shapes_gallery:0:0.5:0.5` in ISO_ShapesGallery (rotation and offsets only, no # config), a `curation_station#artifacts:` roster in Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_0, and the corridor swap pair `mc_shapes_gallery->gyroid_demo` in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces. Not one passes an axis key. The only apply_grid_config call any of them produces is curation_station's {"emissive": false}, which moves no term of the signature and returns early before touching a single node.
dna.was: two @export knobs and not one categorical among them: spacing and shape_scale, both pure magnitudes. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` at line 56, so neither was reachable from a map token at all - the same unreachable-knob shape implicit_surface_modeling's promotion found on its own critical_parameter. What the artifact ARGUES sat in two hardcoded literals instead: six shape names on line 7 against `for i in range(6)` on line 11, and iso_level = 0.0 on line 25. TerrainGeneratorShapes.ShapeType declares THIRTEEN members and MarchingCubesShapes.glsl dispatches all thirteen in evaluate() (id 0..12, every branch present), so seven fully implemented objects - microscope, flask, DNA helix, atom, sculpture, sphere, torus - had never been placed in a world.
dna.note: The sequence truth line is "define a field, extract a surface; the boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry", and this gallery is the only artifact in the sequence that makes the first half a QUESTION. repertoire asks what the field is asked to prove it can be. The artifact's whole claim is that an SDF can be any thing, and it has been arguing that on furniture and crockery: household is a room, laboratory is apparatus and its operator, abstract is six things that were functions before they were objects, and survey is one from each register - the only value that lets the three claims stand beside each other in one frame. Lifting the roster out of a hardcoded array is csg_compose_workbench's algebra move exactly. likeness is the second half: 0.0 on a signed distance field IS the surface, and everything else is a decision. The numbers come off the shader's own literals against the sampling scale - chunk_scale 120 over num_voxels_per_axis 64 is a cell of 1.875 SDF units, so these are real changes and not re-quantisation. broken (-2.0) erodes past the chair legs (sdBox half-extent 2), the cup handle (sdTorus minor radius 0.8), the human's arms (sdCapsule radius 2.5) and the monitor stand (half-extent 3): six things remain, no longer six nameable things. padded (+4.0) swells everything and fills the cup's subtracted bore; the objects go soft but stay identifiable. fused (+10.0) closes the chair's 20-unit leg gaps into one rounded block - the object dissolving back into the field it came from, the truth line run backwards on purpose. BOTH WORDS ARE NEW. `taxonomy` (math_objects_gallery, combine_portals: table|ladder|stack|heap) was considered and REFUSED - it is about WHERE a family stands, not which family; `census` (wall_pattern_gallery) is a count and this roster is always six; `roster` (barber_paradox) is about set membership. `threshold` exists in the corpus exactly once - voxelnoise, sponge|massif|archipelago|wisp - and was deliberately NOT taken: those four rungs name topologies a noise field can hold and a gallery of six designed objects can produce none of them. Taking a word and dropping its answers is the folding_past fault that implicit_surface_modeling names, so the word is left to the artifact that can answer it in full. fusion and metaball_count are already spoken for by raymarched_metaballs / metaballs / implicit_surface_modeling, and neither of these two re-argues them: how much a field merges and how many sources it has are questions about ONE object, and this artifact's questions are about the roster and the cut.
dna.still_note: NOT MEASURED - I have not run Godot and no pixel has been counted. What follows is derived by reading, and the first sweep is what settles it. A still is the right instrument here for once: this is the ONE artifact of the six in this sequence with no _process and no clock, because TerrainGeneratorBase calls set_process(false) as soon as the first mesh exists and continuous_update defaults false. Every frame is a frozen 3x2 grid of six static SDF meshes. repertoire replaces a human, a chair and a house with a microscope, a DNA helix and a torus - a complete change of silhouette in every one of six cells, which should be the largest single-frame difference available anywhere in the sequence. likeness keeps the layout and the count and changes only the outlines: at broken the thin members disappear, at fused the internal holes close (the cup's bore, the chair's gaps, the atom's three orbital rings). FRAMING IS A CALCULATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The capture anchor is 11.0 x 3.25 x 7.0 m, diagonal 13.44, so radius 6.72; capture_config_sweep places the camera at radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, which puts the half-frame width at the subject at 6.72 * 1.9 * framing. At the sweep's yaw 0.62 the six-cell field projects about 10.2 m wide (9 * cos 35.5 + 5 * sin 35.5), so framing 0.5 gives a half-frame of 6.38 against a subject half-width of 5.12 - about 80% of frame width, with margin and no crop. This is a wide flat subject fitted by diagonal, riemann_pump's letterbox case, so if the first sweep shows headroom the number to move is this one and not the axes.
dna.declined: spacing and shape_scale, the artifact's only two previous exports, stay plain exports. Both are pure magnitudes that SELF-CANCEL under an AABB-fitted capture camera - a gallery spread twice as wide is photographed from twice as far and looks identical - which is the fault grabbable_line's promotion recorded when its length and thickness were demoted. invert_faces is a winding flag: it changes shading, not form. The six per-shape hues are colour, not argument, and the code now says so by indexing them off the SLOT rather than the shape id. NO TIME-DOMAIN AXIS WAS AVAILABLE TO REFUSE, which is worth stating in a sequence where four of the six artifacts run _process: this one does not, and that is why an axis over arrangement was reachable here without first having to convert a rate into a standing state.
dna.fixture_why: use_fallback: false, written as a BARE BOOLEAN and not the string "false" - a typed bool export rejects a string assigned before _ready, the trap the catalyst prompter-box pass paid for. It does not make the compute path work; it only removes the deliberate opt-out so that a fallback in the log is unambiguously a device failure. It is forwarded from the gallery root to all six generators, because the sweep sets properties on the INSTANTIATED scene before add_child and the generators do not exist until _ready runs - a fixture key naming the base class's own export would have found no holder and been silently dropped. capture_anchor: "on" builds the invisible bounding box; see rebuild_guard for why it is off by default and why it is not readable from config metadata.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was `pass`. It now stamps config_* metadata, re-reads the overrides, returns immediately if _ready has not run yet, and otherwise compares a signature over every value the build reads - repertoire, likeness, spacing, shape_scale, capture_anchor, use_fallback - returning early when nothing moved. A rebuild frees ONLY what this script created: the old _exit_tree freed every child without an owner, which is also exactly what GridInteractablesComponent's _RotationTimer is, so the script now keeps an _owned array and removes before freeing so a rebuild cannot collide names with children that are queued but not yet gone. THE CAPTURE ANCHOR IS GATED BY CONSTRUCTION. GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb walks MeshInstance3D regardless of its render layers and hands the result to _auto_ground_artifact; this entry carries no auto_ground:false, so an anchor built in a map would lift all four placements by the difference between the domain floor and the deepest real mesh. capture_anchor defaults to "off" and is deliberately NOT read from config metadata, so no map token can reach it - only direct property assignment can, which is what dna.fixture does. use_fallback is withheld from the metadata reader for the same reason: a map token that could set it would replace the artifact with six spheres.
dna.finding: NO RNG AND NO NOISE, and that is checked rather than assumed: the gallery script makes no random call, and MarchingCubesShapes.glsl is pure SDF primitives and boolean operators with no snoise call anywhere in evaluate() - unlike MarchingGyroid.glsl sitting in the same folder. noise_scale is set to 1.0 and nothing in this shader reads it. Six generators therefore produce six deterministic meshes and the sweep needs no seed pin. THE REAL DETERMINISM HAZARD IS THE COMPUTE PATH, AND IT IS SILENT. TerrainGeneratorBase._ready falls back to _create_fallback_mesh() when RenderingServer.create_local_rendering_device() or the SPIR-V load fails, and TerrainGeneratorShapes' fallback is a SphereMesh of radius 10 - so a capture host without a working local rendering device publishes six identical spheres for every value of both axes and the critic files two correct axes as INERT. BEFORE BELIEVING ANY VERDICT ON THIS TOKEN, grep the sweep's stdout for 'Compute initialization failed' and for 'Creating fallback mesh'; if either appears the run is void. SEPARATELY: the shipped value of likeness is named `exact` and not `true`, which is what the design asked for. "true" does not survive the harness - cabinet_sweep.coerce() turns it into a Python boolean, which would be handed to a String-typed property as `true` and silently refused, and would tag its frame `likeness-True` against a registry that says "true". A value name the plumbing rewrites on the way in is the science_screen fault in a new hat, caught before it shipped rather than after.
dna.kin: NOT a hidden family, checked rather than assumed: MarchingShapesGallery.tscn is named by exactly one registry entry across all 108 registry files, and the .tscn root carries the script itself (script = ExtResource("1_script") on the MarchingShapesGallery node), so a map token reaches apply_grid_config on the root without the child-forward path. Its neighbours in this sequence are the opposite shape - raymarched_metaballs, metaballs and implicit_surface_modeling are ONE scene under three registry names, and they own fusion and metaball_count. gyroid_demo and GyroidDemo are another such pair and are not this scene.

interactions: auto-generates on ready
mc_shapes_gallery.name: mc_shapes_gallery
mc_shapes_gallery.qfep_connection: The extraction bestiary: spheres, tori, blends — each shape one implicit function passed through the same fifteen-case mill. The gallery's argument: the surface was never modeled, only *described*.

dna.default: threshold=ring AND intrusion=melted, and both are STRUCTURAL no-ops rather than values that land near the shipped ones. `ring` is a bias of exactly 0.0, applied as `params[2] = float(params[2]) + _threshold_bias()` - index 2 is iso_level, TerrainGeneratorBase.get_params_array's third append - and `x + 0.0` returns the identical bit pattern for every finite float. It is applied to the params ARRAY and not to the property because `iso_level = iso_level + bias` would ACCUMULATE across an apply_grid_config re-entry; the array override is stateless and cannot drift. `melted` is the const triple [8.0, 1.0, 1.0]: the 8.0 is the literal that stood at MarchingCubesTorus.glsl:198, and the two 1.0s multiply terms (`twist`, `bulge`) that previously stood unmultiplied, where `x * 1.0` is bit-identical to `x` for every finite float. THE ONE HONEST CAVEAT, the same one gyroid_demo stated and no larger: `torusDist + deformation*8.0 + twist + bulge` is now `torusDist + deformation*dW + twist*tW + bulge*bW`, which hands a driver two more `a + b*c` sites it MAY contract into an FMA where before there was a bare add. Left-to-right association is unchanged and the same floats travel the same expression; the claim is 'the same arithmetic', not 'the bytes are proven equal'. REACH MEASURED BY READING EVERY MAP FILE, not estimated: 4 placements of this token and NOT ONE passes a config key - `mc_torus_sculpture:0:1:0.04` in ISO_ShapesGallery (the three suffixes are positional rotation / y-offset / scale, not a config dict; config keys arrive after a `#`), a bare `mc_torus_sculpture` in ISO_TorusGyroid, and `curation_station#artifacts:` rosters in Corridor_ISO_TorusGyroid and in Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_0 (whose roster also carries queer_marching_cave and mc_shapes_gallery, both wave-1 promotions). The sibling token marchingcubes_torus_sculpture adds a 5th, a bare cell in ProceduralGenerationMarchingcubesTorusSculpture. No entry declares default_params, so merged_config is empty for all five; and even if apply_grid_config were reached with an empty dictionary the guard returns on an unchanged signature before touching the mesh. All five come out identical.
dna.was: 27 lines: a shader path, a class name, a fallback torus, and an `apply_grid_config` whose whole body was `pass` - a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find something. The audit recorded ZERO exports, which is true and is not the same as having no parameters. Every number this artifact has is a literal inside MarchingCubesTorus.glsl, which writes a torus SDF (major 50, minor 20) at :173-174 and then adds three deformations to it in ONE line at :198 - five octaves of snoise at `deformation * 8.0` (swings about +/-15), a twist `sin(angle*3 + y*0.1) * 3.0` (+/-3), and a bulge `sin(angle*5) * cos(y*0.15) * 4.0` (+/-4) - before comparing the result to a single constant. The registry description above promises `marching cubes extracting torus isosurface`, and the plain torus it names has never been rendered anywhere in this corpus. What four maps place is a lump whose noise term swings three quarters of a tube radius.
dna.note: TWO AXES OUT OF ONE SENTENCE, and they are orthogonal by construction: intrusion varies what is ADDED to the distance, threshold varies where it is CUT. threshold - THE SURFACE IS NOT IN THE FIELD, IT IS IN THE NUMBER YOU COMPARE THE FIELD TO. :202 ends `float density = -sculptureShape;` and main() sets a corner bit when `cubeCorners[i].w < isoLevel`, so the surface sits at sculptureShape = -isoLevel; sculptureShape is a signed distance, so the threshold is EXACTLY an offset on the tube radius, R_eff = 20 - isoLevel - N. There is no space-varying thickness term anywhere in this file, which is the precise condition gyroid_demo named when it refused this axis on ITSELF (`it belongs to a sibling in this sequence that has no thickness term`). This is that sibling, and the axis is bequeathed rather than coined. Rungs as biases on the shipped iso_level of 0.0: ring SHIPPED +0.0, R_eff 20 against a major radius of 50, a 30 m clear hole; swollen -18.0, R_eff 38, the hole narrowed from 30 m of clear radius to 12; closed -35.0, R_eff 55 against a major radius of 50, so GENUS 1 BECOMES GENUS 0 over most of the ring with no change to a single term of the field; beaded +6.0, R_eff 14, and because N swings about +/-22 the tube opens into separate bodies wherever the noise runs positive. intrusion - HOW MUCH OF THE MATHEMATICAL OBJECT SURVIVES BEING WRITTEN INTO A NOISE PIPELINE, gyroid_demo's question asked of a compact SDF instead of a triply-periodic level set. The triple replaces the three multipliers at :198, two of which were implicit 1.0: melted SHIPPED [8.0, 1.0, 1.0]; formula [0, 0, 0], the exact torus SDF, the object the description names; rippled [0.0, 1.0, 1.0], the two ANALYTIC deformations only - strictly periodic, symmetric under the 3-fold twist and the 5-fold bulge, order without noise; roughened [8.0, 0.0, 0.0], noise alone. The amplitudes at :192 (*3.0) and :195 (*4.0) are deliberately NOT touched: the rung triple multiplies the FINISHED terms, so the author's numbers stay where the author put them and the shipped triple's two 1.0s are exact.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE THE CAPTURE, and the prediction is CONDITIONAL - the reading the corpus learned on `join`. CLOSEST PAIR: (intrusion=formula, threshold=ring) vs (intrusion=formula, threshold=beaded), about 3.9% of frame, right on the decoration floor. Arithmetic: at intrusion=formula the deformation is zero, so `beaded` does not bead at all - it merely thins a clean torus from a 40 m tube to a 28 m tube. The ring covers roughly 50% of frame width and 26% of height, so about 13% of frame area, and a 30% loss of tube cross-section changes 30% of that = 3.9%. THE SAME PAIR AT intrusion=melted SHOULD BE THREE TO FOUR TIMES LARGER, because there R_eff = 14 - N with N swinging +/-22, so the ring breaks. SO GROUP BY VALUE PAIR ACROSS CONTEXTS, NOT BY CONTEXT MEAN: a mean over the four intrusion rungs would report threshold WEAK and the weakness would be a fact about one cell. LARGEST PAIR expected: formula vs melted at either threshold, over 40% - a clean ring against a broken lumpy one. SECOND-CLOSEST expected: melted vs roughened, about 6%, since they differ only by the twist (+/-3) and bulge (+/-4) against a noise term already swinging +/-15, so the analytic terms are under a third of the noise's amplitude and are partly masked by it.
dna.still_note: Static and a still is a complete account: evaluate() has no time reference (the shader reads numVoxelsPerAxis, scale, posX/Y/Z, noiseOffset*, noiseScale and now the three weights; main() reads isoLevel; params.time is uploaded and never read), the snoise is the Ashima/stegu simplex function - a pure function of position, no seed, no time input - and the only thing that could move its sample point is noise_offset, which the .tscn sets once to (50, 25, 100) and nothing else touches. Four runs of one rung are the same mesh, so no seed export is needed. TRIANGLE BUDGET, checked because the failure would be silent: TerrainGeneratorBase.process_mesh_data aborts to num_triangles = 0 above 500,000, which empties the mesh and routes to the fallback. At chunk_scale 1000 with 64 voxels per axis the cell is 15.6 m and the deformed torus surface is on the order of 100,000 sq m, so a few hundred crossing cells and well under 1,000 triangles at every rung - three orders of magnitude below the cap. Every combination also stays under the 30,000 cutoff at which _create_collision skips trimesh generation, so collision behaviour is identical at every rung and no rung differs from the shipped one in what it hands the player. NOTE THE OTHER EDGE OF THAT SAME NUMBER: at 15.6 m cells the shipped 40 m tube is only 2.5 cells across and `beaded` is 1.8, so the thin rungs are genuinely coarse. That is the artifact, not a defect - but it is why beaded is +6.0 and not +12.0.
dna.declined: REFUSED, `resolution`, AND THE REASON IS A HARD BLOCKER RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT. This artifact wants the family word (queer_marching_cave's and animated_noise_explorer's) more than anything else in the wave: its chunk_scale is 1000 while its torus is 158 m across, because the radii at :165-166 are world-space literals that do not scale with the box - so on THIS artifact alone chunk_scale is not extent, it is purely how finely the field is sampled, and shrinking it to 260 with noise_scale scaled to 0.52 (holding noiseScale/scale, the only place scale enters the noise) would give an identical field at 3.8x finer cells. It cannot be declared because the axis name must be a settable property and TerrainGeneratorBase:13 already declares `const resolution : int = 8` - the workgroup count from which num_voxels_per_axis and every buffer size are derived - and a subclass cannot shadow an inherited member in GDScript. interior is SHARED, taken from csg_architecture_cavity (boolean_surfaces.json, rungs none|corner|court|room), where it asks whether a solid encloses a void you could occupy. Same question asked of a sampled field instead of a boolean solid, and the shared rung `none` means the same thing in both places -- no interior anywhere. Taking it rather than coining `hollowing` is the check as much as the economy: when a shared word is honest the siblings should measure ALIKE, so a landscape's cave and a wall's court clearing the 3% decoration floor at comparable numbers is itself evidence the word is doing one job. NOT `openwork` (csg_architecture_cavity's other axis, about holes in a face). NOT `resolution`, which this sequence already holds twice -- queer_marching_cave and animated_noise_explorer -- with a different question: how finely the field is SAMPLED, not how much of it is subtracted.

EVERY RUNG WAS SIZED ON A FLOAT32 NUMPY REPLICA of evaluate() over the same 65^3 corner grid at the scene's own iso_level of 0.0, counting columns whose solid/air classification changes more than once down y -- which is exactly the question 'is this still a graph over the plane?' -- with triangle counts taken from the shader's own lengths[256] table:

  rung       k     triangles   columns with an inside   enclosed air cells
  none      0.0       12,824        0 of 4,225 (0.00%)                   0
  undercut  0.3       14,996        8 of 4,225 (0.19%)                   9
  caverned  0.4       16,382       50 of 4,225 (1.18%)                  68
  warren    0.8       24,656      436 of 4,225 (10.32%)             1,157

THE MOST INTERESTING THING THIS PROMOTION FOUND is in the third row. The artifact that has stood in ISO_FlatTerrain all along is 98.8% HEIGHTFIELD -- it has an inside in one column in eighty-five. Nobody knew that, because until now there was nothing to compare it against. `none` is the comparison, and it is the picture nobody in this corpus has seen: the exact heightfield y = surfaceHeight, rolling hills from two snoise reads at :182-183 (amplitudes 15.0 and 5.0), smooth, single-sheeted, no overhang ANYWHERE (0 columns, measured, not assumed), marching cubes reduced to a function plotter. It is the negative half of the sequence's claim: here is what the algorithm looks like when it is not being used.

THE APPROVED DESIGN SAID undercut = 0.2 AND THE REPLICA FALSIFIED IT, which is the one place this promotion departs from its brief. At 0.2, ZERO of the 4,225 columns cross more than once and not one air cell is enclosed: 0.2 is a heightfield with its mass thinned, not an undercut. The design defined the rung as 'the first rung where the ground stops being single-valued in y', so declaring 0.2 would have put a word in the registry that the render does not contain -- the science_screen disease in a new costume, and one that no gate could catch because the enum would still match the code. Scanned: the property first appears at 0.25 (one column) and is robust by 0.30. The design's NUMBER and the design's DEFINITION were in conflict; the definition is what the axis argues, so the definition won. 0.30 also lifts the closest pair from a predicted 4.75% focus (under the critic's 6% twin bar) to 8.55%.

warren at 0.8 is void-dominated RELATIVE TO THE REST -- 10.3% of columns, an order of magnitude past the shipped rung, and the only value whose mesh AABB grows (126.6 m tall against 37-56 m) because its caves reach far below the surface band. Not yet floating islands; that needs k past 1.5, which is outside a ladder whose default has to sit inside it.

THE ARTIFACT NEXT DOOR ASKS A DIFFERENT QUESTION ON THE SAME SUBSTRATE, deliberately. ISO_FlatTerrain places mc_flat_landscape and mc_overhang_landscape in the same room. This shader has exactly ONE 3D term, so the only honest axis over it is HOW MUCH inside; the overhang shader has four, so its axis (`landform`) is WHICH TERMS. Neither had to be watered down to avoid the other.
dna.declined: REFUSED, `iso_level`, and the refusal is inherited. It is real, it is the sequence's central question, and gyroid_demo's declined note explicitly bequeathed it to 'a sibling in this sequence that has no thickness term' -- which this is. It is refused HERE and paid on mc_torus_sculpture instead, because on THIS shader iso_level and interior fight for the same pixels: density = terrainDensity - caveNoise*k, so a constant offset to the threshold and a scale on the cave term both widen the same caves, and the rigid vertical translation that is the rest of iso_level's effect self-cancels under an AABB-fitted camera. The torus has no gradient term at all, so there the threshold is pure. REFUSED, the surface amplitudes 15.0 and 5.0 at :182-183: they are the relief of the heightfield, a magnitude on the half of the field this axis is not about, and the two would read as one axis with a loud rung. REFUSED, the octave count at :170 (`i < 4`): real, and promoted on the cave pair instead, where two sibling scenes resolve a different number of octaves and the axis therefore says something; here there is one scene and it would be a detail knob. REFUSED, `chunk_scale` and `center_position` -- an extent and a placement, both self-cancelling under a fitted camera. REFUSED, `continuous_update`: a RATE, invisible in a still by law, and here only a risk of photographing a half-built mesh. REFUSED, `invert_faces`: two values, below the floor, and it changes what the material culls rather than what the field is. REFUSED, a second axis of any kind -- this shader has one 3D term and one 2D term, and the 2D term is already spoken for by the paragraph above.
dna.fixture_why: Neither key is an axis and both are already the shipped default, so this is a GUARD rather than a pin. It is here because this artifact's silent failure mode ends in a published sheet that is a fact about the host machine rather than about the design: use_fallback true, or a local rendering device / SPIR-V load that fails on the capture host, drops straight into _create_simple_flat_mesh -- a 200 m quad grid with two sin/cos hills, computed entirely in GDScript, which does not read caveStrength or anything else the axis touches. Four frames of the same smooth plane, the axis measuring zero, and a verdict about the GPU. THE RUN IS ONLY VALID IF THE SWEEP LOG SHOWS `TerrainGeneratorFlat: Generation complete!` AND DOES NOT SHOW `Creating fallback flat landscape`. continuous_update true would keep re-dispatching under the settle. Both are written as real booleans, never as the strings `false`, because capture_config_sweep assigns fixture values straight onto the typed export before _ready and a typed bool rejects a String.
dna.framing_why: COMPUTED, then CHECKED against a render, because this subject is the letterbox case CLAUDE.md names by hand: 300 x 50 x 300 m is wide and flat, and fit-by-DIAGONAL frames the diagonal. Arithmetic first: with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9 the fitted frame height is 3.80 x radius x framing, and the box half-extents (150, 24.8, 150) project onto the sweep camera's up vector (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) as 150(0.144) + 24.8(0.966) + 150(0.200) = 75.6, so the subject is 151 m tall against a frame of 811 x framing -- 18.6% of frame height at framing 1.0. Then measured, by ray-marching the real density field through the sweep's own camera: the subject covers 12.0% of frame AREA at framing 1.0 and 54.2% at 0.45. Every predicted pair triples with it (none <-> caverned goes 6.50 -> 18.15 focus). 0.45 crops the far corners of a landscape, which is the right crop for a landscape. NO `layers = 0` ANCHOR, and that was checked rather than assumed: the mesh AABB is 300 x 300 in x and z at every rung and the fitted radius moves only from 212.96 (none) to 221.37 (warren), 3.9%, with the subject share holding between 53.8% and 54.9%. The camera does move -- warren's caves reach 126 m down against none's 37 m band, so the look-at centre travels 49 m in y -- but not enough to confound the pairs, and an anchor sized to the widest rung would change what GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb measures for all four placements to fix a problem that is not there.
dna.rebuild_guard:
apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`. It now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns unless a value the SHADER reads has actually changed. The signature is not a hand-listed tuple: it is get_params_array() itself, stringified, so if a value reaches the GPU it is in the signature and the guard cannot drift out of step with the build.

WITH ONE DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION, and it is the difference between this subclass and TerrainGeneratorGyroid, which used the array whole. Gyroid overrides _process to `pass`, so its `time` is permanently 0.0 and its signature is stable. THIS subclass does not override _process, so `time` advances for the ~102 frames before the base calls set_process(false), and a signature including it would be a CLOCK -- every apply_grid_config arriving in that window would compare unequal and trigger a rebuild that changes nothing. Index 0 is skipped because `params.time` is declared in MarchingCubesFlat.glsl and referenced NOWHERE else in the file (grep returns exactly one hit, the declaration), so it cannot change the mesh. A fact checked in the shader, not an assumption about what `time` is for.

Ordering is load-bearing and was read off the call site rather than assumed: GridInteractablesComponent stamps config metadata at line 1195 and calls add_child at 1220, so metadata always lands BEFORE _ready; _ready reads it, calls super._ready(), and records the signature, and the call_deferred('apply_grid_config') that follows finds the signature unchanged and returns. capture_config_sweep instead sets the export directly before add_child, which _read_metadata_overrides cannot clobber because it only writes when the matching meta key exists.

The rebuild path re-runs the same three calls _ready runs -- run_compute, fetch_and_process_compute_data, create_mesh -- and refuses to run at all while waiting_for_compute or waiting_for_meshthread is set, because resubmitting under an in-flight dispatch is the teardown segfault release() documents. Unlike the gyroid, this subclass's _process CAN hold that state for ~102 frames, so in that case _built_signature is deliberately left stale: the next call with the same config still compares unequal and retries rather than recording a rebuild that did not happen. NOTHING IS FREED BY THIS SCRIPT: it constructs no nodes at all, it keeps an _owned array that is empty by construction so a future edit has a free path to use, create_mesh rewrites array_mesh's single surface in place, and the base's _create_collision removes only the StaticBody3D it created itself. A blanket free of children is what cost three scripts a pass in the last wave -- GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to a spawned artifact.
dna.still_note:
Static, but it needed CHECKING rather than asserting, because unlike TerrainGeneratorGyroid this subclass does NOT override _process. The base's loop therefore re-dispatches once, about 102 frames after _ready (12 for the GPU sync, 90 for the mesh thread), and then calls set_process(false). VERIFIED BY READING: `params.time` is declared in MarchingCubesFlat.glsl's ParamsBuffer and referenced nowhere else in the file, so the second dispatch computes a bit-identical field. The sweep's ~0.1 s settle photographs the first mesh, which _ready built synchronously, and the second would be the same picture if it ever arrived first. NO SEED IS NEEDED: snoise is the Ashima/stegu simplex function, a pure function of position with no seed and no time input, and the only thing that could move its sample point is noise_offset, which the .tscn fixes at (100, 50, 75) and nothing else sets. Four runs of a rung are the same mesh.

TRIANGLE BUDGET, checked because the failure would be silent. TerrainGeneratorBase.process_mesh_data aborts to num_triangles = 0 above 500,000, which yields an empty mesh, which routes to the fallback plane, which measures as a dead axis. The heaviest rung is warren at 24,656 -- 4.9% of the cap. All four also stay under the 30,000 cutoff at which _create_collision skips the trimesh, so collision is built at every rung exactly as it is today; no rung changes what a player can walk on.

THE REPLICA HAD TO BE FLOAT32, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING because it will bite the next person who replicates one of these shaders. A float64 first pass disagreed with the shipped artifact by 3.7x on the mesh AABB. The cause is in the noise: `float n_ = 0.142857142857` is a TRUNCATED 1/7, and float32 rounds it to 0.14285715 -- just ABOVE 1/7 -- while float64 keeps it just below. `floor(j * ns.z)` and `floor(p * ns.z * ns.z)` therefore land on different integers for every p that is a multiple of 49, about 7% of gradient lookups, and each one picks the WRONG SIMPLEX GRADIENT. In float64 snoise ranged +-4.7 with std 0.687; in float32 it is the well-behaved +-0.96. THE VALIDATION, and it is why the numbers in dna.note and dna.predicted_degeneracy are quoted at all: the corrected replica puts the shipped rung's AABB centre at y = -9.38 against this entry's own measured -9.91, and its cell-quantised height at 56.25 m against the measured 49.62 -- inside one 4.6875 m voxel at each end, which is exactly the error a cell-quantised bound should have.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: `none` against `undercut`, at 8.55% focus / 2.11% frame, with `caverned` against `warren` the FARTHEST at 58.37% / 24.28%.

THE APPROVED DESIGN PREDICTED THE EXACT OPPOSITE -- caverned/warren closest, at about 5% of frame -- and named none/undercut as the pair it would be wrong about. It was wrong about it, and that is the whole value of having written it down.

WHY THE DESIGN'S ARITHMETIC MISSED, which is the part worth keeping. It reasoned in METRES OF SURFACE DISPLACEMENT: k rises by 0.4, caveNoise is typically ~0.5, density converts to metres at the :189 gradient of 1/30, so ~6 m of movement. Measured, that model is right about the metres and useless about the picture. none -> undercut moves the top surface 6.66 m on average and undercut -> caverned only 1.89 m, yet they render 8.55% and 13.03% apart: the SMALLER displacement produces the LARGER change. What tracks the picture is added surface AREA, not vertical travel -- a cave mouth that opens adds silhouette where there was none, while a hillside that slides down 6 m looks like the same hillside. The triangle counts say it plainly (12,824 / 14,996 / 16,382 / 24,656), and warren, the only rung that adds eight thousand triangles, is the only rung that is far from everything.

FULL PREDICTED TABLE, closest first. Computed by ray-marching the same float32 density field from the sweep's own standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, dna.framing 0.45) at the 160 x 160 the critic resizes to, Lambert-shaded. NO material, no lights rig, no marching-cubes interpolation, so these must not be quoted as bite numbers -- they answer only which pair is closest and whether this is a 3% axis or a 50% axis.

  none     <-> undercut    8.55 focus /  2.11% frame
  undercut <-> caverned   13.03        /  2.61%
  none     <-> caverned   18.15        /  3.85%
  none     <-> warren     54.85        / 24.45%
  undercut <-> warren     55.75        / 23.92%
  caverned <-> warren     58.37        / 24.28%

SO THE PREDICTED SHAPE IS THREE CLOSE RUNGS AND ONE FAR ONE, and that is itself the prediction: anything paired with warren should land near 24% of frame and everything else between 2% and 4%. It is not a defect. The phenomenon is genuinely non-linear in k -- an inside appears at 0.25, is 1.2% of columns at the shipped 0.4 and 10.3% at 0.8 -- and an axis is allowed to be unevenly spaced when the thing it describes is, provided it says so with numbers.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS. (a) If none <-> undercut comes back under 6% the critic will call it a twin, and the cause will be that a flat Lambert replica overstates how much a shallow cave mouth survives the 160 x 160 downsample; the repair is a higher `undercut`, not a dead axis. (b) If the ranking inverts and caverned <-> warren comes back closest after all, the replica is wrong about occlusion: it ray-marches a first hit with no shadowing, and warren's deep caves are exactly where a real key light would put black. (c) If ANY pair reads 0.00%, do not file it as INERT -- the shader did not reimport. Headless Godot never reimports a .glsl, and a stale compiled shader is this sequence's known way of publishing byte-identical tiles under a correct axis (gyroid_demo, sixteen of them). Check source_md5 in .godot/imported/*.md5 against the file hash, NOT the mtime, which gave seven false positives.

AND ONE THING THAT SHOULD NOT MOVE AT ALL: the x and z extent. The mesh AABB is 300 x 300 in the horizontal plane at every rung, to the voxel, because the field is defined everywhere in the chunk and crosses the threshold out to every side face. If a pair's diff shows the silhouette's left or right edge moving, something is reaching chunk_scale that should not be.
dna.kin:
marchingcubes_flat_landscape, in procgen_extra.json, is THE SAME SCENE -- marchingcubes_flat_landscape.tscn -- and carries one map placement of its own (`marchingcubes_flat_landscape:0:-2` in ProceduralGenerationMarchingcubesFlatLandscape). Named here rather than silently co-declared so the next pass copies it deliberately, having read this, instead of discovering the duplication from a diff.

SEQUENCE-LEVEL, FOUND WHILE DOING THIS AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: the token `marchingcubes_portal_landscape` in procgen_extra.json resolves to Scenes/marchingcubes_overhang_landscape.tscn, while `mc_portal_landscape` in isosurfaces.json resolves to marchingcubes_portal_landscape.tscn. mc_flat_landscape.description: GPU flat terrain — marching cubes landscape with gentle noise.
mc_flat_landscape.name: mc_flat_landscape
mc_flat_landscape.qfep_connection: A heightfield marched into terrain — the gentlest landscape the algorithm can speak, one value per column, the ground as a graph of a function.

dna.default: landform=compound, a SHORT-CIRCUIT and not a formula that lands near the shipped numbers. TerrainGeneratorOverhang.gd declared no @export of its own and never did; the four numbers this artifact has were literals inside MarchingCubesOverhangTerrain.glsl. `compound` is the const 4-tuple LANDFORM_WEIGHTS["compound"] = [0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3], which IS the four literals that used to be written inline at :171, :198, :219 and :229 - they were moved from the shader to a GDScript const and handed back through four uniforms in the same order, so each masked noise product is multiplied by the same float32 it always compiled in. CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: each rung value was packed through PackedFloat32Array's own rounding and compared bit for bit against the float32 the GLSL literal compiles to - 0.8 -> cdcc4c3f, 0.6 -> 9a99193f, 0.4 -> cdcccc3e, 0.3 -> 9a99993e, all four identical. (float64-then-float32 and direct-float32 can only differ on a tie, and none of these four is one.) THE ONE HONEST CAVEAT, stated rather than glossed: the multiplier is now a uniform where it was a literal, so a driver that contracts `a * 0.8` and `a * params.overhangWeight` into different FMA shapes could differ in the last bit. Both are the same single-multiply expression, so there is no known compiler that does - but that is the exact size of the claim: not `the bytes are proven equal`, but `the same floats travel the same expression`. FIVE PLACEMENTS ON THIS SCENE UNDER TWO NAMES, none of which passes a config key, reaching the artifact by two paths. (1) TWO BARE GRID TOKENS: `mc_overhang_landscape` in ISO_FlatTerrain and `marchingcubes_portal_landscape:0:6` in ISO_PortalLandscape, where the `:0:6` is parsed into rotation_y and y_offset and never into config_data. Neither registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is EMPTY, GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate never opens, _apply_artifact_config is never called and no metadata is stamped. (2) THREE curation_station ROSTERS - Corridor_ISO_FlatTerrain and Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_1 here, Corridor_ISO_PortalLandscape on the sibling - and THESE DO CALL apply_grid_config, which an earlier draft of this promotion got wrong. curation_station.gd stamps identity at :376, add_child at :377 (so _ready has already run and _built_signature is already set), then unconditionally calls `inst.apply_grid_config({"emissive": false})` at :381-382. `emissive` is a valid identifier so config_emissive is stamped; _read_metadata_overrides looks only for config_landform and finds none; the recomputed signature equals _built_signature and the method returns at the second guard without regenerating. ArtifactIdentity.stamp() is the one route by which a registry could reach the property before _ready - it stamps config_<k> for each key of default_params - and both entries were checked: neither declares default_params. So all five build at compound, three of them through the guard rather than around it.
dna.was: 60 lines: a class name, a shader path, a fallback flat mesh, and an `apply_grid_config` whose entire body was `pass` - a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find something. The audit recorded ZERO exports, which is true and is not the same as having no parameters. MarchingCubesOverhangTerrain.glsl is not one formula, it is FIVE SCULPTURAL CLAIMS SUMMED, at :234-238 of the pre-promotion file: `density = baseTerrain - overhangDensity - caveStrength - archStrength + outcropStrength`. Each of the four added or subtracted terms carried its own strength literal (overhang 0.8 at :171, cave entrances 0.6 at :198, arches 0.4 at :219, rocky outcrops 0.3 at :229) and each is gated by its own smoothstep mask over elevation. The scene's own Label3D at marchingcubes_overhang_landscape.tscn:90 advertises the list IN WORDS - `Featuring: Rocky Overhangs / Cave Entrances / Natural Arches / Vertical Outcrops`. So the artifact makes a four-item promise in text, and until now the picture was never asked to keep it.
dna.note: landform is a NEW word, and the nearest relatives were read and refused. `taxonomy` (combine_capsule, facade_grammar_demo, +5) sorts a thing into a kind; this does not sort, it accumulates. `formation` (delaunay_triangulation_3d_cell, organic_space, +5) is about how a thing came to be arranged and presumes an agent. `relief` is spent on push_relabel_algorithm with a graph-theory meaning. `repertoire` is spent on mc_shapes_gallery in this very sequence and names a catalogue of separate objects rather than terms summed into one field. It is emphatically NOT `intrusion` (gyroid_demo, also this sequence): that word asks how much noise is allowed to touch a formula, and here EVERY term is noise - this asks which of five formulas are summed. `landform` is chosen because the shader's own local variables are already named for landforms (overhangDensity, caveStrength, archStrength, outcroppNoise), so the axis speaks the artifact's own vocabulary, which is the `fusion` / `bulge` pattern. THE RUNGS ARE AN ACCUMULATING LADDER, not four independent knobs, so every step is attributable to exactly one term: hillside [0,0,0,0] is baseTerrain alone, a pure heightfield with one value of y per column - the same null mc_flat_landscape argues, and the two artifacts STAND IN THE SAME MAP (ISO_FlatTerrain places both), which is the first time in this corpus two artifacts argue the same null side by side. overhung [0.8,0,0,0] is the first rung where the ground is not single-valued in y. quarried [0.8,0.6,0,0] is the rung at which the landscape acquires an INTERIOR - cave entrances open - and it is the rung that answers to the sequence's truth line, because here there starts to be an inside. arched [0.8,0.6,0.4,0] makes the ground a thing you can pass under. compound is what every existing placement has always shown. READ predicted_degeneracy BEFORE THE SWEEP: the replica says the ladder has five rungs but only three pictures, and it says so with numbers that a sweep can falsify.
dna.declined: REFUSED, THE FOUR MASKS, and this was the closest call. elevationFactor = smoothstep(-10, 20, surfaceHeight) at :170, caveMask = smoothstep(40, -10, worldPos.y) at :197, archMask (two smoothsteps at :216-217) and outcropMask at :228 together decide WHERE each landform is allowed to appear - a zoning ordinance written into a density function, and forcing all four to 1.0 would make the features apply everywhere and strip the landscape of its geography. dna.fixture_why: Neither key is an axis and both are already the shipped default, so this is a GUARD rather than a pin. It is here because this artifact's two silent failure modes both end in a published sheet that is a fact about the host machine rather than about the axis. use_fallback true, or a rendering device / SPIR-V load that fails on the capture host, drops straight into _create_fallback_mesh -> _create_simple_flat_mesh: a 60x60 plane of `sin(px*0.02)*cos(pz*0.02)*10.0`. It would also look plausible - a rolling landscape is exactly what you expect to see - which is what makes it dangerous. dna.framing_why: 0.55, and the number was COMPUTED from the field rather than guessed, because the registry's own measurements for this token are WITHHELD with the reason `the artifact simulates during the settle window and its AABB runs away (>500 m on one axis)`. THAT DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG and should not be trusted. The correlation across the six scenes in this wave is exact: every scene whose .tscn sets chunk_scale (flat 300, cave 300, inside_cave 280) measured cleanly at that number, and the only two withheld - overhang and portal - are the only two that leave chunk_scale at TerrainGeneratorBase's default of 1000. The artifact is not unstable; it is a kilometre wide, and the AABB that `ran away` is the correct one. Confirmed on the numpy replica: the SOLID fills the bottom of the box down to y = -484 m, but marching cubes emits triangles only where the field crosses the iso level, so THE MESH IS THE SURFACE BAND ONLY - measured extent 1000.0 x 62.5 x 1000.0 m at hillside and overhung, 1000.0 x 78.1 x 1000.0 m at quarried and above (the cave term opens the band 15.6 m further down). So the subject is a slab of aspect 1000:78:1000, far flatter than the 1000:150:1000 the design assumed, and fit-by-DIAGONAL is exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md names for wide flat subjects: the half-diagonal is 708.6 m while the projected height is 434.1 m. THE ARITHMETIC, at the sweep's own standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, elevation 14.90 deg): the screen-right extent of the box is 2*(0.8139*500 + 0.5810*500) = 1394.9 m and the screen-up extent is 2*(0.14938*500 + 0.96636*39.06 + 0.20925*500) = 434.1 m. Against a frame of 3.80 * 708.6 * framing, framing 0.55 gives a frame 1481 m across, so the subject fills 94.2% of frame WIDTH and 29.3% of frame HEIGHT. Width is the binding constraint - below about 0.52 the slab starts to clip - so 0.55 is close to as tight as this subject can be shot, and the 29% height is a fact about a landscape rather than a framing error.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`. It now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns unless a value the SHADER reads has actually changed. The signature is not a hand-listed tuple: it is get_params_array() itself, stringified - if a value reaches the GPU it is in the signature, so the guard cannot drift out of step with the build. WITH ONE EXCLUSION, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Index 0 is `time`, which this subclass does NOT hold at zero: unlike TerrainGeneratorGyroid it leaves the base's _process in place, so `time += delta` runs for the ~102 frames of the base's second dispatch cycle. Including it would make the signature differ from itself one frame later and turn the guard into an unconditional rebuild - the opposite of what it is for. Excluding it is safe for exactly one reason, checked in the shader rather than assumed: `params.time` is declared in ParamsBuffer and appears NOWHERE else in MarchingCubesOverhangTerrain.glsl - grep confirms zero references in evaluate() or main(). It is a field the terrain shaders inherit and this one does not read. Because the base tick is left in place, a config change can arrive while a dispatch is still outstanding, which the gyroid never has to handle; _drain_inflight() brings it to rest synchronously with the same two calls (fetch_and_process_compute_data, then create_mesh) that _ready makes back to back, and _regenerate keeps the redundant waiting_for_* check as a guard against the resubmit crash that release() documents. NOTHING IS FREED and no _owned array is kept, because this script creates no nodes at all: create_mesh() rewrites array_mesh's single surface in place and the only child added is the StaticBody3D the base's _create_collision() makes and removes itself. A blanket free of children is what cost three scripts a pass in the last wave - GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to the artifact after spawn, and this scene's Label3Ds, lights and WorldEnvironment are SIBLINGS of this node rather than children of it, because the script sits on the `Terrain` child and not on the scene root.
dna.still_note: Static by construction and a still is a complete account. TerrainGeneratorOverhang does not override _process, so the base ticks and re-dispatches ONCE (frame 0 run_compute, ~frame 12 fetch, ~frame 102 create_mesh, then set_process(false)), and that second pass is BIT-IDENTICAL: params.time is never read by the shader, and snoise is the Ashima/stegu simplex function - a pure function of position with no seed and no clock. The only thing that could move its sample point is noise_offset, which nothing sets. NO SEED IS NEEDED, which is worth saying out loud in a sequence of generators: five runs of the same rung are the same mesh. The mesh is finished when _ready returns.
dna.kin: THE SIBLING IS A CROSSED WIRE AND THIS PROMOTION DELIBERATELY DID NOT DECLARE ON IT. procgen_extra.json's token `marchingcubes_portal_landscape` resolves to scene marchingcubes_overhang_landscape.tscn - THIS scene, this script, this shader - while isosurfaces.json's `mc_portal_landscape` resolves to the actual marchingcubes_portal_landscape.tscn with class TerrainGeneratorPortals. So a token whose name says `portal` is placed twice (a bare `marchingcubes_portal_landscape:0:6` in ISO_PortalLandscape and a curation_station roster in Corridor_ISO_PortalLandscape) and both of those placements show an OVERHANG landscape. That makes the true placement count on this scene 5, not 3. The axis is NOT co-declared onto it, and the reason is deliberate rather than an oversight: writing `landform` onto a token whose name says `portal` would entrench the mislabel and make it harder to unpick, and any future reader diffing the two entries would take the shared axis as evidence that the two tokens are meant to be the same family. The next pass should FIX THE WIRE FIRST and co-declare second. Until then this note is the record. (This is the sixth hidden family found in this sequence, and it is the second kind: one scene under two registry names - the same shape as gyroid_demo / GyroidDemo.)
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE APPROVED DESIGN ON TWO COUNTS - which is the point, because a prediction that agrees with the sweep is worth nothing and one that disagrees is worth the whole pass. Method: evaluate() was transcribed into numpy, including the file's own Ashima/stegu snoise block verbatim, and run over the same 65^3 corner grid at the same parameters the scene actually uses (the .tscn sets NO property on the Terrain node, so noise_scale 2.0, iso_level 0.0, chunk_scale 1000, center_position (0,10,0), num_voxels_per_axis 64, centreSnapped (0, 15.625, 0)). Every term is LINEAR in its weight, so the four masked noise products are computed once and recombined per rung, which also proves the five rungs are one field differently weighted rather than five fields.

THE REPLICA HAD TO BE RUN IN float32, AND THIS IS THE KIND OF THING THAT SILENTLY PRODUCES A CONFIDENT WRONG NUMBER. The shader writes the literal 0.142857142857 for 1/7. Parsed to float32 that rounds UP to 0.14285714924, which is GREATER than 1/7; parsed to float64 it stays 0.142857142857, which is LESS. `j` is an integer, so for every j that is an exact multiple of 7 the two disagree about floor(j * ns.z) by one - 6 of the 49 residues, 14.2% of all samples - which sends y_ to 7, off the end of the 0..6 gradient table, and produces gradients of |p|^2 up to 4.7 where taylorInvSqrt's linear approximation goes NEGATIVE. In float64 the replica returned noise of std 0.69 and range +/-4.7; in float32 it returns std 0.359 and range +/-0.97, which is correct simplex noise. The first version of this prediction was computed on the broken one.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `arched` <-> `compound`, AND IT IS ESSENTIALLY ZERO - predicted focus under 0.1%, not the ~0.8% the design estimated. Measured as geometry rather than as pixels, so it does not depend on any rasteriser: over the cells that carry surface in either rung, adding the outcrop term moves the iso surface by a MEAN OF 0.030 m and a 95th percentile of 0.038 m. At framing 0.55 the frame is 1481 m across 760 px, i.e. 1.949 m per pixel, so that is 0.015 px. Not one surface cell appears or disappears. The reason is that outcropMask = smoothstep(surfaceHeight - 5, surfaceHeight + 15, y) puts the outcrop term ABOVE the terrain, where baseTerrain is already strongly negative, so 0.3 * outcropNoise almost never reaches the threshold; its mean contribution to density is 0.0103, which at the :152 gradient of 1/30 is 0.31 m on a body a kilometre wide.

SO `Vertical Outcrops` IS A WORD ON A SIGN AND NOT A THING IN THE PICTURE, and the artifact's own Label3D over-claims. THE DESIGN EXPECTED THAT ONE. IT DID NOT EXPECT THE SECOND: `quarried` <-> `arched` IS ALSO DEAD, at 0.057 m mean displacement = 0.028 px, predicted focus about 0.04%. archMask multiplies by smoothstep(30, 5, |worldPos.y - surfaceHeight|), so the arch term lives in a band 30 m thick around a surface that is sampled every 15.625 m - two samples thick - and the resulting term has |t| mean 0.00048 against the cave term's 0.479, a factor of ONE THOUSAND. `Natural Arches` is a word on a sign too. THE LADDER THEREFORE HAS FIVE RUNGS AND THREE PICTURES: {hillside}, {overhung}, {quarried = arched = compound}.

AND THE THIRD DISAGREEMENT: the design predicted hillside <-> overhung `well over 30%` because it is the only step that changes the topology of the silhouette. The replica says 2.52%, BELOW THE 3% DECORATION FLOOR - mean surface displacement 1.94 m, 95th percentile 7.16 m, about 0.96 px mean. The overhang term is real (it is what makes the ground not single-valued in y) but at 1000 m across and 14.9 degrees of elevation the overhangs are a texture, not a silhouette. THE LARGEST PAIR IS hillside <-> compound at about 8.5%, and the work is done almost entirely by the CAVE term: overhung -> quarried alone is 8.45%, mean displacement 15.8 m, p95 24.6 m, 4438 surface cells appearing and 4516 disappearing, and solid volume dropping 1.72 percentage points. That is the rung the sequence's truth line is about, and it is the only one that clearly bites.

FALSIFIABLE, IN ORDER: (1) arched<->compound under 0.1%; (2) quarried<->arched under 0.2%; (3) hillside<->overhung between 2% and 6%; (4) overhung<->quarried the largest adjacent step, over 6%; (5) the three top rungs cluster within 0.2% of each other. The absolute percentages come from a coarse proxy - the 65^3 corner samples binned into a 480 px orthographic depth image, shaded from the depth gradient, pooled to 160x160 - and the real render has finer geometry, true marching-cubes normals and real lights, so THE SWEEP SHOULD READ HIGHER THAN THESE NUMBERS, NOT LOWER. The four displacement figures in metres are not proxies and should hold. If the sweep reports arched<->compound above 1%, the replica is wrong about where the outcrop term lands and this whole entry should be re-read rather than patched. IF THE PREDICTION HOLDS, the axis should ship as THREE values with arched and compound folded into quarried - but that is a decision for after the measurement, not before it.

mc_overhang_landscape.description: GPU overhang terrain — landscape with overhanging rock formations.
mc_overhang_landscape.name: mc_overhang_landscape

measurements.withheld_reason: measurement withheld: the artifact simulates during the settle window and its AABB runs away (>500 m on one axis). Neither this run's value nor April's frozen-at-frame-2 value describes the body. Needs a stability-aware measure.

mc_overhang_landscape.qfep_connection: The terrain heightfields cannot make: overhangs. A full 3D field permits inside-above-outside, and the cliff leans over your head — the moment the third dimension of the data becomes visible as shelter.

dna.default: strata=all, swell=rolling - both exact no-ops, and one of them needed care to stay that way. _strata_weights() returns the literal Array [1.0, 0.2, 0.3], which is the same three doubles calculate_terrain_density always compiled: 1.0 was the IMPLICIT weight on height_noise (x * 1.0 returns the identical bit pattern for every finite float), 0.2 and 0.3 were the inline literals on the two lines below it. IT IS AN Array AND NOT A Vector3, deliberately: Vector3 components are 32-bit, so Vector3(1.0, 0.2, 0.3).y widened back to a GDScript double is 0.20000000298023224, and the short-circuit would have landed NEAR the shipped weight instead of ON it - a 1.5e-9 error, invisible in any picture, and exactly the class of thing that makes the phrase 'bit-identical' a lie. _swell_height() returns terrain_height itself rather than the number 5.0, so the HeightSlider path is untouched too. FIVE MAP REFERENCES ACROSS TWO NAMES AND NOT ONE PASSES A CONFIG KEY. Three are direct grid tokens - `mc_terrain_demo:0:-2` (ISO_FlatTerrain), `marching_cubes:0:2:0.5` (ISO_Showcase_12) and `marching_cubes:0:2:0.5` (ProceduralGeneration_Marching_Cubes_Algorithm) - rotation, height and scale only, no `#` tail, so the parsed config_data is empty. Neither registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is EMPTY for all three and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate at line 1194 means _apply_artifact_config is never called at all: no metadata is stamped and apply_grid_config is never reached. The other two are curation_station mounts (Corridor_ISO_FlatTerrain, Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_1), and the station DOES call apply_grid_config - with {"emissive": false} (curation_station.gd:382), after add_child, so _ready has already run and recorded the signature. That dictionary contains no axis key, the signature is unchanged, and the guard returns before _rebuild_terrain. Zero of five reach the rebuild branch.
dna.was: 411 lines and ZERO exports: a walkable-terrain demo authored as a standalone scene, with an `apply_grid_config` whose entire body was `pass` - a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find something. It also shipped UNSEEDED. setup_terrain_generator called `TerrainGenerator.new()` with no argument and setup_noise_generators:67 reads `var actual_seed = seed_value if seed_value >= 0 else randi()`, so every launch drew a different terrain. That is not an inference from reading: this registry's own `measurements` block records an aabb_size y of 0.89 here and 0.33 on `marching_cubes` for THE SAME SCENE measured in the same pass on 2026-08-12T04:39:51Z. Two numbers, one scene, one timestamp - which is what a randi() seed looks like from the outside, and it is the thread that led to reading the density function properly.
dna.note:
strata is a NEW word and the nearest taken relatives were each refused for a reason. `landform` (mc_overhang_landscape) and `interior` (mc_flat_landscape) name what a field PRODUCES; strata names which summands it is BUILT FROM. `octaves` (mc_cave, mc_inside_cave) is how many scales of ONE noise survive; this is which of THREE DIFFERENT noises contributes at all. `admixture` and `fusion` are held elsewhere in this same sequence with the sense of blending one field into another, which is a smooth knob; strata is a switchboard.

THE RUNGS, and the arithmetic that sizes them. calculate_terrain_density sums three noises into one height: height_noise (TYPE_PERLIN, frequency 0.05, 4 octaves, gain 0.5, lacunarity 2.0, weight 1.0), detail_noise (TYPE_SIMPLEX, frequency 0.15, 2 octaves, weight 0.2) and feature_noise (TYPE_CELLULAR, RETURN_CELL_VALUE, frequency 0.015, weight 0.3). The axis multiplies those three weights and touches nothing else. all = SHIPPED (1.0, 0.2, 0.3). bedrock = (1, 0, 0), the pure fBm ground with no cells and no crust. cells = (0, 0, 1), cellular alone. fine = (0, 1, 0), simplex alone. The sole-layer rungs carry weight 1.0 rather than the shipped 0.3 and 0.2 so each shows its layer at full strength, which makes `all` about 1.5x the amplitude of a sole rung - stated rather than hidden, and the reason swell is crossed with it.

AND THEN THE FOOTPRINT ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS THE FINDING OF THIS PASS. The controller sets terrain_size 10 against a chunk of 16 x 0.8 = 12.8 m, so the grid is exactly ONE chunk and the whole artifact is 12.8 m across. Measure each layer's feature size against that: Perlin at 0.05 has a 20 m base period, so the footprint is 0.64 of one period plus its 10 / 5 / 2.5 m octaves - a broad ramp with wiggles, which is the picture everyone has seen. Simplex at 0.15 gives 6.7 m and 3.3 m features - about two bumps across the footprint, genuinely the finest of the three. Cellular at 0.015 has a lattice spacing of 66.7 m. THE FOOTPRINT IS 0.19 OF ONE VORONOI CELL. RETURN_CELL_VALUE is constant per cell, so at this artifact's own scale the third summand is not a layer of features at all - it is a single number, a DC offset of up to +/-0.6 m on the shipped weight. That is why `cells` is predicted to photograph as one perfectly flat plate (see predicted_degeneracy), and it is a better answer to `what is the field made of` than a prettier rung would have been: one third of this field is a constant.

swell is also NEW. `relief` was the natural word and is taken once by push_relabel_algorithm, where it means the graph algorithm's relabel operation - an unrelated question, so reusing it would confuse rather than build a family. Not `bulge` (queer_marching_cave), which is a local swelling of a cave wall rather than the global amplitude of a height field. The literal is terrain_height = 5.0, declared twice (TerrainGenerator:21 and TerrainDemoController:30) and reaching the field through update_terrain_parameters()'s "height" key; it scales the entire noise sum and nothing else.

THE LADDER DOES NOT REACH ZERO, and the approved design asked that it should - `plane = 0.0`, a perfectly flat slab, offered as the evidence for the defect below. IT RENDERS NOTHING, and the arithmetic is short. Chunks are created at y = 0.0 (create_terrain_voxel_grid:169) and sampled upward for 12 x 0.8 = 9.6 m, so the box floor IS the mean plane. The density ladder lerps 0.45 -> 0.75 across the unit below the surface and therefore crosses iso 0.5 at surface_factor 1/6, i.e. 0.167 units BELOW the geometric surface. At amplitude 0 the extracted surface sits at y = -0.167, outside the sampled column; every voxel in the box reads 0.45 or less; marching cubes finds no crossing anywhere and the tile is empty. Nor can a small amplitude stand in for it: LOW AMPLITUDE RENDERS LESS, NOT FLATTER, because only the fraction of the footprint where combined_height clears 0.167 gets any geometry at all. So the rungs go UP from the default instead of down to zero: rolling = 5.0 SHIPPED, subdued = 2.5, hills = 9.0, range = 13.0. CEILING ARITHMETIC, do not overshoot: at 13.0 the crest is max_sum x 13 x 0.4, and `all` has a maximum sum near 1.5, so 7.8 m - still inside the 9.6 m column. Above about 15 the terrain leaves the chunk and the rung photographs as holes rather than as mountains.
dna.declined:
REFUSED, surface_threshold (0.5): `threshold` is taken by mc_torus_sculpture, and here it would also be degenerate - calculate_terrain_density is monotone in distance_to_surface, so a constant threshold offset is exactly a vertical translation of the extracted surface and would argue with swell for the same pixels. REFUSED, debug_disable_surface_variation and debug_minimum_density: the controller hardcodes debug_mode true and min_density 0.7, so surface_var is permanently 0.0; switching it on adds detail_value * 0.05 = +/-0.01 into a band 0.30 wide, a 3.3% perturbation of the transition zone, below the bite floor - and two values is below the axis floor anyway. REFUSED, noise_frequency (0.05): a real field property, but the same ratio question as `resolution`, already used twice in this sequence. REFUSED, chunk_size and voxel_scale: the sampling lattice, i.e. resolution again. REFUSED, terrain_size, the chunk material and the wireframe flag: a footprint and chrome.

FOUR THINGS REPORTED AS DEFECTS RATHER THAN SWEPT.

1. THE HEADLINE: THIS ARTIFACT'S FIELD IS TWO-DIMENSIONAL. All three layers are sampled with get_noise_2d(world_pos.x, world_pos.z) and the density is a five-branch piecewise ramp in world_pos.y minus that height. Density is monotone decreasing in y at every column, so there is exactly one crossing per column: the field is a height function extruded, and it cannot produce an overhang, a cave, a bridge or a disconnected body - the entire subject of the sequence it sits in. Its own registry description promises 'configurable noise parameters'; what it cannot do is the thing marching cubes is for.

2. THE LADDER DOES NOT CROSS ITS OWN THRESHOLD AT THE SURFACE. lerp(0.45, 0.75, surface_factor) = 0.5 at surface_factor = 1/6, so the extracted iso-surface sits 0.167 units BELOW the geometric one everywhere. (The approved design put this at 0.833, which is 1 - 1/6 - the complement, not the offset.) Combined with a chunk floor at y = 0 this is why roughly half the footprint carries no geometry at the shipped settings: wherever combined_height < 0.167 the whole column is air. The shipped picture is a partial sheet, not a ground.

3. A 73.36 m DECORATIVE PLANE, 5.7x THE ARTIFACT. marching_cubes_terrain_demo.tscn carries a MeshInstance3D with a PlaneMesh at scale 36.68 and a translucent pink material, sitting at y = -0.1. The terrain is 12.8 m. That plane is the entire content of this registry's `measurements.aabb_size` of [73.36, 0.89, 73.36] and of both entries' footprint_measured of 74 x 74 cells - a spatial contract, a placement footprint and a capture framing all sized to a backdrop rather than to the artifact. It is left in place (it ships in all five placements and defaults are sacred) and dna.framing is set against it instead; see framing_why.

4. A LEAK ON EVERY GENERATION. TerrainGenerator.generate_walkable_collision allocates a bare `Node3D` as temp_parent, parents the navigation tiles and the VR teleport markers to it, and frees it only on its two early-return branches. On the success path it is never freed and never enters the tree, so every regeneration strands a Node3D and its tile children. Not touched here: fixing it changes the shipped path, and this pass owes those five placements a bit-identical build.
dna.fixture_why: TWO KEYS, both guards against publishing a fact about the harness. terrain_seed = 7 is law 4: the shipped call site is `TerrainGenerator.new()` with no argument, setup_noise_generators:67 falls through to randi(), and sixteen tiles of an unseeded generator are sixteen different terrains - the bite number would be noise wearing evidence's clothes. The export defaults to -1, which is the same `seed_value >= 0` test failing exactly as it did before, so nothing shipped changes. build_synchronously = true is law 6: _ready's shipped path is call_deferred("generate_terrain_async") and the generator awaits process_frame at three points, so the mesh does not exist until roughly five frames after _ready. SETTLE is 1.1 s in capture_config_sweep, which is far more than five frames, so this is BELT AND BRACES rather than a fix for a known failure - but a half-built terrain photographs as a smaller subject and the sweep's union AABB is computed in a PRE-PASS with a 0.35 s settle, which is the tighter budget and the one that decides the camera for all sixteen tiles. Both values are written as a real int and a real bool, never as the strings "7" and "true", because capture_config_sweep assigns fixture values straight onto the typed export before _ready and a typed int rejects a String. NOTHING WAS MERGED OVER: this dna block was created by apply_dna_block.py in this same pass and had no fixture key of its own, so there is no second "fixture" for the last one to win over.
dna.framing_why: 0.13, an unusually tight number, and it is set against the 73.36 m decorative plane rather than against the terrain. THE ARITHMETIC, because a number this far from 1.0 should be checkable. capture_config_sweep frames one UNION AABB for the whole sweep (line 395), and that union is dominated by the PlaneMesh: 73.36 x ~4 x 73.36, radius 51.9. dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = radius * 6.215 * framing, and the half-extent of the frame at the look-at plane is dist * tan(17 deg), so half_extent = 98.6 * framing metres. The terrain is a 12.8 m square; at the canonical yaw of 0.62 rad its projected half-width is 12.8 * (cos + sin) / 2 = 8.9 m, and its centre sits 1.4 m off the union centre in x and z (the chunk spans -5.0 to +7.8, not -6.4 to +6.4), which projects to about 1.95 m - so 10.9 m must fit. framing 0.11 fits it exactly; 0.13 gives 12.8 m, a 15% margin. TWO FAILURE SIGNATURES, so the next reader does not have to guess which way to move it: if the terrain comes back at ~3% of frame with a pink field around it, the union is bigger than modelled and framing must go LOWER; if any corner of the terrain is cropped, it must go higher. Precedent for the magnitude: grid3d already declares 0.12. Note also that because ONE union serves all sixteen tiles, the usual worry that an AABB-fitted camera absorbs an amplitude axis does not apply here - the camera does not retreat for `range`.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`. It now reads strata / swell / terrain_seed, builds a signature of every value the build consumes (the two axes plus the seed, terrain_size and noise_frequency) and RETURNS when it has not moved. _ready records that same signature before the first build, so the grid's deferred call - which always arrives after _ready has already built with the same values - returns without doing anything. Rebuilds are SYNCHRONOUS: _rebuild_terrain frees, re-creates the generator (the seed is read once in _init) and calls the new generate_terrain_sync(), so there is no call_deferred in a build path. FREEING IS BY REGISTER, NOT BY NAME. The script keeps an _owned array of the meshes and collision bodies it actually put into the tree and frees only those, remove_child before queue_free so a rebuilt chunk cannot collide with a still-queued sibling and get renamed TerrainChunk_0@2. The pre-existing clear_previous_terrain(), which frees by name prefix, is left exactly as it was for the Generate button. ONE ORDERING HAZARD, checked rather than assumed: curation_station calls apply_grid_config DIRECTLY (not deferred) on every artifact it mounts, with {"emissive": false}. It does so AFTER add_child (curation_station.gd:378-382), so _ready has run - but a null-generator guard is in place regardless, because a composer that configures before parenting would otherwise rebuild against a null.
dna.still_note: Static once built, and a still is a complete account of it. _process exists and runs, but it only moves the demo's own Camera3D (which the sweep stands down as chrome) and updates VR teleport previews for controllers this scene has none of - nothing in the frame moves. The terrain itself is built once and never touched again. THE SYNCHRONOUS TWIN IS AN EXTRACTION, NOT A REWRITE: generate_terrain_meshes_async's loop body was lifted verbatim into build_chunk_mesh(i) and both paths call it, so they cannot drift apart. The three awaits it drops are unconditional yields with no read or write between them, so the mesh should be identical - and that is CHECKABLE rather than assertable: run both paths at the same terrain_seed and compare get_terrain_info().total_vertices, which must agree exactly. If they do not, the synchronous path is wrong and the fixture, not the artifact, is what the sheet is measuring.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
TWO PREDICTIONS, and the second one is the interesting one because it predicts a DEFECT.

strata, PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: all x bedrock, predicted ~7% focus. They differ by exactly (0.2 * detail + 0.3 * feature) * terrain_height * 0.4 = (0.2 d + 0.3 f) * 2.0 at swell=rolling. The cellular term f is a CONSTANT across this footprint (see note - 0.19 of one Voronoi cell), so 0.3 f * 2.0 is a pure vertical offset of up to +/-0.6 m that moves no silhouette at all, and what is actually left between the two frames is 0.2 d * 2.0 = +/-0.4 m of simplex ripple on a sheet whose whole relief is about 1.5 m. That is 27% of the relief but it lives in shading rather than in outline. If it comes back under 3% the two tiles are photographs of the same Perlin ridge and the honest reading is that two of this artifact's three layers are decoration at its own scale.

swell, PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: rolling x subdued, predicted ~6% focus. Note this is NOT the pair with the smallest ratio - hills:range is 1.44 against rolling:subdued's 2.0 - because the camera is pinned by one union AABB and does not retreat, so what the frame sees is the ABSOLUTE difference in relief: rolling minus subdued is 2.5 * 0.4 * max_sum ~ 0.75 m, while hills minus range is 4.0 * 0.4 * max_sum ~ 1.2 m. The low rung also loses coverage - the fraction of the footprint clearing the 0.167 iso offset drops from about 45% to about 30% - so if subdued measures LARGER than predicted, the axis is being read as coverage rather than as relief, and that is a true statement about the artifact rather than an error.

THE RISK THAT IS NOT A CLOSEST PAIR: `cells` MAY PHOTOGRAPH AS FOUR EMPTY FRAMES, and this is predicted deliberately so that an empty tile is not read as a broken harness. With the cellular layer alone, combined_height is the single constant c * terrain_height * 0.4 across the entire footprint, and geometry exists only where that clears 0.167 - i.e. only when c > 0.083 at rolling, c > 0.032 at range. c is one hash of one Voronoi cell under seed 2007 (terrain_seed 7 + 2000) and is roughly uniform on [-1, 1], so it is close to a coin flip. HEADS: four tiles of one perfectly flat plate at four heights - which is, ironically, the flat-slab picture the approved design wanted from swell=plane and could not have. TAILS: four empty tiles. IF IT COMES BACK EMPTY THE FIX IS THE FIXTURE SEED, NOT THE AXIS AND NOT THE WEIGHTS - raise terrain_seed until the cell value is positive, and RECORD which seed, because that number is then load-bearing for every future sweep of this token.
dna.kin: `marching_cubes`, in alternative_geometries.json, is THE SAME SCENE - marching_cubes_terrain_demo.tscn - one of this sequence's one-scene-many-names families, and it carries 2 of the 5 placements under its own name. The declaration is written into BOTH entries rather than one, because check_dna_declarations.registry() and the gallery builder resolve a token to the LAST registry file (sorted) that names a scene, and both of these do; a declaration on only one of them would be reachable from one token and invisible from the other. The two entries' prose is identical on purpose. Their `measurements` blocks are NOT identical (aabb_size y of 0.89 against 0.33) and that difference is the unseeded randi(), not a difference between the artifacts.
