mc_terrain_demo.name: mc_terrain_demo
mc_terrain_demo.qfep_connection: The terrain workbench: density thresholds, noise octaves, resolution — dials on a landscape. Turning them shows the ground to be an opinion held by a field.

dna.family: ONE SCENE, TWO REGISTRY NAMES. `rhizome_cave_demo` and `rhizome_cave_system` both resolve to res://algorithms/spacetopology/marchingcubes/scenes/rhizome_cave_demo.tscn, so both entries declare the same two axes and a sweep of either measures the same object. Path verified rather than assumed: that .tscn's ext_resource names the real RhizomeCaveDemoController.gd and the ROOT node carries it, so both axes are reachable from a map token. DO NOT read algorithms/marchingcubes/scenes/rhizome_cave_demo.tscn — a second file of that name exists there and is an empty three-line stub ([gd_scene format=3] plus a bare Root node), and neither registry entry points at it.
dna.default: anastomosis=netted returns the float 6.0 — the same literal the controller's hardcoded rhizome_params dict has always handed to set_growth_rules — and bore=tunnel returns 1.0, where `radius * 1.0` is the identical bit pattern for every finite float, so carve_sphere receives the argument it always did. Both are SHORT-CIRCUITS out of a constant dictionary, not values re-derived from a formula that happens to land nearby. REACH MEASURED, and it is 3 direct grid placements plus 16 indirect hosts: `rhizome_cave_demo` bare in SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network and bare in ISO_Showcase_12; `rhizome_cave_system:0:-0.5` in Gallery_ProceduralGeneration, which is rotation and y-offset and carries no config; two curation_station rosters (Corridor_SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network and Curation_Bay_postfoundationscrisis_2); and fourteen `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:s#mount:rhizome_cave_demo` mounts across eight Trial_* museum maps. The `#` parameters on those host tokens belong to the HOST and are never forwarded to the mounted artifact. Neither registry entry declares default_params, so merged_config is empty at every one of the nineteen and GridInteractablesComponent does not reach _apply_artifact_config at all — the guarded rebuild below is unreachable from every map that exists.
dna.was: merge_distance = 6.0, typed into the rhizome_params dict at RhizomeCaveDemoController:62. The carve radius had no multiplier at all: carve_sphere used node.radius directly, from the initial node radius 3.0 (RhizomeCaveGenerator:332) and the chamber multiplier 2.0 (:366).
dna.note: WHERE THIS ARTIFACT'S FIELD COMES FROM, which is what wave 3 of the isosurfaces sequence is asking. Nowhere else in the sequence is the answer 'from a history'. Every other member samples a function at each lattice point — a gyroid, a noise, a sum of metaball kernels. This one evaluates nothing: generate_cave_async fills the whole chunk with density 1.0 (:346-349) and then SUBTRACTS, carve_sphere writing min(current, dist/voxel_radius) (:265) along a graph that grew iteration by iteration out of an RNG. The field is a record of what happened. Both axes are lifted out of that record, one from the growth and one from the carve, and they are orthogonal by construction: anastomosis decides the graph and never touches a radius; bore scales the radius and cannot reach the graph, because the graph is finished before the first voxel is written. ANASTOMOSIS asks whether a branch that meets an existing one rejoins it or stops. RhizomeGrowthPattern.find_merge_candidate (:171-176) returns the first existing node within merge_distance of a proposed branch tip; on a hit create_connection adds an EDGE and `continue` suppresses the new node, which is the only way a circuit can enter this graph. tree=0.0: nothing is ever within 0 m, so nothing ever merges — a pure arborescence with dead ends and no circuit, the figure Deleuze and Guattari oppose and the thing this artifact's own truth statement claims to refute, rendered here for the first time. netted=6.0 SHIPPED. matted=12.0. knotted=20.0. THE CONFOUND, stated rather than hidden: raising merge_distance both adds edges and SUPPRESSES nodes, because the merging branch does not create the node it was going to create. The network gets loopier and smaller at the same time and no still can separate the two. BORE asks how wide the same graph is carved. The multiplier lives inside carve_sphere, the single gate every carve passes through (carve_tunnel reaches the field only by calling it), so the graph is bit-for-bit identical across all four rungs — same seed, same nodes, same positions, same rng draws. At thread the carve radius is 1.2 m against a 1.0 m voxel and the solid boundary sits at 0.6 of a voxel, so the tube is thinner than the sampling lattice and a continuous field extracts as a broken string of beads; at hollow the tubes swallow each other and the surface merges what the graph deliberately kept apart. Same field-making history, different surface: the boundary is not a property of the field alone.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: NEW WORDS, both. `anastomosis` is already the project's own — the mycelium substrate work names it as its open gap — and the nearest taken word is `fusion` (the metaballs family), which is how much two FIELDS merge; this is whether two PATHS rejoin, decided in the graph before any field exists. `bore` is not `bulge` (queer_marching_cave), which swells a wall locally as a function of position, and it is deliberately not `resolution`: voxel_scale is held at 1.0 on every rung and only the carve radius moves, which is exactly what makes the lattice interaction legible at thread instead of confounded with it.
dna.crossed_wire: The two axes are orthogonal in the arithmetic and NOT in the picture. A large bore visually fuses tubes the graph never joined, so inside the `hollow` column anastomosis reads weak and inside the `tree` row bore reads weak — both frames are the same swallowed box. GROUP THE CRITIC'S NUMBERS BY VALUE PAIR ACROSS CONTEXTS, not by per-axis mean, or anastomosis will be convicted of the bore's doing. Measured on the replica at the fixture's seed: the weakest single CELL is bore hall x hollow inside the tree row at 0.6%, and the weakest grouped PAIR is anastomosis netted x matted at ~26%. Those two numbers are forty times apart and they are about the same sixteen tiles.
dna.declined: threshold (0.5, RhizomeCaveGenerator:10) — taken by mc_torus_sculpture, and worse: on a field carved as the linear ramp dist/voxel_radius a constant threshold is EXACTLY a uniform change of carve radius, so it would argue with bore for the same pixels. vertical_bias (0.3, applied as direction.y *= vertical_bias at RhizomeGrowthPattern:157) — real and visible, the difference between a flat sheet of tunnels and a ball of them, but it is the same question as `plumb` (mc_cave, mc_inside_cave): which way the field prefers to go. Declined for the rhyme and recorded here rather than dropped. chamber_probability (0.25) — too close to `bulge`, and stochastic: at 0.25 over ~30 iterations the variance between seeds would exceed the difference between rungs. branch_probability (0.6) and max_depth (4) — population counts, the same shape of question as `metaball_count`. voxel_scale and chunk_size — the sampling lattice, i.e. `resolution`, already taken twice. REPORTED, NOT SWEPT: setup_parameters (:285-292) read only chunk_size, voxel_scale and threshold, so the `seed` key every caller has always passed — `"seed": randi()` in this controller, `"seed": 12345, # Reproducible generation` in examples/simple_cave.gd — has never reached the RNG. That key is now read, defaulting to -1, which is the sentinel RhizomeGrowthPattern._init already understood. It is not a bug that shows, which is why it survived.
dna.fixture_why: FOUR NUMBERS AND A FLAG, EACH ANSWERING A MEASURED FAULT. cave_seed=7: RhizomeCaveGenerator:321 built RhizomeGrowthPattern.new(randi()), so five variants of this artifact were five different caves and any bite number would have been noise dressed as evidence (law 4). chunk_extent=24: RhizomeVoxelChunk._init never takes a world_position, so it defaults to Vector3.ZERO and the sampled volume is world 0..N. min/max branch length 3.0..26.0: NOT cosmetic — see `finding`. build_synchronously=true: _ready deferred generate_cave_async and the build then spent five awaited process_frames plus a mesh loop that yields whenever it passes 8 ms, so law 6 was not met as shipped and the capture's 1.1 s settle was a race. The flag is read at the four `await get_tree().process_frame` sites inside the generator and nowhere else, so there is one build path and one thing that can be wrong; every player-facing placement leaves it false, because a 13k-voxel march must not gate map load.
dna.finding: TWO THINGS THE READING FOUND, both invisible to every gate in the loop, both measured on a numpy replica of RhizomeGrowthPattern's growth loop and RhizomeCaveGenerator's carve rather than argued. (1) THE PROPOSED CAPTURE FIXTURE WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A DEAD AXIS THAT LOOKED LIKE A DESIGN FAILURE. find_merge_candidate compares a proposed branch tip against every existing node, and the tip sits at most branch_length from its own parent, which is already a node. So a merge_distance above max_branch_length merges EVERY attempt with its parent, create_connection rejects the self-edge (node1 != node2), and the network never grows past its seed node. At the approved 2.0..6.0 the four rungs replicate as merge rates 0 / 100 / 100 / 100 percent and node counts 175 / 1 / 1 / 1 — netted, matted and knotted would all have photographed as ONE carved sphere, the closest pair would have been 0.00% twice, and the verdict would have been a fact about a fixture. The shipped 5.0..20.0 collapses knotted alone, since 20.0 is exactly max_branch_length. The fixture uses 3.0..26.0, which measures 0 / 34 / 59 / 89 percent merged and 175 / 65 / 18 / 3 nodes: four different graphs, monotone, none degenerate. (2) bore=hollow AT THE APPROVED 3.5 CANNOT BE PHOTOGRAPHED. The multiplier lands on node.radius and create_chambers has already multiplied that by rng 2.0..4.0, so at 3.5 a single chamber reaches 42 m and swallows any chunk this artifact can afford to march. Replicated, the hollow column at 3.5 is 100 / 100 / 93 / 9 percent of the box carved: tree and netted are the same empty box and that anastomosis pair measures 0.0%. hall and hollow are therefore implemented at 1.6 and 2.4, which leaves surface in fifteen of the sixteen cells; thread=0.4 and tunnel=1.0 are exactly as approved, because they are the default and the lattice argument and that is where this axis makes its point.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE THE CAPTURE, from the replica run at the fixture's own seed, extent and branch lengths. Grouped BY VALUE PAIR across all four bore columns — which is how `crossed_wire` demands they be read — the weakest anastomosis pair is netted x matted at ~26% of the projected silhouette: the two middle rungs differ 3.6x in node count (65 against 18) but both silhouettes are dominated by the same root chamber and its first-generation tunnels. tree x netted is ~34% and matted x knotted ~33%. The weakest bore pair is hall x hollow at ~16%. The silhouette is a projection and therefore an UPPER bound on a rendered frame, so expect roughly a third of these on frame: netted x matted around 8%, hall x hollow around 5%. THE APPROVED DESIGN PREDICTED matted x knotted as the closest anastomosis pair at ~7%, and the replica disagrees — it is the strongest of the three, because knotted collapses to three nodes while matted still carries eighteen. A prediction that agrees with the sweep is worth nothing; this one already disagrees with the design it came from, and the disagreement is what found the fixture fault above.
dna.budget: chunk_extent 24 is 13,824 voxels against the shipped 1,728 — 8x — and the mesh march is one 8-corner lookup per voxel per tile. The carve is the real cost and it is bore-dependent: replicated over all sixteen tiles at the fixture's seed it totals 13.0M voxel writes, about 0.8M per tile. That is only affordable because carve_tunnel's sample spacing is now floored at a quarter of the carved radius on the rungs above 1.0; at the shipped half-voxel spacing bore=hollow alone sweeps the entire chunk about fifty times per tunnel. Four samples per radius cannot leave a seam between consecutive spheres, and the gate is `carve_radius_scale > 1.0`, so bore=tunnel and bore=thread evaluate the shipped expression unchanged. Do not reach for 40^3: that is 37x and will meet the 16-second rule.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` — a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find it. It now stamps config_<key> metadata, re-reads the overrides and compares a signature built from the same accessors the build calls (_merge_distance(), _bore_scale(), cave_seed, chunk_extent, both branch lengths, build_synchronously), so the signature cannot drift out of step with what reaches the generator. Equal signature returns before touching anything. A real change calls _rebuild(), which frees ONLY RhizomeCaveGenerator._owned — the CaveMesh and CaveCollision this script created — and re-runs the same build; a blanket free of get_children() is what cost three scripts a pass in an earlier wave. _ready reads the metadata BEFORE building, and on the grid's own ordering (config stamped at GridInteractablesComponent:1195, add_child at :1220, apply_grid_config deferred afterwards) the first build already has the right values and the deferred call finds nothing to do: exactly one build per spawn.
dna.still_note: Nothing in this scene runs _process. More usefully, the picture is unusually literal about the axis: the chunk starts solid and RhizomeVoxelChunk.get_density (:38) returns 1.0 out of bounds, so the outer faces of the box carry no surface of their own and the only geometry is the inner wall of the carved network, drawn cull_mode CULL_DISABLED (:384). The frame IS the graph as a set of tubes, and a tree and a knotted net are different objects on sight. The one thing a still cannot separate is the confound named in `note`: loopier and smaller arrive together.
dna.kin: isosurfaces wave 3, the field-provenance wave. metaballs owns `fusion` and `metaball_count`, gyroid_demo `intrusion` and `period`, mc_torus_sculpture `threshold`, queer_marching_cave `bulge`, mc_cave and mc_inside_cave `plumb` — all of them properties of a function being sampled. This is the only member whose field is carved rather than evaluated, which is why its two words are about a history (whether paths rejoined) and a tool (how wide the cut was).

measurements.withheld_reason: measurement withheld: the artifact simulates during the settle window and its AABB runs away (>500 m on one axis). Neither this run's value nor April's frozen-at-frame-2 value describes the body. Needs a stability-aware measure.

marchingcubes_portal_landscape.qfep_connection: A landscape with a portal, marched from a scalar field — threshold as terrain and doorway at once. The level-set that decides where stone becomes air also decides where a passage opens, so the same number that shapes the ground carves the way through it. The field as both floor and gate.

iso_cave_console.name: Cave threshold comparison desk
iso_cave_console.description: Change plumb, octave, portal count and burial on the original cave fields; hold the question of access open.

dna.default: burial=straddling AND num_portals=7, both exact no-ops, and burial's is a SHORT-CIRCUIT rather than a table lookup. _emergence_height() returns the portal_emergence_height export UNTOUCHED at straddling, so marchingcubes_portal_landscape.tscn's override of 0.0 and the script's own default of -20.0 are BOTH preserved bit for bit, and no rung value has to be written that happens to equal the shipped one. That matters more here than anywhere else in the wave: this is the only scene in the marchingcave folder that overrides an export an axis touches, so a table whose default entry read -20.0 would have silently moved the one placed scene by 20 m and looked correct in every review. num_portals needs no mechanism at all — the axis IS the export, 7 is the export's default, clampi(7, 1, 32) is 7, and get_params_array() already passed float(num_portals) before this pass. So params[11] is the same 7.0 and params[15] the same 0.0, and both travel the same PackedFloat32Array(...).to_byte_array() to the same buffer offsets. REACH MEASURED, and the count is 3, all bare: a grid cell in ISO_Caves at interactables[3][3] with no rotation and no config (the same map holds mc_inside_cave at [3][10], so the map that shows you a cave from inside also shows you the doors, and queer_marching_cave at [6][6]); a curation_station roster in Corridor_ISO_Caves (#artifacts:mc_portal_landscape,mc_inside_cave#layout:row); and another roster in Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_1. None passes a config key and this entry declares no default_params, so merged_config is empty, GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate means apply_grid_config is never called at all, and zero of three reach the regenerate branch.
dna.was: 78 lines. Five @export numbers that fed a compute shader, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was the word `pass` — a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find it, so not one of the five was reachable from any map token. No axis. The artifact's own Label3D makes a strong topological claim, "UNIFIED MARCHING CUBES TOPOLOGY / Terrain and portals are ONE seamless mesh!", and nothing in the shipped configuration could test it, because portal_emergence_height was welded to whatever the .tscn set.
dna.note:
THE CLAIM AND THE ONE LINE THAT MAKES IT. MarchingCubesPortalTerrain.glsl:240 is `float density = max(terrainDensity, -portalsDensity);` — a CSG union of a heightfield with N torus SDFs, extracted as one surface. This is the only artifact in the isosurfaces wave where the boundary is something you could pass THROUGH, so both axes ask the same question, whether the doors are doors, arriving from opposite directions.

burial — WHERE THE RING SITS RELATIVE TO THE GROUND IT IS MADE OF. Because the operator is a UNION, a buried torus does not merely look half-sunk: its hole is filled by the terrain, so the passage closes. The axis is therefore over the GENUS of the extracted surface, argued by moving one number. straddling is shipped, the rings on the surface and the holes half open. sunken (-60.0) leaves only crowns breaking a surface that itself undulates over +/-20 m: stone hoops rising out of rock, all one substance, no way through. standing (+60.0) clears the hilltops while the tube still meets the ground at its feet — one connected mesh, seven doorways. floating (+140.0) puts the bottom of each ring ~65 m clear of the highest ground, the union has EIGHT disconnected components, and the artifact's own claim about ONE seamless mesh is visibly false. THE ARTIFACT ARGUES ITSELF FALSE AT ONE RUNG, which is what an axis is for.

num_portals — HOW MANY DOORS BEFORE A COLONNADE IS A WALL. The shader at :212 computes angleStep = TAU / numPortals and rings the portals around a FIXED circle of radius portal_spacing = 250, so the count does not change the arrangement's size, only its density. 1 is a single arch and the union has two components; 3 is a triangle of doorways you can see between; 7 is shipped; 16 puts them 98 m apart on a 1571 m circumference while each is 110 m wide, so they overlap into a continuous ring wall and the passages close by CROWDING rather than by burial.

THE RESOLUTION FACT A REVIEWER WILL OTHERWISE BLAME ON THE AXIS: this scene leaves chunk_scale at the base default of 1000 with num_voxels_per_axis fixed at work_group_size 8 * resolution 8 = 64, so the sampling cell is 15.6 m and portal_minor_radius is 15.0 — the torus tube is ONE CELL thick. The portals are at the lattice limit and will photograph as lumpy, faceted hoops rather than clean toruses. That is a fact about the shipped artifact, not about either axis.
dna.declined: REFUSED, portal_radius (40.0) and portal_minor_radius (15.0). Real exports, already in ParamsBuffer, and they would have cost nothing — refused because the minor radius is ALREADY one sampling cell, so shrinking it deletes the portals into the lattice and growing it is the same fattening burial gets for free by lifting the ring out of the ground. An axis whose low rung is indistinguishable from a bug is not an axis. REFUSED, portal_spacing (250.0): it is the radius of the arrangement, which is extent, and extent self-cancels under a fitted camera — with the twist that here it would also change the union AABB and so the framing of every tile. REFUSED, and this is the one worth arguing: the CSG OPERATOR at :233 and :240. Swapping max for min turns union into intersection and would say something enormous about what a field operator is. It is refused because `algebra` is spent on csg_compose_workbench and `fusion` on csg_union_demo, implicit_surface_modeling, metaballs and raymarched_metaballs, so the word is not available; and because an intersection of a heightfield with seven toruses is mostly empty, which routes to the portal-less fallback plane. It belongs to a CSG artifact, not to this one. REFUSED, iso_level, chunk_scale, center_position, continuous_update and invert_faces, for the reasons given on the other landscapes in this wave.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, and stated in the weaker currency it was actually computed in: PROJECTED AREA AGAINST FRAME AREA, by hand, not by rasterising the scene. Read it as an order-of-magnitude claim that the sweep can falsify, not as the critic's own hottest-5%-of-crop number.

THE CAMERA IT IS COMPUTED AT. capture_config_sweep sets dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34, PAD 1.9, RES 760, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, and radius = aabb.size.length() * 0.5 of the UNION box over all variants. The extracted surface is the terrain sheet, so the union box is about 1000 x 1000 in X/Z with a shallow Y, giving radius ~710 m. Then dist = 710 * (1.9 / tan 17deg) * 0.25 = 710 * 6.215 * 0.25 = 1103 m, and the frame is 2*tan(17deg) * 1103 = 0.6114 * 1103 = 674 m tall, so the frame is 674^2 = 454,000 sq m.

CLOSEST PAIR ON burial: standing (+60) vs floating (+140), AT ABOUT 7% OF FRAME. Each ring is an annulus of major 40 and minor 15, projecting roughly 2,240 sq m at this oblique angle; seven of them is ~15,700 sq m, and an 80 m translation moves them clear of their old positions, so roughly twice that area changes: 31,400 / 454,000 = 6.9%.

CLOSEST PAIR ON num_portals: 7 (shipped) vs 16, AT ABOUT 9%. Going 7 -> 16 adds nine rings of ~2,240 sq m each, so ~20,000 sq m of new material against 454,000 is 4.4% — doubled because the nine new rings also occlude the seven old ones and close the gaps between them. The largest pair should be 1 vs 16, over 25%.

THE RUNG THAT COULD GO WRONG IS 16: at 15.6 m cells, sixteen overlapping toruses could fuse into a featureless torus of revolution and read as one smooth ring rather than as a colonnade, which would look like a bug. If the tile shows that, the value should come down to 12 rather than the axis being called inert.
dna.framing_why: 0.25 IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC, and the arithmetic above is why. At framing 1.0 the same standing-vs-floating pair computes to about 2.1% of frame and would be filed as decoration — the axis reported dead by a camera standing 4x too far back, which is the letterbox failure in its purest form. At 0.25 the ring of portals (apparent width ~610 m, from a 250 m placement radius plus a 110 m ring) very nearly fills the 674 m frame and the 1 km terrain runs off all four edges, which is the correct crop when the subject of the axis is N objects inside a much larger body. AND THE FRAMING DOES NOT SELF-CANCEL AGAINST burial, which was the thing to check before choosing it: the union radius is 707 m at straddling and 716 m at floating, a 1.3% change, because the terrain sheet dominates both boxes. An extent axis would have moved the camera with the subject and measured near zero; this one does not.
dna.fixture_why:
NO FIXTURE, and it is worth saying which of the usual reasons do not apply. _ready() is not gated — TerrainGeneratorBase._ready() runs init_compute(), run_compute(), fetch_and_process_compute_data() and create_mesh() synchronously, so the artifact builds standalone on the bench with no map, no host and no config. There is no RNG and no seed to pin: the field is Ashima/stegu simplex noise, a pure function of position. And there is no clock to freeze in the picture — params.time is declared in the shared ParamsBuffer prefix at :107 and never referenced anywhere in MarchingCubesPortalTerrain.glsl.

ONE BENCH HAZARD THAT IS NOT A FIXTURE PROBLEM BUT MUST BE READ FROM THE LOG. _create_fallback_mesh() on this class calls _create_simple_terrain(), a smooth 600-segment plane WITH NO PORTALS IN IT. If the capture host cannot build a local RenderingDevice, every tile is that plane and both axes measure zero; and if process_mesh_data() ever trips its 500,000-triangle safety abort it sets num_triangles = 0 and the same decoy appears, which would measure as a colossal bite for entirely the wrong reason. The budget says it will not: at 15.6 m cells the terrain sheet is ~8,200 triangles and sixteen portals add ~13,000, so ~21,000 total, a factor of 24 under the cap. THE RUN IS ONLY VALID IF THE LOG SHOWS "Generation complete!" AND NOT "Creating fallback".
dna.rebuild_guard:
apply_grid_config stamps each config key as config_<key> metadata, re-reads the two overrides, and then compares _config_signature() — the shader's own input array, stringified at %.6f — against the signature captured at the end of _ready(). Equal means return; empty means _ready has not built yet and will read the metadata itself, so there is nothing to do. Only a real change reaches _regenerate(), which re-runs run_compute / fetch_and_process_compute_data / create_mesh in _ready's order and re-captures the signature.

INDEX 0 IS DELIBERATELY SKIPPED IN THE SIGNATURE, and this is a real difference from TerrainGeneratorGyroid, which stringifies all eleven of the base's floats. `time` is the first of the shared prefix, and this subclass does NOT override _process — the base's tick keeps advancing time for ~100 frames after spawn, until create_mesh sets _initial_generation_done and calls set_process(false). Including it would make the signature a CLOCK and every apply_grid_config call would read as a change. It cannot affect the mesh, because the shader never references params.time.

NOTHING IS FREED. This script owns no nodes and keeps no _owned array because it creates none: create_mesh() rewrites array_mesh's single surface in place and the base's _create_collision() removes only the StaticBody3D it made itself. A blanket free of children is what cost three scripts a pass in an earlier wave — GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to the artifact after spawn. _regenerate() also returns early on use_fallback, on a null rendering_device, and on waiting_for_compute / waiting_for_meshthread: resubmitting under a dispatch already in flight is the crash release() documents, and it is reachable here in a way it is not on TerrainGeneratorGyroid, because this subclass keeps the base's _process and is still cycling after _ready.
dna.still_note: Static. No _process override on this subclass, no RNG, no seed, and evaluate() never reads params.time. Four runs of one rung are the same mesh.
dna.kin:
num_portals borrows its SHAPE from raymarched_metaballs' metaball_count [1, 3, 5, 9] in this same sequence — a count axis over a field built by unioning N primitives, where the interesting rungs are 1 (the primitive alone), a small number (they are separate) and a large number (they merge into one body). Declared here so the two can be read against each other: if a count axis on seven toruses and a count axis on nine metaballs measure alike, the family is honest. The NAME has to be the export's own, because the sweep sets the property by name — the same constraint that forced queer_marching_cave to move a float off `resolution` before it could name an enum that.

`burial` is new as an axis name but is not a coined word: TerrainGeneratorPortals.gd:7 already comments portal_emergence_height as "How much of torus is buried". `emergence`, the obvious alternative and the export's own prefix, is TAKEN by catalyst_prompter_box and reusing it would put two unrelated meanings on one word. `grounding` is refused because it already means artifact-base-to-floor placement across this repo. `seam` is held twice (escher_staircase, florensky_sphere), `join` by csg_union_demo with a CSG meaning close enough to confuse, `breach` by fontana_puncture and subtraction_suite, and `hole` by torus_radials_rings — which is the right word for a torus's own proportions, not for where it sits.
dna.shader_contract: NO .glsl FILE WAS TOUCHED, and this is the one artifact in the wave immune to the stale-compiled-shader trap. ParamsBuffer already had all sixteen fields and get_params_array() already appended the five portal floats in that order, so both axes write exports that ALREADY fed the array. FIELD ORDER AND COUNT, BOTH SIDES, verified index by index: TerrainGeneratorBase.get_params_array():329 appends time, noise_scale, iso_level, float(num_voxels_per_axis), chunk_scale, center_position.x/.y/.z, noise_offset.x/.y/.z (indices 0-10); TerrainGeneratorUnifiedPortals.get_params_array() appends float(_portal_count()), portal_spacing, portal_radius, portal_minor_radius, _emergence_height() (indices 11-15). dna.note:
THE SEQUENCE'S TRUTH LINE, LITERALLY. 'Define a field, extract a surface. The boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry.' This script is the one place in the wave where the SAME field is shipped twice, once to be looked at and once to be stood inside, so an axis declared here has to mean something from both sides. You are INSIDE this one: the scene puts a Camera3D at (0, 5, 15) within the field with an OmniLight3D torch parented to it and no DirectionalLight3D anywhere, which is the actual reason it reads as an interior rather than as a block of rock.

plumb - WHICH WAY IS DOWN, AND WHETHER THERE IS A DOWN AT ALL. Everything this shader knows about gravity is one line, MarchingCubes.glsl:180: `density = -(worldPos.y+100)/300 + density`. It is the ONLY anisotropic term in the file; the six octaves above it are isotropic ridged noise, which on its own has no up. That one linear bias is what makes low regions solid and high regions air - from outside, the block's top surface and its sky; from inside, the floor you stand on. plumbScale multiplies it and nothing else. bedded (1.0) SHIPPED. overturned (-1.0) flips the sign: the same noise at the same threshold with inside and outside exchanged, rock overhead and nothing under your feet. weightless (0.0) DELETES the term and leaves pure ridged noise - an isotropic sponge with no floor, no ceiling and no sky, filling the sampled box to all six faces. steep (3.0) triples the gradient so the field swings 3.0 across the 280 m box instead of 1.0 and the solid retreats into the bottom third: a slab with a rough top, a crawl space. The four values are held IDENTICAL across all four declared tokens on purpose - it is one const on one script, and holding them identical is what makes the galleries comparable frame for frame.

octaves - HOW MANY SCALES OF ROCK SURVIVE THE LATTICE, AND THIS IS THE AXIS THAT MAKES THE SIBLINGS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS. :168 opens `for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++)`; each pass halves the amplitude and doubles the frequency, with the weight feedback at :174 gating each octave by the previous one. The literal 6 is the rung. What makes it worth declaring is arithmetic the two scenes do not share. THIS token: noise_scale 3.8, chunk_scale 280.0, so samplePos = worldPos x 0.01357 and octave 0 has ~74 m features; the marching lattice samples at 280.0/64 = 4.375 m, so its Nyquist limit is 8.75 m. The six octaves measure 73.7, 36.9, 18.4, 9.2, 4.6, 2.3 m, which puts 4 of them above the limit and the rest below it. On the sibling the same six octaves land differently, and that is the finding: mc_cave resolves TWO scales of rock, mc_inside_cave resolves FOUR, from the same script, the same shader, the same rungs and the same threshold. The artifact you stand inside can resolve two more octaves than the one you look at. That is the inside/outside asymmetry as a number rather than as a description, and it is why the axis is declared on both rather than on one.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE APPROVED DESIGN, both found by redoing its arithmetic. (1) The design said the inside scene resolves ONE more octave than the outside one; by the Nyquist figures above it is TWO (octaves 0-3 against octaves 0-1). (2) The design said the sub-limit octaves are 'COMPUTED AND THEN THROWN AWAY BY THE EXTRACTOR'. They are not thrown away, they ALIAS: content finer than the sampling cell still perturbs the corner values, which still moves where interpolateVerts puts the crossing. So the sub-limit rungs are predicted to be nearly degenerate, not exactly degenerate, and a small non-zero reading there is the expected result rather than a failed prediction.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE FIELD ITSELF: :170 is `snoise(samplePos) * 2 - 1` before the ridged fold, not the plain `snoise` of the usual Lague construction, so the input to `1 - abs(noise)` spans about [-3, 1] rather than [-1, 1] and the fold is off-centre. The amplitude LADDER still halves exactly (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125), which is what the octave arithmetic above rests on, but the per-octave term is not bounded by 1 and the summed density is not bounded by 1.969. Any claim about an absolute density total should be read as about the ladder, not about the sum.
dna.declined: REFUSED, `iso_level`, and the refusal is deliberate given that this wave promotes `threshold` on the torus. iso_level is the ONE export on which these two sibling scenes already disagree - 0.85 on marchingcubes_cave.tscn against 0.88 on marchingcubes_inside_cave.tscn - so an axis over it would say 'these two artifacts are one object at two thresholds', which is nearly irresistible. It is refused because on THIS shader the density carries a vertical gradient, so a constant offset to the threshold is a vertical translation of the rock/air horizon, which is the same horizon `plumb` moves: a bias of 0.15 is 45 m of horizon on a 300 m box, and plumb=steep moves it further. The two would measure each other at plumb=bedded and separate only at plumb=weightless - a conditional pair bought at the price of a confound. The torus pays gyroid_demo's bequest instead, because its field has no gradient term at all. REFUSED, the weight-gating literal 10 at :174 (`weight = max(0, min(1, noise * 10))`): it is the Lague trick that turns isotropic ridged fBm into connected tunnels and it is the closest thing in the file to an axis about whether the void is a passage or a sealed bubble - refused because at low values it also zeroes every octave after the first, so it conflates connectivity with detail and would be `octaves` wearing another name. REFUSED, `noise_offset` (a different arbitrary sample of the same field, and already fixed by the .tscn), `chunk_scale` and `center_position` (a size and a placement, both self-cancelling under an AABB-fitted camera), `continuous_update` (a rate, invisible in a still by law). REFUSED, `invert_faces`, AND THIS ONE IS A REPORTED DEFECT RATHER THAN A DECLINE. TerrainGeneratorBase:10 documents it as 'Flip triangle winding and normals (useful for objects vs caves)' and NEITHER cave scene sets it, so mc_inside_cave - the artifact whose entire premise is 'marching cubes cave seen from inside' - ships with the same winding as the landscapes, and TerrainMat.tres renders cull_back. Whichever way that winding points, the artifact named 'inside' made no different choice from the one named 'cave'. It is not an axis (two values, below the floor, and a winding order is a material-culling fact rather than a field property). It should be its own fix.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in projected-area currency, computed by hand rather than by rasterising the scene. Read it as an order-of-magnitude claim the sweep can falsify, not as the critic's own hottest-5%-of-crop number. capture_config_sweep places its OWN camera at dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, RES 760.

CLOSEST PAIR ON plumb: bedded (1.0) vs steep (3.0), AT ABOUT 11% OF FRAME. Solid requires the ridged sum to exceed isoLevel + k(y+100)/300. At k=1 that is satisfied up to roughly y = +15 for a typical sum; at k=3 the same sum is exceeded only by about y = -60. The top of the mass drops roughly 75 m in a 280 m box shown at ~53% of frame height, and the newly-empty band is 75/280 x 53% = about 13% of frame height across the ~42% of frame width the body occupies - call it 11% once the silhouette's obliquity is taken off. The LARGEST pair should be bedded vs overturned, over 35%, since the mass moves from the bottom of the frame to the top.

CLOSEST PAIR ON octaves, AND IT IS A PREDICTION THAT THE AXIS IS PARTLY DEGENERATE ON PURPOSE: 3 vs 6, UNDER 2%. The design named that pair too, but for the wrong reason and on the wrong scope. On this token only octaves 0-3 clear the 8.75 m Nyquist limit, so rungs 2, 3 and 6 differ ONLY in octaves that alias rather than resolve - the near-degeneracy is a three-way tie among {2, 3, 6}, not a single close pair, and 3-vs-6 is merely the member of it with the smallest amplitude difference (0.125 + 0.0625 + 0.03125 = 0.219 of the ladder's 1.969, gated down further by :174). The pair that MUST move is 1 vs 6: one octave is a smooth blobby cave with no wall texture at all, predicted over 25%.

IF 3-vs-6 COMES BACK NEAR ZERO ON mc_cave AND ALIVE ON mc_inside_cave, THE AXIS HAS DONE ITS JOB AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS DEAD. The degeneracy IS the finding: it is the Nyquist limit of the extraction lattice showing up as a photograph. A dead reading on the sub-limit rungs of one token and a live one on the other is the result this axis was declared to produce.

THE RUNG THAT COULD GO WRONG IS 1, and the confound is stated rather than hidden. Dropping octaves 1-5 removes up to 0.969 of the amplitude ladder (much less after the weight gating), and against the 1/300 gradient every unit of removed sum is 300 m of horizon. So `1` will look both SMOOTHER and EMPTIER, and the two effects are not separable in a still - octaves is borrowing plumb's pixels at its bottom rung. If that dominates the tile, the low rung should come up to 2 rather than the axis being called confounded.

AND THE ONE NUMBER THIS TOKEN IS EXPECTED TO DISAGREE WITH ITS SIBLING ON: 3-vs-6 should be LARGER here, perhaps 4%, because octave 3 measures 9.2 m against this lattice's 8.75 m limit and so is the one sub-ladder rung that clears it. That single crossing is the whole of the inside/outside asymmetry expressed as a measurement. If both tokens return the same number for 3-vs-6, the Nyquist reading is wrong and the axis is just an amplitude ladder.
dna.framing_why: 0.75, the same value as mc_cave and deliberately so: these two galleries are meant to be read against each other frame for frame, and a different crop would make the comparison an argument about framing. The arithmetic differs only by chunk_scale - the union AABB over the plumb rungs is this scene's 280 m box (weightless fills it to all six faces at every rung, as on the sibling), radius = 280 x sqrt(3) / 2 = 242.5 m, dist = 242.5 / tan(17deg) * 1.9 * 0.75 = 1130 m, and the subject occupies the same ~53% of frame height because both the box and the distance scale together. Which is the point: the two tiles differ in what the field DOES, not in how big the box is.
dna.fixture_why: NO FIXTURE, for the same four reasons as mc_cave: _ready() builds synchronously and ungated, snoise is seedless and noise_offset is pinned by the .tscn at (150, -100, 200), params.time is declared and never read, and the sweep's ~8-frame settle closes long before the base's 102-frame re-dispatch could replace the mesh. THE SAME LOG CHECK APPLIES: if the host cannot build a RenderingDevice, or the 500,000-triangle abort fires, every tile is _create_simple_cave_mesh()'s sine tunnel and both axes measure zero for the wrong reason. Valid only on 'Generation complete!'. INSTALLED AS WELL AS ARGUED (2026-08-12): this entry previously carried this paragraph and NO `fixture` key, so the guard it describes was prose only - cabinet_sweep.py reads `dna.fixture` and probe_anamorphic.py reads it again to render under the same conditions, and both were getting an empty dict. The dict is now present. It is honestly a WEAK guard and that is worth stating rather than overselling: use_fallback and continuous_update are both already false by export default and neither .tscn sets them, and a rendering device that fails on the capture host routes through init_compute() -> _create_fallback_mesh() without consulting use_fallback at all. So the dict cannot prevent the fallback sheet; only the log line can detect it. What the dict does buy is that the gallery and the standpoint probe apply the same config, which is the requirement probe_anamorphic's own header sets out.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config stamps each config key as config_<key> metadata, re-reads the two overrides, then compares _config_signature() - the shader's own input array, stringified at %.6f - against the signature captured at the end of _ready(). Equal means return; empty means _ready has not built yet and will read the metadata itself. Only a real change reaches _regenerate(), which re-runs run_compute / fetch_and_process_compute_data / create_mesh in _ready's order and re-captures the signature. INDEX 0 IS DELIBERATELY SKIPPED, and this is a real difference from TerrainGeneratorGyroid, which stringifies all eleven base floats. `time` is the first of the shared prefix and this subclass does NOT override _process, so the base's tick keeps advancing it for ~102 frames after spawn (12 wait-frames for GPU sync, then 90 for the mesh thread) until create_mesh sets _initial_generation_done and calls set_process(false). Including it would make the guard a CLOCK and every config call would read as a change. It cannot affect the mesh: params.time is declared in ParamsBuffer at :126 and referenced NOWHERE else in the file - grepped, not assumed. _owned IS EMPTY AND STAYS EMPTY. It is kept so the invariant is stated rather than assumed: create_mesh() rewrites array_mesh's single surface in place and the base's _create_collision() removes only the StaticBody3D it made itself, so this script creates no node it could free. A blanket free of children is what cost three scripts a pass in an earlier wave - GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to the artifact after spawn. _regenerate() also returns early on use_fallback, on a null rendering_device, and on waiting_for_compute / waiting_for_meshthread: resubmitting under a dispatch already in flight is the crash release() documents, and that guard is load-bearing HERE in a way it is not on the gyroid, because this subclass keeps the base's _process and is still cycling when a config call could land.

Neither 1.5 nor 0.5 is re-derived from a table that happens to land on the same number, so the density field, the marching loop, the edge interpolation and the vertex colours are computed from identical floats. dna.was: Eight exports and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was the word `pass`. The artifact's own declared critical_parameter, bulginess, was welded at 1.5, so its truth line - "the difference between geology and architecture is just parameter choice" - was argued at exactly one parameter choice, which is the fault `fusion` was promoted to fix on the metaballs next door. The cell size was an export named `resolution` that no scene, no map and no caller has ever set. And the four noise fields were seeded from four bare randi() calls, so "the same cave twice" was not something this artifact could do.
dna.note: bulge is GEOLOGY OR ARCHITECTURE, and it is the artifact's own word - the code already calls the generator bulge_noise and the parameter bulginess, which is the `fusion` pattern: the artifact's own truth made variable, in the artifact's own vocabulary. bulginess does two things in calculate_density_at_position: it warps the sample point by up to bulginess * 10 m of cellular noise, and it scales the primary noise read at the warped point, which then enters the density sum at 0.5 weight. pillowed = 1.5 SHIPPED. gridded = 0.0 is the artifact's own stated null - the term is multiplied by bulginess twice over, so at zero the warp vanishes exactly and what is left is simplex noise plus a vertical gradient plus a smoothstep boundary, the "gridded-out rock" the desire line says it is trying not to be. rounded = 0.75 is the half-step where the warp is legible AS a warp. engulfed = 2.5, deliberately not 3.0: at 0.5 weight the bulge term already swings about +/-1.25 against other terms of similar magnitude, and a higher value risks a wholly solid or wholly empty field - the empty one photographs as NO RENDER, which the critic reads as a dead axis rather than an overdriven one. resolution is HOW FINELY THE FIELD IS SAMPLED, the second half of the sequence's own gap, and it argues against this artifact's own emerges line, "the cubes-and-cases substrate vanishes into the sensed roundness of the result". At coarse it does not vanish. mid = 0.5 m SHIPPED (21x13x21 samples, 20x12x20 marched cells); coarse = 1.0 m (11x7x11 samples, 600 cells - half-metre plates you can read the lattice off); fine = 0.3 m (34x21x34 samples, ~21,800 cells). Three rungs and not four: 0.2 m is ~75,000 samples and ~525,000 FastNoiseLite calls inside _ready, a watchdog risk that buys no extra argument. Same field, same threshold, same noise - only the sampling moves, and the claim of roundness turns out to be a claim about a cell size. The WORD is shared, taken from riemann_pump ("resolution is HOW FINE THE PARTITION IS ... the partition is this artifact's own subject", rungs pump|coarse|mid|fine) and from sphere_mid (coarse|mid|fine|ultra), and declared here with the shipped state named `mid` so the three can be read against each other. When a shared vocabulary is honest the siblings measure ALIKE, which is itself the check.
dna.rename: THE ONE PLACE THE DESIGN COULD NOT BE FOLLOWED LITERALLY. The cell size shipped as `@export var resolution: float = 0.5`, so the shared word was already spent on the number, and an axis name has to be a settable property. riemann_pump and sphere_mid both keep the named rung on `resolution` and the magnitude on a second property (n_strips; rings and radial_segments), so matching them means the float moves to `cell_size` and `resolution` becomes the enum. VERIFIED BY READING that nothing sets the old property: QueerMarchingCave.tscn does not, noise_terrain_with_blobs_demo.tscn instances the scene with a bare `[node ... instance=ExtResource]` line and overrides nothing, no map passes any key to this token, and set_cave_parameters never handled it. get_cave_info() still reports the NUMBER under the key "resolution" - at the shipped defaults the same 0.5 - so its one external contract is unchanged, with the rung added alongside as "resolution_rung". _read_metadata_overrides also accepts a NUMERIC config_resolution and routes it to cell_size, so a token written against the old name lands somewhere instead of being dropped as an unknown rung.
dna.declined: REFUSED BY NAME as time-domain: color_shift_speed and pulse_intensity. They are the only thing _process does - animate_cave_colors writes emission_energy = 1.8 + sin(time * speed) * intensity and lerps the albedo on a second sinusoid - so they are a rate and an animation phase, and a still photographs one arbitrary moment of them. Two frames of the SAME value taken 1.5 s apart would differ, which is the metaballs clock trap. They are pinned by the fixture instead of promoted. Also refused: vertical_bias and cave_density, which are real and visible but are magnitudes on the same density sum that `bulge` already varies, so they would say one thing twice; and cave_size, which is extent, and extent self-cancels under a camera that fits the subject. primary_noise_scale / secondary_noise_scale were considered for the second axis and dropped in favour of resolution: they change the FIELD, whereas resolution changes what the extractor is allowed to see of it, which is the sequence's question.
dna.fixture_why: THE DESIGN BRIEF SAID THIS ARTIFACT WAS SEEDED. IT WAS NOT, AND THAT IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING FINDING OF THE PASS. setup_noise_generators() called randi() four times, once per FastNoiseLite, from Godot's globally-seeded RNG, and regenerate_cave() did it four more. Every instantiation was a different cave, so an unfixed sweep would have photographed twelve unrelated objects and reported the difference between them as an axis - a confident bite number about nothing. cave_seed was added as a new int export where 0 means "keep the shipped randi() calls exactly, in the same order, consuming the global stream identically" (the metaball_seed pattern, and the only way to preserve behaviour that is itself random), and any other value derives the four seeds as seed, seed+1, seed+2, seed+3, assigned BEFORE the first get_noise_3d call. 20260811 pins them. The two zeros freeze animate_cave_colors so emission_energy is a constant 1.8 and the albedo lerp is a constant, which makes two frames of the same variant byte-comparable. Both are written as NUMBERS, never as the strings "0.0": a typed float export rejects a string assigned before _ready.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config stamps every incoming key as config_* metadata, re-reads the overrides, then compares an eleven-field signature (both rungs, cave_seed, the two RESOLVED floats, cave_size, iso_level, cave_density, vertical_bias and the two noise scales) against the one taken before the stamp. Unchanged means return, because a rebuild here is a whole density field plus a whole marching pass plus a new ConcavePolygonShape3D. It also returns early when _built is false, which is the normal case - config lands before _ready, the values are stashed as metadata, and _ready reads them, so the artifact is built once and not twice. NOTHING IS FREED and no _owned array is needed: this script creates no child nodes at all, it writes into the scene's own $CaveMesh.mesh and $CaveCollision/CollisionShape.shape, so the _RotationTimer GridInteractablesComponent attaches to this root after spawn is never in reach. The rebuild also does NOT call setup_noise_generators(): at cave_seed 0 that would draw four fresh randi() values and silently re-roll the cave underneath a config key that only moved `bulge`. The seeds are re-applied only when the cave is pinned.

The tool read them off the trailing `# 1 | 2 | 3 | 6` on the @export line (the trailing-comment branch, last in check_dna_declarations' value order) and wrote ["1", "2", "3", "6"], which would make the cave tokens the only scened entries in the corpus with string-numeric axis values, against ~35 numeric axes (noise_quarry.octaves, lsystem_dungeon.depth, star_primitive.points, mc_portal_landscape.num_portals) every one of which is spelled as numbers. THE DERIVATION CHAIN SURVIVES THE RETYPE, AND THIS WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: apply_dna_block compares `{k: [str(x) for x in v]}` against what it derives, and str(1) == "1", so both `--refresh` and a fresh `--token=... --axes=plumb,octaves` report `already matches the code` and write nothing. check_dna_declarations takes the numeric branch either way and reports ok. WHAT THE RETYPE BUYS IS THE STANDPOINT PROBE, and nothing else. build_dna_gallery reaches cabinet_sweep over a command line, so a value makes the round trip str() -> coerce() -> int and THE GALLERY IS BIT-IDENTICAL EITHER WAY. probe_anamorphic.py does not: at line 103 it reads the registry directly and keeps only `isinstance(v, str)`, writing the survivors straight into the capture spec. Spelled as strings it would hand capture_config_sweep the String "1" for a typed `int` export, and four identical frames would be published as doc/reports/anamorphic_<token>.json - which is the file the critic's standpoint gate reads, so a false 'flat from all five standpoints' becomes a manufactured conviction. Spelled as numbers the probe keeps nothing and returns an obvious null. The two failure modes are asymmetric; this takes the loud one. A SEPARATE CONSEQUENCE OF THE SAME FILTER, worth reporting on its own: probe_anamorphic cannot clear an INERT? verdict on ANY numeric axis in the corpus, because isinstance(str) empties the value list for all ~35 of them. That is a gap in the gate, not in this artifact.

Identical export counts across sibling tokens is the tell for a one-scene-many-names family, and when the shared vocabulary is honest the siblings measure ALIKE - which is itself the check on this pair.

REACH MEASURED FOR THIS TOKEN: 2 placements, neither reaching apply_grid_config. A bare grid cell in ISO_CaveGeneration interactables[9][9] (no `#` config, no default_params on this entry, so merged_config is empty and _apply_artifact_config is never called) and a curation_station roster in Corridor_ISO_CaveGeneration interactables[5][12] (`#artifacts:marchingcave,marchingcubes_cave#layout:row`), which misses because curation_station.gd:381 asks `has_method` of the scriptless Node3D root. dna.was: See mc_cave. Zero @export of its own; apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`.
dna.note:
THE SEQUENCE'S TRUTH LINE, LITERALLY. 'Define a field, extract a surface. The boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry.' This script is the one place in the wave where the SAME field is shipped twice, once to be looked at and once to be stood inside, so an axis declared here has to mean something from both sides. You are OUTSIDE this one: the scene's camera sits at (-15, 35, 50) looking in, with a DirectionalLight3D and five torches, so the field reads as a block of rock with a top surface and a sky.

plumb - WHICH WAY IS DOWN, AND WHETHER THERE IS A DOWN AT ALL. Everything this shader knows about gravity is one line, MarchingCubes.glsl:180: `density = -(worldPos.y+100)/300 + density`. It is the ONLY anisotropic term in the file; the six octaves above it are isotropic ridged noise, which on its own has no up. That one linear bias is what makes low regions solid and high regions air - from outside, the block's top surface and its sky; from inside, the floor you stand on. plumbScale multiplies it and nothing else. bedded (1.0) SHIPPED. overturned (-1.0) flips the sign: the same noise at the same threshold with inside and outside exchanged, rock overhead and nothing under your feet. weightless (0.0) DELETES the term and leaves pure ridged noise - an isotropic sponge with no floor, no ceiling and no sky, filling the sampled box to all six faces. steep (3.0) triples the gradient so the field swings 3.0 across the 300 m box instead of 1.0 and the solid retreats into the bottom third: a slab with a rough top, a crawl space. The four values are held IDENTICAL across all four declared tokens on purpose - it is one const on one script, and holding them identical is what makes the galleries comparable frame for frame.

octaves - HOW MANY SCALES OF ROCK SURVIVE THE LATTICE, AND THIS IS THE AXIS THAT MAKES THE SIBLINGS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS. :168 opens `for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++)`; each pass halves the amplitude and doubles the frequency, with the weight feedback at :174 gating each octave by the previous one. The literal 6 is the rung. What makes it worth declaring is arithmetic the two scenes do not share. THIS token: noise_scale 13.5, chunk_scale 300.0, so samplePos = worldPos x 0.04500 and octave 0 has ~22 m features; the marching lattice samples at 300.0/64 = 4.688 m, so its Nyquist limit is 9.38 m. The six octaves measure 22.2, 11.1, 5.5, 2.8, 1.4, 0.7 m, which puts 2 of them above the limit and the rest below it. On the sibling the same six octaves land differently, and that is the finding: mc_cave resolves TWO scales of rock, mc_inside_cave resolves FOUR, from the same script, the same shader, the same rungs and the same threshold. The artifact you stand inside can resolve two more octaves than the one you look at. That is the inside/outside asymmetry as a number rather than as a description, and it is why the axis is declared on both rather than on one.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE APPROVED DESIGN, both found by redoing its arithmetic. (1) The design said the inside scene resolves ONE more octave than the outside one; by the Nyquist figures above it is TWO (octaves 0-3 against octaves 0-1). (2) The design said the sub-limit octaves are 'COMPUTED AND THEN THROWN AWAY BY THE EXTRACTOR'. They are not thrown away, they ALIAS: content finer than the sampling cell still perturbs the corner values, which still moves where interpolateVerts puts the crossing. So the sub-limit rungs are predicted to be nearly degenerate, not exactly degenerate, and a small non-zero reading there is the expected result rather than a failed prediction.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE FIELD ITSELF: :170 is `snoise(samplePos) * 2 - 1` before the ridged fold, not the plain `snoise` of the usual Lague construction, so the input to `1 - abs(noise)` spans about [-3, 1] rather than [-1, 1] and the fold is off-centre. The amplitude LADDER still halves exactly (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125), which is what the octave arithmetic above rests on, but the per-octave term is not bounded by 1 and the summed density is not bounded by 1.969. Any claim about an absolute density total should be read as about the ladder, not about the sum.
dna.declined: REFUSED, `iso_level`, and the refusal is deliberate given that this wave promotes `threshold` on the torus. iso_level is the ONE export on which these two sibling scenes already disagree - 0.85 on marchingcubes_cave.tscn against 0.88 on marchingcubes_inside_cave.tscn - so an axis over it would say 'these two artifacts are one object at two thresholds', which is nearly irresistible. It is refused because on THIS shader the density carries a vertical gradient, so a constant offset to the threshold is a vertical translation of the rock/air horizon, which is the same horizon `plumb` moves: a bias of 0.15 is 45 m of horizon on a 300 m box, and plumb=steep moves it further. The two would measure each other at plumb=bedded and separate only at plumb=weightless - a conditional pair bought at the price of a confound. The torus pays gyroid_demo's bequest instead, because its field has no gradient term at all. REFUSED, the weight-gating literal 10 at :174 (`weight = max(0, min(1, noise * 10))`): it is the Lague trick that turns isotropic ridged fBm into connected tunnels and it is the closest thing in the file to an axis about whether the void is a passage or a sealed bubble - refused because at low values it also zeroes every octave after the first, so it conflates connectivity with detail and would be `octaves` wearing another name. REFUSED, `noise_offset` (a different arbitrary sample of the same field, and already fixed by the .tscn), `chunk_scale` and `center_position` (a size and a placement, both self-cancelling under an AABB-fitted camera), `continuous_update` (a rate, invisible in a still by law). REFUSED, `invert_faces`, AND THIS ONE IS A REPORTED DEFECT RATHER THAN A DECLINE. TerrainGeneratorBase:10 documents it as 'Flip triangle winding and normals (useful for objects vs caves)' and NEITHER cave scene sets it, so mc_inside_cave - the artifact whose entire premise is 'marching cubes cave seen from inside' - ships with the same winding as the landscapes, and TerrainMat.tres renders cull_back. Whichever way that winding points, the artifact named 'inside' made no different choice from the one named 'cave'. It is not an axis (two values, below the floor, and a winding order is a material-culling fact rather than a field property). It should be its own fix.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in projected-area currency, computed by hand rather than by rasterising the scene. Read it as an order-of-magnitude claim the sweep can falsify, not as the critic's own hottest-5%-of-crop number. capture_config_sweep places its OWN camera at dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, RES 760.

CLOSEST PAIR ON plumb: bedded (1.0) vs steep (3.0), AT ABOUT 11% OF FRAME. Solid requires the ridged sum to exceed isoLevel + k(y+100)/300. At k=1 that is satisfied up to roughly y = +15 for a typical sum; at k=3 the same sum is exceeded only by about y = -60. The top of the mass drops roughly 75 m in a 300 m box shown at ~53% of frame height, and the newly-empty band is 75/300 x 53% = about 13% of frame height across the ~42% of frame width the body occupies - call it 11% once the silhouette's obliquity is taken off. The LARGEST pair should be bedded vs overturned, over 35%, since the mass moves from the bottom of the frame to the top.

CLOSEST PAIR ON octaves, AND IT IS A PREDICTION THAT THE AXIS IS PARTLY DEGENERATE ON PURPOSE: 3 vs 6, UNDER 2%. The design named that pair too, but for the wrong reason and on the wrong scope. On this token only octaves 0-1 clear the 9.38 m Nyquist limit, so rungs 2, 3 and 6 differ ONLY in octaves that alias rather than resolve - the near-degeneracy is a three-way tie among {2, 3, 6}, not a single close pair, and 3-vs-6 is merely the member of it with the smallest amplitude difference (0.125 + 0.0625 + 0.03125 = 0.219 of the ladder's 1.969, gated down further by :174). The pair that MUST move is 1 vs 6: one octave is a smooth blobby cave with no wall texture at all, predicted over 25%.

IF 3-vs-6 COMES BACK NEAR ZERO ON mc_cave AND ALIVE ON mc_inside_cave, THE AXIS HAS DONE ITS JOB AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS DEAD. The degeneracy IS the finding: it is the Nyquist limit of the extraction lattice showing up as a photograph. A dead reading on the sub-limit rungs of one token and a live one on the other is the result this axis was declared to produce.

THE RUNG THAT COULD GO WRONG IS 1, and the confound is stated rather than hidden. Dropping octaves 1-5 removes up to 0.969 of the amplitude ladder (much less after the weight gating), and against the 1/300 gradient every unit of removed sum is 300 m of horizon. So `1` will look both SMOOTHER and EMPTIER, and the two effects are not separable in a still - octaves is borrowing plumb's pixels at its bottom rung. If that dominates the tile, the low rung should come up to 2 rather than the axis being called confounded.

dna.fixture_why:
MINIMAL FIXTURE. Identical to mc_cave's: ungated synchronous _ready, seedless noise, pinned noise_offset, unread params.time. Same fallback-tunnel log check.

FIXTURE, AND IT PINS THE HAZARD NAMED ABOVE RATHER THAN A SEED. {use_fallback: false, continuous_update: false} are both already the base class's defaults and neither cave .tscn overrides either, so the pin changes NOTHING about what any placement renders - it is written as a bool, straight onto the property before _ready, per the fixture-typing rule. What it buys is that the bench cannot silently take the _create_simple_cave_mesh() path and photograph the sine tunnel instead of the field, and cannot be handed a re-dispatching artifact mid-settle. The log check still stands as the real guarantee: valid only on 'Generation complete!', never on 'Creating fallback'.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config stamps each config key as config_<key> metadata, re-reads the two overrides, then compares _config_signature() - the shader's own input array, stringified at %.6f - against the signature captured at the end of _ready(). Equal means return; empty means _ready has not built yet and will read the metadata itself. Only a real change reaches _regenerate(), which re-runs run_compute / fetch_and_process_compute_data / create_mesh in _ready's order and re-captures the signature. INDEX 0 IS DELIBERATELY SKIPPED, and this is a real difference from TerrainGeneratorGyroid, which stringifies all eleven base floats. `time` is the first of the shared prefix and this subclass does NOT override _process, so the base's tick keeps advancing it for ~102 frames after spawn (12 wait-frames for GPU sync, then 90 for the mesh thread) until create_mesh sets _initial_generation_done and calls set_process(false). Including it would make the guard a CLOCK and every config call would read as a change. It cannot affect the mesh: params.time is declared in ParamsBuffer at :126 and referenced NOWHERE else in the file - grepped, not assumed. _owned IS EMPTY AND STAYS EMPTY. It is kept so the invariant is stated rather than assumed: create_mesh() rewrites array_mesh's single surface in place and the base's _create_collision() removes only the StaticBody3D it made itself, so this script creates no node it could free. A blanket free of children is what cost three scripts a pass in an earlier wave - GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to the artifact after spawn. _regenerate() also returns early on use_fallback, on a null rendering_device, and on waiting_for_compute / waiting_for_meshthread: resubmitting under a dispatch already in flight is the crash release() documents, and that guard is load-bearing HERE in a way it is not on the gyroid, because this subclass keeps the base's _process and is still cycling when a config call could land.
dna.still_note: Static. Same as mc_cave.
dna.kin: `octaves` is SHARED, taken from noise_quarry (values [1,2,3,4]) and held also by noise_space and simplex_noise, where it asks the identical thing of a plain fBm sum. The name must BE the property name, because the sweep sets the property by name - the same constraint that forced queer_marching_cave to move a float off `resolution` before it could name an enum that. Declared here with the shipped 6 as the top rung rather than 4, so the family's [1,2,3,4] and this [1,2,3,6] can be read against each other with three rungs in common. If a count-of-scales axis measures alike on a cave and on a quarry, the family is honest. `plumb` is NEW and free across all 437 declared axis names in the corpus. `bed` is held by grid_3d_capture, `ground` by flashlight_demo and light_sphere, `law` by seven artifacts including force_field_zone, `datum` by slack_yard, `incline` by friction_ramp and normal_force_demo. `plumb` is chosen because a plumb line is the instrument that DEFINES down rather than one that measures it, which is the claim: this artifact's down is a term someone wrote, not a fact about the world it is in. NOT re-argued from wave 1: `resolution` is already spent twice in this sequence (queer_marching_cave, animated_noise_explorer) on how finely the field is SAMPLED. `octaves` is the neighbouring question - how much of the field there is to sample - and the two meet in the Nyquist arithmetic under `note`.
dna.shader_contract: TWO trailing floats appended to MarchingCubes.glsl's ParamsBuffer after noiseOffsetZ, taking indices 11 and 12: `float plumbScale;` (was the implicit 1.0 on the y-gradient at :180) and `float octaves;` (was the literal 6 in the loop bound at :168, carried as a float because the whole buffer is floats and read back as int(params.octaves)). Count goes 11 -> 13 on BOTH sides. VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, not by eye: the ParamsBuffer field list was parsed out of the .glsl with comments stripped and compared index by index against TerrainGeneratorBase.get_params_array()'s eleven appends plus TerrainGenerator's two, and the same script confirmed that every `params.<field>` the shader reads is declared and that the shared eleven-field prefix is byte-for-byte the same list as in MarchingCubesFlat, OverhangTerrain, PortalTerrain, Torus, Fountain and Gyroid. GPU: time, noiseScale, isoLevel, numVoxelsPerAxis, scale, posX, posY, posZ, noiseOffsetX, noiseOffsetY, noiseOffsetZ, plumbScale, octaves. CPU: time, noise_scale, iso_level, float(num_voxels_per_axis), chunk_scale, center_position.x/.y/.z, noise_offset.x/.y/.z, _plumb_scale(), float(clampi(octaves, 1, 6)). chunk_scale is the GDScript name for the shader's `scale`. THE ORDER OF THE LAST TWO IS THE ENTIRE RISK SURFACE: swapping them makes plumb read 6.0 and octaves read 1, which produces a plausible mesh and no compile error. Only three lines of the .glsl changed - the two declarations, the loop bound, and the gradient statement. MarchingCubes.glsl is loaded by TerrainGenerator.gd and by nothing else. STALE-SHADER WARNING, WHICH THIS PASS COULD NOT ITSELF CLEAR: headless Godot does not reimport, so an edited .glsl does not reach a sweep until the orchestrator reimports. Wave 1 published sixteen byte-identical gyroid tiles and an INERT verdict on a correct axis for exactly this reason. If both axes come back at 0.00% on all four rungs, suspect the import before the design: check source_md5 in .godot/imported/*.md5 against the file hash, NOT mtime.
dna.crossed_wire: REPORTED, NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS, and confirmed by reading both entries. The registry token `marchingcubes_portal_landscape` (procgen_extra.json) names res://algorithms/proceduralgeneration/isosurfaces/marchingcave/Scenes/marchingcubes_overhang_landscape.tscn - the OVERHANG scene - while `mc_portal_landscape` (isosurfaces.json) names marchingcubes_portal_landscape.tscn. So the long-form name that reads like the portal artifact's sibling is bound to a different artifact, and the portal scene is reachable only through the short token. Not touched here: correcting the scene path would silently change what every existing placement of `marchingcubes_portal_landscape` renders. A SECOND DRIFT FOUND WHILE COUNTING PLACEMENTS, and it belongs to this entry's own family: mc_cave's registry `class_name` field reads TerrainGeneratorBase, not TerrainGenerator. It is the parent class, so it is not a wrong file, but it names the abstract base rather than the script the scene runs - the same shape of drift as mc_portal_landscape's class_name naming TerrainGeneratorPortals where the scene runs TerrainGeneratorUnifiedPortals.
dna.family: ONE SCRIPT, THREE SCENES, SIX REGISTRY NAMES - a hidden family at SCRIPT level rather than at scene level, which is the first one this corpus has found. The five known before it (curation_station's booleans, the grab spheres, the pickup cubes, the synth racks, the translation cubes) all hide one level lower, at the scene. TerrainGenerator.gd is loaded by marchingcubes_cave.tscn (mc_cave, marchingcubes_cave), marchingcubes_inside_cave.tscn (mc_inside_cave, marchingcubes_inside_cave) and marchingcubes.tscn (mc_base, marchingcave), all three by the same script uid c2aji3u2bgmv8. THE AXES ARE DECLARED ON FOUR OF THE SIX, AND THE TWO OMISSIONS ARE DELIBERATE. marchingcubes.tscn sets use_fallback = true, so TerrainGeneratorBase._ready() returns at its line 65, MarchingCubes.glsl is never loaded, and what renders is _create_simple_cave_mesh()'s hand-written 200 m sine tunnel. Both axes are inert there BY CONSTRUCTION. The approved design listed mc_base and marchingcave under also_serves; declaring them would publish four identical pictures of that tunnel and earn a 0.00% verdict about the wrong artifact, which is precisely the false-INERT trap the standpoint gate exists to stop. So they are named here and left undeclared.
